questions.question: You are a lecturer and arrive to find your classroom flooded, so your session cannot go ahead. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, who should you notify as soon as possible after recognising this adverse occurrence?
options: Your line manager
The Principal
The Facilities Manager
The Academic Board
questions.explanation: The policy states that all staff should notify their line manager as soon as possible after recognising an adverse occurrence.
questions.source_excerpt: All staff should: 2.4 Notify their line manager as soon as possible after recognising an adverse occurrence;

questions.question: A power cut forces your afternoon classes to be cancelled. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, how must this adverse occurrence first be reported?
options: By emailing the Registrar and the Principal a written summary of the occurrence within 24 hours
Via the online Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form on the SMS system's Internal Site Link
On a paper Adverse Occurrence Form handed to the Registrar within five working days
By logging an IT Helpdesk ticket, which is then forwarded to the Facilities Manager
questions.explanation: The policy requires any adverse occurrence to be reported first via the online Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form, found in the Staff operational forms / documents section of the Internal Site Link on the SMS system.
questions.source_excerpt: Any adverse occurrence must first be reported via the online Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form which can be found in the Staff ... operational forms / documents section of the Internal Site Link on the SMS system

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, whom must non-academic managers and Course Coordinators notify about an adverse occurrence they believe requires notification to the Principal and/or Facilities Manager?
options: The Academic Board
The Board of Directors
The Quality Assurance team
The College Registrar
questions.explanation: Non-academic managers and Course Coordinators are responsible for notifying the Registrar of any adverse occurrence they believe requires notification to the Principal and/or Facilities Manager.
questions.source_excerpt: All non-academic managers and Course Coordinators have the responsibility to: 2.1 Notify the Registrar regarding any adverse occurrence that occurs which they believe requires notification to the Principal and/or Facilities Manager;

questions.question: According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what does the Registrar do once an adverse occurrence has been reported?
options: Assesses any associated risks and reports them to the Principal
Arranges catch-up classes for all students affected by the occurrence
Moves any affected assessment scripts to a secure location
Informs all prospective students who hold an offer to study
questions.explanation: Under the reporting procedure, the Registrar assesses any risks associated with the adverse occurrence and reports them to the Principal.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will assess any associated risks in relation to the adverse occurrence, and report this to the Principal;

questions.question: When reporting an adverse occurrence, which of the following does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say the report should identify where possible?
options: The names of any staff members believed to be responsible for causing the occurrence
Whether specific student groups, such as disabled students, are disproportionately affected
The estimated financial cost of the occurrence to the College and its awarding bodies
The disciplinary action recommended for any staff member found to be involved in the occurrence
questions.explanation: The policy asks the report to identify, where possible, whether specific student groups (e.g. disabled students or those needing reasonable adjustments) are disproportionately affected.
questions.source_excerpt: Where possible, the report should identify whether any specific student groups are disproportionately affected, including disabled students, students requiring reasonable adjustments, students with caring responsibilities, part-time students, commuting students, or students with digital access needs.

questions.question: According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, how is an 'adverse occurrence' defined?
options: Any planned change to teaching, timetabling or assessment arrangements that results in a formal complaint from students or staff
Any breach of College policy by a member of staff that is referred to the Registrar for a formal investigation
Any unexpected event or incident that leads to an unfavourable or harmful outcome for students, staff or external stakeholders
Any incident that causes the College a financial loss above the threshold recorded in its Master Risk Register
questions.explanation: The policy defines an adverse occurrence as any unexpected event or incident leading to an unfavourable or harmful outcome for students, staff or external stakeholders at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: An adverse occurrence includes any event or incident that unexpectedly happens, and leads to an unfavourable or harmful outcome, for students, staff or external stakeholders at the College.

questions.question: A lecturer on your programme is off sick and several classes have been missed. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, who is responsible for arranging catch-up classes at the earliest opportunity?
options: The absent lecturer, on their return to work
The College Registrar
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
The Course Coordinator
questions.explanation: The policy makes the Course Coordinator responsible for arranging catch-up classes at the earliest opportunity when teaching staff are absent.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of the absence of teaching staff, the Course Coordinator will take the responsibility of arranging catch-up classes at the earliest opportunity.

questions.question: One of the College campuses must close so that an investigation can commence. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what is the assigned Course Coordinator responsible for?
options: Informing the awarding body of the closure and submitting an action plan to mitigate the risks
Deciding whether the risk from the closure should be added to the College's Master Risk Register
Communicating with students about the disruption and providing them with a revised timetable
Updating the College website and social media channels with full details of the closure
questions.explanation: When a campus closes, the policy makes the assigned Course Coordinator responsible for communicating with students about disruption to teaching time and providing a revised timetable.
questions.source_excerpt: Should any of the College campuses have to close due to an adverse occurrence or so an investigation can commence, the assigned Course Coordinator will be responsible for communicating with students about the potential disruption to teaching time, providing students with a revised timetable

questions.question: A roof leak threatens a room where active assessment scripts are stored. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what are Course Coordinators required to do to minimise this risk?
options: Ensure the active scripts and papers are moved to a secure location as soon as possible
Leave the scripts in place until the Registrar has assessed the risk and reported it to the Principal
Obtain the awarding body's approval before moving any of the active scripts or papers
Photograph the scripts and leave them in place until the Facilities Manager has inspected the room
questions.explanation: To minimise the risk of damage to assessment scripts, the policy requires Course Coordinators to ensure active scripts and papers are moved to a secure location as soon as possible.
questions.source_excerpt: In order to minimise this risk, the Course Coordinators are to ensure any active scripts and papers are moved to a secure location as soon as possible;

questions.question: According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, who is responsible for informing the relevant awarding body and the students about incidents affecting assessment scripts?
options: The assigned Course Coordinator and the Principal
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) and the Registrar
The Head of Data and Information Technologies (HoDIT) and the Facilities Manager
The Quality Assurance and Enhancement department and Admissions
questions.explanation: The policy gives HoPAM and the Registrar responsibility for informing the awarding body and students about incidents regarding assessment scripts, supported by an action plan.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the responsibility of the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) and the Registrar to inform the relevant awarding body, as well as the students about any incidents regarding ... assessment scripts at the earliest opportunity, supported by an action plan to mitigate risks.

questions.question: According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, in the event of IT system failures, who is to commence the appropriate actions in accordance with the College Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan?
options: The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM)
The Registrar and the Facilities Manager
The Head of Data and Information Technologies (HoDIT)
The Quality Assurance and Enhancement department
questions.explanation: For IT system failures, the policy states that the Head of Data and Information Technologies (HoDIT) commences the appropriate actions in line with the College Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of IT system failures, the Head of Data and Information Technologies (HoDIT) is to commence the appropriate actions in accordance with the College Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan;

questions.question: According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, on what basis will LCC close programmes when they must be discontinued?
options: Only after a majority of enrolled students on the programme have voted in favour of the closure
Only once the Principal Executive Group has approved the closure as part of its annual review
Only when the Registrar has recorded the closure and its risks on the College's Master Risk Register
Only with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body and/or other accrediting bodies
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC will only close programmes with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body and/or other accrediting bodies.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will only close programmes with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body and/or other accrediting bodies;

questions.question: According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what is the College committed to doing promptly when any adverse occurrence happens?
options: Informing both internal and external stakeholders of the occurrence
Suspending all teaching on the affected campus until it has been reviewed
Referring the occurrence to its awarding body for a formal investigation
Recording the occurrence in the Master Risk Register as a new College risk
questions.explanation: The policy commits the College to promptly informing both internal and external stakeholders of any adverse occurrence, followed by the timely implementation of contingency measures.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is committed to promptly informing both internal and external stakeholders of any adverse occurrence, followed by the timely implementation of contingency measures and actions to address the situation efficiently.

questions.question: Which of the following is explicitly listed in the Adverse Occurrence Policy as one of the areas that the policy covers?
options: A student appeal against a published assessment result
An inability of the College to distribute assessment results
A planned change to the published assessment timetable
A staff request to change their contracted working hours
questions.explanation: The policy's list of areas covered includes the inability of the College to distribute assessment results, alongside items such as staff illness and adverse weather.
questions.source_excerpt: Below is a list of areas that this policy covers which includes (but is not limited to): ... i) Inability of the College to distribute assessment results;

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what kind of culture are non-academic managers and Course Coordinators responsible for establishing?
options: One where only incidents that affect assessments need to be reported
One where incidents are reported anonymously and directly to the Principal
One where it is adequate and safe for staff to report all incidents
One where teams resolve incidents locally before any of them are reported
questions.explanation: Non-academic managers and Course Coordinators must establish a culture where it is adequate and safe for staff to report all incidents regarding an adverse occurrence.
questions.source_excerpt: Establish a culture where it is adequate and safe for staff to report all incidents and/or cases regarding an adverse occurrence;

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what must all staff ensure regarding any sensitive information about an adverse occurrence?
options: It is shared with all of the affected students within one working day
It is posted on the SMS system so that all College staff can view it
It is forwarded to the awarding body together with the report form
It is kept confidential and not disclosed unless permitted and/or required
questions.explanation: All staff must ensure sensitive information about an adverse occurrence is kept confidential and is not disclosed unless they are permitted and/or required to do so.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure any sensitive information regarding an adverse occurrence is kept confidential and not to be disclosed unless permitted and/or required to do so.

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy's reporting procedure, who determines whether a risk related to an adverse occurrence should be considered for the College's Master Risk Register?
options: The Principal
The Registrar
The Facilities Manager
The Academic Board
questions.explanation: After the Registrar has assessed and reported the risks, the Principal determines whether a related risk should be considered for inclusion in the Master Risk Register (MRR).
questions.source_excerpt: The Principal will then determine whether a risk related to the adverse occurrence should be considered for inclusion in the College's Master Risk Register (MRR);

questions.question: When describing the impact of an adverse occurrence on key College functions, which examples of those functions does the Adverse Occurrence Policy give?
options: Admissions, marketing and student recruitment
Assessments, teaching time and timetabling
Payroll, procurement and estates budgets
Graduation, open days and alumni events
questions.explanation: The policy asks reporters to describe the impact on key functions of the College, giving assessments, teaching time and timetabling as examples.
questions.source_excerpt: Describe the impact that the adverse occurrence had on key functions of the College (e.g. assessments, teaching time, timetabling etc.);

questions.question: Besides recording the date and time of an adverse occurrence, what timing detail does the Adverse Occurrence Policy ask the report to outline, if possible?
options: When the Principal expects the investigation to be closed
When the affected staff last completed relevant training
When the effects of the adverse occurrence will be felt
When the awarding body last audited the affected programme
questions.explanation: Under the section on when the occurrence happened, the report should, if possible, outline when the effects of the adverse occurrence will be felt.
questions.source_excerpt: If possible, to ensure that the date and time of the adverse occurrence has been recorded; ... If possible, to outline when the effects of the adverse occurrence will be felt.

questions.question: Besides any student groups that are disproportionately affected, what else does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say an adverse occurrence report should identify?
options: Any tuition fee refunds that affected students may be entitled to
Any changes needed to the programme's published learning outcomes
Any statement the College should issue to the media or the press
Any immediate reasonable adjustments or support measures required
questions.explanation: The policy states that the report should also identify any immediate reasonable adjustments or support measures required.
questions.source_excerpt: The report should also identify any immediate reasonable adjustments or support measures required.

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, how will all assessment data, including provisional assessment grades, be protected?
options: It will be encrypted and accessible only to approved staff members
It will be held on paper by the Registrar until results are released
It will be stored on the awarding body's portal and deleted locally
It will be anonymised and shared with the Quality Assurance team
questions.explanation: The policy states that all assessment data, including provisional grades, will be encrypted and only accessible to approved staff members.
questions.source_excerpt: All the assessment data including provisional assessment grades will be encrypted and will only be accessible to approved staff members;

questions.question: According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which types of data must LCC ensure have a secure back-up?
options: Financial, payroll and procurement data
Personal, assessment and feedback data
Library, catering and estates maintenance data
Attendance, room-booking and timetabling data
questions.explanation: To mitigate IT disruption, LCC must ensure there is a secure back-up for all types of personal, assessment and feedback data.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC is to ensure that there is a secure back-up for all the types of personal, assessment and feedback data;

questions.question: When the College manages disruption to teaching location or delivery, what does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say alternative delivery arrangements, locations or timetables must be?
options: Cost-neutral and temporary
Online and asynchronous
Accessible and inclusive
Standardised and centralised
questions.explanation: In managing disruption to teaching location or delivery, the College will ensure that alternative delivery arrangements, locations or timetables are accessible and inclusive.
questions.source_excerpt: In managing disruption to teaching location or delivery, the College will take specific and proportionate measures to address the needs of affected student groups. ... ensuring that alternative delivery arrangements, locations or timetables are accessible and inclusive;

questions.question: If LCC can no longer deliver any accredited qualifications, which group does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say the College must formally notify, in addition to supporting enrolled students?
options: Former students who graduated within the last five years
Local schools and colleges that refer applicants to LCC
Employers who sponsor students on work placements
Prospective students who have received an offer to study
questions.explanation: Besides implementing a contingency plan for enrolled students, the College must formally notify prospective students who have received an offer to study at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: If London Churchill College is no longer able to deliver any accredited qualifications, the College is responsible for implementing a contingency plan to support and protect all enrolled students. Additionally, the College must formally notify prospective students who have received an offer to study at the College about the situation.

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, when students are seeking a new accreditation provider offering a similar programme, which departments are they invited to speak to about reapplying?
options: The Admissions and Marketing departments
The Registry and Finance departments
The Student Services and Welfare teams
The Quality Assurance and Compliance teams
questions.explanation: Students will be invited to speak to the Admissions and Marketing departments to discuss the reapplication process with the new provider.
questions.source_excerpt: In the process of seeking a new accreditation provider offering a similar programme, students will be invited to speak to the Admissions and Marketing departments to discuss the reapplication process with the new provider;

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which department validates updated public information about affected programmes before it is uploaded via PIMG protocols?
options: The Registry and Student Records department
The Quality Assurance and Enhancement department
The Data and Information Technologies department
The Programmes and Academic Monitoring department
questions.explanation: Admissions and Marketing must make sure that updated programme information is accurate and validated by the Quality Assurance and Enhancement department before upload.
questions.source_excerpt: The Admissions and Marketing Departments will make sure that all information is accurate, validated by the Quality Assurance and Enhancement department, and uploaded via PIMG protocols.

questions.question: When a programme is being closed, until when does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say quality and academic standards are monitored?
options: Until the awarding body formally confirms the programme's closure date
Until the final teaching week of the year in which closure is announced
Until the last student has had sufficient opportunity to complete the programme
Until the Academic Board has approved the final programme closure report
questions.explanation: Quality and academic standards are monitored throughout the closure process until the last student has had sufficient opportunity to complete the programme successfully.
questions.source_excerpt: Quality and academic standards are monitored throughout the closure process, until the last student has had sufficient opportunity to complete the programme of study successfully;

questions.question: According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, where are the detailed procedures for closing a discontinued programme set out?
options: In the College's Master Risk Register
In the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan
In the Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form
In the Programme Closure Policy
questions.explanation: The policy states that the detailed closure procedures are set out in the Programme Closure Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: The detailed closure procedures are stated in the Programme Closure Policy.

questions.question: If a College campus is forced to cease functioning or relocate, what does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say existing students must be informed of?
options: The alternative mechanism of student support for academic and non-academic matters
The revised tuition fees that will apply to them at the new campus location
The deadline for transferring to another provider without any financial penalty
The travel subsidy available to students attending the relocated campus
questions.explanation: Where a campus ceases functioning or relocates, existing students must be informed of the alternative mechanism of student support for both academic and non-academic matters.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event that any of the College campuses are forced to cease functioning or relocate, the College aims to ensure: ... d) Existing students must be informed of the alternative mechanism of student support for both academic and non-academic matters;

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, the Registrar keeps an annual record of all adverse occurrences. To which group is this record reported?
options: The Board of Directors (BoD)
The Principal Executive Group (PEG)
The Senior Management Team (SMT)
The Quality Assurance Committee (QAC)
questions.explanation: The Registrar keeps an annual record of all adverse occurrences and reports it to the Principal Executive Group (PEG).
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will keep an annual record of all adverse occurrences and report it to the Principal Executive Group (PEG).

questions.question: You have just submitted the online Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which sequence of steps then follows?
options: Your line manager assesses the associated risks and reports them to the Academic Board, which decides on Master Risk Register inclusion
The Registrar assesses the associated risks and reports them to the Principal, who decides whether the risk is considered for the Master Risk Register
The Principal assesses the associated risks and reports them to the Registrar, who decides whether the risk is considered for the Master Risk Register
The Facilities Manager assesses the associated risks and reports them to the Registrar, who then adds the risk to the Master Risk Register
questions.explanation: After the report is made via the form, the Registrar assesses the associated risks and reports to the Principal, who then determines whether the risk should be considered for inclusion in the Master Risk Register.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will assess any associated risks in relation to the adverse occurrence, and report this to the Principal; ... The Principal will then determine whether a risk related to the adverse occurrence should be considered for inclusion in the College's Master Risk Register (MRR);

questions.question: Heavy snow disrupts trains and buses, so many students and staff cannot reach campus for their classes. How does the Adverse Occurrence Policy apply to this situation?
options: It is not covered, as the policy only applies where College facilities or assessment scripts are damaged
It is not covered, as weather events are dealt with solely under the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan
It is covered only if the College then has to close one of its campuses for the rest of that day
It is covered, as unexpected travel disruption and adverse weather conditions are both listed areas
questions.explanation: The policy's list of covered areas expressly includes unexpected travel disruption and adverse weather conditions, with no requirement for a campus closure.
questions.source_excerpt: Below is a list of areas that this policy covers which includes (but is not limited to): a) Unexpected travel disruption; ... e) Adverse weather conditions;

questions.question: The same equipment failure has disrupted a Course Coordinator's classes twice this term. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what are Course Coordinators responsible for regarding occurrences like this?
options: Ensuring action is taken and a robust process is in place to help prevent the occurrence repeating
Suspending the affected classes until the Principal has approved a permanent solution to the fault
Referring the matter to the awarding body if the same failure occurs a third time in one term
Recording each repeat on the Master Risk Register without first involving the Registrar
questions.explanation: Non-academic managers and Course Coordinators must ensure action is taken and that a robust process is in place to aid in preventing an adverse occurrence from repeating itself.
questions.source_excerpt: All non-academic managers and Course Coordinators have the responsibility to: ... Ensure that the action is taken and there is a robust process in place to aid in preventing an adverse occurrence from repeating itself;

questions.question: A lab outage only came to light a week later, when a student mentioned it in an email. When you describe the adverse occurrence in your report, which of these does the Adverse Occurrence Policy ask you to include?
options: An explanation of why the student did not use the online reporting form sooner
The names of the staff members who should have noticed the outage sooner
The circumstances in which the occurrence came to be known and reported
A recommended date by which the lab should be fully back in use by students
questions.explanation: The description of an adverse occurrence should cover the circumstance in which it came to be known and reported, alongside the functions affected and the impact on them.
questions.source_excerpt: Describe the circumstance in which the adverse occurrence came to be known and reported.

questions.question: A lecturer's absence has led the Course Coordinator to arrange catch-up classes. According to the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what else must the assigned Course Coordinator ensure?
options: That the Registrar approves the catch-up classes before any of the students are told about them
That all impacted students are contacted and, where required, are given a revised timetable
That the absent lecturer, where possible, delivers every catch-up class personally on return
That HoPAM, where required, informs the awarding body of the teaching time that was lost
questions.explanation: The assigned Course Coordinator must ensure communication is sent to all impacted students and, where required, that a revised timetable is provided to affected students.
questions.source_excerpt: The assigned Course Coordinator will ensure that communication is sent to all impacted students and, where required, a revised timetable will be provided to all students affected by the adverse occurrence.

questions.question: A fire alarm evacuation stops a morning of teaching, and you are completing the Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which key information should the report outline, if possible?
options: Written statements from each of the students who were evacuated from the building
The date on which the building's fire alarm system was last serviced and tested
A recommended disciplinary outcome for the person who set off the fire alarm
The extent to which students, staff and external stakeholders are aware of it
questions.explanation: Under key information, the report should, if possible, outline the extent to which students, members of staff and external stakeholders are sufficiently aware of the adverse occurrence.
questions.source_excerpt: If possible, outline the extent to which students, members of staff, and external stakeholders are sufficiently aware of the adverse occurrence;

questions.question: A campus has to close after a gas leak, and students ask whether their course can continue. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what must the assigned Course Coordinator outline to them?
options: Whether the College can still provide an effective mode of delivery to sustain teaching
Whether the findings of the investigation will be added to the College's Master Risk Register
Whether their tuition fees will be reduced for all of the weeks that the campus stays closed
Whether the days lost will count against their attendance record for the rest of the term
questions.explanation: When a campus closes, the assigned Course Coordinator must communicate with students, provide a revised timetable and outline whether the College can still provide an effective mode of delivery to sustain teaching.
questions.source_excerpt: Should any of the College campuses have to close due to an adverse occurrence or so an investigation can commence, the assigned Course Coordinator will be responsible for communicating with students ... and outlining whether the College can still provide an effective mode of delivery to sustain teaching;

questions.question: Teaching moves to another site after a campus closure, and a disabled student cannot use the new building's facilities. Which measure does the Adverse Occurrence Policy commit the College to in this situation?
options: Offering the student a deferral to the next academic year in place of any adjustments
Referring the student to the awarding body to apply for special consideration instead
Implementing reasonable adjustments to teaching delivery, facilities and support services
Authorising the student's absence until the original campus is able to reopen
questions.explanation: In managing disruption to teaching location or delivery, the College commits to implementing reasonable adjustments to teaching delivery, facilities and support services for affected students.
questions.source_excerpt: In managing disruption to teaching location or delivery, the College will take specific and proportionate measures to address the needs of affected student groups. This will include: ... Implementing reasonable adjustments to teaching delivery, facilities and support services;

questions.question: After a flood damages assessment scripts, HoPAM and the Registrar must inform the awarding body and the students at the earliest opportunity. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what must support this communication?
options: A signed statement from the Course Coordinator
A copy of the completed Adverse Occurrence form
A replacement assessment date for every student
An action plan to mitigate the risks involved
questions.explanation: HoPAM and the Registrar must inform the awarding body and students about incidents regarding assessment scripts at the earliest opportunity, supported by an action plan to mitigate risks.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the responsibility of the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) and the Registrar to inform the relevant awarding body, as well as the students about any incidents regarding ... assessment scripts at the earliest opportunity, supported by an action plan to mitigate risks.

questions.question: An issue arises that prevents assessment results from being released to students. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, who should inform the awarding body and the students, and when?
options: The assigned Course Coordinator, once a revised release date has been agreed with students
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) and the Registrar, as soon as possible
The Principal, but only after deciding whether the issue belongs on the Master Risk Register
The Quality Assurance and Enhancement department, at the end of that academic year
questions.explanation: Where there is any issue in releasing results, HoPAM and the Registrar should inform the awarding body and the students as soon as possible.
questions.source_excerpt: Should there be any issue in releasing the results to the students, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) and the Registrar should inform the awarding body and the students as soon as possible;

questions.question: LCC can no longer deliver its accredited qualifications, and an enrolled student decides to continue their studies with an alternative provider suggested by the College. What does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say LCC will do?
options: Have a team in place to support the student's transition to that provider
Refund the student's tuition fees for the whole of the current academic year
Keep the student's place open in case LCC later regains its accreditation
Issue the student with an interim LCC certificate for the credits achieved
questions.explanation: Enrolled students are told about alternative providers, and if a student decides to continue with the suggested provider, LCC will have a team in place to support the transition.
questions.source_excerpt: Inform all enrolled students about alternative providers who provide the same or similar programmes. Should the student decide to continue their studies with the suggested alternative provider, LCC will have a team in place to support this transition;

questions.question: LCC can no longer deliver its accredited qualifications, and a student decides to withdraw. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, through which process will the College liaise with them about alternative programmes?
options: A Programme Closure Review Panel
An Alternative Provider Open Evening
A Programme Reinstatement Day
A Student Transition Advice Clinic
questions.explanation: The College must liaise with withdrawing and prospective students about alternative programmes, and runs this process through a Programme Reinstatement Day.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has a responsibility to liaise with any withdrawing student, as well as prospective students, to inform them about alternative programmes. The College will run this process through a Programme Reinstatement Day;

questions.question: LCC can no longer deliver an accredited qualification, so public information about the affected programmes needs changing. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, when should that information be updated?
options: At the next scheduled review of the College's website content
Once the Academic Board has reviewed the annual occurrence record
After the last enrolled student has completed the programme
With immediate effect across the website and other channels
questions.explanation: Public information about affected programmes is updated on the website and other College communication channels with immediate effect.
questions.source_excerpt: Any public information about the affected programmes will be updated on the website and other College communication channels (e.g. email, social media) with immediate effect.

questions.question: A programme has to be discontinued following an adverse occurrence. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what must happen to the decisions the College takes throughout the closure?
options: They must be approved by a vote of the students enrolled on the programme
They must be formally recorded at all stages of planning and implementation
They must be kept confidential until the last student has completed
Only the final closure decision needs recording, and only by the Registrar
questions.explanation: When a programme is discontinued, the College ensures that decisions taken at all stages of planning and implementation are formally recorded.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event that any of the programmes and/or courses must be discontinued, the College will ensure that: ... Decisions taken at all stages of planning and implementation are formally recorded;

questions.question: A College campus is relocated after an adverse occurrence. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what kind of support will the College provide to the students affected by the relocation?
options: Targeted academic, pastoral and administrative support
Financial compensation for any additional travel costs
Automatic extensions on all their assessment deadlines
Priority transfer to another provider of their choice
questions.explanation: In implementing relocation or alternative delivery arrangements, the College will provide targeted academic, pastoral and administrative support to affected students.
questions.source_excerpt: In implementing relocation or alternative delivery arrangements, the College will take specific and proportionate measures to address the needs of affected student groups. ... d) providing targeted academic, pastoral and administrative support to affected students.

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, the Registrar's annual record of adverse occurrences is reported to the Principal Executive Group. What then happens to the record at the end of each academic year?
options: It is sent to the awarding body for external verification
It is published on the College website for students to read
It is submitted to the Academic Board for review and oversight
It is archived by the Registrar and closed to any further review
questions.explanation: The Registrar reports the annual record to PEG, and at the end of each academic year the record is submitted to the Academic Board for review and oversight.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will keep an annual record of all adverse occurrences and report it to the Principal Executive Group (PEG). At the end of each academic year, the record will be submitted to the Academic Board for review and oversight.

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which pair of questions will the annual review of adverse occurrences consider?
options: Whether particular student groups were disproportionately affected, and whether mitigation was timely, accessible and effective
Whether the reporting forms were completed in full, and whether mitigation costs stayed within the approved budgets
Whether any staff member was at fault, and whether the Master Risk Register was updated within the required timeframe
Whether the awarding body was satisfied, and whether students rated the mitigation measures highly in their surveys
questions.explanation: The annual review considers whether adverse occurrences had a disproportionate impact on particular student groups and whether the mitigation measures taken were timely, accessible and effective.
questions.source_excerpt: The annual review will include consideration of whether adverse occurrences had a disproportionate impact on particular student groups, including disabled students and students requiring reasonable adjustment, and whether the mitigation measures taken were timely, accessible and effective.

questions.question: An unexpected incident causes a harmful outcome for students, but it does not match any of the areas listed in the Adverse Occurrence Policy's scope. How does the policy treat this incident?
options: As an adverse occurrence, since the list of covered areas is not exhaustive and the incident meets the definition
As outside the policy, since only the ten listed areas count as adverse occurrences for the purposes of reporting
As an adverse occurrence only once the Principal has added it to the College's Master Risk Register as a risk
As outside the policy unless the awarding body confirms in writing that it should be treated as an occurrence
questions.explanation: The list of covered areas 'includes (but is not limited to)' the named items, and any unexpected event leading to an unfavourable or harmful outcome for students, staff or external stakeholders is an adverse occurrence.
questions.source_excerpt: An adverse occurrence includes any event or incident that unexpectedly happens, and leads to an unfavourable or harmful outcome, for students, staff or external stakeholders at the College. Below is a list of areas that this policy covers which includes (but is not limited to):

questions.question: A lecturer and their Course Coordinator both witness an adverse occurrence that the Coordinator believes the Principal should know about. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which split of notification duties is correct?
options: The lecturer notifies the Registrar, and the Course Coordinator notifies the Principal directly
The lecturer notifies their line manager, and the Course Coordinator notifies the Registrar
The lecturer notifies the Principal, and the Course Coordinator notifies the Facilities Manager
The lecturer notifies the Academic Board, and the Course Coordinator notifies the Facilities Manager
questions.explanation: All staff notify their line manager as soon as possible, while Course Coordinators notify the Registrar about occurrences they believe require notification to the Principal and/or Facilities Manager.
questions.source_excerpt: Notify the Registrar regarding any adverse occurrence that occurs which they believe requires notification to the Principal and/or Facilities Manager; ... All staff should: 2.4 Notify their line manager as soon as possible after recognising an adverse occurrence;

questions.question: An adverse occurrence you witnessed involves sensitive details about a colleague, and you hesitate to report it because of confidentiality. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what should you do?
options: Hold off reporting it until the colleague has given written consent for the details to be shared
Tell your line manager verbally only, as confidential matters are exempt from the online form
Report it via the online form, as confidentiality only bars disclosure not permitted or required
Report only the date and location, leaving out any description of what happened or its impact
questions.explanation: Any adverse occurrence must first be reported via the online form; the confidentiality duty stops sensitive information being disclosed unless permitted and/or required, and reporting is required.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure any sensitive information regarding an adverse occurrence is kept confidential and not to be disclosed unless permitted and/or required to do so. ... Any adverse occurrence must first be reported via the online Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form

questions.question: A member of the College community who is not on the staff wants to report an adverse incident they have noticed. What does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say they must do?
options: Ask a non-academic manager to report it, as only managers and Course Coordinators may make reports
Raise it through the student complaints procedure, as the reporting route is for staff members only
Write to the Registrar, who decides whether the incident is serious enough to be formally reported
Follow the reporting link provided in the policy's procedure and submit the report themselves
questions.explanation: The policy states that if a member of the College community wishes to report any adverse occurrence or adverse incident, they must follow the link it provides; the route is not limited to managers or staff.
questions.source_excerpt: If a member of the College community wishes to report any adverse occurrence or adverse incident, they must follow this link here.

questions.question: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which statement correctly separates the roles of the Principal and the Registrar in tracking adverse occurrences and their risks?
options: The Principal decides whether a risk is considered for the Master Risk Register; the Registrar keeps the annual record and reports it to the Principal Executive Group
The Registrar decides whether a risk is considered for the Master Risk Register; the Principal keeps the annual record and reports it to the Principal Executive Group
The Principal keeps the annual record of all occurrences and submits it to the Academic Board; the Registrar adds each new risk to the Master Risk Register
The Registrar decides whether a risk is added to the Master Risk Register; the Principal submits the annual record of all occurrences to the Academic Board
questions.explanation: The Principal determines whether a risk should be considered for the Master Risk Register, and the Registrar keeps an annual record of all adverse occurrences and reports it to the Principal Executive Group (PEG).
questions.source_excerpt: The Principal will then determine whether a risk related to the adverse occurrence should be considered for inclusion in the College's Master Risk Register (MRR); ... The Registrar will keep an annual record of all adverse occurrences and report it to the Principal Executive Group (PEG).

questions.question: A Course Coordinator phones the Registrar about an adverse occurrence and considers the matter fully reported. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what does the reporting procedure still require?
options: A written follow-up to the Principal within 24 hours of the call
A report via the online Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form
A note of the call added to the Master Risk Register entry
A sign-off from the Facilities Manager on the phone report
questions.explanation: Any adverse occurrence must first be reported via the online Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form; notifying the Registrar by phone does not replace this step.
questions.source_excerpt: Any adverse occurrence must first be reported via the online Adverse Occurrence Reporting Form which can be found in the Staff ... operational forms / documents section of the Internal Site Link on the SMS system;

questions.question: You are completing an adverse occurrence report but cannot yet find out how many students were affected. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, how should you treat this detail?
options: Hold the report back until the Registrar has confirmed the exact number of affected students
Pass the report to your line manager, as only managers may submit reports with missing data
Submit the report without it, as data on the numbers affected is requested only if possible
Enter an estimate, as a report cannot be accepted without a figure for the students affected
questions.explanation: The policy asks for data on the number of students and/or staff affected only 'if possible', so a missing figure does not stop the occurrence being reported.
questions.source_excerpt: If possible, provide data regarding the number of students and/or members of staff who were affected by an adverse occurrence;

questions.question: An adverse occurrence mainly affects part-time students and students who commute long distances. What does the Adverse Occurrence Policy expect the report to identify, where possible?
options: Nothing further, since only disabled students and those needing adjustments are identified
Only the total number of students affected, without naming any particular student groups
The fee refunds these groups can claim, and the deadline by which they must submit claims
Whether these groups are disproportionately affected, and any immediate adjustments or support
questions.explanation: Part-time and commuting students are among the groups the report should consider for disproportionate impact, and the report should also identify any immediate reasonable adjustments or support measures required.
questions.source_excerpt: Where possible, the report should identify whether any specific student groups are disproportionately affected, including disabled students, students requiring reasonable adjustments, students with caring responsibilities, part-time students, commuting students, or students with digital access needs. The report should also identify any immediate reasonable adjustments or support measures required.

questions.question: A lecturer is absent, and the Course Coordinator fits the catch-up classes into existing free slots without changing the timetable. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what must the Coordinator still ensure?
options: That communication is sent to all impacted students
That a revised timetable is issued to all students anyway
That the Registrar approves the catch-up arrangements first
That the absent lecturer delivers each of the catch-up classes
questions.explanation: The Course Coordinator must ensure communication is sent to all impacted students; a revised timetable is only provided where required.
questions.source_excerpt: The assigned Course Coordinator will ensure that communication is sent to all impacted students and, where required, a revised timetable will be provided to all students affected by the adverse occurrence.

questions.question: During recovery from an IT system failure, a colleague who is not an approved staff member asks you to email them a cohort's provisional assessment grades. What does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say?
options: It is not allowed until HoDIT has completed recovery under the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan
It is not allowed, as assessment data is accessible only to approved staff members
It is allowed if the grades are sent as an encrypted file rather than in the email body
It is allowed, as provisional grades are not final and so do not count as assessment data
questions.explanation: All assessment data, including provisional grades, is encrypted and only accessible to approved staff members, and nothing in the IT recovery provisions relaxes this.
questions.source_excerpt: All the assessment data including provisional assessment grades will be encrypted and will only be accessible to approved staff members;

questions.question: A burst sprinkler soaks a store of assessment scripts, and the Course Coordinator plans to tell the awarding body and students personally. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, how are these duties divided?
options: The Course Coordinator informs the awarding body; the Registrar informs the affected students
The Course Coordinator informs both, once HoDIT has confirmed the extent of the damage
HoPAM and the Registrar inform both; the Course Coordinator moves active scripts to safety
The Principal informs both, once the Course Coordinator has logged the risk on the register
questions.explanation: Course Coordinators ensure active scripts and papers are moved to a secure location, while HoPAM and the Registrar inform the awarding body and the students about incidents regarding scripts.
questions.source_excerpt: In order to minimise this risk, the Course Coordinators are to ensure any active scripts and papers are moved to a secure location as soon as possible; ... It is the responsibility of the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) and the Registrar to inform the relevant awarding body, as well as the students about any incidents regarding

questions.question: An IT system failure stops assessment results being released to students on the published date. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which combination of responses applies?
options: HoDIT informs the awarding body and students; HoPAM starts the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan actions
The Registrar starts the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan actions; the Course Coordinator informs the awarding body and students
HoPAM starts the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan actions; the Principal informs the awarding body and students
HoDIT starts the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan actions; HoPAM and the Registrar inform the awarding body and students
questions.explanation: HoDIT commences the appropriate actions under the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan for IT failures, and HoPAM and the Registrar inform the awarding body and students of any issue in releasing results.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of IT system failures, the Head of Data and Information Technologies (HoDIT) is to commence the appropriate actions in accordance with the College Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan; ... Should there be any issue in releasing the results to the students, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) and the Registrar should inform the awarding body and the students

questions.question: An adverse occurrence causes LCC to lose its Centre Approval Status, leaving it unable to deliver any accredited qualifications. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which set of obligations applies?
options: Inform the whole College community, support enrolled students via a contingency plan and formally notify offer-holders
Support enrolled students via a contingency plan, but tell offer-holders nothing until they have formally enrolled
Inform the awarding body only, and leave it to contact enrolled students and offer-holders directly on LCC's behalf
Inform staff first, and delay any contact with students or offer-holders until a new accreditation provider is found
questions.explanation: The College must inform all members of the College community if it loses Centre Approval Status, implement a contingency plan for enrolled students and formally notify prospective students holding an offer.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the responsibility of the College to inform all members of the College community in the event the College loses its Centre Approval Status due to the effects of an adverse occurrence; ... the College is responsible for implementing a contingency plan to support and protect all enrolled students. Additionally, the College must formally notify prospective students who have received an offer

questions.question: LCC can no longer deliver an accredited programme, and a colleague wants to post an update about it on social media straight away. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what must be true of that update?
options: It can go out unvalidated, as only website content needs checking by Quality Assurance
It must be approved by the awarding body before it appears on any College channel
It must be accurate, validated by Quality Assurance and Enhancement and uploaded via PIMG
It must wait until the Academic Board has reviewed the annual adverse occurrence record
questions.explanation: Public information on the website and other channels, including social media, is updated with immediate effect, but all information must be accurate, validated by Quality Assurance and Enhancement and uploaded via PIMG protocols.
questions.source_excerpt: Any public information about the affected programmes will be updated on the website and other College communication channels (e.g. email, social media) with immediate effect. The Admissions and Marketing Departments will make sure that all information is accurate, validated by the Quality Assurance and Enhancement department, and uploaded via PIMG protocols.

questions.question: A programme is being discontinued and its remaining students will be taught remotely during the transition. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which requirements apply to the remote teaching and to quality?
options: Remote teaching is optional during the transition, and quality monitoring ends as soon as the closure is formally announced
Remote teaching must be approved by the Principal, and quality is monitored to the end of that academic year
Remote teaching follows the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan, and quality is checked at the annual review
Remote teaching must be secure and meet UKQC expectations, and quality is monitored until the last student can complete
questions.explanation: Remote teaching arrangements must be securely in place and meet UKQC expectations, and quality and standards are monitored until the last student has had sufficient opportunity to complete.
questions.source_excerpt: Remote teaching arrangements are securely in place and meet the expectation set out by the United Kingdom Quality Council (UKQC); ... Quality and academic standards are monitored throughout the closure process, until the last student has had sufficient opportunity to complete the programme of study successfully;

questions.question: A programme is being discontinued. An applicant who has not yet enrolled asks whether the College will consult them. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy's discontinuation provisions, what applies?
options: Potential students, not only existing ones, are to be fully informed, consulted and supported
Only existing students are consulted; applicants are simply told that the programme has closed
Applicants are consulted only if they have already accepted an offer and paid their deposit
Applicants are referred to the awarding body, which consults them on the College's behalf
questions.explanation: When programmes or courses are discontinued, the College ensures that existing or potential students are fully informed, consulted and supported to protect their interests.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event that any of the programmes and/or courses must be discontinued, the College will ensure that: ... Existing or potential students are fully informed, consulted and supported to protect their interests;

questions.question: After a serious adverse occurrence, senior staff propose closing a programme at once and informing the awarding body afterwards. What does the Adverse Occurrence Policy say about this approach?
options: It is not permitted until the Principal has recorded the closure risk on the Master Risk Register
It is not permitted, as programmes close only with the awarding body's full knowledge and consultation
It is acceptable provided the decision is formally recorded and later reported to the Academic Board
It is acceptable in an emergency, provided students are consulted before the closure takes effect
questions.explanation: LCC will only close programmes with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body and/or other accrediting bodies, so informing them afterwards is not permitted.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will only close programmes with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body and/or other accrediting bodies;

questions.question: A College campus is forced to cease functioning and teaching moves to revised delivery methods. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what must the quality of academic delivery follow?
options: The operating standards the Facilities Manager sets for the replacement site
The internal standards the Principal Executive Group sets for each relocation
The good practice guidelines of relevant regulatory bodies, such as QAA and OfS
The interim standards agreed with students at a Programme Reinstatement Day
questions.explanation: Where a campus ceases functioning or relocates, the quality of academic delivery must follow the good practice guidelines of the relevant regulatory bodies (QAA, OfS etc.).
questions.source_excerpt: In the event that any of the College campuses are forced to cease functioning or relocate, the College aims to ensure: ... b) Revised and appropriate delivery methods are implemented to continue with learning and teaching; c) The quality of academic delivery must follow the good practices guidelines by the relevant regulatory bodies (QAA, OfS etc.);

questions.question: When managing disruption to teaching location or delivery after a campus closure, which of these is not one of the measures the Adverse Occurrence Policy commits the College to?
options: Identifying students who may be disproportionately affected, including disabled students
Ensuring alternative delivery arrangements, locations or timetables are accessible and inclusive
Providing additional academic and pastoral support to enable continuity of study
Offering affected students the option to defer their studies to the next academic year
questions.explanation: The campus closure measures are identifying disproportionately affected students, accessible and inclusive alternative arrangements, reasonable adjustments and additional academic and pastoral support; deferral to the next academic year is not one of them.
questions.source_excerpt: identifying students who may be disproportionately affected, including disabled students and those requiring reasonable adjustments; ... ensuring that alternative delivery arrangements, locations or timetables are accessible and inclusive; ... providing additional academic and pastoral support to enable continuity of study.

questions.question: Several details in an adverse occurrence report are requested only 'if possible' or 'where possible'. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which of these must the report include without that qualification?
options: Data on the number of students and staff affected by the occurrence
The date and time at which the adverse occurrence happened
A description of the College functions the occurrence impacted
The location where the adverse occurrence took place
questions.explanation: The policy asks the reporter to describe which College functions were impacted with no qualification, whereas the numbers affected, the date and time, and the location are each requested only 'if possible'.
questions.source_excerpt: Describe what functions of the College were impacted by the adverse occurrence; ... If possible, provide data regarding the number of students and/or members of staff who were affected ... If possible, to ensure that the date and time of the adverse occurrence has been recorded; ... If possible, to ensure that the location of the adverse occurrence has been recorded.

questions.question: A non-academic manager tells their team to report only major adverse occurrences and to ignore minor ones, so that the annual record stays short. Which statement correctly applies the Adverse Occurrence Policy to this instruction?
options: Minor occurrences fall outside the policy, which is aimed only at major disruption to assessment, teaching or learning
The policy covers minor as well as major occurrences, and managers must make it safe for staff to report all incidents
Minor occurrences are reported only where the Registrar believes that the Principal needs to be told about them
Minor occurrences are logged locally by the manager and added to the Registrar's annual record at the end of the year
questions.explanation: The policy's framework covers major or minor adverse occurrences, and managers must establish a culture where it is adequate and safe for staff to report all incidents regarding an adverse occurrence.
questions.source_excerpt: The objective of this policy is to establish a comprehensive framework for managing major or minor adverse occurrences that could disrupt the student assessment cycle, teaching, or learning processes ... Establish a culture where it is adequate and safe for staff to report all incidents and/or cases regarding an adverse occurrence;

questions.question: LCC can no longer deliver any accredited qualifications. An applicant who holds an offer but has not yet enrolled asks what the College will do for them. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, what applies?
options: Their offer is transferred automatically to a partner provider, so LCC does not need to contact them
Their details are passed to the awarding body, which contacts all applicants about the change for LCC
Their offer is withdrawn by letter and their application closed, with no further contact from the College
They are formally notified, and informed of alternative programmes through a Programme Reinstatement Day
questions.explanation: The College must formally notify prospective students who have received an offer, and it liaises with prospective students about alternative programmes through a Programme Reinstatement Day.
questions.source_excerpt: the College must formally notify prospective students who have received an offer to study at the College about the situation. ... The College has a responsibility to liaise with any withdrawing student, as well as prospective students, to inform them about alternative programmes. The College will run this process through a Programme Reinstatement Day;

questions.question: After a campus closure, teaching moves online and students with digital access needs struggle to take part. Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, which pair of actions applies?
options: The report leaves them out, as it flags only disabled students, and they are sent paper-based study packs instead
They are considered only at the annual review, and online delivery stays unchanged until the campus reopens
The report identifies whether they are disproportionately affected, and online delivery must be accessible and inclusive
HoDIT decides under the Disaster Recovery and Contingency Plan whether their needs are met, and the report omits them
questions.explanation: The report should identify, where possible, whether groups such as students with digital access needs are disproportionately affected, and in managing disrupted delivery the College must ensure alternative arrangements are accessible and inclusive.
questions.source_excerpt: Where possible, the report should identify whether any specific student groups are disproportionately affected, including ... students with digital access needs. ... ensuring that alternative delivery arrangements, locations or timetables are accessible and inclusive;

questions.question: According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, what must the monitoring of every LCC programme include?
options: Student feedback and pass rates, with staff and external views reported to the PEG instead
Staff appraisal outcomes, recruitment targets and a review of the marketing budget
Student, staff and external feedback, grade analysis and a review of resources
External examiner comments and pass rates, with student feedback collected every three years
questions.explanation: Section 2.1 states that all programmes must be monitored and include student, staff and external feedback, an analysis of grades and other performance indicators, and the learning, library and other resources available.
questions.source_excerpt: All programmes must be monitored and include student, staff and external feedback, an analysis of grades and other academic performance indicators, learning, library, and other resources available to staff and students;

questions.question: According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, how should annual monitoring reports be written?
options: Reflective and evidence-based, showing good practice as well as items needing improvement
Descriptive and chronological, recording the year's activities without evaluating them
Focused on problems needing improvement, with good practice reported separately to the Academic Board
Promotional in tone, highlighting successes so the programme is presented in a positive light
questions.explanation: The policy states that reviews are critical rather than descriptive, and that monitoring reports should be reflective and evidence-based, indicating both good practice and items that require improvement.
questions.source_excerpt: Reviews are critical, rather than descriptive; ... Annual monitoring reports should be reflective and evidence-based and indicate areas of good practice as well as items that require improvement.

questions.question: Your programme recently had an external review that identified good practice and some required actions. You are now drafting its monitoring report. Under the Annual Monitoring Policy, what should you do with the review's findings?
options: Include both the actions and the good practice from the review in the report
Leave them out, as external reviews are reported separately to the Oversight Board
Include the good practice but leave the actions for the external body to track
Pass them to the Student Representatives to decide whether they are included
questions.explanation: Section 2.4 states that actions and good practice arising from external reviews should be included in the monitoring reports.
questions.source_excerpt: Actions and good practice arising from external reviews should be included in the monitoring reports;

questions.question: You are a Unit Tutor and have just finished teaching a unit. According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, when should the Unit Evaluation Report (UER) for that unit be completed?
options: When the unit's pass rate falls below the programme average for that year
When an External Examiner or Standard Verifier requests it for their visit
After each instance of the unit's delivery, on LCC's standard UER form
Once every three years, as part of the periodic programme review cycle
questions.explanation: Section 3.2.2 states that a Unit Evaluation Report should be completed after each instance of Unit delivery, and 3.2.1 says LCC uses a standard UER across its taught provision, completed by the Unit Tutor.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC uses a standard Unit Evaluation Report (UER) across its taught provision, for completion by the Unit Tutor. ... A Unit Evaluation Report should be completed after each instance of Unit delivery.

questions.question: According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, how is the Principal's Executive Group (PEG) kept informed about programme delivery during the year?
options: Written reports each month and an oral report once a year
Oral reports each term and a written report at the end of the year
A single written report submitted at the end of each academic year
Oral reports each month and written reports submitted each term
questions.explanation: Section 3.1.1 states that oral reports are made to the PEG monthly and written reports are submitted each term, allowing a timely response to issues arising from programmes.
questions.source_excerpt: In order to secure oversight of programme delivery, oral reports are made to the PEG on a monthly basis and written reports are submitted each term.

questions.question: Under the Annual Monitoring Policy, which body tracks and monitors suggested and agreed changes throughout the following year and reports back to the Academic Board?
options: The College Oversight Board
The Principal's Executive Group
The Programme Committee
The Quality Assurance Department
questions.explanation: Section 2.7 states that the Principal's Executive Group (PEG) will track and monitor suggested and agreed changes throughout the following year and report back to the Academic Board.
questions.source_excerpt: The Principal's Executive Group (PEG) will track and monitor suggested and agreed changes throughout the following year and report back to the Academic Board at such times as the Board may require.

questions.question: A colleague's draft Unit Evaluation Report (UER) contains only the unit's pass statistics. Under the Annual Monitoring Policy, what else should the UER incorporate?
options: Attendance registers for each teaching session and the unit's timetable for the year
Student feedback, comparative figures, tutor reflections and a review of unit outcomes
The minutes of the Programme Committee meetings and the QESC terms of reference
The College Annual Monitoring Report action plan and its completion timeframes
questions.explanation: Section 3.2.1 states that the UER should incorporate quantitative and qualitative information, including student feedback, unit statistics and comparative figures, plus reflections from the Unit Tutor/teaching team and a review of Unit outcomes.
questions.source_excerpt: The UER should incorporate quantitative and qualitative information including student feedback, unit statistics and comparative figures. They should also include reflections from the Unit Tutor and/or teaching team, any feedback from External Examiners/Standard Verifiers and a review of Unit outcomes and student performance;

questions.question: According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, who is responsible for authoring the Programme Annual Monitoring Report (PAMR)?
options: The Unit Tutor for each unit on the programme
The Principal or his/her designated person
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
The Course Coordinators for the programme
questions.explanation: The PAMR reporting arrangement in section 3.3.2 names the Course Coordinators as the author; Unit Tutors author UERs and the Principal authors the College report.
questions.source_excerpt: Reporting arrangement: Review Cycle: Annually, January Author: Course Coordinators Output: Programme Annual Monitoring Report

questions.question: According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, what should the action plan in the College Annual Monitoring Report (CAMR) specify?
options: Each programme's budget allocation and staffing levels for the next academic year
Individual staff performance ratings, with training requirements and review dates
Student recruitment targets and marketing activity planned for each programme
Good practice to share, areas for improvement, timeframes and who is responsible
questions.explanation: Section 3.4.1 states that an action plan should specify good practice to be shared, areas for improvement/development, and the timeframe for their completion and by whom.
questions.source_excerpt: An action plan should be used to specify good practice to be shared, areas for improvement /development and the timeframe for their completion and by whom.

questions.question: You are a Programme Leader and, part-way through the term, you identify a matter on your programme that needs the PEG's immediate attention. Under the Annual Monitoring Policy, which report is designed to highlight such matters to the PEG?
options: The Termly Monitoring Report
The Unit Evaluation Report
The Programme Annual Monitoring Report
The College Annual Monitoring Report
questions.explanation: Section 3.1.2 requires Programme Leaders to complete the Termly Monitoring Report once per term; its template is designed to highlight to the PEG any matters requiring immediate attention.
questions.source_excerpt: Programme Leaders are required to complete the Termly Monitoring Report once per term according to the template, which is designed to highlight to the PEG any matters that require their immediate attention;

questions.question: Under the Annual Monitoring Policy, what is the review cycle for the Programme Annual Monitoring Report (PAMR)?
options: Annually, by November
Annually, in March
Annually, in January
Once per term
questions.explanation: The PAMR reporting arrangement sets its review cycle as annually, in January; the UER is due by November and the College report in March.
questions.source_excerpt: Reporting arrangement: Review Cycle: Annually, January Author: Course Coordinators

questions.question: An External Examiner asks to see the Programme Annual Monitoring Report (PAMR) for the programme you work on. According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, what is the position?
options: It cannot be provided, as PAMRs are internal documents kept within the College
It can be provided, as the PAMR is intended for External Examiners on request
It must be refused, as External Examiners receive the CAMR instead of the PAMR
External Examiners may see Unit Evaluation Reports but not the PAMR itself
questions.explanation: The PAMR reporting arrangement in section 3.3.2 states that it is intended for the Programme Committee, QESC and the External Examiner (if requested), so it can be provided on request.
questions.source_excerpt: Intended for: Programme Committee, QESC and External Examiner (if requested)

questions.question: According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, which programmes are covered by its quality assurance processes for annual monitoring?
options: Only programmes validated by Pearson, since other awarding bodies carry out their own annual monitoring
All award-bearing programmes for which the College is responsible for maintaining academic standards
Only programmes that received a critical External Examiner report in the previous academic year
Only undergraduate degree programmes, with short and non-credit courses monitored separately
questions.explanation: Section 1.1 states that the policy sets out annual monitoring processes for all award-bearing programmes for which the College is responsible for the maintenance of academic standards.
questions.source_excerpt: This document sets out the quality assurance processes for annual monitoring in place across London Churchill College (LCC) for all award-bearing programmes for which the College is responsible for the maintenance of academic standards.

questions.question: According to the Annual Monitoring Policy, what do the College's Annual Monitoring procedures support, in line with one of LCC's institutional strategies?
options: Setting individual lecturers' annual performance objectives
Allocating teaching budgets between programmes for each year
Approving new programmes before they are offered to students
The identification and monitoring of areas for enhancement
questions.explanation: Section 1.2 states that, in line with LCC's Enhancement Strategy, the Annual Monitoring procedures support the identification and monitoring of areas for enhancement.
questions.source_excerpt: In line with LCC's Enhancement Strategy, the Annual Monitoring procedures support the identification and monitoring of areas for enhancement;

questions.question: Under the Annual Monitoring Policy, why do Course Coordinators construct their reports through a set template?
options: To allow cross-comparison of data, enabling an overall College collective annual report
To let reports go straight to the awarding body without being reviewed by the College
To let External Examiners complete the statistical sections on the coordinators' behalf
