questions.source_excerpt: A learner undertaking a qualification with London Churchill College will not be assessed by a family member. Also, internal quality assurance for assessments for the said learner will not be undertaken by a family member.

questions.question: Under the Conflict of Interest Policy, what applies when family members both work for London Churchill College?
options: They may assess one another's work provided a third, unrelated colleague second-marks every piece
They must not work in the same department or report to the same line manager as each other
They may internally quality assure and invigilate for one another, but must not assess each other's work
They must not assess or internally quality assure one another, nor invigilate exams the other sits
questions.explanation: The policy states that family members working for the College will not be allowed to assess and/or internally quality assure one another, nor act as an invigilator for any examinations they may sit.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of any family members working for London Churchill College they will not be allowed to assess and/or internally quality assure one another, nor act as an invigilator for any examinations they may sit.

questions.question: You are asked to invigilate an examination and notice that your cousin is one of the candidates taking it. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say?
options: You must not invigilate that examination while your cousin is present
You may invigilate provided you are not the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator
You may invigilate if you stay at the far end of the room from your cousin
You may invigilate provided you note the relationship on the attendance register
questions.explanation: The policy states that no relative of, or person directly interested in, a candidate may invigilate an examination when that candidate is present.
questions.source_excerpt: No relative of, or person directly interested in, a candidate may invigilate an examination when this candidate is present.

questions.question: According to the Conflict of Interest Policy, how are the interests of individuals involved in delivering learning units declared and recorded?
options: Each individual submits an annual declaration form to HR, which records it on their personnel file
The Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring collects the declarations each term and records them on the Pearson portal
Individuals declare once a complaint has been raised, and the Quality Assurance team records it in the complaints log
The Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board ensures they are declared and recorded in the Board minutes
questions.explanation: The policy makes the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board responsible for ensuring that individuals involved in delivering learning units declare their interest, and this must be recorded in the Board minutes.
questions.source_excerpt: The Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board must ensure that all the individuals declare their interest if they are involved in the delivery of learning units. This must be recorded in the Board minutes.

questions.question: You sit on the admissions panel for a course and your nephew applies to join that course. How does the Conflict of Interest Policy treat this situation?
options: As a potential conflict of interest, because you are related to an applicant and responsible for admission decisions
As no conflict, provided your nephew meets the published entry requirements like any other applicant
As a conflict of commitment, because reviewing his application takes up time outside your normal teaching role
As not yet a conflict; one arises once your nephew has enrolled and you begin assessing or grading his work
questions.explanation: The policy lists, as a potential conflict of interest, a member of staff being related to an applicant to a College course while being responsible for admission decisions for that course.
questions.source_excerpt: Involvement in the provision of College: If a member of staff is related to an applicant to a course provided by the College and would be responsible for admission decisions for that course.

questions.question: The Conflict of Interest Policy specifically requires all employees and associates to declare any conflict of interest relating to which group?
options: Former students they taught at a previous institution
Potential funding partners of the College
Professional bodies they belong to as individual members
Other colleges where they have previously worked
questions.explanation: The policy states that all employees and associates of the College should declare any conflict of interest relating to potential funding partners.
questions.source_excerpt: All employees and associates of London Churchill College should declare any conflict of interest relating to potential funding partners.

questions.question: According to the Conflict of Interest Policy, what is meant by a 'conflict of commitment'?
options: Any paid employment held outside the College, whatever its hours and regardless of its effect on the person's College duties
Committing to teaching or marking deadlines at the College that the person later finds they are unable to meet
An outside engagement, paid or unpaid, needing a commitment of time that may conflict with the person's College role
An outside engagement that is treated as a conflict when it is paid, but not when it is unpaid or voluntary work
questions.explanation: The policy defines a conflict of commitment as an engagement or professional activity outside the College, whether paid or unpaid, that involves a commitment of time which may conflict with the individual's role and obligations to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: ...engagement outside the College/professional activity, whether it is paid or unpaid, would involve a commitment of time which may conflict with their role and obligations to the College.

questions.question: Under the Conflict of Interest Policy, by when must the College inform awarding bodies in order to manage conflicts of interest?
options: Within 10 working days after results are published
Before the published deadline for entries
At the end of each academic year
When a learner or the awarding body raises a concern
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College must manage conflicts of interest by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries, which can be done through the Pearson portal.
questions.source_excerpt: The College must manage conflict of interests by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries. This submission can be done through the Pearson portal.

questions.question: According to the aims of the Conflict of Interest Policy, what will all members of staff, associated persons and partner organisations need to ensure?
options: That they complete a declaration of interest form every term
That they obtain written approval before any outside work
That they attend conflict of interest training every year
That they are aware of the potential conflict of interest
questions.explanation: The policy's aims state that all staff, associated persons and partner organisations will need to ensure they are aware of the potential conflict of interest.
questions.source_excerpt: All members of staff, associated persons, and partner organisations will need to ensure that they are aware of the potential conflict of interest.

questions.question: According to its scope, the purpose of the Conflict of Interest Policy is to ensure the disclosure and management of which conflicts of interest?
options: Actual or potential conflicts of interest
Actual conflicts only, not potential ones
Only conflicts that have caused a complaint
Conflicts of students rather than of staff
questions.explanation: The policy's stated purpose is to ensure the disclosure and management of actual or potential conflicts of interest, not only those of a particular type or already complained about.
questions.source_excerpt: The purpose of this policy is to ensure the disclosure and management of actual or potential conflicts of interest to protect the integrity and dignity of the College and its members.

questions.question: According to its scope, the Conflict of Interest Policy applies to individuals involved in which aspects of the College offering qualifications, tests and assessments?
options: Assessment design and marking, as other activities are covered elsewhere
Any aspect, including creation, marketing, sales, distribution and marking
Marking and quality assurance, but not marketing, sales or distribution
Only activities carried out by academic staff who teach on the course
questions.explanation: The scope covers individuals involved with any aspect of the creation, marketing, sales, distribution, marking or any other activity connected with the College offering qualifications, tests and assessments.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy applies to individuals involved with any aspects of the creation, marketing, sales, distribution, marking or any other activity connected with the College offering qualifications, tests, and assessments, and supporting resources and services.

questions.question: According to its scope, the Conflict of Interest Policy applies to all LCC employees and which other group?
options: Former employees
Course applicants
Visiting academics
Learners' guardians
questions.explanation: The scope states that the policy applies to all LCC employees and visiting academics.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy applies to all LCC employees and visiting academics.

questions.question: What are staff covered by the Conflict of Interest Policy encouraged to do about any conflict between the College's interests and their personal, professional or business interests?
options: Keep a private note of it until their next annual appraisal
End the outside interest before taking on any College duties
Raise it only if a learner or colleague makes a complaint
Report it so that it can be appropriately managed
questions.explanation: The policy encourages those it applies to to report any conflict between the College's interests and their personal, professional and business interests so it can be appropriately managed.
questions.source_excerpt: it will be encouraged to report any conflict of interest between the interests of the College and personal, professional, and business interests to ensure they are being appropriately managed.

questions.question: The Conflict of Interest Policy lists examples of what a conflict of interest can include. How does the policy describe that list of examples?
options: Conflicts can include those examples but are not limited to them
It is the complete list of situations the College treats as conflicts
It applies to academic staff only, not to professional services staff
It must be confirmed by the awarding body before it can be applied
questions.explanation: The policy introduces its examples by saying that a conflict of interest can include the listed situations but is not limited to them.
questions.source_excerpt: For the purpose of this policy, conflict of interest can include the following but is not limited:

questions.question: According to the Conflict of Interest Policy, when can a conflict of interest occur?
options: When a staff member's performance targets differ from those set for the rest of their team
When duties staff owe the College compete with personal interest, relationships or other duties
When a staff member disagrees with a decision made by their line manager or a College board
When a staff member takes annual leave in a teaching or examination period without approval
questions.explanation: The policy defines a conflict of interest as occurring when duties owed to the College by staff compete with their personal interest, relationships or other duties to another person.
questions.source_excerpt: A conflict of interest can occur when duties owed to the College by members of staff compete with either their personal interest, relationships, or other duties to another person.

questions.question: The Conflict of Interest Policy lists a 'close personal relationship' as a potential conflict of interest. Which situation does that item describe?
options: A staff member forms a close relationship with another member of staff in their team
A staff member develops a close personal relationship with a visiting academic
A staff member develops a close personal relationship with a student whose work they grade
A student develops a close personal relationship with another student on the same course
questions.explanation: The policy describes this conflict as a member of staff developing a close personal relationship with a student whose work they are responsible for grading.
questions.source_excerpt: Close personal relationship: If a member of staff develops a close personal relationship with a student whom they have responsibility for grading work.

questions.question: Under the Conflict of Interest Policy, apart from a relative of the candidate, who may not invigilate an examination while that candidate is present?
options: A member of staff who joined the College that term
Any member of staff on a part-time or hourly contract
A member of staff based in another department
A person directly interested in that candidate
questions.explanation: The policy states that neither a relative of, nor a person directly interested in, a candidate may invigilate an examination when that candidate is present.
questions.source_excerpt: No relative of, or person directly interested in, a candidate may invigilate an examination when this candidate is present.

questions.question: Under the Conflict of Interest Policy, which activity requires the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring?
options: Procuring goods or services from a party in whose activity you have an interest
Taking on paid or unpaid work outside the College alongside your College role
Invigilating an examination sat by candidates you have taught in that subject
Declaring a conflict of interest that relates to a potential funding partner
questions.explanation: The policy states that no employee or associate should procure goods or services where they have an interest in the other party's activity without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring.
questions.source_excerpt: No employee or associate of London Churchill College should procure goods or services where he or she also has an interest in the activity of the other party without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring.

questions.question: The Conflict of Interest Policy says employees and associates should not share company sensitive information with external sources. What concern about such information does it give?
options: It could breach learners' rights under data protection law
It could be used by others to obtain a competitive advantage
It could delay the College's entries to its awarding bodies
It could be used to challenge assessment decisions on appeal
questions.explanation: The policy says company sensitive information should not be shared with external sources because it could be used by others to obtain a competitive advantage.
questions.source_excerpt: All employees and associates of London Churchill College should not share any company sensitive information to external sources that could be used by others to obtain a competitive advantage.

questions.question: According to the Conflict of Interest Policy, how can the College's submission informing awarding bodies about conflicts of interest be made?
options: Through the College's HR system
In the Assessment Board minutes
Through the Pearson portal
By letter from the Principal
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College informs awarding bodies of conflicts before the published deadline for entries, and that this submission can be done through the Pearson portal.
questions.source_excerpt: The College must manage conflict of interests by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries. This submission can be done through the Pearson portal.

questions.question: A lecturer agrees to volunteer, unpaid, as a charity trustee on several weekday afternoons that clash with their timetabled teaching. How does the Conflict of Interest Policy classify this?
options: As no conflict, because the policy covers only outside work for which the person is paid
As a conflict of commitment, since the unpaid role needs time that may clash with College duties
As a close personal relationship, since trustees work closely with the charity's own beneficiaries
As a procurement matter needing approval from the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring
questions.explanation: The policy defines a conflict of commitment as an outside engagement, whether paid or unpaid, involving a commitment of time that may conflict with the person's role and obligations to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Conflict of commitment: An individual's engagement outside the College/professional activity, whether it is paid or unpaid, would involve a commitment of time which may conflict with their role and obligations to the College.

questions.question: You taught several of the candidates who are sitting next week's Business Law examination. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say about your role in that examination?
options: You may be Lead invigilator if a colleague who did not teach them invigilates with you
You may act as sole invigilator provided the paper is set and marked externally
You must not act as the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator for that examination
You must not be Lead invigilator unless you have declared it to the Chair of the Board
questions.explanation: The policy states that no person who has taught any of the candidates in the examination subject may act as the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator, and it gives no exception for co-invigilators, external papers or declarations.
questions.source_excerpt: No person who has taught any of the candidates in the examination subject may act as the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator.

questions.question: A lecturer who delivers two of the learning units under review attends the Assessment and Progression Board. She has no relatives among the learners. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy require?
options: Nothing, as only staff with relatives among the learners need to declare an interest
The Chair must ensure she declares her interest, and it is recorded in the Board minutes
Nothing, as the Chair's own declaration covers everyone who attends the Board
She must declare it herself to the awarding body through the Pearson portal
questions.explanation: The Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board must ensure that all individuals involved in delivering learning units declare their interest, recorded in the Board minutes; this is not limited to those with relatives among the learners.
questions.source_excerpt: The Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board must ensure that all the individuals declare their interest if they are involved in the delivery of learning units. This must be recorded in the Board minutes.

questions.question: An associate engaged by London Churchill College, who is not an employee, wants to buy training materials for the College from a company in which they have an interest. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say?
options: The rule applies only to employees, so an associate needs no approval to go ahead
They need approval from the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring first
They may go ahead once the purchase has been recorded in the Board's minutes
They may go ahead once they have declared their interest to the awarding body
questions.explanation: The procurement rule covers employees and associates alike: neither should procure goods or services from a party in whose activity they have an interest without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring.
questions.source_excerpt: No employee or associate of London Churchill College should procure goods or services where he or she also has an interest in the activity of the other party without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring.

questions.question: Your sister is a director of an organisation the College is approaching as a potential funding partner. You are not involved in the talks. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy expect of you?
options: Nothing, as only staff who take part in the funding talks need to declare
To get Head of Programme approval before any funding is accepted
To declare the conflict of interest relating to that potential funding partner
To inform the awarding body via the Pearson portal before the entry deadline
questions.explanation: The policy says all employees and associates should declare any conflict of interest relating to potential funding partners; the duty is not limited to those involved in the negotiations.
questions.source_excerpt: All employees and associates of London Churchill College should declare any conflict of interest relating to potential funding partners.

questions.question: A former colleague now working at a competing college asks you for LCC's unpublished plans for next year's fees and recruitment. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say?
options: You may share them if your former colleague agrees in writing to keep them confidential
You should not share them unless the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring approves
You may share them once they have been noted in the Board minutes
You should not share them, as others could use them to gain a competitive advantage
questions.explanation: The policy says employees and associates should not share any company sensitive information with external sources that could be used by others to obtain a competitive advantage, and it gives no exception for confidentiality promises or approval.
questions.source_excerpt: All employees and associates of London Churchill College should not share any company sensitive information to external sources that could be used by others to obtain a competitive advantage.

questions.question: A member of the marketing team, who promotes and sells College courses but never teaches or marks, asks whether the Conflict of Interest Policy applies to their work. What is the answer?
options: Yes; it covers any aspect of the work, including marketing and sales
No; it covers only staff who assess, mark or quality assure learners' work
No; it covers only academic staff and visiting academics who teach courses
Only if they also sit on the Assessment and Progression Board as a member
questions.explanation: The scope covers individuals involved with any aspect of the creation, marketing, sales, distribution, marking or other activity connected with the College offering qualifications, and it applies to all LCC employees.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy applies to individuals involved with any aspects of the creation, marketing, sales, distribution, marking or any other activity connected with the College offering qualifications, tests, and assessments ... This policy applies to all LCC employees and visiting academics.

questions.question: You face a possible conflict of interest that is not one of the examples listed in the Conflict of Interest Policy and are unsure how the policy applies. What approach does the policy's scope support?
options: Treat it as outside the policy, since only the listed examples count as conflicts
Treat it as a conflict of commitment until the awarding body decides otherwise
Seek advice if necessary, using the policy's references to conflicts as guidance
Wait for the next Board meeting, where the Chair decides whether it counts
questions.explanation: The scope recognises that conflicts can arise in a wide range of situations, says members must seek advice if necessary, and states that the policy's references to conflicts should be used as guidance.
questions.source_excerpt: There are a wide range of situations in which conflicts of interest may arise and members of the College must seek advice, if necessary. Where applicable, references to conflicts of interest in this policy should be used as guidance.

questions.question: You are asked to shortlist applicants for a job at the College, and a close friend of yours has applied. Which potential conflict listed in the Conflict of Interest Policy best describes this?
options: Conflict of commitment, as shortlisting takes time away from your usual College duties
Close personal relationship, which covers friendships with anyone you assess or select
Conflict of interest, as your duty to the College competes with a personal relationship
Involvement in the provision of College, which covers friends applying for College jobs
questions.explanation: A conflict of interest occurs when duties owed to the College compete with personal interest or relationships; the 'close personal relationship' and 'involvement in the provision of College' items cover students being graded and relatives applying to courses.
questions.source_excerpt: A conflict of interest can occur when duties owed to the College by members of staff compete with either their personal interest, relationships, or other duties to another person.

questions.question: Alongside your College role you run a private tutoring business that competes to recruit the same learners as the College. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy encourage you to do?
options: Report the conflict between the College's interests and your business interests
Nothing, provided the business operates only outside your College working hours
Close the business, since the policy bars staff from holding business interests
Ask the awarding body to approve the business through the Pearson portal
questions.explanation: The policy encourages those it applies to to report any conflict between the College's interests and their personal, professional and business interests so that it can be appropriately managed.
questions.source_excerpt: it will be encouraged to report any conflict of interest between the interests of the College and personal, professional, and business interests to ensure they are being appropriately managed.

questions.question: You are the internal quality assurer for a unit. An unrelated colleague assessed the work, but one learner in your sample is your daughter. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say?
options: You may quality assure her work, because the assessor is not related to her
You may quality assure it once the relationship is noted in the Board minutes
You should not quality assure it unless an external examiner also samples her work
You should not internally quality assure your daughter's assessments
questions.explanation: The policy states that internal quality assurance for a learner's assessments will not be undertaken by a family member, even where the assessor is unrelated.
questions.source_excerpt: Also, internal quality assurance for assessments for the said learner will not be undertaken by a family member.

questions.question: Your brother is an assessor at London Churchill College and you are an internal quality assurer there. You are asked to sample and check his assessment decisions. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say?
options: You must not internally quality assure your brother's assessment decisions
You must not do so unless a second, unrelated quality assurer also signs them off
You may do so as long as you do not invigilate exams that his learners sit
You may do so, as the policy only stops family members assessing each other
questions.explanation: The policy states that family members working for the College will not be allowed to assess and/or internally quality assure one another.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of any family members working for London Churchill College ... they will not be allowed to assess and/or internally quality assure one another

questions.question: A partner organisation working with London Churchill College assumes that being aware of potential conflicts of interest is a matter only for College employees. According to the policy's aims, is this right?
options: Yes; partner organisations follow their own policies rather than the College's
No; staff, associated persons and partner organisations must all ensure awareness
Yes, unless the partner organisation is also a potential funding partner
No, but only partner organisations that deliver assessments are included
questions.explanation: The policy's aims state that all members of staff, associated persons and partner organisations will need to ensure they are aware of the potential conflict of interest.
questions.source_excerpt: All members of staff, associated persons, and partner organisations will need to ensure that they are aware of the potential conflict of interest.

questions.question: A visiting academic at London Churchill College is asked to assess a unit's assignments, and one of the learners is her niece. She says the rules on relatives bind only permanent LCC staff. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say?
options: She must not assess her niece's work, as the policy applies to visiting academics too
She may assess it, provided an unrelated colleague internally quality assures her niece's work
She is right; visiting academics are covered only by the rules on company sensitive information
She may assess it, provided the relationship is first recorded in the Assessment Board minutes
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all LCC employees and visiting academics, and a learner will not be assessed by a family member.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy applies to all LCC employees and visiting academics. ... A learner undertaking a qualification with London Churchill College will not be assessed by a family member.

questions.question: A member of LCC's finance team, who plays no part in admissions, learns that his niece has applied for an LCC course. Does this match the Conflict of Interest Policy's listed example of 'involvement in the provision of College'?
options: Yes; that example covers any member of staff who is related to an applicant to a College course
Yes, but only once she enrols, as the example covers relatives studying at the College
No; that example covers only staff who will teach or assess the applicant after enrolment
No; that example applies where the staff member is responsible for admission decisions for the course
questions.explanation: The policy's example requires a staff member to be related to an applicant and to be responsible for admission decisions for that course; without that responsibility the example does not apply.
questions.source_excerpt: Involvement in the provision of College: If a member of staff is related to an applicant to a course provided by the College and would be responsible for admission decisions for that course.

questions.question: A lecturer realises she has developed a close personal relationship with a student whose assignments she grades. Which response is consistent with the Conflict of Interest Policy?
options: End the relationship at once, as the policy prohibits all personal relationships between staff and students
Report it so it can be managed, as the policy lists it as a potential conflict of interest
Take no action, as the policy's examples cover relationships with applicants but not current students
Report it only if the student later complains or appeals about a grade she has given them
questions.explanation: The policy lists a close personal relationship with a student whose work the staff member grades as a potential conflict and encourages staff to report conflicts so they can be appropriately managed; it neither bans such relationships nor waits for a complaint.
questions.source_excerpt: it will be encouraged to report any conflict of interest between the interests of the College and personal, professional, and business interests to ensure they are being appropriately managed. ... Close personal relationship: If a member of staff develops a close personal relationship with a student whom they have responsibility for grading work.

questions.question: You make admission decisions for a course. Your niece applied, was admitted and has now joined the group whose work you mark. How does the Conflict of Interest Policy apply across these two stages?
options: Only the application stage raised a conflict; now she has enrolled, you may assess her as normal
Neither stage raised a conflict, provided she met the course's published entry requirements
Her application was a listed potential conflict, and now that she has enrolled you must not assess her
Her application raised a conflict of commitment; now you may assess her if a colleague quality assures it
questions.explanation: The policy lists being related to an applicant while responsible for admission decisions as a potential conflict, and once the relative is a learner they will not be assessed by a family member.
questions.source_excerpt: If a member of staff is related to an applicant to a course provided by the College and would be responsible for admission decisions for that course. ... A learner undertaking a qualification with London Churchill College will not be assessed by a family member.

questions.question: Your husband works in LCC's finance team and is sitting an examination for an LCC qualification. You are rostered as an additional invigilator under an unrelated Lead invigilator, and you have never taught him. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say?
options: You must not invigilate any examination that he sits, whatever your invigilation role
You may, as the rules bar a colleague's family member only from the sole or Lead role
You may, as the family rules protect learners and do not apply when staff sit examinations
You may, provided the relationship is recorded in the Assessment Board minutes beforehand
questions.explanation: Family members working for the College must not act as an invigilator for any examinations the other may sit; the sole or Senior/Lead restriction is a separate rule about people who taught the candidates.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of any family members working for London Churchill College they will not be allowed to assess and/or internally quality assure one another, nor act as an invigilator for any examinations they may sit.

questions.question: Your nephew has joined a cohort you lead. Which arrangement for his assessment, internal quality assurance and examinations meets the Conflict of Interest Policy?
options: An unrelated colleague assesses his work, you internally quality assure it, and you do not invigilate his exams
You assess his work, an unrelated colleague quality assures it, and you do not invigilate his exams
Unrelated colleagues assess and quality assure his work, and you invigilate his exams only as a non-Lead
Unrelated colleagues assess and quality assure his work, and you do not invigilate while he sits an exam
questions.explanation: A learner must not be assessed or internally quality assured by a family member, and no relative of a candidate may invigilate an examination while that candidate is present, whatever the invigilation role.
questions.source_excerpt: A learner undertaking a qualification with London Churchill College will not be assessed by a family member. Also, internal quality assurance for assessments for the said learner will not be undertaken by a family member. ... No relative of, or person directly interested in, a candidate may invigilate an examination when this candidate is present.

questions.question: An exams officer is rostering two invigilators for an exam. Amir taught several of the candidates in that subject; Beth has no link to any candidate. Which rostering meets the Conflict of Interest Policy?
options: Amir as Lead invigilator, with Beth assisting him
Amir as sole invigilator, with Beth kept on standby
Beth as Lead invigilator, with Amir assisting her
Amir as Lead, once his link is noted in the Board minutes
questions.explanation: A person who has taught any of the candidates in the examination subject may not act as the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator; the policy does not bar them from assisting an unconnected Lead invigilator.
questions.source_excerpt: No person who has taught any of the candidates in the examination subject may act as the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator.

questions.question: Carla taught a cohort Business English but has never taught any of them Accounting, and has no other link to them. Under the Conflict of Interest Policy, may she be the Lead invigilator for their Accounting exam?
options: No; the bar covers anyone who has taught any of the candidates in any subject
Yes; the bar covers only people who taught candidates in the examination subject
No, unless her English teaching ended at least one academic year before the exam
Yes, but only if an Accounting tutor assists her throughout the examination
questions.explanation: The policy bars from the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator role a person who has taught any of the candidates in the examination subject; teaching them a different subject does not trigger it.
questions.source_excerpt: No person who has taught any of the candidates in the examination subject may act as the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator.

questions.question: Dev taught just one of the 30 candidates in the examination subject, two years ago. The exams officer asks him to be the sole invigilator for that exam. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy say?
options: He may, as he taught fewer than half of the candidates sitting the examination
He may, as his teaching of that candidate was not in the current academic year
He may, provided he declares the link to the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board
He must not, as he has taught one of the candidates in the examination subject
questions.explanation: The rule covers any person who has taught any of the candidates in the examination subject, with no minimum number of candidates or time limit, and it gives no exception for a declaration.
questions.source_excerpt: No person who has taught any of the candidates in the examination subject may act as the sole or Senior/Lead invigilator.

questions.question: You are arranging for the College to buy catering services from a firm in which you hold a stake. The Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring has approved the purchase. Does the Conflict of Interest Policy still prevent it?
options: No; the rule bars such procurement only when that approval has not been given
Yes; staff may never procure from a party in whose activity they have an interest
Yes, until the awarding body has also been informed through the Pearson portal
Yes, until the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board agrees in the minutes
questions.explanation: The policy says no employee or associate should procure goods or services from a party whose activity they have an interest in without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring; once that approval is given, the rule is met.
questions.source_excerpt: No employee or associate of London Churchill College should procure goods or services where he or she also has an interest in the activity of the other party without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring.

questions.question: You are a director of a consultancy firm but hold no shares in it. You want to commission the firm to run staff training for the College. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy require before you do so?
options: Nothing, as the procurement rule covers goods but not services such as training
Nothing, as holding no shares means you have no interest in the firm's activity
The approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring to procure its services
A declaration of your role, recorded in the minutes by the Chair of the Board
questions.explanation: The procurement rule covers goods or services and applies wherever the person has an interest in the other party's activity, as a director does; it requires the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring.
questions.source_excerpt: No employee or associate of London Churchill College should procure goods or services where he or she also has an interest in the activity of the other party without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring.

questions.question: You are arranging the College's purchase of IT equipment. A company you part-own is bidding for the order and is also in talks to become a College funding partner. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy require of you?
options: Declare the funding-partner conflict; that declaration also serves as approval to buy from the company
Only get Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring approval to buy, as the company is not yet a funding partner
Declare the funding-partner conflict and get Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring approval to buy
Have both recorded in the Board minutes, then inform the awarding body before the entry deadline
questions.explanation: The policy separately requires a declaration of any conflict relating to potential funding partners and bars procuring from a party you have an interest in without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring; neither step replaces the other.
questions.source_excerpt: No employee or associate of London Churchill College should procure goods or services where he or she also has an interest in the activity of the other party without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring. ... All employees and associates of London Churchill College should declare any conflict of interest relating to potential funding partners.

questions.question: The College is in early talks with a rival training provider about it becoming a funding partner. The provider's owner, your brother, asks you for LCC's unpublished recruitment figures. What should you do under the Conflict of Interest Policy?
options: Declare the conflict; once it is on record, you may share the figures with him
Share the figures once the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring approves
Share them, as a potential funding partner is not treated as an external source
Declare the funding-partner conflict and do not share the figures with him
questions.explanation: Employees should declare any conflict relating to potential funding partners and should not share company sensitive information with external sources that could use it to obtain a competitive advantage, as a rival provider could.
questions.source_excerpt: All employees and associates of London Churchill College should declare any conflict of interest relating to potential funding partners. ... All employees and associates of London Churchill College should not share any company sensitive information to external sources that could be used by others to obtain a competitive advantage.

questions.question: A lecturer accepts a paid weekend consultancy role that she expects will soon need weekday meetings during her teaching hours. She plans to say nothing until a clash actually happens. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy support?
options: Reporting it now, as a commitment of time that may conflict with her role is a conflict of commitment
Saying nothing until a clash occurs, as the policy covers actual conflicts rather than potential ones
Saying nothing, as paid work at weekends falls outside the scope of the policy altogether
Getting Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring approval before she accepts the role
questions.explanation: The policy covers actual or potential conflicts, defines a conflict of commitment as an outside engagement needing time that may conflict with College obligations, and encourages staff to report conflicts so they can be managed.
questions.source_excerpt: The purpose of this policy is to ensure the disclosure and management of actual or potential conflicts of interest ... Conflict of commitment: An individual's engagement outside the College/professional activity, whether it is paid or unpaid, would involve a commitment of time which may conflict with their role and obligations to the College.

questions.question: A conflict of interest affecting candidates for a Pearson qualification is identified in January. The published entry deadline is in March, and the Assessment and Progression Board next meets in April. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy require of the College?
options: Inform the awarding body before the March entry deadline, without waiting for the April Board
Record it at the April Board first, and then inform the awarding body through the Pearson portal
Wait for the April Board, as only interests recorded in its minutes may be sent to the awarding body
Inform the awarding body once results are published, so the conflict can be reviewed alongside them
questions.explanation: The College must manage conflicts of interest by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries; the policy does not make this wait for a Board meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: The College must manage conflict of interests by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries. This submission can be done through the Pearson portal.

questions.question: The Chair has ensured that everyone delivering a Pearson unit declared their interests, and these are recorded in the Board minutes. A colleague says the College has now met all the Conflict of Interest Policy's requirements for managing those conflicts. Is that right?
options: Yes; recording the declarations in the Board minutes completes the College's duties
No; the College must also inform the awarding bodies before the published entry deadline
No; each declaration must also be approved by the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring
Yes, unless a learner or the awarding body later raises a concern about one of the conflicts
questions.explanation: Besides the Chair ensuring declarations are recorded in the Board minutes, the College must manage conflicts of interest by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries.
questions.source_excerpt: The Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board must ensure that all the individuals declare their interest if they are involved in the delivery of learning units. This must be recorded in the Board minutes. ... The College must manage conflict of interests by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries.

questions.question: A supplier you part-own offers the College a discount if it orders by Friday. You place the order straight away and plan to ask the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring for approval next week. Does this follow the Conflict of Interest Policy?
options: Yes, provided you seek that approval within 30 days of placing the order
No; staff may never buy from a supplier they part-own, even with that approval
Yes, as a time-limited discount justifies seeking the approval after ordering
No; you should not procure from a supplier you part-own without that approval
questions.explanation: The policy bars employees and associates from procuring goods or services from a party whose activity they have an interest in without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring; it gives no grace period or urgency exception, though with that approval the purchase is allowed.
questions.source_excerpt: No employee or associate of London Churchill College should procure goods or services where he or she also has an interest in the activity of the other party without the approval of the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring.

questions.question: Your sister has enrolled on a specialist unit at London Churchill College, and you are the only qualified assessor for it. The College plans to tell the awarding body about the relationship before the entry deadline. Under the Conflict of Interest Policy, may you assess her work?
options: Yes, as informing the awarding body before the entry deadline manages the conflict
No; she will not be assessed by a family member, even if no other assessor is qualified
Yes, provided an unrelated colleague internally quality assures all of her work
No, unless the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board records it in the minutes first
questions.explanation: The policy states that a learner will not be assessed by a family member and gives no exception for staff shortages; informing the awarding body, recording it in Board minutes or using unrelated quality assurance does not replace that rule.
questions.source_excerpt: A learner undertaking a qualification with London Churchill College will not be assessed by a family member.

questions.question: A declared conflict of interest affects candidates entered for a qualification from an awarding body other than Pearson, so the Pearson portal cannot be used. What does the Conflict of Interest Policy require of the College?
options: Nothing further, as the submission duty covers only Pearson qualifications
It must still inform that awarding body before the published deadline for entries
It must record the conflict in the Board minutes instead of informing the awarding body
It must inform that awarding body within 10 working days of results being published
questions.explanation: The policy says the College must manage conflicts of interest by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries; the Pearson portal is a route the submission can use, not a limit on which awarding bodies must be told.
questions.source_excerpt: The College must manage conflict of interests by informing the awarding bodies before the published deadline for entries. This submission can be done through the Pearson portal.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what applies to speakers from organisations proscribed by the UK government?
options: They must not, in any circumstances, be involved in or supported through college events and meetings
They may speak on-site only if the Prevent lead approves a mitigating action at least one week in advance
They may speak at off-site events organised by students, but must not speak on college premises
They may speak if the core questions raise no flags and the topic has been formally risk-assessed
questions.explanation: The policy states that events and meetings must not, in any circumstances, involve speakers or support of speakers from proscribed organisations listed by the UK government.
questions.source_excerpt: Any activity relating to events and meetings must not, in any circumstances, involve speakers or support of speakers from proscribed organisations listed by the UK government.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, how far in advance must organisers conclude their consideration of the core questions for a speaker or event?
options: At least one week before the proposed event
At least four weeks before the proposed event
At least two weeks before the proposed event
At least 48 hours before the proposed event
questions.explanation: The policy requires the core question considerations to be concluded at least two weeks prior to the proposed event or speaker activity.
questions.source_excerpt: The core questions must be addressed by organisers of each speaker and event activity involving the college. These considerations must be concluded at least two weeks prior to the proposed event / speaker activity.

questions.question: You are organising a seminar with an external speaker and, while working through the core questions, you have doubts about the speaker's suitability. What should you do under the External Speakers and Events Policy?
options: Report the speaker directly to the police before taking any other step
Refer the decision to the Head of Student Engagement, who approves all external speakers
Ask the students attending to vote on whether the speaker should appear
Make an informed assessment as organiser and seek the advice of the Prevent lead
questions.explanation: The policy places responsibility on the event organiser to make an informed assessment and to seek the advice of the Prevent lead if they have any doubts or concerns.
questions.source_excerpt: Responsibility is placed clearly on the organiser of the event to make informed assessment and seek advice of the prevent lead should they have any doubts or concerns.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what must an external speaker sign?
options: An external speaker indemnity form accepting liability for any damage to college property during the event
A consent form allowing the college to carry out a criminal records (DBS) check
The external speaker statement form, agreeing to abide by college policies and free speech statements
A declaration confirming that their talk will contain no controversial, objectionable or offensive content
questions.explanation: The policy requires the external speaker to sign the external speaker statement form (Appendix 1), confirming they will abide by college policies and the statements on academic freedom and freedom of speech.
questions.source_excerpt: The external speaker must sign the external speaker statement form (appendix 1), confirming that they will abide by college policies and the statements on academic freedom and freedom of speech.

questions.question: You are organising an external speaker event on 20 May and have completed the core questions. Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, what is the latest date by which the outcome of the Prevent lead's review should be communicated to you?
options: 13 May, one week before the event date
6 May, two weeks before the event date
17 May, three days before the event date
19 May, the day before the event date
questions.explanation: The policy states that the outcome of the Prevent lead's review will be communicated to the event organiser at least one week before the proposed event date, so no later than 13 May for a 20 May event.
questions.source_excerpt: The outcome of this review will be communicated to the event organiser at least one week prior to the proposed event date.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what happens when the Prevent lead's review of an external speaker event identifies a possible risk posed by the speaker?
options: The event is cancelled automatically and the speaker is barred from the college
A mitigating action is identified and applied to reduce the level of risk
The speaker is automatically referred to the police in every such case
The event must be postponed until the following academic term for re-approval
questions.explanation: Under the review procedure, the Prevent lead considers a review to lessen possible risks, and a mitigating action is identified and applied to reduce the level of risk.
questions.source_excerpt: For any external speaker event the prevent lead will consider a review to lessen possible risks (if any) posed by an external speaker. A mitigating action will be identified and applied to reduce the level of risk.

questions.question: A lecturer invites an industry practitioner to deliver a routine teaching session within a unit, and the core questions raise no flags. What level of approval does the External Speakers and Events Policy expect?
options: No general expectation of the most senior level of approval; escalation only if flags are raised
Formal approval by the college oversight board at least two weeks before the session takes place
Written sign-off from the Principal and the Prevent lead at least four weeks before the session
None at all, because speakers in routine teaching are fully exempt from the policy and core questions
questions.explanation: The policy says speakers involved in routine teaching, learning and research are not generally expected to need the most senior level of approval, and matters are escalated to senior level only if flags are raised through the core questions.
questions.source_excerpt: The college considers that there would not be a general expectation that speakers involved with the college in routine teaching, learning, and research require the most senior level of approval at the college. ... Engagement is considered through a series of core questions and only escalated to senior level of consideration if flags are raised.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the core questions that organisers must address under the External Speakers and Events Policy?
options: Has the speaker previously spoken at events held by London Churchill College or any of its partner institutions?
Will the speaker charge a fee or claim travel and accommodation expenses from the college for the event?
Has the speaker been refused permission to speak publicly at other educational establishments or organisations?
Has the speaker published peer-reviewed research or academic papers on the event topic within the last five years?
questions.explanation: One of the listed core questions asks whether the speaker has been refused permission to speak publicly at other educational establishments or organisations, including a student body or union at another HEI.
questions.source_excerpt: Has the speaker been refused permission to speak publicly at other educational establishments or organisations (including the student body / union at another HEI)?

questions.question: After a guest lecture, a student tells you the external speaker expressed views they found offensive, although the speaker did not incite hatred or violence. Which statement reflects the External Speakers and Events Policy?
options: The speaker breached the policy, because any view that causes offence to a student is prohibited at college events
Freedom of speech gives no broad right not to be offended, and such views are not generally unlawful
The organiser must immediately report the speaker to the police as a breach of the college's Prevent duty
The lecture topic must be removed from the curriculum, because it caused offence to members of the college
questions.explanation: The policy's principles state that academic freedom and freedom of speech do not establish a broad right not to be offended, and that expressing views some find objectionable or offensive is not generally unlawful.
questions.source_excerpt: Exercising academic freedom and freedom of speech does not establish a broad right not to be offended. ... It is not generally unlawful to express views or undertake research or teaching that some might find objectionable or offensive.

questions.question: Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, who maintains the records of speaker and event activity on the college's behalf?
options: The college's Prevent lead
The Head of Human Resources
The Head of Quality Assurance and Standards
The Head of Student Engagement
questions.explanation: The organiser must keep records of the decision-making processes and outcomes, and the Head of Student Engagement maintains these records on the college's behalf.
questions.source_excerpt: The organiser must maintain records regarding the speaker and event activity, recording the processes followed in decision-making and outcomes. The Head of Student Engagement will maintain these records on the college's behalf.

questions.question: A student society tells you it plans to host an off-site event with an external speaker. Which statement reflects the External Speakers and Events Policy?
options: Student-led events fall outside the policy, which covers only staff-organised teaching and corporate activity
The policy applies only to events held on college premises, so an off-site society event is excluded from review
Only members of staff may organise events involving external speakers, so the society's event must be cancelled
The student body is a recognised organiser expected to help maintain Prevent and other policies, on or off-site
questions.explanation: The policy recognises the student body as a potential organiser of events and speakers and expects it to play an active and positive role in maintaining Prevent and other policies, whether on or off-site.
questions.source_excerpt: The college's student body is recognised as a potential organiser of events and speakers. It is expected to play an active and positive role in ensuring and maintaining the college prevent and other policies whether on or off-site.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, how does the college regard undertaking research on controversial topics?
options: As permitted only with prior written approval from the Prevent lead for each project
As an expected part of generating new knowledge and academic development
As prohibited wherever it involves the use of college systems
As permitted only when carried out off-site and entirely outside college systems
questions.explanation: The policy confirms that research on controversial topics is an expected part of generating new knowledge and academic development, including using college systems for bona fide teaching and research purposes.
questions.source_excerpt: The college confirms that undertaking research on controversial topics is an expected part of generating new knowledge and academic development. This would include using college systems and allowing access for bona fide teaching and research purposes.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what kind of approach does the college take to external speakers and events?
options: A zero-tolerance approach, requiring board-level approval for every external speaker
A proportionate and risk-based approach, as advised in the Prevent duty guidance
A self-certification approach, relying solely on each speaker's declaration
A centralised approach, in which senior managers personally vet every event booking
questions.explanation: The policy states that its approach is based on taking a proportionate and risk-based approach, as advised in the Prevent duty guidance.
questions.source_excerpt: The approach is based on taking a proportionate and risk-based approach, as advised in the prevent duty guidance.

questions.question: The External Speakers and Events Policy addresses whether its procedures target any particular faith or belief. What does it state?
options: They apply chiefly to speakers from religious groups, who are subject to extra checks
They apply only to speakers who represent political or campaigning organisations
They focus on groups the Prevent duty guidance identifies as being of particular concern
They are not directed at any specific religion, religious group or other set of beliefs
questions.explanation: The policy states that it and its procedures are not directed at any specific religion, religious group or the proponents of any other set of beliefs.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy and set of procedures are not directed at any specific religion, religious group or at the proponents of any other set of beliefs.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what does taking a proportionate approach to events and speakers involve?
options: Reviewing, assessing and authorising events and speakers, both off-site and on-site
Reviewing and authorising on-site events only, as off-site events fall outside its scope
Authorising only events expected to attract more than fifty external attendees
Assessing speakers only once a complaint has been received about their planned event
questions.explanation: The policy explains that a proportionate approach involves reviewing, assessing and authorising events and speakers both off-site and on-site.
questions.source_excerpt: Taking a proportionate approach involves reviewing, assessing, and authorising events and speakers off and on-site.

questions.question: Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, what responsibility does the college have regarding individuals or groups who incite hatred or violence against others?
options: To offer them a right of reply at a moderated debate held on college premises
To allow them to speak on-site provided that the event is closed to the public
To ensure that such individuals or groups are not supported or promoted
To permit them to speak only if the Prevent lead attends the whole event
questions.explanation: The policy states that the college has a responsibility to ensure that individuals or groups who incite hatred or violence are not supported or promoted.
questions.source_excerpt: The college has a responsibility to ensure that individuals or groups who incite hatred or violence against any individuals or groups, or seek to undermine a society's, a group's or an individual's fundamental democratic rights and freedoms, are not supported or promoted.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what kind of teaching and curricula does the college encourage?
options: Teaching that avoids potentially controversial topics so that no student is offended
Teaching that challenges norms and conventional wisdom, including on controversial topics
Teaching confined to topics that the Prevent lead has pre-approved for each academic year
Teaching that presents established consensus views only, leaving debate to societies
questions.explanation: The policy encourages teaching and curricula that challenge norms, conventional wisdom and viewpoints, involving learning and assessment on potentially controversial topics.
questions.source_excerpt: The college encourages development and teaching by academic staff and curricula which extends the academy, challenging norms and conventional wisdom and viewpoints, involving learning and assessment on potentially controversial topics.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what are speakers and events expected to meet?
options: Core college values and the expected standards of those speaking
The accreditation standards of the college's awarding university partners
The student satisfaction targets set out in the college's annual plan
The commercial sponsorship criteria set by the college's finance team
questions.explanation: The policy states that speakers and events are expected to meet core college values and the expected standards of those speaking.
questions.source_excerpt: The speakers and events are expected to meet core college values and expected standards of those speaking.

questions.question: Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, who is required to address the core questions before a speaker or event goes ahead?
options: The Prevent lead, acting on behalf of the college
The Head of Student Engagement, on request
The organiser of that speaker or event activity
PEG, as part of its monitoring of these activities
questions.explanation: The policy requires the core questions to be addressed by the organisers of each speaker and event activity involving the college.
questions.source_excerpt: The core questions must be addressed by organisers of each speaker and event activity involving the college.

questions.question: One of the core questions in the External Speakers and Events Policy asks whether a situation is likely to arise in which people might experience what?
options: Financial loss, reputational harm or negative press coverage linked to the college
Harassment, intimidation, verbal abuse or violence, or damage to person or property
Discomfort or offence at hearing views that challenge their own personal beliefs
Travel disruption, overcrowding or delays in gaining entry to college premises
questions.explanation: One core question asks whether there is a likelihood of a situation in which people might experience harassment, intimidation, verbal abuse or violence, or damage to person or property.
questions.source_excerpt: Is there a likelihood of a situation arising in which people might experience harassment, intimidation, verbal abuse or violence, damage to person or property?

questions.question: Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, who considers a review to lessen any possible risks posed by an external speaker at an event?
options: The organiser of the event
The Head of Student Engagement
The college oversight board
The college's Prevent lead
questions.explanation: The review procedure states that, for any external speaker event, the Prevent lead will consider a review to lessen possible risks posed by an external speaker.
questions.source_excerpt: For any external speaker event the prevent lead will consider a review to lessen possible risks (if any) posed by an external speaker.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, to whom does PEG report the outcomes of its monitoring of external speaker and event activities?
options: The college oversight board, as appropriate
The academic board, at each termly meeting
The Head of Student Engagement, each month
The elected student body representatives
questions.explanation: The policy states that PEG will monitor these activities and report outcomes to the college oversight board as appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: PEG will monitor these activities and report outcomes to the college oversight board as appropriate.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what is the purpose of the post-event process held after a speaker or event?
options: To collect attendee feedback scores for the speaker's formal performance review
To publish a public summary of each event and its outcomes on the college website
To help formulate responses and inform future planning, booking and any sanctions
To calculate final event costs and recover any speaker fees paid in advance
questions.explanation: The post-event process helps formulate responses and assists the college in determining how future events are planned, the booking process and any sanctions to be imposed.
questions.source_excerpt: A post-event process will be held to help formulate the responses and assist the college in determining how the future events are planned, the booking process, and or the type of sanctions which might be imposed post event.

questions.question: On information sharing, the External Speakers and Events Policy states that the Prevent lead must meet the Prevent statutory duty in which situation?
options: Where a speaker has refused to sign the external speaker statement form
Where referrals have been made to partners or authorities beyond the college
Where an event is open to members of the public from outside the college
Where an event organiser has submitted a formal written complaint
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Prevent lead must meet the Prevent statutory duty where referrals have been made to partners and/or authorities beyond the college.
questions.source_excerpt: The Prevent lead must meet the prevent statutory duty where referrals have been made to partners and or to authorities beyond the college.

questions.question: According to the External Speakers and Events Policy, what are student representatives provided with as part of their training?
options: Delegated authority to approve external speakers for society events
Accreditation as deputy Prevent leads for all student-led events
Access to the Head of Student Engagement's records of past events
Guidance and advice on policies concerning student welfare
questions.explanation: The policy states that student representatives are provided with guidance and advice on policies concerning student welfare as part of their training.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are provided with guidance and advice on policies concerning student welfare as part of their training.

questions.question: You are organising a college seminar with an external speaker on 24 June. Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, what is the latest date by which your consideration of the core questions must be concluded?
options: 17 June, one week before the seminar
10 June, two weeks before the seminar
27 May, four weeks before the seminar
21 June, three days before the seminar
questions.explanation: The core question considerations must be concluded at least two weeks before the proposed event, so no later than 10 June for a 24 June seminar.
questions.source_excerpt: The core questions must be addressed by organisers of each speaker and event activity involving the college. These considerations must be concluded at least two weeks prior to the proposed event / speaker activity.

questions.question: Based on the deadlines in the External Speakers and Events Policy, which sequence correctly reflects the stages for an external speaker event?
options: Prevent lead's review outcome communicated; event held; organiser concludes core questions; post-event process
Organiser concludes core questions; event held; Prevent lead reviews the risks; post-event process
Organiser concludes core questions; Prevent lead's review outcome communicated; event held; post-event process
PEG approves the event; organiser concludes core questions; event held; Prevent lead's review outcome communicated
questions.explanation: Organisers must conclude the core questions at least two weeks before the event, the Prevent lead's review outcome is communicated at least one week before it, and a post-event process follows the event.
questions.source_excerpt: These considerations must be concluded at least two weeks prior to the proposed event / speaker activity. ... The outcome of this review will be communicated to the event organiser at least one week prior to the proposed event date. ... A post-event process will be held to help formulate the responses

questions.question: You are organising a public seminar with an external speaker. Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, what are you as the organiser required to keep records of?
options: The processes followed in decision-making and the outcomes for the speaker and event activity
Nothing, as these records are kept solely by the Head of Student Engagement for the college
Only the outcome of the Prevent lead's review, not your own decision-making as organiser
Only events where the core questions raised flags; routine events need no record kept
questions.explanation: The organiser must maintain records of the speaker and event activity, recording the processes followed in decision-making and the outcomes; the Head of Student Engagement then maintains these on the college's behalf.
questions.source_excerpt: The organiser must maintain records regarding the speaker and event activity, recording the processes followed in decision-making and outcomes. The Head of Student Engagement will maintain these records on the college's behalf.

questions.question: A society proposes a college event to raise support for a speaker from an organisation proscribed by the UK government; the speaker would not attend. What does the External Speakers and Events Policy say?
options: It may go ahead, because the policy only bars proscribed speakers from attending in person
It may go ahead if it is held off-site, so that no college premises are used for the event
It may go ahead if the Prevent lead's review identifies and applies a suitable mitigating action
It must not go ahead, as events must not involve support of speakers from proscribed groups
questions.explanation: The policy bars any event or meeting activity from involving speakers, or support of speakers, from proscribed organisations in any circumstances, so the speaker's absence makes no difference.
questions.source_excerpt: Any activity relating to events and meetings must not, in any circumstances, involve speakers or support of speakers from proscribed organisations listed by the UK government.

questions.question: A panel event has three external speakers, but only the lead panellist has signed the external speaker statement form. Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, what should happen?
options: Nothing more, as the lead panellist's signature covers the whole panel
Each external speaker must sign the statement form, not just the lead
The organiser may sign the form on behalf of all of the remaining panellists
The other panellists need only confirm their agreement verbally on the day
questions.explanation: The core questions consider whether each speaker can abide by college policies, and the external speaker must sign the statement form confirming this, so every external panellist must sign.
questions.source_excerpt: Do we know or think that each speaker would not be able to confirm that he/she would be able to abide by all relevant college policies ... The external speaker must sign the external speaker statement form (appendix 1), confirming that they will abide by college policies

questions.question: An external organisation books a college room to run its own conference with its own speakers. How does the External Speakers and Events Policy treat this?
options: It is outside the policy, because the college is not the organiser of the event
It is within scope only if college staff or students are among the speakers
It is covered, as externally booked and led conferences are college-connected events
It is outside the policy unless the conference is advertised to the general public
questions.explanation: The policy lists externally booked and led conferences and events among the ways events take place in connection with the college, so such a conference is within its scope.
questions.source_excerpt: The different ways that events take place in connection with the college are identified as: ... Externally booked and led conferences and events.

questions.question: An outside organisation asks to co-run an event with the college. Under the External Speakers and Events Policy, which of these must you establish as part of the core questions?
options: Whether it is run by an external or college-aligned body, and if all involved and speakers are clear
Whether the organisation has been approved in advance by PEG as an official partner of the college
Whether the organisation has signed the external speaker statement form on behalf of its speakers
Whether the organisation's previous events have been reviewed by the college oversight board
questions.explanation: One core question asks whether the event is run by an external organisation or one aligned to the college, and whether all those involved and the speakers are clear.
questions.source_excerpt: Is the event run by an external organisation, or one aligned to the college / university, are all those involved and speakers clear?

questions.question: You plan to advertise a debate under a deliberately provocative title. Which consideration does the External Speakers and Events Policy require you, as organiser, to address?
options: Whether the title has been cleared by the college marketing team before it is advertised
Whether the subject, topic or title is controversial if advertised publicly or within the college
Whether the advertised title matches the wording of an approved unit or course specification
Whether the event must be advertised within the college community only, and not to the public
questions.explanation: One of the core questions organisers must address is whether the subject matter, topic or title is controversial if advertised to the public or within the college community.
questions.source_excerpt: Is the subject matter, topic, or title controversial if advertised to the public or within the college community?
