questions.source_excerpt: Willful contravention of this Code of Practice will lead to disciplinary actions being taken under either the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure or Staff Disciplinary Procedure, as appropriate, and, if necessary, by recourse to law or external agency referral.

questions.question: A lecturer wants to research extremism-related materials for a project and, separately, is worried that one of their students is being radicalised. Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, which routes apply?
options: Research: refer to the Prevent Steering Group for approval; concern: contact the Director of Studies
Research: seek the Director of Studies' approval; concern: refer it to the Prevent Steering Group
Both: refer to the Prevent Steering Group, which handles research approvals and individual concerns
Both: contact the Director of Studies, who approves research and liaises on concerns about students
questions.explanation: Research into sensitive or extremism-related materials must be referred to the Prevent Steering Group for approval, whereas concerns about a student in the context of extremism go to the Director of Studies.
questions.source_excerpt: If any staff or students are concerned about a staff member or student in the context of extremism or terrorism, they should contact the Director of Studies ... Staff or students who seek to research sensitive or extremism-related materials, must refer proposed activity to the `Prevent' Steering Group for approval.

questions.question: A student uses a College social media account to plan a non-violent extremist campaign, then complains that the College had no right to look at their messages. Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, what is the position?
options: The planning is permitted because it is non-violent, and the College may not monitor student messages
The planning is forbidden, but the College may monitor only staff communications, not those of students
Such use is forbidden; students are told the College may monitor or intercept communications
The planning is permitted until promotion begins, and any monitoring needs the student's prior consent
questions.explanation: Using College social media to plan violent or non-violent extremism is forbidden, and students are told through the Student Handbook that the College may monitor and/or intercept communications.
questions.source_excerpt: It is forbidden to use the College's MIS, IT and social media ... for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism ... the steps the College may take to monitor and/or intercept communications. This information is provided to students in the Student Handbook.

questions.question: Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, which of the following activities by LCC staff or students is not permitted?
options: Researching extremism-related materials once the Prevent Steering Group has given its approval
Teaching lawful material on a contested topic that some students find objectionable or offensive
Using College email to promote non-violent radicalisation in the name of an ideology or belief
Undertaking lawful research on a controversial topic as part of generating new knowledge
questions.explanation: Using College IT to promote violent or non-violent radicalisation is forbidden; approved extremism-related research, lawful objectionable teaching and controversial research are all permitted or expected.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not unlawful to express views or undertake research or teaching that some might find objectionable or offensive, providing it is within the law. ... It is forbidden to use the College's MIS, IT and social media ... for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation ... must refer proposed activity to the `Prevent' Steering Group for approval.

questions.question: A staff member says the College's warnings that it may monitor or intercept communications apply only to students, because the information appears in the Student Handbook. According to the Freedom of Speech Policy, is this right?
options: No, the Information Security Policy advises staff as well as students
Yes, the monitoring warnings are addressed only to students in the Student Handbook
Yes, staff communications may be monitored only with the Director of Studies' consent
No, but staff are advised only through their employment contracts and not by any policy
questions.explanation: The Information Security Policy advises both staff and students about the steps the College may take to monitor and/or intercept communications; the Student Handbook is how the information reaches students.
questions.source_excerpt: The Information Security Policy advises staff and students of the consequences of accessing inappropriate material and the steps the College may take to monitor and/or intercept communications. This information is provided to students in the Student Handbook.

questions.question: A student's research into extremism-related materials has Prevent Steering Group approval. The student then uses a College social media account to promote the extremist group being studied. Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, what is the position?
options: It is permitted, as Prevent Steering Group approval covers all activity connected with the research
It is permitted, provided the posts are clearly labelled as part of an approved research project
It is permitted, provided the Director of Studies is told about the posts before they are published
It is forbidden, as research approval does not allow using College social media to promote extremism
questions.explanation: Prevent Steering Group approval relates to the proposed research, while the policy separately forbids using College social media for the promotion of extremism.
questions.source_excerpt: It is forbidden to use the College's MIS, IT and social media or other elements of the information management systems or processes for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism ... Staff or students who seek to research sensitive or extremism-related materials, must refer proposed activity to the `Prevent' Steering Group for approval.

questions.question: One student posts a lawful but harshly worded criticism of a College decision that some staff find offensive; another posts defamatory claims about a named lecturer. Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, which post leads to disciplinary action?
options: Both posts, as each one caused offence to members of the College's staff
Only the defamatory post; offensive views within the law are not unlawful
Only the critical post, as it concerns the College rather than an individual
Neither post, as both are protected by the College's commitment to freedom of expression
questions.explanation: Expressing views some find objectionable or offensive is not unlawful providing it is within the law, whereas disciplinary action is taken against those found to have made defamatory comments about staff.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not unlawful to express views or undertake research or teaching that some might find objectionable or offensive, providing it is within the law. ... has a responsibility not to make libelous and/or defamatory comments about the College, its staff, or students. Disciplinary action will be taken against individuals

questions.question: A lecturer gives a lawful talk that many students find offensive. A group of students then systematically disrupts the lecturer's sessions to stop the talk being repeated. Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, who may face disciplinary processes?
options: The disrupting students, as activity aimed at preventing freedom of speech attracts discipline
The lecturer, as teaching that offends many students is likely to be unlawful under the Code
Both parties, as the lecturer caused offence and the students disrupted the teaching sessions
Neither party, as offensive teaching and protest are both protected forms of free expression
questions.explanation: Lawful teaching that some find offensive is not unlawful, whereas the College will apply disciplinary processes to protest or systematic activity aimed at preventing freedom of speech.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not unlawful to express views or undertake research or teaching that some might find objectionable or offensive, providing it is within the law. ... The College will apply disciplinary processes as appropriate in the event of actions of protest or systematic activity aimed at preventing freedom of speech.

questions.question: Several staff repeatedly block-book the only suitable room so that a student society's invited speakers cannot be heard. They argue that, as this is not a protest, the Freedom of Speech Policy does not cover it. Are they right?
options: Yes, disciplinary processes under the policy apply only to actions of protest by students
Yes, room bookings are an operational matter handled outside the Code of Practice
No, systematic activity aimed at preventing free speech is also covered
No, but the matter must first be referred to the Prevent Steering Group for a decision
questions.explanation: The College will apply disciplinary processes as appropriate to actions of protest or systematic activity aimed at preventing freedom of speech, so non-protest obstruction is also covered.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will apply disciplinary processes as appropriate in the event of actions of protest or systematic activity aimed at preventing freedom of speech.

questions.question: A student tells their personal tutor they fear a member of staff is being drawn into terrorism. The tutor believes the policy's reporting route covers only concerns about students. Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, where should the concern go?
options: To the Prevent Steering Group, which considers concerns raised about the activity of members of staff
To the Director of Studies, as the route covers concerns about staff members as well as students
To HR under the Staff Disciplinary Procedure, as the person of concern is a member of staff
To the Metropolitan Police directly, as the College's route does not cover concerns about staff
questions.explanation: Any staff member or student concerned about a staff member or student in the context of extremism or terrorism should contact the Director of Studies, so the route is not limited to concerns about students.
questions.source_excerpt: If any staff or students are concerned about a staff member or student in the context of extremism or terrorism, they should contact the Director of Studies, who will liaise with relevant internal contacts and, if required, appropriate external agencies

questions.question: A member of staff deliberately uses the College's MIS to help plan a non-violent extremist campaign. Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, what is the position and what may follow?
options: It is permitted, as the ban on using College systems covers violent extremism and social media only
It is forbidden, but staff breaches go to the Prevent Steering Group instead of any disciplinary route
It is forbidden, and is handled under the Student Code of Conduct because the MIS holds student data
It is forbidden; staff discipline applies and, if necessary, recourse to law or external referral
questions.explanation: Using the College's MIS to plan violent or non-violent extremism is forbidden, and wilful contravention of the Code leads to action under the Staff Disciplinary Procedure and, if necessary, recourse to law or external agency referral.
questions.source_excerpt: It is forbidden to use the College's MIS ... for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism ... Willful contravention of this Code of Practice will lead to disciplinary actions being taken under ... Staff Disciplinary Procedure, as appropriate, and, if necessary, by recourse to law or external agency referral.

questions.question: A lecturer plans to research extremist propaganda and to end the project with a public seminar at LCC given by an external researcher. Under the Freedom of Speech Policy, which requirements apply?
options: Prevent Steering Group approval of the research also covers the seminar, so no further checks apply
The seminar's risk assessment also covers the research, so no Prevent Steering Group referral applies
Prevent Steering Group approval for the research; a risk assessment and signed speaker form for the seminar
The Director of Studies approves the research and signs the External Speaker Statement Form for the seminar
questions.explanation: Research into extremism-related materials must be referred to the Prevent Steering Group for approval, while an event with an external individual needs a risk assessment and the external participant's signed External Speaker Statement Form.
questions.source_excerpt: each event involving an external individual or group to be staged at LCC will be subject to a risk assessment ... The external participant is required to sign the External Speaker Statement Form ... Staff or students who seek to research sensitive or extremism-related materials, must refer proposed activity to the `Prevent' Steering Group for approval.

questions.question: A lecturer argues that, because the Education Act 1986 duty quoted in the Freedom of Speech Policy falls on those who govern the College, upholding freedom of expression is not a matter for teaching staff. Is this right?
options: No, the College expects all of its stakeholders to uphold its commitment to freedom of expression within the law
Yes, the policy makes the Board of Directors alone responsible for upholding freedom of expression at LCC
No, the quoted Act places its duty on individual lecturers rather than on the persons who govern the College
Yes, teaching staff must uphold freedom of expression only while chairing formal debates on campus
questions.explanation: The quoted Act places a duty on persons concerned in the government of the establishment, but the Code of Practice, which applies to staff, says the College expects all its stakeholders to uphold its commitment to freedom of expression within the law.
questions.source_excerpt: Persons concerned in the government of any establishment ... shall take such steps as are reasonably practicable to ensure that freedom of speech within the law is secured ... The College expects all its stakeholders to uphold its commitment to Freedom of Expression within the law.

questions.question: A finance officer finds evidence suggesting a colleague may have committed a financial irregularity. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, how is a suspected case like this handled?
options: The line manager deals with it informally within the department, reporting it to the Board of Directors once any loss has been confirmed
A formal investigation is started under defined procedures, with findings reported to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee
It is added to the Master Risk Register and considered by the Board of Directors at its next annual review of risk appetite
It is referred straight to the police and external authorities, and the College carries out no internal investigation of its own
questions.explanation: Suspected fraud, bribery or financial irregularity triggers a formal investigation under defined procedures, with findings reported to the ARRC and, where appropriate, the Board and external authorities.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of suspected fraud, bribery or financial irregularity, a formal investigation process is initiated under defined procedures. Findings are reported to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee and, where appropriate, to the Board of Directors and external authorities.

questions.question: You wish to raise a confidential concern about suspected malpractice involving your own senior manager. Under the Whistleblowing Policy described in the Internal Control Arrangements, which reporting route is available to you?
options: Your line manager, who must approve the concern before it can be passed to anyone else
The Office for Students, as internal routes cannot be used for concerns about managers
The Company Secretary, or directly to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee
The senior manager concerned, who must be given the chance to respond first
questions.explanation: The Whistleblowing Policy provides reporting routes that include the Company Secretary or going directly to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee, as well as escalation to senior management.
questions.source_excerpt: provides clear reporting routes, including escalation to senior management, the Company Secretary or directly to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee;

questions.question: A student tells you they want to report suspected unethical behaviour by a member of staff in confidence. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which statement is correct?
options: The Whistleblowing Policy enables students, as well as staff, to raise concerns in confidence
The Whistleblowing Policy is for staff, so the student must use the academic appeals process instead
The student must first obtain written permission from the Board of Directors to raise the concern
The concern can be raised provided the student agrees to be named to the member of staff involved
questions.explanation: The Whistleblowing Policy enables staff, students and other stakeholders to raise concerns about suspected wrongdoing or unethical behaviour in confidence and without fear of detriment.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has a Whistleblowing Policy in place that enables staff, students and other stakeholders to raise concerns about suspected wrongdoing, malpractice or unethical behaviour in confidence and without fear of detriment.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what level of assurance does the College's system of internal control provide against loss, misconduct or failure to comply with regulatory requirements?
options: Absolute assurance, as the system is designed to eliminate rather than merely manage all risk
Full assurance over financial risks, with partial assurance over academic and regulatory risks
Reasonable, but not absolute, assurance, as it is designed to manage rather than eliminate risk
No assurance until the external auditors have signed off the College's annual accounts for the year
questions.explanation: The policy states the system is designed to manage, rather than eliminate, risk, so it provides reasonable but not absolute assurance.
questions.source_excerpt: The system of internal control is designed to manage, rather than eliminate, risk, and therefore provides reasonable, but not absolute, assurance against material misstatement, loss, misconduct or failure to comply with regulatory requirements.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which body is the College's governing body and ultimately responsible for ensuring that effective systems of internal control, risk management and ethical conduct are in place?
options: The Board of Directors
The College Oversight Board
The Company Secretary
The Academic Board
questions.explanation: The policy names the Board of Directors as the College's governing body with ultimate responsibility for internal control, risk management and ethical conduct.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board of Directors (BoD) is the College's governing body and is ultimately responsible for ensuring that effective systems of internal control, risk management and ethical conduct are in place.

questions.question: You are asked to approve a purchase and are unsure whether it falls within your authority. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which document sets out delegated financial and operational authority limits and approval thresholds?
options: The Whistleblowing Policy and its reporting routes
The Master Risk Register and its risk appetite statement
The Scheme of Delegation and Decision Making
The Anti-Bribery Policy on prohibited behaviours
questions.explanation: The formally approved Scheme of Delegation and Decision Making sets out delegated financial and operational authority limits and approval thresholds.
questions.source_excerpt: a formally approved Scheme of Delegation and Decision Making, which sets out delegated financial and operational authority limits and approval thresholds, reducing the risk of unauthorised or improper activity;

questions.question: As a risk owner, you notice that a risk you are responsible for now exceeds its tolerance level. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, what should happen to the risk?
options: You accept the risk locally as its owner and raise its tolerance level without reporting it further
It is escalated through the formal arrangements for risks that exceed tolerance levels
It is removed from the Master Risk Register and managed in your department until back within tolerance
It stays unchanged until the Board's next annual review of the College's risk appetite
questions.explanation: The key elements of the College's Risk Management Framework include formal escalation arrangements where risks exceed tolerance levels.
questions.source_excerpt: defined risk owners, mitigating controls and review schedules; use of a likelihood-impact risk matrix and an articulated risk appetite; and formal escalation arrangements where risks exceed tolerance levels.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, the Whistleblowing Policy supports protection for individuals who raise concerns in which circumstance?
options: When the concern is later proven to be true
When the concern is raised anonymously
When the concern was first raised with their line manager
When they raise the concern in good faith
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Whistleblowing Policy supports protection for individuals who raise concerns in good faith.
questions.source_excerpt: ensures that concerns are handled sensitively, proportionately and independently; and ... supports protection for individuals who raise concerns in good faith.

questions.question: Under the Internal Control Arrangements, what happens when an internal or external review identifies recommendations for improvement?
options: Management action plans with defined deadlines and responsible officers are developed, with progress monitored until completion
The recommendations are noted in the minutes and revisited at the next scheduled review, without a formal action plan
Management decides whether to act on each recommendation, and no progress reporting to governance bodies is required
The recommendations are passed to the Office for Students, which sets the deadlines and monitors their implementation
questions.explanation: The policy requires management action plans with defined deadlines and responsible officers, with progress monitored through governance reporting cycles until completion.
questions.source_excerpt: Where internal or external reviews identify recommendations for improvement, management action plans are developed with defined deadlines and responsible officers. Progress against these actions is monitored through governance reporting cycles until completion.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Internal Control Arrangements as a way the effectiveness of the system of internal control is monitored and reviewed?
options: Regular reports from executive management
Monthly self-certification of controls by every member of staff
Termly and annual committee assurance to the Board
Periodic internal and external reviews of governance effectiveness
questions.explanation: The policy lists executive management reports, termly and annual committee assurance, review of risk registers and policy compliance, and periodic internal and external reviews; monthly staff self-certification is not listed.
questions.source_excerpt: The effectiveness of the system of internal control is monitored and reviewed on an ongoing basis through: ... regular reports from executive management; ... termly and annual committee assurance to the Board; ... review of risk registers, policy compliance and mitigation plans; and ... periodic internal and external reviews of governance effectiveness.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, how does the College maintain its accounting records?
options: Under International Financial Reporting Standards, reconciled and reviewed by the internal finance team each year
Using each department's own local accounting conventions, consolidated by the finance office once a year
Under UK Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, with independent review reserved for cases of suspected fraud
Under UK Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, supported by reconciliation and periodic independent review
questions.explanation: The policy states that complete and accurate accounting records are kept in accordance with UK GAAP, supported by reconciliation processes and periodic independent review.
questions.source_excerpt: The College maintains complete and accurate accounting records in accordance with UK Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, supported by reconciliation processes and periodic independent review.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which risks does the College's Master Risk Register encompass?
options: Financial and regulatory risks, with academic risks held separately by each department
Corporate, financial and reputational risks, excluding Prevent Duty risks
Health and safety, data protection and estates risks
Corporate, academic, financial, regulatory and Prevent Duty risks
questions.explanation: The Risk Management Framework includes a Master Risk Register encompassing corporate, academic, financial, regulatory and Prevent Duty risks.
questions.source_excerpt: a Master Risk Register encompassing corporate, academic, financial, regulatory and Prevent Duty risks; defined risk owners, mitigating controls and review schedules;

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what do clear segregation of duties and collective decision-making at the College ensure?
options: That no individual holds unfettered authority
That every decision is approved by the full Board
That each department sets its own authority limits
That managers may act alone when a matter is urgent
questions.explanation: The policy lists clear segregation of duties and collective decision-making as a key governance mechanism, ensuring that no individual holds unfettered authority.
questions.source_excerpt: clear segregation of duties and collective decision-making, ensuring that no individual holds unfettered authority;

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what approach does London Churchill College take to bribery and corruption?
options: A proportionate approach, with small cash gifts permitted if they are declared
A case-by-case approach, decided by the line manager of the staff member involved
A zero-tolerance approach, articulated through the College's Anti-Bribery Policy
A risk-based approach, tolerating minor breaches that fall below a set value
questions.explanation: The College operates a zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption, which is articulated through its Anti-Bribery Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: The College operates a zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption, which is articulated through its Anti-Bribery Policy.

questions.question: Under the Internal Control Arrangements, which control applies to higher-risk decisions at the College?
options: Approval by the most senior manager available
Dual-authorisation and collective approval
Prior sign-off by the Office for Students
Retrospective review at the annual Board meeting
questions.explanation: The internal controls listed in the policy include dual-authorisation and collective approval for higher-risk decisions.
questions.source_excerpt: dual-authorisation and collective approval for higher-risk decisions;

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which committee has oversight of financial management, propriety and value for money at the College?
options: The Finance and General Purposes Committee
The Academic Board and its sub-committees
The Senior Leadership Team's budget group
The Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee
questions.explanation: The policy lists oversight of financial management, propriety and value for money by the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee among the College's internal controls.
questions.source_excerpt: oversight of financial management, propriety and value for money by the Audit, Remuneration ... and Risk Committee

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, how are risks relating to fraud, bribery, corruption, financial misconduct and governance failure treated?
options: They are explicitly captured within the risk registers and reviewed regularly through governance committees
They are kept out of the risk registers and dealt with only through formal investigations as cases arise
They are recorded in a confidential log held by the Company Secretary and reviewed only by the Chair
They are added to the risk registers only once a case has been proven and reported to external authorities
questions.explanation: The policy states that these risks are explicitly captured within the risk registers and reviewed regularly through governance committees.
questions.source_excerpt: Risks relating to fraud, bribery, corruption, financial misconduct and governance failure are explicitly captured within the risk registers and reviewed regularly through governance committees.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, how often does the Board of Directors review the College's risk appetite?
options: Termly, at each meeting of the governance committees
Every three years, when the risk framework is renewed
Annually, considering whether it remains appropriate
Only when a risk has exceeded its agreed tolerance level
questions.explanation: The Board reviews the College's risk appetite annually and considers whether it remains appropriate in light of financial performance, regulatory developments and strategic objectives.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board reviews the College's risk appetite annually and considers whether it remains appropriate in light of financial performance, regulatory developments and strategic objectives

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what happens to the minutes of the College's governance board and committee meetings?
options: They are kept confidential to members and destroyed once all agreed actions are complete
They are published and retained as formal records of challenge, scrutiny and decision-making
They are circulated to attendees only and summarised in the College's annual report
They are held by each chair and released only if the regulator formally requests them
questions.explanation: The policy states that minutes of meetings are published and retained as formal records of challenge, scrutiny and decision-making.
questions.source_excerpt: Minutes of meetings are published and retained as formal records of challenge, scrutiny and decision-making.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what do the regular assurance reports received by the Board of Directors confirm?
options: That no fraud or misconduct of any kind has occurred during the reporting period
That every member of staff has completed internal controls training this year
That the external auditors have approved each department's budget for the year
That internal controls have operated as intended during the reporting period
questions.explanation: The Board receives regular assurance reports confirming that internal controls have operated as intended during the reporting period and that any weaknesses have been addressed.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board receives regular assurance reports confirming that internal controls have operated as intended during the reporting period

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, how does the Whistleblowing Policy ensure that concerns raised are handled?
options: Informally, quickly and within the local department
Publicly, transparently and by the line manager
Sensitively, proportionately and independently
Anonymously, and only through the Office for Students
questions.explanation: The Whistleblowing Policy ensures that concerns are handled sensitively, proportionately and independently.
questions.source_excerpt: ensures that concerns are handled sensitively, proportionately and independently;

questions.question: Under the Internal Control Arrangements, what is reported annually to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee about whistleblowing?
options: A summary including the number of concerns raised and the status of investigations
The full names of every staff member and student who raised a concern that year
Only those concerns upheld after a completed investigation, with outcomes
A list of concerns rejected as vexatious, without any detail of the others raised
questions.explanation: A summary of whistleblowing activity, including the number of concerns raised and the status of investigations, is reported annually to the ARRC.
questions.source_excerpt: A summary of whistleblowing activity, including the number of concerns raised and the status of investigations, is reported annually to the ARRC to provide assurance regarding transparency and responsiveness.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, the College's governance, risk management and assurance processes operate in practice to protect what?
options: Tuition fee income, awarding-body links and league table standing
Public funds, academic standards and institutional integrity
Staff pay, pension arrangements and employment contracts
Commercial partnerships, overseas recruitment and market share
questions.explanation: The policy describes how governance, risk management and assurance processes operate in practice to protect public funds, academic standards and institutional integrity.
questions.source_excerpt: to demonstrate how governance, risk management and assurance processes operate in practice to protect public funds, academic standards and institutional integrity.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, how does the Board of Directors discharge its responsibilities?
options: Through the Chair, who may decide any matter alone between meetings
Through the Principal, who acts alone on the Board's behalf
Individually, with each director responsible for one department
Collectively, supported by a structured committee framework
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Board discharges its responsibilities collectively and is supported by a structured committee framework.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board discharges its responsibilities collectively and is supported by a structured committee framework.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee's formal assurance to the Board includes compliance with which two policies?
options: The Admissions and Academic Appeals policies
The Data Protection and Freedom of Information policies
The Whistleblowing and Anti-Bribery policies
The Health and Safety and Safeguarding policies
questions.explanation: The ARRC provides formal assurance to the Board on internal controls, risk management and governance, including compliance with the Whistleblowing and Anti-Bribery policies.
questions.source_excerpt: The Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee provides formal assurance to the Board on the adequacy and effectiveness of internal controls, risk management and governance arrangements, including compliance with the Whistleblowing and Anti-Bribery policies.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which tool does the College's Risk Management Framework use, alongside an articulated risk appetite, to assess risks?
options: A cost-benefit scoring model
A likelihood-impact risk matrix
A red-amber-green audit checklist
A pass-or-fail compliance scorecard
questions.explanation: Key elements of the Risk Management Framework include use of a likelihood-impact risk matrix and an articulated risk appetite.
questions.source_excerpt: use of a likelihood-impact risk matrix and an articulated risk appetite;

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, the Board of Directors is satisfied that the College's internal control arrangements remain appropriate to what?
options: The scale and complexity of the College's operations
The expectations of the College's awarding university partners
The number of students enrolled in the previous academic year
The size of the College's annual operating surplus or deficit
questions.explanation: The Board confirms it has reviewed the internal control arrangements and is satisfied that they remain appropriate to the scale and complexity of the College's operations.
questions.source_excerpt: is satisfied that they remain appropriate to the scale and complexity of the College's operations.

questions.question: A colleague took part in a procurement decision despite an undeclared conflict of interest. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, how does this relate to the misconduct the College's internal controls are designed to address?
options: It falls outside them, as the controls cover only fraud and bribery involving public funds
It falls outside them unless the conflict has led to a proven financial loss to the College
It falls within them, as conflicts of interest are expressly named among the misconduct covered
It falls within them only where the colleague is a director or governor of the College
questions.explanation: The College's system of internal controls is designed to detect, prevent and address misconduct, which expressly includes conflicts of interest alongside fraud, bribery and corruption.
questions.source_excerpt: London Churchill College (LCC) has established a comprehensive system of governance, risk management and internal controls designed to detect, prevent and address misconduct, including (but not limited to) fraud, bribery, corruption, conflicts of interest, financial irregularity

questions.question: A colleague says the College's internal control arrangements are checked only once, when they are first approved. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which statement is correct?
options: They are subject to ongoing scrutiny, monitoring and assurance by the Board of Directors and its committees
They are reviewed only when the Office for Students asks for evidence of compliance with its conditions
They are checked once on approval and then again only if a case of fraud or bribery is reported
They are reviewed by each department itself, with no role for the Board or its governance committees
questions.explanation: The arrangements are not a one-off check: they are subject to ongoing scrutiny, monitoring and assurance by the Board of Directors and its committees.
questions.source_excerpt: These arrangements are embedded within the College's governance framework and are supported by formal policies, procedures and reporting mechanisms. They are subject to ongoing scrutiny, monitoring and assurance by the Board of Directors and its committees

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which of the following does the Board of Directors acknowledge the College's system of internal control is intended to do?
options: Guarantee that no loss, misconduct or regulatory breach can ever occur at the College
Safeguard the College's assets and ensure the proper use of public funds
Replace the need for formal policies on ethical conduct and regulatory compliance
Move responsibility for internal control from the Board to individual members of staff
questions.explanation: The Board acknowledges a system that safeguards the College's assets and ensures the proper use of public funds; it manages rather than eliminates risk and operates alongside formal policies, with the Board remaining responsible.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board of Directors acknowledges its responsibility for establishing and maintaining a sound system of internal control that supports the achievement of the College's strategic objectives, safeguards its assets, ensures the proper use of public funds, and enables compliance with regulatory and legal obligations.

questions.question: During the reporting period, a weakness is found in one of the College's controls. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what should the Board's regular assurance reports be able to confirm about such weaknesses?
options: That they were corrected informally by the team concerned and so did not need to be recorded
That they were reported directly to the Office for Students before the end of the period
That the staff responsible have been referred for formal disciplinary action
That they have been identified, documented and addressed through agreed action plans
questions.explanation: The Board's regular assurance reports confirm that any control weaknesses have been identified, documented and addressed through agreed action plans.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board receives regular assurance reports confirming that internal controls have operated as intended during the reporting period and that any control weaknesses have been identified, documented and addressed through agreed action plans.

questions.question: A manager is asked to approve a decision that goes beyond the authority delegated to them. Under the governance framework described in the Internal Control Arrangements, what applies?
options: They may approve it provided they inform the Board of Directors once the decision is taken
They may split it into smaller decisions that each fall within their own authority limit
It is taken through the defined escalation routes, as delegated authority has clear limits
Their line manager may informally raise their authority limit for this one decision
questions.explanation: Authority is delegated with clearly defined limits, escalation routes and reporting requirements, which prevents decision-making power being concentrated in any single individual.
questions.source_excerpt: Authority is delegated appropriately, with clearly defined limits, escalation routes and reporting requirements. These arrangements ensure effective checks and balances and prevent the concentration of decision-making power in any single individual.

questions.question: A new member of a College governance committee wants to confirm the committee's remit, authority and reporting lines. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which source sets these out?
options: The committee's formally approved terms of reference
The published minutes of the committee's previous meetings
The College's Master Risk Register and its risk owners
The annual whistleblowing summary reported to the ARRC
questions.explanation: Committees operate under formally approved terms of reference, reviewed periodically to ensure clarity of remit, authority and reporting lines; minutes are records of challenge, scrutiny and decision-making.
questions.source_excerpt: All governance boards and committees operate under formally approved terms of reference which are reviewed periodically to ensure clarity of remit, authority and reporting lines.

questions.question: Your department identifies a new financial risk to be added to the College's Master Risk Register. Under the Risk Management Framework described in the Internal Control Arrangements, what is defined for risks on the register?
options: A named insurer, a budget code and an external auditor
A whistleblowing contact, an investigator and a disciplinary panel
An approval threshold, a second signatory and a delegated budget
A risk owner, mitigating controls and a review schedule
questions.explanation: Key elements of the Risk Management Framework include defined risk owners, mitigating controls and review schedules for the risks held on the Master Risk Register.
questions.source_excerpt: a Master Risk Register encompassing corporate, academic, financial, regulatory and Prevent Duty risks; defined risk owners, mitigating controls and review schedules;

questions.question: The College's financial performance has changed significantly this year. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, how is this taken into account in relation to the College's risk appetite?
options: Each risk owner immediately adjusts the tolerance levels for their own risks to reflect it
At its annual review, the Board considers whether the risk appetite remains appropriate
It is not, as the risk appetite is fixed when the Risk Management Framework is approved
The Company Secretary revises the risk appetite without needing to refer it to the Board
questions.explanation: The Board reviews the risk appetite annually and considers whether it remains appropriate in light of financial performance, regulatory developments and strategic objectives.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board reviews the College's risk appetite annually and considers whether it remains appropriate in light of financial performance, regulatory developments and strategic objectives

questions.question: You have been asked to read the College's Anti-Bribery Policy. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which of the following does that policy set out?
options: The delegated financial authority limits and approval thresholds for budget holders
The likelihood-impact risk matrix used to score the College's bribery risks
Prohibited behaviours and arrangements for reporting and investigating suspected bribery
The dual-authorisation rules that apply to the College's higher-risk decisions
questions.explanation: The Anti-Bribery Policy sets out expectations of conduct, prohibited behaviours, responsibilities of staff and governors, and arrangements for reporting and investigating suspected bribery or corruption.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy sets out expectations of conduct, prohibited behaviours, responsibilities of staff and governors, and arrangements for reporting and investigating suspected bribery or corruption.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, how is compliance with the Anti-Bribery Policy monitored, and which body gives the Board formal assurance on it?
options: Through governance oversight and internal controls, with formal assurance given by the ARRC
Through annual staff self-declarations, with formal assurance given by the Office for Students
Through spot checks by line managers, with formal assurance given by the Company Secretary
Through external audit alone, with formal assurance given by the College Oversight Board
questions.explanation: Compliance with the Anti-Bribery Policy is monitored through governance oversight and internal controls, and the ARRC gives the Board formal assurance that includes compliance with that policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Compliance with the policy is monitored through governance oversight and internal controls. ... The Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee provides formal assurance to the Board on the adequacy and effectiveness of internal controls, risk management and governance arrangements, including compliance with the Whistleblowing and Anti-Bribery policies.

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what is the purpose of the delegated financial and operational authority limits and approval thresholds set out in the Scheme of Delegation?
options: To set the risk appetite for each College department
To provide routes for staff to raise concerns about suspected wrongdoing
To pass the Board's ultimate responsibility for internal control to managers
To reduce the risk of unauthorised or improper activity at the College
questions.explanation: The Scheme of Delegation and Decision Making sets out authority limits and approval thresholds, reducing the risk of unauthorised or improper activity; the Board remains ultimately responsible for internal control.
questions.source_excerpt: a formally approved Scheme of Delegation and Decision Making, which sets out delegated financial and operational authority limits and approval thresholds, reducing the risk of unauthorised or improper activity;

questions.question: A whistleblowing concern you raised has now been investigated. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, where are the findings and actions reported?
options: Only to you as the person who raised it, and not to any governance body
To the relevant governance body, and escalated to the Board where necessary
To the Office for Students in every case, before any internal action is agreed
To your line manager, who decides whether any governance body needs to be told
questions.explanation: Findings and actions from whistleblowing investigations are reported to the relevant governance body and, where necessary, escalated to the Board of Directors.
questions.source_excerpt: All whistleblowing concerns are investigated appropriately, with findings and actions reported to the relevant governance body and, where necessary, escalated to the Board of Directors.

questions.question: A colleague asks why a summary of whistleblowing activity, including the number of concerns raised, is reported to the ARRC each year. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what is the reason?
options: To identify the individuals who raised concerns so the ARRC can contact them
To decide which concerns can be closed without any further investigation
To provide assurance regarding transparency and responsiveness
To set targets for reducing the number of concerns raised in future years
questions.explanation: The annual summary of whistleblowing activity is reported to the ARRC to provide assurance regarding transparency and responsiveness; all concerns are investigated.
questions.source_excerpt: A summary of whistleblowing activity, including the number of concerns raised and the status of investigations, is reported annually to the ARRC to provide assurance regarding transparency and responsiveness.

questions.question: Under the Internal Control Arrangements, which of the following statements about the timing of governance and assurance activity at the College is correct?
options: The Board reviews the College's risk appetite at the end of every term
A summary of whistleblowing activity is reported to the ARRC every month
Committee terms of reference are fixed on approval and are not reviewed again
Committees give assurance on internal control to the Board termly and annually
questions.explanation: Internal control is monitored through termly and annual committee assurance to the Board; risk appetite and the whistleblowing summary are annual, and terms of reference are reviewed periodically.
questions.source_excerpt: The effectiveness of the system of internal control is monitored and reviewed on an ongoing basis through: ... termly and annual committee assurance to the Board;

questions.question: According to the Internal Control Arrangements, on what basis does the Board of Directors confirm that the College has an effective system of internal control?
options: The assurance it receives through the processes described in the arrangements
An annual certificate of compliance issued to the College by the Office for Students
Signed declarations from every member of staff that they have followed all policies
A single end-of-year inspection of every department carried out by the Principal
questions.explanation: The Board's confirmation of an effective system of internal control is based on the assurance received through the processes described in the document.
questions.source_excerpt: Based on the assurance received through the processes described above, the Board of Directors confirms that London Churchill College has in place an effective system of internal control

questions.question: An investigation into suspected bribery by a College supplier has concluded. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, which statement about who receives its findings is correct?
options: The Board of Directors in every case, and the ARRC only where a financial loss to the College is confirmed
External authorities in every case, and the ARRC only if the Board of Directors decides it is appropriate
The ARRC, and also the Board of Directors and external authorities where appropriate
Only the Company Secretary, who then decides whether any committee or authority needs to be told
questions.explanation: Findings of investigations into suspected fraud, bribery or financial irregularity always go to the ARRC; the Board and external authorities receive them where appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of suspected fraud, bribery or financial irregularity, a formal investigation process is initiated under defined procedures. Findings are reported to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee and, where appropriate, to the Board of Directors and external authorities.

questions.question: To speed up approvals, a manager proposes that one senior officer should approve all higher-risk contracts alone, with no second signatory or collective decision. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, why is this not permitted?
options: Higher-risk decisions need dual-authorisation and collective approval, and no individual may hold unfettered authority
Higher-risk contracts may be approved only by the Office for Students, which must countersign each one in advance
Higher-risk contracts may be approved only by the ARRC, the sole body able to sign contracts for the College
Higher-risk contracts must first be entered on the Master Risk Register and signed off by their named risk owner
questions.explanation: The controls require dual-authorisation and collective approval for higher-risk decisions, and segregation of duties ensures no individual holds unfettered authority.
questions.source_excerpt: clear segregation of duties and collective decision-making, ensuring that no individual holds unfettered authority; ... dual-authorisation and collective approval for higher-risk decisions;

questions.question: The Board of Directors has confirmed that the College's system of internal control is effective, yet a small fraud is later discovered. Which statement in the Internal Control Arrangements explains how both can be true?
options: The Board's confirmation covers only academic standards, so a financial fraud falls outside the system
The system is designed to manage rather than eliminate risk, giving reasonable but not absolute assurance
The Board's confirmation is provisional until the Office for Students has approved the annual accounts
Controls apply only to decisions above approval thresholds, so small frauds are outside their scope
questions.explanation: An effective system still only manages risk: it gives reasonable, not absolute, assurance against loss or misconduct, so a fraud can occur despite the Board's confirmation.
questions.source_excerpt: The system of internal control is designed to manage, rather than eliminate, risk, and therefore provides reasonable, but not absolute, assurance against material misstatement, loss, misconduct or failure to comply with regulatory requirements.

questions.question: A member of staff has a whistleblowing concern that involves both their senior manager and the Company Secretary. Under the Whistleblowing Policy described in the Internal Control Arrangements, which route lets them avoid both?
options: Raising it with the College Oversight Board, which receives every concern first
Raising it with their line manager, who must pass it to the Company Secretary
Holding it back until the annual whistleblowing summary goes to the ARRC
Raising it directly with the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee
questions.explanation: The Whistleblowing Policy's reporting routes include going directly to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee, so neither senior management nor the Company Secretary needs to be involved.
questions.source_excerpt: provides clear reporting routes, including escalation to senior management, the Company Secretary or directly to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee;

questions.question: A member of staff blows the whistle on suspected bribery, and a formal investigation follows. Which combination of reporting is consistent with the Internal Control Arrangements?
options: Findings go only to the line manager, and bribery concerns are left out of the annual whistleblowing summary
Findings go to the ARRC, and the concern is counted in the annual whistleblowing summary to the ARRC
Findings go first to the Office for Students, and the concern is removed from the annual summary for secrecy
Findings are kept by the Company Secretary alone, and no annual whistleblowing summary is prepared
questions.explanation: Findings on suspected bribery are reported to the ARRC, and the annual whistleblowing summary to the ARRC includes the number of concerns raised and the status of investigations.
questions.source_excerpt: Findings are reported to the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee and, where appropriate, to the Board of Directors and external authorities. ... A summary of whistleblowing activity, including the number of concerns raised and the status of investigations, is reported annually to the ARRC

questions.question: A risk is identified that could damage the College's reputation but has no direct financial or compliance impact. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, does it fall within the Risk Management Framework?
options: No, the framework covers only risks that have a direct and measurable financial impact on the College
No, unless it also involves fraud, bribery, corruption or another form of financial misconduct
Only once the reputational harm exceeds its tolerance level and is escalated to the Board
Yes, as it covers risks that could threaten the College's objectives, reputation or sustainability
questions.explanation: The Risk Management Framework is designed to identify, assess, manage and monitor risks that could threaten the College's objectives, reputation, sustainability or regulatory compliance.
questions.source_excerpt: a comprehensive Risk Management Framework, aligned to ISO 31000, to identify, assess, manage and monitor risks that could threaten the College's objectives, reputation, sustainability or regulatory compliance.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee (ARRC) and the College Oversight Board (COB) under the Internal Control Arrangements?
options: Both receive assurance on internal controls; the ARRC also receives the annual whistleblowing summary
Only the COB receives assurance on internal controls, as the ARRC deals solely with staff pay and remuneration
The COB receives fraud investigation findings and the annual whistleblowing summary in place of the ARRC
The COB oversees financial management and value for money, while the ARRC has no role in governance matters
questions.explanation: Both specialist committees receive assurance on internal controls, governance effectiveness and regulatory compliance, and the annual whistleblowing summary is reported to the ARRC.
questions.source_excerpt: oversight by specialist committees, including the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee (ARRC) and the College Oversight Board (COB), which receive assurance on internal controls, governance effectiveness and regulatory compliance. ... A summary of whistleblowing activity ... is reported annually to the ARRC

questions.question: A manager says a type of misconduct not named in the Internal Control Arrangements cannot be addressed by the College's internal controls. According to the arrangements, why is this wrong?
options: The list is updated every term, and new types of misconduct are addressed once they have been added
The misconduct covered is expressly stated to include, but not be limited to, the types listed
Any misconduct missing from the list is automatically treated as a form of financial irregularity
Any misconduct missing from the list is handled by the Office for Students and referred back
questions.explanation: The internal controls are designed to detect, prevent and address misconduct 'including (but not limited to)' the listed types, so the list is not exhaustive.
questions.source_excerpt: designed to detect, prevent and address misconduct, including (but not limited to) fraud, bribery, corruption, conflicts of interest, financial irregularity, regulatory non-compliance, and breaches of public interest governance principles.

questions.question: You are the responsible officer for an action arising from an external review. Its deadline has passed and the action is only half complete. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, what happens to it?
options: It is closed as partly complete, and the remaining work is left to your own discretion
It lapses automatically, as actions are monitored only up to their original deadline
Progress continues to be monitored through governance reporting cycles until completion
It is dropped from governance reporting and reconsidered at the next external review
questions.explanation: Management action plans have defined deadlines and responsible officers, and progress is monitored through governance reporting cycles until the actions are completed.
questions.source_excerpt: management action plans are developed with defined deadlines and responsible officers. Progress against these actions is monitored through governance reporting cycles until completion.

questions.question: A colleague raised a whistleblowing concern in good faith, but the investigation found no wrongdoing. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, how does this affect the protection the Whistleblowing Policy supports?
options: It is withdrawn, as protection applies only to concerns that are upheld after investigation
It still applies, as protection is supported for individuals who raise concerns in good faith
It applies only if the colleague raised the concern anonymously and never gave their name
It applies only if the concern was first escalated through senior management before any other route
questions.explanation: The Whistleblowing Policy supports protection for individuals who raise concerns in good faith; it is not conditional on the concern being upheld.
questions.source_excerpt: ensures that concerns are handled sensitively, proportionately and independently; and ... supports protection for individuals who raise concerns in good faith.

questions.question: A College governor says the Anti-Bribery Policy is a staff policy and places no expectations on governors. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which statement is correct?
options: The governor is right, as governors are bound only by the Scheme of Delegation
The governor is right, as governors follow a separate code set by the ARRC
The governor is wrong: the policy sets out responsibilities of staff and governors
The governor is right unless they also hold a paid staff contract with the College
questions.explanation: The Anti-Bribery Policy sets out expectations of conduct, prohibited behaviours and the responsibilities of staff and governors.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy sets out expectations of conduct, prohibited behaviours, responsibilities of staff and governors, and arrangements for reporting and investigating suspected bribery or corruption.

questions.question: A colleague says the Board's annual review of internal control only confirms that controls were working on the last day of the year reviewed. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, what does the Board confirm?
options: That the arrangements were in place throughout the period and remain effective at the date of approval
That the arrangements were in place at year end and will be reviewed again only if a weakness arises
That the arrangements worked in most months, with any gaps to be addressed in the following year
That the arrangements have been in place since the date of approval, with earlier months not covered
questions.explanation: The Board confirms that the arrangements have been in place throughout the period reviewed and remain effective at the date of approval, not just at year end.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board has undertaken a review of the effectiveness of the system of internal control for the year ended December 2025 and confirms that the arrangements described in this document have been in place throughout the period and remain effective at the date of approval.

questions.question: A team identifies that a new overseas partnership creates a potential bribery risk, although no wrongdoing is suspected. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, how should this risk be treated?
options: It is captured in the risk registers, where bribery risks are recorded and reviewed through governance committees
A formal investigation is opened at once under the defined procedures, as for every bribery risk that is identified
It is reported straight to external authorities, as the College must disclose all potential bribery risks
It is kept off the risk registers until a case of bribery has actually been proven and reported
questions.explanation: Bribery risks are explicitly captured in the risk registers and reviewed regularly; the formal investigation process is for suspected bribery, which is not the case here.
questions.source_excerpt: Risks relating to fraud, bribery, corruption, financial misconduct and governance failure are explicitly captured within the risk registers and reviewed regularly through governance committees. ... In the event of suspected fraud, bribery or financial irregularity, a formal investigation process is initiated under defined procedures.

questions.question: A whistleblowing concern alleges malpractice in a department, and the department's manager, who is implicated, offers to investigate it personally. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, why is this inconsistent with the Whistleblowing Policy?
options: Concerns must be handled independently, as well as sensitively and proportionately
Concerns must always be investigated by the Office for Students rather than by the College
Concerns about a department may be handled only by the full Board of Directors itself
Concerns must wait until the annual ARRC summary is presented before any investigation can begin
questions.explanation: The Whistleblowing Policy ensures that concerns are handled sensitively, proportionately and independently, which an implicated manager investigating their own department would not satisfy.
questions.source_excerpt: ensures that concerns are handled sensitively, proportionately and independently;

questions.question: Because authority is delegated under the Scheme of Delegation, a colleague claims the Board of Directors is no longer responsible for internal control. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, who is ultimately responsible for ensuring it is effective?
options: The ARRC, once it has given the Board formal assurance on internal controls
Each manager, for all decisions that fall within their own delegated limit
The Company Secretary, as the officer who maintains and updates the Scheme of Delegation
The Board of Directors, which delegates authority but remains ultimately responsible
questions.explanation: The Board is the governing body and is ultimately responsible for effective internal control; authority is delegated with defined limits, but that responsibility stays with the Board.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board of Directors (BoD) is the College's governing body and is ultimately responsible for ensuring that effective systems of internal control, risk management and ethical conduct are in place. ... Authority is delegated appropriately, with clearly defined limits, escalation routes and reporting requirements.

questions.question: Which of the following would NOT be consistent with the Internal Control Arrangements?
options: A student raising a concern about unethical behaviour in confidence through the Whistleblowing Policy
Leaving a financial misconduct risk off the risk registers because the subject is considered too sensitive
A risk owner using the formal escalation arrangements once a risk has exceeded its tolerance level
A member of staff taking a whistleblowing concern directly to the ARRC without going to senior management
questions.explanation: Risks of financial misconduct must be explicitly captured in the risk registers; the other actions are all expressly provided for in the arrangements.
questions.source_excerpt: Risks relating to fraud, bribery, corruption, financial misconduct and governance failure are explicitly captured within the risk registers and reviewed regularly through governance committees.

questions.question: A whistleblowing concern appears minor, and a manager suggests closing it without investigation because concerns are to be handled proportionately. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which statement is correct?
options: It may be closed without investigation, as proportionate handling allows minor concerns to be set aside
It may be closed if the person who raised it agrees, and is then left out of the annual summary
It may be closed by the manager, provided the Company Secretary is told within the reporting period
All whistleblowing concerns are investigated appropriately, so it cannot simply be closed unexamined
questions.explanation: Proportionate handling does not remove the requirement that all whistleblowing concerns are investigated appropriately.
questions.source_excerpt: ensures that concerns are handled sensitively, proportionately and independently; ... All whistleblowing concerns are investigated appropriately, with findings and actions reported to the relevant governance body

questions.question: A colleague believes reviewing the risk registers is separate from checking whether the College's internal controls work. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which statement is correct?
options: Risk registers are reviewed only by individual risk owners and play no part in assurance
Risk registers are reviewed only when the Board sets its risk appetite, not for control checks
Reviewing risk registers is one of the listed ways that control effectiveness is monitored
Risk registers are checked only by external reviewers, whose reports go directly to the OfS
questions.explanation: The effectiveness of internal control is monitored on an ongoing basis through, among other things, review of risk registers, policy compliance and mitigation plans.
questions.source_excerpt: The effectiveness of the system of internal control is monitored and reviewed on an ongoing basis through: ... review of risk registers, policy compliance and mitigation plans;

questions.question: An external review of payroll recommends tightening an approval control and, separately, flags one payment as suspected fraud. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, how should each matter be handled?
options: Both go into a single management action plan, each with a defined deadline and a responsible officer
Both are referred for formal investigation under defined procedures, with findings reported to the ARRC
The suspected fraud goes into an action plan with a deadline; the recommendation is formally investigated
The recommendation goes into an action plan with a deadline; the suspected fraud is formally investigated
questions.explanation: Review recommendations lead to management action plans with defined deadlines and responsible officers, whereas suspected fraud triggers a formal investigation under defined procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of suspected fraud, bribery or financial irregularity, a formal investigation process is initiated under defined procedures. ... Where internal or external reviews identify recommendations for improvement, management action plans are developed with defined deadlines and responsible officers.

questions.question: A committee chair proposes reviewing the committee's terms of reference only if the Board asks, and keeping its minutes on file without publishing them. Under the Internal Control Arrangements, which assessment is correct?
options: Both are acceptable, as long as the minutes are retained as formal records of challenge and scrutiny
Only the review proposal conflicts, as retaining minutes on file without publishing them is sufficient
Both conflict: terms of reference are reviewed periodically, and the minutes are published and retained
Only the minutes proposal conflicts, as terms of reference are reviewed only when the Board requests it
questions.explanation: Committee terms of reference are reviewed periodically, not only on request, and minutes must be both published and retained, so neither proposal is permitted.
questions.source_excerpt: All governance boards and committees operate under formally approved terms of reference which are reviewed periodically to ensure clarity of remit, authority and reporting lines. Minutes of meetings are published and retained as formal records of challenge, scrutiny and decision-making.

questions.question: You are preparing a briefing on who does what in the College's internal control arrangements. According to the Internal Control Arrangements, which pairing of an activity with the body responsible for it is correct?
options: Reviewing the College's risk appetite each year: the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee
Approving and overseeing the College's Risk Management Framework: the Board of Directors
Receiving the yearly summary of whistleblowing activity: the College Oversight Board
Overseeing financial management, propriety and value for money: the Company Secretary
questions.explanation: The Board approved and oversees the Risk Management Framework; the Board (not the ARRC) reviews risk appetite, while the whistleblowing summary and financial oversight sit with the ARRC.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board has approved and oversees a comprehensive Risk Management Framework ... The Board reviews the College's risk appetite annually ... A summary of whistleblowing activity ... is reported annually to the ARRC ... oversight of financial management, propriety and value for money by the Audit, Remuneration

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, which body must approve all programme closures at London Churchill College?
options: The Board of Directors
The Principal's Executive Group (PEG)
The College's Academic Board
The College's Oversight Board
questions.explanation: The policy states plainly that all programme closures must be approved by the Academic Board.
questions.source_excerpt: All closures must be approved by the Academic Board;

questions.question: The Programme Closure Meeting has recommended closing a programme, but the closure is imminent and unavoidable and cannot wait for the normal approval route. What does the Programme Closure Policy say should happen?
options: The Principal may close the programme without any approval being sought or recorded
The closure must be delayed until the next scheduled Academic Board meeting approves it
The Oversight Board permanently approves the closure in place of the Academic Board
Chair's Action is sought, and the Academic Board is informed at its following meeting
questions.explanation: Recommendations normally go to the Academic Board for formal approval, but where closure is imminent and unavoidable, Chair's Action is sought and the Academic Board is informed at its next meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: Recommendations for closure will then be sent to the Academic Board for formal approval. If closure is imminent and unavoidable, Chair's Action will be sought, and the Academic Board informed at the following meeting;

questions.question: A programme being closed has no registered students, no applicants who have accepted offers, and no impact on other programmes. A colleague says the formal closure procedure is unnecessary. What does the Programme Closure Policy say?
options: The procedure can be skipped, provided the Principal gives verbal agreement at the next PEG meeting
The procedure must still be followed, and a permanent record of the closure kept
A brief notice to the Academic Board is sufficient, with no pro-forma needed
The procedure is intended for closures affecting students or applicants, so it can be waived here
questions.explanation: The policy states the procedure is followed even where no students or accepted applicants exist and other programmes are unaffected, and the College keeps permanent records of all closures.
questions.source_excerpt: This procedure will be followed, even in cases where no students are registered on the programme being closed, there are no applicants who have accepted offers on the course, and there is no impact from the closure on other programmes. The College will maintain permanent records of all programme closures;

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, who completes the Programme Closure Pro-forma, and to whom is the completed form submitted?
options: The Programme Leader, who submits it to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, who submits it to the Registrar
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer, who submits it to the Academic Board
The Registrar, who submits it to the Principal as Chair of the Programme Closure Meeting
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader completes the Programme Closure Pro-forma and submits it to the College's Senior Quality Assurance Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader will complete the Programme Closure Pro-forma (see in appendix) and submit the completed form to the College's Senior Quality Assurance Officer;

questions.question: You are a Programme Leader and the closure proposal for your programme has just been approved. Under the Programme Closure Policy, what is your responsibility regarding publicity for the programme?
options: Keep the programme advertised on the College website and in prospectuses until the last enrolled student has completed
Ask the awarding body to remove all references to the programme from both its own and the College's published materials
Liaise with recruiting and marketing staff to get publications, the website and external references amended or removed
Wait for the Quality Department to update College publications and the website as part of the next annual monitoring review
questions.explanation: Once closure is approved, the Programme Leader must liaise with recruiting and marketing staff to amend all College publications and the website and remove external references to the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Once a programme closure proposal has been approved it is the responsibility of the Programme Leader to liaise with recruiting and marketing staff members to ensure all necessary amendments are made to all London Churchill College publications and the website

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, whatever the reason for a programme closure, whose needs is the College committed to ensuring are met?
options: Existing students currently attending classes, but not suspended students, applicants or prospective candidates
