Existing students (including suspended students), but not applicants or prospective candidates
Existing students and applicants offered a place, but not suspended students or prospective candidates
Existing students (including suspended students), applicants offered a place, and prospective candidates
questions.explanation: The policy commits the College to meeting the needs of existing students including suspended students, applicants already offered a place, and prospective candidates, and is triggered in all cases.
questions.source_excerpt: Whatever the reason for closure, the College is committed to ensuring that the needs of existing students (including suspended students), applicants who have already been offered a place, and prospective candidates are met. This Policy is triggered in all cases;

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, until when must quality and academic standards be monitored during the closure of a programme?
options: Until the Academic Board has formally approved the closure and the pro-forma has been signed off
Until the final intake of students has enrolled and completed its first year
Until the end of the academic year in which the Academic Board approved the programme closure
Until the last student has had sufficient opportunity to complete the programme successfully
questions.explanation: The policy requires quality and academic standards to be monitored throughout the closure process until the last student has had sufficient opportunity to complete successfully.
questions.source_excerpt: Quality and Academic Standards are monitored throughout the closure process, until the last student has had sufficient opportunity to complete the programme successfully;

questions.question: A student on a programme that LCC is closing still needs to resubmit an assessment. Under the Programme Closure Policy, how should the teach-out plans treat this student?
options: They are excluded, as teach-out plans cover students who have no outstanding assessed work
They must transfer to another College programme in order to complete the resubmission
They are covered, as the plans must include arrangements for students needing to resubmit work
They may resubmit provided they do so before the Academic Board formally approves the closure
questions.explanation: The student is covered: the policy requires teach-out plans to include arrangements for students who have suspended their studies, need to resubmit work, or have deferred entry.
questions.source_excerpt: Plans will include arrangements for students who have suspended their studies, need to resubmit work or those who have deferred entry;

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, who oversees the teaching-out arrangements for a programme that is being closed?
options: The Registrar, in consultation with staff from the Recruitment and Admissions Department
The Programme Leader, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer, in consultation with the external examiner for the programme
The Principal, in consultation with the company director and the College's Oversight Board
questions.explanation: The policy gives the Programme Leader, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, responsibility for overseeing teaching-out arrangements.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, will oversee teaching out arrangements.

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, what is the position of the awarding body or other accrediting bodies when LCC closes a programme?
options: They are informed only after the last student has completed the programme
LCC will only close programmes with their full knowledge and consultation
They are involved only where they themselves requested the closure
They chair the Programme Closure Meeting and sign off the pro-forma
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC will only close programmes with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body or other accrediting bodies.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will only close Programmes with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body, or other accrediting bodies.

questions.question: A student on a programme that LCC is closing asks you whether the College will help them continue their studies. Which statement reflects the commitment in the Programme Closure Policy?
options: The College will make all efforts to ensure students are offered alternative study wherever possible
The College guarantees each student a place on their preferred course at another provider
Students must arrange any alternative study themselves once the Academic Board has approved the closure
The College offers alternative study to continuing students, excluding those who have suspended their studies
questions.explanation: The policy commits the College to making all efforts to ensure students are offered alternative study wherever possible.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will make all efforts to ensure that students are offered alternative study wherever possible.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Programme Closure Policy as a matter the Programme Closure Meeting will consider in particular?
options: The proposed redundancy and redeployment terms for staff teaching on the programme
The proposed arrangements for applicants to the programme
The proposed arrangements for delivering units/modules shared with other programmes
The proposed time scale for closure, allowing time for applicants and students to adjust
questions.explanation: The meeting particularly considers the rationale, timescale, and arrangements for registered students, applicants and shared units/modules; proposed redundancy and redeployment terms for staff are not listed.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Closure Meeting will consider the proposal based on the information provided on the programme closure form, in particular: 3.1.2.1. Rationale for closure; 3.1.2.2. Proposed time scale for closure ... 3.1.2.4. Proposed arrangements for applicants; 3.1.2.5. Proposed arrangements for delivering units/modules shared with other programmes.

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, what is London Churchill College committed to providing students with in the event of a programme closure?
options: A full refund of all tuition fees already paid for the programme, whatever stage of study they have reached
The fullest information, advice and guidance possible so that they can make well-informed decisions
A guaranteed place on an equivalent programme at a partner provider of their own choosing
Automatic transfer onto the College's closest alternative programme without needing to reapply
questions.explanation: The Aim section commits the College to ensuring students receive the fullest information, advice and guidance possible so they can make well-informed decisions if a programme closes.
questions.source_excerpt: London Churchill College is committed to ensuring that students are provided with the fullest information, advice, and guidance possible to enable them to make well-informed decisions in the event of programme closure.

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, how must the College document the decisions it takes during a programme closure?
options: Only the final Academic Board approval decision is formally recorded
They are recorded only where the closure affects enrolled students or applicants
They are all formally recorded, at every stage of the closure
They are shared verbally with staff and noted informally in PEG discussions
questions.explanation: The policy aims to ensure that decisions taken at all stages of planning and implementation are formally recorded, not only the final approval and not only where students are affected.
questions.source_excerpt: Decisions taken at all stages of planning and implementation are formally recorded;

questions.question: The Programme Closure Policy gives examples of reasons why the College may decide to permanently close a programme of study. Which of the following is one of those examples?
options: Key staff essential to the programme leaving the College
Applications rising beyond the places available on the programme
A planned increase in the programme's tuition fees for the next intake
The College moving its administrative offices to new premises
questions.explanation: Key staff essential to the programme leaving the College is one of the example reasons for closure listed in the policy, alongside declining student numbers and changing strategic priorities.
questions.source_excerpt: The College may wish to permanently close a programme of study for several reasons, for example:  Changing strategic priorities;  Declining student numbers;  Key staff essential to the programme leaving the College;

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, a proposed Programme Closure will be considered upon receiving what?
options: A written petition from students enrolled on the programme
A formal request from the programme's external examiner
A formal rationale from the Registrar
A formal rationale from the Principal
questions.explanation: The policy states that a Programme Closure will be considered upon receiving a formal rationale from the Principal.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Closure will be considered upon receiving a formal rationale from the Principal;

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, who discusses the prospects for closing a programme in the context of the College's current and changing business and academic needs?
options: The Academic Board, together with the awarding body
The Programme Leader and the programme's student representatives
Members of the Principal's Executive Group (PEG) and Directors
The Registrar and the Senior Quality Assurance Officer
questions.explanation: The first step of the procedure is for members of PEG and Directors to discuss prospects for closing a programme in the context of the College's business and academic needs.
questions.source_excerpt: Members of PEG and Directors will discuss prospects for closing a programme in the context of the College's current and changing business and academic needs.

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, based on the preliminary decisions taken, who instructs the Programme Leader to commence the formal closure process?
options: The Senior Quality Assurance Officer
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
A representative of the Recruitment and Admissions Department
The Chair of the Academic Board
questions.explanation: Based on the preliminary decisions taken, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring instructs the Programme Leader to commence the formal closure process.
questions.source_excerpt: Based upon preliminary decisions taken, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring will instruct the Programme Leader to commence the formal closure process.

questions.question: When the Quality Department reviews a completed Programme Closure Pro-forma, what does the Programme Closure Policy say it is checking for?
options: That the programme's teaching staff have been offered redeployment to other programmes
That every enrolled student has agreed in writing to the proposed closure timetable
That the awarding body has already approved the proposed closure in writing
That all parts have been completed correctly and the statistical data provided are accurate
questions.explanation: The Quality Department reviews the completed pro-forma to ensure all parts have been completed correctly and that the statistical data provided are accurate.
questions.source_excerpt: The Quality Department will review the completed Programme Closure pro-forma to ensure that all parts have been completed correctly and the statistical data provided are accurate;

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, who convenes the Programme Closure Meeting once the details on the completed pro-forma have been approved?
options: The Senior Quality Assurance Officer
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
The College Registrar
The Programme Leader of the programme being closed
questions.explanation: Once the details on the completed form have been approved, the Senior Quality Assurance Officer convenes the Programme Closure Meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: Once details provided on the completed form have been approved, the Senior Quality Assurance Officer will convene a Programme Closure Meeting

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, who chairs the Programme Closure Meeting?
options: The Registrar
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
The Principal
The company director
questions.explanation: The policy lists the Principal as Chair of the Programme Closure Meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: Defacto membership will include: The Principal (as Chair),

questions.question: Besides its de facto members, who does the Programme Closure Policy say may also be invited to attend the Programme Closure Meeting?
options: The external examiner and a student representative
A representative of the awarding body and the Chair of the Academic Board
The College's Data Protection Officer and a member of the Finance team
The company director and a member of the College's Oversight Board
questions.explanation: In addition to the de facto members, the company director and a member of the College's Oversight Board may be invited to attend the meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: In addition, the company director and a member of the College's Oversight Board may be invited to attend.

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, who informs students enrolled on the programme about the proposed closure, explains the reasons for it and discusses the implications with them?
options: The Principal, as Chair of the Programme Closure Meeting
The Programme Leader of the programme being closed
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer
The Registrar, through the Recruitment and Admissions team
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader informs enrolled students about the proposed closure, explains the reasons and discusses the implications with them.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader will inform students enrolled on the programme about the proposed closure, explain the reasons for the proposal, and discuss the implications with them

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, which of the following remains in place for the duration of the teach-out phase of a programme that is closing?
options: External examining procedures for the programme
Advertising of the programme on the College website
Monthly teach-out progress reviews chaired by the Principal
Termly teach-out reports submitted to the awarding body
questions.explanation: Student surveys, annual unit and programme monitoring reports and external examining procedures remain in place for the whole teach-out phase; the other options are not required by the policy, and publicity must be removed once closure is approved.
questions.source_excerpt: Student surveys, annual unit and programme monitoring reports and external examining procedures will remain in place for the duration of the teach-out phase.

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, who oversees and monitors the closure process to ensure that student interests are protected and sufficient support is in place?
options: The Principal and the College's Oversight Board, in consultation with the programme's external examiner
The Recruitment and Admissions Department, in consultation with the Programme Leader and student representatives
The company director and the Finance team, in consultation with the Chair of the Academic Board
The Registrar and Quality Assurance Officers, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
questions.explanation: The Registrar and the Quality Assurance Officers, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, oversee and monitor the closure process to protect student interests.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar and the Quality Assurance Officers, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, will oversee and monitor the closure process to ensure that student interests are protected and that sufficient levels of support are in place to facilitate programme completion.

questions.question: According to the Programme Closure Policy, what is the stated purpose of the Programme Closure Meeting?
options: To agree redundancy and redeployment terms for all staff currently teaching on the programme
To confirm and record that student interests, welfare and timescale have been appropriately considered
To set the tuition fees that will apply to the final graduating cohort on the programme
To approve the replacement programme that will be launched in place of the one being closed
questions.explanation: The Senior Quality Assurance Officer convenes the Programme Closure Meeting to confirm and record that student interests, welfare and timescale have been appropriately considered.
questions.source_excerpt: the Senior Quality Assurance Officer will convene a Programme Closure Meeting to confirm and record the student interests, welfare and timescale have been appropriately considered.

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, which sequence correctly describes how a programme closure moves from first discussion to formal approval?
options: Programme Leader completes the pro-forma; PEG and Directors discuss; Academic Board approves; Programme Closure Meeting is held
PEG and Directors discuss; Programme Leader completes the pro-forma; Programme Closure Meeting is held; Academic Board approves
PEG and Directors discuss; Programme Closure Meeting is held; Academic Board approves; Programme Leader completes the pro-forma
Academic Board approves; PEG and Directors discuss; Programme Leader completes the pro-forma; Programme Closure Meeting is held
questions.explanation: PEG and Directors first discuss the prospects, the Programme Leader then completes the pro-forma, the Programme Closure Meeting considers it, and its recommendation goes to the Academic Board for formal approval.
questions.source_excerpt: Members of PEG and Directors will discuss prospects for closing a programme ... The Programme Leader will complete the Programme Closure Pro-forma ... the Senior Quality Assurance Officer will convene a Programme Closure Meeting ... Recommendations for closure will then be sent to the Academic Board for formal approval.

questions.question: The Senior Quality Assurance Officer has just received a completed Programme Closure Pro-forma. Under the Programme Closure Policy, what must happen before a Programme Closure Meeting is convened?
options: The Academic Board must formally approve the closure recommendation set out on the pro-forma
The Principal's Executive Group must sign off the pro-forma and notify students on the programme
The Quality Department reviews it for completeness and accurate statistics, and its details are approved
The external examiner must confirm in writing that academic standards on the programme remain secure throughout
questions.explanation: The Quality Department first reviews the pro-forma for correct completion and accurate statistical data; only once its details are approved does the Senior Quality Assurance Officer convene the meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: The Quality Department will review the completed Programme Closure pro-forma to ensure that all parts have been completed correctly and the statistical data provided are accurate; ... Once details provided on the completed form have been approved, the Senior Quality Assurance Officer will convene a Programme Closure Meeting

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, what normally happens to the decisions taken at a Programme Closure Meeting when closure is not imminent and unavoidable?
options: They are recorded on the pro-forma and signed off by the Chair, and the recommendation goes to the Academic Board
They are recorded in the PEG minutes and take effect at once, with the Academic Board informed afterwards
They are signed off by the Senior Quality Assurance Officer and sent to the awarding body for approval
They are signed off by the Programme Leader and sent to the College's Oversight Board for final approval
questions.explanation: Decisions are recorded on the Programme Closure Pro-forma and signed off by the meeting's Chair, and the recommendation for closure is then sent to the Academic Board for formal approval.
questions.source_excerpt: Decisions taken will be recorded on the Programme Closure Pro-forma and signed off by the Chair of the meeting. Recommendations for closure will then be sent to the Academic Board for formal approval.

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, which pair are both de facto members of the Programme Closure Meeting, rather than people who may be invited to attend?
options: The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring and the company director
The Registrar and a member of the College's Oversight Board
The company director and the programme's external examiner
The Registrar and the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
questions.explanation: The Registrar and the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring are both de facto members; the company director and an Oversight Board member may only be invited, and the external examiner is not listed.
questions.source_excerpt: Defacto membership will include: The Principal (as Chair), the Registrar, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, the Programme Leader of the programme scheduled for closure; ... In addition, the company director and a member of the College's Oversight Board may be invited to attend.

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, at what point does the Programme Leader inform enrolled students about the proposed closure of their programme?
options: Only after the Oversight Board has reviewed the Programme Closure Meeting minutes
Following the decisions taken by the Principal's Executive Group to close it
Once all references to the programme have been removed from the College's website
Once the Registrar has confirmed an alternative study offer for every student
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader informs enrolled students of the proposed closure, its reasons and implications following the decisions taken by PEG to close the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader will inform students enrolled on the programme about the proposed closure, explain the reasons for the proposal, and discuss the implications with them following decisions taken by the Principal's Executive Group (PEG) to close the programme.

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, when enrolled students are told about a proposed programme closure, what must they be given besides the reasons and the implications?
options: Plans for teaching out the programme and how the College will maintain the quality of learning during teach-out
A deadline by which each student must find and register on an alternative course at another provider
Details of the compensation each student will receive for the disruption caused by the programme closure
The names of staff who will leave the College once the programme closure has been formally approved
questions.explanation: Students must also be told the plans for teaching out the programme and how the College intends to maintain the quality of their learning experience during the teach-out phase.
questions.source_excerpt: They will also be informed of plans for teaching-out the programme and provided with the details of how the College intends to maintain the quality of the student learning experience during the teach-out phase.

questions.question: During the teach-out phase of a closing programme, who does the Programme Closure Policy make responsible for ensuring the College's quality assurance framework and procedures continue to be followed?
options: The Recruitment and Admissions Department, in consultation with the Principal
The programme's external examiner, in consultation with the awarding body
The company director, in consultation with a member of the College's Oversight Board
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer, in consultation with the Registrar
questions.explanation: During teach-out, the Senior Quality Assurance Officer, in consultation with the Registrar, ensures the College's quality assurance framework and procedures continue to be followed.
questions.source_excerpt: The Senior Quality Assurance Officer, in consultation with the Registrar, will ensure that the College's quality assurance framework and procedures continue to be followed.

questions.question: A manager suggests pausing student surveys and annual monitoring reports for a programme in its teach-out phase, since it is closing anyway. What does the Programme Closure Policy require?
options: They may be paused once the Academic Board approves closure, provided external examining continues
They may be paused once fewer than half of the original cohort remain registered on the programme
They remain in place for the whole teach-out phase, and monitoring maintains parity of learning experience
They pass to the awarding body, which runs its own surveys and monitoring for teach-out students
questions.explanation: Student surveys, monitoring reports and external examining remain in place for the whole teach-out phase, and ongoing monitoring ensures parity of learning experience for teach-out students.
questions.source_excerpt: Student surveys, annual unit and programme monitoring reports and external examining procedures will remain in place for the duration of the teach-out phase. Ongoing monitoring will ensure that parity of learning experiences for students in the teach-out programme is maintained;

questions.question: The Programme Closure Pro-forma asks for the expected final completion date of the programme. Under the Programme Closure Policy, what must that date take into account?
options: Students currently attending only, as those on leave of absence are withdrawn when a programme closes
The end of the academic year in which the Academic Board approves the proposed closure
Any students currently on leave of absence and any other deferral and/or referral considerations
The date of the most recent intake plus the standard length of the programme, ignoring any deferrals
questions.explanation: The pro-forma asks for the expected final completion date considering any students on leave of absence and any other deferral and/or referral considerations.
questions.source_excerpt: What is the expected final complete date of the programme, considering any students currently on leave of absence and any other deferral and/or referral considerations?

questions.question: Several applicants have expressed interest in a programme shortly before it closes. What does the Programme Closure Pro-forma require the Programme Leader to set out for these applicants?
options: A guarantee of an automatic place on the College's nearest equivalent programme without reapplying
A list of partner providers they must apply to before the programme's final closure date
Nothing, as only applicants who have accepted an offer need to be considered at closure
A strategy and methods for ensuring they are informed about the closure in a timely manner
questions.explanation: The pro-forma requires a strategy for applicants who expressed interest before closure, covering how they will be informed in a timely manner and the methods to be used.
questions.source_excerpt: Strategy for applicants who have expressed interest in the programme prior to closure. How will you ensure that interested applicants will be informed about closure in a timely manner? What methods will be adopted to do this?

questions.question: In the Communication section of the Programme Closure Pro-forma, what is the person completing the form asked to describe?
options: The press statement to be issued to local media announcing the College's decision to close the programme
Discussions held or planned with key stakeholders, such as lecturers and continuing students
The wording of the final letter the Academic Board will send each student confirming the closure
The social media schedule marketing will use to promote a replacement programme to applicants
questions.explanation: The Communication section asks what discussions have taken place or are planned with key stakeholders, such as PEG members, lecturers, continuing students, collaborative partners and marketing, recruiting and admissions staff.
questions.source_excerpt: What discussions, if any, have already taken place or have been planned with key stakeholders: for example: Principal's Executive Group members, lecturers currently delivering on the programme, continuing students, collaborative partners and/or marketing, recruiting and admissions staff members?

questions.question: A student asks whether consumer protection law applies when LCC closes their programme. What does the Programme Closure Policy say about the College's compliance?
options: It complies fully with the Consumer Rights Act 2015, CMA-advocated practices and related OfS expectations
Consumer law does not apply, as closures are governed solely by the awarding body's own regulations
It applies consumer law to applicants only, not to students who are already enrolled on the programme
It applies consumer law only to students paying their own fees rather than those funded by a loan
questions.explanation: The Aim states that, in giving students information about programme closure, the College complies fully with the Consumer Rights Act 2015, CMA-advocated practices and related OfS expectations.
questions.source_excerpt: In this respect, the College complies fully with the Consumer Rights Act 2015, practices advocated by the Competition and Marketing Authority (CMA) and related regulations and expectations set out in the OfS Conditions.

questions.question: A programme is closing because of concerns about its quality and academic standards. A manager says the College's commitments to applicants do not apply to quality-driven closures. What does the Programme Closure Policy say?
options: The manager is right, as quality-driven closures follow the awarding body's procedures instead
The policy is triggered whatever the reason, so the needs of applicants offered a place must be met
The commitments apply only where closure results from declining student numbers or strategy changes
Applicants are covered only if they paid a deposit before the proposed closure was announced
questions.explanation: Quality concerns are one listed reason for closure, but whatever the reason the policy is triggered and the College must meet the needs of applicants already offered a place.
questions.source_excerpt: Concerns about the quality and academic standards on the programme; ... Whatever the reason for closure, the College is committed to ensuring that the needs of existing students (including suspended students), applicants who have already been offered a place, and prospective candidates are met. This Policy is triggered in all cases;

questions.question: A draft pro-forma proposes closing a programme at the end of the current term to save costs, although students are part-way through their studies. Under the Programme Closure Policy, what must the proposed timescale provide for?
options: The earliest closure date the College can achieve, keeping programme running costs to a minimum
Closure by the end of the academic year, with any remaining students transferred to other providers
An appropriate amount of time to accommodate the adjustment of any applicants or existing students
A closure date agreed by a majority vote of the students currently registered on the programme
questions.explanation: The Programme Closure Meeting considers the proposed timescale, which must allow an appropriate amount of time for any applicants or existing students to adjust.
questions.source_excerpt: Proposed time scale for closure (with an appropriate amount of time to accommodate the adjustment of any applicants or existing students);

questions.question: In the 'Reasons for closure' part of the Programme Closure Pro-forma, what must be explained in addition to the rationale for closure?
options: How the closure affects each lecturer's teaching workload
Which competitor providers offer a similar programme
Why student feedback on the programme was unfavourable
How the closure impacts the College's portfolio
questions.explanation: Alongside the rationale for closure, the pro-forma asks how the closure impacts upon the College's portfolio.
questions.source_excerpt: What is the rationale for closure? How does closure impact upon the College's portfolio?

questions.question: A manager plans to tell current students about a programme closure without consulting them, and to tell potential students nothing until advertising stops. Which statement reflects the aims of the Programme Closure Policy?
options: Telling current students is enough; only applicants who already hold offers must also be consulted
Existing and potential students must both be fully informed, consulted and supported to protect their interests
Potential students need be told about the closure only once all publicity for the programme has been fully removed
Students must be consulted only where the closure is driven by concerns about academic quality and standards
questions.explanation: The policy aims to ensure that existing or potential students are fully informed, consulted and supported to protect their interests, so neither consulting only some nor delaying information for potential students is permitted.
questions.source_excerpt: Existing or potential students are fully informed, consulted and supported to protect their interests;

questions.question: A colleague believes the Principal both proposes and approves programme closures. Under the Programme Closure Policy, which statement correctly separates the roles of the Principal and the Academic Board?
options: The Academic Board provides the formal rationale, and the Principal approves the closure
The Principal provides the formal rationale, and the Oversight Board approves the closure
The Registrar provides the formal rationale, and the Academic Board approves the closure
The Principal gives a formal rationale, and the Academic Board approves all closures
questions.explanation: A closure is considered on receipt of a formal rationale from the Principal, but all closures must be approved by the Academic Board.
questions.source_excerpt: All closures must be approved by the Academic Board; ... The Programme Closure will be considered upon receiving a formal rationale from the ... Principal;

questions.question: A member of the College's Oversight Board attended a Programme Closure Meeting and supported a closure that is not urgent. Under the Programme Closure Policy, does this amount to approval of the closure?
options: No; Oversight Board members attend only if invited, and all closures are approved by the Academic Board
Yes; an Oversight Board member's support at the meeting stands in place of Academic Board approval
Yes, provided the company director also attended the meeting and agreed to the proposed closure
No; the awarding body gives formal approval instead, once the meeting's minutes have been sent to it
questions.explanation: A member of the Oversight Board may be invited to attend but is not a de facto member, and all closures must be approved by the Academic Board, so their support at the meeting is not approval.
questions.source_excerpt: All closures must be approved by the Academic Board; ... In addition, the company director and a member of the College's Oversight Board may be invited to attend. ... Recommendations for closure will then be sent to the Academic Board for formal approval.

questions.question: Several years after a programme closed, an auditor asks what records the College should hold about the closure. Under the Programme Closure Policy, which statement is correct?
options: Closure records may be securely destroyed once the last student has completed the programme and graduated
Only closures that affected enrolled students or applicants need to be kept on permanent record
The College keeps permanent records of all closures, with meeting outcomes recorded on the pro-forma
Meeting outcomes are held only in Academic Board papers, not on the Programme Closure Pro-forma
questions.explanation: The Programme Closure Meeting is minuted with its outcomes recorded on the pro-forma, and the College maintains permanent records of all programme closures.
questions.source_excerpt: The meeting will be minuted, and the outcomes recorded on the Programme Closure Pro-forma; ... The College will maintain permanent records of all programme closures;

questions.question: After a Programme Closure Meeting, which individual signs off the decisions recorded on the Programme Closure Pro-forma, according to the Programme Closure Policy?
options: The Senior Quality Assurance Officer, who convened the meeting
The Principal, who attends the meeting as one of its de facto members
The Programme Leader, who completed and submitted the pro-forma
The Registrar, who attends the meeting as one of its de facto members
questions.explanation: Decisions are signed off by the Chair of the meeting, and the policy names the Principal as Chair of the Programme Closure Meeting; the Registrar is a de facto member but not the Chair.
questions.source_excerpt: Defacto membership will include: The Principal (as Chair), ... Decisions taken will be recorded on the Programme Closure Pro-forma and signed off by the Chair of the meeting.

questions.question: A draft invitation list for a Programme Closure Meeting names the Principal (Chair), the Registrar, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, the Programme Leader and the Senior Quality Assurance Officer. Under the Programme Closure Policy, which de facto member is missing?
options: The company director of London Churchill College
A nominated member of the College's Oversight Board
The external examiner appointed to the programme
A Recruitment and Admissions representative
questions.explanation: A Representative from the Recruitment and Admissions Department is a de facto member; the company director and an Oversight Board member may only be invited, and the external examiner is not listed.
questions.source_excerpt: Defacto membership will include: The Principal (as Chair), the Registrar, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, the Programme Leader of the programme scheduled for closure; the Senior Quality Assurance Officer and a Representative from the Recruitment and Admissions Department.

questions.question: During the teach-out of a closing programme, how does the Programme Closure Policy divide responsibility for overseeing teach-out arrangements and for ensuring the quality assurance framework is still followed?
options: Programme Leader, consulting the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, oversees teach-out; Senior QA Officer, consulting the Registrar, ensures QA
Senior QA Officer, consulting the Registrar, oversees teach-out; Programme Leader, consulting the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, ensures QA
Registrar, consulting the Programme Leader, oversees teach-out; Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, consulting the Principal, ensures QA
Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, consulting the Principal, oversees teach-out; the Registrar, consulting the awarding body, ensures QA
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader oversees teach-out in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, while the Senior Quality Assurance Officer, in consultation with the Registrar, ensures the quality assurance framework continues to be followed.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, will oversee teaching out arrangements. The Senior Quality Assurance Officer, in consultation with the Registrar, will ensure that the College's quality assurance framework and procedures continue to be followed.

questions.question: The Registrar has several roles under the Programme Closure Policy. Which of the following is not one of them?
options: Attending the Programme Closure Meeting as one of its de facto members
Being consulted by the Senior QA Officer on continued QA framework compliance
Reviewing the completed pro-forma to check its statistical data are accurate
Overseeing and monitoring the closure process with the Quality Assurance Officers
questions.explanation: Reviewing the pro-forma for correct completion and accurate statistics is the Quality Department's task; the Registrar is a de facto meeting member, is consulted on the QA framework and oversees the closure process with the QA Officers.
questions.source_excerpt: The Quality Department will review the completed Programme Closure pro-forma to ensure that all parts have been completed correctly and the statistical data provided are accurate; ... The Senior Quality Assurance Officer, in consultation with the Registrar, ... The Registrar and the Quality Assurance Officers ... will oversee and monitor the closure process

questions.question: Under the Programme Closure Policy, on which matters is the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring consulted by others during a programme closure?
options: By the Senior QA Officer on the QA framework, and by the Academic Board on formal approval of the closure
By the Principal on the formal rationale, and by the Quality Department on reviewing the pro-forma's data
By Recruitment and Admissions on publicity, and by the awarding body on the timetable for the teach-out
By the Programme Leader on teach-out, and by the Registrar and QA Officers on monitoring the closure process
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader oversees teach-out in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, and the Registrar and QA Officers monitor the closure process in consultation with the same post-holder.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, will oversee teaching out arrangements. ... The Registrar and the Quality Assurance Officers, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, will oversee and monitor the closure process

questions.question: A closing programme has continuing students who will need support to finish their studies. How does the Programme Closure Policy make sure that this support is both planned and then checked?
options: The Registrar plans the support in the pro-forma, and the Programme Leader then monitors it each term
The Programme Leader plans it on the pro-forma; the Registrar and QA Officers monitor it
The awarding body plans the support, and the Oversight Board checks it at each of its scheduled meetings
The Academic Board sets the support strategy on approval, and the Principal monitors it until completion
questions.explanation: The pro-forma, completed by the Programme Leader, sets out the strategy for supporting ongoing students, and the Registrar and Quality Assurance Officers monitor the closure to ensure sufficient support is in place.
questions.source_excerpt: (To be completed by the Programme Leader) ... Strategy for supporting ongoing students. How will you ensure that ongoing students have sufficient support to complete their studies? ... The Registrar and the Quality Assurance Officers ... will oversee and monitor the closure process to ensure ... that sufficient levels of support are in place to facilitate programme completion.

questions.question: After a programme closure is approved, the programme still appears on a third-party course-listing website and in printed leaflets held by an external partner. Under the Programme Closure Policy, what is the Programme Leader's responsibility?
options: None, as the duty covers only College publications and the College's own website
None, as external listings are the sole responsibility of the external partner itself
To liaise with recruiting and marketing staff so these external references are removed
To ask the awarding body to have them removed, as it owns all external programme listings
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader's duty extends beyond College publications and the website to external references visible on external websites or available in hard copy, which must be removed.
questions.source_excerpt: it is the responsibility of the Programme Leader to liaise with recruiting and marketing staff members to ensure all necessary amendments are made to all London Churchill College publications and the website, and that any external references to the programme publicity visible through external websites or available in hard copy have been removed.

questions.question: In a closing programme's final year, every attending student finishes, but one student on leave of absence will return next year to complete. Under the Programme Closure Policy, when may External Examiner reports and Annual Monitoring Reports stop?
options: Once all students who were attending in the final scheduled year have completed
At the end of the academic year in which the Academic Board approved the closure
Once the programme's last scheduled intake has been assessed in its final year
Only once the last student, including the one on leave, has completed the programme
questions.explanation: External Examiner reports and Annual Monitoring Reports are required until the last student has completed the programme, and the expected completion date must take account of students on leave of absence.
questions.source_excerpt: What is the expected final complete date of the programme, considering any students currently on leave of absence ... Note: External Examiner reports and Annual Monitoring Reports will be required until the last student has completed the programme.

questions.question: A programme being closed has no registered students and no applicants with accepted offers, but one of its units is shared with a continuing programme. Under the Programme Closure Policy, which statement is correct?
options: The procedure is followed, and the meeting considers arrangements for delivering the shared unit
The procedure may be waived, as no students or accepted applicants are affected by the closure
Only the continuing programme's leader needs to be told, as the closing programme has no students
The shared unit must close at once with the programme, as it has no students of its own left
questions.explanation: The procedure is followed even with no students or accepted applicants, and the Programme Closure Meeting considers arrangements for delivering units shared with other programmes.
questions.source_excerpt: Proposed arrangements for delivering units/modules shared with other programmes. ... This procedure will be followed, even in cases where no students are registered on the programme being closed, there are no applicants who have accepted offers on the course,

questions.question: To save time, a Programme Leader plans to send a completed Programme Closure Pro-forma straight to the Academic Board. Under the Programme Closure Policy, which route should the pro-forma follow instead?
options: To the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, who signs it off and sends it to the Academic Board
To the Registrar, who checks the student numbers and then forwards it to the awarding body to approve
To the Senior QA Officer for Quality Department review, then a closure meeting, then the Academic Board
To the Principal's Executive Group, which approves it and passes it to the Oversight Board to note
questions.explanation: The pro-forma goes to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer, is reviewed by the Quality Department, is considered at a Programme Closure Meeting, and only then is the recommendation sent to the Academic Board.
questions.source_excerpt: submit the completed form to the College's Senior Quality Assurance Officer; ... The Quality Department will review the completed Programme Closure pro-forma ... the Senior Quality Assurance Officer will convene a Programme Closure Meeting ... Recommendations for closure will then be sent to the Academic Board for formal approval.

questions.question: Closure of a programme is imminent and unavoidable, so Chair's Action is being sought. A manager says the urgency means the College's terms and conditions with students can be set aside. What does the Programme Closure Policy say?
options: Chair's Action allows the terms and conditions to be varied without notice to students
They may be set aside once the Academic Board is informed at its following meeting
They apply only to applicants who have not yet enrolled on the programme being closed
For each closure, the College follows its obligations and terms and conditions
questions.explanation: Chair's Action changes only how the closure is approved; for every programme closure the College must follow its obligations and terms and conditions.
questions.source_excerpt: For each Programme Closure, the College will ensure that it follows its obligations and ... terms and conditions;

questions.question: A Programme Leader hears informally that recruitment on their programme is causing concern and starts the formal closure process on their own initiative. Under the Programme Closure Policy, what should have prompted the formal process?
options: A written request from the awarding body, sent directly to the Programme Leader after its annual review
An instruction from the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, based on PEG and Directors' decisions
A vote of the Academic Board taken at its next meeting, before any discussion by PEG or the Directors
A recommendation from the Senior Quality Assurance Officer after reviewing the programme's recruitment data
questions.explanation: PEG and Directors first discuss prospects for closure, and based on their preliminary decisions the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring instructs the Programme Leader to commence the formal process.
questions.source_excerpt: Members of PEG and Directors will discuss prospects for closing a programme in the context of the College's current and changing business and academic needs. Based upon preliminary decisions taken, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring will instruct the Programme Leader to commence the formal closure process.

questions.question: Which set of tasks does the Programme Closure Policy assign to the Programme Leader of a programme that is being closed?
options: Completing the pro-forma, informing enrolled students, overseeing teach-out and arranging removal of publicity
Convening the Programme Closure Meeting, signing off its recorded decisions and giving the formal rationale
Reviewing the pro-forma's statistical data, ensuring QA procedures are followed and monitoring the closure
Discussing closure prospects with the Directors, instructing that the formal process begin and approving closure
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader completes the pro-forma, informs enrolled students, oversees teach-out and liaises with marketing staff to remove publicity; convening, sign-off, rationale, data review, QA oversight, monitoring and approval belong to others.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader will complete the Programme Closure Pro-forma ... The Programme Leader will inform students enrolled on the programme about the proposed closure ... The Programme Leader, in consultation with the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, will oversee teaching out arrangements. ... it is the responsibility of the Programme Leader to liaise with recruiting and marketing staff members

questions.question: An applicant accepted an offer on a programme but deferred entry for a year, and the programme is now closing. A colleague says the applicant need only be told of the closure in good time, like any interested applicant. Under the Programme Closure Policy, which statement is correct?
options: The teach-out plans must include arrangements for the applicant, as they cover those who have deferred entry
The colleague is right, as deferred entrants are treated as interested applicants who need only timely notice
The applicant must be referred to another provider, as teach-out plans cover only students already enrolled
The applicant is covered only if the Academic Board agrees to admit a final intake during the teach-out phase
questions.explanation: The policy states that teach-out plans will include arrangements for those who have deferred entry, and its commitment extends to applicants already offered a place, so timely notice alone is not enough.
questions.source_excerpt: the needs of existing students (including suspended students), applicants who have already been offered a place, and prospective candidates are met ... Plans will include arrangements for students who have suspended their studies, need to resubmit work or those who have deferred entry;

questions.question: PEG members and Directors reach a preliminary decision to close a programme, and the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring then instructs the Programme Leader to start the formal process. No record of PEG's decision is kept, as it is only preliminary. Under the Programme Closure Policy, which is correct?
options: Both steps comply, as formal recording is required only from the Programme Closure Meeting onwards
The instruction complies, but PEG's decision should have been formally recorded, like decisions at every stage
The instruction breaches the policy, as only the Principal may direct the Programme Leader to begin the process
The instruction breaches the policy, as the Programme Leader must wait for the Academic Board to approve closure
questions.explanation: The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring instructs the Programme Leader based on preliminary decisions, but the policy requires decisions at all stages of planning and implementation to be formally recorded.
questions.source_excerpt: Decisions taken at all stages of planning and implementation are formally recorded; ... Based upon preliminary decisions taken, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring will instruct the Programme Leader to commence the formal closure process.

questions.question: In a closure, the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring tells the Programme Leader to start; the pro-forma goes to the Senior QA Officer; the Principal chairs the closure meeting; and, although closure is not urgent, Chair's Action approves it. Under the Programme Closure Policy, which step was wrong?
options: The Principal chairing the meeting, as the Registrar chairs it and the Principal attends only if invited
Sending the pro-forma to the Senior QA Officer, as it must go to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
Using Chair's Action, as a non-urgent closure recommendation must go to the Academic Board for formal approval
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring starting it, as the Academic Board must approve closure first
questions.explanation: Chair's Action is sought only when closure is imminent and unavoidable; otherwise the recommendation is sent to the Academic Board for formal approval. The other steps follow the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Recommendations for closure will then be sent to the Academic Board for formal approval. If closure is imminent and unavoidable, Chair's Action will be sought, and the Academic Board informed at the following meeting;

questions.question: A manager lists four planned actions for closing a programme. Which of them would breach the Programme Closure Policy?
options: Holding the Programme Closure Meeting with neither the company director nor an Oversight Board member present
Seeking Chair's Action for an imminent, unavoidable closure and informing the Academic Board at its following meeting
Running the full closure procedure for a programme with no registered students and no applicants holding accepted offers
Closing the programme without informing or consulting its awarding body, as the reasons for closure are purely strategic
questions.explanation: LCC will only close programmes with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body; the other actions are allowed or required (optional attendees, Chair's Action for imminent closures, following the procedure even with no students).
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will only close Programmes with the full knowledge and consultation of the awarding body, or other accrediting bodies. ... the company director and a member of the College's Oversight Board may be invited to attend. ... This procedure will be followed, even in cases where no students are registered on the programme being closed

questions.question: A journalist contacts you asking for your comments on a College-related matter. Under the Public Information Policy, what should you do?
options: Give a brief factual response, then inform the Marketing Department afterwards
Respond using facts already published on the College website, without approval
Obtain permission first, as all such requests must go through the Chair of the PIMG
Refer the journalist directly to the Registrar, who handles all media enquiries
questions.explanation: The policy states that staff must obtain permission to contact the media or respond to requests on College matters, and all requests go through the Chair of the Public Information Management Group (PIMG).
questions.source_excerpt: Members of staff must obtain permission to contact the media or respond to requests for the College related matters. All requests are to go through the Chair of Public Information Management Group (PIMG).

questions.question: A colleague uses the College logo on a flyer without authorisation, although the flyer's content is accurate. According to the Public Information Policy, what is the position?
options: It is acceptable, since the policy's concern is limited to flyers carrying inaccurate content
Action under the policy applies to Brand Advocates, while staff misuse is left to line managers
The College accepts no liability, so no action is taken against the staff member
The College will act against any staff member using the logo without authorisation
questions.explanation: The policy states the College will act against any member of staff or Brand Advocate found using the College logo without authorisation, regardless of whether the content is accurate.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will act against any member of staff or Brand Advocate found to be using the College logo without authorisation or publishing information about the College and/or its courses that has not been approved or is inaccurate.

questions.question: You want to post an announcement about a College event on the College's social media channels. According to the Public Information Policy, who must verify or approve this information?
options: The Academic Quality Assurance Officer
The Public Information Management Group
The Principal's Executive Group
The Registrar, who reports on website changes
questions.explanation: The policy requires information disseminated through the social media platform to be verified or approved by the Public Information Management Group (PIMG).
questions.source_excerpt: Information disseminated through the Social Media Platform must be verified or approved by PIMG.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, how should the College's marketing communications be handled?
options: Issued by the Admissions team, scrutinised by the PIMG and with dissemination authorised by the Principal
Issued by the PIMG, scrutinised by the Academic Board and with dissemination authorised by the Registrar
Issued by Brand Advocates, scrutinised by MRAC and with dissemination authorised by the Marketing Manager
Issued by the Marketing Department, scrutinised by MRAC and with dissemination authorised by the PIMG
questions.explanation: Marketing communications are issued by the Marketing Department and scrutinised by the Marketing, Recruitment and Admission Committee (MRAC); their dissemination must be authorised by the PIMG.
questions.source_excerpt: All marketing communications should be issued by the Marketing Department and scrutinised by the Marketing, Recruitment and Admission Committee (MRAC). Dissemination of marketing information must be authorised by PIMG.

questions.question: You have produced a document for the public domain that is not listed in the Public Information Policy's publication table. What does the policy require?
options: Treat it as public information, reviewed by an internal reviewer authorised by the Principal
Publish it directly, as documents not listed in the table fall outside the scope of the policy
Submit it to the Academic Board for formal approval before it is placed in the public domain
Ask the Marketing Manager to review it, as unlisted material is treated as promotional content
questions.explanation: Any unlisted document produced for the public domain is to be considered public information and reviewed by an internal reviewer authorised by the Principal.
questions.source_excerpt: Any other document not listed above produced for the purpose of being placed in the public domain should be considered as public information and should be reviewed by an internal reviewer authorised by the Principal.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, which of the following is specifically listed as information that Brand Advocate communications must always state accurately?
options: Graduate employment rates for the courses
The fees for the College's courses
Student satisfaction survey results
Staff-to-student ratios on the courses
questions.explanation: The policy lists the awarding bodies, the levels and duration of courses, course fees and any other vital information as details that must always be accurate.
questions.source_excerpt: Communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy or any policy that refers to the liability of or represents the College, must always be accurate regarding: ... the awarding bodies of the courses; the levels and duration of the courses; course fees; any other vital information about the College or courses.

questions.question: You are preparing information on a course delivered in partnership with another institution. Under the Public Information Policy, how must this information be produced and approved?
options: In line with the College's own marketing guidelines, with approval from the Marketing Department
In line with the Academic Partner's regulations and the agreed Collaborative Procedures Manual (CPM)
In line with the Brand Advocate Policy, approved by the Brand Advocates promoting the course
By the partner institution under its own rules, with the College playing no part in approval
questions.explanation: Partnership course information must be produced and approved in line with the Academic Partner's regulations and the agreed Collaborative Procedures Manual, which sets out both parties' roles.
questions.source_excerpt: Information on courses that are delivered in partnership with other institutions must be produced and approved in line with the Academic Partner's regulations and the agreed Collaborative Procedures Manual (CPM) that describes the roles and responsibilities of the College and the partner.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, what liability does the College accept for unauthorised third-party communication?
options: None; the College has no liability for any unauthorised third-party communication
Full liability, since the College answers for any third-party communication made about it
Shared liability with the third party wherever the College logo is used
Liability where the unauthorised communication comes from one of its Brand Advocates
questions.explanation: The policy explicitly states that the College has no liability for any unauthorised third-party communication.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has no liability for any unauthorised third-party communication.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy, how is internal information primarily made available to College staff?
options: Through the public College website
Through termly email bulletins from the Registrar
Through the Staff VLE and Google Drive
Through the Student and Course Handbooks
questions.explanation: The policy states that internal information is made available to staff via the Staff VLE and Google Drive (and to students via the VLE).
questions.source_excerpt: Internal information is primarily made available to students via the Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) and staff via the Staff VLE and Google Drive.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy, what happens to required changes to the College website once they have been identified and agreed by the PIMG?
options: They are passed to the Marketing Department to update directly
They go to the Principal's Executive Group for final sign-off
They are held until the Registrar's yearly website report
They are forwarded to the IT department for implementation
questions.explanation: The policy states that required changes identified and agreed by the PIMG are forwarded to the IT department for implementation.
questions.source_excerpt: Required changes identified and agreed by the PIMG are forwarded to the IT department for implementation.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, who oversees regular checks to identify websites, including assignment writing services, that may be using the College's name or copyright materials without consent?
options: The Quality Assurance Officer and/or IT department
The Marketing Manager and/or Head of Student Engagement
The Senior Admissions Officer and/or Registrar
The Chair of the PIMG
questions.explanation: The policy assigns oversight of these regular checks to the Senior Admissions Officer and/or Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: The Senior Admissions Officer and/or Registrar oversees regular checks to identify websites, including assignment writing services, that may be using the College's name or copyright materials without its consent.

questions.question: As a Programme Leader, you are preparing new content to place on the Student VLE. Under the Public Information Policy's publication arrangements, who reviews this content before publication?
options: The Academic Quality Assurance Officer
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
The Head of Student Engagement
The Programme Manager
questions.explanation: The policy's publication table assigns content placed on the Student VLE to Programme Leaders, with review by the Academic Quality Assurance Officer before publication.
questions.source_excerpt: The preparation and review/authorisation of documentation, prior to publication, shall be carried out as follows: ... Document Responsible Reviewed by ... Content placed on the Student VLE Programme Leaders Academic Quality Assurance Officer

questions.question: The Public Information Policy lists the qualities London Churchill College aims for in the information it publishes. Which of the following is one of those listed qualities?
options: Externally verified
Consistently branded
Legally compliant
Independently endorsed
questions.explanation: The policy states the College aims to publish information that is accurate, fit for purpose, trustworthy, transparent and open, timely and up to date, accessible and legally compliant.
questions.source_excerpt: London Churchill College aims to publish information which is: ... Legally compliant

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, what is the primary source of the College's external information?
options: The College's website
The College prospectus
The Staff VLE and Google Drive
Official social media channels
questions.explanation: The policy states that the primary source for external information is posted on the College's website.
questions.source_excerpt: The primary source for external information is posted on the College's website.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy, information on programmes of study is made available for the benefit of candidates applying to the College through which publication?
options: The Unit Handbooks
The College prospectus
The Registrar's yearly report
The Student VLE
questions.explanation: The policy states that programme information is available through the College prospectus for candidates, and through the Course Handbooks for enrolled students.
questions.source_excerpt: Information on the programmes of study is available through the College prospectus for the benefit of candidates and in the Course Handbooks for the benefit of enrolled students.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, what does the Student Handbook inform students about?
options: The fees, awarding bodies and duration of every course on offer
The College's admission requirements and application procedures
The outcomes of the termly VLE audits and website reviews
What the College expects of them and what they can expect in return
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Student Handbook informs students what the College expects of current students and what current students can expect of the College.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Handbook informs students as to what the College expects of current students and what current students can expect of the College.

questions.question: The Public Information Policy lists sets of information that the College ensures are regularly maintained and current. Which of the following is on that list?
options: Governance and risk management
Annual financial statements
Graduate salary outcomes data
Staff research publications
questions.explanation: Governance and risk management is one of the sets of information the policy says the College keeps regularly maintained and current, alongside items such as its mission, values and strategy framework.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that the following sets of information are regularly maintained and current: ... Mission, values, and strategy framework. Governance and risk management.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, what is the College's commitment on providing information in accessible formats?
options: Accessible formats are offered for marketing materials only, via MRAC
Accessible formats are provided to enrolled students, not to applicants
All information will be provided in accessible formats on request
Accessible formats need written approval from the Chair of the PIMG
questions.explanation: The policy commits the College to providing all information in accessible formats on request to meet the needs of individuals.
questions.source_excerpt: All information will be provided in accessible formats on request to meet the needs of individuals.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, which body is the only one that can authorise any form of public document?
options: The Senior Admissions Officer
The Public Information Management Group
The Marketing, Recruitment and Admission Committee
The Registrar
questions.explanation: The policy states that any form of public document can only be authorised by the Public Information Management Group (PIMG).
questions.source_excerpt: Any form of public document can only be authorised by PIMG.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, what is the purpose of the College's working agreement with selected Brand Advocates?
options: To answer media requests about College matters
To check websites for misuse of the College's name and logo
To review the prospectus before it is published
To promote awareness of the College and its courses
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College has a working agreement with selected Brand Advocates to promote awareness of itself and its courses.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has a working agreement with selected Brand Advocates to promote awareness of itself and its courses.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, what is the Public Information Management Group (PIMG) responsible for in relation to College publications?
options: Managing the placement and removal of all College publications
Drafting every Course Handbook and Unit Handbook itself
Implementing agreed changes directly on the College website
Producing the yearly report on changes made to the website
questions.explanation: The policy makes the PIMG responsible for managing the placement and removal of all publications, including handbooks, the prospectus, websites, social media and advertisements.
questions.source_excerpt: The PIMG is responsible for managing the placement and removal of all publications, including Student Handbook, Course Handbooks, prospectus, websites, social media, and advertisements.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy's publication arrangements, who reviews the College's Policies and Procedures before they are published?
options: The Academic Quality Assurance Officer
The Head of Student Engagement
The Principal's Executive Group
The Programme Manager
questions.explanation: The publication table assigns Policies and Procedures to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer, with review by the Principal's Executive Group.
questions.source_excerpt: Document ... Responsible ... Reviewed by ... Policies and Procedures ... Senior Quality Principal's Executive Group Assurance Officer

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy's publication arrangements, who is responsible for preparing materials published on the College's websites and social media sites?
options: The Senior Quality Assurance Officer
The Head of Student Engagement
The Registrar
The Marketing Manager
questions.explanation: The publication table makes the Head of Student Engagement responsible for materials on websites and social media sites, with review by the Public Information Management Group.
questions.source_excerpt: All materials published on Websites Head of Student Public Information Management Group ... and Social Media sites ... Engagement

questions.question: A Unit Tutor has prepared a Unit Handbook. Under the Public Information Policy's publication arrangements, who reviews it before it is published?
options: The Programme Leader
The Registrar
The Head of Student Engagement
The Programme Manager
questions.explanation: The publication table assigns the Unit Handbook to the Unit Tutor, with review by the Programme Manager.
questions.source_excerpt: Unit Handbook ... Unit Tutor ... Programme Manager

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, how often does the Public Information Management Group (PIMG) meet?
options: A minimum of three times per year
A minimum of twice per year
A minimum of four times per year
A minimum of six times per year
questions.explanation: The policy states that the PIMG meets a minimum of three times per year and oversees all public information.
questions.source_excerpt: The Public Information Management Group (PIMG) meets a minimum of three times per year and oversees all public information.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, who completes the termly VLE audits that are received by the Public Information Management Group?
options: The Registrar
The IT department
The Quality Assurance Officer
The Head of Student Engagement
questions.explanation: The policy states that the PIMG receives termly VLE audits completed by the Quality Assurance Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: It is responsible for reviewing the College website and receiving termly VLE audits completed by the Quality Assurance Officer.

questions.question: According to the Public Information Policy, who produces the yearly report on changes made to the College website?
options: The Chair of PIMG
The Registrar
The IT department
The QA Officer
questions.explanation: The policy states that a yearly report on changes made to the website is produced by the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: A yearly report is produced by the Registrar on changes made to the website.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy, what will the College do if an organisation with which it has no relationship is found using the College's name or logo to promote its services to LCC students?
options: Invite it to join the Brand Advocate arrangement
Note it in the Registrar's yearly website report
Ask it to add a disclaimer to its materials
Take action against the organisation concerned
questions.explanation: The policy states the College will act against any organisation or individual with no relationship to it that uses the College's name, logo or other intellectual property to promote its services to students or prospective students.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will act against any organisation or individual, with whom the College has no relationship, found to be using the College's name, logo, or any other intellectual property of the College to promote its services to London Churchill College's students or prospective students.

questions.question: A colleague assumes the Public Information Policy applies only at the moment material is published. According to the policy's aim, which processes does it actually govern?
options: Commissioning, drafting, translating, printing and archiving the College's marketing materials
Recruiting, briefing, monitoring and removing the Brand Advocates who promote the College
Identifying, formulating, authorising, publishing and managing information about the College
Auditing, benchmarking and reporting on information that other providers publish about themselves
questions.explanation: The policy's aim covers the whole life cycle of public information: identifying, formulating, authorising, publishing and managing information about the College placed in the public domain.
questions.source_excerpt: This includes governing the processes involved in identifying, formulating authorising, publishing, and managing information about the College that is placed within the public domain.

questions.question: A newly enrolled student asks where the College primarily makes internal information available to its students. Under the Public Information Policy, what should you tell them?
options: On the College's website, where internal notices for students are mainly posted
On the Staff VLE and Google Drive, which hold internal information for everyone
On the Virtual Learning Environment (VLE), the main route for students
In the College prospectus, which is given to every student when they enrol
questions.explanation: The policy states that internal information is primarily made available to students via the VLE; the Staff VLE and Google Drive serve staff, and the website is the primary source of external information.
questions.source_excerpt: The primary source for external information is posted on the College's website. ... Internal information is primarily made available to students via the Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) and staff via the Staff VLE and Google Drive.
