questions.question: An enrolled student asks where to find detailed information on their programme of study. Under the Public Information Policy, which publication provides this for enrolled students, as distinct from candidates?
options: The College prospectus
The Registrar's yearly report
The Student Handbook
The Course Handbooks
questions.explanation: Programme information is provided through the prospectus for candidates and through the Course Handbooks for enrolled students; the Student Handbook covers what the College and students expect of each other.
questions.source_excerpt: Information on the programmes of study is available through the College prospectus for the benefit of candidates and in the Course Handbooks for the benefit of enrolled students.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy, which collaborative activity must the College keep quality assurance and enhancement records for, as part of its framework for managing academic standards?
options: Collaborative activity carried out informally, before any agreement is signed
All collaborative activity that is subject to a formal agreement
Collaborative activity above a value threshold set by the Principal's Executive Group
Collaborative activity that the Marketing, Recruitment and Admission Committee approves
questions.explanation: The policy states the College maintains quality assurance and enhancement records, by type and category, of all collaborative activity that is subject to a formal agreement.
questions.source_excerpt: The College robustly maintains the framework for managing academic standards and quality assurance and enhancement records (by type and category) of all collaborative activity that is subject to a formal agreement.

questions.question: A member of staff drafts a communication on the College's behalf; it is not written by a Brand Advocate. Under the Public Information Policy, does the accuracy requirement that governs Brand Advocate communication also apply to it?
options: No; that requirement covers communication by Brand Advocates only
No; staff communication is checked only through the termly VLE audits
Only where MRAC has scrutinised the communication before release
Yes; it covers communication under any policy that represents the College
questions.explanation: The accuracy requirement applies to communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy or by any policy that refers to the liability of, or represents, the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy or any policy that refers to the liability of or represents the College, must always be accurate regarding: ... the awarding bodies of the courses; the levels and duration of the courses; course fees

questions.question: A Brand Advocate's post tells applicants that a College course is pitched higher and runs for less time than it really does. Under the Public Information Policy, which requirement has the post breached?
options: That Brand Advocates post only after the Registrar's yearly review
That communication is always accurate about course levels and duration
That Brand Advocates show the College logo on every promotional post
That Brand Advocates mention only course fees and the awarding bodies
questions.explanation: Communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy must always be accurate about the levels and duration of the courses, among other vital details.
questions.source_excerpt: Brand Advocates operate in accordance with the Brand Advocate Policy; ... Communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy or any policy that refers to the liability of or represents the College, must always be accurate regarding: ... the levels and duration of the courses;

questions.question: As a Programme Leader, you have updated your Programme Handbook. Under the Public Information Policy's publication arrangements, who reviews it before it is published?
options: The Academic Quality Assurance Officer
The Programme Manager for the relevant programme
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
The Principal's Executive Group
questions.explanation: The publication table makes the Programme Leader responsible for Programme Handbooks, with review by the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring.
questions.source_excerpt: Programme Handbooks ... Programme Leader Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring

questions.question: Your team is producing a promotional leaflet for a new course. Under the Public Information Policy's publication arrangements, who is responsible for preparing it and who reviews it?
options: The Head of Student Engagement prepares it; the Principal's Executive Group reviews it
The Programme Leader prepares it; the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring reviews it
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer prepares it; the Programme Manager reviews it
The Marketing Manager prepares it; the Public Information Management Group reviews it
questions.explanation: The publication table assigns advertisements, leaflets and other promotional material to the Marketing Manager, with review by the Public Information Management Group.
questions.source_excerpt: Advertisement/Leaflet or any Marketing ... promotional material ... Manager ... Public Information Management Group

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy's publication arrangements, which type of document is the Senior Quality Assurance Officer responsible for preparing before it goes for review?
options: Policies and Procedures
Programme Handbooks
Content on the Student VLE
Advertisements and leaflets
questions.explanation: The publication table makes the Senior Quality Assurance Officer responsible for Policies and Procedures, which are then reviewed by the Principal's Executive Group.
questions.source_excerpt: Policies and Procedures ... Senior Quality Principal's Executive Group Assurance Officer

questions.question: The College prospectus contains out-of-date information and must be withdrawn from circulation. Under the Public Information Policy, which body is responsible for its removal?
options: The Marketing, Recruitment and Admission Committee
The Public Information Management Group
The Registrar's office
The Principal's Executive Group
questions.explanation: The PIMG is responsible for managing the placement and removal of all publications, including the prospectus, handbooks, websites, social media and advertisements.
questions.source_excerpt: The PIMG is responsible for managing the placement and removal of all publications, including Student Handbook, Course Handbooks, prospectus, websites, social media, and advertisements.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy, which sequence correctly describes how required changes to the College website are agreed, implemented and then reported?
options: IT identifies the change, the Registrar agrees it, and the PIMG reports on it each year
The Registrar identifies and makes the change, and the PIMG reviews it each term
The PIMG identifies and agrees it, IT implements it, and the Registrar reports yearly
Marketing makes the change, and the QA Officer records it in the next termly audit
questions.explanation: Changes identified and agreed by the PIMG are forwarded to the IT department for implementation, and the Registrar produces a yearly report on changes made to the website.
questions.source_excerpt: Required changes identified and agreed by the PIMG are forwarded to the IT department for implementation. A yearly report is produced by the Registrar on changes made to the website.

questions.question: A Brand Advocate publishes accurate information about a College course that has not been approved. Under the Public Information Policy, what is the position?
options: No action follows, because the policy is concerned only with inaccurate information
The College will act, as unapproved information is covered even if it is accurate
The College has no liability, so the matter falls outside the policy altogether
No action follows, as the misuse provisions apply to members of staff only
questions.explanation: The College will act against any staff member or Brand Advocate publishing information about the College or its courses that has not been approved or is inaccurate, so unapproved information is covered even when accurate.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will act against any member of staff or Brand Advocate found to be using the College logo without authorisation or publishing information about the College and/or its courses that has not been approved or is inaccurate.

questions.question: The Head of Student Engagement has prepared a post for the College's social media and intends to publish it immediately, as the officer responsible for such material. Under the Public Information Policy, is this permitted?
options: Yes; for social media, the responsible officer's own sign-off completes the approval
No; it must first be scrutinised by MRAC, which reviews every College social media post
Yes, provided the Registrar logs the post in the yearly report on changes to the website
No; the PIMG must review it and verify or approve it before it is disseminated
questions.explanation: The publication table makes the Head of Student Engagement responsible for website and social media material but assigns its review to the PIMG, and anything disseminated through social media must be verified or approved by the PIMG.
questions.source_excerpt: Information disseminated through the Social Media Platform must be verified or approved by PIMG. ... All materials published on Websites Head of Student Public Information Management Group ... and Social Media sites ... Engagement

questions.question: Programme Leaders appear in more than one row of the Public Information Policy's publication table. Which two types of material are Programme Leaders responsible for preparing?
options: Content placed on the Student VLE, and Programme Handbooks
Unit Handbooks, and the Programme Handbooks for their programme
Policies and Procedures, and content placed on the Student VLE
Programme Handbooks, and materials on the College's website
questions.explanation: The publication table makes Programme Leaders responsible for content placed on the Student VLE and for Programme Handbooks; Unit Handbooks belong to Unit Tutors and Policies and Procedures to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: Content placed on the Student VLE ... Programme Leaders ... Programme Handbooks ... Programme Leader Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring

questions.question: A Unit Tutor drafts a Programme Handbook and sends it to the Programme Manager for review before publication. Under the Public Information Policy's publication arrangements, what should have happened instead?
options: Nothing different; Unit Tutors prepare all handbooks and Programme Managers review them
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer should prepare it and the Principal's Executive Group review it
The Programme Leader should prepare it and the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring review it
The Unit Tutor may prepare it, but the Academic Quality Assurance Officer must review it
questions.explanation: The Unit Tutor and Programme Manager pairing applies to Unit Handbooks; Programme Handbooks are the Programme Leader's responsibility and are reviewed by the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring.
questions.source_excerpt: Programme Handbooks ... Programme Leader Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring ... Unit Handbook ... Unit Tutor ... Programme Manager

questions.question: A Programme Leader wants to email a promotional message about their programme directly to prospective students. Under the Public Information Policy, how must this marketing communication be handled?
options: Sent by the Programme Leader after review by the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
Issued by the Marketing Department after approval by the Academic Quality Assurance Officer
Sent by the Programme Leader once the Chair of the PIMG has given permission to make contact
Issued by the Marketing Department, scrutinised by MRAC, with dissemination authorised by PIMG
questions.explanation: All marketing communications are to be issued by the Marketing Department and scrutinised by MRAC, with dissemination authorised by the PIMG, whoever originates the idea.
questions.source_excerpt: All marketing communications should be issued by the Marketing Department and scrutinised by the Marketing, Recruitment and Admission Committee (MRAC). Dissemination of marketing information must be authorised by PIMG.

questions.question: In the Public Information Policy's publication table, the Public Information Management Group is the reviewer for two types of material. Which two?
options: Policies and Procedures, and the Programme Handbooks prepared by Programme Leaders
Website and social media materials, and advertisements, leaflets or other marketing material
Content placed on the Student VLE, and the Unit Handbooks prepared by Unit Tutors
Programme Handbooks, and all materials published on the College's websites and social media sites
questions.explanation: The PIMG reviews materials published on websites and social media sites and advertisements, leaflets or other marketing promotional material; the other document types have different reviewers.
questions.source_excerpt: All materials published on Websites Head of Student Public Information Management Group ... and Social Media sites ... Advertisement/Leaflet or any Marketing ... promotional material ... Manager ... Public Information Management Group

questions.question: A department has produced a guide for the public that is not listed in the Public Information Policy's publication table. How should its review, and its authorisation as a public document, be handled?
options: Reviewed by an internal reviewer authorised by the Principal, and authorised only by the PIMG
Reviewed by the PIMG, and then authorised for publication by the Principal personally
Reviewed by MRAC as promotional content, and then authorised for release by the Marketing Department
Reviewed by the Principal's Executive Group, and then authorised by the Registrar
questions.explanation: An unlisted document for the public domain is treated as public information and reviewed by an internal reviewer authorised by the Principal, while any form of public document can only be authorised by the PIMG.
questions.source_excerpt: Any form of public document can only be authorised by PIMG. ... Any other document not listed above produced for the purpose of being placed in the public domain should be considered as public information and should be reviewed by an internal reviewer authorised by the Principal.

questions.question: A private tutor with no connection to the College uses its copyright course materials, but not its name or logo, to advertise tutoring to LCC students. Under the Public Information Policy, what is the position?
options: The College will act, as the policy covers any other intellectual property of the College
The College will act only if the tutor also uses its name or logo in the advert
No action follows, as the College has no liability for unauthorised third-party communication
No action follows, as that provision applies to organisations and not to private individuals
questions.explanation: The College will act against any organisation or individual with no relationship to it that uses its name, logo or any other intellectual property to promote services to its students; having no liability for such communication does not prevent action.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will act against any organisation or individual, with whom the College has no relationship, found to be using the College's name, logo, or any other intellectual property of the College to promote its services to London Churchill College's students or prospective students.

questions.question: A Brand Advocate working under an agreement with the College uses its logo without authorisation. A colleague says the College cannot act, as it acts only against parties with no relationship to it. Under the Public Information Policy, is the colleague right?
options: Yes; a Brand Advocate's misuse is dealt with solely under the Brand Advocate Policy
Yes; the College accepts no liability for any communication issued by a third party about it
No; the College will act against any staff member or Brand Advocate misusing the logo
No; Brand Advocates are treated as parties with no relationship to the College
questions.explanation: Action against unconnected organisations and individuals is a separate provision; the policy also states the College will act against any member of staff or Brand Advocate using the College logo without authorisation.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will act against any member of staff or Brand Advocate found to be using the College logo without authorisation ... The College will act against any organisation or individual, with whom the College has no relationship,

questions.question: A Brand Advocate says the Public Information Policy requires their posts to be accurate only about awarding bodies, course levels, duration and fees. What is the correct position?
options: They are right; the policy's accuracy requirement is limited to exactly those four items
Accuracy is also required on any other vital information about the College or courses
Accuracy on those items is required only in posts that quote the fee for a particular course
Those items bind staff only; Brand Advocates follow the CPM on matters of accuracy instead
questions.explanation: Besides awarding bodies, levels, duration and fees, communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy must always be accurate on any other vital information about the College or courses.
questions.source_excerpt: Communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy or any policy that refers to the liability of or represents the College, must always be accurate regarding: ... the awarding bodies of the courses; the levels and duration of the courses; course fees; any other vital information about the College or courses.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy, which pair of responsibilities involves the Registrar?
options: Completing the termly VLE audits, and implementing agreed changes to the College website
Preparing Policies and Procedures, and issuing the College's marketing communications
Reviewing the Unit Handbooks, and preparing material for the College's social media sites
Producing the yearly website-change report, and overseeing checks for misuse of the College name
questions.explanation: The Registrar produces the yearly report on website changes and, with or instead of the Senior Admissions Officer, oversees regular checks for websites using the College's name or copyright materials without consent.
questions.source_excerpt: A yearly report is produced by the Registrar on changes made to the website. ... The Senior Admissions Officer and/or Registrar oversees regular checks to identify websites, including assignment writing services, that may be using the College's name or copyright materials without its consent.

questions.question: Under the Public Information Policy, content on the Student VLE is reviewed before publication and audited afterwards. Which pairing of these checks is correct?
options: Before: review by the PIMG; afterwards: the Registrar's yearly report on changes made
Before: review by the Academic QA Officer; afterwards: termly VLE audits received by the PIMG
Before: review by the Programme Manager; afterwards: termly audits carried out by the IT department
Before: review by the Head of Student Engagement; afterwards: the PIMG's website review
questions.explanation: The publication table assigns review of Student VLE content to the Academic Quality Assurance Officer, and the PIMG receives termly VLE audits completed by the Quality Assurance Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: Content placed on the Student VLE ... Programme Leaders ... Academic Quality Assurance Officer ... It is responsible for reviewing the College website and receiving termly VLE audits completed by the Quality Assurance Officer.

questions.question: The College has a working agreement with Brand Advocates and also delivers some courses with partner institutions. Under the Public Information Policy, which frameworks govern each?
options: Brand Advocates: the Brand Advocate Policy; partner course information: partner regulations and the CPM
Both follow the Collaborative Procedures Manual, which sets out the roles of the College and partners
Brand Advocates: the CPM; partner course information: the Brand Advocate Policy and partner rules
Both follow the Brand Advocate Policy, as it covers anyone who represents the College externally
questions.explanation: Brand Advocates operate in accordance with the Brand Advocate Policy, whereas information on partnership courses follows the Academic Partner's regulations and the agreed Collaborative Procedures Manual.
questions.source_excerpt: Brand Advocates operate in accordance with the Brand Advocate Policy; ... Information on courses that are delivered in partnership with other institutions must be produced and approved in line with the Academic Partner's regulations and the agreed Collaborative Procedures Manual (CPM)

questions.question: The College website still lists a campus facility that closed last year, and an applicant relied on it when deciding to apply. Which commitment in the Public Information Policy has the College failed to meet?
options: Keeping its application requirements and admission procedures current
Keeping its mission, values and strategy framework regularly maintained
Keeping governance and risk management information regularly maintained
Keeping information on the College's location and facilities current
questions.explanation: Among the sets of information the College ensures are regularly maintained and current is information on its location and the facilities available; the other items on that list are unaffected by an outdated facility listing.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that the following sets of information are regularly maintained and current: ... relevant information regarding the location of and the facilities available at the College.

questions.question: This year the Public Information Management Group met three times but received no VLE audits from the Quality Assurance Officer. Under the Public Information Policy, what is the position?
options: The meeting minimum is met, but the PIMG should be receiving termly VLE audits
The meeting minimum is missed, but audits go only to the Registrar
Neither requirement is met, as the PIMG must meet at least four times a year
Both requirements are met, as the VLE audits are carried out only once a year
questions.explanation: Three meetings satisfies the PIMG's minimum of three per year, but the PIMG is also responsible for receiving termly VLE audits completed by the Quality Assurance Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: The Public Information Management Group (PIMG) meets a minimum of three times per year and oversees all public information. It is responsible for reviewing the College website and receiving termly VLE audits completed by the Quality Assurance Officer.

questions.question: The PIMG identifies an out-of-date page on the College website, prepared by the Head of Student Engagement, and agrees the change required. Under the Public Information Policy, who implements the change?
options: The Head of Student Engagement, as the officer responsible for website material
The Registrar, who produces the yearly report on changes made to the website
The IT department, to which the PIMG forwards required changes for implementation
The Marketing Department, which issues the College's marketing communications
questions.explanation: Although the Head of Student Engagement is responsible for preparing website material, required changes identified and agreed by the PIMG are forwarded to the IT department for implementation.
questions.source_excerpt: All materials published on Websites Head of Student Public Information Management Group ... Required changes identified and agreed by the PIMG are forwarded to the IT department for implementation.

questions.question: A colleague says the Public Information Policy's rule for documents not listed in its publication table applies to every unlisted document, including internal staff guidance shared only on the Staff VLE. Is the colleague right?
options: Yes; every unlisted document is treated as public information, wherever it is shared
No; the rule covers unlisted documents produced to be placed in the public domain
Yes; the policy treats the Staff VLE as forming part of the College's public website
No; the rule covers only marketing material that MRAC has scrutinised before release
questions.explanation: The rule applies to other unlisted documents produced for the purpose of being placed in the public domain; internal information for staff is made available via the Staff VLE and Google Drive instead.
questions.source_excerpt: Any other document not listed above produced for the purpose of being placed in the public domain should be considered as public information ... Internal information is primarily made available to students via the Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) and staff via the Staff VLE and Google Drive.

questions.question: You want to contact a local newspaper yourself to suggest a story about a student's achievement at the College. Under the Public Information Policy, what must you do before making contact?
options: Nothing, as the permission rule applies only to replying to requests from the media
Obtain permission first, with the request going via the Chair of the PIMG
Get sign-off from the Registrar, who logs all media contact in a yearly report
Tell the Head of Student Engagement once the story has gone to the newspaper
questions.explanation: Staff need permission to contact the media, not only to respond to media requests, and all such requests go through the Chair of the PIMG.
questions.source_excerpt: Members of staff must obtain permission to contact the media or respond to requests for the College related matters. All requests are to go through the Chair of Public Information Management Group (PIMG).

questions.question: The Marketing Department has issued a new recruitment campaign and MRAC has scrutinised it. Under the Public Information Policy, what is still required before the campaign is disseminated?
options: Review by the Principal's Executive Group before the campaign is released
Nothing further, as MRAC's scrutiny is the final approval for marketing material
Sign-off from the Registrar, who reports on the changes made to the website
Authorisation of its dissemination by the Public Information Management Group (PIMG)
questions.explanation: Marketing communications are issued by the Marketing Department and scrutinised by MRAC, but their dissemination must still be authorised by the PIMG.
questions.source_excerpt: All marketing communications should be issued by the Marketing Department and scrutinised by the Marketing, Recruitment and Admission Committee (MRAC). Dissemination of marketing information must be authorised by PIMG.

questions.question: Someone with no connection to the College posts incorrect LCC course fees on an online forum. A colleague says the College is liable for the post. Under the Public Information Policy, is the colleague right?
options: Yes; the College is liable for any statement published about its course fees
Yes; the fee accuracy rule for Brand Advocates applies to all members of the public
No; the College has no liability for unauthorised third-party communication
No; the College is liable only where such a post also uses the College logo
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College has no liability for any unauthorised third-party communication; the fee accuracy rule applies to communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy or policies that represent the College.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has no liability for any unauthorised third-party communication.

questions.question: A lecturer reposts a course flyer that was approved last year, but the fees shown in it are now out of date. Under the Public Information Policy's provisions on misuse of College information, what is the position?
options: No action follows, as material that was approved is protected from misuse action
The College will act only if the lecturer also used the College logo without authorisation
The College will act, as publishing inaccurate information is covered even if it was approved
No action follows, as the provisions on inaccurate information cover Brand Advocates only
questions.explanation: The College will act against staff publishing information that has not been approved or is inaccurate; either condition is enough, so earlier approval does not protect out-of-date content.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will act against any member of staff or Brand Advocate found to be using the College logo without authorisation or publishing information about the College and/or its courses that has not been approved or is inaccurate.

questions.question: A Brand Advocate is drafting a post that shows the College logo and quotes course fees. Under the Public Information Policy, which combination of requirements applies to the post?
options: Use of the logo must be authorised, and the course fees quoted must be accurate
Brand Advocates may use the logo freely, but the course fees quoted must be accurate
Use of the logo must be authorised, but fee accuracy binds staff, not Brand Advocates
Neither, as Brand Advocates are third parties for whom the College has no liability
questions.explanation: The College will act against a Brand Advocate using the logo without authorisation, and communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy must always be accurate about course fees.
questions.source_excerpt: Communication governed by the Brand Advocate Policy or any policy that refers to the liability of or represents the College, must always be accurate regarding: ... course fees; ... The College will act against any member of staff or Brand Advocate found to be using the College logo without authorisation

questions.question: Your department runs a course with a partner institution under a formal agreement. Under the Public Information Policy, which pair of requirements applies to this collaborative activity?
options: Records are kept by the partner institution alone, and course information follows the Brand Advocate Policy
The College keeps QA and enhancement records, and course information follows partner rules and the CPM
Records are optional for formally agreed activity, and course information is approved by MRAC alone
No records are needed once it is agreed, and course information is approved by the PIMG alone
questions.explanation: The College maintains quality assurance and enhancement records for all collaborative activity subject to a formal agreement, and partnership course information must follow the Academic Partner's regulations and the agreed CPM.
questions.source_excerpt: The College robustly maintains the framework for managing academic standards and quality assurance and enhancement records (by type and category) of all collaborative activity that is subject to a formal agreement. ... must be produced and approved in line with the Academic Partner's regulations and the agreed Collaborative Procedures Manual (CPM)

questions.question: Four colleagues each describe how some College material was handled. Under the Public Information Policy, which of these would be a breach of the policy?
options: A document for the public was authorised for release by MRAC instead of by the PIMG
A Unit Handbook prepared by a Unit Tutor was reviewed by the Programme Manager
Student VLE content prepared by a Programme Leader was reviewed by the Academic QA Officer
A website change agreed by the PIMG was forwarded to the IT department to implement
questions.explanation: Any form of public document can only be authorised by the PIMG; the other three follow the publication table and the website monitoring arrangements.
questions.source_excerpt: Any form of public document can only be authorised by PIMG.

questions.question: A student who has just submitted an assignment asks you when they will receive their summative feedback. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what timeframe applies?
options: Within two weeks of submission
Within six weeks of submission
After the Assessment and Progression Board meets at the end of term
Within four weeks of submission
questions.explanation: The Manual's academic feedback section states that students receive accurate and useful summative feedback within four weeks of submission.
questions.source_excerpt: Students receive accurate and useful summative feedback on their assessments within four weeks of assessments of submission.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, which four key stages make up the College's Quality Cycle?
options: Plan, Do, Check and Act
Design, Deliver, Assess and Report
Plan, Deliver, Review and Evaluate
Plan, Implement, Audit and Approve
questions.explanation: The Manual states that the key stages of the College's Quality Cycle are Plan, Deliver, Review and Evaluate, with evaluation feeding into the next planning stage to close the loop.
questions.source_excerpt: Figures 1 and 2 reflect the key stages of the College's Quality Cycle and the documentation required to Plan, Deliver, Review and Evaluate.

questions.question: You have written a new assignment brief and plan to release it to students tomorrow. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what must happen before it is released?
options: It must be approved by the Academic Board at its next meeting before students can see it
It must be checked to confirm it has enough information for students to complete the tasks
It must be signed off by the external examiner to confirm it meets national standards for the unit
It must be reviewed and approved by the elected student representatives for the course
questions.explanation: Tutors must ensure every assignment brief is checked before release so that it contains sufficient information for students to carry out the tasks and demonstrate mastery of the assessment criteria.
questions.source_excerpt: Tutors must ensure that before any assignment brief is released to students, it should be checked to ensure that it contains sufficient information to enable them to carry out the defined tasks and produce evidence to demonstrate mastery of the assessment criteria.

questions.question: A tutor wants to display students' marked work on the classroom wall. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, which approach is acceptable?
options: Display the work with each student's grade so that peers can compare their results
Display the work to celebrate cohort achievement without disclosing individual grades
Display the highest-graded work, labelled with the grade each student was awarded
Do not display it, as showing students' work in the classroom is not permitted
questions.explanation: Tutors may display students' work in the classroom to celebrate cohort achievement, but the Manual states that individual student grades should not be disclosed in public.
questions.source_excerpt: Additionally, tutors can display students' work in the classroom. The purpose of the display is to celebrate cohort achievement. Individual student grades should not be disclosed in public.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, whose responsibility is the oversight of institutional quality at the College?
options: All members of the College, with oversight being management-led
The Quality Assurance team, working independently of management
The external examiners, reporting directly to the College's awarding bodies
The Office for Students, as the regulator the College is registered with
questions.explanation: The Manual states that oversight of institutional quality is the responsibility of all members of the College and is management-led.
questions.source_excerpt: Oversight of institutional quality is the responsibility of all members of the College and is management-led.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how often must every tutor be reviewed under the College's Teaching Observation plan?
options: At least once during the academic year
At least once in every term of the year
At least once every two academic years
When student feedback raises a concern about their teaching
questions.explanation: At the planning stage a Teaching Observation plan is set which ensures that all tutors are reviewed at least once during the academic year.
questions.source_excerpt: A plan for Teaching Observations is set, which ensures that all tutors are reviewed at least once during the academic year

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what is the internal verification (IV) of assessment decisions concerned with?
options: A second tutor independently re-marking the scripts to agree a final mark with the assessor
Confirming that students' attendance met the College benchmark for the unit
The accuracy and reliability of assessor judgements across the programme
Replacing the external examiner's oversight of assignment marks and cohort statistics
questions.explanation: The Manual states that IV of assessment decisions is not the same as double marking of student work; it is concerned with the accuracy and reliability of assessor judgements across the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Internal verification of assessment decision is not the same as double marking of student work. Internal verification is concerned with the accuracy and reliability of assessor judgements across the programme.

questions.question: Your department needs to revise one of its existing policies. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what is the correct route for the revised draft?
options: Written by the Quality Assurance team, then published on the College website once the Principal has signed it
Produced by the departmental Head, reviewed by the Registrar, then sent directly to the Board of Directors for approval
Produced by the departmental Head, reviewed by the QA team, scrutinised by QESC, then submitted to Academic Board
Drafted by student representatives in SEG, scrutinised by the Programme Committee Meeting, then approved by PEG
questions.explanation: Policies, new or revised, are produced by the relevant departmental Heads, reviewed by the Quality Assurance team and scrutinised by QESC before final submission to the Academic Board.
questions.source_excerpt: Policies are produced by the relevant departmental Heads and are reviewed by the Quality Assurance team and scrutinised by the QESC prior to final submission to Academic Board; ... This applies to policies, whether they are new or revisions of pre-existing policies.

questions.question: You want to give one student individual feedback in front of the whole class. According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what type of feedback may be given this way?
options: Only feedback that is positive about the student's work
Feedback that corrects the student's most serious mistakes
Any feedback, as long as it is also given in writing
Only feedback the internal verifier has agreed in advance
questions.explanation: The Manual lists different methods of giving individual feedback and specifies that feedback given in front of the class is positive feedback only.
questions.source_excerpt: Different methods of providing individual feedback - sometimes privately, sometimes in front of the class (positive feedback only), sometimes written, sometimes verbal

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what are the two components of internal verification at London Churchill College?
options: IV of assessment papers, and IV of assessment decisions and summative feedback
IV of lecture slides and handbooks, and IV of student attendance and retention records
IV of admissions interviews and English tests, and IV of assessment decisions
IV of assessment papers, and IV of external examiner and awarding body reports
questions.explanation: The Manual defines internal verification as having two components: IV of assessment papers, and IV of assessment decisions and summative feedback.
questions.source_excerpt: Internal verification has two components: internal verification of assessment papers and internal verification of assessment decisions and summative feedback.

questions.question: You are a Course Coordinator preparing for the next term. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, by when should programme handbooks be produced and the VLE updated?
options: At least 1 week before the start of term
At least 1 month before the start of term
By the end of the first week of term
Within four weeks after the start of term
questions.explanation: Activity D 04 requires programme handbooks to be produced and the VLE updated at least one month prior to the start of term, approved by HoPAM.
questions.source_excerpt: D 04: Programme handbooks produced and VLE updated for start of next teaching block/term at least 1 month prior to start of term. To be approved by HoPAM.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what must the marking sheet provided with each piece of assessment identify, for transparency?
options: The name of the internal verifier who will sample the marking, and the date the sample is due
The student's marks from earlier assessments on the programme and their current overall grade
The average grade achieved by the previous cohort on the same unit, for comparison purposes
The learning outcomes being assessed and the performance needed for each level of the marking range
questions.explanation: For transparency, the marking sheet identifies which learning outcomes are being assessed and the performance necessary to achieve each level of the marking range.
questions.source_excerpt: As students undertake each piece of assessment, a marking sheet is provided identifying which learning outcomes are being assessed and the performance necessary to achieve each level of the marking range, for transparency

questions.question: As an internal verifier, you are planning the sample for a newly appointed, inexperienced assessor. Under the IV Sampling Plan in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what is the minimum sample?
options: A minimum of 2 students in total, regardless of grade band
5% in each grade band or 3 students, whichever is lower
A 25% sample of the assessor's marked work for that term
10% in each grade band or 6 students, whichever is higher
questions.explanation: The IV Sampling Plan requires a minimum sample of 10% in each grade band or 6 students, whichever is higher, for new or inexperienced assessors (a minimum of 2 students applies only to experienced assessors).
questions.source_excerpt: For new/inexperienced assessors: minimum 10% sample in each grade band or 6 students (whichever is higher)

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, Course Coordinators produce the Programme Annual Monitoring Report (PAMR). When should the PAMR normally be completed?
options: In December of the same calendar year in which the programme is completed
In October of the same calendar year in which the programme is completed
In July, at the end of the academic year in which the programme is completed
In January of the calendar year after the programme is completed
questions.explanation: The Manual states that PAMRs should normally be completed in October of the same calendar year as the programme is completed; December is the deadline for the College Annual Monitoring Report (CAMR), not the PAMR.
questions.source_excerpt: PAMRs should normally be completed in October of the same calendar year as the programme is completed in and will be produced by the Course Coordinators of the relevant programmes.

questions.question: LCC uses the mnemonic WIRE to describe the journey of a policy or procedure. According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what does WIRE stand for?
options: Writing, Inspection, Revision and Evaluation
Workshop, Induction, Review and Enhancement
Writing, Implementation, Reporting and Enforcement
Writing, Implementation, Review and Embedding
questions.explanation: The Manual states that WIRE describes a policy's journey from Writing, Implementation, to Review and Embedding.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC uses the mnemonic WIRE to describe the journey of a Policy or Procedure, from Writing, Implementation, to Review and Embedding.

questions.question: You notice that course information on the College website is out of date. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, which group has the specific remit for monitoring the website so public information is accurate?
options: The Student Engagement Group (SEG)
The Marketing, Recruitment and Admissions Committee (MRAC)
The Public Information Monitoring Group (PIMG)
The Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee (ARRC)
questions.explanation: The PIMG is responsible for ensuring all public information is accurate and complete, and monitoring the website is its specific remit.
questions.source_excerpt: The Public Information Monitoring Group (PIMG) has a responsibility to ensure that all public information is accurate and complete. Monitoring the website is the specific remit of the PIMG

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, which of the following is NOT one of the stated requirements of Internal Verifiers?
options: Validate assessors' judgements, including grading decisions, against the standards
Ensure consistent judgements across the whole assessment team
Ensure that students have equality of opportunity
Write the assignment briefs for each unit on behalf of the assessors
questions.explanation: IVs are required to validate assessors' judgements, ensure consistency and ensure equality of opportunity; the Manual's IV flowchart shows the assessor, not the IV, prepares the assignment.
questions.source_excerpt: Internal Verifiers (IV) are required to: ... Validate assessors' judgements (including grading decisions) against the standards. Ensure consistent judgements across all the assessment team Ensure that students have equality of opportunity. ... Assessor prepares assignment

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what is a Key Performance Indicator (KPI)?
options: A measure determined by the OfS as part of its ongoing conditions of registration for providers
A measure determined by LCC as an early indicator of KPM outcomes or of areas it wishes to measure
An indicator used by HESA to rank registered providers nationally against sector benchmarks
A satisfaction indicator drawn from the National Student Survey's five theme measures
questions.explanation: The Manual defines KPIs as performance measures determined by LCC, either as early indicators of KPM outcomes or for specific areas LCC wishes to measure; KPMs are the ones set by the OfS.
questions.source_excerpt: Key Performance Measures (KPM): Performance measures determined by OfS as part of the ongoing conditions of registration. Key Performance Indicators (KPI): Performance measures determined by LCC either as early indicators of KPM outcomes or specific areas that LCC wishes to measure.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what is the role of the external verifier or examiner once students' work has been marked?
options: To write the assignment briefs for the following academic year and check them against the unit specification
To decide on students' extenuating circumstances claims before the Assessment Board meets
To ensure national standardisation by overseeing marks and looking at cohort statistics
To carry out the College's annual teaching observations of tutors and report the results to QESC
questions.explanation: Once work is marked, the external verifier or examiner's role is to ensure national standardisation by overseeing assignment marks and looking at cohort statistics.
questions.source_excerpt: Once marked, an external verifier or examiner, whose role is to ensure national standardisation, oversees assignment marks and looks at cohort statistics.

questions.question: At initial IV sampling, an assessor's marking standards are judged not to be satisfactory. What does the IV Sampling Plan in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual require next?
options: Further samples should be taken from that assessor, increasing in frequency and size
The internal verifier should re-mark the assessor's work and withdraw the original marks
The same sample size should be rechecked at the start of the next academic year
The case should be referred to the external examiner instead of further internal sampling
questions.explanation: Where an assessor's standards are not judged satisfactory at initial sampling, the IV Sampling Plan requires further samples to be taken from that assessor, increasing in frequency and size.
questions.source_excerpt: Further sample are taken for assessors whose standards are not judged to be satisfactory at initial sampling, further samples should be taken, increasing in frequency and size.

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what does the College's Admissions Procedure include to ensure an applicant is competent to study the relevant programme?
options: An academic interview conducted by the academic team and an English test with four components
A written aptitude test marked by the Registrar and a reference from a previous tutor
A personal statement assessed by Admissions and a numeracy test with two components
A group interview with current students and a portfolio review by the Marketing Manager
questions.explanation: The Admissions Procedure includes an academic interview conducted by the academic team and an English test with four components, to ensure the student is competent to study the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: The procedure includes an academic interview conducted by the academic team and an English test (which includes four components) to ensure the student is competent to study the relevant programme

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what is the key document of the Induction Procedure, through which new students learn about learning, assessment and the welfare offered at LCC?
options: The Student Charter and Code of Conduct
The course or programme handbook
The Learning Resource Strategy and Plan
The College Annual Monitoring Report
questions.explanation: During the Induction Procedure students learn about the programme's learning and assessment requirements and pastoral care, and the key document is the course/programme handbook.
questions.source_excerpt: Induction Procedure: the student learns about the learning and assessment of the programme and its requirements (pedagogy) and welfare offered at LCC (pastoral care). The key document is the course/programme handbook

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how should feedback gathered through quality assurance processes be handled?
options: Formalised and minuted, then reported upwards to senior management only, not back down to staff
Recorded informally within each department and kept there unless a formal complaint is made
Formalised, minuted, turned into actions and outcomes, and reported up and down the College
Summarised once a year by the Quality Assurance team and sent only to the Board of Directors
questions.explanation: The Manual states that feedback should be formalised, minuted, actions produced, outcomes achieved and reported up and down the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Feedback should be formalised, minuted, actions produced, outcomes achieved and reported up and down the College.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, which body is the primary governing body of LCC, with legal and statutory responsibility for its solvency, sustainability and compliance?
options: The Academic Board
The Board of Directors
The College Oversight Board
The Principal's Executive Group
questions.explanation: The Board of Directors is the primary governing body of LCC; the College Oversight Board is only an advisory board to it.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board of Directors (BoD) is the primary governing body of LCC and has legal and statutory responsibility to ensure that the College is financially solvent and operationally sustainable and compliant with the legal and regulatory requirements and expectations.

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how often does the College undergo a subject review, in line with the College Provision Review Policy?
options: Every two years
Every three years
Every seven years
Every five years
questions.explanation: The College undergoes a subject review every five years in line with the College Provision Review Policy, less frequently than annual monitoring.
questions.source_excerpt: The College undergoes a subject review every five years, in line with the College Provision Review Policy.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how are the full College Annual Monitoring Report (CAMR) and its Action Plan made available to students?
options: Through the Virtual Learning Environment (VLE)
By email from their Course Coordinator
As an appendix to the programme handbook
On written request to the Registrar's office
questions.explanation: The Manual states that the full CAMR and its Action Plan are made available to students through the VLE.
questions.source_excerpt: The full CAMR and its Action Plan are made available to students through the VLE.

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, who signs off the Regulatory Body Action Plan before it is published on the College website?
options: The Chair of the Academic Board
The Head of Quality Assurance
The Principal of the College
The Chair of the College Oversight Board
questions.explanation: The Regulatory Body Action Plan is produced by PEG and signed off by the Principal before being published on the College website.
questions.source_excerpt: It is signed off by the Principal and published on the College website, along with a link to the report page on OfS's website if required

questions.question: You need to check the current reporting lines between the College's main post-holders. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, who maintains the College Organogram as a dynamic document?
options: The Registry
The Quality Assurance team
The Principal's Office
The HR Department
questions.explanation: The Organogram showing the main College post-holders and reporting structure is maintained by the HR Department and updated regularly.
questions.source_excerpt: The Organogram, showing the interrelationship of the main College post-holders and reporting structure, is maintained by the HR Department as a dynamic document and updated regularly to adjust to changing circumstances.

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, Course Coordinators work closely with HoPAM and the quality assurance team on internal verification (IV). Where should all evidence related to IV be kept?
options: In the student records system
In the Google Drive
On the College VLE
In paper files held by Registry
questions.explanation: Course Coordinators should work with HoPAM and the quality assurance teams so that all evidence related to IV is kept in the Google Drive.
questions.source_excerpt: Course coordinators should work closely with HoPAM and the quality assurance teams so that all evidence related to IVs are kept in the Google Drive.

questions.question: You are reviewing your module's attendance figures against the College KPI Benchmarks and Targets in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual. What is the minimum benchmark for student attendance?
questions.explanation: The College KPI Benchmarks and Targets set a minimum benchmark of 50% for attendance, with a higher expected target.
questions.source_excerpt: Appendix 3: College KPI Benchmarks and Targets ... Minimum Benchmark ... Attendance ... 50%

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, academic staff performance is reported in relation to achieving the College benchmarks and targets. What does this report cover?
options: Satisfaction scores, complaints and appeals from the students on the lecturer's modules
The lecturer's teaching observation grades, CPD hours and research publications
NSS results, graduate salaries and DiscoverUni rankings for the lecturer's course
Attendance, submission, pass and progression rates of the students taught by the lecturer
questions.explanation: Activity E06 reports on academic staff performance against College benchmarks and targets, covering the attendance, submission, pass and progression rates of students taught by the lecturers.
questions.source_excerpt: E06: Academic staff performance in relation to achieving the College benchmarks and targets. [To cover attendance, submission, pass, progression rate of students taught by the lecturers].

questions.question: Because the OfS measure of first class degrees does not directly apply to HNDs, what does the College measure instead, according to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual?
options: The proportion of students who achieve an overall Distinction in their HNC/HND
The proportion of students who progress from an HND on to a top-up honours degree
The proportion of students who achieve a Merit or above in every unit of the HND
The proportion of students who pass all units of the HNC/HND at the first attempt
questions.explanation: As the OfS first-class degree measure does not directly apply to two-year awards such as HNDs, the College measures the proportion of students achieving overall Distinction in their HNC/HND.
questions.source_excerpt: this metric does not directly apply to two-year awards such as HNDs. However, the College measures the proportion of students who have achieved overall Distinction in their HNC/HND.

questions.question: In the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's components of the Quality Cycle, End of Term Feedback, Programme Annual Monitoring Reports (PAMR) and External Examiner Reports all belong to which stage?
options: The Plan stage
The Delivery stage
The Evaluation stage
The Review stage
questions.explanation: Figure 2 lists End of Term Feedback, PAMRs and External Examiner Reports under the Review stage; the Evaluation stage covers the Boards and Committees that receive those reports.
questions.source_excerpt: REVIEW ... End of Term Feedback Teaching Observation NSS and Graduate Outcome Survey Admission and Induction Survey Programme Annual Monitoring Reports (PAMR) External Examiner Reports

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, where a programme's delivery is franchised to the College, who may undertake the role of overseeing assignment marks and cohort statistics to ensure national standardisation?
options: The College's Lead Internal Verifier
The awarding body for the programme
The College's Quality Assurance team
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
questions.explanation: This oversight is normally the role of an external verifier or examiner, but where delivery is franchised to the College the Manual states that the awarding body may undertake it.
questions.source_excerpt: Once marked, an external verifier or examiner, whose role is to ensure national standardisation, oversees assignment marks and looks at cohort statistics. ... In instances where delivery is franchised to the College, the awarding body may undertake this role;

questions.question: The Principal's Executive Group (PEG) wants approval for a non-academic matter concerning strategy. According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, to which body does PEG make its recommendation?
options: To the Academic Board, via the QESC
To the Board of Directors (BoD)
To the College Oversight Board
To the Audit, Remuneration and Risk Committee
questions.explanation: PEG recommends academic policies and matters to the Academic Board via QESC, but recommends non-academic matters concerning strategy to the Board of Directors for approval.
questions.source_excerpt: It makes recommendations to the Academic Board, via the Quality and Enhancement Steering Committee (QESC), for approval of academic policies and academic matters. It makes recommendations to the BoD for approval of non-academic matters concerning strategy and related matters.

questions.question: The Marketing, Recruitment and Admissions Committee (MRAC) has reviewed recruitment, admission and induction after an admission period. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what happens to its recommendations?
options: They are considered by the Academic Board, with the aim of implementing them by the next admission period
They are approved by the Board of Directors, with the aim of implementing them in the next academic year
They are sent to the College Oversight Board, which implements them within two admission periods
They are implemented directly by the Marketing Manager, without being considered by any board
questions.explanation: MRAC convenes after each admission period, and its recommendations are considered by the Academic Board with the aim of implementing them by the next admission period.
questions.source_excerpt: It convenes after each admission period to review recruitment, admission and induction. Its recommendations are considered by the Academic Board with an aim to implement them by the next admission period

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how does the College's Provision (Periodic) Review differ from the Annual Monitoring process?
options: It takes place more often, has a narrower remit and focuses on the latest year's unit data
It replaces Annual Monitoring every third year and is carried out by the Office for Students
It takes place less often, has a broader remit and is informed by trends over time
It is limited to staff performance and is reported to the Board of Directors, not the AB
questions.explanation: The Provision Review occurs less frequently than Annual Monitoring, to an agreed cycle, and has a broader remit informed by a view of trends over time.
questions.source_excerpt: The Provision Review occurs less frequently than the Annual Monitoring process, but periodically and to an agreed cycle. It has a broader remit and is informed by a view of trends over time.

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what must happen to the CAMR Action Plan before the College Annual Monitoring Report is submitted to the Academic Board for discussion and approval?
options: The Principal's Executive Group reviews it and agrees College-level actions
The external examiners review it and sign off the College-level actions
The Student Engagement Group votes on it and publishes it to students
The College Oversight Board audits it and sets the College-level targets
questions.explanation: PEG reviews the CAMR Action Plan regularly and agrees College-level actions before the CAMR goes to the Academic Board for discussion and approval.
questions.source_excerpt: The Principal's Executive Group will review the CAMR Action Plan on a regular basis and to agree College-level actions before the CAMR is submitted to the Academic Board for discussion and approval.

questions.question: Once the Regulatory Body Action Plan has been published, how does the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual say its progress is monitored and communicated?
options: It is reviewed once a year by the Academic Board and progress is reported only to the OfS
It is reviewed by the College Oversight Board and progress is shared through the staff VLE
It is regularly reviewed by PEG and updates on progress are posted on the College website
It is reviewed by QESC at the end of each term and progress is emailed to student representatives
questions.explanation: The Regulatory Body Action Plan is regularly reviewed by the Principal's Executive Group, and updates on progress are posted on the College website.
questions.source_excerpt: The Regulatory Body Action Plan is regularly reviewed by the Principal's Executive Group and updates on progress are posted on the College website.

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how are responsibilities for the Enhancement Action Plan divided between the Academic Board and the College Oversight Board?
options: The College Oversight Board has oversight; the Academic Board reviews and evaluates its operation
The Academic Board has oversight; the College Oversight Board reviews and evaluates its operation
The Academic Board drafts and approves it; the College Oversight Board has no role in it
Both boards share oversight, and the Board of Directors reviews and evaluates its operation
questions.explanation: The Academic Board has oversight of the Enhancement Action Plan, while the College Oversight Board reviews and evaluates its operation.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic Board has oversight of the Enhancement Action Plan and the College Oversight Board reviews and evaluates its operation.

questions.question: A revised College policy has completed its approval route. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, who is responsible for the process of implementing a new or revised policy?
options: The departmental Head who produced it
The Quality Assurance team and HoPAM
The Principal's Executive Group
The College Oversight Board (COB)
questions.explanation: Departmental Heads produce policies, but the Manual states that the process of implementing a new or revised policy is the responsibility of the Principal's Executive Group.
questions.source_excerpt: The process of implementing a new or revised policy is the responsibility of the Principal's Executive Group.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's academic governance arrangements, what is the Board of Directors' role in relation to academic quality and standards?
options: It delegates responsibility to the Academic Board and actively seeks assurance that its academic governance is robust
It retains direct responsibility and approves every academic decision, overriding the Academic Board where needed
It shares responsibility equally with the Academic Board, with the two boards voting jointly on academic matters
It delegates responsibility to the College Oversight Board, which reports to the Academic Board for information
questions.explanation: The BoD delegates responsibility for maintaining and enhancing academic quality and standards to the Academic Board, and actively seeks and receives assurance that academic governance is robust and effective.
questions.source_excerpt: Delegate responsibility for maintaining and enhancing academic quality and standards to the Academic Board. The BoD actively seek and receive assurance from the academic board that academic governance is robust and effective.

questions.question: A Course Coordinator has organised the term's peer reviews and teaching observations. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what happens to them next?
options: They go straight to the Academic Board for approval at its next meeting
They are passed to HR, which produces an annual report for the Board of Directors
They are submitted to HoPAM, who produces a termly report for review by the QESC
They are presented by the Course Coordinator to the College Oversight Board
questions.explanation: Course Coordinators submit peer reviews and teaching observations to HoPAM, who produces a termly report (January, May and September) for review by the QESC.
questions.source_excerpt: The Course Coordinators organises Peer Review and/or Teaching Observation and submit them for the HoPAM's attention for the production of a termly report in January, May and September every year for previous term. The HoPAM produces the report to review by the QESC.

questions.question: According to the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's flowchart for internal verification of assessment decisions, what happens after the assessor has marked the assignments?
options: The external examiner selects a sample of the marked work, and the IV then reviews that sample
A second tutor double marks every script, and the IV then agrees a final mark for each student
The IV reviews every marked script in full and completes a separate IV form for each student
The IV selects and reviews a sample, then accepts or refers the decisions back to the assessor
questions.explanation: The flowchart for IV of assessment decisions shows the IV selecting and reviewing a sample of the marked work, then accepting the decisions or referring them back to the assessor; IV samples work rather than double marking every script.
questions.source_excerpt: Flow Chart of IV of Assessment Decisions ... Select samples by IV ... Review sample assignments by IV ... IV Form-Assessment Decisions; IV Feedback to ... Accept or Refer back

questions.question: After marking an assessment, you notice that many students in the cohort made the same mistake. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's academic feedback guidance, what is the appropriate approach?
options: Point out the mistake to each affected student in front of the class
Give feedback on the common mistake to the entire cohort
Hold all feedback on it until the Assessment Board has met
Refer the mistake to the external examiner for them to address
questions.explanation: Summative feedback includes cohort feedback: common mistakes are given to the entire cohort on completion of assessment tasks; feedback in front of the class is for positive feedback only.
questions.source_excerpt: Provide cohort feedback as necessary - common mistakes or learning aspects will be given to the entire cohort on completion of assessment tasks, where there is opportunity for learning by the group

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, OfS KPM 1 and KPM 2 both use continuation, completion and progression data. What distinguishes KPM 2 from KPM 1?
options: KPM 2 is benchmarked against similar institutions, as identified by the OfS
KPM 2 compares the College with providers in its own English region only
KPM 2 is reported only for full-time students on two-year HND programmes
KPM 2 is measured against an overall average across all registered providers
questions.explanation: KPM 1 benchmarks the data against similar institutions identified by the OfS, whereas KPM 2 uses the same data but measures it against an overall average across all registered providers.
questions.source_excerpt: the data is benchmarked against similar institutions (as identified by OfS). ... This is calculated using the same continuation, completion and progression data as for KPM 1 but is measured against an overall average across all registered providers

questions.question: Your programme's retention over the whole course is 72% and its assessment submission rate is 71%. Against the minimum benchmarks in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's College KPI Benchmarks, which statement is correct?
options: Both meet their minimum benchmarks, which are set at 70% for each
Retention is below its 75% minimum, but submission meets its 70% minimum
Both fall below their minimum benchmarks, which are set at 80% for each
Retention meets its 70% minimum, but submission is below its 75% minimum
questions.explanation: The minimum benchmark is 70% for retention over the whole course and 75% for assessment submission, so 72% retention meets its minimum while 71% submission falls below it.
questions.source_excerpt: Retention (over the whole course) ... 70% ... Assessment Submission ... 75%

questions.question: Under the Unit Level Sampling Plan in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's IV Sampling Plan, 50 students on a unit were awarded a Fail. What sample size applies to the Fail grade band?
options: 3 students
4 students
5 students
10 students
questions.explanation: The Unit Level Sampling Plan sets the Fail band sample at 3 or 10% whichever is higher; 10% of 50 is 5, which is higher than 3.
questions.source_excerpt: Unit Level Sampling Plan ... Fail ... 3 or 10% whichever is higher

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what must the Lead IV's annual audit report on assessment processes and IV documents include, and to which body is it submitted?
options: Commentary on discrepancies between first markers and IV, with an action plan; submitted to QESC in October
A list of every student's final grade for each unit, with a pass-rate summary; submitted to Academic Board in July
Copies of all IV-sampled scripts from the year, with the assessors' CVs attached; submitted to the OfS in December
Teaching observation grades for each assessor, with a CPD plan; submitted to the HR Department in January
questions.explanation: The annual audit requires the Lead IV report to include commentary on discrepancies between first markers and IV and an action plan, reviewed by QA and submitted to QESC in October for the previous academic year.
questions.source_excerpt: Annual audit of assessment processes, assessment documentation, and review of IV documents. [Lead IV Report to include commentary on discrepancies between first markers and IV and an action plan, to be reviewed by QA and submitted to QESC in October for the previous academic year.

questions.question: A programme at LCC is delivered with an external awarding organisation that operates its own quality assurance mechanisms. How does the framework set out in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual approach this?
options: It keeps complete College oversight while incorporating the awarding organisation's QA mechanisms
It applies one identical College process to every programme and sets aside the partner's mechanisms
It suspends College oversight for that programme and defers entirely to the partner's own mechanisms
It replaces the partner's mechanisms with the College KPI benchmarks after the first full year
questions.explanation: The Manual's framework provides complete oversight of the QA process while differentiating between programmes and incorporating the QA mechanisms of external partners and/or awarding organisations; it neither sets them aside nor defers wholly to them.
questions.source_excerpt: provides a complete oversight of the QA process but also differentiates between the programmes provided and incorporates quality assurance mechanisms of external partners and/or awarding organisations

questions.question: In the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's components of the Quality Cycle, at which stages do 'Assessment and IV', 'Development of Assessment Materials' and the 'Assessment and Progress Board' respectively appear?
options: Delivery, then Plan, then Review
Plan, then Delivery, then Evaluation
Review, then Delivery, then Evaluation
Plan, then Review, then Evaluation
questions.explanation: Figure 2 places Assessment and IV under Plan, Development of Assessment Materials under Delivery, and the Assessment and Progress Board under Evaluation.
questions.source_excerpt: PLAN ... Assessment and IV Learning Resource Strategy and Plan ... DELIVERY ... Development of Assessment Materials ... EVALUATION ... SEG Assessment and Progress Board Periodic Review

questions.question: A new student asks how they will receive feedback at LCC. Taking the Student Journey and academic feedback sections of the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual together, which description is accurate?
options: Summative feedback on class activity, and formative feedback on submitted assessments within four weeks
Formative feedback on class activity, with summative feedback given only after the Assessment Board meets
Formative feedback on class activity, and summative feedback on submitted assessments within four weeks
Formative feedback on submitted assessments within two weeks, and no feedback at all on class activity
questions.explanation: The Student Journey gives formative feedback on class activity and summative feedback on submissions, and the academic feedback section sets summative feedback within four weeks of submission.
questions.source_excerpt: Each student is given clear formative feedback on class activity and summative feedback on their submissions ... Students receive accurate and useful summative feedback on their assessments within four weeks of assessments of submission.

questions.question: According to the Quality and the Institution section of the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how does the College's quality system operate?
options: Formally only, through minuted Boards and Committees, with informal feedback kept outside the system
Mainly informally, with formal reporting reserved for regulatory bodies such as the OfS
Through the Quality Assurance team alone, which collects feedback and reports it to the Board of Directors
Both formally and informally, with its focus on collecting feedback and producing measurable outcomes
questions.explanation: The Manual states that the quality system operates both formally and informally, with its focus on collecting feedback and producing meaningful, demonstrative and measurable outcomes.
questions.source_excerpt: The quality system operates both formally and informally, but its focus is again on collecting feedback and producing meaningful, demonstrative and measurable outcomes

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's governance structure, which of these bodies reports into the Principal's Executive Group (PEG), rather than to the Academic Board?
options: The Programme Committee Meeting (PCM)
The Assessment and Progression Board (APB)
The Student Engagement Group (SEG)
The Quality and Enhancement Steering Committee (QESC)
questions.explanation: SEG formalises, approves and reports into PEG on student engagement activities, whereas the PCM and Assessment Board report to the Academic Board via the QESC, and the QESC reports to the Academic Board.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Engagement Group (SEG) formalises, approves and reports into PEG on student engagement activities ... The QESC reports to the AB ... The Programme Committee Meeting reports to the AB via the QESC

questions.question: A programme cohort completes its course in June. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's annual monitoring arrangements, when should that programme's PAMR and the College's CAMR normally be completed?
options: PAMR in October and CAMR in December of that same calendar year
PAMR in December and CAMR in October of that same calendar year
PAMR in October of that year and CAMR in January of the next year
PAMR in July and CAMR in September, before the new academic year
questions.explanation: PAMRs are normally completed in October, and the CAMR, which uses the PAMRs as its primary data source, in December of the same calendar year in which the courses are completed.
questions.source_excerpt: The CAMR should normally be completed in December of the same calendar year in which the courses are completed. The PAMRs will serve as a primary data source for the analysis in the CAMR. The PAMRs should normally be completed in October of the same calendar year in which the courses are completed.
