questions.question: The Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual sets out the areas on which the College's Periodic Review focuses. Which of the following is not one of those areas?
options: The currency of subject, programme, unit and module materials and academic content
The teaching observation grades awarded to individual tutors during the year
Implementation of external verification of the subject offer
Effective usage of the resources underpinning subjects
questions.explanation: The Periodic Review focuses on subject-level matters such as standards, currency of materials, external verification, use of data and resources; individual tutors' observation grades are not among the listed areas.
questions.source_excerpt: The review will focus on how the College achieves the following: ... c) The currency of subject, programme, unit and module materials and ... d) Implementation of external verification of the subject offer ... f) Effective usage of resources underpinning subjects

questions.question: Following an OfS Quality Standards Review, the College must produce a Regulatory Body Action Plan in response to the report's conclusions. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, who produces the plan and whom do they consult?
options: The QESC produces it, after consulting Course Coordinators and the Quality Assurance team
The Student Engagement Group produces it, after consulting the Principal's Executive Group
The Principal's Executive Group produces it, after consulting student representatives in SEG
The Academic Board produces it, after consulting the external members of the Oversight Board
questions.explanation: The Regulatory Body Action Plan is produced by the Principal's Executive Group, which consults jointly with student representatives in SEG, before it is signed off by the Principal and published.
questions.source_excerpt: Following a Higher Education Review (HER) or Quality Standards Review (QSR) by a regulatory body including the OfS, the College produces an action plan in response to the conclusions of the report. ... This Action Plan is produced by the PEG which has consulted jointly with student representatives in SEG

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's section on Policies and Procedures, which pairing correctly allocates responsibility for implementing a new or revised policy and for the operational maintenance of Policies and Procedures?
options: Implementing: the Principal's Executive Group; maintenance: the Registrar, reporting to the College Oversight Board
Implementing: the Principal's Executive Group; maintenance: the QESC, reporting to the Academic Board
Implementing: the departmental Head; maintenance: the QESC, reporting to the Academic Board
Implementing: the Principal's Executive Group; maintenance: the Academic Board, reporting to the BoD
questions.explanation: Implementing a new or revised policy is the Principal's Executive Group's responsibility, while operational responsibility for maintaining Policies and Procedures rests with the QESC and is reported to the Academic Board; departmental Heads produce policies but do not implement them.
questions.source_excerpt: Operational responsibility for their maintenance rests with the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee and is reported to the Academic Board. ... The process of implementing a new or revised policy is the responsibility of the Principal's Executive Group.

questions.question: Reviewing an assignment brief, an internal verifier sees that the tasks ask students to 'describe' where the unit specification requires them to 'evaluate'. Which review question in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual addresses this directly?
options: Do the required tasks relate to the same active verbs as the unit specification?
Will it be possible to confirm the authenticity of each student's work?
Are the timescales realistic for the tasks that students must complete?
Does the brief follow the common template with a Front Sheet and Student's Brief?
questions.explanation: The IV review questions include whether required tasks relate to the same active verbs as stated in the unit specification, and a describe/evaluate mismatch fails that check.
questions.source_excerpt: Do required tasks relate to the same active verbs as stated in the unit specification?

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's description of OfS KPM 1, completion outcomes for full-time entrants are generally tracked four years and 15 days after they start. What exception applies to full-time HND students?
options: Completion is tracked six years and 15 days after they started
Completion is tracked two years and 15 days after they started
Completion is tracked one year and 15 days after they started
Completion is tracked 15 months after they gain their qualification
questions.explanation: Completion is normally tracked four years and 15 days after entry (six for part-time), but the Manual notes it is two years and 15 days for full-time HND students.
questions.source_excerpt: track how many continue in active study or qualify four years and 15 days after they started (six years and 15 days for part-time students). Please note that this will be two years and 15 days for full-time HND students.

questions.question: A graduate who is not UK-domiciled responds to the Graduate Outcomes survey 15 months after qualifying and reports progressing to further study. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's description of KPM 1c, how is this response treated?
options: It counts as a positive progression outcome, as further study is a positive outcome
It is excluded, because the progression data is restricted to UK-domiciled qualifiers
It counts only if the further study is with the same provider as the original course
It is transferred to the continuation measure, which covers students of any domicile
questions.explanation: Progression counts respondents reporting professional or managerial employment, further study or other positive outcomes 15 months after qualifying, but the data is restricted to UK-domiciled qualifiers.
questions.source_excerpt: Progression outcomes are measured as the proportion of Graduate Outcomes survey respondents who reported they have progressed to professional or managerial employment, further study or other positive outcomes, 15 months after gaining their qualification. The data is restricted to UK-domiciled qualifiers

questions.question: Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's description of OfS KPM 4 (students' views on aspects of quality), an NSS respondent chooses the second possible answer to a theme question. How is that answer treated?
options: As a neutral answer, because only the first possible answer counts as positive
As a negative answer, because only the top answer on the scale counts as positive
As excluded, because KPM 4 uses only the overall satisfaction question in the NSS
As a positive answer, because the first two possible answers both count as positive
questions.explanation: KPM 4 is the proportion of students giving a positive answer to the five NSS theme measures, with a positive answer being the first two possible answers to the question.
questions.source_excerpt: It is measured by the proportion of students who gave a positive answer to the five theme measures in the NSS with a positive answer being the first two possible answers to the question.

questions.question: A manager asks how LCC tracks OfS KPMs 5, 6 and 7, such as access to Higher Education and degree attainment by ethnicity. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, which statement is correct?
options: Annually by intake using proxy data, identified as KPIs as they are not directly comparable to OfS KPMs
In line with the OfS metrics, exactly as for KPMs 1 to 4, and benchmarked against similar institutions
They are not measured, as they are market measures that do not apply to an individual organisation
Termly through the NSS five theme measures, with the results reported to PEG as performance indicators
questions.explanation: The Manual states that OfS KPMs 5-8 are measured using proxy data sources, where available, annually by intake, and are identified as KPIs because they are not directly comparable; only KPMs 1-4 follow the OfS metrics, and KPMs 8-11 are the market measures.
questions.source_excerpt: The College measures KPMs 1-4 in line with OfS metrics ... The OfS KPMs 5-8 are measured using proxy data sources, where available and on an annual basis, by intake. These are identified as KPIs as they are not directly comparable to OfS KPMs. ... KPMs 8-11 are market measures and not directly applicable to an individual organisation.

questions.question: The Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual explains which data sources feed the TEF metrics, which also form part of the OfS ongoing conditions of registration. Where does the TEF retention/continuation metric come from?
options: The Graduate Outcome Surveys and the HMRC data match
The UK Performance Indicators published by HESA
The National Student Survey teaching quality measures
The College's own KPI 2 on retention by course and intake
questions.explanation: The Manual states that retention/continuation comes from the UK Performance Indicators published by HESA; employment uses the Graduate Outcome Surveys and satisfaction uses the NSS.
questions.source_excerpt: Retention/continuation - from the UK Performance Indicators which are published by Higher Education Statistics Agency (HESA)

questions.question: Course Coordinators report termly on the student timetable and on programme handbooks and VLE updates. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual's planning and implementing activities, to whom does each report go?
options: Timetable report to the Programme Committee; handbook and VLE report to PEG
Both reports to the QESC, which forwards them to the Academic Board
Timetable report to PEG; handbook and VLE report to the Programme Committee
Both reports to the College Oversight Board, via the Registrar
questions.explanation: The student timetable report goes to PEG, while the programme handbooks and VLE report goes to the Programme Committee; Course Coordinators report on both termly.
questions.source_excerpt: D 03: Student timetable determined one calendar month prior to start of next term ... Report: termly Report by: Course Coordinators Report to: PEG ... D 04: Programme handbooks produced and VLE updated ... Report: termly Report by: Course Coordinators Report to: Programme Committee

questions.question: HoPAM reports on academic staff performance and on personal tutor performance against College benchmarks. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what does the personal tutor report include that the academic staff report does not?
options: Progression rates of the students taught, reported using quantitative data only
Student satisfaction scores from the NSS, alongside complaints and appeals
Staff turnover and absenteeism, with a performance appraisal action plan
Continuation of students, with qualitative as well as quantitative data
questions.explanation: The personal tutor report covers attendance, submission, pass rates and continuation using quantitative and qualitative data, whereas the academic staff report covers attendance, submission, pass and progression.
questions.source_excerpt: [To cover attendance, submission, pass, progression rate of students taught by the lecturers]. ... E07: Personal tutor performance in achieving College benchmarks for student attendance, submission, pass rates and continuation of students. To include both quantitative and qualitative data as appropriate.

questions.question: On a programme, 100 students enrolled, 60 completed the entire course and 45 of those 60 achieved their award. Under the College KPI Benchmarks in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how does this compare with the minimum awards benchmark?
options: It is below the 70% minimum, as only 45% of all enrolled students achieved their award
It is below the 80% minimum, as 75% of those completing falls short of the awards benchmark
It meets the 70% minimum, as 75% of those who completed the entire course achieved their award
It meets the 60% minimum, as 45 awards from 60 completers exceeds the awards benchmark
questions.explanation: The awards minimum benchmark is 70% and is measured against those who completed the entire course: 45 of 60 is 75%, which meets it.
questions.source_excerpt: Minimum Benchmark ... Awards Target [of those who completed the entire course] ... 70%

questions.question: You are planning IV sampling for an experienced assessor whose unit was assessed by both a case study and a professional discussion. Under the IV Sampling Plan in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what must the plan include?
options: A sample of at least 2 students covering both the case study and the professional discussion
A sample of at least 2 students taken from the case study only, as the main written method
A sample of 10% in each grade band or 6 students, whichever is higher, from the case study only
No sample at all, as experienced assessors are sampled only when a concern has been raised
questions.explanation: The plan must sample the full range of assessment methods used, and for experienced assessors the minimum sample is 2 students.
questions.source_excerpt: a) Must sample the full range of assessment methods used, (eg assignment, case study, direct observation of performance of a task, professional discussion, question and answer) b) For experienced assessors: sample size is minimum 2 students

questions.question: An internal verifier who is short of time proposes to review the assessment briefs for only a sample of a programme's units this term. Under the IV Sampling Plan in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what applies?
options: Briefs may be sampled at 10% of units or 3 units, whichever is higher, as for marked work
Only the briefs for units marked by new or inexperienced assessors need to be reviewed
Briefs need reviewing only for units whose pass rate fell below the 75% minimum benchmark
The assessment briefs of all units must be reviewed, even though marked work is sampled
questions.explanation: The IV Sampling Plan allows marked student work to be sampled, but it lists reviewing the assessment brief of all units as a separate factor, so briefs cannot be sampled.
questions.source_excerpt: Factors considered a) Must sample the full range of assessment methods used ... d) Review assessment brief of all units

questions.question: Sampling an assessor's marked work, an internal verifier finds the grades are accurate but the feedback to students does not highlight areas for improvement. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, what should the IV do?
options: Record this and give feedback to the assessor, including details of any corrective action required
Accept the decisions without comment, as IV of assessment decisions covers grades rather than feedback
Re-mark the sampled scripts and write new feedback directly to the students on the assessor's behalf
Leave the feedback as it is and raise the point only in the Lead IV's annual audit report
questions.explanation: IV covers assessment decisions and summative feedback, and IVs must provide feedback to the assessor; the IV feedback form asks whether feedback highlights areas for improvement and records any corrective action required.
questions.source_excerpt: Internal verification has two components: internal verification of assessment papers and internal verification of assessment decisions and summative feedback. ... Provide feedback to assessor ... Does the feedback highlight areas for improvement? ... Further comments to assessor: (including details of any corrective action required)

questions.question: OfS KPM 1 (extent of poor student outcomes) includes continuation and completion indicators. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, at what points are these outcomes measured for a cohort of part-time entrants?
options: Continuation at one year and 15 days; completion at four years and 15 days after starting
Continuation at two years and 15 days; completion at four years and 15 days after starting
Continuation at one year and 15 days; completion at six years and 15 days after starting
Continuation at two years and 15 days; completion at six years and 15 days after starting
questions.explanation: Continuation is normally checked one year and 15 days after starting and completion four years and 15 days after starting, but for part-time students these become two years and 15 days and six years and 15 days respectively.
questions.source_excerpt: track how many continue in active study or qualify one year and 15 days after they started (two years and 15 days for part-time students). ... track how many continue in active study or qualify four years and 15 days after they started (six years and 15 days for part-time students).

questions.question: An internal verifier is applying the Unit Level Sampling Plan in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual to a unit where 40 students were awarded a Pass and 12 were awarded a Distinction. How many students' work should be sampled from each of these two grade bands?
options: 3 from the Pass band and 3 from the Distinction band
4 from the Pass band and 2 from the Distinction band
3 from the Pass band and 2 from the Distinction band
4 from the Pass band and 3 from the Distinction band
questions.explanation: The Pass band is sampled at 3 or 10% and the Distinction band at 2 or 10%, whichever is higher: 10% of 40 is 4, which exceeds 3, while 10% of 12 is only 1.2, so the minimum of 2 applies.
questions.source_excerpt: Grades ... Fail ... Pass ... Merit ... Distinction ... Sample size ... 3 or 10% whichever is higher ... 3 or 10% whichever is higher ... 2 or 10% whichever is higher ... 2 or 10% whichever is higher

questions.question: The termly check on whether handbooks, guides and other academic documents have been uploaded to the College VLE is due. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, who is responsible for this audit and to whom is it reported?
options: The QA team and HoPAM ensure it is carried out, and HoPAM reports it to the QESC and PEG
The Student Engagement Manager carries it out with the termly student survey and reports it to PEG
The Registrar carries it out with the annual website content review and reports it to the Academic Board via PEG
The Lead IV carries it out with the annual audit of assessment documentation and reports it to QESC
questions.explanation: The Quality Assurance team and HoPAM ensure the termly VLE audit takes place, and HoPAM reports it to the QESC and PEG; the other activities belong to separate reports with different leads.
questions.source_excerpt: The Quality Assurance team and HoPAM ensure that termly audit of the College VLE and comment on whether relevant academic documents, guides, handbooks are uploaded. This is then reported by the HoPAM to the QESC and PEG.

questions.question: An external examiner's report on your programme has just been received. Under the planning and implementing activities in the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, how should the report's outcomes be taken forward?
options: The Lead IV adds them to the annual audit of IV documents, which QA reviews before it goes to QESC in October
The Principal covers them in a written commentary to the Board of Directors via PEG in January
HoPAM and the Course Coordinators review them, develop an action plan and report to QESC in November
The Registrar reviews them with the effectiveness of oversight committees and reports to the Academic Board in November
questions.explanation: Activity R 02 requires the outcomes of external examiners' reports to be reviewed and an action plan developed, reported by HoPAM and Course Coordinators to QESC in November; E 03 covers IV discrepancies and E 01 covers regulatory body visits.
questions.source_excerpt: R 02: Review outcomes in external examiners and awarding organisations' visit reports and develop action plan. ... Report in: November Report by: HoPAM and Course Coordinators Report to: QESC

questions.question: A departmental Head drafts a new policy on their own, has it reviewed by the Quality Assurance team and sends it to QESC for scrutiny before final submission to the Academic Board, with PEG overseeing. Under the Quality Cycle and Assurance Manual, which requirement has been missed?
options: Drafting by the Quality Assurance team, with the departmental Head only reviewing it
Approval by the Board of Directors before the draft is sent on to QESC for its scrutiny
Joint consultation with student representatives in SEG before the Quality Assurance review
Input, during its development, from the staff responsible for delivering the policy's contents
questions.explanation: Departmental Heads produce policies for QA review and QESC scrutiny under PEG oversight, but the Manual also requires new policies to be developed with the input of the staff responsible for delivering their contents, which a Head drafting alone has not obtained.
questions.source_excerpt: Policies are produced by the relevant departmental Heads and are reviewed by the Quality Assurance team and scrutinised by the QESC prior to final submission to Academic Board; ... The College ensures new policies are developed with the input of the staff responsible for delivering the contents of the policy.

questions.question: According to the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what are the timeframes for a Stage One (formal) admissions appeal?
options: Appeal received within 10 working days of the decision; outcome issued within 15 working days
Appeal received within 15 working days of the decision; outcome issued within 10 working days
Appeal received within 20 working days of the decision; outcome issued within 20 working days
Appeal received within 30 calendar days of the decision; outcome issued within 5 working days
questions.explanation: The policy states a Stage One appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original application decision, and the decision is to be issued to the applicant within 10 working days.
questions.source_excerpt: Appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original application decision Decision to be issued to the applicant within 10 working days

questions.question: Informal discussion has not resolved an unsuccessful applicant's concerns and they want to lodge a formal appeal. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, how should they submit it?
options: Complete the Stage One Admission Appeal Form and submit it via reception for the attention of the Registrar
Email a letter setting out their grounds of appeal directly to the Programme Leader for the course
Complete the Stage Two Admission Appeal form and send it to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer
Raise it through the College's complaints procedure by emailing the Admissions Department at admission@lcc.ac.uk
questions.explanation: A formal (Stage One) appeal must be made on the Stage One Admission Appeal Form, submitted via reception for the attention of the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: An applicant wishing to make an appeal must do so by completing the Stage One Admission Appeal Form, which can be downloaded obtained from reception and should be submitted via reception for the attention of the Registrar at LCC.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which of the following is a permissible ground for a Stage One admissions appeal?
options: The applicant believes they are better qualified than other applicants who were made offers
There is evidence that the College has not followed its own admissions policy
The applicant disagrees with the programme's published entry requirements
The applicant has since received an offer from another provider for a similar course
questions.explanation: An appeal is permissible only on two grounds, one being evidence that the College's Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy (its own admissions policy) has not been followed; appeals on any other grounds will not be considered.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following two grounds: ... In circumstances where there is evidence that the College's Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy has not been followed. ... Appeals put forward on any other grounds will not be considered.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, an applicant wanting a Stage Two review of their Stage One appeal outcome must submit the Stage Two form to whom, and by when?
options: The Registrar (or the appeal reviewer they nominated), within 15 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
The Admissions Manager (or their deputy), within 5 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
The Programme Leader (or their line manager), within 20 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
questions.explanation: The Stage Two Admission Appeal form must be submitted to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: An applicant who wishes to have the Stage One decision reviewed must complete the Stage Two Admission Appeal form and submit it to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.

questions.question: An applicant who was refused a place tells you they will use the College's complaints procedure to get the academic decision overturned. What does the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy say?
options: The complaints procedure is the correct route for challenging a refusal, and the Registrar will reconsider the decision
A complaint can overturn the refusal if it is lodged within 15 working days of the original decision
The complaints procedure cannot be used to challenge an academic decision to refuse an application
Complaints about refusals are passed to the Programme Leader, who has the authority to reverse the decision
questions.explanation: The complaints procedure covers complaints about the application process, but the policy states it cannot be used to challenge an academic decision to refuse an application.
questions.source_excerpt: An applicant who wishes to make a complaint about the application process may do so using the College's complaints procedure. Please note that the complaints procedure cannot be used to challenge an academic decision to refuse an application.

questions.question: According to the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what is the minimum English Language requirement for applicants recruited onto LCC courses?
options: CEFR level B2, equivalent to IELTS 5.5-6.5 depending on the level of the course
CEFR level B1, equivalent to IELTS 4.5 for every course regardless of level
CEFR level C1, equivalent to IELTS 7.0 for every course regardless of level
CEFR level A2, equivalent to IELTS 4.0 for every course regardless of level
questions.explanation: The policy sets the minimum English Language requirement at CEFR level B2, equivalent to IELTS 5.5-6.5 depending on the level of the course.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC ensures that all applicants recruited onto all courses meet the minimum English Language requirement assessed at Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) level B2, equivalent to 5.5-6.5 (depending on the level of the course) on the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) framework.

questions.question: An applicant who was unsuccessful for the current intake asks whether they can submit a fresh application for that same intake. What does the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy say?
options: They may reapply for the same intake, provided they submit new supporting documents
They may reapply once within the same intake if the Registrar approves it
Unsuccessful applicants are not permitted to reapply within the same intake
They may reapply within the same intake after completing informal resolution
questions.explanation: The policy is explicit that applicants who are unsuccessful are not permitted to reapply within the same intake.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants who are unsuccessful are not permitted to reapply within the same intake.

questions.question: An applicant with dyslexia is required to sit an English language exam to gain admission and asks whether they can have extra time. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what applies?
options: Adjustments are not available for admissions exams; disability support is arranged after enrolment
They should submit a Stage One appeal to the Registrar to have extra time considered
Additional time is granted to any applicant who requests it, without the need for supporting evidence
They can request adjustments such as additional time, assuming they have supporting evidence
questions.explanation: Applicants with disabilities such as dyslexia can request adjustments such as additional time for the English language exam, provided they have supporting evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: Some applicants may be required to undergo an English language exam to gain admission to the College. Applicants with disabilities, such as dyslexia, can request adjustments such as additional time, assuming they have supporting evidence.

questions.question: According to the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, applicants to which programme undergo an enhanced DBS check with barred lists at the final stage, and why?
options: All programmes, because every student may come into contact with children or vulnerable adults while on campus
HND in Healthcare Professions' Support for England, as students complete placements in health and care settings
Any programme where the applicant declares a previous criminal conviction, so the Registrar can assess the risk
Any programme entered through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), because prior work experience must be verified
questions.explanation: HND in Healthcare Professions' Support for England students must complete work placements in health and care settings, so an enhanced DBS check with barred lists is conducted at the final stage for applicants to this programme.
questions.source_excerpt: HND in Healthcare Professions' Support for England students must complete work placements in health and care settings. Therefore, an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check with barred lists will be conducted at the final stage for applicants to this programme.

questions.question: You interview a prospective student whose certificates fall short of the published entry requirements, but the course accepts prior experiential learning. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what is your role as interviewer?
options: Give final sign-off on the application, since the interviewer decides whether entry requirements are met
Reject the application, since prior experiential learning cannot replace certificated qualifications for entry
Determine whether their prior experiential and/or certificated learning meets the entry requirements
Refer the prior learning claim to the Registrar so it can be handled as a Stage One admissions appeal
questions.explanation: The interviewer determines whether the prospective student's prior experiential and/or certificated learning meets the entry requirements; the Senior Admissions Officer gives final sign-off.
questions.source_excerpt: The interviewer shall be responsible for determining if the prospective student's prior experimental and/or certificated learning meets the entry requirements, and the Senior Admissions Officer shall be responsible for the final sign-off on the application.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, who must approve Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) decisions?
options: The relevant programme leaders or their line managers
The Registrar, following an initial evaluation of the claim
The Admissions Officer who received the application
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer or their nominee
questions.explanation: All RPL decisions must be processed in line with awarding body requirements and approved by the relevant programme leaders or their line managers.
questions.source_excerpt: All RPL decisions are to be processed in line with the requirements of the awarding bodies and must be approved by the relevant programme leaders or their line managers.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, if a Stage One admissions appeal is based on valid grounds and the Registrar nominates an appeal reviewer, who must that reviewer be?
options: The member of staff who interviewed the applicant during selection
The Admissions Officer who guided the applicant's application
An external assessor appointed by the programme's awarding body
A member of staff who has had no previous involvement in the matter
questions.explanation: The Registrar conducts the review or nominates an appeal reviewer, who must be a member of staff with no previous involvement in the matter.
questions.source_excerpt: If the appeal is based on valid grounds, the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim. This will be a member of staff who has had no previous involvement in the matter.

questions.question: According to the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what do LCC's admissions policy and procedures support the College in doing?
options: Filling each of its programmes to full capacity before every intake closes
Meeting the annual recruitment targets that are set by the awarding bodies
Selecting the applicants who are able to successfully complete their programme
Selecting the applicants with the highest prior qualifications for each programme
questions.explanation: The policy states that its policy and procedures support the College in the selection of applicants who can successfully complete their programme.
questions.source_excerpt: They support the College in the selection of applicants who can successfully complete their programme.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, when must prospective students be given information about the courses offered, the structure of courses and fees/costs?
options: Before they are expected to reach a decision about joining the College
At induction, once they have enrolled on their chosen programme
Once an offer has been issued following their admission interview
On request only, once they have formally accepted a place on a course
questions.explanation: Information about courses, course structure and fees/costs must be made available before prospective students are expected to reach a decision about joining the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Prospective students are provided with information about the courses offered by the College, the structure of courses and fees/costs. This information is made available to them before they are expected to reach a decision about joining the College.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what must happen when no offer can be issued to an applicant for their chosen programme?
options: Their decision is held until the intake closes in case a place becomes free
Their application is carried forward to the next intake without review
They are referred to the Registrar to open a Stage One appeal
They are advised promptly of other options available to them
questions.explanation: The policy requires prospective applicants to be advised promptly of other options available if no offer can be issued for their chosen programme.
questions.source_excerpt: prospective applicants are advised promptly of other options available if no offer can be issued for their chosen programme.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what can an applicant with additional needs arrange before enrolment?
options: An exemption from the admission interview for their chosen programme
A meeting to discuss reasonable adjustments that could be put in place
A waiver of the minimum English Language requirement for their course
A deferred start date agreed directly with their Programme Leader
questions.explanation: Applicants with additional needs can arrange a meeting prior to enrolment to discuss the reasonable adjustments that could be put into place for them.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants with additional needs can arrange a meeting to discuss these prior to enrolment. This allows applicants to discuss the reasonable adjustments that could be put into place for them should they join the College as a student.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which applicants will be invited for an interview as part of the College's selection process?
options: Every applicant whose application form has been fully completed
Only shortlisted applicants who are applying through RPL
Every applicant who has been shortlisted for their programme
Only shortlisted applicants who lack English-medium schooling
questions.explanation: The policy states that all shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview as part of the College's selection process.
questions.source_excerpt: All shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview as part of the College's selection process.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which applicants must demonstrate their capability in English comparable to the required standard?
options: Anyone whose first language, as stated on their application form, is not the English language
Anyone who did not complete their final year of school at an institution based in the UK
Anyone who has not lived in an English-speaking country for at least two years before applying
Anyone who did not complete their final two years of school in an English-speaking institution
questions.explanation: Any applicant who has not completed their final two years of school in an English-speaking institution must demonstrate English capability comparable to the required standard.
questions.source_excerpt: Any applicant who has not completed their final two years of school in an English-speaking institution must demonstrate their capability in English comparable to the required standard covered by level B2.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what does a successful application for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) give the applicant?
options: Exemption from the module whose learning outcomes they already meet
Automatic entry to the programme without an admission interview
A reduction in the tuition fees for the rest of the programme
Credit that can be transferred to another higher education provider
questions.explanation: RPL is for applicants whose prior learning or experience already meets a module's learning outcomes; if successful, it gives them exemption from the module.
questions.source_excerpt: RPL is available to applicants who feel that their prior learning or experience already meets the learning outcomes of one or more of the programme's modules. If successful, their application for RPL would give them exemption from the module.

questions.question: At the informal resolution stage of the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, who can an applicant discuss the reasons their application was unsuccessful with?
options: An Appeal Panel of College members who are independent of the case
Admissions staff, who can provide feedback on request
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer or their nominee
The Programme Leader for the course they applied to
questions.explanation: At the informal stage, applicants can discuss why their application was unsuccessful with admissions staff, who can provide feedback on request.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants can discuss why their application was unsuccessful with admissions staff who can provide feedback on request.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, in what circumstances may a Stage One appeal reviewer form an Appeal Panel?
options: Whenever the applicant asks to present their case at a formal hearing
Where the appeal was received after the Stage One submission deadline
Only after the Registrar has rejected the appeal as not made on valid grounds
In cases where additional impartial expertise is required to decide
questions.explanation: The appeal reviewer has authority to form an Appeal Panel in cases where additional impartial expertise is required to decide.
questions.source_excerpt: The appeal reviewer has authority to take the following courses of action: ... To form an Appeal Panel in cases where additional impartial expertise is required to decide.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what will an applicant be invited to do once their Stage Two review request has been referred to an Appeal Panel?
options: Attend a second admission interview with their Personal Tutor first
Nominate a member of staff of their choice to sit on the Panel
Give a written statement and evidence, and attend the Panel in person
Resubmit their Stage One Admission Appeal Form with new documents
questions.explanation: The applicant will be invited to provide a written statement and any additional evidence to the Panel, and to attend the Panel meeting in person.
questions.source_excerpt: If the request is deemed to be on reasonable grounds, the Senior Quality Assurance Officer will refer it to an Appeal Panel. ... The applicant will be invited to provide a written statement and any additional evidence to the Panel and will be invited to attend the Panel meeting in person.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, how should an applicant who has not been offered a place first request feedback on the decision?
options: By emailing the Admissions Department at admission@lcc.ac.uk
By submitting a Stage One Admission Appeal Form via reception
By using the College's complaints procedure for applicants
By writing to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer at reception
questions.explanation: Applicants wanting feedback on the decision should contact the Admissions Department in the first instance by emailing admission@lcc.ac.uk.
questions.source_excerpt: Any applicant who wishes to obtain feedback regarding the decision made in respect of their application for admission, should contact the Admissions Department in the first instance by emailing: admission@lcc.ac.uk

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which role is the key contact for all applicants, guiding them through the application process?
options: The Admissions Manager
The Admissions Officer
The Registrar
The Programme Leader
questions.explanation: The policy names the Admissions Officer as the key contact for all applicants, guiding them through the application process.
questions.source_excerpt: Admissions Officer 5.2.1. The key contact for all applicants, guiding them through the application process.

questions.question: According to the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which of the following is a responsibility of the Registrar?
options: Conducting admission interviews with all shortlisted applicants
Providing the final sign-off on every application to the College's programmes
Supporting the Induction Programme so applicants transition smoothly
Ensuring support and advice is available to students with additional needs
questions.explanation: Among the Registrar's responsibilities, the policy lists ensuring support and advice is made available to students with additional needs.
questions.source_excerpt: 5.5. Registrar 5.5.1. Processes Appeals and Complaints relating to Admission. 5.5.2. Ensures support and advice is made available to students with additional needs.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, induction is arranged for which applicants, and which role supports the Induction Programme to help them make a smooth transition to becoming students?
options: All shortlisted applicants, with the Admissions Officer supporting the Induction Programme
Successful applicants, with the Programme Leader supporting the Induction Programme
Applicants granted RPL exemptions, with their Personal Tutor supporting the Induction Programme
Applicants with additional needs, with the Registrar supporting the Induction Programme
questions.explanation: Induction is arranged for successful applicants, and the Programme Leader supports the Induction Programme to help applicants make a smooth transition to becoming students.
questions.source_excerpt: Induction is arranged for successful applicants to introduce them to the College, their Programme, the Awarding Body, the teaching and administration staff, fellow students, and the facilities that this College provides. ... Programme Leader 5.4.1. Supports the Induction Programme, helping to ensure applicants can make a smooth transition to becoming students.

questions.question: A shortlisted applicant is to be invited for an admission interview. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, who arranges the interview and who conducts it?
options: The Registrar arranges it with the Admissions Manager, who then conducts the interview
The Programme Leader arranges it with the Registrar, who then conducts the interview
The Admissions Manager arranges it with the External English Assessor, who conducts it
The Admissions Officer arranges it with Personal Tutors, and a Personal Tutor conducts it
questions.explanation: All shortlisted applicants are invited to interview; the Admissions Officer liaises with Personal Tutors to arrange admission interviews, and the Personal Tutor conducts them.
questions.source_excerpt: All shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview as part of the College's selection process. ... Admissions Officer ... Liaises with the External English Assessor to coordinate internal English tests and with Personal Tutors to arrange admission interviews. ... Personal Tutor ... Conducts admission interviews.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, an applicant completed only their final year of school at an English-speaking institution and has no comparable English qualification. What applies?
options: They are exempt, because their final year of school was completed at an English-speaking institution
They must demonstrate B2-comparable English and are invited to take an appropriate test as advised by LCC
They must first obtain IELTS 7.0 at an external test centre before any interview can be offered
They are referred for Recognition of Prior Learning so their schooling counts towards the requirement
questions.explanation: Anyone who has not completed their final two years of school in an English-speaking institution must demonstrate English comparable to B2, and applicants without comparable qualifications are invited to take an appropriate test as advised by LCC.
questions.source_excerpt: Any applicant who has not completed their final two years of school in an English-speaking institution must demonstrate their capability in English comparable to the required standard covered by level B2. ... Applicants who do not already possess comparable qualifications in the English Language ... are invited to take an appropriate test as advised by LCC.

questions.question: An applicant believes their work experience already meets the learning outcomes of one of their programme's modules. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, who guides their RPL application and who approves the decision?
options: Their Personal Tutor guides it; the relevant programme leader or their line manager approves it
The Admissions Officer guides it; the Registrar approves it after carrying out an initial evaluation
The Programme Leader guides it; the Senior Quality Assurance Officer or nominee approves it
The Senior Admissions Officer guides it; the Admissions Manager approves it at final sign-off
questions.explanation: The Personal Tutor is responsible for guiding applicants through making an RPL application, and all RPL decisions must be approved by the relevant programme leaders or their line managers.
questions.source_excerpt: All RPL decisions are to be processed in line with the requirements of the awarding bodies and must be approved by the relevant programme leaders or their line managers. ... Personal Tutor 5.3.1. Responsible for guiding applicants and students through the process of making an application for RPL.

questions.question: An unsuccessful applicant received their original application decision 12 working days ago and now wants to lodge a Stage One appeal. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, are they in time?
options: No; a Stage One appeal must be received within 10 working days of the original decision
No; a Stage One appeal must be received within 5 working days of the original decision
Yes; a Stage One appeal may be lodged at any point before the relevant intake begins
Yes; a Stage One appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original decision
questions.explanation: A Stage One appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original application decision, so an appeal at 12 working days is in time.
questions.source_excerpt: Appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original application decision

questions.question: On receipt of a Stage One admissions appeal, the Registrar carries out an initial evaluation. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what does that evaluation check?
options: Whether the applicant meets entry requirements, holds B2-level English and has a DBS check
Correct procedures, valid grounds, submission within the deadline and the required format
Whether the interview scores were accurate and the original decision was academically sound
Whether informal resolution was attempted first and the Programme Leader supports the appeal
questions.explanation: The Registrar's initial evaluation checks that the appeal was submitted under the correct procedures, falls within the permitted grounds, was submitted within the deadline and is in the required format.
questions.source_excerpt: On receipt of an academic appeal, the Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation to check that the applicant's academic appeal was submitted under the correct procedures, that it falls within the grounds upon which an appeal may be made, that it was submitted within the deadline and is in the required format.

questions.question: An applicant could not supply a key transcript during the admissions process because they were in hospital. They were refused and now have it. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, can they appeal at Stage One?
options: No; new evidence can only be raised at Stage Two, after a Stage One appeal has been decided
No; they should use the complaints procedure instead, as a refusal cannot be challenged by appeal
No; they must reapply for a later intake instead and submit the transcript with that application
Yes; new information they could not provide earlier owing to exceptional circumstances is a valid ground
questions.explanation: One of the two permissible Stage One grounds is new information not made available during the admissions process because the applicant was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide it earlier.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following two grounds: ... In instances where there is new information that was not made available during the admissions process because the applicant was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances to provide it earlier in the process.

questions.question: A Stage One admissions appeal has been investigated and is not upheld. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what must the applicant be informed of?
options: That the decision is final and no further review of the Stage One decision is available
That they may reapply for the same intake once they have obtained further evidence
Their right to request a review of Stage One, how to do so and the time limits
That any further challenge must go through the College's complaints procedure
questions.explanation: If a Stage One appeal is not upheld, the applicant is informed in writing of their right to request a review of Stage One, with instructions on how to do so and the time limits.
questions.source_excerpt: The outcome of the appeal will be communicated to the applicant in writing. If the appeal is not upheld, the applicant will be informed of their right to request a review of Stage One, as well as instructions on how to do so and the time limits.

questions.question: An applicant whose Stage One admissions appeal failed believes the appeals process itself was handled unfairly. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what route is open to them?
options: A new Stage One appeal, since a procedural unfairness claim restarts the formal stage
A formal complaint, since the appeals process cannot be reviewed once Stage One ends
A Stage Two review request, citing procedural unfairness in the appeals process
None, since a Stage Two review is limited to new material evidence that has emerged
questions.explanation: Procedural unfairness in the appeals process is one of the limited grounds on which a Stage Two review of the Stage One decision can be requested.
questions.source_excerpt: A request for a review must be based on the following limited grounds: ... The applicant believes that there has been procedural unfairness in the appeals process.

questions.question: A Personal Tutor who interviewed an applicant is asked to sit on the Appeal Panel for that applicant's Stage Two review. What does the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy say?
options: They should not sit, as the Panel is made up of College members who are independent of the case
They may sit, provided the Senior Quality Assurance Officer also attends the Panel as its chair
They may sit, since knowledge of the original interview is needed to review the admissions decision
They may sit, provided the applicant has agreed to this in writing before the Panel meeting
questions.explanation: The Appeal Panel is composed of members of the College who are independent of the case, so the applicant's interviewer should not sit on it.
questions.source_excerpt: The Appeal Panel will be composed of members of the College who are independent of the case.

questions.question: At Stage Two, the Appeal Panel does not accept the original admissions decision. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what is the outcome of the review?
options: The Panel issues the applicant an offer of a place on their chosen programme
The applicant is permitted to submit a new application within the same intake
The case is passed to the College's complaints procedure for a final decision
It confirms the Admissions Department must review or revise its decision
questions.explanation: A Stage Two review either confirms that the Admissions Department will be required to review or revise its decision, or accepts the original decision; the Panel does not issue offers itself.
questions.source_excerpt: The review will lead to one of the following outcomes: ... To confirm that the Admissions Department will be required to review or revise their decision in respect of the applicant; To accept the original decision of the Admissions Department and to issue a letter stating this.

questions.question: An Appeal Panel has met to consider an applicant's Stage Two review request. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, by when should the outcome be issued to the applicant?
options: Within 10 working days of the Panel meeting
Within 15 working days of the Panel meeting
Within 15 working days of submitting the Stage Two form
Within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
questions.explanation: At Stage Two, the outcome is issued to the applicant within 15 working days of the Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: Outcome issued to applicant within 15 working days of Panel

questions.question: An unsuccessful applicant emails admission@lcc.ac.uk asking why they were not offered a place. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which role is responsible for providing feedback to unsuccessful applicants?
options: The Admissions Manager
The Registrar
The Programme Leader for the course
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer
questions.explanation: Feedback requests go to the Admissions Department by email in the first instance, and the Admissions Manager is responsible for providing feedback to unsuccessful applicants.
questions.source_excerpt: should contact the Admissions Department in the first instance by emailing: admission@lcc.ac.uk ... Admissions Manager ... 5.1.2. Responsible for providing feedback to unsuccessful applicants.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, the MRAC analyses admission data alongside progression, retention, withdrawal, transfer and non-completion data. What does it use this analysis to evaluate?
options: Whether each admissions officer has met their individual recruitment targets for the intake
Which Stage Two review requests should be referred on to an Appeal Panel for a decision
The extent to which the procedures support LCC's mission and its strategic objectives
Which unsuccessful applicants should be allowed to reapply within the same intake
questions.explanation: The MRAC considers admission data alongside progression, retention, withdrawal, transfer and non-completion data, and evaluates the extent to which the procedures support LCC's mission and strategic objectives.
questions.source_excerpt: The MRAC conducts an analysis of recruitment, selection, and admission data, considered alongside data such as progression and retention rates of students, withdrawal and transfer, and reasons for non-completion and evaluates the extent to which the procedures support LCC's mission and the achievement of its strategic objectives.

questions.question: An unsuccessful applicant received their decision 10 working days ago, then discussed it informally with admissions staff. Still unhappy, they want to escalate. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what applies?
options: They may lodge a Stage One appeal, which must be received within 15 working days of the informal feedback
They should request a Stage Two review, which must be submitted within 10 working days of the informal feedback
They may proceed to a Stage One appeal, which must be received within 15 working days of the original decision
They must first raise a complaint, which must be lodged within 15 working days of the original application decision
questions.explanation: If informal resolution does not address the applicant's concerns they can proceed to the formal stage, and the Stage One deadline runs from the original application decision, not from the informal feedback.
questions.source_excerpt: Should an applicant's concerns not be satisfactorily addressed, they can proceed to the formal stage. ... Appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original application decision

questions.question: An applicant submits a Stage One Admission Appeal Form, but it only complains about how a staff member treated them during the application process, not about the decision. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what can the Registrar's initial evaluation lead to?
options: Referral to a different procedure, as complaints about the application process use the complaints procedure
Referral to a nominated appeal reviewer, as any concern raised on a Stage One form must be investigated
Referral to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer, as conduct concerns are dealt with at the Stage Two review
Referral to an Appeal Panel, as allegations about a staff member's conduct need additional impartial expertise
questions.explanation: The Registrar's initial evaluation checks the appeal was submitted under the correct procedures and may refer the applicant to a different procedure; complaints about the application process go through the College's complaints procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: the Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation to check that the applicant's academic appeal was submitted under the correct procedures ... The applicant is being referred to a different procedure. ... An applicant who wishes to make a complaint about the application process may do so using the College's complaints procedure.

questions.question: A Stage One admissions appeal arrives on time and on the correct form, but its only argument is that the interviewer judged the applicant too harshly. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what should follow the Registrar's initial evaluation?
options: A nominated reviewer with no previous involvement in the matter re-examines the interview
The appeal goes to an Appeal Panel so that impartial experts can reassess the interview
The appeal is passed to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer as a Stage Two review request
It is rejected as not made for valid reasons, and the Registrar writes to tell the applicant
questions.explanation: Disagreeing with the interviewer's judgement is neither of the two permitted grounds, so the appeal is rejected as not made for valid reasons and the applicant receives a letter from the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following two grounds: ... Appeals put forward on any other grounds will not be considered. ... The appeal is being rejected if it is not made for valid reasons, in which case the applicant shall receive a letter from the Registrar informing them of this outcome.

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which of the following is not among the courses of action a Stage One appeal reviewer has authority to take?
options: Investigating the appeal and requesting any of the supporting documents that are required
Referring the appeal to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer for a Stage Two review
Approving the validity of an appeal that has been received, following an investigation
Forming an Appeal Panel in cases where additional impartial expertise is required to decide
questions.explanation: The reviewer may investigate and request documents, approve an appeal's validity, or form an Appeal Panel; a Stage Two review is only started by the applicant submitting the Stage Two form to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: The appeal reviewer has authority to take the following courses of action: ... To investigate the appeal and request any supporting documents required. To approve the validity of any appeal received following investigation. To form an Appeal Panel in cases where additional impartial expertise is required to decide. ... An applicant who wishes to have the Stage One decision reviewed

questions.question: Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, how does the way a case reaches an Appeal Panel differ between Stage One and Stage Two of the admissions appeals process?
options: Stage One: the Registrar refers every appeal found to be valid to a Panel; Stage Two: the applicant decides whether a Panel should sit to hear their case
Stage One: a Panel sits only if the applicant asks for a formal hearing; Stage Two: the Registrar refers every request received to a Panel for a decision
Stage One: the reviewer forms one where impartial expertise is required; Stage Two: the Senior Quality Assurance Officer refers requests on reasonable grounds
Stage One: a Panel sits only for appeals lodged after the deadline; Stage Two: the Admissions Manager refers requests that meet the programme entry criteria
questions.explanation: At Stage One the appeal reviewer may form an Appeal Panel where additional impartial expertise is required; at Stage Two the Senior Quality Assurance Officer refers requests deemed to be on reasonable grounds to an Appeal Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: To form an Appeal Panel in cases where additional impartial expertise is required to decide. ... If the request is deemed to be on reasonable grounds, the Senior Quality Assurance Officer will refer it to an Appeal Panel.

questions.question: An applicant received their Stage One appeal outcome 8 working days ago and plans to hand a Stage Two Admission Appeal form to the Registrar, who handled Stage One. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what is the position?
options: The plan is correct, as the Stage Two form goes to the Registrar within 15 working days of the outcome
They are in time, but the form must go to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee)
They are out of time, as a Stage Two request must be made within 5 working days of the Stage One outcome
They are out of time, as the Stage Two form must reach the Registrar within 7 working days of the outcome
questions.explanation: A Stage Two request must be submitted within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome, so 8 working days is in time, but it goes to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), not the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: An applicant who wishes to have the Stage One decision reviewed must complete the Stage Two Admission Appeal form and submit it to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.

questions.question: A Stage Two review request argues only that the applicant would perform better at a second interview; it raises no new evidence and no procedural issue. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what should happen to the request?
options: It is rejected as outside the limited grounds, and the applicant is issued with a letter stating this
It is referred to an Appeal Panel, since every Stage Two request must be heard by a Panel in person
It is returned to the Registrar so that a nominated reviewer can arrange a second admission interview
It is passed to the Admissions Officer, who arranges a second interview with a Personal Tutor
questions.explanation: A Stage Two request must be based on the limited grounds (new material evidence, a procedurally incorrect decision, or procedural unfairness in the appeals process); if it is rejected, the applicant is issued with a letter stating this.
questions.source_excerpt: A request for a review must be based on the following limited grounds: ... If the request is deemed to be on reasonable grounds, the Senior Quality Assurance Officer will refer it to an Appeal Panel. However, if the request is rejected, the applicant shall be issued with a letter stating this.

questions.question: Across both stages of the admissions appeals process in the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which two deadlines are set at 15 working days?
options: Receipt of a Stage One appeal after the decision, and submission of a Stage Two form after the Stage One outcome
Issue of the Stage One decision to the applicant, and issue of the Stage Two outcome after the Panel has met
Submission of a Stage Two form after the Stage One outcome, and issue of the Stage One decision to the applicant
Receipt of a Stage One appeal after the original decision, and issue of the Stage Two outcome after the Panel
questions.explanation: A Stage One appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original decision and the Stage Two outcome is issued within 15 working days of the Panel; the other two deadlines are 10 working days.
questions.source_excerpt: Appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original application decision Decision to be issued to the applicant within 10 working days ... Must be made within 10 working days of Stage One outcome Outcome issued to applicant within 15 working days of Panel

questions.question: A refused applicant realises they forgot to include a relevant certificate with their application; nothing prevented them from supplying it. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which statement is accurate?
options: They may reapply within the same intake, provided the missing certificate is included with the new application
They may lodge a Stage One appeal, as any document not seen during the admissions process is a valid ground
They cannot reapply within the same intake, and new information is a ground only if exceptional circumstances prevented it
They should use the complaints procedure, which lets a refused application be reconsidered with new documents
questions.explanation: Unsuccessful applicants cannot reapply within the same intake, and new information is a Stage One ground only where exceptional circumstances meant the applicant was unable to provide it earlier.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants who are unsuccessful are not permitted to reapply within the same intake. ... In instances where there is new information that was not made available during the admissions process because the applicant was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances to provide it earlier in the process.

questions.question: To save time, an admissions team proposes holding all decisions for an intake and notifying every applicant together once the last application has been processed. What does the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy require instead?
options: Decisions are released only after the Admissions Manager signs off the full intake
Decisions are recorded and conveyed to applicants at the earliest opportunity
Decisions are conveyed within 15 working days of each applicant's interview
Decisions are conveyed at induction, once the programme's places are confirmed
questions.explanation: The policy requires all admission decisions to be recorded and conveyed to prospective applicants at the earliest opportunity, so batching them until the end of the intake does not comply.
questions.source_excerpt: All admission decisions are recorded and conveyed to prospective applicants at the earliest opportunity

questions.question: An applicant with no English language qualification says they completed their final two years of school at an English-speaking institution but cannot provide any evidence of this. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what applies?
options: They are invited to take an appropriate English test as advised by LCC
Their own declaration is accepted, so no English test or evidence is needed
They must obtain IELTS 7.0 externally before the application can proceed
Their English is assessed through an RPL claim approved by a Programme Leader
questions.explanation: Applicants without comparable English qualifications, and those who cannot provide evidence of their English language schooling, are invited to take an appropriate test as advised by LCC.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants who do not already possess comparable qualifications in the English Language, as well as those who cannot provide evidence of their English language schooling, are invited to take an appropriate test as advised by LCC.

questions.question: An applicant without a comparable English qualification has been invited to take an internal English test. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which role coordinates internal English tests, and with whom?
options: The Personal Tutor, in liaison with the Programme Leader for the course
The Registrar, in liaison with the Senior Quality Assurance Officer
The Admissions Manager, in liaison with the awarding body's English moderator
The Admissions Officer, in liaison with the External English Assessor
questions.explanation: Applicants without comparable English qualifications are invited to take an appropriate test, and the Admissions Officer liaises with the External English Assessor to coordinate internal English tests.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants who do not already possess comparable qualifications in the English Language ... are invited to take an appropriate test as advised by LCC. ... Admissions Officer ... Liaises with the External English Assessor to coordinate internal English tests

questions.question: Applicant A wants exemption from a module through RPL. Applicant B lacks certificated qualifications and seeks entry through prior experiential learning. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, who approves A's RPL decision and who gives final sign-off on B's application?
options: A: the Senior Admissions Officer; B: the relevant programme leader or their line manager
A: the relevant programme leader or their line manager; B: the Senior Admissions Officer
A: the Personal Tutor who guided the claim; B: the interviewer who assessed the learning
A: the Registrar after an initial evaluation; B: the Senior Quality Assurance Officer
questions.explanation: RPL decisions for module exemption must be approved by the relevant programme leaders or their line managers, whereas for entry through prior experiential learning the Senior Admissions Officer gives final sign-off.
questions.source_excerpt: must be approved by the relevant programme leaders or their line managers. ... Certain courses allow prospective students to use their prior experiential learning to gain entry to the course ... the Senior Admissions Officer shall be responsible for the final sign-off on the application.

questions.question: A programme leader wants to approve an RPL module exemption quickly, using a local checklist that departs from the awarding body's requirements. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, is this permitted?
options: Yes, since approving RPL decisions is the programme leader's own responsibility under the policy
Yes, provided the Personal Tutor who guided the applicant's RPL application agrees to the checklist
No; all RPL decisions must be processed in line with the requirements of the awarding bodies
No; RPL exemptions may only be approved by the Registrar once the applicant has enrolled
questions.explanation: Although programme leaders (or their line managers) approve RPL decisions, every RPL decision must be processed in line with the requirements of the awarding bodies.
questions.source_excerpt: All RPL decisions are to be processed in line with the requirements of the awarding bodies and must be approved by the relevant programme leaders or their line managers.

questions.question: A proposed admissions rule would apply equally to every applicant but would particularly disadvantage applicants of one religion. What does the equality commitment in the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy say about this?
options: It is covered: the College commits to eliminating unlawful indirect as well as direct discrimination
It is acceptable, because the commitment covers direct discrimination against individuals only
It is acceptable, provided the rule is applied consistently and published to all applicants
It is a matter for the Registrar only if an affected applicant makes a formal complaint
questions.explanation: The College commits to equality of opportunity irrespective of religion or belief and to eliminating all aspects of unlawful direct and indirect discrimination, so a uniformly applied rule is not automatically acceptable.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is committed to providing equality of opportunity for all, irrespective of: ... Religion or belief ... Eliminating all aspects of unlawful direct and indirect discrimination, intimidation, harassment, and victimisation.

questions.question: An application meets the programme's entry criteria, but one piece of relevant documentation is still outstanding. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, what must the Admissions Manager's final sign-off ensure?
options: Only that entry criteria are met, as missing documents can be supplied at induction
Only that a Personal Tutor recommended the applicant at their admission interview
That the entry criteria are met and all relevant documentation has been provided
That the Registrar has checked the documents under the Stage One initial evaluation
questions.explanation: The Admissions Manager's final sign-off ensures both that programme entry criteria are met and that all relevant documentation has been provided, so the outstanding document must be resolved first.
questions.source_excerpt: Provides final sign-off on all applications, ensuring that programme entry criteria are met, and that all relevant documentation has been provided.

questions.question: During an admission period the Registrar processes a Stage One appeal and a complaint about the application process. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, how do these feed into the monitoring of admissions procedures?
options: The Senior Quality Assurance Officer reports them to the MRAC with the Stage Two review outcomes
The Registrar summarises them in a report to the MRAC on complaints and appeals received
The Admissions Manager includes them in the MRAC report on the outcomes of the Induction survey
The Programme Leader summarises them for the awarding body as part of the Induction Programme
questions.explanation: The Registrar processes admission appeals and complaints and provides the MRAC, which monitors the procedures, with a report summarising the complaints and appeals received during the admission period.
questions.source_excerpt: Processes Appeals and Complaints relating to Admission. ... LCC's Recruitment, Selection and Admission Procedures are monitored by the MRAC. ... The Registrar provides the MRAC with a report summarising any Complaints and Appeals received during the admission period.

questions.question: An applicant was rejected for failing to meet a criterion that had never been published or made available to applicants. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, could this support a Stage One appeal?
options: Yes; entry requirements must be clear and made available, and evidence the policy was not followed is a ground
No; disputes about entry criteria can only be raised through the College's complaints procedure instead
No; a Stage One appeal is permitted only where new information has come to light owing to exceptional circumstances
No; the applicant must reapply within the same intake so that the unpublished criterion can be assessed properly
questions.explanation: Entry requirements must be clear and made available to applicants, so selecting on an unpublished criterion is evidence the policy was not followed, which is one of the two permitted Stage One grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: Selection processes for entry into the Programmes are underpinned by entry requirements that are clear and made available to applicants. ... In circumstances where there is evidence that the College's Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy has not been followed.

questions.question: An applicant who was eventually offered a place is unhappy with how slowly and poorly the admissions process was handled and wants the matter formally raised. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which route applies and which role processes it?
options: A Stage One appeal submitted via reception, which the Registrar evaluates against the two permitted grounds
The College's complaints procedure, with complaints relating to admission processed by the Registrar
