A feedback request emailed to admission@lcc.ac.uk, which the Admissions Manager is responsible for answering
A Stage Two review request, which the Senior Quality Assurance Officer refers to an Appeal Panel
questions.explanation: Complaints about the application process go through the College's complaints procedure, and the Registrar processes complaints relating to admission; appeals challenge selection decisions and feedback is for applicants not offered a place.
questions.source_excerpt: An applicant who wishes to make a complaint about the application process may do so using the College's complaints procedure. ... Registrar 5.5.1. Processes Appeals and Complaints relating to Admission.

questions.question: A refused applicant wants (a) to understand why they were not offered a place and (b) to challenge the refusal, having evidence the admissions policy was not followed. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which routes apply?
options: (a) Email the Admissions Department at admission@lcc.ac.uk; (b) submit a Stage One Admission Appeal Form via reception for the Registrar
(a) Email the Admissions Department at admission@lcc.ac.uk; (b) raise a complaint under the College's complaints procedure
(a) Submit a Stage One Admission Appeal Form via reception; (b) send a Stage Two Admission Appeal form to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer
(a) Use the College's complaints procedure; (b) send a Stage One Admission Appeal Form to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer
questions.explanation: Feedback is requested from the Admissions Department by emailing admission@lcc.ac.uk, while a refusal is challenged by a Stage One appeal submitted via reception for the Registrar; the complaints procedure cannot be used to challenge an academic decision to refuse.
questions.source_excerpt: should contact the Admissions Department in the first instance by emailing: admission@lcc.ac.uk ... An applicant wishing to make an appeal must do so by completing the Stage One Admission Appeal Form ... submitted via reception for the attention of the Registrar ... the complaints procedure cannot be used to challenge an academic decision to refuse an application.

questions.question: A Stage One admissions appeal passes the Registrar's initial evaluation and is found to be on valid grounds. The Registrar, who has had no previous involvement in the matter, wants to conduct the review personally. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, is this permitted?
options: No; the Registrar only screens appeals, so an appeal reviewer must always be nominated to investigate
No; an appeal found to be on valid grounds must be referred straight to an Appeal Panel to decide
Yes; the Registrar may either conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate
No; once an appeal is found valid, the Senior Quality Assurance Officer must conduct the review
questions.explanation: Where an appeal is on valid grounds the Registrar shall conduct the review or nominate a reviewer; an Appeal Panel is formed only where additional impartial expertise is required, and the Senior Quality Assurance Officer's role arises at Stage Two.
questions.source_excerpt: If the appeal is based on valid grounds, the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim. This will be a member of staff who has had no previous involvement in the matter. ... To form an Appeal Panel in cases where additional impartial expertise is required to decide.

questions.question: An applicant's Stage One appeal was received 14 working days after the original decision. They then received the Stage One outcome and, 12 working days later, submitted a Stage Two form to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer. Under the Recruitment, Selection and Admissions Policy, which is correct?
options: Both were in time, as each stage allows 15 working days from the preceding decision or outcome
The Stage One appeal was late, as it had to be received within 10 working days of the decision
Both were late, as each stage allows only 10 working days from the preceding decision or outcome
Stage One was in time, but the Stage Two request was late, as its limit is 10 working days
questions.explanation: A Stage One appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original decision, so 14 days is in time; a Stage Two form must be submitted within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome, so 12 days is late.
questions.source_excerpt: Appeal must be received within 15 working days of the original application decision ... submit it to the Senior Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.

questions.question: You see someone behaving suspiciously near a staff office but are not sure any crime has occurred. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what should you do?
options: Report it immediately to the safeguarding staff, even though it is only suspected
Wait until you have clear evidence of a crime, then report it to the safeguarding staff
Write down what you saw and raise it with your line manager at the next team meeting
Ask the IT helpdesk to check the door access logs before deciding whether to report it
questions.explanation: The policy requires everyone to report all activity of a criminal nature, suspected or real, or any suspicious activity immediately to the safeguarding staff.
questions.source_excerpt: Everyone should report all activity, suspected or real, of a criminal nature or any suspicious activity immediately to the safeguarding staff.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what is the College's duty where there is a cause for concern about the abuse of a vulnerable adult?
options: To conduct its own full investigation into the abuse before informing any outside agency
To take no action until the vulnerable adult submits a formal written complaint
To act and notify the appropriate agencies so they can investigate
To refer the matter to the adult's family to resolve privately
questions.explanation: The policy states it is not the College's responsibility to investigate abuse, but it has a duty to act on a cause for concern and notify the appropriate agencies so they can investigate.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not the College's responsibility to investigate abuse. Nevertheless, it has a duty to act if there is a cause for concern and to notify the appropriate agencies so that they can investigate and take any necessary action.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, who has a legal responsibility to take seriously any vulnerable adult concerns that come to their attention?
options: Designated Persons and senior managers, but not general teaching or support staff
All staff, including agency staff, governors, temporary staff and volunteers
Academic and support staff employed by the College, but not agency staff or volunteers
All permanent staff, but not agency staff, temporary staff or governors
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all staff, including agency staff, governors, temporary staff and volunteers, and states that all have a legal responsibility to take vulnerable adult concerns seriously and follow the procedures given.
questions.source_excerpt: This Policy applies to all staff (including agency staff and governors), academic and support staff employed by the College, temporary staff, and ... volunteers. All have a legal responsibility to take seriously any vulnerable adult concerns that come to their attention and follow the procedures given.

questions.question: A personal tutor becomes concerned about the welfare of a vulnerable adult student. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, which role is the Designated Safeguarding Officer for student-related issues?
options: The Registrar
The HR Manager
The Facilities Manager
The Principal
questions.explanation: The policy's safeguarding structure names the Registrar as the Designated Safeguarding Officer for student-related issues, providing management and coordination.
questions.source_excerpt: For student-related issues: Designated Safeguarding Officer, Registrar provides management and coordination role including investigations if required.

questions.question: You realise you have lost your LCC ID card. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, to whom should you report the loss as soon as possible?
options: The HR Manager
The Registrar
The IT helpdesk
Your line manager
questions.explanation: The policy requires the loss of an LCC ID card to be reported as soon as possible to the IT helpdesk, so that card access can be cancelled.
questions.source_excerpt: Loss of one of these ID cards should be reported, as soon as possible to the IT helpdesk.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what do staff need in order to work in their office outside normal opening hours?
options: Verbal approval from their own line manager
Written permission from the Facilities Manager
Written permission from the HR Manager
An access request logged with the IT helpdesk
questions.explanation: The out-of-hours access procedure states that staff need written permission from the Facilities Manager to work in their office outside normal opening hours.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff who require access to work in their office outside normal opening hours, need written permission from the Facilities Manager.

questions.question: A laptop appears to have been stolen from your department's office. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, who should the suspected theft be reported to promptly?
options: The IT helpdesk, so the laptop can be remotely locked and traced
Both the HR Manager and the Designated Safeguarding Officer
Both the Facilities Manager and the Facilities Officer
Your line manager, at the next scheduled team meeting
questions.explanation: The equipment safeguarding procedure requires suspected thefts of equipment to be reported promptly to both the Facilities Manager and the Facilities Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: Suspected thefts of equipment should be reported promptly to both Facilities Manager and Facilities Officer

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy's safeguarding structure, which role acts as the Designated Safeguarding Officer for staff-related issues?
options: The Registrar
The Facilities Manager
The Principal
The HR Manager
questions.explanation: The policy names the HR Manager as the Designated Safeguarding Officer for staff-related issues, supporting key staff and providing legislative support.
questions.source_excerpt: For staff-related issues: Designated Safeguarding Officer, HR Manager supports key staff and provides legislative support.

questions.question: You are the member of staff responsible for an ad-hoc contractor visiting LCC. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what must you ensure when they sign out to leave the campus?
options: That they return the pass to the IT helpdesk within 24 hours
That their visitor's pass is collected from them
That they keep their pass for any future visits
That the Facilities Manager countersigns their exit
questions.explanation: The policy makes the responsible member of staff ensure the visitor's pass is collected when the visitor or contractor signs out on leaving the campus.
questions.source_excerpt: The member of staff responsible for the visitor/contractor should ensure that they collect the visitor's pass when signing out upon leaving the campus.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what is the role of the two staff identified as Designated Persons for vulnerable adult matters?
options: To receive training and act as a source of advice and support to other staff
To hold overall Board-level responsibility for vulnerable adult matters across the College
To investigate allegations of abuse themselves, in place of the appropriate agencies
To ensure that safeguarding resources and training are properly funded
questions.explanation: The policy states the two Designated Persons receive training and act as a source of advice and support to other College staff, especially personal tutors and front-of-house staff; overall responsibility sits with a Board member and a PEG member.
questions.source_excerpt: By identifying a member of the Board of Directors and a member of the Principal Executive Group (PEG) who have overall responsibility for vulnerable adult matters and two other staff as Designated Persons, who will receive training in this field and act as a source of advice and support to other College staff

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what may happen if a staff member or student fails to show their College card to safeguarding staff on request?
options: An automatic written warning placed on their personnel or student record
A fine deducted from their wages or tuition fees for each refusal
Permanent cancellation of their College card and all building access rights
An immediate request to leave if their identity cannot be confirmed
questions.explanation: The policy states that failure to show a College card on request may result in an immediate request to leave College premises if the person's identity cannot be confirmed.
questions.source_excerpt: All staff and students are required to show their College card to safeguarding staff on request. Failure to do so may result in an immediate request to leave College premises, if a person's identity cannot be confirmed.

questions.question: A student tells you their phone was stolen from a bag left in a classroom and asks whether the College will compensate them. What does the Safeguarding and Security Policy state?
options: The College replaces any stolen item reported to the Safeguarding Team within seven days
The College's insurance policy covers all student personal property while it is on campus
The College is not liable unless its own or its employees' negligence is established
The College is liable if the item was security-marked using the approved method
questions.explanation: The policy states the College does not accept liability for loss or damage to students' personal property unless negligence of the College or its employees can be established, and advises students to insure their own property.
questions.source_excerpt: The College does not accept liability for loss and/or damage to Students personal property unless negligence of the College or its employees can be established. Students are strongly advised to make their own arrangements for insuring their personal property.

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, whose requests must staff cooperate with, especially in emergency or evacuation situations?
options: The Registry team
The Safeguarding Team
The Human Resources team
The local Police liaison officer
questions.explanation: The policy requires all staff to cooperate with requests from the Safeguarding Team, especially in emergency or evacuation situations and in relation to safeguarding procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: They must also cooperate with requests from the Safeguarding Team, especially in emergency or evacuation situations and in relation to safeguarding procedures.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what is the stated responsibility of the College's senior managers in relation to the policy?
options: To personally investigate every reported incident of crime on College premises
To authorise each request for out-of-hours access to College offices
To act as the first point of contact for all safeguarding concerns raised
To ensure support and resources are available to staff to implement the policy
questions.explanation: The policy states that senior management should ensure support and resources are available to staff for the implementation of the Safeguarding & Security Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Senior Managers: the senior management of the College should ensure that support and resources are available to staff for the implementation of the Safeguarding & Security Policy.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, the two Designated Persons for vulnerable adult matters act as a source of advice and support especially to which College staff?
options: Senior managers and heads of department
Facilities Officers and IT helpdesk staff
Personal tutors and front-of-house staff
Agency staff and newly appointed volunteers
questions.explanation: The policy states the Designated Persons act as a source of advice and support to other College staff, especially personal tutors and front-of-house staff.
questions.source_excerpt: two other staff as Designated Persons, who will receive training in this field and act as a source of advice and support to other College staff especially personal tutors and front-of-house staff.

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, how must subcontractors deal with any vulnerable adult concerns that are reported to them?
options: By contacting the College's Designated Person for Vulnerable Adult Protection
By reporting them directly to the Police without first involving the College
By passing them to their own employer's HR department to investigate
By recording them in the Facilities Officer's daily incident log for review
questions.explanation: The policy requires subcontractors to be informed of the policy and to deal with concerns reported to them by contacting the Designated Person with responsibility for Vulnerable Adult Protection.
questions.source_excerpt: Subcontractors must be informed of this Policy and deal with any concerns reported to them by contacting the Designated Person with responsibility for Vulnerable Adult Protection in College.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, who will make patrols of the premises, where available, to help identify safeguarding risks and act as a deterrent against crime?
options: External security contractors
Facilities Officers
Designated Persons
Student ambassadors
questions.explanation: The policy states that, where available, Facilities Officers will patrol the premises to help identify safeguarding risks, monitor public safety and deter crime.
questions.source_excerpt: Where available Facilities Officers will make patrols of the premises, to aid in the identification of safeguarding risks, monitor public safety and act as a deterrent against crime.

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy's safeguarding structure, who provides overall leadership of safeguarding at London Churchill College?
options: The Principal
The HR Manager
The Registrar
The Facilities Manager
questions.explanation: The safeguarding structure names the Principal as having overall leadership of safeguarding; the Registrar and HR Manager are Designated Safeguarding Officers for student and staff issues.
questions.source_excerpt: Principal: Overall leadership of Safeguarding

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, how should College access control cards be regarded for safeguarding purposes?
options: The same as a door code
The same as a visitor badge
The same as a door key
The same as a library card
questions.explanation: The policy states that access cards should be regarded for safeguarding purposes the same as a key, so cardholders must safeguard them and report any loss.
questions.source_excerpt: Access cards should be regarded for safeguarding purposes the same as a key.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what information do the visitor's passes issued to visitors and ad-hoc contractors contain?
options: The host's name and a guest Wi-Fi login code
The visitor's photograph and home address
A map of the areas open to visitors
Emergency and health & safety information
questions.explanation: The policy states visitors and ad-hoc contractors should wear their passes, which contain emergency and health & safety information, throughout their visit.
questions.source_excerpt: Visitors and ad-hoc Contractors will be issued with a ... should wear these passes which contain emergency and health & safety information, throughout their visit to the College.

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, when must staff return keys that were issued to them locally?
options: At the end of each academic term or semester
When they move offices or leave the College
Before any period of annual leave over one week
Whenever the lock on their office is replaced
questions.explanation: The policy requires Facilities Officers to keep a record of keys issued locally and ensure staff return keys when they move offices or leave the College's employment.
questions.source_excerpt: Facilities Officers should keep a record of all keys issued locally and ensure that staff return keys when they move offices or leave the College's employment.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, from whom can advice be sought on marking valuable equipment using the appropriate identification method?
options: The Safeguarding Team and IT helpdesk
The Finance Office and the Registrar
The HR Manager and your line manager
The Principal's Executive Group
questions.explanation: The policy states valuable equipment should be marked using the appropriate identification method, with advice available from the Safeguarding Team and IT helpdesk.
questions.source_excerpt: All valuable equipment should be marked using the appropriate identification method. Advice on this can be sought from the Safeguarding Team and IT helpdesk.

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what is required for a department such as Library Services to operate a local CCTV system in its area?
options: Approval by the Principal and notice in the staff bulletin
Written consent from every student and staff member in the area
Authorisation by the Facilities Manager and compliance with GDPR
Agreement from the local Police and a data-sharing form
questions.explanation: The policy states the operation of local CCTV systems and any future departmental installations must be authorised by the Facilities Manager and comply with the GDPR.
questions.source_excerpt: The operation of these systems and any future installations in departmental areas, must be authorised by the Facilities Manager and comply with the GDPR.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, as well as helping to identify and prosecute offenders, what may College CCTV be used to provide evidence for?
options: Staff performance appraisals
Student attendance monitoring
Overtime and timesheet checks
Internal disciplinary hearings
questions.explanation: One stated objective of the College's CCTV is to secure evidence to identify, apprehend and prosecute offenders and to provide evidence for internal disciplinary hearings.
questions.source_excerpt: Assist in the detection, deterrence, and prevention of crime on campus by securing evidence to identify, apprehend and prosecute offenders and to provide evidence for internal disciplinary hearings.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what must apply to any request by the Police to remove College CCTV recordings?
options: It must comply with GDPR and be registered
It must be approved in writing by the Principal
It must be refused unless a court order is produced
It must be referred to the Registrar within 48 hours
questions.explanation: The policy states that requests by the Police to remove CCTV recordings must comply with the GDPR and will be registered accordingly.
questions.source_excerpt: Requests by Police to remove CCTV recordings must comply with the ... GDPR and will be registered accordingly.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, why is incident reporting by staff and students described as crucial?
options: It is required for any College insurance claim
It helps identify patterns of criminal activity
It determines the outcome of disciplinary cases
It is needed for the Police's annual crime statistics
questions.explanation: The policy states incident reporting is crucial to the identification of patterns of criminal activity, allowing investigation and recommendations to prevent a recurrence.
questions.source_excerpt: Incident reporting is crucial to the identification of patterns of criminal activity.

questions.question: According to the aim of the Safeguarding and Security Policy, to what extent will the College endeavour to ensure the personal safety and safeguarding of students, staff and bona fide visitors on its premises?
options: Only during normal opening hours
As far as is reasonably practical
Only in card-controlled areas
In all circumstances, without limit
questions.explanation: The policy's aim is that the College will endeavour to ensure personal safety and safeguarding as far as is reasonably practical, for all students, staff and bona fide visitors on its premises.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will endeavour to ensure, as far as is reasonably practical, the personal safety and safeguarding of all students, staff, and bona fide visitors on LCC's premises.

questions.question: During a fire evacuation, a visitor you are hosting asks whose directions they should follow. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, whose instructions must visitors follow, particularly in emergency situations?
options: The Registrar, as Designated Safeguarding Officer
The IT helpdesk, which issued their pass
Any front-of-house volunteer on duty
The Safeguarding Team or their host department
questions.explanation: The policy states visitors must follow instructions from the Safeguarding Team or from their host department, particularly in emergency situations.
questions.source_excerpt: Visitors must follow instructions from the Safeguarding Team or from their host department, particularly in emergency situations.

questions.question: A lecturer leaves their College ID card in their office while teaching in another building on campus. What does the Safeguarding and Security Policy require of staff regarding their ID cards?
options: To carry it at all times on College premises, under their employment contract
To carry it only when entering areas with card-controlled barriers or doors
To carry it only outside normal opening hours, when buildings are locked
To carry it only when meeting visitors or contractors for the College
questions.explanation: The policy states staff are required, under the terms of their employment contracts, to carry their ID card at all times whilst on College premises.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff are required under the terms of their employment contracts, to carry their ID card at all times whilst on College premises.

questions.question: A department head identifies a necessary measure to improve safeguarding in an essential area of the College. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, how should senior management treat such measures?
options: They should be funded from the proposing department's budget
They should wait for the next annual budget review
They should receive priority consideration
They should first be approved by the Police
questions.explanation: The policy states that necessary measures to improve safeguarding in essential areas should receive priority consideration from senior management.
questions.source_excerpt: Necessary measures to improve safeguarding in essential areas should receive priority consideration.

questions.question: In a seminar, a student expresses violent extremist views and claims freedom of speech protects them. How does the open culture described in the Safeguarding and Security Policy treat this?
options: It permits violent extremist views in an academic setting if no one is named
It treats freedom of speech as overriding all other considerations in teaching
It accepts violent extremist views unless another student complains
It recognises freedom of speech but does not accept violent extremist views
questions.explanation: The College's open culture recognises the right to freedom of speech but does not accept the expression of violent extremist views.
questions.source_excerpt: Through the creation of an open culture which respects all individuals' rights, discourages bullying and discrimination of all kinds and, while recognising the right to freedom of speech, does not accept the expression of violent extremist views.

questions.question: A student tells you they are worried about the way an adult at the College behaves towards them. According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what can the student use the policy to do?
options: Require the College to investigate the adult itself
Ensure that their concerns are taken seriously
Obtain compensation for any distress caused
Have the adult removed from campus at once
questions.explanation: The policy states that students who have concerns about other students or the behaviour of adults towards them can use the policy to ensure they are taken seriously.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who have concerns about other students or the behaviour of adults towards them can use this Policy to ensure they are taken seriously.

questions.question: According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, who has been identified as having overall responsibility for vulnerable adult matters at the College?
options: A member of the Board of Directors and a member of the PEG
The two Designated Persons trained in vulnerable adult matters
The Registrar and the HR Manager as Designated Safeguarding Officers
The Facilities Manager and the College Safeguarding Team
questions.explanation: The policy identifies a member of the Board of Directors and a member of the Principal Executive Group (PEG) as having overall responsibility for vulnerable adult matters; the two Designated Persons provide advice and support.
questions.source_excerpt: By identifying a member of the Board of Directors and a member of the Principal Executive Group (PEG) who have overall responsibility for vulnerable adult matters and two other staff as Designated Persons

questions.question: You are leaving your shared office for a short meeting and your wallet is on your desk. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy's crime prevention procedure, what should you do with it?
options: Leave it on the desk, as the office has a card-controlled door
Leave it where it is if you expect to be back within 15 minutes
Lock it away, put it out of sight or keep it on your person
Hand it to the nearest Facilities Officer for safekeeping
questions.explanation: The procedure states personal valuables should be locked away, placed out of sight or kept on the person, and personal property should never be left unattended.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal valuables should be locked away or placed out of sight or kept on the person, and personal property should never be left unattended;

questions.question: A colleague thinks there is no point reporting a minor theft from the staff room. According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what does comprehensive reporting of incidents achieve?
options: It lets the College recover the cost of stolen items from its insurers
It removes the need for Police involvement in lower-value thefts
It automatically triggers a review of CCTV footage for that area
It gives an accurate picture of crime so adequate resources are provided
questions.explanation: The policy states comprehensive reporting provides an accurate picture of the level of crime throughout the College and ensures adequate resources are provided to combat it.
questions.source_excerpt: Comprehensive reporting of incidents provides an accurate picture of the level of crime throughout the College and thus ensures that adequate resources are provided to combat that crime.

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, why must a cardholder report the loss of their College access card to the IT helpdesk as soon as possible?
options: So the card access can be cancelled
So a disciplinary note can be recorded
So a replacement fee can be charged
So the Police can be told of the loss
questions.explanation: The policy requires cardholders to report any loss to the IT helpdesk as soon as possible so the card access can be cancelled, as access cards are treated like keys.
questions.source_excerpt: Cardholders must safeguard their card and report any loss to the IT helpdesk as soon as possible, so the card access can be cancelled

questions.question: You discover that the office key issued to you by your department is missing. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what must you do?
options: Report it to the IT helpdesk so the key can be cancelled
Report the loss immediately to the Facilities Manager
Ask your department to issue a new key and log it locally
Report it to the Registrar at the end of the working week
questions.explanation: The policy makes everyone issued keys or cards responsible for their safe keeping and for reporting any loss immediately to the Facilities Manager.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the responsibility of all individuals who are always issued keys or cards to ensure their safe keeping and report any loss immediately to the Facilities Manager.

questions.question: Staff in your building are asked to show their College cards as part of a random check. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, who may arrange such random checks?
options: The IT helpdesk team, liaising with the Human Resources team
The Designated Safeguarding Officers, liaising with Police
The College Management Team, liaising with the Facilities Team
The Registrar's office, liaising with the Students' Union
questions.explanation: The policy states the College Management Team may liaise with the Facilities Team to arrange random checks of College cards and Student cards.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Management Team may liaise with the Facilities Team to arrange for random checks of College cards and Student cards.

questions.question: The College operates a suited key system for new premises and refurbishments. According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, how do operator keys and master keys differ?
options: An operator key opens one building; a master key opens the whole campus
An operator key opens one floor; a master key opens one department
An operator key opens one department; a master key opens one floor
An operator key opens one room; a master key opens a building
questions.explanation: The suited key system allows various levels of access, from an operator key for one room to a master key for a building.
questions.source_excerpt: the College operates a suited key system which allows various levels of access (an `operator key' for one room, to a `master key' for a building).

questions.question: Your department wants to fit its own lock to a storage cupboard to protect equipment. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what is required before any such lock is installed?
options: The approval of the head of department
The authority of the Facilities Manager
A spare key lodged with the IT helpdesk
Written consent from the Safeguarding Team
questions.explanation: The policy states no other lock or key should be installed on College premises without the authority of the Facilities Manager.
questions.source_excerpt: No other lock or key should be installed on College premises without the authority of the Facilities Manager.

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy's rules on locks and keys, which keys may be issued to departments for local use and for issue to individual staff?
options: Operator keys or sub master keys
Sub master keys or full master keys
Master keys only, with written approval
Any level of key, if it is recorded locally
questions.explanation: The policy states operator keys or sub master keys may be issued to departments for local use and issue to individual staff; master keys are not included.
questions.source_excerpt: Operator keys or sub master keys may be issued to departments for local use and issue to individual staff.

questions.question: You take a department laptop to an off-site conference. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, does the need to physically protect IT and AV equipment still apply?
options: No, the equipment rules apply only while it is on College premises
Only if the laptop holds personal data covered by the GDPR
Yes, physical protection of this equipment matters on and off campus
Only if the laptop was signed out through the IT helpdesk first
questions.explanation: The policy states that the physical protection of IT and AV equipment is important both on and off campus.
questions.source_excerpt: The physical protection of IT and AV equipment is important on and off campus.

questions.question: At the end of the working day you have finished using a department laptop. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy's equipment procedure, what must you do with it?
options: Leave it on the desk with the screen locked and the door shut
Leave it docked and switched on so overnight updates install
Hand it in to the Facilities Officer on the evening patrol
Lock it away out of sight until it is next needed
questions.explanation: The procedure requires valuable portable IT and AV equipment such as laptops to be locked away out of sight when not in use, especially overnight.
questions.source_excerpt: All valuable portable IT and AV equipment such as laptops, must be locked away out of sight when not in use, especially overnight.

questions.question: A local police team asks to use the College CCTV system for a training exercise. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, on what basis may this be allowed?
options: On request, as the Police may always access CCTV
By prior arrangement with the Facilities Manager
Only with a court order obtained for the exercise
With the written consent of the Registrar
questions.explanation: The Police should not generally access College CCTV, except in listed circumstances including liaison and training purposes by prior arrangement with the Facilities Manager.
questions.source_excerpt: In general, the Police should not require access to (nor be allowed access to) College CCTV systems except under the following circumstances: ... Liaison and training purposes, by prior arrangement with the Facilities ... Manager

questions.question: A visitor says the cameras around the campus make them feel safer. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, which stated objective of the College's CCTV monitoring does this reflect?
options: Reducing the fear of crime and offering public reassurance
Monitoring visitor numbers for fire evacuation purposes
Supporting the visitor sign-in and pass return process
Recording visitor movements for their host departments
questions.explanation: One stated objective of the College's CCTV monitoring is to reduce the fear of crime and offer public reassurance for all students, staff and visitors to the campus.
questions.source_excerpt: Reduce the fear of crime and offer public reassurance for all students, staff, and visitors to the campus.

questions.question: A visitor on campus sees someone trying the handles of locked office doors and asks whether reporting is only a duty for staff and students. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what is the position?
options: Visitors should tell their host, who decides whether to report it after the visit
Only staff and students must report; visitors have no reporting responsibility
Everyone, visitors included, should report it immediately to the safeguarding staff
Visitors should report it only once it is clear that a crime has been committed
questions.explanation: The policy places responsibility for safeguarding on students, staff and visitors alike and says everyone should report suspicious activity immediately to the safeguarding staff; it is not limited to staff and students or to confirmed crimes.
questions.source_excerpt: Responsibility for safeguarding rests with all students, staff, and visitors to the College. Everyone should report all activity, suspected or real, of a criminal nature or any suspicious activity immediately to the safeguarding staff.

questions.question: During an evacuation, a new colleague asks whose requests staff and students are each specifically told to cooperate with. According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, which pairing is correct?
options: Staff: the Safeguarding Team; students: the Facilities Team
Staff: the Facilities Team; students: the Safeguarding Team
Staff and students: their Designated Safeguarding Officer
Staff: the Facilities Manager; students: their personal tutor
questions.explanation: The staff responsibilities name the Safeguarding Team, while the student responsibilities name the Facilities Team, in each case especially in emergency or evacuation situations.
questions.source_excerpt: They must also cooperate with requests from the Safeguarding Team, especially in emergency or evacuation situations ... Students must cooperate with requests from the Facilities Team, especially in emergency or evacuation situations

questions.question: A student plans to bring an expensive laptop to campus and asks whether they must arrange insurance for it. What does the Safeguarding and Security Policy say about students insuring their personal property?
options: They must register it with the IT helpdesk to be covered by College insurance
They are required to take out insurance before bringing it onto College premises
It is covered by College insurance while it is kept in a locked College room
They are strongly advised to make their own arrangements for insuring it
questions.explanation: Insurance is strongly advised, not required, and the College does not accept liability for students' personal property unless its own or its employees' negligence is established.
questions.source_excerpt: The College does not accept liability for loss and/or damage to Students personal property unless negligence of the College or its employees can be established. Students are strongly advised to make their own arrangements for insuring their personal property.

questions.question: An agency cleaner and a worker employed by a catering subcontractor both hear a concern about a vulnerable adult. How does the Safeguarding and Security Policy treat each of them?
options: Neither is covered, as the policy applies only to staff the College employs directly
The agency cleaner is covered as staff; the subcontractor must contact the Designated Person
The subcontractor is covered as staff; the agency cleaner must contact the Designated Person
Both must report the concern straight to the Police without involving the College
questions.explanation: The policy's scope expressly includes agency staff, whereas subcontractors must be informed of the policy and deal with concerns by contacting the Designated Person for Vulnerable Adult Protection.
questions.source_excerpt: This Policy applies to all staff (including agency staff and governors), academic and support staff employed by the College, temporary staff, and ... Subcontractors must be informed of this Policy and deal with any concerns reported to them by contacting the Designated Person with responsibility for Vulnerable Adult Protection in College.

questions.question: A personal tutor suspects a vulnerable adult student is being abused and plans to interview the people involved to establish the facts before telling anyone. What approach does the Safeguarding and Security Policy support?
options: Carry out the interviews first, as personal tutors investigate abuse on the College's behalf
Refer it to the HR Manager, who investigates all abuse concerns about students
Seek advice from a Designated Person, as agencies, not the College, investigate abuse
Note it on the student's file and review it at the next scheduled tutorial
questions.explanation: Designated Persons act as a source of advice and support especially to personal tutors, and the College does not investigate abuse itself: it must act on a cause for concern and notify the appropriate agencies.
questions.source_excerpt: two other staff as Designated Persons, who will receive training in this field and act as a source of advice and support to other College staff especially personal tutors ... It is not the College's responsibility to investigate abuse. Nevertheless, it has a duty to act if there is a cause for concern and to notify the appropriate agencies

questions.question: A manager argues that safeguarding arrangements should cover every conceivable risk, however small and whatever the cost. Which principle in the Safeguarding and Security Policy does this approach conflict with?
options: Arrangements should be proportionate and based upon common sense
Arrangements must be agreed with the Police before they are adopted
Arrangements are set by each department without central guidance
Arrangements apply only to students who are vulnerable adults
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College's safeguarding arrangements are to be proportionate and based upon common sense, which an unlimited, cost-blind approach contradicts.
questions.source_excerpt: The College seeks to ensure that its policy and procedures comply with statutory duties; reflect guidance and good practice in safeguarding vulnerable adults; and that safeguarding arrangements are proportionate and based upon common sense.

questions.question: The Safeguarding and Security Policy's crime prevention procedure treats personal valuables and portable IT equipment differently. Which statement correctly describes the difference?
options: Both may simply be placed out of sight, provided the room has a card-controlled door
Valuables must be handed to a Facilities Officer on patrol; IT equipment may stay on open desks
Valuables must always be locked away; IT equipment needs locking away only at weekends
Valuables may be locked away, hidden or kept on you; IT equipment must be locked out of sight
questions.explanation: Personal valuables may be locked away, placed out of sight or kept on the person, whereas IT and other portable equipment must be locked out of sight when not in use, particularly overnight.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal valuables should be locked away or placed out of sight or kept on the person, and personal property should never be left unattended; ... IT Equipment and other portable equipment should be locked out of sight when not in use, particularly overnight, in closed areas.

questions.question: To save time, a manager plans to collect suspected crimes in their area and report them to the Safeguarding Team in a single monthly summary. Which statement in the Safeguarding and Security Policy does this plan conflict with?
options: Incident reports should always reach the Police before the Safeguarding Team is told
Success against crime is greatly enhanced by fast, efficient and detailed reporting
Only incidents confirmed as crimes need to be reported to the Safeguarding Team
Reporting incidents is voluntary for staff but compulsory for students
questions.explanation: The policy requires suspicious activity to be reported immediately and says success against crime is greatly enhanced by fast, efficient and detailed reporting, so batching reports monthly conflicts with it.
questions.source_excerpt: All suspicious activity should be immediately reported as set out in 3.3 below; ... Success in the College's fight against crime is greatly enhanced by fast, efficient, and detailed reporting.

questions.question: Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy's safeguarding structure, which statement correctly contrasts the roles of the two Designated Safeguarding Officers?
options: The HR Manager coordinates student issues and investigations; the Registrar gives legislative support
The Registrar leads safeguarding overall; the HR Manager handles every investigation for staff and students
The Registrar coordinates student issues, including investigations; the HR Manager gives legislative support
Both officers investigate abuse themselves; the Principal then notifies the appropriate outside agencies
questions.explanation: For student-related issues the Registrar provides management and coordination including investigations if required; for staff-related issues the HR Manager supports key staff and provides legislative support.
questions.source_excerpt: For student-related issues: Designated Safeguarding Officer, Registrar provides management and coordination role including investigations if required. ... For staff-related issues: Designated Safeguarding Officer, HR Manager supports key staff and provides legislative support.

questions.question: In a corridor, a lecturer asks a student to show their ID card. The student refuses, saying only safeguarding staff are entitled to ask. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, is the student right?
options: No; students must show their ID card to officers or employees on request
Yes; only safeguarding staff may ask anyone to show a College card
Yes; students must carry their card but never have to show it to staff
No, but only because the student is standing in a card-controlled area
questions.explanation: Students must show their ID card to officers or employees on request, so the duty is not limited to safeguarding staff or to card-controlled areas.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are required to always carry their student ID card with them and to show their ID card to officers or employees on request.

questions.question: A visitor takes off their visitor's pass once their host has signed them in, saying they will only be in one meeting room. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what should happen?
options: Nothing; once the host has signed them in, the pass has served its purpose
They may keep it in a pocket and show it to safeguarding staff on request
They need to wear it only when passing card-controlled barriers or doors
They should wear the pass throughout their visit to the College
questions.explanation: Visitors must always wear their badge where one is issued, and passes are to be worn throughout the visit, not just at entry or in controlled areas.
questions.source_excerpt: They must follow safeguarding procedures designed to protect College property and where issued, always wear their visitors' badge. ... should wear these passes which contain emergency and health & safety information, throughout their visit to the College.

questions.question: A new colleague says card-controlled doors now cover every area of the College, so keys no longer matter. According to the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what is the actual position on access control systems?
options: They now cover the whole College, and all keys have been withdrawn from use
They operate in some areas, and the strategy is to expand them College-wide
They are being phased out and replaced by the College's suited key system
They are limited to computer rooms and will not be expanded any further
questions.explanation: Access control systems currently operate in some areas only, and the safeguarding strategy will move towards expanding them throughout the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Access Control Systems operate in some areas. Card controlled barriers/doors are an effective method of preventing unauthorised access and the safeguarding strategy will move towards expansion of access control systems throughout the College.

questions.question: Your access card still opens your building on a Saturday, outside normal opening hours, and your line manager has verbally agreed you can work there. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what else do you need?
options: Nothing further; a working card and manager approval suffice
Written approval from your line manager, copied to HR
Written permission from the Facilities Manager
A weekend visitor's pass issued by the IT helpdesk
questions.explanation: Working in your office outside normal opening hours needs written permission from the Facilities Manager; a working card or a line manager's verbal agreement does not replace it.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff who require access to work in their office outside normal opening hours, need written permission from the Facilities Manager.

questions.question: Police investigating a serious assault on campus ask to view College CCTV footage that evening, and nothing has been arranged with the Facilities Manager in advance. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, how should the request be treated?
options: It must be refused, as Police access is limited to liaison and training arranged in advance
It must wait for a court order, as the policy permits Police CCTV access only under a warrant
It may be allowed, as investigation of a serious incident is one of the listed circumstances
It may proceed only if a Facilities Officer on patrol agrees to supervise the viewing
questions.explanation: Police should not generally access College CCTV, but emergencies or investigation of serious incidents are a listed circumstance in their own right; prior arrangement with the Facilities Manager applies to liaison and training.
questions.source_excerpt: In general, the Police should not require access to (nor be allowed access to) College CCTV systems except under the following circumstances: ... Emergencies or investigation of serious incidents

questions.question: Your department has been issued sub master keys for local use and hands one to a newly appointed lecturer. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, who should keep a record of this key?
options: The head of department that issued it
The IT helpdesk, with access card records
The HR Manager, on the personnel file
The College's Facilities Officers
questions.explanation: Departments may issue operator or sub master keys locally, but Facilities Officers must keep a record of all keys issued locally and ensure they are returned.
questions.source_excerpt: Operator keys or sub master keys may be issued to departments for local use and issue to individual staff. ... Facilities Officers should keep a record of all keys issued locally and ensure that staff return keys when they move offices or leave the College's employment.

questions.question: Your department receives a delivery of new laptops for staff to share. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy's equipment procedure, which combination of steps applies to them?
options: Register them with the Police and keep them in a card-controlled room by day
Mark them using the appropriate identification method; lock away when not in use
Mark them only if they leave campus, and lock them away only at weekends
Log them with the HR Manager and leave them docked on open desks overnight
questions.explanation: Valuable equipment should be marked using the appropriate identification method, and valuable portable IT equipment such as laptops must be locked away out of sight when not in use.
questions.source_excerpt: All valuable portable IT and AV equipment such as laptops, must be locked away out of sight when not in use, especially overnight. ... All valuable equipment should be marked using the appropriate identification method.

questions.question: A police officer phones asking to view College CCTV of an adjacent street for a routine survey. There is no incident, no offender to identify and nothing arranged with the Facilities Manager. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what applies?
options: Access must be given, as the Police may view College CCTV whenever they ask
Any Facilities Officer may give access, provided the request is logged
Access should not be given unless the Facilities Manager authorises it
Access may be given once the officer signs the GDPR removal register
questions.explanation: In general the Police should not be allowed access to College CCTV except in the listed circumstances; with no emergency, serious incident, offender or prior arrangement, only Facilities Manager authorisation would permit it.
questions.source_excerpt: In general, the Police should not require access to (nor be allowed access to) College CCTV systems except under the following circumstances: ... Identification of offenders ... As authorised by the Facilities Manager

questions.question: Several College roles appear in the Safeguarding and Security Policy. Which of these responsibilities does the policy give to the Facilities Manager?
options: Authorising any other lock to be installed on College premises
Giving advice on how valuable equipment should be marked
Keeping the local record of keys issued to individual staff
Providing overall leadership of safeguarding at the College
questions.explanation: No other lock or key may be installed without the Facilities Manager's authority; marking advice comes from the Safeguarding Team and IT helpdesk, local key records are kept by Facilities Officers, and overall leadership sits with the Principal.
questions.source_excerpt: No other lock or key should be installed on College premises without the authority of the Facilities Manager.

questions.question: A colleague makes several claims about the College's CCTV. Which one is consistent with the Safeguarding and Security Policy?
options: The cameras are hidden so that offenders do not know they are being recorded
Any department may install its own local system as long as it puts up signs
The cameras cover College buildings only and never the adjacent streets
Recorded images are kept securely and in line with GDPR requirements
questions.explanation: Recorded images are kept securely in line with GDPR; the cameras are overt, cover adjacent streets as well as the campus, and local systems need Facilities Manager authorisation.
questions.source_excerpt: The College uses CCTV systems around the campus covering many of the vulnerable areas, public access points and adjacent streets. ... overt cameras ... must be authorised by the Facilities Manager and comply with the GDPR. ... Images will be kept securely and in line with the requirements of GDPR

questions.question: A lecturer loses a wallet holding their College access card and an office key their department issued to them. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, how should each loss be reported?
options: Both to the IT helpdesk, which cancels card access and also records and replaces any lost keys
The card to the IT helpdesk so its access can be cancelled; the key at once to the Facilities Manager
The key to the Facilities Officer who logged it; the card to the Registry so a new one can be printed
Both to the Facilities Officer, who keeps the department's local record of the keys it has issued
questions.explanation: Lost access cards are reported to the IT helpdesk so card access can be cancelled, and lost keys must be reported immediately to the Facilities Manager; Facilities Officers keep the local key record but are not the reporting point for losses.
questions.source_excerpt: Cardholders must safeguard their card and report any loss to the IT helpdesk as soon as possible, so the card access can be cancelled ... Facilities Officers should keep a record of all keys issued locally ... It is the responsibility of all individuals who are always issued keys or cards to ensure their safe keeping and report any loss immediately to the Facilities Manager.

questions.question: A department projector goes missing from a teaching room on campus and theft is suspected. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, who must the suspected theft be reported to?
options: The Facilities Manager and Facilities Officer, but not the Safeguarding Team, as it is College equipment
The Safeguarding Team, which then decides whether the Facilities Manager needs to be told about it
The Safeguarding Team and the IT helpdesk, which advises on marking valuable equipment
The Safeguarding Team, and also promptly both the Facilities Manager and the Facilities Officer
questions.explanation: A suspected crime on College premises must be reported to the Safeguarding Team, and the equipment procedure separately requires suspected equipment thefts to be reported promptly to both the Facilities Manager and the Facilities Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: All incidents of crime on College premises, real and suspected, must be reported to the Safeguarding Team. ... Suspected thefts of equipment should be reported promptly to both Facilities Manager and Facilities Officer

questions.question: Police investigating a serious incident on campus have viewed College CCTV footage and now ask to remove copies of the recordings. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, what applies to this further request?
options: As a removal request, it must comply with the GDPR and be registered accordingly
No further conditions apply, as viewing for a serious incident was already allowed
It must be refused, as the Police may view College recordings but never remove them
It must first be approved in writing by the Principal as the overall safeguarding lead
questions.explanation: Viewing for a serious incident is a permitted circumstance, but a separate rule governs removal: Police requests to remove CCTV recordings must comply with the GDPR and be registered.
questions.source_excerpt: Emergencies or investigation of serious incidents ... Requests by Police to remove CCTV recordings must comply with the ... GDPR and will be registered accordingly.

questions.question: A College technician's negligence is established after they damage a student's personal laptop during a lab session. Under the Safeguarding and Security Policy, how does the College's position on students' personal property apply here?
options: The College still accepts no liability despite the negligence, as students are advised to insure their property
Only the technician is liable for the negligence, as the College accepts no liability for students' property
The College's refusal of liability does not apply, because negligence by one of its employees is established
The College accepts liability for the negligence only if the laptop had been security-marked beforehand
questions.explanation: The College excludes liability for students' personal property unless negligence of the College or its employees can be established; here an employee's negligence is established, so the exclusion does not apply.
questions.source_excerpt: The College does not accept liability for loss and/or damage to Students personal property unless negligence of the College or its employees can be established. Students are strongly advised to make their own arrangements for insuring their personal property.

questions.question: A colleague claims the Principal alone holds overall responsibility for vulnerable adult matters at the College. Which statement reflects the Safeguarding and Security Policy?
options: The two Designated Persons hold overall responsibility; the Principal advises them on each case
The claim is correct; the Principal holds overall responsibility for vulnerable adult matters
The Registrar holds it for students and the HR Manager for staff; the Principal has no named role
A member of the Board of Directors and a member of PEG hold it; the Principal leads safeguarding overall
questions.explanation: The policy gives overall responsibility for vulnerable adult matters to a member of the Board of Directors and a member of PEG, while the Principal provides overall leadership of safeguarding.
questions.source_excerpt: By identifying a member of the Board of Directors and a member of the Principal Executive Group (PEG) who have overall responsibility for vulnerable adult matters ... Principal: Overall leadership of Safeguarding

questions.question: On campus, safeguarding staff ask a lecturer to show their College card. The lecturer has left it at home, but a colleague immediately confirms who they are. Which statement reflects the Safeguarding and Security Policy?
options: The carry-at-all-times rule was breached, but a request to leave is linked to identity not being confirmed
The carry rule was breached, so the lecturer must be asked to leave even though their identity is confirmed
No rule was broken, as staff need to carry their card only when passing card-controlled barriers or doors
No rule was broken, but the lecturer must report the card as lost to the IT helpdesk so access is cancelled
questions.explanation: Staff must carry their ID card at all times on College premises, so the rule was breached; however, the policy links an immediate request to leave to cases where a person's identity cannot be confirmed.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff are required under the terms of their employment contracts, to carry their ID card at all times whilst on College premises. ... Failure to do so may result in an immediate request to leave College premises, if a person's identity cannot be confirmed.

questions.question: The Whistleblowing Policy encourages anyone with issues or concerns about the organisation to do what before raising them externally?
options: Raise them internally through existing processes and procedures
Obtain written approval to proceed from the whistleblowing charity Protect
Gather conclusive evidence and submit it directly to the police first
Raise them with the press so that the public interest can be tested
questions.explanation: The policy encourages people to be confident raising concerns internally through existing processes and procedures before they raise them externally.
questions.source_excerpt: The Whistleblowing Policy encourages any person(s) who may have any issues or concerns about the organisation to be confident over raising them internally through existing processes and procedures before they raise them externally.

questions.question: During a whistleblowing investigation, the colleague accused of malpractice asks the investigator who raised the concern. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, when may the whistleblower's personal details be disclosed to them?
options: Only where written permission has been given
Once the investigation has formally begun
Once the accused has made a written request
Whenever their line manager considers it fair
questions.explanation: Matters are treated in the strictest confidence and personal details will not be disclosed to the person accused without written permission.
questions.source_excerpt: Any matter raised under this procedure will be treated in the strictest confidence and personal details will not be disclosed to the person against whom the allegation has been made without written permission.

questions.question: According to the Whistleblowing Policy, which of the following is NOT intended to be raised under the policy?
options: Evidence of academic malpractice by a member of teaching staff
Damage to the environment caused by College activity
Financial or non-financial maladministration in a department
A challenge to a decision properly taken by the College
questions.explanation: The policy expressly excludes individuals seeking to challenge decisions properly taken by the College, whereas academic malpractice, environmental damage and maladministration are listed as matters covered.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy is NOT intended to be used for any complaints relating to a member of staff's employment or treatment, any complaints concerning a student's studies or personal circumstances, matters that should be addressed under other procedures, or for individuals seeking to challenge decisions properly taken by the College.

questions.question: A colleague plans to speak to a local newspaper about suspected financial irregularities at the College. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, when may talking to the media be treated as a serious disciplinary offence?
options: When the allegations are later found by the investigator to be unfounded
When done without first notifying their line manager and the Registrar in writing
Whenever done without the Public Information Management Group's permission
When done during working hours or using College equipment or premises
questions.explanation: The policy lists talking to the press or any other media outlet at any time without the Public Information Management Group's permission as a potential serious disciplinary offence.
questions.source_excerpt: The following may be considered as serious disciplinary offences: ... Talking to the press, radio, TV, or other media outlet at any time without the Public Information Management Group's permission.

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, what is expected of a complainant who discloses information about wrongdoing?
options: To provide conclusive proof of the wrongdoing before making a report
To have first raised the concern with an external regulator
To agree to their identity being shared with the person accused
To act in good faith and have reasonable grounds for their belief
questions.explanation: The policy expects the complainant to act in good faith and have reasonable grounds for believing the information indicates one of the listed problems; conclusive proof is not required.
questions.source_excerpt: It is expected that the complainant will be acting in good faith and have reasonable grounds for believing that the information disclosed indicates the existence of one of the following problems:

questions.question: A staff member wants to challenge a management decision on their department's budget, suspecting it was made to hide fraud. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, can this be raised through whistleblowing?
options: No, appeals against management decisions are excluded from whistleblowing
Yes, but it must first be reported to the police by the staff member
Yes, as the exclusion does not apply where suspected fraud is involved
No, budget matters must be handled under the Staff Grievance Policy instead
questions.explanation: Whistleblowing is not for appealing management decisions unless they involve suspected fraud, corruption or malpractice, so a decision suspected of hiding fraud can be raised.
questions.source_excerpt: Whistleblowing is not intended to be used to raise grievances relating to an individual's personal employment circumstances or to appeal against decisions of management, unless they involve suspected fraud, corruption, or malpractice.

questions.question: According to the Whistleblowing Policy, which of the following may be considered a serious disciplinary offence?
options: Raising a concern internally before raising it externally
Asking the investigator for details of the protection offered by PIDA
Raising a concern directly with a peer, tutor or line manager
Abusing the system by maliciously raising unfounded allegations
questions.explanation: Abuse of the whistleblowing system through maliciously raising unfounded allegations is listed as a potential serious disciplinary offence; the other actions are encouraged or supported by the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: The following may be considered as serious disciplinary offences: ... Any abuse of the whistleblowing system through maliciously raising unfounded allegations;

questions.question: A staff member believes the person investigating their whistleblowing concern is not handling it properly. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, with whom may they raise this in confidence?
options: The Public Information Management Group, which oversees all disclosures
The Chair of the College Oversight Board or any other Board member
The investigator's own line manager or the Head of Human Resources
The Internal Audit Service, which will then take over the investigation
questions.explanation: The policy states that if the investigator is not handling the matter properly, it may be raised in confidence with the Chair of the College Oversight Board or any other member of the Board.
questions.source_excerpt: If it is found that the person responsible for the investigation is not handling the matter properly, the matter may be raised in confidence with the Chair of the College Oversight Board, or any other member of the Board.

questions.question: A technician wants to report a health and safety concern about teaching equipment under the Whistleblowing Policy. What must the concern indicate to meet the policy's criteria?
options: Any level of risk, including the normal risks of using the equipment as intended
A greater danger than normal use, or a danger not usually associated with it
An injury that has already occurred and been formally recorded in the accident book
A risk that has been confirmed in writing by an external safety inspector
questions.explanation: For health and safety disclosures, the policy requires the concern to indicate greater danger than is associated with normal use, or a danger not usually associated with it.
questions.source_excerpt: That the health and safety of any individual has been, is being or is likely to be damaged. It must indicate greater danger than is associated with the normal use of the process/product, or a danger that is not usually associated with it;

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, serious misconduct that may prompt a disclosure can relate to matters at which point in time?
options: Matters ongoing at the date of the report, but not past events
Matters occurring now, in the past, or likely to occur in the future
Current or past matters, but not those merely likely to occur later
Matters that occurred within the twelve months before the report is made
questions.explanation: The policy states that disclosable misconduct covers matters whether currently occurring, having occurred in the past, or likely to occur in the future.
questions.source_excerpt: Serious misconduct that may prompt such a disclosure includes behaviour indicating one or more of the following matters, whether currently occurring, having occurred in the past, or likely to occur in the future

questions.question: According to the Whistleblowing Policy, if the outcome of a whistleblowing concern is 'no further action', what must accompany that outcome?
options: A referral of the case to the Internal Audit Service
A written warning issued to the whistleblower
A clear explanation provided to the whistleblower
A public statement naming those who were implicated
questions.explanation: The policy lists 'no further action' as a possible outcome only with a clear explanation provided to the whistleblower.
questions.source_excerpt: No further action (with clear explanation provided to the whistleblower).

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, the designated investigator must ensure the employee is aware of PIDA protection and has the contact details for which independent organisation?
options: Protect
ACAS
Citizens Advice
The Office of the Independent Adjudicator
questions.explanation: The investigator must ensure the employee knows about PIDA protection and has the contact details for the independent whistleblowing charity Protect (formerly Public Concern at Work).
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure that the employee is aware of the protection offered by the PIDA (Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998) and has the contact details for the independent whistleblowing charity Protect (formerly Public Concern at Work);

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, which other College policy should the Whistleblowing Policy be read in conjunction with?
options: The Data Protection Policy
The Public Information Policy
The Staff Disciplinary Policy
The Safeguarding and Security Policy
questions.explanation: The Aim section states that the Whistleblowing Policy should be read in conjunction with the Public Information Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy should be read in conjunction with the Public Information Policy.

questions.question: The Whistleblowing Policy aligns with which piece of legislation that protects employees from being treated unfairly for reporting corruption or malpractice in the workplace?
options: The Bribery Act 2010
The Freedom of Information Act 2000
The Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998
The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
questions.explanation: The policy aligns with the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998 (PIDA), which protects employees from unfair treatment for reporting corruption or malpractice.
questions.source_excerpt: The policy aligns with the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998 (PIDA) and protects employees from being treated unfairly for reporting corruption or malpractice in the workplace.

questions.question: According to the Whistleblowing Policy, what is the main purpose of the policy?
options: To encourage the reporting of wrongdoing and reassure that confidentiality will be respected
To give staff a route to appeal management decisions that were properly taken by the College
To replace the Staff Grievance Policy for complaints about pay, contracts and working conditions
To set out how the College handles media enquiries about allegations made against its staff
questions.explanation: The policy's main purpose is to encourage the reporting of wrongdoing and to provide reassurance that confidentiality will be respected throughout the process.
questions.source_excerpt: The main purpose of the policy is to encourage the reporting of wrongdoing and to provide reassurance that confidentiality will be respected throughout the process.

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, how should the people accused of wrongdoing in a whistleblowing concern be treated?
options: Suspended from duty until the investigation has been concluded
Told who raised the concern so that they can respond in full
Named to their department once the investigation has formally begun
Fairly and confidentially, during and after the investigation period
questions.explanation: The policy is intended to protect all parties, including ensuring that the accused are treated fairly and confidentially during and after the investigation.
questions.source_excerpt: This includes safeguarding the whistleblowers and ensuring that the accused are treated fairly and confidentially, during and after the period of investigation.

questions.question: Besides existing procedures, forums and committees, the Whistleblowing Policy says concerns may also be raised through direct contact with whom, where appropriate?
options: Peers, tutors, line managers or other senior members of staff
The Public Information Management Group or a named media contact
Members of the Academic Board or the Quality Assurance Department
Student representatives or members of the Students' Union executive
questions.explanation: The policy states that concerns may also be raised through direct contact with peers, tutors, line managers or other senior members of staff, where appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: Concerns may also be raised through direct contact with peers/tutors/line managers or other senior members of staff, where appropriate.

questions.question: The Whistleblowing Policy lists matters of serious misconduct that may prompt a disclosure. Which of the following is included in that list?
options: A staff member's dissatisfaction with their own annual pay award
Deliberate covering up of information relating to the listed matters
A student's request to defer studies due to personal circumstances
An appeal against a properly taken decision to close a course
