questions.explanation: Deliberate covering up of information relating to any of the listed matters is itself a listed matter; the other options are staff employment, student circumstances or properly taken decisions, which the policy excludes.
questions.source_excerpt: Serious misconduct that may prompt such a disclosure includes behaviour indicating one or more of the following matters ... Deliberate covering up of information which relates to any of the above matters.

questions.question: According to the Whistleblowing Policy, what does the College have in place to deal with employee grievances about specific employment issues?
options: An external mediation service commissioned separately for each case
The whistleblowing procedure, overseen by the College Oversight Board
An annual review panel drawn from members of the Academic Board
A well-established system designed to resolve them quickly and fairly
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College has a well-established system designed to quickly resolve and address employee grievances in a fair and professional manner.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has a well-established system designed to quickly resolve and address employee grievances, i.e. relating to specific employment issues, in a fair and professional manner.

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, what does the term 'whistleblowing' generally refer to?
options: Raising any complaint about pay, contracts or working conditions
Appealing a management decision to the College Oversight Board
The reporting of suspected fraud, corruption or malpractice
Sharing information about College activities with the press or media
questions.explanation: The policy defines whistleblowing as generally referring to the reporting of suspected fraud, corruption or malpractice.
questions.source_excerpt: 'Whistleblowing' generally refers to the reporting of suspected fraud, corruption or malpractice

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, how may the College treat any management or staff action designed to deter an individual from raising a genuine concern about fraud?
options: It should be resolved informally by the individual's line manager
It may be considered a serious disciplinary offence by the College
It should be raised by the individual as a staff grievance
It must be referred to the Internal Audit Service for review
questions.explanation: Any management or staff action designed to prevent or deter someone from raising a genuine concern about fraud, corruption or malpractice may be considered a serious disciplinary offence.
questions.source_excerpt: The following may be considered as serious disciplinary offences: ... Any management or staff action designed to prevent or deter an individual from raising a genuine concern relating to fraud, corruption, or malpractice

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, how does the Public Interest Disclosure Act's definition of 'worker' compare with the definition of 'employee'?
options: It is narrower and covers permanent staff only
It is identical to 'employee' under a contract of employment
It covers employees and contractors but excludes agency workers
It is broader than 'employee' and covers more people
questions.explanation: The policy states that the definition of 'worker' is broader than 'employee', extending to agency workers and learners as well as those employed under contract.
questions.source_excerpt: The definition of 'worker' is broader than 'employee' and applies to individuals who:

questions.question: The Whistleblowing Policy's definition of 'worker' includes people introduced or supplied to do work by a third person. What example of this group does the policy give?
options: Volunteers
External examiners
Agency workers
Governors
questions.explanation: The policy gives agency workers as the example of individuals introduced or supplied to do work by a third person.
questions.source_excerpt: S/he is or was introduced or supplied to do that work by a third person, i.e., agency workers;

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, a disclosure may indicate that a person has failed, is failing or is likely to fail to comply with what?
options: Any legal obligation to which they are subject
Any instruction given to them by their line manager
Any request made of them by a student or colleague
Any informal custom or practice of their department
questions.explanation: One of the problems a disclosure may indicate is that a person has failed, is failing or is likely to fail to comply with any legal obligation to which they are subject.
questions.source_excerpt: That a person has failed, is failing or is likely to fail to comply with any legal obligation to which s/he is subject;

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, whom will the designated investigator normally inform that a whistleblowing concern has been raised?
options: The Chair of the Academic Board
The Head of the Quality Assurance Department
The Public Information Management Group
The Chair of the College Oversight Board
questions.explanation: The designated investigator informs the Chair of the College Oversight Board (COB) that a concern has been raised, except where the concern relates to the Chair.
questions.source_excerpt: Inform the Chair of the College Oversight Board (COB) that a concern has been raised, except when any concern relates to the Chair

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, when clarifying the details of a concern, what will the designated investigator establish?
options: Whether internal procedures have already been exhausted
Whether the concern has already been reported to the police
Whether the accused person agrees to take part in an interview
Whether the whistleblower has sought their own legal advice
questions.explanation: The designated investigator will clarify any details and establish if internal procedures have been exhausted.
questions.source_excerpt: Clarify any details and establish if internal procedures have been exhausted.

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, which of the following is listed as a possible outcome of a whistleblowing concern?
options: Automatic dismissal of the line manager responsible for the area
Compensation paid to the whistleblower from College funds
Disciplinary action or another suitable penalty against any wrongdoer
Publication of the names of everyone implicated in the concern
questions.explanation: Possible outcomes include internal disciplinary action or other suitable penalty against any wrongdoer; publishing names would breach confidentiality.
questions.source_excerpt: The possible outcomes include the following: ... Internal disciplinary action or other suitable penalty against any wrongdoer;

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, how will any investigation into a whistleblowing concern be carried out?
options: Openly, with a summary of the allegations shared with all staff
Discreetly, without the allegations or names implicated made public
Publicly, once the Chair of the College Oversight Board approves it
Jointly with the press office so that the facts are reported accurately
questions.explanation: The policy states that any investigation will be carried out discreetly and that the nature of the allegations and the names of those implicated will not be made public.
questions.source_excerpt: Furthermore, any investigation will be carried out discreetly and the nature of the allegations and the name of those implicated will not be made public.

questions.question: A contractor working on a College project suspects that a supplier is being paid for work never delivered. According to the aim of the Whistleblowing Policy, who should be able to raise legitimate concerns without fear of reprisal?
options: Salaried staff only, once their probation has ended
Staff and students, but not the College's contractors
Staff, contractors and other stakeholders
Senior managers only, acting on behalf of their teams
questions.explanation: The policy's aim is a climate of openness in which staff, contractors and other stakeholders can raise legitimate concerns without fear of reprisal, so the contractor is included.
questions.source_excerpt: The aim of this policy is to acknowledge the need to operate in a climate of openness in which staff, contractors and other stakeholders can raise legitimate concerns externally without fear of reprisal

questions.question: A member of staff is reluctant to report suspected malpractice because they think it will simply be ignored. What does the Whistleblowing Policy's stated purpose say will happen to a concern raised under its procedure?
options: It will be promptly and appropriately investigated and acted upon
It will be held until a second, matching concern is received
It will be investigated only if the person raising it agrees to be named
It will be passed to the press office to decide whether any action is needed
questions.explanation: The purpose section states that the policy provides a clear procedure under which a concern will be promptly and appropriately investigated and acted upon.
questions.source_excerpt: It provides a clear procedure for concerns to be raised by an individual, where it will be promptly and appropriately investigated and acted upon

questions.question: A lecturer's serious concern about a colleague does not match any item in the Whistleblowing Policy's list of matters covered word for word. How does the policy describe that list of matters?
options: As a complete list, so only the matters named in it may be raised
As a guide that applies only to concerns raised by students
As a list the Chair must extend before any other matter is raised
As a list that includes, but is not limited to, the matters named
questions.explanation: The policy says the matters that may prompt a disclosure include but are not limited to those listed, so a serious concern need not match an item word for word.
questions.source_excerpt: Serious misconduct that may prompt such a disclosure includes behaviour indicating one or more of the following matters, whether currently occurring, having occurred in the past, or likely to occur in the future includes but is not limited to:

questions.question: A member of staff fears that a colleague's behaviour towards students could lead to sexual misconduct, although nothing has happened yet. Can this concern be raised under the Whistleblowing Policy?
options: No, only sexual misconduct that has already taken place can be reported under it
Yes, it covers concerns that sexual harassment or misconduct may happen in the future
No, it must first be raised by an affected student under the Student Complaints Policy
Yes, but only after the colleague has received a formal warning from their line manager
questions.explanation: Sexual harassment and/or misconduct is a listed matter whether it has already happened or there are concerns that it may happen in the future.
questions.source_excerpt: Any form of sexual harassment and/or misconduct, whether it has happened already or there are concerns that it may happen in the future;

questions.question: A student asks an administrator to log a whistleblowing concern because their request for extra time, based on personal circumstances, was handled slowly. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, is this an appropriate use of the policy?
options: Yes, any student complaint may be raised as a whistleblowing concern
Yes, provided the student puts the complaint in writing to the Registrar
Yes, provided the administrator raises it formally on the student's behalf
No, complaints about a student's studies or personal circumstances are excluded
questions.explanation: The policy is not intended for complaints concerning a student's studies or personal circumstances, which should be addressed under other procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy is NOT intended to be used for any complaints relating to a member of staff's employment or treatment, any complaints concerning a student's studies or personal circumstances, matters that should be addressed under other procedures

questions.question: A lecturer is unhappy that their teaching hours have been increased and wants to use the Whistleblowing Policy. There is no suggestion of fraud, corruption or malpractice. How does the policy indicate this should be handled?
options: As a disclosure made in confidence to the Chair of the College Oversight Board
As an external investigation carried out by the Internal Audit Service
Through the College's established system for resolving employee grievances
As a matter reported to the Public Information Management Group
questions.explanation: Whistleblowing is not for personal employment grievances unless fraud, corruption or malpractice is involved; the College has a well-established system for resolving employee grievances.
questions.source_excerpt: Whistleblowing is not intended to be used to raise grievances relating to an individual's personal employment circumstances or to appeal against decisions of management, unless they involve suspected fraud, corruption, or malpractice. The College has a well-established system designed to quickly resolve and address employee grievances

questions.question: A colleague has repeatedly been acting contrary to the staff code of ethics, although no money is involved. According to the Whistleblowing Policy's description of 'whistleblowing', can reporting this fall within it?
options: No, whistleblowing is limited to fraud and other financial irregularities
Yes, acting contrary to the staff code of ethics is expressly included
No, code of ethics breaches must go through the Staff Grievance Policy
Only if the conduct has already been reported to the police
questions.explanation: The policy's description of whistleblowing expressly includes acting contrary to the staff code of ethics, alongside fraud, corruption and other malpractice.
questions.source_excerpt: 'Whistleblowing' generally refers to the reporting of suspected fraud, corruption or malpractice, including financial irregularities, bribery, dishonesty, criminal activities, personal misconduct, creating or disregarding serious risks to health, safety or the environment, or acting contrary to the staff code of ethics.

questions.question: A member of staff raises a concern in good faith and with reasonable grounds, but the investigation finds no wrongdoing. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, may this be treated as a serious disciplinary offence?
options: No, the listed offence is maliciously raising unfounded allegations
Yes, any allegation later found to be unfounded is an abuse of the system
Yes, unless the concern was first raised with their own line manager
No, but they must meet the costs of the investigation that was carried out
questions.explanation: Only abuse of the system through maliciously raising unfounded allegations is listed as an offence; a complainant acting in good faith with reasonable grounds is what the policy expects.
questions.source_excerpt: Any abuse of the whistleblowing system through maliciously raising unfounded allegations; ... It is expected that the complainant will be acting in good faith and have reasonable grounds for believing that the information disclosed indicates the existence of one of the following problems

questions.question: A trainee on a work experience placement at the College, with no contract of employment, witnesses what appears to be a criminal offence. Under the Whistleblowing Policy's account of PIDA, are they within the definition of 'worker'?
options: No, only those employed under a contract of employment are workers
No, trainees must use the Student Complaints Policy and Procedure
Only if they were supplied to the College by an employment agency
Yes, it covers those given work experience as part of a training course
questions.explanation: The definition of 'worker' is broader than 'employee' and includes those provided with work experience as part of a training course or programme, not under a contract of employment.
questions.source_excerpt: The definition of 'worker' is broader than 'employee' and applies to individuals who: ... Is or was provided with work experience as part of a training course or programme, or with employment-related training not under a contract of employment

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, the Public Interest Disclosure Act protects workers from dismissal or penalisation by their employer on what condition?
options: That they have completed two years of continuous service with the College
That they disclose it anonymously through Protect
That they disclose the information in the correct manner
That they first report the matter to the police
questions.explanation: The policy states that PIDA protects workers who disclose information in the correct manner from dismissal or penalisation by their employer.
questions.source_excerpt: The Public Interest Disclosure Act provides protection for workers who disclose information in the correct manner, protecting them from dismissal or penalisation by their employer.

questions.question: A whistleblowing concern relates to the conduct of the Chair of the College Oversight Board. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, when will the Chair be informed that the concern has been raised?
options: Immediately, in the same way as for every other concern
At an appropriate time in the investigation, not at the outset
Never, as the Chair must not be told of it at any stage
Only if the Chair asks the investigator whether a concern exists
questions.explanation: The investigator normally informs the Chair of the COB, but where the concern relates to the Chair they are informed at an appropriate time in the investigation and not at the outset.
questions.source_excerpt: Inform the Chair of the College Oversight Board (COB) that a concern has been raised, except when any concern relates to the Chair, in which case they would be informed at an appropriate time in the investigation that the concern has been raised and not at the outset

questions.question: Under the Whistleblowing Policy, when will the investigator involve senior managers such as the Registrar or the Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM)?
options: In every case, at the very start of the investigation
Only when the whistleblower has given written consent
Where their involvement is appropriate and proportionate
Only when the concern relates to the Chair of the Board
questions.explanation: The investigator will involve members of senior management such as the Registrar or HoPAM where appropriate and proportionate, not automatically in every case.
questions.source_excerpt: The investigator will involve members of the senior management such as the Registrar or Head of Programme and Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) where appropriate and proportionate.

questions.question: The designated investigator finds that a whistleblowing concern raises complex legal questions. What does the Whistleblowing Policy allow the investigator to do?
options: Close the case and refer the whistleblower to Protect instead
Ask the whistleblower to obtain and pay for legal advice
Pause the case until the police have reviewed the concern
Obtain legal or other advice where it is necessary
questions.explanation: One of the designated investigator's listed steps is to obtain legal or other advice where necessary.
questions.source_excerpt: The designated investigator will: ... Obtain legal or other advice where necessary;

questions.question: An investigation under the Whistleblowing Policy finds evidence that a criminal offence has been committed. Which of the policy's listed possible outcomes fits this finding?
options: A report to an external body, such as the police
Referral to the Public Information Management Group
Mediation between the whistleblower and the accused
Transfer of the case to the Student Complaints Policy
questions.explanation: The listed possible outcomes include a report to an external body, which includes a report to the police.
questions.source_excerpt: The possible outcomes include the following: ... Report to an external body; ... Report to the police;

questions.question: To stop rumours, a head of department wants to email the team explaining the allegations under investigation and naming the colleague implicated. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, is this permitted?
options: Yes, once the investigation has formally begun and the accused has been told
No, the nature of the allegations and names implicated will not be made public
Only if the Chair of the College Oversight Board has approved the email
Yes, provided the whistleblower's own identity is kept out of the email
questions.explanation: Investigations are carried out discreetly, and the nature of the allegations and the names of those implicated will not be made public.
questions.source_excerpt: Furthermore, any investigation will be carried out discreetly and the nature of the allegations and the name of those implicated will not be made public.

questions.question: After a lecturer raises a genuine concern about corruption, their team leader begins excluding them from meetings and making hostile remarks about them. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, how may the team leader's conduct be treated?
options: Solely as a staff grievance, since it concerns the lecturer's treatment at work
As a disciplinary matter only once the corruption concern has been upheld
As a possible serious disciplinary offence for harassing the person raising it
As a matter to be referred to the Public Information Management Group
questions.explanation: The policy lists any management or staff action to harass an individual showing concerns about fraud, corruption or malpractice as a potential serious disciplinary offence; it does not depend on the concern being upheld.
questions.source_excerpt: The following may be considered as serious disciplinary offences: ... Any management or staff action designed to prevent or deter an individual from raising a genuine concern relating to fraud, corruption, or malpractice, or to harass the individual showing those concerns;

questions.question: A learner on a College course wants to raise two matters under the Whistleblowing Policy: the refusal of their own coursework extension, and a staff member they saw falsifying attendance records to claim funding. How does the policy treat these?
options: Only the falsified records; the extension is a complaint concerning their studies
Both fall within it, as learners come within PIDA's broader definition of 'worker'
Neither falls within it, as learners must use the Student Complaints Policy for everything
Only the extension falls within it, as it is the matter that directly affects the learner
questions.explanation: Complaints concerning a student's studies are excluded from the policy, whereas falsifying records to claim funding is suspected fraud, which whistleblowing covers.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy is NOT intended to be used for any complaints relating to a member of staff's employment or treatment, any complaints concerning a student's studies or personal circumstances ... 'Whistleblowing' generally refers to the reporting of suspected fraud, corruption or malpractice

questions.question: A whistleblowing concern is about the Chair of the College Oversight Board, and the whistleblower believes the investigator is not handling it properly. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, what may the whistleblower do about the handling?
options: Wait until the Chair has been told of the concern, as only then can the handling be reviewed
Raise it in confidence with any other member of the College Oversight Board
Ask the Registrar, as a senior manager, to take over the investigation
Refer the handling to the Public Information Management Group to decide
questions.explanation: Improper handling may be raised in confidence with the Chair of the COB or any other member of the Board, with no waiting condition, so another Board member can be approached when the concern is about the Chair.
questions.source_excerpt: Inform the Chair of the College Oversight Board (COB) that a concern has been raised, except when any concern relates to the Chair ... If it is found that the person responsible for the investigation is not handling the matter properly, the matter may be raised in confidence with the Chair of the College Oversight Board, or any other member of the Board.

questions.question: In an interview a whistleblower tells the investigator 'I don't mind if they know it was me' but signs nothing. The accused then asks who raised the concern. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, what should the investigator do?
options: Disclose it, as a clear verbal agreement recorded in the interview notes is enough
Disclose it once the Chair of the College Oversight Board has been told of the concern
Disclose it if the Registrar agrees it is appropriate and proportionate in the case
Withhold it, as disclosure to the accused needs the whistleblower's written permission
questions.explanation: Personal details are not disclosed to the person accused without written permission, so an unsigned verbal remark is not enough.
questions.source_excerpt: Any matter raised under this procedure will be treated in the strictest confidence and personal details will not be disclosed to the person against whom the allegation has been made without written permission.

questions.question: The Whistleblowing Policy lists the possible outcomes of a concern, some with an example. Which pairing of outcomes and examples matches the policy?
options: External investigation by the police; report to an external body such as Internal Audit Service
External investigation by Protect; report to an external body such as the Oversight Board
External investigation by Internal Audit Service; report to an external body such as the police
External investigation by the Public Information Management Group; report to an external body such as Protect
questions.explanation: The policy gives the Internal Audit Service as an example of external investigation, and a report to the police as a form of report to an external body.
questions.source_excerpt: The possible outcomes include the following: ... External investigation e.g. by Internal Audit Service; ... Report to an external body; ... Report to the police;

questions.question: An investigator closes a whistleblowing case with 'no further action' and refuses to give the whistleblower any reason. Which statement reflects the Whistleblowing Policy?
options: A clear explanation is expected, and mishandling may be raised with the COB Chair or a Board member
No reason is owed as the matter is confidential, and the investigator's outcome is final
A reason is owed only where the case was passed to the Internal Audit Service to investigate
No reason is owed, but the whistleblower may then brief the media as internal routes are exhausted
questions.explanation: 'No further action' is listed with a clear explanation provided to the whistleblower, and improper handling may be raised in confidence with the Chair of the COB or any other Board member.
questions.source_excerpt: No further action (with clear explanation provided to the whistleblower). ... If it is found that the person responsible for the investigation is not handling the matter properly, the matter may be raised in confidence with the Chair of the College Oversight Board, or any other member of the Board.

questions.question: A member of staff plans to pass evidence of suspected bribery to a TV journalist, believing PIDA shields them from any consequence. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, which statement is correct?
options: PIDA protects any disclosure made in good faith, so no disciplinary action can follow at all
Without the Public Information Management Group's permission, it may be a serious disciplinary offence
Media contact is protected once the concern has first been raised internally without success
Media contact is protected if the investigator has confirmed internal procedures are exhausted
questions.explanation: Talking to any media outlet at any time without the Public Information Management Group's permission may be a serious disciplinary offence, and PIDA protects only disclosures made in the correct manner.
questions.source_excerpt: Talking to the press, radio, TV, or other media outlet at any time without the Public Information Management Group's permission. ... The Public Interest Disclosure Act provides protection for workers who disclose information in the correct manner

questions.question: After an investigation clears a colleague, a manager proposes emailing all staff to name the colleague and confirm they did nothing wrong. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, is this appropriate?
options: Yes, the duty of confidentiality applies only while the investigation is still in progress
Yes, provided the whistleblower's identity is left out of the email to staff
Yes, once the Chair of the College Oversight Board has been informed of the final outcome
No, the accused are treated confidentially afterwards too, and names are not made public
questions.explanation: The accused are treated fairly and confidentially during and after the investigation, and the names of those implicated will not be made public.
questions.source_excerpt: This includes safeguarding the whistleblowers and ensuring that the accused are treated fairly and confidentially, during and after the period of investigation. ... the nature of the allegations and the name of those implicated will not be made public.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the designated investigator's responsibilities under the Whistleblowing Policy?
options: Clarify details and establish whether internal procedures have been exhausted
Refer every concern to the Internal Audit Service for an external investigation
Involve senior managers such as the Registrar where appropriate and proportionate
Ensure the employee knows of PIDA protection and has the contact details for Protect
questions.explanation: External investigation, e.g. by the Internal Audit Service, is one possible outcome rather than a step the investigator takes for every concern; the other three are listed duties of the designated investigator.
questions.source_excerpt: The designated investigator will: ... Clarify any details and establish if internal procedures have been ... The investigator will involve members of the senior management such as ... The possible outcomes include the following: ... External investigation e.g. by Internal Audit Service;

questions.question: A freelance trainer, not an employee, is contracted to deliver workshops for the College personally and sees evidence of bribery. Under the Whistleblowing Policy's account of PIDA, is the trainer within the definition of 'worker'?
options: Yes, it includes other contracts to perform work or services personally
No, it is limited to people employed under a contract of employment with the College
No, unless the trainer was introduced or supplied to the College by an employment agency
Yes, but only while the trainer is also enrolled on a training course run by the College
questions.explanation: The definition of 'worker' is broader than 'employee' and includes individuals employed under any other contract to perform work or services personally.
questions.source_excerpt: The definition of 'worker' is broader than 'employee' and applies to individuals who: ... Are employed under any other contract to perform work or services personally;

questions.question: An agency worker who left the College six months ago now wants to disclose fraud they saw while placed there. Under the Whistleblowing Policy's account of PIDA, does the definition of 'worker' still include them?
options: No, it covers only people still working at the College when the disclosure is made
No, agency workers fall outside it because they are not College employees
Yes, it covers anyone who is or was supplied to do the work by a third person
Only if the agency agrees to raise the concern with the College on their behalf
questions.explanation: The definition covers those who work or worked for a person where they are or were introduced or supplied by a third person, such as agency workers, so a former agency worker is included.
questions.source_excerpt: Work or worked for a person in circumstances which: ... S/he is or was introduced or supplied to do that work by a third person, i.e., agency workers;

questions.question: A staff member overhears a manager's credible plan to inflate student numbers in next month's funding claim; nothing has been submitted yet. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, what is expected of a disclosure made now?
options: Proof that the claim has been submitted, as only acts already committed can be disclosed
Written confirmation of the plan from a second colleague who also overheard it
Evidence strong enough for the police to accept a formal criminal complaint
Good faith and reasonable grounds to believe that an offence is likely to be committed
questions.explanation: The complainant is expected to act in good faith with reasonable grounds, and a qualifying problem includes a criminal offence that is likely to be committed, so proof of a completed act is not needed.
questions.source_excerpt: It is expected that the complainant will be acting in good faith and have reasonable grounds for believing that the information disclosed indicates the existence of one of the following problems: ... That a criminal offence has been committed, is being committed or is likely to be committed;

questions.question: An estates manager knowingly ignores a serious risk that chemical waste could leak into drains, although no leak has yet occurred. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, can reporting this fall within whistleblowing?
options: No, only environmental damage that has actually occurred can be reported under it
Yes, it includes disregarding serious environmental risks and matters likely to occur
No, estates matters must be raised through the Staff Grievance Policy instead
Only once the risk has been confirmed in writing by an external inspector
questions.explanation: Whistleblowing includes creating or disregarding serious risks to the environment, and covered matters include those likely to occur in the future.
questions.source_excerpt: whether currently occurring, having occurred in the past, or likely to occur in the future ... 'Whistleblowing' generally refers to the reporting of suspected fraud, corruption or malpractice, including ... creating or disregarding serious risks to health, safety or the environment

questions.question: A whistleblowing concern relates to an ordinary member of the College Oversight Board, not its Chair. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, how should the investigator approach informing the Chair of the COB?
options: Inform the Chair as usual, as the exception covers only concerns about the Chair
Delay telling the Chair until an appropriate time, as the concern involves a Board member
Inform no member of the Board until the investigation has been fully concluded
Inform the Chair only if the Board member concerned gives written permission
questions.explanation: The investigator informs the Chair of the COB that a concern has been raised; the later-notice exception applies only when the concern relates to the Chair.
questions.source_excerpt: Inform the Chair of the College Oversight Board (COB) that a concern has been raised, except when any concern relates to the Chair, in which case they would be informed at an appropriate time in the investigation that the concern has been raised and not at the outset

questions.question: A whistleblower gives written permission for their details to be shared with the person accused, and also asks for the allegations to be posted on the staff intranet. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, what is the position?
options: Both requests may be met, as written permission lifts confidentiality over the whole matter
Neither may be met, as personal details can never be disclosed to the person accused
Details may go to the accused, but the allegations will not be made public
Both need the Public Information Management Group's approval before either is met
questions.explanation: Written permission allows personal details to be disclosed to the accused, but the nature of the allegations and the names of those implicated will not be made public.
questions.source_excerpt: personal details will not be disclosed to the person against whom the allegation has been made without written permission. Furthermore, any investigation will be carried out discreetly and the nature of the allegations and the name of those implicated will not be made public.

questions.question: Taking the Whistleblowing Policy's purpose and policy statements together, where can individuals raise concerns without fear of reprisal or victimisation?
options: Within the College only; concerns raised outside lose that protection
Outside the organisation only; internal routes carry no such assurance
With the designated investigator alone, via the whistleblowing route
Within the College and also outside of the organisation
questions.explanation: The purpose covers raising concerns within the College without fear of reprisals, and the policy statement covers raising concerns outside the organisation without fear of detriment, victimisation or reprisal.
questions.source_excerpt: The policy ensures that it enables individuals to raise any concerns they may have within the College without fear of reprisals/victimisation. ... which enables individuals to raise concerns outside of the organisation without fear of detriment, victimisation, or reprisal.

questions.question: Colleague A disagrees with a promotion decision that followed the correct procedure. Colleague B has evidence that the panel chair falsified scores to favour a friend. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, which of them can use whistleblowing?
options: Only Colleague A, as the concern is about a management decision affecting them
Only Colleague B, as falsified scores point to malpractice, not a properly taken decision
Both of them, as each concern relates to a decision taken by College management
Neither, as promotion decisions must go through the Staff Grievance Policy instead
questions.explanation: Challenges to decisions properly taken are excluded, but appeals against management decisions are allowed where they involve suspected fraud, corruption or malpractice, such as falsified scores.
questions.source_excerpt: or for individuals seeking to challenge decisions properly taken by the College. ... Whistleblowing is not intended to be used to raise grievances relating to an individual's personal employment circumstances or to appeal against decisions of management, unless they involve suspected fraud, corruption, or malpractice.

questions.question: A staff member has reasonable grounds to believe a manager deliberately concealed a breach of a legal obligation, although the breach itself has since been put right. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, can the concealment still be a qualifying problem?
options: No, once the underlying breach is corrected there is nothing left to disclose
No, concealment counts only where a criminal offence was the matter concealed
Yes, deliberate concealment of a listed problem is itself listed
Only if the concealment is still continuing when the disclosure is made
questions.explanation: Failing to comply with a legal obligation is a listed problem, and deliberate concealment of any listed problem that has occurred is itself a listed problem.
questions.source_excerpt: That a person has failed, is failing or is likely to fail to comply with any legal obligation to which s/he is subject; ... That deliberate concealment of any of the above has occurred, is occurring, or is likely to occur.

questions.question: A member of staff suspects their own line manager of malpractice and wants to raise it internally first. Under the Whistleblowing Policy, which internal route is open to them?
options: The Public Information Management Group, which handles concerns about managers
Protect alone, since internal routes are closed where a manager is involved
Only the line manager, as every concern must first go through line management
Direct contact with another senior member of staff, or existing forums and committees
questions.explanation: The policy allows concerns to be raised through existing forums and committees or by direct contact with peers, tutors, line managers or other senior members of staff, where appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: or through existing forums and committees as appropriate. Concerns may also be raised through direct contact with peers/tutors/line managers or other senior members of staff, where appropriate.

questions.question: A student tells you they want to appeal because they feel the assessor should have marked their work more generously. They report no administrative errors and no mitigating circumstances. How does the Academic Appeals Policy treat this?
options: It is not a valid appeal, as it relates solely to academic judgement
It is a valid appeal on the ground of procedural irregularity
It is valid as long as it is submitted within the deadline
It should go straight to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
questions.explanation: The policy states that academic appeals are not valid where they relate solely and directly to claims concerning academic judgement, which is what a disagreement with the marker's judgement is.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic appeals are not valid where they relate solely and directly to claims concerning academic judgement

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, within what timeframe must a Stage One academic appeal be received?
options: Within 10 working days of the Result Publication Date
Within 15 working days of the Result Publication Date
Within 20 working days of the Result Publication Date
Within 30 calendar days of the Result Publication Date
questions.explanation: The Stage One (Formal Stage) timeline in the policy states that the appeal must be received within 15 working days of the Result Publication Date.
questions.source_excerpt: Appeal must be received within 15 working days of Result Publication Date

questions.question: The Registrar asks you to act as the appeal reviewer for a Stage One academic appeal, but you marked the assignment being appealed. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure require?
options: You may act, provided you declare your prior involvement to the Registrar in writing
You may act, as long as a second marker independently reviews the case alongside you
You should not act, as the reviewer must have had no previous involvement in the matter
You may act, since the member of staff who marked the work is best placed to review the appeal
questions.explanation: The policy requires appeals to be considered by someone impartial, and the nominated appeal reviewer must be a member of staff with no previous involvement in the matter.
questions.source_excerpt: the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim. This will be a member of staff who has had no previous involvement in the matter

questions.question: A student asks you how to lodge a Stage One academic appeal. According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what should you tell them?
options: Email the Stage One Academic Appeal Form to their Personal Tutor, who forwards it to the Assessment and Progression Board
Complete the Stage One Academic Appeal Form via the Student Portal, or submit it at reception for the Registrar
Send the Stage One Academic Appeal Form directly to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator with its Complaint Form
Post the Stage One Academic Appeal Form to the Quality Assurance Officer, copying in their Personal Tutor
questions.explanation: The policy says the Stage One Academic Appeal Form is in the Student Portal and submitted via Online Form, or can be obtained and submitted at reception for the attention of the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: A student wishing to make an appeal must do so by completing the Stage One Academic Appeal Form, which is in the Student Portal and should be submitted via Online Form. Alternatively, the form can be obtained and submitted at reception for the attention of the Registrar at LCC

questions.question: A student contacts you after missing the Stage One academic appeal deadline and asks whether they can still appeal. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure say they should do?
options: Accept the result, as the policy does not permit appeals after the 15-working-day Stage One deadline
Explain in writing, with evidence, why an appeal was not possible in time; the College then decides
Request a Stage Two review directly from the Quality Assurance Officer, who is responsible for handling late appeals
Submit the appeal as normal, as late appeals are accepted automatically
questions.explanation: Under the late appeals section, the student must give a written reason, supported by evidence, for not appealing within the time limit, and the College decides whether to accept the late appeal.
questions.source_excerpt: they should provide a reason in writing why it was not possible or reasonable to submit an appeal within the time limit. This is important as they need to provide evidence to support their explanation; ... The college will consider the reason(s) for the lateness and will decide whether or not to accept the late appeal.

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, to whom must a student submit the Stage Two Academic Appeal form, and within what time?
options: The Registrar (or nominee), within 15 working days of the original Result Publication Date
Their Personal Tutor (or nominee), within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
The Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
The Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), within 15 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
questions.explanation: The policy requires the Stage Two form to be submitted to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: A student who wishes to have the Stage One decision reviewed must complete the Stage Two Academic Appeal form and submit it to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what authority do an appeal reviewer and the members of an Appeal Panel have over the decision of the assessors?
options: Neither has authority to set aside the assessors' decision or recommend an award
They may set aside the assessors' decision where the appeal is upheld on valid grounds
They may recommend an award directly to the awarding body
They may overturn the assessors' decision once the Registrar has given written approval
questions.explanation: The policy is explicit that neither a reviewer nor any Appeal Panel member can set aside the assessors' decision or recommend an award; they can instead ask the Assessment and Progression Board to review or revise its decision.
questions.source_excerpt: Neither a reviewer nor any member of the Appeal Panel have the authority to set aside the decision of the assessors or recommend award

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, which of the following is NOT one of the limited grounds on which a student may request a Stage Two review?
options: New material evidence that exceptional circumstances prevented the student from providing earlier
The student believes the Stage One decision is procedurally incorrect
The student believes there was procedural unfairness in the appeals process
The student believes a different reviewer would reach a more favourable decision
questions.explanation: The policy limits Stage Two review requests to new material evidence, a procedurally incorrect decision, or procedural unfairness; wanting a different reviewer is not a listed ground.
questions.source_excerpt: A request for a review must be based on the following limited grounds: ... New material evidence has emerged which the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier in the process; ... The student believes that the decision is procedurally incorrect; ... The student believes that there has been procedural unfairness in the appeals process.

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, if a student appeals on the ground of mitigating circumstances the assessors were not aware of, what must support the request?
options: A supporting statement from their Personal Tutor, instead of medical or documentary evidence
The student's own written statement, as no supporting evidence is needed at Stage One
A letter of support from the student representative body
Medical certificates or other documentary evidence acceptable to the Appeal Panel
questions.explanation: Where an appeal rests on unknown mitigating circumstances, the policy requires it to be supported by medical certificates or other documentary evidence acceptable to the Appeal Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: If resting on this ground, the candidate's request must be supported by medical certificates or other documentary evidence acceptable to the Appeal Panel

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what does the Registrar check during the initial evaluation of a Stage One academic appeal?
options: Whether the assessor's academic judgement on the student's grade was correct and consistently applied
Whether the student has already referred the case to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
Whether the student's Personal Tutor has formally agreed, in writing, to support the appeal
Whether it used the correct procedure, is on valid grounds, was on time and is in the required format
questions.explanation: On receipt of an appeal, the Registrar's initial evaluation checks the procedure used, the grounds, the deadline and the required format.
questions.source_excerpt: On receipt of an academic appeal, the Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation to check that the student's academic appeal was submitted under the correct procedures, that it falls within the grounds upon which an appeal may be made, that it was submitted within the deadline and is in the required format.

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, who makes up the Appeal Panel at Stage Two (Review Stage)?
options: The Registrar and the chair of the Assessment and Progression Board, with a student representative
Two academic staff members who also sat on the Stage One panel
Two academic staff independent of the case who did not sit on the Stage One panel
The Quality Assurance Officer and the student's Personal Tutor, advised by the appeal reviewer
questions.explanation: The Stage Two Appeal Panel comprises two academic staff who are independent of the case and did not take part as panel members at Stage One.
questions.source_excerpt: The Appeal Panel will be comprised of two members of the academic staff who are independent of the case and have not participated as a member of the panel in stage one

questions.question: A student has been invited to attend their Stage Two Appeal Panel meeting and asks whether they can bring someone with them. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure allow?
options: They may bring a current LCC student or member of staff as a companion
They may bring a legal representative of their choice to speak for them
They may bring a family member, but not an LCC student or member of staff
They may not bring anyone, because the proceedings are confidential
questions.explanation: At Stage Two, the student is invited to attend the Panel meeting in person and is entitled to bring a current LCC student or member of staff as a companion.
questions.source_excerpt: The student will be invited to provide a written statement and any additional evidence to the Panel and will be invited to attend the Panel meeting in person. They will be entitled to bring a current LCC student/member of staff as a companion

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what is an academic appeal?
options: A request for a second marker to re-grade work where the student disagrees with the assessor's academic judgement
A formal complaint about the quality of teaching, facilities or services, made to the Registrar at reception
A request for a review of an Assessment and Progression Board decision on a student's assessment or progression
A referral to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator asking it to overturn a decision of the awarding body
questions.explanation: The policy defines an academic appeal as a request for a review of an Assessment and Progression Board decision in relation to a student's assessment or progression.
questions.source_excerpt: An academic appeal is a request for a review of an Assessment and Progression Board decision in relation to assessment or progression for any given student.

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, which students do the procedures described in the policy apply to?
options: Students on degree programmes awarded by a partner university
Students of HND Programmes awarded by Pearson
Applicants refused a place on an HND course
Students on short courses leading to a College certificate
questions.explanation: The policy states that its procedures apply to students of HND Programmes awarded by Pearson.
questions.source_excerpt: The procedures described in this policy apply to students of HND Programmes awarded by Pearson.

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what assurance is given to a student who makes an academic appeal?
options: Their appeal will be upheld if it is received within 15 working days
Their appeal will be reviewed by the assessor who marked the work
Their case details will be shared with all teaching staff
They will not be disadvantaged as a result of making the appeal
questions.explanation: The policy states that no student will be disadvantaged as a result of making an academic appeal.
questions.source_excerpt: No student will be disadvantaged as a result of making an academic appeal

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what follows for any appeal where the student has completed the course and received an award certificate?
options: It implies the closure of any action or appeal within the College's procedure
The appeal must be fast-tracked straight to the Stage Two Review Stage
The student may appeal to the Registrar within 12 months of the award date
The appeal continues, but the certificate is withheld until the outcome
questions.explanation: The policy states that completing the course and receiving an award certificate implies the closure of any action or appeal within the College's procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: For students who have completed the course and received an award certificate, this implies the closure of any action/appeal within the College's procedure

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, when may a student include personal data about another person in their academic appeal?
options: Only if the Registrar has approved the disclosure in advance
Only if the other person is also a current student of the College
Only if that person has given them written permission to do so
Only if their Personal Tutor has first anonymised the information
questions.explanation: Students must avoid disclosing another person's personal data in an appeal unless that person has given written permission.
questions.source_excerpt: A student must also avoid disclosing personal data of any other person in the appeal unless they have been given written permission by the person/s to do so

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, when is a group appeal against a decision acceptable?
options: When the group is represented by a member of the student representative body
When all students in the group are affected by the same set of circumstances
When at least half of the students on the module have signed the appeal form
When each student in the group has first had an individual appeal rejected
questions.explanation: Group appeals are acceptable provided that all students within the group are affected by the same set of circumstances.
questions.source_excerpt: Group appeals against decisions are acceptable, provided that all students within the group are affected by the same set of circumstances

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the grounds on which a student can bring an academic appeal under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure?
options: Disagreement with the assessor's academic judgement about the quality or standard of the submitted work
Dissatisfaction with the teaching, supervision or learning resources provided during the module
A wish to be reassessed by a different assessor because the student expected a higher grade
An administrative error in processing marks that casts doubt on whether the result might have been different
questions.explanation: An administrative error or procedural irregularity in processing marks that casts doubt on whether the result might have been different is a listed ground; academic judgement is expressly excluded.
questions.source_excerpt: There was an administrative error or procedural irregularity or other inadequacy in the conduct of the assessor(s) or processing of marks or grades of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different if the error never occurred.

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what should a student do if the medical or documentary evidence for their appeal cannot be submitted in English?
options: Provide an authorised translation of the relevant documents
Submit the originals, and the College will arrange a translation
Ask their Personal Tutor to summarise the documents in English
Submit the documents as they are, since any language is accepted
questions.explanation: Evidence should be submitted in English; if that is not possible, the student should provide an authorised translation of the relevant documents.
questions.source_excerpt: Any medical or documentary evidence should be submitted in English. If this is not possible, the student should provide an authorised translation of the relevant documents to support such claims.

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what is the first stage for an HND student who is unhappy with an assessment decision?
options: Seek informal resolution with their Personal Tutor
Submit a Stage One Academic Appeal Form to the Registrar
Request a Stage Two review from the Quality Assurance Officer
Lodge a case with Pearson or the Independent Adjudicator
questions.explanation: The stages for HND students begin with the student seeking informal resolution with their Personal Tutor, before the formal Stage One appeal.
questions.source_excerpt: Student seeks informal resolution with Personal ... Students can discuss their results with their Personal Tutors

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, when is an appellant who requires reasonable adjustments encouraged to provide details of the support they need?
options: Once the Stage Two Appeal Panel meeting has been arranged
After the Registrar has issued the Stage One outcome letter
When they first discuss their results with their Personal Tutor
At the beginning of the formal stage of the procedure
questions.explanation: An appellant who requires reasonable adjustments is encouraged to provide details of the support required at the beginning of the formal stage.
questions.source_excerpt: An appellant who requires reasonable adjustments during the procedure is encouraged to provide details of the support required at the beginning of the formal stage

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, within what time should a Stage One (Formal Stage) appeal decision be issued to the student?
options: Within 5 working days
Within 10 working days
Within 20 working days
Within 30 calendar days
questions.explanation: The Stage One timeline states that the decision is to be issued to the student within 10 working days.
questions.source_excerpt: Decision to be issued to the student within 10 working days

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what is the status of a revised Assessment and Progression Board decision resulting from the Stage One appeal process?
options: It may be appealed again at Stage One within 15 working days
It is provisional until confirmed by the Quality Assurance Officer
It is final and may not be the subject of further appeal
It takes effect only once the student has agreed to it in writing
questions.explanation: A revised decision of the Assessment and Progression Board resulting from the Stage One process is final and cannot be appealed further.
questions.source_excerpt: A revised decision of the Assessment and Progression Board resulting from this process shall be final and may not be the subject of further appeal

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, within what time should the outcome of a Stage Two (Review Stage) be issued to the student?
options: Within 5 working days of the Panel
Within 10 working days of the Panel
Within 15 working days of the Panel
Within 20 working days of the Panel
questions.explanation: The Stage Two timeline states that the outcome is issued to the student within 15 working days of the Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: Outcome issued to student within 15 working days of Panel

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what should the annual monitoring report on the appeals process consider?
options: Timeliness of the process, appeals outcomes and protected characteristics
Individual assessors' marking accuracy, grade profiles and resit rates
Student satisfaction scores, complaint volumes and staff training records
The names of appellants, their final grades and the reviewers assigned
questions.explanation: The annual monitoring report should comment on the timeliness of the process, appeals outcomes and the protected characteristics for the appeals procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: This report should consider the commentary on timeliness of the process, appeals outcomes, and consideration of the protected characteristics for the appeals procedures.

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, within what time must the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA) receive a student's signed complaint form?
options: Within 6 months of the date of the Completion of Procedures letter
Within 12 months of the original Result Publication Date
Within 3 months of receiving the Stage Two Appeal Panel outcome
Within 12 months of the date of the Completion of Procedures letter
questions.explanation: The OIA must receive the signed form within 12 months of the date of the Completion of Procedures (COP) letter, otherwise the complaint is out of time.
questions.source_excerpt: The OIA must receive the signed form within 12 months of the date of the COP letter, otherwise it will consider the complaint to be out of time.

questions.question: A student tells you they want to 'appeal' about poor classroom facilities and the quality of teaching on their HND course; no assessment or progression decision is involved. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, where should they be directed?
options: To the Stage One Academic Appeal Form, submitted via the Student Portal for the Registrar's attention
To the Quality Assurance Officer, who reviews teaching concerns under Stage Two of the appeals process
To the Complaints Policy and Procedure, as this is a complaint rather than an academic appeal
To the Assessment and Progression Board, which reviews concerns about teaching at its next meeting
questions.explanation: An academic appeal is a request for review of an Assessment and Progression Board decision on assessment or progression; for complaints, students should refer to the Complaints Policy and Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: An academic appeal is a request for a review of an Assessment and Progression Board decision in relation to assessment or progression for any given student. ... For complaints, students should refer to the Complaints Policy and Procedure.

questions.question: A student preparing an academic appeal asks whether they must describe all of their medical conditions on the form. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure advise?
options: They must list every condition, even unrelated ones, unless their Personal Tutor agrees otherwise
They should avoid unnecessary personal information, unless they feel it is relevant to the issues raised
They should give full medical details to their Personal Tutor, who then decides what to pass on
They must not mention any medical condition at all, as health data cannot be used in an appeal
questions.explanation: At all stages a student should avoid disclosing unnecessary personal information, such as medical conditions, unless they feel it is relevant to the issues raised.
questions.source_excerpt: At all stages of the appeal process a student should ensure that they avoid disclosing unnecessary personal information (e.g., medical conditions etc.) unless s/he feels it is relevant to the issues raised.

questions.question: During the appeal process, a student asks you who they can turn to for help with their academic appeal. According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, who may they seek assistance from?
options: Only the Registrar, since the Registrar receives all Stage One academic appeals
The appeal reviewer nominated by the Registrar to investigate their claim
Only a member of the Appeal Panel that will hear any Stage Two review
Their assigned Personal Tutor or any member of the student representative body
questions.explanation: The policy states that during the appeal process a student may seek assistance from their assigned Personal Tutor or any member of the student representative body.
questions.source_excerpt: During the appeal process, a student may seek assistance from his/her assigned Personal Tutor or any member from the student representative body

questions.question: You are a member of staff involved in handling a student's academic appeal. A colleague with no role in the case asks you for the details. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure expect of you?
options: Maintain the confidentiality of the student and the proceedings, as far as the process allows
Share the details, as appeal cases are discussed openly with all teaching staff at the College
Share the details once the Registrar has issued the Stage One outcome letter to the student
Share the details only with the colleague's line manager, who can then decide on disclosure
questions.explanation: Staff members involved in an appeal must maintain the confidentiality of the student and the proceedings as far as possible within the effective operation of the process.
questions.source_excerpt: As far as possible, within the effective operation of the process, confidentiality of the student and the proceedings will be maintained by staff members involved

questions.question: For an academic appeal on the ground of mitigating circumstances, which conditions does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure require those circumstances to meet?
options: The assessors knew of them when deciding but gave them too little weight in the final decision
They arose after results were published and prevented the student from preparing for a resit
The assessors were unaware of them when deciding, and they could not reasonably have been presented
They were reported to the Personal Tutor within 15 working days, with a signed statement of support
questions.explanation: The mitigating circumstances ground covers existing circumstances the assessors were not aware of when the decision was reached and which could not reasonably have been presented to them.
questions.source_excerpt: There were existing mitigating circumstances affecting the student's performance which the assessor(s) were not aware of when a decision was reached, and which could not reasonably have been presented to the assessors.

questions.question: A student finds that one of their unit results was keyed into the records incorrectly, casting doubt on whether their overall outcome would have been different. Under which ground of the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure can they appeal?
options: Administrative error or procedural irregularity in the processing of marks or grades
Existing mitigating circumstances that were unknown to the assessors when they decided
New material evidence that exceptional circumstances prevented them providing earlier
Procedural unfairness in the way the appeals process itself was carried out by staff
questions.explanation: An error in processing marks that casts doubt on whether the result might have been different falls under the administrative error or procedural irregularity ground; the other options are a different ground or Stage Two review grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: There was an administrative error or procedural irregularity or other inadequacy in the conduct of the assessor(s) or processing of marks or grades of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different if the error never occurred.

questions.question: According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, which sequence correctly shows the stages available to an HND student who is dissatisfied with an assessment decision?
options: Stage One formal appeal, informal resolution with the Personal Tutor, Stage Two review, then Pearson/OIA
Informal resolution with the Personal Tutor, Stage One formal appeal, Stage Two review, then Pearson/OIA
Informal resolution with the Personal Tutor, Stage One formal appeal, Pearson/OIA, then Stage Two review
Informal resolution with the Personal Tutor, Stage Two review, Stage One formal appeal, then Pearson/OIA
questions.explanation: The stages for HND students run from informal resolution with the Personal Tutor, to Stage One, to the Stage Two review, and only then to Pearson or the OIA once a Completion of Procedures letter is issued.
questions.source_excerpt: Student seeks informal resolution with Personal ... LCC considers Appeal at formal Stage One ... LCC conducts review of decision at Stage Two ... Once a Completion of Procedures letter has been issued, the student may lodge a case at the Pearson/OIA

questions.question: A student discusses their results with their Personal Tutor, but their concerns are not satisfactorily addressed and they ask to proceed to the formal stage. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what can the Personal Tutor do?
options: Revise the student's grade themselves if they agree that the original mark was set too low
Refer the case directly to a Stage Two Appeal Panel, as informal resolution counts as Stage One
Submit the student's case to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator for an external review
Provide guidance, and the relevant forms, for the student to make an Academic Appeal
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors can provide guidance and the relevant forms for students to make an Academic Appeal where their concerns are not satisfactorily addressed and they ask to proceed to the formal stage.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors can also provide guidance, and relevant forms, for students to make an Academic Appeal, should their concerns not be satisfactorily addressed, and they request to proceed to the formal stage.

questions.question: During the initial evaluation of a Stage One academic appeal, the Registrar finds that it is not made for valid reasons. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what happens?
options: The appeal passes to a two-member Appeal Panel, which decides whether its reasons are valid
The student is issued a Completion of Procedures letter and referred to the Independent Adjudicator
The appeal is rejected, and the student receives a letter from the Registrar informing them of this
The appeal is returned to the student's Personal Tutor to be resolved through informal resolution
questions.explanation: If the initial evaluation finds the appeal is not made for valid reasons, it is rejected and the Registrar writes to the student informing them of this outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: The appeal(s) being rejected if it is not made for valid reasons, in which case the student shall receive a letter from the Registrar informing them of this outcome

questions.question: When an appeal reviewer forms an Appeal Panel at Stage One of the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what role must the reviewer take in relation to the panel?
options: Chair the panel and hold the casting vote if its two academic members disagree
Act as an administrator for the two independent academic panel members
Present the student's case to the panel on the student's behalf at the meeting
Sit as a third voting member alongside the two independent academic members
questions.explanation: A Stage One Appeal Panel consists of two academic members independent of the case, and the appeal reviewer must contribute as an administrator for the panel members.
questions.source_excerpt: To form an Appeal Panel, where membership consists of two academic members who are independent of the case. The appeal reviewer must contribute as an administrator for the panel members

questions.question: An appeal reviewer investigating a Stage One appeal finds, for valid reasons, that the grounds had a material impact on the student's progression. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what may the reviewer do?
options: Set aside the assessors' decision and confirm the corrected result directly to the student
Recommend an award for the student directly to Pearson as the awarding organisation
Refer the matter to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator for a binding decision
Request the Assessment and Progression Board to review or revise its decision or process
questions.explanation: The reviewer may ask the Assessment and Progression Board to review or revise its decision or process, but has no authority to set aside the assessors' decision or recommend an award.
questions.source_excerpt: To request the members of the Assessment and Progression Board to review or revise its decision or process where, for valid reasons, the grounds for appeal are found to have had material impact on the performance or progression of a student. ... Neither a reviewer nor any member of the Appeal Panel have the authority to set aside the decision of the assessors or recommend award

questions.question: A student's Stage One academic appeal is not upheld. According to the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what must the student be informed of?
options: Their right to request a review, together with instructions on how to do so and the time limits
That the decision is final and may not be the subject of any further appeal within the College
Their right to lodge a case directly with the OIA, which must receive it within 12 months
That they must return to their Personal Tutor to restart informal resolution before appealing
questions.explanation: If a Stage One appeal is not upheld, the student is informed of their right to request a review of Stage One, with instructions on how to do so and the time limits.
questions.source_excerpt: If the appeal is not upheld, the student will be informed of their right to request a review of Stage One, as well as instructions on how to do so and the time limits

questions.question: Following a Stage One appeal, the Assessment and Progression Board revises its decision. The student is unhappy with the revised decision and wants to appeal against it. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure say?
options: They may appeal the revised decision by submitting a new Stage One form within 15 working days
They may request a Stage Two review of it within 10 working days of receiving the revised decision
The revised decision is final, and the policy does not allow it to be the subject of further appeal
They may take the revised decision straight to the OIA without a Completion of Procedures letter
questions.explanation: A revised decision of the Assessment and Progression Board resulting from the Stage One process is final and may not be the subject of further appeal.
questions.source_excerpt: A revised decision of the Assessment and Progression Board resulting from this process shall be final and may not be the subject of further appeal

questions.question: A student had a relevant medical letter throughout Stage One but chose not to submit it. After the appeal is not upheld, they want a Stage Two review on the ground of new material evidence. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure indicate?
options: It qualifies, as any evidence not seen at Stage One counts as new material evidence for a review
It qualifies, provided the letter is submitted within 10 working days of the Stage One outcome
It cannot qualify, as the policy never allows new evidence to be used once Stage One has concluded
It does not fit: the ground needs exceptional circumstances to have prevented earlier submission
questions.explanation: The new material evidence ground covers only evidence the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier; a letter they simply chose not to submit does not meet it.
questions.source_excerpt: A request for a review must be based on the following limited grounds: ... New material evidence has emerged which the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier in the process

questions.question: The Quality Assurance Officer decides that a student's Stage Two review request is not on reasonable grounds and rejects it. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what happens next?
options: The request is returned to the Registrar, who then treats it as a fresh Stage One appeal
The student is issued a Completion of Procedures Letter and told of their right to go to the OIA
The request is passed to an Appeal Panel of two academic staff, which makes the final decision
The student may resubmit the same request on the same grounds within a further 10 working days
questions.explanation: If a Stage Two request is rejected, the student is issued a Completion of Procedures Letter and informed of their right to refer the matter to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator; only requests on reasonable grounds go to an Appeal Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: If the request is deemed to be on reasonable grounds, then the Quality Assurance Officer will refer it to an Appeal Panel. However, if the request is rejected, the student shall be issued a Completion of Procedures Letter and will be informed of their right to refer the matter to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
