questions.question: A Stage Two Appeal Panel reviews a case and accepts the original decision of the Assessment and Progression Board. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what follows for the student?
options: They are issued a Completion of Procedures letter, as the College's internal process is complete
The Board chair is required to review or revise the decision in respect of the student
They may request a second Stage Two review from the Quality Assurance Officer within 10 days
Their case is referred back to the Registrar for the Stage One appeal to be heard again
questions.explanation: One of the Stage Two outcomes is to accept the original decision of the Assessment and Progression Board and to issue a Completion of Procedures letter.
questions.source_excerpt: To accept the original decision of the Assessment and Progression Board and to issue a Completion of Procedures letter

questions.question: A student whose Stage One academic appeal was not upheld wants to take the matter straight to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, when can they put their case to the OIA?
options: Immediately, as the OIA accepts cases as soon as a Stage One appeal has not been upheld
Only once the Registrar has given written permission for the case to go to the OIA
Once Stage Two is exhausted and a Completion of Procedures letter has been issued
Only after the Assessment and Progression Board has met again to confirm its decision
questions.explanation: The student may put their case to Pearson or the OIA following the exhaustion of Stage Two, once a Completion of Procedures letter has been issued.
questions.source_excerpt: Following the exhaustion of Stage Two, the student shall be issued with a Completion of Procedures (COP) letter, following which the student may, if the matter has not been resolved to their satisfaction, put their case to the Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA)

questions.question: The Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure assigns two separate reporting duties to the Academic Board. Which pairing of role and report is correct?
options: The Quality Assurance Officer reports on appeals activity and outcomes; the Registrar produces the annual monitoring report
The Registrar reports on appeals activity and outcomes; the Assessment and Progression Board produces the annual monitoring report
The Assessment and Progression Board reports on appeals activity and outcomes; the Registrar produces the annual monitoring report
The Registrar reports on appeals activity and outcomes; the Quality Assurance Officer produces the annual monitoring report
questions.explanation: The Registrar reports to the Academic Board each year on the activity and outcomes of appeals, while the Assessment and Progression Board produces the annual monitoring report on the effectiveness of the appeals process.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will report to the Academic Board after the end of each academic year ... on the activity and outcomes of academic appeals made during that year ... The Assessment and Progression Board is responsible for producing an annual monitoring report to the Academic Board to ensure the effectiveness of appeals process

questions.question: A student's academic appeal disputes the marker's academic judgement and also shows that one unit mark was omitted when grades were processed, casting doubt on the result. How does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure treat the appeal?
options: It must be rejected outright, since any appeal that raises academic judgement is invalid under the policy
It can proceed on the processing-error ground, as it does not relate solely to academic judgement
It must be redirected to the Complaints Policy and Procedure, because it combines two different issues
It must first be referred to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator to separate out the two claims
questions.explanation: Only appeals relating solely and directly to academic judgement are invalid; an error in processing marks that casts doubt on the result is a listed ground, so the appeal can proceed on that basis.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic appeals are not valid where they relate solely and directly to claims concerning academic judgement; ... There was an administrative error or procedural irregularity or other inadequacy in the conduct of the assessor(s) or processing of marks or grades of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different if the error never occurred.

questions.question: Five HND students want to lodge one group academic appeal. Three were affected by a marks-processing error on a unit; the other two were affected by a separate, unrelated illness. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure allow?
options: All five may appeal together, since they are on the same programme and were assessed by the same Board
All five may appeal together, provided a member of the student representative body submits the appeal
The five cannot appeal as one group, as they are not all affected by the same set of circumstances
All five may appeal together, provided each student first gives the others written permission to do so
questions.explanation: Group appeals are acceptable only where all students in the group are affected by the same set of circumstances; two different sets of circumstances do not meet that condition.
questions.source_excerpt: Group appeals against decisions are acceptable, provided that all students within the group are affected by the same set of circumstances

questions.question: A student has completed their HND and received their award certificate. They now want to lodge a Stage One appeal against a unit grade, using the late appeals provision to explain the delay. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure indicate?
options: The late appeal may proceed if the student gives written reasons, with evidence, for the delay
The award certificate implies closure of any appeal within the College's procedure
The appeal may proceed only at Stage Two, as Stage One closes once a certificate is issued
The Registrar must accept it, as late appeals from graduates are considered automatically
questions.explanation: For students who have completed the course and received an award certificate, the policy treats any action or appeal within the College's procedure as closed, so the late appeals route does not reopen it.
questions.source_excerpt: For students who have completed the course and received an award certificate, this implies the closure of any action/appeal within the College's procedure

questions.question: The Registrar receives a Stage One academic appeal about a decision-making process in which the Registrar was personally involved. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, how should the appeal review be handled?
options: The Registrar conducts the review personally, as the policy names the Registrar as the reviewer
The Quality Assurance Officer takes over Stage One whenever the Registrar has a conflict
The chair of the Assessment and Progression Board reviews the appeal instead of the Registrar
The Registrar nominates an appeal reviewer who has had no previous involvement in the matter
questions.explanation: Appeals must be considered by someone impartial who was not involved in the processes leading to the claim, and the Registrar may nominate an appeal reviewer with no previous involvement.
questions.source_excerpt: All appeals are considered by someone who is impartial, and was not involved in processes leading to the appeal claim. ... the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim. This will be a member of staff who has had no previous involvement in the matter

questions.question: A student suffered a bereavement before an assessment and could easily have reported it before the Board decided, but chose not to. They now want to appeal on mitigating circumstances. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure indicate?
options: The ground applies, because the assessors were unaware of the bereavement when they made the decision
The ground applies, provided the appeal is lodged within 15 working days of the Result Publication Date
The ground does not fit, as it covers circumstances that could not reasonably have been presented
The ground applies only if the student's Personal Tutor confirms the bereavement in a signed statement
questions.explanation: The mitigating circumstances ground requires both that the assessors were unaware and that the circumstances could not reasonably have been presented to them; the second condition is not met here.
questions.source_excerpt: There were existing mitigating circumstances affecting the student's performance which the assessor(s) were not aware of when a decision was reached, and which could not reasonably have been presented to the assessors.

questions.question: A student was in hospital throughout Stage One and could not obtain a key medical report until after receiving the Stage One outcome. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what route is open to them?
options: Lodge a second Stage One appeal, since new evidence restarts the 15-working-day window
Request a Stage Two review on new material evidence within 10 working days of the outcome
Send the report straight to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator with its Complaint Form
Ask the Assessment and Progression Board directly to revise its decision using the report
questions.explanation: New material evidence that exceptional circumstances prevented the student from providing earlier is a ground for a Stage Two review, which must be requested within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: submit it to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome. ... New material evidence has emerged which the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier in the process

questions.question: A student lodges a Stage One academic appeal on the 14th working day after results are published and receives the Stage One outcome 10 working days later. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, by which working day after publication must their Stage Two form be submitted?
options: The 25th working day
The 29th working day
The 34th working day
The 39th working day
questions.explanation: The Stage One outcome arrives on working day 24, and the Stage Two form must be submitted within 10 working days of receiving that outcome, so by working day 34.
questions.source_excerpt: A student who wishes to have the Stage One decision reviewed must complete the Stage Two Academic Appeal form and submit it to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.

questions.question: After results are published, a student asks their Personal Tutor for help. Which of the following is a role that the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure gives to Personal Tutors rather than to other staff?
options: Advising how the student might achieve a higher grade in a future assessment
Carrying out the initial evaluation of whether an appeal falls within valid grounds
Nominating an independent appeal reviewer to investigate the student's claim
Deciding whether to accept the student's reasons for submitting a late appeal
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors can advise students on how they might achieve a higher grade in a future assessment; checking grounds and nominating a reviewer are for the Registrar, and late appeals are decided by the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can discuss their results with their Personal Tutors, who can advise the student on how they might achieve a higher grade in a future assessment.

questions.question: Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, who first decides whether an academic appeal or review request goes forward at each of the two formal stages?
options: Stage One: the Personal Tutor; Stage Two: the Registrar
Stage One: the Registrar; Stage Two: the Quality Assurance Officer
Stage One: the appeal reviewer; Stage Two: the chair of the Board
Stage One: the Quality Assurance Officer; Stage Two: the Registrar
questions.explanation: At Stage One the Registrar's initial evaluation decides whether the appeal proceeds to formal consideration; at Stage Two the Quality Assurance Officer refers requests on reasonable grounds to an Appeal Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: On receipt of an academic appeal, the Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation ... The academic appeal proceeding to formal consideration. ... If the request is deemed to be on reasonable grounds, then the Quality Assurance Officer will refer it to an Appeal Panel.

questions.question: Comparing the Appeal Panels at Stage One and Stage Two of the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, which statement is correct?
options: Both have two academic members independent of the case; Stage Two members must not have sat on the Stage One panel
Stage One has three voting members including the reviewer; Stage Two has two academics chosen by the Registrar
Both are chaired by the Registrar, with one academic member and one member of the student representative body
Stage One has two academic members; Stage Two reuses the same two members so the case is heard consistently
questions.explanation: Both panels have two academic members independent of the case, and Stage Two members must not have participated as members of the Stage One panel.
questions.source_excerpt: To form an Appeal Panel, where membership consists of two academic members who are independent of the case. ... The Appeal Panel will be comprised of two members of the academic staff who are independent of the case and have not participated as a member of the panel in stage one

questions.question: A Stage Two Appeal Panel agrees with how Stage One was handled and with its outcome, but identifies factors that have since come to light which mean the Board's decision should change. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what is the outcome?
options: A Completion of Procedures letter is issued, because the Stage One procedure and its outcome were both upheld
The case returns to the Registrar so that Stage One can be reopened to consider the new factors
The Panel sets aside the Board's decision and issues the student with a revised result directly
The student is told the review upheld the earlier investigation, but the Board's decision needs revising
questions.explanation: One Stage Two outcome is to inform the student that the review upheld the previous investigation, but other factors since identified require revision of the Assessment and Progression Board's decision.
questions.source_excerpt: To inform the student that the review upheld the procedure and outcome of the previous investigation, but other factors have since been identified as leading to a requirement for revision of the Assessment and Progression Board's decision.

questions.question: A Stage Two review concludes that the Assessment and Progression Board's decision about a student must be looked at again. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, who is then required to review or revise that decision?
options: The chair of the Assessment and Progression Board, or their nominated person
The two members of the Stage Two Appeal Panel, who substitute a new grade
The Quality Assurance Officer, who issues the revised result to the student
The original assessor, who re-marks the work in line with the Panel's findings
questions.explanation: The Stage Two outcome requires the chair of the Assessment and Progression Board (or nominee) to review or revise the decision; Panel members have no authority to set aside the assessors' decision.
questions.source_excerpt: To confirm that the chair of the Assessment and Progression Board (or his/her nominated person) will be required to review or revise their decision or process in respect of the student; ... Neither a reviewer nor any member of the Appeal Panel have the authority to set aside the decision of the assessors

questions.question: A Stage One appeal reviewer finds the student's grounds valid but concludes they had no material impact on the student's performance or progression. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, can the reviewer ask the Assessment and Progression Board to review its decision?
options: Yes, because any appeal found to rest on valid grounds must be referred back to the Board
No, because that power applies only where the grounds had a material impact on the student
Yes, provided that an Appeal Panel of two independent academics agrees with the referral
No, because only the Quality Assurance Officer may ask the Board to review its decisions
questions.explanation: The reviewer may ask the Board to review or revise its decision only where the grounds are found to have had a material impact on the student's performance or progression.
questions.source_excerpt: To request the members of the Assessment and Progression Board to review or revise its decision or process where, for valid reasons, the grounds for appeal are found to have had material impact on the performance or progression of a student.

questions.question: A student's Completion of Procedures letter is dated 1 March 2025. They post their signed OIA complaint form on 25 February 2026 and it reaches the OIA on 4 March 2026. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, how will the OIA treat it?
options: As in time, because the form was posted within 12 months of the date of the COP letter
As in time, because the 12 months run from the date of the Stage Two Panel's outcome
As in time, because the OIA allows 12 months from when the student received the letter
As out of time, because the OIA must receive the form within 12 months of the letter's date
questions.explanation: The OIA must receive the signed form within 12 months of the date of the COP letter; posting it within that period is not enough if it arrives afterwards.
questions.source_excerpt: The OIA must receive the signed form within 12 months of the date of the COP letter, otherwise it will consider the complaint to be out of time.

questions.question: A student has exhausted Stage Two and holds a Completion of Procedures letter, but the matter is not resolved to their satisfaction. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, how can they take their case further?
options: By completing the Complaint Form of Pearson or the OIA; the COP letter advises where to obtain it
By asking the Registrar to forward the whole case file to the OIA on their behalf for a decision
By requesting a further review from the Academic Board, which must be completed before the OIA
By applying to Pearson first, as the OIA will only accept cases that Pearson has already rejected
questions.explanation: After the COP letter the student may put their case to Pearson or the OIA by completing the relevant organisation's Complaint Form, and the COP letter advises where to obtain it.
questions.source_excerpt: put their case to the Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA) by completing the relevant organisation's Complaint Form; ... In addition, the COP letter will advise the student of where to obtain the Complaint Form and Guidance Note of the relevant organisations

questions.question: An internal check finds that Stage One appeal decisions are regularly issued later than the policy's timeline. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, which report is expected to comment on the timeliness of the appeals process?
options: The Quality Assurance Officer's Stage Two review report to the Registrar
The appeal reviewer's investigation report to the Assessment and Progression Board
The Assessment and Progression Board's annual monitoring report to the Academic Board
The Office of the Independent Adjudicator's annual report on its member institutions
questions.explanation: The Assessment and Progression Board's annual monitoring report to the Academic Board should include commentary on the timeliness of the appeals process.
questions.source_excerpt: The Assessment and Progression Board is responsible for producing an annual monitoring report to the Academic Board to ensure the effectiveness of appeals process; ... This report should consider the commentary on timeliness of the process

questions.question: A student wants a member of the student representative body to help prepare their appeal, and a friend who graduated from LCC last year to accompany them to the Stage Two Panel meeting. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure allow?
options: Both are allowed, as former LCC students count as members of the College community
Neither is allowed, as only the Personal Tutor may assist and companions are not permitted
The graduate may attend as companion, but representatives may not assist at Stage Two
The representative may assist, but the companion must be a current LCC student or staff member
questions.explanation: A student may seek assistance from any member of the student representative body, but a Stage Two companion must be a current LCC student or member of staff.
questions.source_excerpt: During the appeal process, a student may seek assistance from his/her assigned Personal Tutor or any member from the student representative body; ... They will be entitled to bring a current LCC student/member of staff as a companion

questions.question: A student appealing on mitigating circumstances wants to rely on a hospital letter about their mother's illness, and the letter is written in Bengali. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what should the student do with this evidence?
options: Submit it unchanged; the Registrar arranges a translation, and no consent is needed as the mother is the next of kin
Obtain their mother's written permission to disclose her data, and provide an authorised translation of the letter
Provide an authorised translation only, as medical evidence for this ground is exempt from third-party consent
Obtain their mother's written permission only, as medical letters may be given to the Panel in any language
questions.explanation: Another person's personal data may be disclosed in an appeal only with that person's written permission, and evidence that cannot be submitted in English needs an authorised translation.
questions.source_excerpt: A student must also avoid disclosing personal data of any other person in the appeal unless they have been given written permission by the person/s to do so; ... Any medical or documentary evidence should be submitted in English. If this is not possible, the student should provide an authorised translation of the relevant documents to support such claims.

questions.question: A student's Stage One appeal is not upheld and they pursue the matter all the way to the OIA. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, which set of time limits applies from the Stage One outcome onwards?
options: Review request within 10 working days; outcome within 15 working days of Panel; OIA form within 12 months of COP letter
Review request within 15 working days; outcome within 10 working days of Panel; OIA form within 12 months of COP letter
Review request within 10 working days; outcome within 15 working days of Panel; OIA form within 6 months of COP letter
Review request within 10 working days; outcome within 10 working days of Panel; OIA form within 12 months of Panel date
questions.explanation: A Stage Two review must be requested within 10 working days of the Stage One outcome, the outcome is issued within 15 working days of the Panel, and the OIA must receive the form within 12 months of the COP letter.
questions.source_excerpt: Must be made within 10 working days of Stage One outcome ... Outcome issued to student within 15 working days of Panel ... The OIA must receive the signed form within 12 months of the date of the COP letter

questions.question: A student's results letter misspells their surname, but every mark and grade was recorded and processed correctly. They want to appeal on the ground of administrative error. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure indicate?
options: It does not fit, as the error must be such as to cause doubt on whether the result might have been different
It fits, as any administrative error in the processing of results is a valid ground for an academic appeal
It does not fit, as administrative errors are handled under the Complaints Policy and Procedure instead
It fits, provided the student supports it with documentary evidence acceptable to the Appeal Panel
questions.explanation: The administrative error ground covers errors of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different; a misspelt name on correctly processed marks does not meet that test.
questions.source_excerpt: There was an administrative error or procedural irregularity or other inadequacy in the conduct of the assessor(s) or processing of marks or grades of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different if the error never occurred.

questions.question: The Registrar plans to nominate a student's Personal Tutor as the Stage One appeal reviewer. The tutor did not mark the work but discussed the disputed results with the student at the informal stage and supplied the appeal forms. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure indicate?
options: The tutor may act, as only staff who marked or assessed the work count as involved in the matter
The tutor should not act, as the reviewer must not have been involved in processes leading to the appeal
The tutor should not act, as the Registrar must conduct every Stage One appeal review in person
The tutor may act, provided the student agrees in writing, as the tutor already knows the case and results well
questions.explanation: Appeals must be considered by someone impartial who was not involved in the processes leading to the appeal claim, and a nominated reviewer must have had no previous involvement in the matter; the tutor handled this case at the informal stage.
questions.source_excerpt: All appeals are considered by someone who is impartial, and was not involved in processes leading to the appeal claim ... the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim. This will be a member of staff who has had no previous involvement in the matter

questions.question: A student whose Stage One appeal was not upheld sends the Stage Two form to the Quality Assurance Officer 9 working days after the outcome. Their only argument is that the marker's academic judgement was too harsh. Under the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, what should follow?
options: It is referred to an Appeal Panel, as it reached the correct officer within 10 working days
It is returned to the Registrar, who reopens Stage One to reconsider the marker's judgement
It is rejected as outside the review grounds and a Completion of Procedures Letter follows
It is sent to the chair of the Assessment and Progression Board to review the unit's marking
questions.explanation: A Stage Two request must rest on the limited review grounds, and appeals relating solely to academic judgement are not valid; a rejected request leads to a Completion of Procedures Letter and notice of the right to go to the OIA.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic appeals are not valid where they relate solely and directly to claims concerning academic judgement ... A request for a review must be based on the following limited grounds ... if the request is rejected, the student shall be issued a Completion of Procedures Letter

questions.question: An entire HND cohort wants to lodge a group academic appeal because they all believe one unit was marked too harshly. No administrative error, irregularity or mitigating circumstances are alleged. What does the Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure indicate?
options: It is valid, as group appeals are acceptable where all students are affected by the same circumstances
It is valid only if a member of the student representative body submits it for the whole cohort
It must go straight to a Stage Two review, as group appeals bypass the Stage One formal stage
It is not valid, as appeals relating solely to academic judgement are not valid, even from a group
questions.explanation: Group appeals are acceptable where all students share the same circumstances, but academic appeals are not valid where they relate solely and directly to academic judgement, so a cohort disagreeing with the marking has no valid ground.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic appeals are not valid where they relate solely and directly to claims concerning academic judgement ... Group appeals against decisions are acceptable, provided that all students within the group are affected by the same set of circumstances

questions.question: According to LCC's Academic Freedom Policy, members of the academic community are free to question received wisdom and put forward controversial or unpopular opinions without fear of what?
options: Being challenged by colleagues or students in debate
Their work being reviewed by the Academic Board
Being required to support their arguments with sound and reliable evidence
Legal or disciplinary action being taken against them
questions.explanation: The policy's definition of academic freedom (from the Education Reform Act 1988) states that members of the academic community can put forward controversial or unpopular opinions without fear of legal or disciplinary action. The Code of Practice still expects debate to be challenged and supported by sound evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: ensures that members of the academic community are free to question, and test received wisdom and put forward new ideas and controversial or unpopular opinions without fear of legal or disciplinary action.

questions.question: A lecturer wants to share their personal political views while teaching a module on public policy. What does the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice expect of them?
options: Avoid discussing politics in teaching sessions, as political topics fall outside the scope of academic freedom
Obtain written approval from the Registrar before sharing their personal views with the class
Clearly differentiate their personal beliefs from objective academic observations and judgements
Ask students to adopt the same view so that the discussion stays focused on the module's learning outcomes
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice requires staff to differentiate clearly their personal beliefs from objective academic observations and judgements, and not to attempt to impose beliefs on others.
questions.source_excerpt: To differentiate clearly one's personal beliefs from objective academic observations and judgments;

questions.question: You are invited to comment on local radio, in a personal capacity, about a controversial issue in your subject area. What does the Academic Freedom Policy require of you?
options: Indicate clearly that you are not speaking on behalf of LCC unless expressly authorised
Decline the invitation, as staff may not comment publicly on controversial issues in their subject
Present your view as LCC's official position so that it carries the College's authority
Agree to speak on condition that the station does not mention your name or job title
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice states that when communicating in public, staff should indicate clearly that they are not communicating on behalf of LCC unless expressly authorised to do so.
questions.source_excerpt: If communicating in public, staff and students should indicate clearly that they are not communicating on behalf of LCC unless expressly authorised to do so.

questions.question: A colleague tells you they believe the Academic Freedom Policy is being breached in their department. To whom does the policy say concerns about breaches should be reported?
options: The HR Director
The Registrar
The Principal
The Students' Union President
questions.explanation: The Monitoring and Review section states that concerns about breaches of the Academic Freedom Policy should be reported to the Registrar (LCC's complaints procedures can also be used).
questions.source_excerpt: Concerns about breaches of this policy should be reported to the Registrar

questions.question: A member of staff wants to raise, in good faith, a concern about academic standards at LCC but fears repercussions. What does the Academic Freedom Policy state?
options: They will not be treated less favourably, and LCC will take the concern seriously and investigate
They must first provide documentary proof that the concern is valid before LCC will investigate it
They may face disciplinary action if the concern is later found to be unfounded following investigation
They should raise it anonymously, as LCC does not investigate concerns submitted under a staff member's name
questions.explanation: The policy guarantees that anyone raising concerns about academic or professional standards in good faith will not be treated less favourably, and that LCC will take such disclosures seriously and investigate them.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will ensure that no member of staff, director, student or third party will be treated less favourably by LCC where they raise concerns about academic or professional ... standards at LCC, where such matters are raised in good faith. LCC will take all such disclosures seriously and investigate in accordance with the appropriate policies and procedures.

questions.question: You believe you have witnessed a SERIOUS breach of the Academic Freedom Policy. Through which LCC policy does the Academic Freedom Policy say serious breaches may be reported?
options: The Student Academic Appeals and Assessment Procedure
The Staff Performance Appraisal and Probation Policy
The Mitigating Circumstances Policy
The Protected Disclosures (Whistleblowing) Policy
questions.explanation: The policy states that serious breaches may be reported through LCC's Protected Disclosures (Whistleblowing) Policy, which reflects the principles of openness, accountability and natural justice.
questions.source_excerpt: Serious breaches of this policy may be reported though LCC's Protected Disclosures (Whistleblowing) Policy

questions.question: Under the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice, which of the following is NOT one of the behaviours expected of staff and students?
options: To be objective and open to new ideas and opinions at all times
To avoid challenging others' views so that disagreement never arises
To have regard for appropriate ethical considerations when conducting research
To listen and take account of views and arguments contrary to one's own
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice expects people to challenge, in a way that is not harmful or disruptive, and to engage with contrary views; avoiding challenge altogether is not an expected behaviour. The other three options are listed behaviours.
questions.source_excerpt: To challenge in a way that is not harmful to others or to the reputation of LCC or disruptive to teaching, and discussion;

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, how should the Prevent Duty relate to balanced discussion of controversial issues such as religion, politics and current affairs?
options: It requires staff to avoid discussing religion and politics in teaching to reduce the risk of radicalisation
It overrides academic freedom whenever a topic is considered controversial or politically sensitive
It should not be obstructive, but ensure an environment in which such discussion can thrive
It requires such discussions to be pre-approved by the Academic Board before they take place in class
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Prevent Duty should not be obstructive to academic freedom, freedom of speech or balanced discussion of controversial issues, but should ensure an environment in which these can thrive.
questions.source_excerpt: The Prevent duty should not be obstructive to academic freedom, freedom of speech or balanced discussion of controversial issues such as religion, politics, and current affairs, rather it should ensure an environment in which these can thrive.

questions.question: A lawful external organisation asks to book an LCC room for an event. A colleague suggests refusing because the organisation's views are unpopular. What does the Academic Freedom Policy say?
options: Premises must not be denied on grounds of the body's beliefs, views, policies or objectives, if use is within the law
The booking may be refused if a majority of staff consulted find the organisation's views objectionable
The booking may proceed on condition that the organisation also presents LCC's institutional views at the event
The booking should be refused, as unpopular views belong in peer-reviewed academic research rather than public events
questions.explanation: The policy commits LCC to ensuring its premises are not denied on grounds connected with the beliefs, views, policies or objectives of an individual or body, provided the use is within the law.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will ensure the use of its premises is not denied on grounds connected with the beliefs, views, policies, or objectives of an individual or body of individuals, if such use is always within the law.

questions.question: The Academic Freedom Policy states that LCC will ensure its core values are incorporated within its policies and procedures for the management of which of the following?
options: Staff recruitment, induction and probation reviews
External speakers and off-campus events
Student tuition fees and refunds
IT security, data backups and system access
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC will incorporate its core values (the fundamental British values) within its policies and procedures for managing external speakers and off-campus events.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will ensure the above tenets are incorporated within its policies and procedures for the management of external speakers and off-campus events.

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, the statutory duty to take reasonably practicable steps to secure freedom of speech within the law applies to which people?
options: Academic staff while teaching or publishing research, but not students or visiting speakers
Students and employees of the establishment, but not visiting speakers invited to LCC
Members, students and employees of the establishment, and visiting speakers
Governors and directors acting in an official capacity for LCC
questions.explanation: The policy explains that the legal duty is to ensure freedom of speech within the law is secured for members, students and employees of the establishment and for visiting speakers.
questions.source_excerpt: take such steps as are reasonably practicable to ensure that freedom of speech within the law is secured for members, students, and employees of the establishment and for visiting speakers.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed in the Academic Freedom Policy as a freedom LCC will take deliberate measures to lawfully safeguard?
options: Freedom from review of one's teaching strategies by the Academic Board
Freedom to decide which LCC policies and codes apply to one's teaching
Freedom to set aside legal obligations where they limit academic debate
Freedom to participate in professional and representative academic bodies
questions.explanation: Freedom to participate in professional and representative academic bodies is one of the freedoms the policy lists. The other options contradict the policy, which requires staff to adhere to it and to applicable laws, and provides for the Academic Board to review teaching strategies and practices.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will take deliberate measures to lawfully safeguard: ... Freedom to participate in professional and representative academic bodies;

questions.question: The Academic Freedom Policy states that it should be read in conjunction with which other LCC document?
options: The Academic Integrity Policy and Misconduct Procedure
The Freedom of Speech Policy and Code of Practice
The External Speakers and Events Booking Procedure
The Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy
questions.explanation: The Aim section states that the Academic Freedom Policy should be read in conjunction with the Freedom of Speech Policy and Code of Practice.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy should be read in conjunction with the Freedom of Speech Policy and Code of Practice.

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, how does LCC interpret freedom of speech within the context of higher education?
options: Being able to speak on any subject, in any setting, without having to justify one's views
Being able to express views on academic subjects, provided they reflect LCC's published values
Being able to express, encounter, negotiate and enjoy difference in a climate of respect and learning
Being able to voice opinions in timetabled teaching sessions, where staff can moderate the debate
questions.explanation: The policy states that, within higher education, LCC interprets freedom of speech as being able to express, encounter, negotiate and enjoy difference in a climate of respect and learning.
questions.source_excerpt: Within the context of Higher Education LCC interprets this as being able to ... express, encounter, negotiate and enjoy difference in a climate of respect and learning

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, LCC considers the principle of academic freedom to be central to the development of what?
options: Its academic policies and teaching strategies
Its academic calendar and term-date planning
Its staff appraisal and promotion criteria
Its estates strategy and room booking rules
questions.explanation: The definitions section states that LCC considers academic freedom central to the development of its academic policies and teaching strategies.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC considers the principle of Academic Freedom to be central to the development of its academic policies and teaching strategies

questions.question: The Academic Freedom Policy lists competencies that LCC, as a UK higher education provider, must inculcate in students. Which of the following is one of them?
options: Commercial and enterprise skills
Fluency in a second language
Personal financial and budgeting skills
Media and internet literacy
questions.explanation: Media and internet literacy is listed alongside healthy scepticism, critical and introspective thinking, rational methodologies and understanding of history. The other options are not listed.
questions.source_excerpt: to inculcate students the values of democracy and the competencies of healthy scepticism, critical and introspective thinking, rational methodologies, understanding of history and media and internet literacy.

questions.question: In return for LCC respecting their right to exercise academic freedom and freedom of speech, what does the Academic Freedom Policy require of staff and students?
options: That they obtain line manager approval before exercising those rights publicly
That they sign an annual declaration of political neutrality
That they adhere to this policy when exercising those rights
That they limit public comment to their own area of expertise
questions.explanation: The policy states that, in return for respecting this right, LCC requires staff and students to adhere to the policy in exercising it.
questions.source_excerpt: In respecting the right of staff and students to exercise academic freedom and freedom of speech, LCC requires that they, in return, adhere to this policy in exercising this right.

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, where is oversight of the effectiveness of LCC's policies and processes for protecting academic freedom and freedom of speech maintained?
options: At senior levels of governance
At programme level, through annual module reviews
By the Students' Union executive
By external auditors
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC ensures oversight of the effectiveness of these policies and processes is maintained at senior levels of governance.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC has in place clear policies and processes for the protection of academic freedom and freedom of speech within the law and ensures that oversight of their effectiveness is maintained at senior levels of governance.

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, for the purposes of the Education (No 2) Act 1986, LCC's duty to secure freedom of speech extends to which of the following?
options: Local council venues
Overseas partner campuses
Placement providers
Student activities
questions.explanation: The Legal Obligations section states that, for the purposes of the Act, LCC's duty extends to student activities.
questions.source_excerpt: For the purposes of the Act, LCC's duty extends to Student activities.

questions.question: Which of the following does the Academic Freedom Policy list among the obligations LCC must also fulfil while preserving academic freedom and freedom of speech?
options: The duty to keep teaching politically neutral
The duty of care to staff, students and visitors
The duty to vet public statements made by staff
The duty to protect LCC's commercial brand
questions.explanation: The duty of care to staff, students and visitors is one of the listed obligations that may set limits on certain freedoms. The other duties are not in the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC must ensure in preserving academic freedom and freedom of speech that it fulfils other relevant obligations and commitments under the following legislation: ... The duty of care to staff, students and visitors

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, in which areas does LCC ensure its principles of academic freedom and freedom of speech are applied?
options: In taught modules and research, but not professional services
In Academic Board and committee business only
In all aspects of LCC's professional and academic work
At public events held on LCC premises only
questions.explanation: The Principles section states that LCC ensures its principles of academic freedom and freedom of speech are applied in all aspects of its professional and academic work.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC ensures that its principles of Academic Freedom and Freedom of Speech are applied in all aspects of the LCC's professional and academic work

questions.question: The Academic Freedom Policy names the fundamental British values as LCC's core values. Which of the following is one of them?
options: Support for the equality of opportunity for all
Respect for the authority of senior academic staff in debate
Loyalty to LCC's mission ahead of personal opinion
Support for the College's strategic and commercial aims
questions.explanation: Support for the equality of opportunity for all is one of the fundamental British values the policy lists as LCC's core values. The other options are not listed.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will be guided by its core values, which are the fundamental British values of: ... Support for the equality of opportunity for all

questions.question: Under the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice, academic debate should be guided by rational enquiry and supported by what?
options: The programme team's agreed view
Academic Board approval
Participants' personal experience
Sound and reliable evidence
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice expects everyone to ensure academic debate is guided by rational enquiry and supported by sound and reliable evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: To ensure academic debate is guided by rational enquiry and supported by sound and reliable evidence;

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, by what method is LCC committed to resolving problems and controversies?
options: Formal mediation by HR
Rational discussion
An Academic Board vote
A ruling by the Registrar
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice section states that LCC is committed to resolving problems and controversies by the method of rational discussion.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC is committed to resolving of problems and controversies by the method of rational discussion

questions.question: How does the Academic Freedom Policy describe disruptive acts that interfere with campus activities or with students' freedom to pursue their studies?
options: As an exercise of academic freedom linked to public interest
As a matter for the Students' Union to address rather than LCC
As the antithesis of academic freedom, which LCC will not tolerate
As acceptable if peaceful and no longer than one teaching session
questions.explanation: The policy states that acts or threats of physical force, or disruptive acts interfering with campus activities or students' studies, are the antithesis of academic freedom and will not be tolerated.
questions.source_excerpt: disruptive acts which interfere with campus activities, freedom of movement on the campus, or freedom for students to pursue their studies are the antithesis of academic freedom and will not be tolerated by LCC.

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, which body is the custodian of academic freedom and freedom of speech at LCC?
options: The Academic Board
The Board of Directors
The Registrar
The Quality and Enhancement Steering Committee
questions.explanation: The Responsibility section states that the Academic Board is the custodian of academic freedom and freedom of speech at LCC.
questions.source_excerpt: the Academic Board is the custodian of academic freedom and freedom of speech at LCC.

questions.question: Alongside LCC's staff, students and executive members, who does the Academic Freedom Policy say is responsible for upholding the policy and its Code of Practice?
options: Parents and guardians of students enrolled on LCC courses
Employers who go on to recruit LCC graduates
Members of the public attending LCC open days
External parties invited to contribute to learning
questions.explanation: The policy makes upholding it the responsibility of all members of LCC's community and of any external parties invited by LCC to contribute to the learning experience.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the responsibility of all members of LCC's community (extending to all staff, students, and executive members), as well any external parties invited by LCC to contribute to the learning experience, to uphold this policy

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, to whom does the Academic Board report its activities and findings from reviewing teaching strategies and practices?
options: The Office for Students
The Board of Directors
The Registrar
The Students' Union
questions.explanation: The Monitoring and Review section states that the Academic Board reviews teaching strategies and practices and reports its activities and findings to the Board of Directors.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic Board will intermittently review teaching strategies and practices at LCC ... it will report its activities and findings to the Board of Directors.

questions.question: Apart from reporting concerns to the Registrar, what does the Academic Freedom Policy say can be used to report and address risks to academic freedom and freedom of speech?
options: LCC's complaints procedures
The annual staff survey
Module evaluation questionnaires
The staff suggestion scheme
questions.explanation: The policy states that, as an alternative to reporting to the Registrar, LCC's complaints procedures can be used to report and address these risks.
questions.source_excerpt: Alternatively, LCC's complaints procedures can be used to report and address risks associated with academic freedom and freedom of speech.

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, the Prevent Duty is LCC's statutory duty to have due regard for the need to do what?
options: Monitor all student communications for extremist content
Report every controversial visiting speaker to the police
Stop people from being drawn into terrorism
Ban discussion of religion and politics on campus
questions.explanation: The policy defines the Prevent Duty as the statutory duty to have due regard for the need to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism, without obstructing academic freedom.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC has a statutory duty to have due regard for the need to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism; this is formally referred to as the Prevent Duty.

questions.question: The Academic Freedom Policy commits LCC to an environment in which staff and students can exercise their civil rights as citizens, including the right to do what?
options: Take industrial action without giving notice to the College
Book College premises for private events free of charge
Publish under the College's name without prior authorisation
Contribute to social change through free expression of opinion
questions.explanation: The policy commits LCC to preserving an environment where staff and students can exercise their rights, including contributing to social change through free expression of opinion on matters of public interest.
questions.source_excerpt: including the right to contribute to social change through free expression of opinion on matters of public interest.

questions.question: The Academic Freedom Policy defines academic freedom and freedom of speech separately. Which description matches its definition of freedom of speech rather than its definition of academic freedom?
options: The right of all people to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority
The freedom of members of the academic community to question and test received wisdom without fear of legal or disciplinary action
The freedom of the academic community to put forward new ideas and controversial or unpopular opinions in their work
The right of staff and students to express opinions on LCC premises provided they reflect the fundamental British values
questions.explanation: The policy defines freedom of speech, under the Human Rights Act 1998, as the right of all people to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority. Questioning received wisdom and putting forward new or unpopular ideas is its definition of academic freedom.
questions.source_excerpt: Freedom of speech (or expression) as defined under the Human Rights Act 1998 refers more broadly to the rights of all people ... to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority and regardless of frontiers.

questions.question: A student society plans a debate at LCC with a visiting speaker whose lawful views are controversial. A colleague says LCC's freedom of speech duty covers only staff-run events. What does the Academic Freedom Policy say?
options: The duty covers staff-run events only; student society events are governed by the Students' Union's own rules
The duty extends to student activities and includes securing freedom of speech within the law for visiting speakers
The duty applies to student events only where a member of academic staff chairs the debate and moderates questions
Student events are covered only once the Registrar has approved the visiting speaker in writing beforehand
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC's duty under the Act extends to student activities, and that the duty is to secure freedom of speech within the law for members, students, employees and visiting speakers.
questions.source_excerpt: ensure that freedom of speech within the law is secured for members, students, and employees of the establishment and for visiting speakers. ... For the purposes of the Act, LCC's duty extends to Student activities.

questions.question: A colleague argues that academic freedom means LCC can never place any limit on what is said at a College event. According to the Academic Freedom Policy, why may certain freedoms be limited?
options: Because the marketing team may restrict views that conflict with the College's brand and recruitment messaging
Because freedoms apply only to published research and peer-reviewed work, not to College events or teaching
Because legal obligations may set limits on them to protect the rights and freedoms of others
Because the Academic Board may restrict any opinion that a majority of staff consider unpopular or offensive
questions.explanation: The policy recognises that legal obligations may set limits on certain freedoms in order to protect the rights and freedoms of others, and LCC must fulfil those obligations while preserving academic freedom.
questions.source_excerpt: Legal obligations also exist which may set limits on certain freedoms, to protect the rights and freedoms of others.

questions.question: An organisation asks to hire an LCC room, and it is clear the planned event would involve unlawful activity. How does the Academic Freedom Policy's commitment on the use of LCC premises apply?
options: LCC must still allow the booking, since premises cannot be denied on grounds of a body's policies or objectives
The booking must go ahead, but LCC may require its institutional view to be presented at the event
LCC may refuse only if a majority of the Academic Board votes that the organisation's views are objectionable
LCC's commitment not to deny premises on grounds of beliefs or views applies only where use is within the law
questions.explanation: LCC commits not to deny the use of its premises on grounds connected with beliefs, views, policies or objectives, but only where such use is within the law.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will ensure the use of its premises is not denied on grounds connected with the beliefs, views, policies, or objectives of an individual or body of individuals, if such use is always within the law.

questions.question: An LCC governor and an industry guest speaker both contribute to a seminar for students. According to the Academic Freedom Policy, who is expected to exemplify the Code of Practice behaviours?
options: Both of them, along with the staff and students taking part, as contributors to learning at LCC
Only the staff and students, as governors and guest speakers fall outside the Code of Practice
The governor only, since external third parties are covered by separate visiting speaker rules
The guest speaker only, since governors are bound instead by the Board of Directors' own code
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice applies to all staff, students, governors and any external third parties contributing to the delivery of learning opportunities at LCC.
questions.source_excerpt: In the exercise of academic freedom, all staff, students, governors and any external third parties contributing to the delivery of learning opportunities at LCC are expected to exemplify the following behaviours

questions.question: A tutor proposes excluding students with caring responsibilities from an evening research group, assuming they will not attend reliably. How does the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice apply?
options: Caring responsibilities are not among the personal characteristics the Code refers to, so it is permitted
Everyone should refrain from excluding others from academic activity on grounds such as caring responsibilities
The exclusion is acceptable if the reason is recorded in the module handbook before the group starts
The exclusion is acceptable provided the students are offered a place in an equivalent daytime group
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice requires everyone to refrain from discrimination or the exclusion of others from academic activity on grounds including caring responsibilities or any other personal characteristics.
questions.source_excerpt: To refrain from all forms of discrimination or the exclusion of others form academic activity whether on grounds of gender, racial background, sexual orientation, age, ... disability, religious belief, marital status, caring responsibilities or any other personal characteristics;

questions.question: A lecturer plans to present an argument that some students will find contrary to their cultural or religious beliefs. What does the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice expect of the lecturer?
options: They should not present it at all, as ideas contrary to students' own beliefs fall outside academic freedom
They must first obtain written consent from each student before presenting the contrary argument
They may present it but should respect others' beliefs and not cause unnecessary distress in doing so
They may present it only if students are told in advance that they cannot respond or disagree
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice allows contrary ideas to be expressed but expects people to be respectful of others' personal beliefs, cultural attitudes and opinions and not to cause unnecessary distress.
questions.source_excerpt: To be respectful to the personal beliefs, cultural attitudes and opinions of others, and not to cause unnecessary distress in the expression of contrary ideas and opinions

questions.question: In a programme meeting, a colleague dismisses a well-argued proposal simply because it contradicts LCC's institutional position. Which Code of Practice behaviour in the Academic Freedom Policy does this fall short of?
options: Deferring to the College's published position whenever any proposal is discussed at programme level
Keeping discussion confined to matters already approved by the Academic Board and senior governance
Raising any challenge to LCC's institutional position formally with the Registrar before discussing it
Taking account of views contrary to one's own beliefs, whether personally or institutionally held
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice expects everyone to listen and take account of views and arguments contrary to their own beliefs and opinions, whether those beliefs are personally or institutionally held.
questions.source_excerpt: To listen and take account of views and arguments contrary to one's own beliefs and opinions, whether these be personally or institutionally held;

questions.question: A lecturer wants to share course materials in a way that would breach copyright law, arguing that academic freedom permits it. What does the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice say?
options: Professional and academic activities must not conflict with applicable laws and statutes
Freedom in teaching and discussion takes priority over copyright rules when materials are used in class
Copyright breaches are acceptable if materials are used only in timetabled teaching and never published
Such breaches are acceptable provided the Academic Board is informed once the module has finished
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice requires everyone to ensure that their professional or academic activities do not conflict with applicable laws and statutes; academic freedom does not override the law.
questions.source_excerpt: To ensure that professional or academic activities do not conflict with applicable laws and statutes;

questions.question: Which pairing of a person or body with its role is correct under the Academic Freedom Policy?
options: Board of Directors: intermittently reviews LCC's teaching strategies and practices
Registrar: the person to whom concerns about breaches of the policy are reported
Board of Directors: holds ultimate responsibility for academic standards at LCC
Registrar: the custodian of academic freedom and freedom of speech at LCC
questions.explanation: Concerns about breaches are reported to the Registrar. The Academic Board, not the Board of Directors or the Registrar, reviews teaching strategies and practices, holds ultimate responsibility for academic standards and is the custodian of academic freedom.
questions.source_excerpt: the Academic Board is the custodian of academic freedom and freedom of speech at LCC. ... The Academic Board will intermittently review teaching strategies and practices at LCC ... Concerns about breaches of this policy should be reported to the Registrar

questions.question: According to the Academic Freedom Policy, what is the purpose of the Academic Board's intermittent review of teaching strategies and practices at LCC?
options: To approve in advance the content of any lecture that covers a controversial or sensitive topic
To identify staff whose personal views conflict with the College's institutional position
To satisfy itself that the policy's principles and Code of Practice are duly upheld throughout LCC
To decide which external speakers and organisations may use LCC premises in the following year
questions.explanation: The Academic Board reviews teaching strategies and practices to satisfy itself that the policy's principles and Code of Practice are duly upheld throughout the institution, reporting to the Board of Directors.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic Board will intermittently review teaching strategies and practices at LCC to satisfy itself that principles and code of practice outlined herein are duly upheld throughout the institution

questions.question: A member of staff asks what routes the Academic Freedom Policy provides for raising concerns about breaches of the policy. Which statement correctly describes them?
options: All concerns must go through the Whistleblowing Policy, as the Registrar deals only with student complaints and appeals
Concerns go only to the Academic Board, which then decides whether the complaints procedures should apply
Concerns go first to a line manager, then to HR, and finally to the Board of Directors if still unresolved
Concerns go to the Registrar or via the complaints procedures; serious breaches may use the Whistleblowing Policy
questions.explanation: Concerns about breaches should be reported to the Registrar, or LCC's complaints procedures can be used; serious breaches may be reported through the Protected Disclosures (Whistleblowing) Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Concerns about breaches of this policy should be reported to the Registrar ... Alternatively, LCC's complaints procedures can be used to report and address risks associated with academic freedom and freedom of speech. ... Serious breaches of this policy may be reported though LCC's Protected Disclosures (Whistleblowing) Policy

questions.question: A colleague claims LCC's legal duty on freedom of speech means it must guarantee unlimited speech in all circumstances. How does the Academic Freedom Policy describe the duty?
options: To take such steps as are reasonably practicable to secure freedom of speech within the law
To guarantee freedom of speech in every circumstance, whatever the cost or practical difficulty
To secure freedom of speech only for opinions that are consistent with LCC's core values
To secure freedom of speech on LCC premises only, leaving off-campus activity to other bodies
questions.explanation: The statutory duty described in the policy is to take such steps as are reasonably practicable to ensure that freedom of speech within the law is secured, not to guarantee unlimited speech.
questions.source_excerpt: take such steps as are reasonably practicable to ensure that freedom of speech within the law is secured for members, students, and employees of the establishment and for visiting speakers.

questions.question: A member of staff wants to campaign publicly, in their own time, for social change on a matter of public interest. Which statement reflects the Academic Freedom Policy?
options: It falls outside the policy, which protects expression only in teaching, research and publication
LCC respects this right and, in return, requires them to adhere to the policy in exercising it
They must first obtain approval from the Academic Board, as custodian of academic freedom at LCC
LCC supports this only where the campaign is consistent with the College's published strategic aims
questions.explanation: LCC is committed to staff exercising their civil rights, including contributing to social change through free expression on matters of public interest, and in return requires them to adhere to the policy when doing so.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC is committed to preserving an environment in which staff and students can exercise their civil rights as citizens ... including the right to contribute to social change through free expression of opinion on matters of public interest. ... LCC requires that they, in return, adhere to this policy in exercising this right.

questions.question: A researcher argues that because the Academic Freedom Policy safeguards freedom in carrying out research, ethical considerations do not apply to their project. What does the policy's Code of Practice expect?
options: Freedom in carrying out research takes priority, so ethics are left to the researcher's discretion
Ethical considerations apply only to research funded by LCC or carried out on College premises
Everyone conducting research is expected to have regard for appropriate ethical considerations
Ethical considerations apply only once findings are to be published under LCC's name
questions.explanation: Although the policy safeguards freedom in carrying out research, its Code of Practice expects everyone to have regard for appropriate ethical considerations when conducting research.
questions.source_excerpt: To have regard for appropriate ethical considerations when conducting research;

questions.question: A student asks for disciplinary action against a lecturer purely because the lecturer argued a lawful but unpopular position in class, using evidence and without disrupting teaching. Under the Academic Freedom Policy, what is the correct position?
options: Disciplinary action is appropriate where the view conflicts with LCC's stated institutional position
Unpopular opinions are protected from disciplinary action, provided the lecturer adheres to this policy
Disciplinary action is appropriate if most students in the class formally object to the view expressed
The matter must be referred under the Prevent Duty, as unpopular views require a formal risk review
questions.explanation: Academic freedom lets members of the academic community put forward controversial or unpopular opinions without fear of legal or disciplinary action; in return, LCC requires them to adhere to the policy when exercising that right.
questions.source_excerpt: put forward new ideas and controversial or unpopular opinions without fear of legal or disciplinary action. ... LCC requires that they, in return, adhere to this policy in exercising this right.

questions.question: A colleague argues that freedom of speech, as defined in LCC's Academic Freedom Policy, covers only information and ideas originating within the UK. Which part of the policy's definition shows this is wrong?
options: The right to receive and impart information and ideas applies regardless of frontiers
The right applies to overseas material once a public authority has approved its content
The right covers foreign ideas only when they are shared within timetabled teaching
The right applies to international sources once the Registrar has verified them
questions.explanation: The policy defines freedom of speech as the right to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority and regardless of frontiers, so it is not limited to UK material.
questions.source_excerpt: to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority and regardless of frontiers.

questions.question: A programme leader has been expressly authorised by LCC to present the College's position at a public consultation. How does the Academic Freedom Policy's rule on communicating in public apply to them?
options: They must still state that they are not speaking for LCC, as the rule covers all public communication
They may represent LCC's position only if the Registrar attends the consultation alongside them
Authorisation makes no difference, as staff may never present LCC's position in a public forum
They need not disclaim speaking for LCC, as the rule makes an exception where expressly authorised
questions.explanation: Staff communicating in public must indicate that they are not speaking on behalf of LCC unless expressly authorised to do so; an authorised spokesperson falls within that exception.
questions.source_excerpt: If communicating in public, staff and students should indicate clearly that they are not communicating on behalf of LCC unless expressly authorised to do so.

questions.question: A lawful charity asks to book an LCC room. A manager wants to refuse because one of the charity's trustees has publicly expressed views that staff find objectionable. What does the Academic Freedom Policy say?
options: Refusal is permitted, as the duty protects a body's own objectives but not the views of its members
Refusal is permitted once the Registrar confirms that the trustee's views are unpopular with staff
Premises should not be denied on any ground connected with the views of any member of the body
Refusal is permitted, provided the charity is offered an alternative venue away from the campus
questions.explanation: The duty described in the policy extends to ensuring premises are not denied on any ground connected with the beliefs or views of an individual or of any member of a body, so a trustee's views are not a valid reason to refuse.
questions.source_excerpt: that the use of any premises of the establishment is not denied to any individual or body of persons on any ground connected with (a) the beliefs or views of that individual or of any member of that body

questions.question: A manager says that, because LCC must pay particular attention to the Prevent Duty when implementing the Academic Freedom Policy, balanced seminars on religion and politics should be cancelled. What does the policy say?
options: Prevent takes precedence, so balanced seminars should be cancelled wherever any risk is perceived
Prevent applies only to off-campus events, so seminars held on College premises are unaffected
Prevent applies only to students, so staff-led seminars on these topics fall outside its scope
Prevent should not obstruct balanced discussion of such issues, but help it to thrive
questions.explanation: LCC pays particular attention to the Prevent Duty, but the policy states that Prevent should not be obstructive to balanced discussion of controversial issues such as religion and politics; it should ensure an environment in which such discussion can thrive.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC also pays particular attention to the requirements of the Prevent Duty when implementing this Policy and Code of Conduct. ... The Prevent duty should not be obstructive to academic freedom, freedom of speech or balanced discussion of controversial issues such as religion, politics, and current affairs, rather it should ensure an environment in which these can thrive.

questions.question: An admissions officer in professional services says the Academic Freedom Policy concerns only lecturers and researchers. Which statement correctly reflects the policy?
options: It does not apply to them, as it covers only teaching, research and publication by academic staff
It applies to all of LCC's professional and academic work, and all staff must uphold it
It applies to them only when they support a teaching session or sit on an academic committee
It applies only where their job description includes an academic or research component
questions.explanation: The policy's principles apply in all aspects of LCC's professional and academic work, including freedom for staff in carrying out their roles, and upholding it is the responsibility of all staff.
questions.source_excerpt: applied in all aspects of the LCC's professional and academic work ... Freedom for staff in carrying out their roles. ... It is the responsibility of all members of LCC's community (extending to all staff, students, and executive members)

questions.question: A department organises an off-campus study visit. A colleague says the core values set out in LCC's Academic Freedom Policy guide only activity on College premises. Which statement is correct?
options: Core values apply off campus only where a visit involves an overnight stay
Core values guide on-campus activity only; visits follow the host venue's rules
Core values guide learning opportunities, premises and off-campus activities
Core values apply off campus only once the Academic Board has approved the visit
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC will be guided by its core values in managing its learning opportunities, its premises and its off-campus activities.
questions.source_excerpt: In the management of its learning opportunities, its premises, and its off-campus ... activities, LCC will be guided by its core values

questions.question: A student society argues that the core value of tolerance in LCC's Academic Freedom Policy protects religious faiths only, not non-religious beliefs. Which statement is correct?
options: It covers faiths and beliefs only where they are shared by a majority of students
It covers only faiths that are formally recognised in England, not other beliefs
It covers non-religious beliefs only where they are held by a registered society
It covers tolerance of different faiths and religious and other beliefs
questions.explanation: The core value listed in the policy is respect for and tolerance of different faiths and religious and other beliefs, so it is not limited to religious faiths.
questions.source_excerpt: Respect for and tolerance of different faiths and religious and other beliefs

questions.question: A tutor tells students that their essays must endorse the tutor's personal position on a contested issue in order to pass. Which behaviour set out in the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice does this breach?
options: Not to attempt to impose a set of beliefs on others
To keep all personal views out of teaching and assessment
To present only positions endorsed by the programme team
To obtain students' consent before discussing contested issues
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice expects everyone not to attempt to impose a set of beliefs on others. It does not require personal views to be excluded altogether, only clearly differentiated from objective academic judgements.
questions.source_excerpt: Not to attempt to impose a set of beliefs on others;

questions.question: During a lecture, a student repeatedly shouts objections to the lecturer's argument so that the session cannot continue. How does the Academic Freedom Policy treat this conduct?
options: Students may challenge ideas, but not disruptively; disruption of teaching will not be tolerated
It is protected, as the right to challenge received wisdom outweighs the running of a single session
It is acceptable provided the student's objections are supported by sound and reliable evidence
It is a matter for the Students' Union alone, as the Code of Practice governs staff conduct only
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice expects people to challenge in a way that is not disruptive to teaching and discussion, and disruptive acts that interfere with students' freedom to pursue their studies will not be tolerated.
