questions.source_excerpt: To challenge in a way that is not harmful to others or to the reputation of LCC or disruptive to teaching, and discussion; ... disruptive acts which interfere with campus activities, freedom of movement on the campus, or freedom for students to pursue their studies are the antithesis of academic freedom and will not be tolerated by LCC.

questions.question: Students stage a sit-in that blocks the entrance to a teaching block, preventing others from reaching classes, and say it is free expression on a matter of public interest. What does the Academic Freedom Policy say?
options: It is protected, as LCC safeguards the right to contribute to social change through free expression
Acts interfering with freedom of movement or study are the antithesis of academic freedom
It is tolerated where the cause concerns a matter of public interest rather than a private grievance
It is tolerated provided no physical force is used and the Registrar is notified in advance
questions.explanation: Although LCC supports free expression on matters of public interest, disruptive acts that interfere with freedom of movement on campus or students' freedom to pursue their studies are the antithesis of academic freedom and will not be tolerated.
questions.source_excerpt: Acts or threats of physical force or disruptive acts which interfere with campus activities, freedom of movement on the campus, or freedom for students to pursue their studies are the antithesis of academic freedom and will not be tolerated by LCC.

questions.question: An external contractor raises, in good faith, a concern about professional standards at LCC. The investigation does not uphold the concern. Under the Academic Freedom Policy, how should LCC treat the contractor?
options: Protection covers staff and students only, so the contractor's contract may be reviewed
Good faith alone is not enough; protection applies only where the concern is upheld
They must not be treated less favourably, as the concern was raised in good faith
Protection applies only if the concern was raised under the Whistleblowing Policy
questions.explanation: The policy protects any member of staff, director, student or third party from less favourable treatment where they raise concerns about academic or professional standards in good faith; it does not depend on the concern being upheld.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will ensure that no member of staff, director, student or third party will be treated less favourably by LCC where they raise concerns about academic or professional ... standards at LCC, where such matters are raised in good faith.

questions.question: A student believes a lecturer is suppressing lawful debate and wants to use LCC's complaints procedures rather than approach the Registrar. What does the Academic Freedom Policy allow?
options: The complaints procedures are an alternative route for reporting and addressing such risks
The Registrar must be approached first; complaints may be used only if the matter is unresolved
The complaints procedures apply only to serious breaches reported under the Whistleblowing Policy
The complaint may proceed only once the Academic Board confirms that a breach has occurred
questions.explanation: Concerns about breaches should be reported to the Registrar, but the policy states that LCC's complaints procedures can alternatively be used to report and address risks to academic freedom and freedom of speech.
questions.source_excerpt: Concerns about breaches of this policy should be reported to the Registrar ... Alternatively, LCC's complaints procedures can be used to report and address risks associated with academic freedom and freedom of speech.

questions.question: A lecturer witnesses what they consider a serious breach of the Academic Freedom Policy and asks whether they are obliged to report it through the Whistleblowing Policy. What does the policy say?
options: Serious breaches must go through the Whistleblowing Policy; the Registrar handles minor ones only
Serious breaches must first be raised with a line manager before any other route can be used
Serious breaches may be reported through the Whistleblowing Policy, but it is not the only route
Serious breaches can be reported only to the Board of Directors, which oversees the Registrar
questions.explanation: The policy says serious breaches may be reported through the Protected Disclosures (Whistleblowing) Policy; concerns about breaches of the policy can also be reported to the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: Concerns about breaches of this policy should be reported to the Registrar ... Serious breaches of this policy may be reported though LCC's Protected Disclosures (Whistleblowing) Policy

questions.question: A programme team proposes removing a unit that teaches students to question the reliability of sources, saying students should simply accept established theories. Which commitment in the Academic Freedom Policy does this conflict with?
options: LCC's obligation to inculcate healthy scepticism and critical and introspective thinking
LCC's duty to secure freedom of speech within the law for visiting speakers on its premises
LCC's commitment to incorporate its core values into its external speaker procedures
LCC's core value of respect for the basis on which the law is made and applies
questions.explanation: The policy recognises LCC's obligation as a UK higher education provider to inculcate in students the competencies of healthy scepticism and critical and introspective thinking, and it defines academic freedom as including the freedom to question and test received wisdom.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC is aware of its legal obligations, as a higher education provider in the UK to inculcate students the values of democracy and the competencies of healthy scepticism, critical and introspective thinking

questions.question: A seminar leader keeps excluding a student from group work because of the student's regional accent, arguing that accent is not a characteristic named in the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice. Which statement is correct?
options: Only the characteristics named in the Code are covered, so this exclusion falls outside it
It is permitted where the leader believes it improves the quality of the group's discussion
It is covered only if the student has first raised a formal complaint with the Registrar
The Code also covers exclusion on any other personal characteristics, so it is not permitted
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice requires everyone to refrain from excluding others from academic activity on the listed grounds or any other personal characteristics, so the list is not exhaustive.
questions.source_excerpt: To refrain from all forms of discrimination or the exclusion of others form academic activity whether on grounds of gender, racial background, sexual orientation, age, ... caring responsibilities or any other personal characteristics;

questions.question: A lecturer disagrees with a colleague's published research and responds on social media with personal insults about the colleague, adding that they do not speak for LCC. What does the Academic Freedom Policy's Code of Practice say?
options: The post is acceptable because it states clearly that they are not speaking on behalf of LCC
Challenge is expected, but not in a way that is harmful to others or to LCC's reputation
Challenging a colleague's published research falls outside academic freedom and should be avoided
Posts on personal social media accounts fall wholly outside the Code of Practice
questions.explanation: The Code of Practice expects people to challenge in a way that is not harmful to others or to LCC's reputation. Stating that they do not speak for LCC is a separate requirement and does not make harmful conduct acceptable.
questions.source_excerpt: To challenge in a way that is not harmful to others or to the reputation of LCC or disruptive to teaching, and discussion; ... If communicating in public, staff and students should indicate clearly that they are not communicating on behalf of LCC unless expressly authorised to do so.

questions.question: A lecturer presents a controversial claim in class and, when students ask, refuses to offer any evidence, saying academic freedom means they need not justify it. What does the Academic Freedom Policy expect?
options: Academic freedom means lecturers need not justify controversial views, even when asked
Controversial claims may be presented, but only after prior approval by the Academic Board
Controversial views are protected, but debate should rest on rational enquiry and reliable evidence
Controversial claims fall outside academic freedom and should not be presented in class at all
questions.explanation: Academic freedom protects putting forward controversial opinions, but the Code of Practice expects academic debate to be guided by rational enquiry and supported by sound and reliable evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: put forward new ideas and controversial or unpopular opinions without fear of legal or disciplinary action. ... To ensure academic debate is guided by rational enquiry and supported by sound and reliable evidence;

questions.question: Facilities staff are asked to refuse four room bookings from lawful external groups, each for a different reason. Under the Academic Freedom Policy's commitment on the use of LCC premises, which reason for refusal is ruled out?
options: The room is already booked for a timetabled class at the time requested
The expected audience would exceed the room's safe capacity for visitors
The group's stated objectives conflict with positions LCC has taken in public
The group wants the room overnight, outside the hours the building is open
questions.explanation: The policy rules out denying premises on any ground connected with a body's beliefs, views, policies or objectives where use is within the law. A clashing booking, building hours or visitor safety (LCC's duty of care) are not grounds of that kind.
questions.source_excerpt: so far as is reasonably practicable, that the use of any premises of the establishment is not denied to any individual or body of persons on any ground connected with (a) the beliefs or views of that individual or of any member of that body; or (b) the policy or objectives of that body. ... The duty of care to staff, students and visitors

questions.question: A student society invites a speaker whose planned talk, the organisers accept, would unlawfully encourage support for terrorism. A colleague says the Academic Freedom Policy means Prevent can never be used to restrict a speaker. Which statement is correct?
options: The talk must go ahead, as Prevent must not obstruct freedom of speech or discussion of politics
LCC has no role, as its freedom of speech duty does not extend to events run by student societies
The talk may go ahead if the society agrees that LCC's institutional view is also presented
Speech is secured only within the law, and LCC must still have due regard to the Prevent Duty
questions.explanation: Prevent must not obstruct lawful, balanced discussion, but the policy secures freedom of speech (and use of premises) only within the law, and LCC keeps its statutory duty to have due regard to preventing people being drawn into terrorism. The duty also extends to student activities.
questions.source_excerpt: ensure that freedom of speech within the law is secured for members, students, and employees of the establishment and for visiting speakers. ... For the purposes of the Act, LCC's duty extends to Student activities. ... LCC has a statutory duty to have due regard for the need to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism

questions.question: A member of staff knowingly makes a false allegation about a colleague's academic standards in order to damage the colleague's reputation, then claims the Academic Freedom Policy's protection from less favourable treatment. Which statement is correct?
options: It covers any concern about standards once formally lodged, whatever the motive behind it
It covers only concerns raised in good faith, so this allegation falls outside it
It covers them, because members of staff are among the groups the policy expressly names
It covers them unless the colleague accused is a director or an Academic Board member
questions.explanation: The policy's assurance against less favourable treatment applies where concerns about academic or professional standards are raised in good faith. A knowingly false allegation made to damage a colleague is not raised in good faith, so it falls outside that assurance.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will ensure that no member of staff, director, student or third party will be treated less favourably by LCC where they raise concerns about academic or professional ... standards at LCC, where such matters are raised in good faith.

questions.question: A guest speaker delivering a session within a taught module says that, as a visitor, the Academic Freedom Policy only protects their speech and expects nothing of their conduct. Which statement reflects the policy?
options: Their freedom of speech within the law is secured, and they are expected to uphold the policy and its Code
Visiting speakers' freedom of speech overrides LCC's other legal obligations while they are on its premises
The Code of Practice binds only LCC staff and students, so the speaker's conduct is for their own employer
Visiting speakers fall outside the freedom of speech duty, which covers LCC members, students and employees
questions.explanation: LCC's duty secures freedom of speech within the law for visiting speakers, and external parties invited to contribute to learning are expected to uphold the policy and exemplify its Code of Practice behaviours.
questions.source_excerpt: ensure that freedom of speech within the law is secured for members, students, and employees of the establishment and for visiting speakers. ... as well any external parties invited by LCC to contribute to the learning experience, to uphold this policy and exemplify the behaviours given in its Code of Practice.

questions.question: While marking assignments, a lecturer suspects a student's work involves academic malpractice. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what should the lecturer do in the first instance?
options: Award a mark of zero for the work and inform the student in writing of the reason for the penalty
Contact the student directly and ask them to resubmit an original piece of work within 14 days
Urgently complete the Referral of Suspected Academic Misconduct Form, giving all required evidence
Refer the case directly to the Assessment Board, attaching the Turnitin report so it can decide
questions.explanation: Marking staff who suspect malpractice must, in the first instance and as a matter of urgency, complete the Referral of Suspected Academic Misconduct Form with all sections and evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a suspicion of academic malpractice is identified by staff involved in the marking process, the individual staff member shall in the first instance as a matter of urgency, complete the Referral of Suspected Academic Misconduct form, ensuring all sections are completed and correctly filled, giving all the evidences required by the Academic Offence Panel

questions.question: How does the Academic Misconduct Policy define an academic offence?
options: When it is shown on the balance of probabilities that a student used unfair means, deliberately or through culpable negligence
When it is proven beyond reasonable doubt that a student knowingly and deliberately used unfair means in an assessed piece of work
When a Turnitin similarity score exceeds the College's set threshold, regardless of whether the student intended to cheat
When the student admits in writing that they intentionally used unfair means, following an interview with the QA team
questions.explanation: An academic offence is where it can be demonstrated on the balance of probabilities that a student used unfair means, either deliberately (knowingly) or through culpable negligence (unknowingly).
questions.source_excerpt: Academic offences are identified as occasions or circumstances within which it can be demonstrated on the balance of probabilities that a student has deliberately (knowingly), or through culpable negligence (unknowingly), used unfair means in the assessment

questions.question: Months after a student's work was graded and the credit ratified, you find evidence that it was produced by someone else. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which statement is correct?
options: It cannot be investigated, because the Assessment Board has already ratified the credit
It is time-barred, as allegations must be raised within three months of the grade being issued
It can be investigated, but the penalty is limited to a formal written warning on the student's file
It can be investigated, as there is no time limit, and the ratified credit may be withdrawn
questions.explanation: The policy states that the investigation of academic misconduct has no time limit, and where misconduct is proven after work has been graded the College may withdraw credit ratified by the Assessment Board.
questions.source_excerpt: The investigation of academic misconduct at London Churchill College has no time limit. Where academic misconduct is proven after work has been assessed and graded, the College reserves the right to withdraw credit ratified by the Assessment Board

questions.question: You are marking a piece of work that is the subject of an academic offence investigation. According to the Academic Misconduct Policy, how should you handle it?
options: Mark and grade it as submitted, mark it as referred on Turnitin, and inform Registry
Leave it unmarked and unreferred until the Academic Offence Panel has reached its decision
Mark it, but cap the grade at a pass until the investigation has been fully completed
Award a provisional zero and ask Registry to release the mark to the student straight away
questions.explanation: Work under investigation is marked and graded on the basis of the submission but marked as referred on Turnitin, and Registry is informed so marks are not processed until the investigation ends.
questions.source_excerpt: Where work submitted by a student is the subject of an academic offence investigation, it should be marked and graded on the basis of the submission but marked as referred on Turnitin. The Registry department should also be informed to ensure marks are not processed for confimation until the investigation is completed;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, who decides whether suspected malpractice should be treated as an academic offence or an academic concern?
options: The marker who raised the referral, based on the Turnitin similarity report and the marking rubric
The student's Personal Tutor, after meeting the student to discuss how the work was produced
The QA team, after checking the student's records for previous activity and level of study
The Registry department, when processing the student's marks for the next Assessment Board
questions.explanation: The policy states that the QA team decides whether suspected malpractice is an academic offence or an academic concern, checking the student's records for previous activity and level of study.
questions.source_excerpt: A decision will be made by the QA team as to whether suspected malpractice should be considered as an academic offence or an academic concern and the students' records are checked to determine previous activity and their level of study;

questions.question: On a student's second offence, the only issue is a source acknowledged in the text but missing from the reference list; the rest of the work is correctly referenced. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, how may this be treated?
options: It must be treated as an academic offence, because it is a second offence
It must go to the Academic Offence Panel with a recommendation of withdrawal
It may be disregarded, as referencing errors fall outside the scope of the policy
It may be considered an academic concern rather than an offence, as it is minor
questions.explanation: The policy allows a second offence to be considered an academic concern rather than an offence where it is minor, giving exactly this example of an in-text citation missing from the reference list.
questions.source_excerpt: Where there is a second offence, this may also be considered as an academic concern if: ... Where the concern is minor, such as the student has a referencing error where they have acknowledged the source in the text, but forgotten to include it in the reference list, and the rest of the submission is correctly referenced.

questions.question: A student who has been notified of an academic offence allegation tells you they accept it. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what happens about the Panel meeting?
options: They must still attend the Panel in person to confirm their acceptance and sign the record
They will not be invited to speak to the Panel but may submit a written statement
The case closes without a Panel meeting and a formal warning is issued to them automatically
They must first attend a viva so that the Panel can confirm the work is their own
questions.explanation: Where a student accepts the allegation, the policy says they are not invited to attend to speak to the Panel but may submit a written statement for consideration.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a student accepts the allegation, s/he will not be invited to attend the meeting to speak to the Panel but may submit a written statement for consideration;

questions.question: According to the Academic Misconduct Policy, what counts as self-plagiarism?
options: Resubmitting one's own work previously submitted for summative assessment at LCC, but not work assessed at other institutions
Working jointly with another student on an individual assignment and submitting near-identical work
Paraphrasing a published source in one's own words without citing the original author in the text or reference list
Reproducing or resubmitting one's own work already submitted for summative assessment at LCC or another institution
questions.explanation: The policy defines self-plagiarism as reproducing or resubmitting a student's own work already submitted for summative assessment at LCC or any other institution, not just at LCC.
questions.source_excerpt: Self-Plagiarism: which is the reproduction/resubmission of a student's own work which has already been submitted for summative assessment at LCC or any other institution.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which upheld Panel outcome applies where the severity of malpractice is high?
options: Referral with a resubmission opportunity, with the grade limited to a pass mark
Repeat the unit and lower the grade by a further 15-credit unit in the concurrent semester
Repeat the unit with class attendance, with the grade limited to a pass mark
Immediate withdrawal from the College without entitlement to any award
questions.explanation: For high-severity malpractice the policy specifies repeating the unit with class attendance and a grade limited to a pass mark; resubmission is for moderate cases and the 15-credit reduction for very high cases.
questions.source_excerpt: Repeat the unit with class attendance and the grade is limited to a pass mark, if the severity of malpractice is high;

questions.question: According to the Academic Misconduct Policy, when a student is emailed about an academic offence allegation, what are they advised to do?
options: Contact the marker who raised the referral and ask them to withdraw it before the Panel meets
Contact their Personal Tutor for advice and, if required, bring a friend or student representative
Appoint a legal representative, as friends and student representatives may not attend the Panel
Submit a revised version of the work so that the Panel can consider it in place of the original submission
questions.explanation: The allegation email advises the student to contact their Personal Tutor for advice and, if required, to bring a friend or student representative to the Panel meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: The student will also be advised to contact the Personal Tutor for advice and, if required, to bring a friend or student representative to the Panel meeting;

questions.question: According to the Academic Misconduct Policy, how do penalties for academic misconduct relate to decisions on mitigating circumstances applications?
options: Penalties override any decision taken on mitigating circumstances applications
An approved mitigating circumstances claim cancels any misconduct penalty applied
The Panel must pause the case until any mitigating circumstances claim has been decided
Approved mitigating circumstances claims reduce any penalty applied by one severity level
questions.explanation: The policy states that any penalties applied override any decision taken on mitigating circumstances applications.
questions.source_excerpt: Any penalties applied override any decision taken regarding mitigating circumstances applications.

questions.question: You suspect a student has submitted work produced by someone else. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what may the student be invited to attend to help staff reach a conclusion?
options: A supervised resit examination whose mark replaces the original submission
A viva, with notes taken that the Panel can consider as evidence
A meeting with Registry to verify their identity documents
A written test on the module content, marked by the External Examiner
questions.explanation: For suspected submission of work produced by someone else, the student may be invited to a viva, and the notes taken can be considered as evidence by the Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of suspected submission of work produced by someone else, the student may be invited to attend a viva to help staff reach a conclusion about the nature and extent of any suspected offence. The notes taken at the viva can be considered as evidence by the Panel.

questions.question: According to the Academic Misconduct Policy, which students do the processes described in the policy apply to?
options: Students who have already received an academic concern on an earlier assessment
All students studying on HND courses at London Churchill College
Only final-year students whose results are going to the Assessment Board
Only students whose assignments are submitted and checked through Turnitin
questions.explanation: The policy states that its processes apply to all students studying on HND courses at London Churchill College, covering misconduct in any form of assessment.
questions.source_excerpt: The processes described in this policy apply to all students studying on HND courses at London Churchill College. This policy serves to cover misconduct in any form of assessment;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, at what point are new students given information about how to avoid unacceptable academic practice?
options: At their induction
At their enrolment
At their first tutorial
At their first exam
questions.explanation: The policy states that new students are provided with information about how to avoid unacceptable academic practice at induction.
questions.source_excerpt: New students are provided with information about how to avoid unacceptable academic practice at induction.

questions.question: How does the Academic Misconduct Policy treat the unauthorised use of Generative AI in an assignment?
options: It is not covered, as the policy deals only with plagiarism, collusion and cheating
It is covered only when a Turnitin AI score above a set College threshold is recorded
It is listed as one of the examples of offences covered by the policy
It is covered only in examinations; assignments are dealt with under separate guidance
questions.explanation: The unauthorised use of Generative AI in an assignment is listed among the examples of offences covered by the policy, with no score threshold attached.
questions.source_excerpt: The following are examples of offences that are covered by this policy: ... The unauthorised use of Generative AI in an assignment;

questions.question: The Academic Misconduct Policy distinguishes between two forms of unacceptable academic practice, which follow different courses of action. What are they?
options: Minor malpractice and major malpractice
Poor academic practice and academic fraud
Assessment offences and examination offences
Academic concerns and academic offences
questions.explanation: Because alleged misconduct varies in severity, the College distinguishes between academic concerns and academic offences, which follow different courses of action.
questions.source_excerpt: the College distinguishes between two different forms of unacceptable academic practice, which follow different courses of action: ... Academic concerns occur where ... Academic offences are identified as occasions or circumstances

questions.question: According to the Academic Misconduct Policy, when does an academic concern occur?
options: When a student admits using unfair means before the Academic Offence Panel has met to consider the case
When integrity may be compromised, so the College lacks reasonable confidence the work conforms to the regulations
When a Turnitin similarity score is above the programme's set limit but below the threshold for an offence
When a second marker disagrees with the first marker's grade during the internal moderation of the work
questions.explanation: An academic concern arises where the integrity of the academic process is potentially compromised, so the College lacks a reasonable level of confidence that the work conforms to the regulations.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic concerns occur where the integrity of academic process has been deemed potentially to be compromised such that the College does not have a reasonable level of confidence that the work submitted conforms to the regulations.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what applies where academic malpractice is identified by staff invigilating an examination?
options: The existing regulations governing the conduct of the examination's procedures
An immediate viva, with the invigilator's notes considered as evidence by the Panel
A referral to Registry, which cancels the student's results for the whole exam session
An automatic referral with the grade limited to a pass, confirmed by the Assessment Board
questions.explanation: For malpractice identified during invigilation, the policy says the existing regulations governing the conduct of the examination's procedures will apply.
questions.source_excerpt: Where academic malpractice is identified by staff invigilating an examination, the existing regulations governing the conduct of the examination's procedures will apply;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, a similarity found in which part of a student's work may be considered more serious than one in the literature review?
options: The reference list and bibliography
The introduction and background
The conclusion and recommendations
The appendices and supporting data
questions.explanation: When deciding on a first offence, the policy notes that a similarity in the conclusion and recommendations may be considered more serious than one in the literature review.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the similarity occurs; for example, a similarity within the conclusion and recommendations may be considered more serious than a similarity in the literature review.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, where is the Programme Leader's decision on whether a case can be argued as an academic offence recorded?
options: In the minutes of the next Assessment Board meeting
On the student's Turnitin submission, as a referral note
In the student's file held by their Personal Tutor
On the Referral of Suspected Academic Misconduct Form
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Programme Leader's decision is recorded on the Referral of Suspected Academic Misconduct Form (RSAMF).
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader or equivalent decides whether a case can be argued for an academic offence following the decision made by the QA team ... The decision is recorded on the Referral of Suspected Academic Misconduct Form (RSAMF).

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, who chairs the Academic Misconduct Panel at which a student is given the opportunity to defend the case?
options: The Programme Leader for the student's course
The Deputy Vice Principal (Quality Assurance)
The Chair of the relevant Assessment Board
The External Examiner for the programme
questions.explanation: The policy states that the student is invited to an Academic Misconduct Panel chaired by the Deputy Vice Principal (Quality Assurance), where they can defend the case.
questions.source_excerpt: the student will be invited to an Academic Misconduct Panel chaired by the Deputy Vice Principal (Quality Assurance), in which s/he will be given the opportunity to defend the case.

questions.question: According to the Academic Misconduct Policy, how is the Academic Offence Panel made up?
options: A Chair and two additional panel members
A Chair and four additional panel members
A Chair, one panel member and a student representative
Two panel members, with no separate Chair appointed
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Academic Offence Panel consists of a Chair and two additional panel members, drawn from a membership pool.
questions.source_excerpt: The panel will consist of a Chair, and two additional panel members.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, who writes to the student to advise them of an academic offence allegation and the Panel meeting arrangements?
options: The marker who first raised the referral, copying in the Programme Leader
The Registry department, once the student's marks have been put on hold
The student's Personal Tutor, after first discussing the case with the student
The Quality Assurance Officer, with approval from the Deputy Vice Principal (QA)
questions.explanation: The Quality Assurance Officer, with approval from the Deputy Vice Principal (Quality Assurance), emails the student with the allegation and the Panel arrangements.
questions.source_excerpt: The Quality Assurance Officer with approval from the Deputy Vice Principal (Quality Assurance) will write (email) to the student to advise of the allegation, giving details of the arrangements for the Panel meeting.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what happens to a student's work if they successfully defend the allegation?
options: It is marked under normal procedures, but the grade is capped at a pass mark
It must be resubmitted as a new piece of work, which is then marked without penalty
It is marked normally, with the full range of marks available without penalty
It is marked normally, but a formal warning is kept on the student's record
questions.explanation: If the student successfully defends the allegation, the matter is dropped and the work is marked under normal procedures with the full range of marks available without penalty.
questions.source_excerpt: In cases where the student successfully defends the allegation, the matter will be dropped and the student's work will be marked according to normal procedures with the full range of marks being available without penalty;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, if a student is withdrawn from the College for multiple and serial offences, what will they normally be entitled to?
options: A refund of this year's tuition fees
A transfer to another College programme
Readmission after one academic year
Any award for which they are eligible
questions.explanation: A student withdrawn for multiple and serial or deliberate and severe offences will normally be entitled to any award for which they are eligible.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a student has multiple and serial offences, or where the offence is considered to be deliberate and severe, the student may be withdrawn from the College and not permitted to continue with studies. S/he will normally be entitled to any award for which they are eligible;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, when can penalties for an academic offence be expected to be applied?
options: As soon as the student accepts the allegation in writing
Once the Assessment Board has met and ratified the decision
Immediately after the Academic Offence Panel reaches its decision
Once the External Examiner has reviewed the Panel's minutes
questions.explanation: The policy states that penalties can be expected to be applied once the Assessment Board has met and ratified the decision.
questions.source_excerpt: The application of penalties can be expected to be applied once the Assessment Board has met and ratified the decision;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, where is the procedure for a student to appeal against an academic misconduct decision described?
options: In LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure
In LCC's Student Complaints Policy and Procedure
In an appendix to the Academic Misconduct Policy
In the Assessment Board's terms of reference
questions.explanation: Students have the right to appeal, and the procedure is described in LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, available on the College's website.
questions.source_excerpt: Students have the right to Appeal against the decision and the procedure is described in LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, which can be accessed on the College's website.

questions.question: According to the Academic Misconduct Policy, what is the function of the Academic Offence Panel?
options: To moderate marks for all assessments before the results are sent to the Assessment Board
To hear student appeals against the penalties imposed for proven academic misconduct
To ensure all alleged offences are investigated and handled consistently across the College
To give students guidance on referencing after they receive a first academic concern
questions.explanation: The Academic Offence Panel exists to ensure all alleged cases of academic offence are investigated and to ensure consistency of approach across the College.
questions.source_excerpt: The function of the Academic Offence Panel is to ensure all alleged cases of academic offence are investigated and to ensure consistency of approach across the College.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, if a student receives a penalty on a referred unit, what may the Panel consider?
options: Waiving the penalty where the student has an approved mitigating circumstances claim
Allowing an uncapped resubmission of the same unit in the following academic semester
Carrying the credit deficit forward to the student's final-year project unit instead
Offering a different unit to make up the credit deficit, limited to the minimum pass mark
questions.explanation: If a student receives a penalty on a referred unit, the Panel may consider offering a different unit to make up the credit deficit, limited to the minimum pass mark.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student receives a penalty on a referred unit, the Panel may consider offering a different unit to make up the credit deficit, that module will be limited to the minimum pass mark;

questions.question: A colleague believes the Academic Misconduct Policy covers only written assignments, so a misconduct issue in a presentation assessment falls outside it. Under the policy, is this right?
options: Yes; presentations are handled under the examination regulations rather than this policy
No; the policy serves to cover misconduct in any form of assessment
Yes; the policy is limited to submitted work that is checked through Turnitin
No; it applies only where the presentation is summatively assessed
questions.explanation: The policy states that it serves to cover misconduct in any form of assessment, so it is not limited to written or Turnitin-checked work.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy serves to cover misconduct in any form of assessment;

questions.question: A new HND student with a relevant protected characteristic asks for the induction guidance on avoiding unacceptable academic practice in another format. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, how should this be handled?
options: They must submit a mitigating circumstances application before any other format is considered
The guidance exists only in the standard induction format, so a Personal Tutor explains it verbally
The College can provide the information in other formats on request from such students
The request must first be approved by the Academic Offence Panel and recorded in its minutes
questions.explanation: New students receive this information at induction, and the College can provide it in other formats on request from students with relevant protected characteristics.
questions.source_excerpt: New students are provided with information about how to avoid unacceptable academic practice at induction. The College can provide this information in other formats on request from students with relevant protected characteristics.

questions.question: Misconduct is proven after a student's work was graded, and the College withdraws the credit ratified by the Assessment Board. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what may the College advise the student to do?
options: Either resit the exam, retake the module or withdraw from the course
Submit a mitigating circumstances claim so the original credit is reinstated
Wait for the next Assessment Board, which re-ratifies the credit automatically
Appeal to the External Examiner, who may then restore the withdrawn credit
questions.explanation: Where misconduct is proven after grading, the College may withdraw ratified credit and advise the student to resit the exam, retake the module or withdraw from the course.
questions.source_excerpt: Where academic misconduct is proven after work has been assessed and graded, the College reserves the right to withdraw credit ratified by the Assessment Board and advise the student(s) involved to either resit the exam, retake the module or withdraw from the course;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what may lead to a suspected case of unacceptable practice being treated as an academic concern rather than an academic offence?
options: The student having no Turnitin similarity report recorded on any of their previous submissions
The student accepting the allegation in writing before an Academic Offence Panel meets
The marker judging that the work would still have passed without the sections that are affected
The nature of the offence or the point of study indicating that guidance is the best course
questions.explanation: A concern is considered when the nature of the offence or the student's point of study indicates that seeking guidance and treating it as a concern would be the best course of action.
questions.source_excerpt: A concern would be considered when the nature of the offense or the point of study indicates that seeking guidance and treating the situation as a concern would be the best course of action

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which sequence correctly describes how a concern raised by the academic team progresses towards an Academic Offence Panel?
options: QA team decides offence or concern; academic team verifies it; Programme Leader then convenes the Panel
Forwarded to the QA team; QA decides offence or concern; Programme Leader decides if an offence case can be argued
Programme Leader decides if a case can be argued; QA team verifies it; Registry then convenes the Panel
Forwarded to Registry; Registry decides offence or concern; QA team decides if an offence case can be argued
questions.explanation: The academic team forwards concerns to the QA team, which decides whether it is an offence or a concern; the Programme Leader then decides whether an offence case can be argued, leading to a Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic team will forward all concerns raised to the QA team for verification and investigation. ... A decision will be made by the QA team as to whether suspected malpractice should be considered as an academic offence or an academic concern ... The Programme Leader or equivalent decides whether a case can be argued for an academic offence following the decision made by the QA team

questions.question: The QA team is deciding whether a student's first offence is a potential concern or an offence. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which set of factors may affect this decision?
options: The student's attendance record, the module's overall pass rate and the marker's length of service
The grade the work would earn, the student's fee status and whether they have a Personal Tutor
The Turnitin similarity, any attempt to acknowledge sources, and where the similarity occurs
How many days late the work was, its final word count and whether the second marker agreed
questions.explanation: For a first offence, the listed factors are the amount of Turnitin similarity, whether there was an attempt to acknowledge sources, and where in the work the similarity occurs.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the issue is a first offence, factors affecting this decision and if this is a potential concern or offence may include: ... a) The amount of similarity identified via Turnitin; b) Whether there was an attempt to acknowledge the sources, c) Where the similarity occurs;

questions.question: A student's second submission raises similar issues to their first concern. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which circumstance allows this second offence to be considered an academic concern?
options: It was submitted before the student would have received guidance on the first concern
It was submitted for a different unit from the one in which the first concern arose
Its Turnitin similarity score is lower than the score recorded on the first submission
It was submitted in the same semester as the first concern, before the Assessment Board
questions.explanation: A second offence may be considered an academic concern where it was submitted before the student would have received guidance following the first concern.
questions.source_excerpt: Where there is a second offence, this may also be considered as an academic concern if: ... a) The submission date was before the student would have received guidance following the first concern;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what does the Chair of the Academic Misconduct Panel do once they have identified the evidence of the concern?
options: Refer the case to the Assessment Board, which alone may decide any penalty that is to be applied
Only issue a warning, as penalties may be decided by the Academic Offence Panel alone
Record the outcome on the RSAMF and leave any penalty for the Programme Leader to decide
Give a penalty or a warning, as the Chair deems appropriate under the stipulated regulations
questions.explanation: The Chair of the Academic Misconduct Panel identifies the evidence of the concern and gives a penalty or a warning as they deem appropriate under the stipulated regulations.
questions.source_excerpt: The Chair of the panel will identify the evidence of the concern and give a penalty or a warning, as s/he deems appropriate according to the stipulated regulations.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, from which membership pool are the Chair and members of an Academic Offence Panel drawn?
options: The Programme Leader, the student's Personal Tutor and the lecturer who raised the referral
The Deputy Vice Principal (QA), the QA Officer and a Senior Academic Administrator from Registry
The External Examiner, the Head of Department and an elected student representative
The Head of Registry, the student's Programme Leader and the Chair of the Assessment Board
questions.explanation: The Panel's Chair and two members come from a pool of the Deputy Vice Principal (Quality Assurance), the Quality Assurance Officer and a Senior Academic Administrator from Registry.
questions.source_excerpt: The panel will comprise from a membership pool of the Deputy Vice Principal (Quality Assurance), Quality Assurance Officer and a Senior Academic Administrator from the Registry department;

questions.question: A student does not accept an academic offence allegation but cannot attend the Panel meeting on the specified date. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, what might the student do?
options: Nothing further, as not attending means the allegation is treated as accepted
Ask Registry to process their marks without penalty until they are able to attend
Ask for the case to be referred back to the QA team and treated as a concern
Submit a written statement for the Panel's consideration instead
questions.explanation: A student who does not accept the allegation is invited to attend the Panel; if this is not possible, they might submit a written statement for consideration.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the student does not accept the allegation, s/he will be invited to attend the Panel meeting on a specified date, time and location. If this is not possible, the student might submit a written statement for consideration;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which upheld Panel outcome gives the student a resubmission opportunity, and in what circumstances does it apply?
options: Referral for plagiarism with resubmission and the grade limited to a pass mark, where severity is moderate
Referral for plagiarism with resubmission and the full range of marks available, where severity is moderate
Referral for plagiarism with resubmission and the grade limited to a pass mark, where severity is high
Referral with resubmission and the grade lowered by a further 15-credit unit, where severity is very high
questions.explanation: Referral with a resubmission opportunity, with the grade limited to a pass mark, is the upheld outcome where the severity of malpractice is moderate.
questions.source_excerpt: Referred due to plagiarism with a resubmission opportunity, and the grade is limited to a pass mark, if the severity of malpractice is moderate;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which two aims should the Academic Offence Panel balance when imposing penalties for an academic offence?
options: Deterring other students, while protecting the College's standing with its awarding bodies
Equitable treatment of all students, while letting the student recover their standing and progress
Consistency with previous years' cases, while reflecting any mitigating circumstances claimed
Upholding the Turnitin evidence, while keeping any credit ratified by the Assessment Board
questions.explanation: Penalties should constitute equitable treatment of all students while allowing a student found guilty to recover their standing and progress in their studies.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic Offence Panel shall seek to impose penalties for an academic offence that constitutes equitable treatment of all students and at the same time allow a student found guilty of an academic offence to recover their standing and to progress in their studies;

questions.question: An academic offence case cannot be completed before the Assessment Board meets. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, how is the decision then handled?
options: The case is suspended and restarted from the referral stage after the Assessment Board has met
The Assessment Board takes over the case and decides the outcome itself at that meeting
The student's marks are processed without penalty and the case is closed with a warning
The Panel decides, it is approved by Chair's Action and presented at the next board
questions.explanation: If the procedure is not completed before the Assessment Board, the Academic Offence Panel takes the decision, it is approved by Chair's Action and presented at the next board for notification.
questions.source_excerpt: The procedures outlined by this policy must therefore be completed before any Assessment Board takes place and in the case where this is not done, a decision is taken by the Academic Offence Panel and approved by Chair's Action, and presented at the next board for notification;

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, in which circumstances may a student be withdrawn from the College and not permitted to continue with their studies?
options: Where they have received any second academic concern, whatever its nature or severity
Where they fail to attend a viva held about work suspected to have been produced by someone else
Where they have multiple and serial offences, or an offence considered deliberate and severe
Where they decline to submit a written statement for the Panel's consideration of the case
questions.explanation: Withdrawal may follow where a student has multiple and serial offences, or where the offence is considered deliberate and severe.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a student has multiple and serial offences, or where the offence is considered to be deliberate and severe, the student may be withdrawn from the College and not permitted to continue with studies.

questions.question: A student facing an academic offence allegation says they never meant to cheat and did not realise their referencing was inadequate. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, can this still be an academic offence?
options: No; an offence needs proof that the student knowingly used unfair means, so a lack of intent ends the case
No; where a student did not intend to cheat, the matter must always be dealt with as an academic concern
Yes; culpable negligence counts, where unfair means are shown on the balance of probabilities
Yes, but only where the student has already received an academic concern about their referencing
questions.explanation: An academic offence covers unfair means used deliberately (knowingly) or through culpable negligence (unknowingly), judged on the balance of probabilities, so a lack of intent does not by itself rule out an offence.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic offences are identified as occasions or circumstances within which it can be demonstrated on the balance of probabilities that a student has deliberately (knowingly), or through culpable negligence (unknowingly), used unfair means in the assessment

questions.question: A student's second referral was submitted after they had received guidance on their first concern. They have clearly applied that guidance but need more feedback on a few minor errors. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, how may this be treated?
options: It must be treated as an offence, since it was submitted after the student had received guidance
It may be considered an academic concern, as the guidance was applied and only minor errors remain
It must be treated as an offence, as a second referral can never be handled as an academic concern
It may be closed with no further action, as minor errors fall outside the scope of the policy
questions.explanation: Although the submission came after the guidance, a second offence may still be considered an academic concern where the student has applied the guidance from the first concern but needs further feedback on minor errors.
questions.source_excerpt: Where there is a second offence, this may also be considered as an academic concern if: ... Where the student has been seen to apply the guidance from the first concern but requires additional feedback to address minor errors;

questions.question: Two students are emailed about academic offence allegations. Student A accepts the allegation; Student B does not accept it and is able to attend. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, how is each involved in the Panel meeting?
options: A attends in person to confirm the acceptance; B is invited to attend on a specified date, time and location
A is not invited to speak but may send a written statement; B is also limited to a written statement
Neither attends; the Panel decides both cases on the RSAMF and the evidence gathered by QA
A is not invited to speak but may send a written statement; B is invited on a specified date and time
questions.explanation: A student who accepts is not invited to speak to the Panel but may submit a written statement; a student who does not accept is invited to attend on a specified date, time and location.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a student accepts the allegation, s/he will not be invited to attend the meeting to speak to the Panel but may submit a written statement for consideration; ... Where the student does not accept the allegation, s/he will be invited to attend the Panel meeting on a specified date, time and location.

questions.question: An Academic Offence Panel upholds two cases: one where the severity of malpractice is high and one where it is very high. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, how do the outcomes for these two severities differ?
options: Both repeat the unit; very high also lowers the grade by a further 15-credit unit in the concurrent semester
High is referred for resubmission at a pass mark; very high repeats the unit with class attendance
High repeats the unit with class attendance; very high is referred for resubmission with no grade cap
High repeats the unit with class attendance; very high always results in withdrawal from the College
questions.explanation: High severity means repeating the unit with class attendance and a grade limited to a pass mark; very high severity means repeating the unit and lowering the grade by a further 15-credit unit in the concurrent semester.
questions.source_excerpt: Repeat the unit with class attendance and the grade is limited to a pass mark, if the severity of malpractice is high; ... Repeat the unit and lower the grade by a further 15-credit unit in the concurrent semester if the severity of malpractice is very high.

questions.question: A student's mitigating circumstances claim for a unit was approved, and the Panel later upholds an academic offence in that unit. The student says the claim should cancel the penalty. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which is correct?
options: The approved claim cancels the penalty, although the Assessment Board must still ratify this
The penalty overrides the claim decision; the student may appeal under the Academic Appeals Policy
The penalty overrides the claim decision and, as Board decisions are final, the student cannot appeal
The Panel must rehear the case in full, with the final outcome then decided by the External Examiner
questions.explanation: Penalties override any decision on mitigating circumstances applications, and although Assessment Board decisions are final, students still have the right to appeal under LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Any penalties applied override any decision taken regarding mitigating circumstances applications. The decisions of the Assessment Board are final and cannot be overridden. ... Students have the right to Appeal against the decision and the procedure is described in LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure

questions.question: An External Examiner reviewing an upheld academic offence case disagrees with a decision that the Assessment Board has ratified. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which statement is correct?
options: The Panel's minutes are confidential to the College and are not shared with External Examiners
The External Examiner may override the Board's decision once they have reviewed the Panel minutes
The Panel's minutes are available to them, but the Board's decisions are final and cannot be overridden
The External Examiner may refer the case back to the Panel, which must then reconsider the penalty
questions.explanation: The Minutes of the Academic Offence Panel are available to External Examiners, but the decisions of the Assessment Board are final and cannot be overridden.
questions.source_excerpt: The decisions of the Assessment Board are final and cannot be overridden. The Minutes of the Academic Offence Panel are available to External Examiners;

questions.question: A student's second referral was submitted well after they received guidance on their first concern, shows no sign of that guidance being applied, and has extensive unacknowledged similarity in its conclusion. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which statement is correct?
options: It may be a concern, as similarity in a conclusion is less serious than similarity in a literature review
It must be a concern, because the QA team is required to treat every second referral in that way
None of the conditions listed for treating a second offence as an academic concern is met
It must go straight to the Assessment Board, as second offences fall outside the Panel's remit
questions.explanation: A second offence may be treated as a concern only if it was submitted before guidance, the guidance was applied with minor errors remaining, or the issue is a minor referencing error; none applies here.
questions.source_excerpt: Where there is a second offence, this may also be considered as an academic concern if: a) The submission date was before the student would have received guidance following the first concern; b) Where the student has been seen to apply the guidance from the first concern but requires additional feedback to address minor errors; c) Where the concern is minor

questions.question: A lecturer invigilating an exam sees a candidate using hidden notes. Later, while marking coursework, the same lecturer suspects another student of malpractice. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which routes apply?
options: The RSAMF for both cases, since the same member of staff identified each of them
The exam regulations for the first; the RSAMF, completed urgently, for the second
The exam regulations for both cases, since the same lecturer was involved in each
A viva for the first; the exam regulations for the second, as it arose in marking
questions.explanation: Malpractice identified while invigilating is handled under the existing examination regulations, whereas malpractice suspected during marking requires the staff member to complete the RSAMF as a matter of urgency.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a suspicion of academic malpractice is identified by staff involved in the marking process, the individual staff member shall in the first instance as a matter of urgency, complete the Referral of Suspected Academic Misconduct form ... Where academic malpractice is identified by staff invigilating an examination, the existing regulations governing the conduct of the examination's procedures will apply;

questions.question: To save time, an Academic Offence Panel member proposes applying the same fixed penalty to every upheld case, whatever its circumstances. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, why is this not permitted?
options: The Panel sets each penalty's severity, which depends on the details of the case
Penalties are set by the Programme Leader when the decision is recorded on the RSAMF
Every upheld case must lead to withdrawal, as penalties must be applied consistently
The Assessment Board, not the Panel, sets the penalty once it has ratified the outcome
questions.explanation: Penalties must be proportionate as well as consistent, and the Panel determines the severity of each penalty depending on the details of the case.
questions.source_excerpt: Penalties for proven cases of unacceptable practice are clear, proportionate and consistently and equitably applied; ... The Panel shall determine the severity of the penalty, which is dependent on details of the case;

questions.question: Two first-offence submissions show the same Turnitin similarity. In A it is in the literature review and sources were acknowledged; in B it is in the conclusion and recommendations, with no acknowledgement. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which is correct?
options: They must be treated identically, since the amount of similarity identified via Turnitin is the same
A may be considered more serious, as a literature review carries more of the marks for the work
Neither can be treated as an offence, since first offences must always be dealt with as concerns
B may be considered more serious, given where its similarity occurs and the lack of acknowledgement
questions.explanation: For a first offence, the amount of similarity, any attempt to acknowledge sources and where the similarity occurs are all factors; similarity in the conclusion and recommendations may be considered more serious than in the literature review.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the issue is a first offence, factors affecting this decision and if this is a potential concern or offence may include: ... a) The amount of similarity identified via Turnitin; b) Whether there was an attempt to acknowledge the sources, c) Where the similarity occurs; ... recommendations may be considered more serious than a similarity in the literature review.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which statement correctly divides responsibility between the Academic Offence Panel and the Assessment Board in an academic offence case?
options: The Board decides whether an offence occurred; the Panel then sets the penalty and applies it to the unit
The Panel decides guilt only; the Programme Leader sets the penalty and records it on the RSAMF
The Panel decides the offence and penalty; penalties apply once the Board has ratified the decision
The Panel recommends a penalty; the Board then sets its severity based on the details of the case
questions.explanation: The Panel determines whether an offence has been committed and the appropriate penalty; penalties are applied once the Assessment Board has met and ratified the decision.
questions.source_excerpt: The panel determines whether an academic offence has been committed and determines an appropriate penalty and/or further action; ... The application of penalties can be expected to be applied once the Assessment Board has met and ratified the decision;

questions.question: A student facing an academic offence allegation wants to see the evidence against them and to offer an explanation. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which is correct?
options: Evidence is shared only after the Panel has reached its decision, to protect the investigation
They may see the evidence, but mitigation can only be raised later through an academic appeal
Only their Personal Tutor may view the evidence and speak for them at the Panel meeting
The allegation email includes the evidence, and they may test it and offer explanation or mitigation
questions.explanation: The College gives students the opportunity to put their case, test the evidence and offer explanation or mitigation, and the allegation email includes any evidence to be considered.
questions.source_excerpt: provide students who are believed to have engaged in unacceptable practice with the opportunity to put their case forward, test the evidence and offer any explanation or mitigation; ... The email will include full details of the allegation,any evidence to be considered and the Academic Misconduct Policy as a reference.

questions.question: A lecturer marking a first-year student's work suspects minor plagiarism and, given the student's early point of study, plans to give guidance informally rather than pass it on. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which is correct?
options: All concerns go to the QA team, which decides whether it is an academic concern or an offence
The lecturer may treat it as a concern, as minor issues are resolved by the staff member involved
It is forwarded only if the Turnitin similarity score is above the programme's set threshold
It should go to the Personal Tutor, who can close minor cases without involving the QA team
questions.explanation: The academic team forwards all concerns raised to the QA team, and it is the QA team, not the lecturer, that decides whether the case is an academic concern or an offence, weighing factors such as the point of study.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic team will forward all concerns raised to the QA team for verification and investigation. ... A decision will be made by the QA team as to whether suspected malpractice should be considered as an academic offence or an academic concern and the students' records are checked to determine previous activity and their level of study;

questions.question: A marker suspects unauthorised Generative AI use in an assignment, but Turnitin shows little similarity. A colleague says no case can proceed without Turnitin similarity. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which is correct?
options: The colleague is right, as first-offence decisions depend on the similarity identified via Turnitin
The colleague is wrong; GenAI misuse is a listed offence, and similarity is only one possible factor
The colleague is right, as GenAI use is dealt with under the examination regulations instead
The colleague is wrong, but the case may proceed only if the student admits the use at a viva
questions.explanation: Unauthorised use of Generative AI in an assignment is a listed offence, and Turnitin similarity is only one of the factors that may be considered, so low similarity does not stop a case.
questions.source_excerpt: The following are examples of offences that are covered by this policy: ... The unauthorised use of Generative AI in an assignment; ... factors affecting this decision and if this is a potential concern or offence may include: a) The amount of similarity identified via Turnitin;

questions.question: A student with a disability is the subject of an academic offence case. A colleague says the policy requires every case to be handled in exactly the same way. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which is correct?
options: Case handling takes account of the student's needs, including those from protected characteristics
The penalty is automatically reduced by one level for a student with a protected characteristic
The colleague is right; consistency means individual needs are not considered in handling a case
The case must be treated as an academic concern because of the characteristic, whatever the evidence
questions.explanation: The handling of individual cases takes account of the student's needs, including those arising from protected characteristics; this does not mean automatic penalty reductions or reclassification.
questions.source_excerpt: The handling of individual cases takes account of the needs of the student, including those arising from protected characteristics;

questions.question: A student has a single academic offence, which the Panel considers deliberate and severe. A colleague says withdrawal from the College is only possible after multiple offences. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which is correct?
options: The colleague is right; withdrawal requires multiple and serial offences on the student's record
The colleague is wrong; withdrawal is automatic for any offence the Panel finds to be deliberate
The colleague is right; a single offence can at most lead to repeating the unit with a lower grade
The colleague is wrong; withdrawal may also follow one offence considered deliberate and severe
questions.explanation: Withdrawal may follow either multiple and serial offences or an offence considered deliberate and severe, so a single offence can be enough; it is not automatic.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a student has multiple and serial offences, or where the offence is considered to be deliberate and severe, the student may be withdrawn from the College and not permitted to continue with studies.

questions.question: Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which of these correctly matches a role to its responsibility in an academic misconduct case?
options: Personal Tutor: deciding whether the suspected malpractice is an academic concern or an offence
Registry: ensuring marks for referred work are not processed until the investigation is completed
Programme Leader: emailing the student with the full details of the allegation and all of the evidence
Quality Assurance Officer: approving the allegation email that is sent to the student
questions.explanation: Registry is informed so that marks are not processed for confirmation until the investigation is completed; the QA team classifies cases, and the QA Officer emails the student with the Deputy Vice Principal's approval.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registry department should also be informed to ensure marks are not processed for confimation until the investigation is completed;

questions.question: The College is not reasonably confident that a submission conforms to the regulations, but it cannot be shown on the balance of probabilities that the student used unfair means. Under the Academic Misconduct Policy, which form of unacceptable practice is this?
options: An academic concern, as integrity is potentially compromised and confidence is lacking
An academic offence, as any lack of confidence in the work is enough to establish unfair means
Neither, as the policy applies only where unfair means are proven beyond reasonable doubt
An academic offence through culpable negligence, as the student did not intend unfair means
questions.explanation: A concern arises where integrity is potentially compromised and the College lacks reasonable confidence that the work conforms; an offence requires unfair means to be demonstrated on the balance of probabilities.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic concerns occur where the integrity of academic process has been deemed potentially to be compromised such that the College does not have a reasonable level of confidence that the work submitted conforms to the regulations. ... Academic offences are identified as occasions or circumstances within which it can be demonstrated on the balance of probabilities

questions.question: A first-year student has passed 5 of their 15-credit units. According to the Continuation and Completion Policy, what is their position regarding progression to Year 2?
options: They automatically continue to Year 2, as 75 credits meets the minimum Level 4 requirement for progression
They automatically continue to Year 2 but must resit the failed unit alongside their Level 5 units
They cannot automatically continue, as a minimum of 6 unit passes (90 credits) is required
They are automatically discontinued, as every first-year unit must be passed to progress
questions.explanation: The policy states each first-year unit carries 15 credits, so a student must pass at least 6 units (90 credits); students who do not achieve 90 credits cannot automatically continue to Year 2.
questions.source_excerpt: In the first year, each unit carries 15 credits, hence the student must pass a minimum of 6 units; ... Students who are unsuccessful in achieving 90 credits (achieve pass grade in minimum 6 units), cannot automatically continue to Year 2;

questions.question: According to the Continuation and Completion Policy, who must ratify and record the academic status of students being considered for continuation from Year 1 to Year 2, and when?
options: The Programme Leader, at the start of the second year
The Assessment Board, at the end of the first year
The Academic Registrar, when the student re-enrols
The awarding body (Pearson), after final results are issued
questions.explanation: The policy requires the academic status of students considered for continuation to be ratified and recorded by the Assessment Board at the end of the first year.
questions.source_excerpt: For students who are considered for continuation from Year 1 to Year 2, their academic status needs to be ratified and recorded by the Assessment Board at the end of first year;

questions.question: A student has submitted every assignment for a unit but has not satisfied all the pass criteria. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, how should the result be treated?
options: Award a Pass, because all the assignments have been completed
Award a Pass, provided the Assessment Board judges the effort reasonable
Do not award a Pass; the student should be reported as unclassified
Do not award a Pass; the student should be recorded as withdrawn from the unit
questions.explanation: The policy states a pass is a defined level of performance and cannot be given solely for completing assignments; students who do not satisfy the pass criteria should be reported as unclassified.
questions.source_excerpt: The award of a pass is a defined level of performance and cannot be given solely on the basis of a student completing assignments. Students who do not satisfy the pass criteria should be reported as unclassified.

questions.question: At the end of Year 1, a student who has not met the continuation requirements asks you what could happen next. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, which answer is correct?
options: They may be required to repeat units in Year 2 Term 1, or their studies could be discontinued
They will automatically continue to Year 2 if their attendance has been satisfactory
They will be automatically transferred to a different Level 4 programme at the start of the next year
They must retake the entire first year, including units already passed, before any further assessment
questions.explanation: The policy states that students who do not meet continuation requirements may be required to repeat units in Year 2 Term 1, or their studies could be discontinued.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who do not meet continuation requirements may either be required to repeat units in Year 2 Term 1, or their studies could be discontinued;

questions.question: According to the Continuation and Completion Policy, what must students achieve to be awarded an HND qualification?
options: The minimum Pass grade for Level 5 units only, amounting to 120 credits
At least a Merit grade across Level 4 and 5 units, amounting to 240 credits
The minimum Pass grade in 90 credits at Level 4 and 90 credits at Level 5
The minimum Pass grade for Level 4 and 5 units, amounting to 240 credits
questions.explanation: The policy states that to be awarded an HND, students must achieve the minimum Pass grade for Level 4 and 5 units, amounting to 240 credits.
questions.source_excerpt: To be awarded an HND qualification, students must achieve the minimum Pass grade for Level 4 and 5 units (amounting to 240 credits);

questions.question: Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, what must a student have done at each of Level 4 and Level 5 to be eligible for a compensated award?
options: Attended units equivalent to 90 credits and passed at least 75 credits
Attended units equivalent to 120 credits and passed at least 105 credits
Attended units equivalent to 120 credits and passed at least 90 credits
Attended units equivalent to 105 credits and passed at least 60 credits
questions.explanation: For a compensated award, the policy requires a student to have attended units equivalent to 120 credits and achieved at least a pass in 105 credits, at both Level 4 and Level 5.

Students who are unsuccessful in achieving 90 credits (achieve pass grade in minimum 6 units), cannot automatically continue to Year 2;
