questions.question: Under the compensated award rules in the Continuation and Completion Policy, what is the most credit a student who attended units equivalent to 120 credits at each level can leave unpassed and remain eligible?
options: 15 credits at each of Level 4 and Level 5
15 credits in total across Level 4 and Level 5
Two 15-credit units at each of Level 4 and 5
30 credits at Level 5, but none at Level 4
questions.explanation: With 120 credits attended at each level and at least 105 needing to be passed at each, no more than 15 credits can be left unpassed at each of Level 4 and Level 5.
questions.source_excerpt: For a compensated award, a student must have: 1. Attended units equivalent to 120 credits and achieved at least a pass in 105 credits at level 4; 2. Attended units equivalent to 120 credits and achieved at least a pass in 105 credits at level 5;

questions.question: An HND student has passed Level 4 and 5 units amounting to 240 credits. A colleague says this always completes the award. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, which is correct?
options: Correct, as 240 credits at Pass or above is the only requirement for every HND award
Not always, as some awards have added work placement or core module requirements
Not always, as a Merit in at least 105 credits at each level is also required
Correct, provided the 240 credits were achieved within 12 months of enrolment
questions.explanation: Beyond the 240-credit Pass requirement, some awards may have additional requirements based on work placements or core modules, which are outlined in the appendices.
questions.source_excerpt: minimum Pass grade for Level 4 and 5 units (amounting to 240 credits); ... Some awards that may have additional requirements based on work placements or core modules. These are outlined in the appendices.

questions.question: A Programme Leader tells a student who passed 7 of their first-year units that only students who pass every unit may enter Year 2. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, which is correct?
options: The Programme Leader is wrong, as 90 credits, or 6 units, is the enrolment minimum
The Programme Leader is right, as only passing all units allows continuation
The Programme Leader is right, unless the Assessment Board compensates the unit
The Programme Leader is wrong, as 60 credits, or 4 units, is the minimum
questions.explanation: Passing all units guarantees automatic continuation, but the enrolment minimum is 90 credits; at 15 credits per unit, that is 6 units, which this student has exceeded.
questions.source_excerpt: To be enrolled into the second year of study, a student must achieve minimum 90 credits in the first year (Level 4) ... In the first year, each unit carries 15 credits, hence the student must pass a minimum of 6 units;

questions.question: A first-year student has passed 6 units (90 credits). A colleague says these same 90 credits will also meet the Level 4 requirement for a compensated award at the end of the programme. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, which is correct?
options: The colleague is wrong: 90 credits meets the Year 2 minimum, but a compensated award needs at least 105 passed at Level 4
The colleague is right: 90 credits is the Level 4 minimum for both Year 2 enrolment and a compensated award
The colleague is wrong: 90 credits is below the Year 2 minimum, and a compensated award needs 120 passed at Level 4
The colleague is right, provided the student also attended units equivalent to 120 credits at Level 4
questions.explanation: Year 2 enrolment needs a minimum of 90 credits in the first year (Level 4), but a compensated award needs units equivalent to 120 credits attended and at least 105 credits passed at Level 4, so 90 credits is not enough.
questions.source_excerpt: To be enrolled into the second year of study, a student must achieve minimum 90 credits in the first year (Level 4) ... For a compensated award, a student must have: 1. Attended units equivalent to 120 credits and achieved at least a pass in 105 credits at level 4;

questions.question: An HND student attempted a 15-credit Level 5 unit but did not satisfy all of its pass criteria; every other unit on the programme has been passed. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, what is the position?
options: The unit is reported as unclassified, so the HND cannot be awarded until all 240 credits have been passed
The unit is recorded as a Pass because it was attempted, so the HND is awarded in the usual way
The unit is reported as withdrawn, and the HND can be awarded once the board uses its discretion to compensate it
The unit is reported as unclassified, but the HND can still be awarded under the HND compensation provision
questions.explanation: A student who does not satisfy the pass criteria is reported as unclassified; the HND compensation provision allows the HND to be awarded where one attempted 15-credit Level 5 unit is not passed and all the remaining units are passed.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who do not satisfy the pass criteria should be reported as unclassified. ... can be awarded the HND if they have attempted but not achieved a Pass in one of the 15 credit units completed at level 4 and similarly if they have attempted but not achieved a pass in one of the 15 credit units at Level 5. However, they must complete and pass all the remaining units

questions.question: A first-year student's unit results are 1 Pass, 3 Merits, 2 Distinctions and 2 unclassified. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, what is their position against the credit minimum for enrolment into Year 2?
options: They fall short of it, as only units awarded the Pass grade itself count, giving 15 of the 90 credits
They meet it only if every assignment for the 2 unclassified units was submitted, as those units then count
They meet the 90-credit minimum, as Merit and Distinction grades also satisfy the pass criteria
They fall short of it, as all 120 first-year credits must be passed before enrolment into Year 2
questions.explanation: Merit and Distinction both require all the pass criteria to be satisfied, so the student has 6 unit passes at 15 credits each, meeting the 90-credit minimum; the unclassified units do not count.
questions.source_excerpt: a student must achieve minimum 90 credits in the first year (Level 4) ... each unit carries 15 credits, hence the student must pass a minimum of 6 units; ... To achieve a merit, a student must satisfy all the merit criteria (and therefore the pass criteria) ... To achieve a Distinction, a student must have satisfied all the distinction criteria (and therefore the pass and merit criteria)

questions.question: An HND student's programme ended on 30 June 2025 with every unit passed. Their award has a work experience requirement, and their PLAD evidence was validated on 1 March 2026. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, which is correct?
options: They completed on 30 June 2025, as every unit had been passed by the programme end date
They could be considered complete only from 1 March 2026, within 12 months of the end date
They could be considered complete only from 1 March 2026, outside the 6 months allowed after the end date
They did not complete in time, as PLAD evidence must be validated before the programme end date
questions.explanation: Work experience evidence in the PLAD must be submitted and validated before the student can be considered to have completed, and completion is expected within 12 months from the programme end date; 1 March 2026 falls within that window.
questions.source_excerpt: evidence of the work experience which is kept in the Professional Learning and Development portfolio (PLAD) will need to be submitted and validated before the student can be considered to have completed the course successfully. A student should complete the programme within 12 months from the end date of the programme of study.

questions.question: A registry officer is checking whether an unpassed 15-credit unit could fall within the HNC or the HND compensation provision. Under the Continuation and Completion Policy, what condition does each provision set for that unit?
options: HNC: the student has exhausted their submission attempts and not passed; HND: the unit was attempted but not passed
HNC: the unit was attempted but not passed; HND: the student has exhausted their submission attempts and not passed
HNC: the unit was not attempted or submitted; HND: the student has exhausted their submission attempts and not passed
HNC: the student has exhausted their submission attempts and not passed; HND: the unit was not attended or attempted
questions.explanation: The HNC provision applies to a student who has exhausted their submission attempts and not passed, whereas the HND provision refers to a 15-credit unit that was attempted but not passed.
questions.source_excerpt: consider compensating one 15-credit (core/optional/specialist) unit based on the Pearson programme specification for a student who has exhausted his or her submission attempts and not passed. ... can be awarded the HND if they have attempted but not achieved a Pass in one of the 15 credit units

questions.question: According to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, by when must all students on distance learning courses be registered with the awarding body?
options: Before the programme commencing date
Within four weeks from the programme commencing date
Within two weeks from the programme commencing date
By the end of the first unit of the programme
questions.explanation: The policy requires all distance learning students to be registered with the awarding body within two weeks from the programme commencing date.
questions.source_excerpt: All students on distance learning courses must be registered with the awarding body within two weeks from the programme commencing date.

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, a student's pre-submission Turnitin report showed high similarity, but the report on their final submission is low. Which report is used to decide whether an Academic Concern or Offence has been committed?
options: The pre-submission report, as it shows the student's original work
Whichever of the two reports shows the higher similarity score
An average of the pre-submission and final similarity reports
Only the final report, in line with the Academic Misconduct Policy
questions.explanation: The policy states that only the final Turnitin report is used to determine whether any Academic Concern or Offence has been committed, in line with the Academic Misconduct Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Only the final report will be used to determine if any Academic Concern or Offence has been committed, in line with the Academic Misconduct Policy.

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, how many Turnitin similarity reports can a student obtain before the final submission of each assessment?
options: One similarity report for each assessment
Two similarity reports for each assessment
Three similarity reports for each assessment
As many as needed up to the submission deadline
questions.explanation: The Turnitin submission limit allows one similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment; after the final submission the work can no longer be resubmitted through Turnitin.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can obtain one similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment. A final similarity report is generated for the final submission of the assessment, at which point the student can no longer resubmit the work through Turnitin

questions.question: According to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which of the following applies when a student is given a resubmission of an assessment they did not pass?
options: A new assignment brief is set and the grade is capped at the pass mark
The same assignment brief is used and the grade is capped at the pass mark
The same assignment brief is used and the full grade range remains available
A new assignment brief is set and the full grade range remains available
questions.explanation: The Guidance on Reassessment states that a resubmission uses the same assignment brief as the original submission and the grade is capped at the pass mark.
questions.source_excerpt: The resubmission will comprise the same assignment brief as the original submission and the grade will be capped at the pass mark

questions.question: A distance learning student has not passed the resubmission of an assessment. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what may the student receive?
options: A second resubmission using a new assignment brief, with the grade capped at the pass mark
Automatic compensation for the unit, granted by their Unit Tutor without referral to the APB
A repeat opportunity, studying with full attendance and paying the relevant fees
An uncapped reassessment at no extra cost, using the original assignment brief
questions.explanation: After an unsuccessful resubmission, the policy says the student may receive a repeat opportunity, in which they must study with full attendance and pay the relevant fees.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of an unsuccessful outcome in the resubmission, a student may receive a repeat opportunity where the student must study with full attendance and pay the relevant fees

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what must happen to all assessment decisions made by the Assessment and Progression Board before they are recorded and communicated to students?
options: They must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval
They must be verified by the Programme Leader and forwarded to the awarding body for approval
They must be checked by the Unit Tutor and forwarded to the Board of Directors for approval
They must be reviewed by Student Representatives and forwarded to the Programme Committee
questions.explanation: The policy requires all Assessment and Progression Board decisions to be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval, then recorded and communicated to students promptly.
questions.source_excerpt: All assessment decisions by the Assessment and Progression Board must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval and recorded and communicated to students promptly

questions.question: A student repeats a core unit on a distance learning programme and does not achieve a pass. According to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which statement is correct?
options: The core unit can be replaced with an optional unit, provided the relevant fee is paid
The student must be withdrawn from the programme, as compensation is not available for core units
The core unit can be replaced with any unit of equal credit value at no cost
The core unit cannot be replaced with a different unit, but compensation may be granted
questions.explanation: Unlike an optional/specialist unit, a failed repeated core unit cannot be replaced with a different unit, but the student may be granted compensation, with the APB following the compensation regulation.
questions.source_excerpt: if a student repeats a core unit and does not achieve a pass that can not be replaced with a different unit but the student may granted compensation. In respect of compensation being granted, the APB must follow the compensation regulation

questions.question: According to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what may a student who repeats an optional/specialist unit and still does not achieve a pass be allowed to do to meet the total credit value for the qualification?
options: Resubmit the same unit a further time with the grade uncapped
Complete a different unit with full attendance and payment of the relevant fee
Complete a different unit fully online, with no attendance requirement and no fee payable
Nothing further, as an optional/specialist unit cannot be replaced by a different unit
questions.explanation: For a failed repeat of an optional/specialist unit, the policy allows the student to complete a different unit with full attendance and payment of the relevant fee to meet the total credit value.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student repeats an optional/specialist unit and does not achieve a pass, s/he may be allowed to complete a different unit with full attendance and with payment of the relevant fee in order to meet the total credit value to achieve the qualification

questions.question: The Distance Learning & Assessment Policy says Distance Learning Programmes should be directly comparable with on-campus courses at the same level in content and standard. Who must approve any variation from this?
options: The Assessment and Progression Board
The Programme Leader
The External Examiner
The College's Academic Board
questions.explanation: The Learning and Teaching section states that any variation from direct comparability with on-campus courses must be approved by the Academic Board.
questions.source_excerpt: Distance Learning Programmes should be directly comparable with on-campus courses at the same level in terms of content and standard. Any variation must be approved by the Academic Board.

questions.question: The External Examiner for a distance learning programme asks to see the assessment materials for a unit. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what is the correct position?
options: A sample of the materials may be shared once the Academic Board has approved the request
The materials may be shared once the students concerned have given their written consent
All assessment materials should be available to them as a matter of course
Materials for failed or borderline work must be made available, but not the remaining work
questions.explanation: The Assessment section states that all assessment materials should be available to the external examiner as a matter of course, so no special approval or sampling restriction applies.
questions.source_excerpt: All assessment materials should be available as a matter of course to the external examiner.

questions.question: According to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which group of learners falls outside the scope of the policy?
options: Learners released from employment to attend classroom-based learning or sessions
Learners studying wholly through the College's dedicated online learning platform
Distance learners who need reasonable adjustments for a disability or additional need
Distance learners who are repeating a unit with full attendance and relevant fees
questions.explanation: The policy states it does not apply to learners undertaking practical experience out of the classroom as part of the qualification, or to learners released from employment to attend classroom-based learning or sessions.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy does not apply to learners that are undertaking practical experience, out of the classroom which is part of the qualification, or learners that are released from employment to attend classroom-based learning or sessions.

questions.question: A distance learning student wants to raise an issue about their studies. According to the student support procedures in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what is the route for raising it?
options: Unit Tutor, then the Programme Leader, then senior staff of the College as required
Programme Leader first, then the Unit Tutor, then the Academic Board as required
Student Representatives, then the External Examiner, then the awarding body
Directly to the Academic Board, which then refers it on to the relevant Unit Tutor
questions.explanation: The Student Support section states that procedures enable students to raise issues with their Unit Tutors, then the Programme Leader, and thence senior staff of the College as required.
questions.source_excerpt: Procedures enable students to raise issues with their Unit Tutors and onto the Programme Leader and thence to senior staff of the College as required

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, who should approve in detail the course content, procedures for assessment and teaching arrangements for a distance learning programme?
options: The awarding body
The Unit Tutor
The Programme Leader
The External Examiner
questions.explanation: The Learning and Teaching section states that course content, assessment procedures and teaching arrangements should be approved in detail by the awarding body.
questions.source_excerpt: The course content, procedures for assessment and teaching arrangements should be approved in detail by the awarding body.

questions.question: According to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which review processes is the College's distance learning (DL) provision subject to?
options: A termly audit by the Board of Directors and an annual staff survey
Annual Monitoring and the College Periodic Review process
Monthly reviews by Student Representatives and an awarding body audit
Weekly checks by Unit Tutors and an external audit
questions.explanation: The policy states that the DL provision is subject to Annual Monitoring and the College Periodic Review process.
questions.source_excerpt: The DL provision is subject to Annual Monitoring and the College Periodic Review process.

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what must the College produce and disseminate for its distance learning programmes?
options: A weekly attendance report on each student for the awarding body
A printed pack of lecture notes posted to every student
Recordings of every online class, kept on the Student VLE for a full year
A clear schedule for the delivery of online classes and assessments
questions.explanation: The Learning and Teaching section requires the College to produce and disseminate a clear schedule for the delivery of online classes and assessments.
questions.source_excerpt: The College must produce and dissiminate a clear schedule for the delivery of online classes and assessments.

questions.question: Under the Delivery Platform section of the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, besides contingency plans in case the designed modes of delivery fail, what must have been done to the delivery system of any programme or element offered for study?
options: The reliability of its delivery system must have been tested
The delivery system must have been approved by the External Examiner
It must first have been piloted with on-campus students
The system must have been chosen with the Student Representatives
questions.explanation: The Delivery Platform section requires any programme or element offered for study to have had the reliability of its delivery system tested, with contingency plans ready to operate if the designed modes of delivery fail.
questions.source_excerpt: Any programme or element offered for study has had the reliability of its delivery system tested, and that contingency plans would come into operation in the event of the failure of the designed modes of delivery

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, delivery of study materials direct to students remotely, for example through e-learning or correspondence, must be secure and reliable. What must there also be a means of doing?
options: Tracking how long each student spends on the materials
Recovering the materials once the unit has ended
Charging students for replacement copies of them
Confirming the safe receipt of the materials
questions.explanation: The Delivery Platform section requires remote delivery of study materials to be secure and reliable, with a means of confirming their safe receipt.
questions.source_excerpt: The delivery of any study materials direct to students remotely through, for example, e-learning methods or correspondence, is secure and reliable, and that there is a means of confirming its safe receipt.

questions.question: According to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what must assessment tasks on a distance learning programme be based on?
options: The previous cohort's assessment results for the unit
The published learning outcomes of the units
The topics chosen by students at the start of the unit
The Unit Tutor's choice of topics
questions.explanation: The Assessment section requires assessment briefs to be fit for purpose and assessment tasks to be based on the published learning outcomes of the units.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure that all assessment briefs are fit for purpose and assessment tasks are based on published learning outcomes of the units

questions.question: The Distance Learning & Assessment Policy allows assessment procedures for distance learning to take a variety of forms. What must those procedures be subject to?
options: Lighter safeguards, as students are assessed remotely
Separate safeguards set by each Unit Tutor for their unit
The same safeguards and scrutiny as apply to on-campus courses
Prior sign-off by Student Representatives before being set
questions.explanation: Although assessment procedures may vary in form, the policy states they should be subject to the same safeguards and scrutiny as on-campus courses.
questions.source_excerpt: Assessment procedures may take a variety of forms but should be subject to the same safeguards and scrutiny as that applicable to on-campus courses.

questions.question: The professional standards in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy require all assessed work to be the student's own and correctly referenced. Which referencing protocols are specified?
options: Harvard referencing protocols
APA referencing protocols
MLA referencing protocols
OSCOLA referencing protocols
questions.explanation: The Professional Standards section requires all assessed work to be the student's own and correctly referenced using Harvard referencing protocols.
questions.source_excerpt: All assessed work is the student's own work and correctly referenced (using ... Harvard referencing protocols) from where material has been sourced

questions.question: Under the professional standards in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what must happen when a student does not attend a class?
options: Nothing, as attendance at online classes is optional for DL students
Staff must be informed of the non-attendance, with mitigation
The Student Representative must notify the awarding body in writing
The student must submit a formal claim to the APB within two weeks
questions.explanation: Students are expected to attend all classes and, as in the workplace, staff must be informed of any non-attendance with mitigation.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are encouraged and expected to attend all classes and as in the workplace staff must be informed of a non-attendance with mitigation

questions.question: Under the student support provisions of the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, students have a personal tutor to raise issues with or seek advice from. According to the same provision, what else will they have access to support on?
options: Finding private accommodation
Buying course textbooks
Renewing student visas
Securing work experience
questions.explanation: The Student Support section states that students will have a personal tutor and will also have access to support on securing work experience.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will have a personal tutor to whom they can raise issues or seek advice. They will also have access to support on securing work experience

questions.question: According to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, how is student support regularly reviewed?
options: At the Board of Directors, through the awarding body and with employer panels
At the Assessment and Progression Board and through annual staff appraisals
At the Academic Board, through Programme Committees and with Student Representatives
Through the Graduate Outcomes survey alone, without any Student Representatives
questions.explanation: The Student Support section states that student support is regularly reviewed at the Academic Board, through Programme Committees and with Student Representatives.
questions.source_excerpt: Student support is regularly reviewed at both the Academic Board and through Programme Committees and with Student Representatives.

questions.question: The Distance Learning & Assessment Policy lists mechanisms, focused on student outcomes, that the College uses to enhance learning and teaching. Which of these is one of them?
options: Staff appraisal reports
External Examiner reports
Awarding body audit letters
VLE login statistics
questions.explanation: The Monitoring and Evaluation section names Unit evaluation reports, the Programme Annual Monitoring process, External Examiner reports, the NSS and the Graduate Outcomes.
questions.source_excerpt: The College utilises a range of mechanisms which focus on student outcomes to enhance learning and teaching. These include Unit evaluation reports, the Programme Annual Monitoring process, External Examiner reports, the NSS and the Graduate Outcomes.

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, whose authorisation is needed for a student who has not passed an assessment to be given a resubmission opportunity?
options: The External Examiner for the programme
The Programme Leader for the course
The student's personal tutor
The Assessment and Progression Board
questions.explanation: The Guidance on Reassessment states that a student who does not pass may have a resubmission opportunity at the authorisation of the APB (Assessment and Progression Board).
questions.source_excerpt: Following a submission, a student may have a resubmission opportunity of that assessment should s/he not pass, at the authorisation of APB

questions.question: One aim of the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy is that the College operates equitable, valid and reliable assessment processes. What must be maintained for assessment decisions?
options: Summary pass rates for each unit, sent to the awarding body
Signed marker declarations held by the Programme Leader
Accurate and detailed records of each decision reached
Anonymised mark sheets for each unit, kept by the Unit Tutor
questions.explanation: Among the aims for equitable, valid and reliable assessment, the policy requires accurate and detailed records of assessment decisions to be maintained.
questions.source_excerpt: operate equitable, valid and reliable processes of assessment by ensuring: ... Accurate and detailed records of assessment decisions are maintained.

questions.question: Under the aims of the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, a tutor proposes a distance learning assessment that only learners able to travel to the campus could complete. Which requirement in the aims is this proposal at risk of breaching?
options: Assessment decisions must be communicated to students within two weeks of the submission date
Assessment methodology must not advantage or disadvantage any group of learners or individuals
Assessment tasks must be set by the External Examiner rather than by the Unit Tutor
All assessed work must be checked through Turnitin by the External Examiner before marking
questions.explanation: The aims require equitable, valid and reliable assessment, including a methodology that does not advantage or disadvantage any group of learners or individuals; an assessment only campus-based learners could complete would disadvantage distance learners.
questions.source_excerpt: operate equitable, valid and reliable processes of assessment by ensuring: ... Assessment methodology is valid, reliable and does not advantage or disadvantage any group of learners or individuals

questions.question: A learner's qualification includes practical experience undertaken out of the classroom. Does the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy apply to the learner while they are undertaking that practical experience?
options: Yes, as long as the practical experience is supervised through the online learning platform
Yes, but only once the Academic Board has approved the practical experience as a variation
No, the policy does not apply to learners undertaking that practical experience
Only if the learner registered with the awarding body within two weeks of starting
questions.explanation: The policy's scope excludes learners undertaking practical experience out of the classroom that is part of the qualification, so it does not apply to them in that situation.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy does not apply to learners that are undertaking practical experience, out of the classroom which is part of the qualification

questions.question: A tutor is preparing new study materials for a distance learning unit. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, whose expectations must the materials meet on the quality of teaching and learning-support material?
options: The External Examiner's, as set out in their most recent annual report
The Student Representatives', as agreed at the Programme Committee
The Programme Leader's, as recorded in the handbook for the unit
The awarding body's, for a programme leading to one of its awards
questions.explanation: The Learning and Teaching section requires all study materials used for delivery to meet the awarding body's expectations on the quality of teaching and learning-support material for a programme leading to one of its awards.
questions.source_excerpt: All the study materials used for programme delivery must meet the expectations of the awarding body in respect of the quality of teaching and learning-support material for a programme or element of study leading to one of its awards.

questions.question: A distance learning programme commences on 6 January. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, by when must every student on the programme be registered with the awarding body?
options: By 20 January
By 3 February
By 13 January
By 31 January
questions.explanation: All distance learning students must be registered with the awarding body within two weeks from the programme commencing date, so a programme starting on 6 January requires registration by 20 January.
questions.source_excerpt: All students on distance learning courses must be registered with the awarding body within two weeks from the programme commencing date.

questions.question: The College is choosing an e-learning system to deliver a distance learning unit. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which requirement must the delivery system meet?
options: It must be hosted and maintained directly by the awarding body for the unit's duration
It must be fit for purpose, with appropriate availability and life expectancy
It must be the same system as the one used for on-campus teaching of the unit
It must be approved each term by Student Representatives before teaching starts
questions.explanation: The Delivery Platform section requires a system delivering study through e-learning methods to be fit for its purpose and to have an appropriate availability and life expectancy.
questions.source_excerpt: The delivery system of the programme or element of study delivered through e-learning methods is fit for its purpose, and has an appropriate availability and life expectancy

questions.question: A distance learning student with a visual impairment finds the virtual learning platform hard to use. What does the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy provide for this student?
options: The student must switch to postal study materials, as the platform need not be accessible
The student must transfer to on-campus study, where reasonable adjustments can be made
The platform should have mechanisms for accessibility, and reasonable adjustments are available
Reasonable adjustments apply only to on-campus students, so the platform stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The policy requires the virtual learning platform to have appropriate mechanisms to address accessibility, and states that reasonable adjustments are made available to students with disabilities and additional needs.
questions.source_excerpt: The virtual learning platform should have appropriate mechanism to address the accessibility features. ... Reasonable adjustments are made available to students with disabilities and additional needs.

questions.question: A distance learning unit plans to use an online timed quiz where the on-campus version of the unit uses a written exam. What is the position under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy?
options: It is permitted, provided it has the same safeguards and scrutiny as on-campus assessment
It is not permitted, as distance learning assessment must take the same form as on campus
It is permitted, and an online quiz needs less scrutiny than an on-campus written exam
It is permitted only if the External Examiner writes and marks the quiz personally
questions.explanation: Assessment procedures may take a variety of forms, but they must be subject to the same safeguards and scrutiny as those applicable to on-campus courses.
questions.source_excerpt: Assessment procedures may take a variety of forms but should be subject to the same safeguards and scrutiny as that applicable to on-campus courses.

questions.question: A new tutor is starting to teach a distance learning unit. Under the professional standards in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what is expected regarding contact between staff and students?
options: Tutors give students their personal contact numbers so they can call at any time
Contact details are kept current, availability is publicised and channels are agreed
Students make contact only through Student Representatives, never directly
Tutors reply to contact from students only during scheduled online class times
questions.explanation: The professional standards require contact details for staff and students to be current, staff availability to be publicised and appropriate communication channels to be agreed.
questions.source_excerpt: Contact details for staff and students are current, staff availability is publicised and appropriate communication channels are agreed

questions.question: A tutor tells a distance learning class that the professional standards in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy apply only to students. Is the tutor correct?
options: Yes, the standards apply only to students, as staff follow a separate code of conduct
No, they apply only to staff, who must model workplace standards for their students
No, both staff and students must reinforce the standards required in the workplace
Yes, but only for students whose programmes include work-related learning
questions.explanation: To support the learning strategy, the policy requires both staff and students to reinforce the standards required in the workplace.
questions.source_excerpt: In order to support the learning strategy there is a requirement that both staff and students reinforce standards required in the workplace

questions.question: A distance learning student has an on-going health condition that affects their learning but no specific learning difficulty. What does the Student Support section of the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy say?
options: Support is only available to students with a diagnosed specific learning need
The student must move to on-campus study to be eligible for learning support
Support is offered only once the student has failed a first assessment attempt
Students with other on-going needs affecting learning are appropriately supported
questions.explanation: The Student Support section covers students with specific learning needs or with other on-going needs which affect their learning, and says they are appropriately supported.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with specific learning needs or with other on-going needs which affect their learning are appropriately supported

questions.question: A distance learning student used their pre-submission similarity report, made their final Turnitin submission, then spotted an error. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, can they resubmit the work through Turnitin?
options: Yes, they may resubmit once more if the assessment deadline has not yet passed
No, once the final similarity report is generated they can no longer resubmit
Yes, they may resubmit if the Unit Tutor agrees the error is minor and records it
Yes, they may resubmit, but only if the final report shows a high similarity score
questions.explanation: A final similarity report is generated for the final submission, at which point the student can no longer resubmit the work through Turnitin.
questions.source_excerpt: A final similarity report is generated for the final submission of the assessment, at which point the student can no longer resubmit the work through Turnitin

questions.question: A student repeating a unit fails to achieve a Pass at the first assessment opportunity within that repeated unit. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what is the student expected to do?
options: Transfer to the on-campus version of that unit for the rest of the year
Repeat the whole unit again from the start with the following cohort
Undertake a resubmission of the assessment for that repeated unit
Accept compensation for that unit, as agreed by the Programme Leader
questions.explanation: The Guidance on Reassessment states that a student who fails to achieve a Pass at the first assessment opportunity within a repeated unit is expected to undertake a resubmission.
questions.source_excerpt: A student who, for the first assessment opportunity within a repeated unit, has failed to achieve a Pass for that unit, shall be expected to undertake a resubmission

questions.question: A student has repeated a core unit without achieving a pass, and the APB is considering granting compensation. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what must the APB follow in doing so?
options: The compensation regulation in the Pearson BTEC Centre Guide to Quality Assurance and Assessment
The compensation rules in the College's Mitigating Circumstance Policy and Procedure
The compensation rules set out in the College's Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Policy and Procedure
The compensation recommendation in the External Examiner's most recent annual report
questions.explanation: Where compensation is granted for a failed repeated core unit, the APB must follow the compensation regulation stated in the Pearson BTEC Centre Guide to Quality Assurance and Assessment.
questions.source_excerpt: if a student repeats a core unit and does not achieve a pass that can not be replaced with a different unit but the student may granted compensation. In respect of compensation being granted, the APB must follow the compensation regulation stated in the Pearson BTEC Centre Guide to Quality Assurance and Assessment

questions.question: A tutor needs the Internal Verification Policy, which the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy says should be read in conjunction with it. According to its Introduction, where are these related policies available?
options: On the awarding body's website
In the staff handbook
Through the HR portal
Through the Student VLE
questions.explanation: The Introduction lists related policies, including the Internal Verification Policy, which support the College's Learning and Assessment process and are available through the Student VLE.
questions.source_excerpt: should be read in conjunction with the following non-exclusive list of policies and procedures, which support the College's Learning and Assessment process and are available through the Student VLE ... Internal Verification Policy

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, a student keeps failing the same optional/specialist unit. In what order does the policy describe the stages that may follow the first failed submission?
options: Repeat opportunity, then an APB-authorised resubmission, then compensation, then a different unit
APB-authorised resubmission, then compensation, then a repeat opportunity, then a different unit
APB-authorised resubmission, then a repeat opportunity, then a resubmission, then a different unit
APB-authorised resubmission, then a different unit, then a repeat opportunity, and finally compensation
questions.explanation: A failed submission may lead to an APB-authorised resubmission and then a repeat opportunity; failing the first opportunity in the repeated unit leads to a resubmission, and a failed repeated optional unit may then be replaced by a different unit. Compensation is described only for core units.
questions.source_excerpt: a student may have a resubmission opportunity of that assessment should s/he not pass, at the authorisation of APB; ... In the event of an unsuccessful outcome in the resubmission, a student may receive a repeat opportunity ... shall be expected to undertake a resubmission; ... If a student repeats an optional/specialist unit and does not achieve a pass, s/he may be allowed to complete a different unit

questions.question: A distance learning student has repeated one optional/specialist unit and one core unit and has not achieved a pass in either. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which outcome is possible?
options: The optional unit may be replaced by a different unit; the core unit cannot, but compensation may be granted
The core unit may be replaced by a different unit; the optional unit cannot, but compensation may be granted
Both units may be replaced by different units, with full attendance and payment of the relevant fees
Neither unit may be replaced by a different unit, but the APB may grant compensation for each of them
questions.explanation: A failed repeated optional/specialist unit may be replaced by a different unit (with full attendance and the relevant fee), whereas a failed repeated core unit cannot be replaced, although compensation may be granted.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student repeats an optional/specialist unit and does not achieve a pass, s/he may be allowed to complete a different unit ... if a student repeats a core unit and does not achieve a pass that can not be replaced with a different unit but the student may granted compensation

questions.question: A Programme Leader wants a distance learning programme's content to differ from the on-campus course at the same level. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which statement about approval is correct?
options: The APB must approve the variation, and course content should be approved in detail by the External Examiner
The Academic Board must approve the variation, and course content should be approved in detail by the awarding body
The awarding body must approve the variation, and course content should be approved in detail by the Academic Board
The Programme Committee must approve the variation, after consulting Student Representatives on the content
questions.explanation: Any variation from direct comparability with on-campus courses must be approved by the Academic Board, while course content, assessment procedures and teaching arrangements should be approved in detail by the awarding body.
questions.source_excerpt: The course content, procedures for assessment and teaching arrangements should be approved in detail by the awarding body. ... Distance Learning Programmes should be directly comparable with on-campus courses at the same level in terms of content and standard. Any variation must be approved by the Academic Board.

questions.question: Three weeks after a distance learning programme began, its students were not yet registered with the awarding body and no schedule of online classes had been issued. What is the position under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy?
options: Only the missing schedule is a breach, as registration is due within four weeks of the start date
Only the late registration is a breach, as a schedule is required for assessments but not for classes
Both are breaches: registration was due within two weeks and a clear schedule must be disseminated
Neither is a breach, as both matters are left to the Programme Leader's discretion for each cohort
questions.explanation: Students must be registered with the awarding body within two weeks of the programme commencing, and the College must produce and disseminate a clear schedule for the delivery of online classes and assessments.
questions.source_excerpt: The College must produce and dissiminate a clear schedule for the delivery of online classes and assessments. All students on distance learning courses must be registered with the awarding body within two weeks from the programme commencing date.

questions.question: The College is considering an e-learning system that its supplier will withdraw before current distance learning students finish their programme. Which Delivery Platform requirement in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy does this put at risk?
options: The delivery system must be fit for purpose, with an appropriate availability and life expectancy
Study materials sent remotely must be secure and reliable, with a means of confirming safe receipt
The virtual learning platform must have an appropriate mechanism to address accessibility features
Study materials must meet the awarding body's expectations for quality of learning-support material
questions.explanation: A system delivering study through e-learning methods must be fit for purpose with an appropriate availability and life expectancy; one withdrawn before students finish would not have an appropriate life expectancy.
questions.source_excerpt: The delivery system of the programme or element of study delivered through e-learning methods is fit for its purpose, and has an appropriate availability and life expectancy

questions.question: A distance learning student waited until the end of term to report a problem with a unit, saying nobody had told them that problems should be reported without delay. Which professional standard in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy was not met?
options: Staff and students work to sustain a culture of mutual respect in all their dealings with each other
Staff and students work with professional integrity at all times, in online classes and elsewhere
Students are encouraged and expected to attend all classes, informing staff of non-attendance with mitigation
Students are informed that any concerns should be raised promptly through appropriate channels
questions.explanation: The professional standards require students to be informed that any concerns should be raised promptly through appropriate channels; a student who was never told this shows that standard was not met.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are informed that any concerns should be raised promptly through appropriate channels.

questions.question: A Programme Committee meeting with Student Representatives plans to review student support and to approve the APB's latest assessment decisions. What does the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy allow?
options: It may approve the APB decisions, but student support may be reviewed only by the Board of Directors
It may review student support; APB decisions need External Examiner verification and Academic Board approval
It may do both, provided the Student Representatives present agree to the APB decisions being approved
It may do neither, as both matters are reserved to the External Examiner under the policy
questions.explanation: Student support is reviewed through Programme Committees and with Student Representatives, but APB assessment decisions must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval.
questions.source_excerpt: Student support is regularly reviewed at both the Academic Board and through Programme Committees and with Student Representatives. ... All assessment decisions by the Assessment and Progression Board must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval

questions.question: A review finds that the level of achievement needed to pass a programme has been allowed to fall over several years, equally for campus and distance learning cohorts. Which requirement in the aims of the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy does this breach?
options: Assessment methodology does not advantage or disadvantage any group of learners or individuals
Accurate and detailed records of assessment decisions are maintained
Academic standards for all Programmes are rigorously set and maintained
Students develop as independent learners, studying chosen subjects in depth
questions.explanation: To operate equitable, valid and reliable assessment, the aims require academic standards for all Programmes to be rigorously set and maintained; letting the pass standard fall breaches that, and because it affects all cohorts equally no group is advantaged or disadvantaged.
questions.source_excerpt: operate equitable, valid and reliable processes of assessment by ensuring: a) Academic standards for all Programmes are rigorously set and maintained

questions.question: A team redesigning distance learning delivery wants to reflect the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy's aim for the delivery of learning. Which description matches that aim?
options: Structured approaches that guide every student through a broad common syllabus with close tutor direction
Flexible approaches that let each student move at their own pace across a wide range of subjects
Blended approaches that pair online study with regular campus seminars and group projects
Measured approaches that help students develop as independent learners and study chosen subjects in depth
questions.explanation: The aims call for measured approaches to the delivery of learning which enable every student to develop as an independent learner, studying chosen subjects in depth and enhancing employability.
questions.source_excerpt: Articulate measured approaches to the delivery of learning which enables every student to develop, as independent learners, studying chosen subject(s) in depth and enhancing employability

questions.question: A new quality officer is summarising the External Examiner's roles described in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy. Which summary is accurate?
options: Sees a sample of assessment materials, approves APB decisions and authorises resubmission opportunities
Sees all assessment materials as a matter of course, verifies APB decisions, and their reports help enhance teaching
Sets assessment briefs, verifies APB decisions and approves any variation from on-campus comparability
Sees all assessment materials, grants compensation for core units and reviews student support with Student Representatives
questions.explanation: All assessment materials should be available to the External Examiner as a matter of course, the External Examiner verifies APB decisions, and External Examiner reports are among the mechanisms used to enhance learning and teaching.
questions.source_excerpt: All assessment materials should be available as a matter of course to the external examiner. ... All assessment decisions by the Assessment and Progression Board must be verified by the External Examiner ... These include Unit evaluation reports, the Programme Annual Monitoring process, External Examiner reports

questions.question: Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which pairing of bodies and responsibilities is correct in both parts?
options: APB authorises resubmission opportunities; Academic Board approves variations from on-campus comparability
APB approves variations from on-campus comparability; Academic Board authorises resubmission opportunities
External Examiner authorises resubmission opportunities; APB approves variations from on-campus comparability
APB follows the compensation regulation; External Examiner approves variations from on-campus comparability
questions.explanation: A resubmission opportunity is at the authorisation of the APB, and any variation from direct comparability with on-campus courses must be approved by the Academic Board.
questions.source_excerpt: a student may have a resubmission opportunity of that assessment should s/he not pass, at the authorisation of APB ... Distance Learning Programmes should be directly comparable with on-campus courses at the same level in terms of content and standard. Any variation must be approved by the Academic Board.

questions.question: A colleague says only the policies listed in the Introduction to the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy may be read with it, yet its Student Support section also cites the Student Welfare Policy. Which is correct?
options: The colleague is right, as the Student Welfare Policy applies only to on-campus students
The Introduction describes its list of related policies and procedures as non-exclusive
The colleague is right, and the Student Support section's reference should be disregarded
Only related policies that the awarding body has approved may be read with this policy
questions.explanation: The Introduction says the policy should be read with a non-exclusive list of policies and procedures, so other policies, such as the Student Welfare Policy cited in Student Support, can also apply.
questions.source_excerpt: This Policy and Strategy should be read in conjunction with the following non-exclusive list of policies and procedures ... including Mitigating Circumstances Policy; Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy; Student Welfare Policy

questions.question: According to the reassessment guidance in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, in which two situations must a student study with full attendance and pay the relevant fee?
options: An APB-authorised resubmission, and a repeat opportunity following an unsuccessful resubmission
An APB-authorised resubmission, and compensation granted for a failed repeated core unit
Compensation granted for a failed repeated core unit, and a different unit replacing a failed optional unit
A repeat opportunity after a failed resubmission, and a different unit replacing a failed optional unit
questions.explanation: A repeat opportunity after an unsuccessful resubmission requires full attendance and the relevant fees, as does completing a different unit to replace a failed repeated optional/specialist unit; the policy attaches no such requirement to resubmission or compensation.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of an unsuccessful outcome in the resubmission, a student may receive a repeat opportunity where the student must study with full attendance and pay the relevant fees ... s/he may be allowed to complete a different unit with full attendance and with payment of the relevant fee

questions.question: The awarding body approved a distance learning unit's content, assessment procedures and teaching arrangements in detail, but the written assignment set for the unit tests topics the unit does not cover. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which requirement is breached?
options: Assessment briefs must be fit for purpose, with tasks based on the units' published learning outcomes
Course content, assessment procedures and teaching arrangements must be approved by the awarding body
All assessment decisions must be verified by the External Examiner before release to students
All assessment materials should be available to the External Examiner as a matter of course
questions.explanation: Assessment briefs must be fit for purpose and assessment tasks based on the units' published learning outcomes; awarding body approval of the content does not cure a brief that tests topics outside the unit.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure that all assessment briefs are fit for purpose and assessment tasks are based on published learning outcomes of the units

questions.question: A distance learning unit has two separate assessments. Under the Turnitin submission limit in the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, how many pre-submission similarity reports can a student obtain across both?
options: One in total, as the limit applies to the unit rather than to each assessment
Two in total: one prior to the final submission of each assessment
Four in total: two prior to the final submission of each assessment
None, as a pre-submission report is offered only for a unit's first assessment
questions.explanation: Students can obtain one similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment, so two separate assessments allow two pre-submission reports in total.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can obtain one similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment.

questions.question: The External Examiner has verified an APB assessment decision, but the Academic Board has not yet approved it. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, may staff now tell the student the confirmed outcome?
options: Yes, as External Examiner verification alone is enough for a decision to be released
Yes, provided the Unit Tutor and the Programme Leader both agree that it may be released early
No, it must first go to the Academic Board for approval, then be recorded and communicated
No, outcomes are released only after the College Periodic Review has considered them
questions.explanation: APB decisions must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval before being recorded and communicated to students promptly, so verification alone is not enough.
questions.source_excerpt: All assessment decisions by the Assessment and Progression Board must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval and recorded and communicated to students promptly

questions.question: Consider three College learners: one studies wholly online while in full-time work; one is released by their employer to attend classroom sessions; one is on out-of-classroom practical experience that forms part of their qualification. To whom does the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy apply?
options: To all three, as each of them is working towards a qualification
To the online learner in full-time work and the learner released to attend classroom sessions
To the online learner in full-time work and the learner on out-of-classroom practical experience
Only to the learner who studies wholly online while in full-time work
questions.explanation: The policy excludes learners undertaking out-of-classroom practical experience that is part of the qualification and learners released from employment to attend classroom-based learning; being employed does not by itself exclude a learner who studies online.
questions.source_excerpt: a mode of delivering education and instruction to learners who are not physically present in a traditional setting such as a classroom. ... This policy does not apply to learners that are undertaking practical experience, out of the classroom which is part of the qualification, or learners that are released from employment to attend classroom-based learning or sessions.

questions.question: A distance learner fails an assessment. Their Unit Tutor, without referring to anyone, offers a resubmission on a revised brief and says the full grade range will be available. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, what must change?
options: The APB must authorise it, the same brief must be used and the grade capped at the pass mark
The APB must authorise it, but the revised brief and the full grade range may both stand
The same brief must be used and the grade capped, but the Unit Tutor may authorise it alone
The Academic Board must authorise it, and the revised brief may then be used with a capped grade
questions.explanation: A resubmission is at the authorisation of the APB, uses the same assignment brief as the original submission and has its grade capped at the pass mark, so all three elements of the tutor's offer must change.
questions.source_excerpt: Following a submission, a student may have a resubmission opportunity of that assessment should s/he not pass, at the authorisation of APB; ... The resubmission will comprise the same assignment brief as the original submission and the grade will be capped at the pass mark

questions.question: A distance learner's final Turnitin report shows passages copied from a journal article with no reference; their earlier pre-submission report had flagged the same passages. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which statement is correct?
options: The student may resubmit through Turnitin once more to add the missing Harvard references first
The pre-submission report, which flagged the passages first, is the one used to determine any offence
The work is not correctly referenced, and only the final report is used to determine any offence
No concern arises, as the student used their single pre-submission report exactly as the policy permits
questions.explanation: Assessed work must be the student's own and correctly referenced using Harvard protocols, and only the final Turnitin report is used to determine any Academic Concern or Offence; after the final submission the work can no longer be resubmitted through Turnitin.
questions.source_excerpt: All assessed work is the student's own work and correctly referenced (using ... Harvard referencing protocols) from where material has been sourced ... at which point the student can no longer resubmit the work through Turnitin; ... Only the final report will be used to determine if any Academic Concern or Offence has been committed

questions.question: A distance learning platform had its reliability tested before launch, but when it failed during an assessment week no alternative arrangements came into effect. Under the Distance Learning & Assessment Policy, which Delivery Platform requirement has been breached?
options: The reliability of the delivery system must be tested before the programme is offered
The virtual learning platform must have an appropriate mechanism to address accessibility
Study materials delivered remotely must be secure, with a means of confirming safe receipt
Contingency plans must come into operation if the designed modes of delivery should fail
questions.explanation: The Delivery Platform section requires both a tested delivery system and contingency plans that come into operation if the designed modes of delivery fail; the testing was done, but no contingency arrangements operated when the platform failed.
questions.source_excerpt: Any programme or element offered for study has had the reliability of its delivery system tested, and that contingency plans would come into operation in the event of the failure of the designed modes of delivery

policies.title: Learning Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy

questions.question: According to the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, within what timeframe should markers provide feedback on submitted assessments?
options: Within 10 working days of the actual submission date
Within 4 weeks of the Progression Board meeting
Within 3 weeks from the submission deadline
Within 6 weeks from the submission deadline
questions.explanation: The policy states that feedback from markers should be provided within 3 weeks from the submission deadline and must be clear, legible, constructive and linked to the learning outcomes.
questions.source_excerpt: Feedback from markers should be provided within 3 weeks from the submission deadline and the feedback must be clear, legible and constructive. It must also be linked to the learning outcomes and the assessment;

questions.question: A student who passed a unit at the first attempt asks to resubmit the work to improve their grade. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, how should you respond?
options: Accept it, provided the resubmission is made within 3 weeks of the original submission deadline
Accept it, but cap the new grade at the pass mark, as happens with any other resubmission
Refer the request to the External Examiner, who decides whether a grade improvement is permitted
Decline: work for a unit passed at the first attempt cannot be resubmitted to improve the grade
questions.explanation: The policy states that a student who has passed a unit in the first attempt is not allowed to submit the work again with the intention of improving the grade.
questions.source_excerpt: A student who has passed a unit in the first attempt is not allowed to submit the work again with the intention of improving the grade;

questions.question: Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy's guidance on reassessment, which statement correctly describes a resubmission?
options: It uses the same assignment brief and the grade is capped at the pass mark
It uses a new assignment brief and the grade is capped at the pass mark
It uses the same assignment brief and the full range of grades is available
It uses a revised assignment brief and the grade is capped at merit level
questions.explanation: The policy states that a resubmission comprises the same assignment brief as the original submission and the grade is capped at the pass mark.
questions.source_excerpt: The resubmission will comprise the same assignment brief as the original submission and the grade will be capped at the pass mark;

questions.question: A student asks how many Turnitin similarity reports they can obtain before making the final submission of an assessment. What does the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy allow?
options: One similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment
Up to three similarity reports prior to the final submission for each assessment
Unlimited reports until the submission deadline for the assessment has passed
None; the first similarity report is generated at the final submission
questions.explanation: To discourage academic malpractice the College limits Turnitin submissions: students can obtain one similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment.
questions.source_excerpt: the College has a limit on the number of times a student may submit an individual assessment through Turnitin, the plagiarism detection software used by the College; ... Students can obtain one similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment.

questions.question: Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, which Turnitin report is used to determine whether an Academic Concern or Offence has been committed?
options: The first similarity report the student obtains before final submission
Whichever report shows the highest similarity score across all submissions for the assessment
An average of all similarity reports generated for the assessment
The final report generated for the final submission of the assessment
questions.explanation: The policy states that a final similarity report is generated at final submission and only that final report is used to determine any Academic Concern or Offence, in line with the Academic Misconduct Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: A final similarity report is generated for the final submission of the assessment, at which point the student can no longer resubmit the work through Turnitin; ... Only the final report will be used to determine if any Academic Concern or Offence has been committed, in line with the Academic Misconduct Policy.

questions.question: A student in your unit asks whether you will look at a draft of their assignment before they submit it. Under the plagiarism section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what is the correct approach?
options: Decline it, because tutors reviewing drafts would compromise the integrity of the summative assessment
Welcome it, as tutors request drafts for formative feedback, which also reduces the chance of misconduct
Agree once the draft has been run through Turnitin and its final similarity report has been generated
Refer the draft to the Internal Verifier, who is responsible for giving formative feedback on all drafts
questions.explanation: The policy states that tutors request students to present draft submissions for formative feedback, helping towards a better final submission and reducing the chance of academic misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: Tutors request students to present draft assignment submissions for formative feedback. This allows the tutor and student to work towards a better final submission and also reduces the chance the student committing academic misconduct;

questions.question: What does the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy require regarding the internal verification of summative assessment papers?
options: Every formative and summative paper must be internally verified before feedback is released
Internal verification is limited to papers awarded a fail grade, before results are released
A prescribed sample must be internally verified using the correct form and procedure
Internal verification is left to the External Examiner, who samples papers at their discretion
questions.explanation: The policy requires a prescribed sample of summative assessment papers to be internally verified using the correct form and procedure, to ensure decisions are valid, fair, consistent and reliable.
questions.source_excerpt: A prescribed sample of summative assessment papers must be internally verified using the correct form and procedure;

questions.question: A student raises a concern about how a unit is being run and is not satisfied with the initial response. Under the Student Support section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what is the escalation route?
options: Directly to the Academic Board, then on to the External Examiner if still unresolved
Student Representative first, then the Programme Committee, then the Principal
Programme Leader first, then the Unit Tutor, then the Academic Board as required
Unit Tutor first, then the Programme Leader, then senior College staff as required
questions.explanation: The policy's student support procedures enable students to raise issues with their Unit Tutors, then the Programme Leader, and thence senior staff of the College as required.
questions.source_excerpt: Procedures enable students to raise issues with their Unit Tutors and onto the Programme Leader and thence to senior staff of the College as required;

questions.question: A student failed an assessment and then also failed the resubmission. Under the reassessment guidance in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what may the student receive next?
options: An automatic second resubmission using the same brief, capped at the pass mark
Compensation for the unit, granted directly by the unit tutor on request
A repeat opportunity, studying with full attendance and paying the relevant fees
A free repeat of the unit, with attendance left to the student's discretion
questions.explanation: The policy states that after an unsuccessful resubmission a student may receive a repeat opportunity, in which they must study with full attendance and pay the relevant fees.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of an unsuccessful outcome in the resubmission, a student may receive a repeat opportunity where the student must study with full attendance and pay the relevant fees;

questions.question: A student asks what they should do if they have to miss one of your classes. According to the Professional Standards section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what is expected?
options: Inform staff of the non-attendance with mitigation, as would be expected in the workplace
Nothing, since attending classes is encouraged for students but is not actually expected of them
Submit a formal Mitigating Circumstances claim to the Academic Board before the class takes place
Tell their Student Representative, who records the absence on their behalf after the class
questions.explanation: The policy states that students are encouraged and expected to attend all classes and, as in the workplace, staff must be informed of a non-attendance with mitigation.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are encouraged and expected to attend all classes and as in the workplace staff must be informed of a non-attendance with mitigation;

questions.question: The Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy says plagiarism is minimised through good assessment design. Which of the following is one of the measures it lists?
options: Reusing a standard generic assignment each term so that copying from past submissions is easier to spot
Allowing students unlimited Turnitin checks so they can reduce similarity before final submission
Using the same assessment method for every unit so that students know what to expect
Building an oral element into units, such as presentations, role playing or academic debates
questions.explanation: The policy lists a built-in oral element in units (e.g. presentations, role playing, academic debates) as a way of reducing the risk of students submitting work that is not their own; it also requires avoiding generic assignments and applying different assessment methods, and limits students to one similarity report before final submission.
questions.source_excerpt: Plagiarism is minimised through good assessment design. This includes: 3.4.1. Reducing the risk of students submitting work that is not their own, through the use of a built-in oral element in units, such as presentations, role playing, academic debates and sales negotiations;

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a requirement set out in the Assessment section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy?
options: Assessment briefs are fit for purpose and based on the published learning outcomes of the units
Students are summatively assessed several times on each learning outcome to confirm achievement
Assessors and Internal Verifiers are trained so that they are competent in their roles
Reasonable adjustments are made available to students with disabilities and additional needs
questions.explanation: The Assessment section states that students will not be over-assessed on learning outcomes, so repeated summative assessment of each outcome is not a requirement; the other three options are all stated requirements of that section.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will not be over-assessed on learning outcomes;

questions.question: Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, when must the unit handbook be prepared and distributed to students?
options: Before the first summative deadline, so that students can plan their assignments in time
At enrolment, so students are fully aware of the learning outcomes and assessment strategies
At the end of the first week of teaching, once class timetables have been confirmed
After the first Programme Committee meeting, once student feedback has been gathered
questions.explanation: The policy commits the College to preparing and distributing the unit handbook to students at enrolment so they are fully aware of learning outcomes, unit content and assessment strategies.
questions.source_excerpt: the College undertakes to ensure that the unit handbook is prepared and distributed to students at enrolment, so that students are fully aware of: a) Learning outcomes; b) Content of the unit(s); c) Assessment strategies;

questions.question: According to the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what do the Expected Answer Guidelines (EAGs) that the Lecturer provides for each unit give students?
options: Model answers from the previous cohort, released once the External Examiner has verified the results
