The detailed marking criteria that Internal Verifiers use when sampling assessment decisions
An example of how to structure assignments and the relevant content needed for a satisfactory grade
A schedule of all formative and summative deadlines for the unit, issued to students at enrolment
questions.explanation: The policy states that EAGs, provided by the Lecturer for each unit and made available through the VLE, give students an example of how to structure assignments and the relevant content to include to achieve a satisfactory grade.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are provided with Expected Answer Guidelines (EAG) for each unit by the Lecturer. The EAGs are made available through the VLE and give students an example of how to structure assignments and the relevant content to be included in order to achieve a satisfactory grade of the unit;

questions.question: According to the reassessment guidance in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies if a student repeats a core unit and does not achieve a pass?
options: It may be replaced with a different optional unit of equal credit, with full attendance and fees
It cannot be replaced with a different unit, but the student may be granted compensation
The student must withdraw from the programme, because a failed core unit cannot be compensated
The unit tutor may award a pass for the unit after reviewing the student's attendance record
questions.explanation: The policy states that a failed repeated core unit cannot be replaced with a different unit (unlike an optional/specialist unit), but the student may be granted compensation, with the APB following the relevant compensation regulation.
questions.source_excerpt: if a student repeats a core unit and does not achieve a pass that cannot be replaced with a different unit, but the student may be granted a compensation. In respect of compensation being granted, the APB must follow the compensation regulation

questions.question: The Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy applies to which students?
options: All students, irrespective of their teaching and learning delivery mode
Only students who attend face-to-face classes at a College campus
Only full-time students, with part-time students covered separately
Only students on Pearson BTEC programmes delivered by the College
questions.explanation: The introduction states that the Policy applies to all students irrespective of teaching and learning delivery mode, so face-to-face, mixed and online learners are all covered.
questions.source_excerpt: The Policy applies to all students irrespective of teaching and learning delivery mode.

questions.question: Under the assessment aims of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what must the College's assessment methodology be?
options: Identical across all units, so every learner is assessed by one method
Norm-referenced, so that a set proportion of learners achieve each grade band
Valid and reliable, without advantaging or disadvantaging any group or individual
Based mainly on timed examinations, so all work is verifiably the learner's own
questions.explanation: The assessment aims require an assessment methodology that is valid, reliable and does not advantage or disadvantage any group of learners or individuals.
questions.source_excerpt: Assessment methodology is valid, reliable and does not advantage or disadvantage any group of learners or individuals;

questions.question: According to the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, which students are offered learning strategies and tutorial support, including remedial intervention and training where necessary?
options: Students who have used up all of their resubmission opportunities
Students for whom English is not their first language
Students studying through the College's distance learning route
Students who have been referred for an academic misconduct offence
questions.explanation: The policy states that learning strategies and tutorial support are available for students where English is not their first language, offering remedial intervention and training where necessary.
questions.source_excerpt: Learning strategies and tutorial support are available for students where English is not their first language and offer remedial intervention and training where necessary;

questions.question: According to the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, which process primarily oversees the representation of groups with various characteristics, as part of ensuring inclusive learning?
options: The Internal Verification process
The Academic Appeals process
The Recognition of Prior Learning process
The Annual Monitoring process
questions.explanation: The policy states that the representation of groups with various characteristics is overseen primarily within the Annual Monitoring process, with the NSS also helpful in this regard.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure the provision of inclusive learning through promoting equality, diversity and equal opportunity. The representation of groups with various characteristics is overseen primarily within the Annual Monitoring process.

questions.question: According to the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, when should tutors check on students' progress against the learning outcomes?
options: During lessons and at the end of each lesson
Only after the summative work has been marked
At the mid-point of each unit, at peer review
At the start of each unit, during induction
questions.explanation: The policy requires teaching to be directed towards attaining the learning outcomes, with tutors checking on progress against them during and at the end of lessons.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure that teaching is directed towards the goal of attainment of the learning outcomes that lecturers make use of in plenary sessions. Further, during and at the end of lessons, tutors to check on progress against the learning outcomes;

questions.question: Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, who must verify all assessment decisions made by the Assessment and Progression Board before they are forwarded to the Academic Board for approval?
options: The Programme Leader
The Principal's Executive Group
The External Examiner
The Quality Assurance Department
questions.explanation: The policy states that all assessment decisions by the Assessment and Progression Board must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval.
questions.source_excerpt: All assessment decisions by the Assessment and Progression Board must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval and recorded and communicated to students promptly;

questions.question: Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what does the College provide to all new academic staff members to support their teaching?
options: A bank of previously verified assignment briefs to reuse
A template and an exemplar Unit Handbook
Marked samples of the previous cohort's work
A completed scheme of work for every unit
questions.explanation: As part of promoting student inclusiveness, the policy commits the College to providing a template and an exemplar Unit Handbook to all new academic staff members.
questions.source_excerpt: Template and an exemplar Unit Handbook to all new academic staff members;

questions.question: According to the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, which software systems are all academic and support staff trained to use?
options: Blackboard, SafeAssign and the student records system
Canvas, Grammarly and the online timetabling system
Google Classroom, Copyleaks and the HR portal
The VLE (Moodle), Turnitin and bespoke College systems
questions.explanation: The policy states that all academic and support staff are trained in the use of the software systems, including the VLE (Moodle), Turnitin and bespoke College systems.
questions.source_excerpt: All academic and support staff are trained in the use of the software systems including the VLE (Moodle), Turnitin and bespoke College systems.

questions.question: Under the plagiarism section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, how often do lecturers produce contextualised assessments that require students to research and analyse their findings?
options: In each term
Once a year
Every two years
At each revalidation
questions.explanation: To avoid generic assignments, the policy states that lecturers produce contextualised assessments in each term that require students to research and analyse their findings.
questions.source_excerpt: Avoiding the use of generic assignments. Lecturers produce contextualised assessments in each term that require the students to research and analyse their findings;

questions.question: Under the Professional Standards section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, which referencing protocols must be used for sourced material in assessed work?
options: APA referencing protocols
Vancouver referencing protocols
Harvard referencing protocols
Chicago referencing protocols
questions.explanation: The Professional Standards section requires all assessed work to be the student's own and correctly referenced using Harvard referencing protocols.
questions.source_excerpt: All assessed work is the student's own work and correctly referenced (using Harvard referencing protocols) from where material has been sourced;

questions.question: Under the Student Support section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, who will every student have to raise issues with or seek advice from?
options: A peer mentor
A personal tutor
A Student Representative
An Internal Verifier
questions.explanation: The Student Support section states that students will have a personal tutor to whom they can raise issues or seek advice, as well as access to support on securing work placements.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will have a personal tutor to whom they can raise issues or seek advice. They will also have access to support on securing work placements;

questions.question: Which of the following does the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy list among the mechanisms, focused on student outcomes, that the College uses to enhance learning and teaching?
options: Ofsted inspection reports and employer satisfaction surveys
Mystery shopper audits and university league table rankings
Staff timesheet audits and reviews of student social media posts
External Examiner reports and the Graduate Outcomes
questions.explanation: The Monitoring and Evaluation section lists Unit evaluation reports, the Programme Annual Monitoring process, External Examiner reports, the NSS and the Graduate Outcomes as mechanisms focused on student outcomes.
questions.source_excerpt: The College utilises a range of mechanisms which focus on student outcomes to enhance learning and teaching. These include Unit evaluation reports, the Programme Annual Monitoring process, External Examiner reports, the NSS and the Graduate Outcomes.

questions.question: Under the reassessment guidance in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, whose authorisation is needed for a student to have a resubmission opportunity after not passing an assessment?
options: The Assessment and Progression Board (APB)
The unit tutor who marked the original work
The External Examiner for the programme
The Internal Verifier who sampled the work
questions.explanation: The reassessment guidance states that a student who does not pass may have a resubmission opportunity at the authorisation of the APB (Assessment and Progression Board).
questions.source_excerpt: Following a submission, a student may have a resubmission opportunity of that assessment should s/he not pass, at the authorisation of APB;

questions.question: A tutor wants to point a student to the Academic Appeals Policy and the Mitigating Circumstance Policy, which support the College's assessment process. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, where are these available?
options: Through the Student Virtual Learning Environment (VLE)
In the unit handbook distributed to students at enrolment
On request from the Quality Assurance Department only
In printed form at the Learning Resource Centre only
questions.explanation: The introduction states that the supporting policies listed in the policy, including the Academic Appeals and Mitigating Circumstance policies, support the College's Assessment process and are available through the Student VLE.
questions.source_excerpt: This Policy and Strategy should be read in conjunction with the following non-exclusive list of policies and procedures, which support the College's Assessment process and are available through the Student Virtual Learning Environment (VLE); ... Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure ... Mitigating Circumstance Policy and Procedure

questions.question: A colleague says the College's commitment to equitable, valid and reliable assessment covers only taught coursework, not recognition of prior learning (RPL) claims. Under the assessment aims of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, is this right?
options: Yes: RPL claims are decided by the External Examiner, outside the College's processes
No: the College's assessment processes expressly include recognition of prior learning
Yes: RPL applies only to distance learners, so it falls outside this policy's scope
No, but only for RPL claims that are submitted after the student has enrolled
questions.explanation: The assessment aims state that the College operates equitable, valid and reliable processes of assessment, including for the recognition of prior learning (RPL).
questions.source_excerpt: operate equitable, valid and reliable processes of assessment, including for the recognition of prior learning (RPL), which enables all students to demonstrate the extent to which they have achieved the intended learning outcomes

questions.question: An adverse occurrence closes the campus and stops on-site classes for several weeks. What does the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy require of learning and teaching during this period?
options: Teaching pauses until the Academic Board approves a revised scheme of work for each unit
Units switch to self-study, with the EAGs on the VLE replacing all of the taught sessions
Practices are rigorously maintained, via a suitable mode that supports all students
Affected students are offered a fee-free repeat of the units in the following academic year
questions.explanation: The policy requires learning and teaching practices to be rigorously maintained in cases of any adverse occurrences, with delivery by a suitable mode that supports all students.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure that learning and teaching practices are rigorously maintained in cases of any adverse occurrences and deliver learning and teaching by a suitable mode that supports all students.

questions.question: A tutor notices discourteous posts between students on a unit's online discussion forum. Which standard in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy applies to this online forum?
options: None: the standard covers physical classrooms, so online forums fall under IT acceptable use rules
Virtual learning environments must be safe and reliable, promoting dignity, courtesy and respect
The standard applies online only while a lecturer is actively moderating the discussion
Online forums are the responsibility of the Student Representatives at Programme Committee
questions.explanation: The policy requires physical, virtual and social learning environments to be safe, accessible and reliable for every student, promoting dignity, courtesy and respect in their use.
questions.source_excerpt: Maintain physical, virtual and social learning environments that are safe, accessible and reliable for every student, promoting dignity, courtesy and respect in their use;

questions.question: A Programme Leader wants the effectiveness of a new teaching approach evaluated in line with the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy. Where should its effectiveness be critically discussed and evaluated?
options: At the deliberative committees and boards at which Student Representatives are present
In a staff-only teaching meeting, so that student opinion does not bias the evaluation
In the External Examiner's annual report, as the sole route for evaluating teaching
In each lecturer's own reflective log, reviewed only at their annual appraisal
questions.explanation: The policy requires learning and teaching practices to be critically discussed and their effectiveness evaluated at deliberative committees/boards at which Student Representatives are present.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure that learning and teaching practices are critically discussed, and their effectiveness is evaluated at various deliberative committees/boards, at which Student Representatives are present;

questions.question: A marker returns feedback two weeks after the submission deadline, consisting only of a grade and the comment 'Well done'. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what is wrong with this?
options: It is late, as feedback must be returned within one week of the submission deadline
Nothing, as it was returned in time and feedback content is left to each marker
The timing is fine, but feedback must be constructive and linked to the learning outcomes
Feedback should have been withheld until the External Examiner had verified the grade
questions.explanation: Feedback within 3 weeks of the deadline meets the timeframe, but the policy also requires feedback to be clear, legible and constructive and linked to the learning outcomes and the assessment.
questions.source_excerpt: Feedback from markers should be provided within 3 weeks from the submission deadline and the feedback must be clear, legible and constructive. It must also be linked to the learning outcomes and the assessment;

questions.question: A tutor plans a unit whose only assessment is a single summative assignment set at the very end. Which expectation in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy does this plan fail to meet?
options: Summatively assessing every learning outcome at least twice before the unit ends
Providing regular formative assessment with feedback, to build confidence for summative work
Submitting the unit's assessment plan to the External Examiner before teaching begins
Setting a timed written examination alongside every coursework assignment in the unit
questions.explanation: Tutors are expected to provide regular and appropriate formative assessment opportunities with feedback that helps students progress and build confidence to tackle summative assessments.
questions.source_excerpt: Tutors are expected to direct the learning process towards achievements of learning outcomes and provide regular and appropriate formative assessment opportunities with appropriate feedback that enables students to progress and build confidence to tackle summative assessments;

questions.question: Two newly appointed lecturers start in the same term as a new cohort of students. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, who is to be provided with an induction?
options: The new students only, as new staff are covered by the College's HR onboarding instead
The new lecturers only, as students receive the unit handbook in place of an induction
Only those new to UK higher education, whether they are staff members or students
Both the new academic staff members and all the new students embarking on a programme
questions.explanation: To promote student inclusiveness, the policy commits the College to providing induction for all new academic staff members and new students embarking on a programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Student inclusiveness is encouraged through the active promotion of equality, diversity, and equal opportunity by providing: a) Induction for all new academic staff members and new students embarking on a programme;

questions.question: After a teaching team meeting, a colleague suggests skipping the minutes to save time. What does the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy require for teaching and staff meetings?
options: They are conducted transparently, with proceedings documented and outcomes shared
Minutes are needed only for Academic Board meetings, not for teaching team meetings
Only decisions affecting assessment are recorded, and only by the Programme Leader
Proceedings are recorded only when a Student Representative has attended the meeting
questions.explanation: The policy requires teaching and staff meetings to be regularly conducted in a transparent way, with the proceedings documented and outcomes shared.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensuring teaching and staff meetings are regularly conducted in a transparent way with the proceedings documented and outcomes shared;

questions.question: To save time, a lecturer plans to reuse last year's essay assignment, unchanged, for a new cohort. Which plagiarism-minimising measure in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy does this conflict with?
options: Setting a timed, invigilated examination in place of coursework in every unit
Requiring each draft to be approved by the Internal Verifier before submission
Restricting students to a fixed list of approved sources for each assignment
Producing contextualised assessments each term and designing new ones
questions.explanation: The plagiarism section calls for avoiding generic assignments, with lecturers producing contextualised assessments in each term, and for frequently designing new assessments.
questions.source_excerpt: Avoiding the use of generic assignments. Lecturers produce contextualised assessments in each term that require the students to research and analyse their findings; ... Frequently designing new assessments and applying different assessment methods.

questions.question: A new lecturer asks what the Professional Standards section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy expects regarding contact with students. Which of the following is required?
options: Staff give students a personal mobile number and are reachable at all times in term
Staff availability is shared only with the Programme Leader, who relays queries
Contact details are current, availability is publicised and channels are agreed
Staff respond to every student message within 24 hours, including at weekends
questions.explanation: The Professional Standards section requires contact details for staff and students to be current, staff availability to be publicised and appropriate communication channels to be agreed.
questions.source_excerpt: Contact details for staff and students are current, staff availability is publicised and appropriate communication channels are agreed;

questions.question: A student on a programme that requires work-integrated learning asks what support the College gives for it. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies?
options: None; finding and completing a placement is entirely the student's own responsibility
Support is given for the activity during the programme, including on securing a placement
Support starts only once the student has completed all of the programme's taught units
Their personal tutor must arrange a guaranteed paid placement for them in each year
questions.explanation: The Student Support section states that students on programmes requiring work-related or integrated learning require support for this during their programmes, and have access to support on securing work placements.
questions.source_excerpt: Students undertaking programmes requiring work-related or integrated learning require support for this activity during their academic programmes. ... They will also have access to support on securing work placements;

questions.question: A student is repeating a unit and fails to achieve a Pass at the first assessment opportunity within that repeated unit. Under the reassessment guidance in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what is the student expected to do?
options: Undertake a resubmission of the failed assessment
Repeat the whole unit again at the next intake
Accept a fail, as a repeated unit has no reassessment
Sit an alternative task set by the External Examiner
questions.explanation: The reassessment guidance states that a student who fails to achieve a Pass at the first assessment opportunity within a repeated unit shall be expected to undertake a resubmission.
questions.source_excerpt: A student who, for the first assessment opportunity within a repeated unit, has failed to achieve a Pass for that unit, shall be expected to undertake a resubmission;

questions.question: A student repeats an optional/specialist unit and does not achieve a pass. Under the reassessment guidance in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what may the student be allowed to do to meet the total credit value for the qualification?
options: Take a different unit free of charge, with attendance left to the student's discretion
Have the unit's credit awarded on the Programme Leader's recommendation
Complete a different unit with full attendance and payment of the relevant fee
Nothing; failing a repeated optional unit ends the student's qualification
questions.explanation: The reassessment guidance states that a student who repeats an optional/specialist unit and does not pass may be allowed to complete a different unit, with full attendance and payment of the relevant fee, to meet the total credit value.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student repeats an optional/specialist unit and does not achieve a pass, the student may be allowed to complete a different unit with full attendance and with payment of the relevant fee in order to meet the total credit value to achieve the qualification;

questions.question: A student makes the final submission of an assessment through Turnitin, then spots an error and wants to upload a corrected version. What does the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy say?
options: They may, as long as the submission deadline for the assessment has not yet passed
They may, if their tutor authorises it within 3 weeks of the submission deadline
They may once more, and the report with the lower similarity score is then used
No; the final similarity report closes the work to resubmission via Turnitin
questions.explanation: A final similarity report is generated for the final submission, at which point the student can no longer resubmit the work through Turnitin.
questions.source_excerpt: A final similarity report is generated for the final submission of the assessment, at which point the student can no longer resubmit the work through Turnitin;

questions.question: A colleague says online learners can be given a narrower range of learning resources than face-to-face students, because the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy is mainly about classroom teaching. Is this consistent with the policy?
options: Yes, provided online learners are signposted to the Learning Resource Centre for anything that is missing
No: the policy covers every delivery mode, and resources must give every student an equal, effective opportunity
Yes, as online study is governed by the Distance Learning and Assessment Policy instead of this policy
No, but only where the unit's learning outcomes are assessed through a built-in oral element
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all students irrespective of delivery mode, and learning and teaching activities and resources must give every student an equal and effective opportunity using face-to-face, mixed or online delivery.
questions.source_excerpt: The Policy applies to all students irrespective of teaching and learning delivery mode. ... Learning and teaching activities and associated resources provide every student with an equal and effective opportunity to achieve the intended learning outcomes using face-to-face, mixed or online delivery methods.

questions.question: After an assessment board, a colleague proposes keeping only students' final grades and deleting the notes showing how each assessment decision was reached. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, is this acceptable?
options: Yes, as the policy requires a record of final assessment outcomes only, not of how they were reached
Yes, once the External Examiner has verified the decisions and the Academic Board has approved them
No: the assessment aims require accurate and detailed records of assessment decisions to be maintained
No, but only for decisions on students who were granted reasonable adjustments or compensation
questions.explanation: The assessment aims require accurate and detailed records of assessment decisions to be maintained, so reducing the record to final grades alone is not consistent with the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Accurate and detailed records of assessment decisions are maintained.

questions.question: A senior manager plans to write the College's next learning and teaching strategy with a small group of managers, without involving teaching staff or students. Is this consistent with the aims of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy?
options: Yes, as the Principal's Executive Group sets the strategy and informs staff and students afterwards
Yes, provided the finished draft is later shared with Student Representatives at a Programme Committee
No, as the External Examiner must approve the learning and teaching strategy before it is adopted
No: the aims require staff and students to be fully engaged in formulating the strategy
questions.explanation: One of the learning and teaching aims is to fully engage staff and students in the formulation of the learning and teaching strategy, which a managers-only drafting process does not do.
questions.source_excerpt: Fully engage staff and students in the formulation of its learning and teaching strategy;

questions.question: A department proposes to stop peer reviews and class observations of teaching and rely only on end-of-unit student evaluation forms for feedback on teaching. Is this consistent with the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy?
options: Yes, as Unit evaluation reports are listed among the mechanisms the College uses to enhance teaching
No: the policy commits the College to undertaking regular peer reviews and class observations
Yes, provided the evaluation forms are then discussed at the Programme Committee meetings each term
No, as each lecturer's teaching must instead be observed once a year by the External Examiner
questions.explanation: Unit evaluation reports are one monitoring mechanism, but they do not replace the policy's commitment to undertaking regular peer reviews and class observations of teaching staff.
questions.source_excerpt: Provide opportunities for students and staff to give feedback both informally and formally through programme committees, peer review and observation, appraisal forms and to enhance programmes continuously by: ... Undertaking regular peer reviews and class observations; ... peer reviews of teaching staff and teaching meetings are regularly conducted in a transparent manner

questions.question: A learning support assistant who helps students in class, but does not lecture or verify assessments, asks whether the policy's requirement to be appropriately qualified, supported and developed applies to them. What does the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy say?
options: No: the requirement names lecturers and internal verifiers, so it applies to those two roles only
Only if they hold a professional teaching qualification, such as accreditation by Advance HE
Yes: it covers anyone involved in teaching or supporting student learning, not only lecturers
Only once they begin to mark summative work, as the requirement concerns assessment roles
questions.explanation: The policy requires lecturers, internal verifiers and anyone involved in teaching or supporting student learning to be appropriately qualified, supported and developed.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure lecturers, internal verifiers and anyone involved in teaching or supporting student learning are appropriately qualified, supported and developed;

questions.question: A tutor designs a unit using only abstract, theory-based lectures and tasks, with no link to workplace practice. The unit has no work experience requirement. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies?
options: It falls short: tutors are required to fully introduce work-relevant learning and assessment methods
It is acceptable, as work-relevant methods are needed only where a unit lists a work experience requirement
It is acceptable, as linking learning to the workplace is left to placement providers rather than tutors
It falls short, but only because theory-only units need External Examiner approval before teaching begins
questions.explanation: The policy requires tutors to fully introduce work-relevant learning and assessment methods and teaching to transfer learning to the workplace; this applies whether or not the unit has a work experience requirement.
questions.source_excerpt: Learning strategies and teaching methods engender transfer of learning from classroom to workplace and fully support work-based learning; ... Tutors are required to fully introduce learning and assessment methods that are work-relevant;

questions.question: A lecturer drafts an assignment brief around a topical issue they find interesting, which is not covered by the unit's published learning outcomes. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, can this brief be used?
options: Yes, if the topic is contextualised each term, as the plagiarism section encourages
Yes, if the Internal Verifier samples the marked work once it has been assessed
No, as assessment tasks must be based on the published learning outcomes of the units
No, as every new brief must first be approved by the Academic Board before its release
questions.explanation: The policy requires assessment briefs to be fit for purpose and assessment tasks to be based on the published learning outcomes of the units; contextualising or later sampling does not override this.
questions.source_excerpt: Ensure that all assessment briefs are fit for purpose and assessment tasks are based on published learning outcomes of the units;

questions.question: A unit's submission deadline is 8 March. A student hands in their work early, on 1 March. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, by when should the marker's feedback be provided?
options: By 22 March, 3 weeks from the day the student actually submitted
By 15 March, one week after the unit's submission deadline
By 5 April, four weeks from the unit's submission deadline
By 29 March, 3 weeks from the unit's submission deadline
questions.explanation: The 3-week feedback timeframe runs from the submission deadline (8 March), not from the date the student handed in early, so feedback is due by 29 March.
questions.source_excerpt: Feedback from markers should be provided within 3 weeks from the submission deadline

questions.question: Student A passed a unit at the first attempt; Student B did not pass the same assessment. Both now want to submit improved work. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies?
options: Both may resubmit if the APB authorises it, with both of their grades capped at the pass mark
A may not resubmit to improve the grade; B may, if the APB authorises, capped at a pass
A may resubmit once to improve the grade; B must repeat the unit with full attendance and fees
Neither may resubmit; both must repeat the unit with full attendance and pay the relevant fees
questions.explanation: A student who passed at the first attempt may not resubmit to improve the grade, whereas a student who did not pass may have a resubmission at the APB's authorisation, using the same brief with the grade capped at the pass mark.
questions.source_excerpt: A student who has passed a unit in the first attempt is not allowed to submit the work again with the intention of improving the grade; ... a student may have a resubmission opportunity of that assessment should s/he not pass, at the authorisation of APB; ... the grade will be capped at the pass mark;

questions.question: A newly appointed lecturer who holds Advance HE accreditation is asked to act as an Internal Verifier next month. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies before they take on the role?
options: They must be trained to ensure they are competent in their IV role and responsibilities
Nothing further, as Advance HE accreditation already confirms competence to verify
Training is needed only if the External Examiner queries their verification decisions
They may verify straight away, provided the Programme Leader countersigns each decision
questions.explanation: Advance HE accreditation is given only as an example of professional development; separately, everyone involved in assessment processes, including Internal Verifiers, must be trained to ensure they are competent in their roles.
questions.source_excerpt: Those who are involved in the assessment processes [e.g. Assessor, Internal Verifiers (IV)] must be trained to ensure that they are competent to undertake their roles and responsibilities; ... Mechanisms for teaching staff to gain appropriate professional teaching qualifications and/or continuous professional development, for example, accreditation by Advance HE;

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy as something the unit handbook, distributed at enrolment, makes students fully aware of?
options: The Expected Answer Guidelines (EAGs)
The scheme of work for the unit
Any work experience requirement
Relevant reference books and journals
questions.explanation: The unit handbook covers learning outcomes, content, assessment strategies, scheme of work, any work experience requirement and reference materials; EAGs are provided separately by the Lecturer through the VLE.
questions.source_excerpt: the unit handbook is prepared and distributed to students at enrolment, so that students are fully aware of: a) Learning outcomes; b) Content of the unit(s); c) Assessment strategies; d) Scheme of work; e) Work experience requirement (if any); f) Relevant reference materials, books, and journals. ... The EAGs are made available through the VLE

questions.question: A tutor writes detailed comments on summative work but returns formative drafts marked only 'Seen'. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what is expected instead?
options: Nothing more, as the policy's feedback requirements apply only to summative assessment
Clear feedback on formative work as well, with clear guidance on how to improve
A formative grade for each draft, recorded and forwarded to the Assessment and Progression Board
A Turnitin similarity report for each draft, attached alongside the tutor's formative comments
questions.explanation: The policy calls for clear feedback on formative and summative work with clear guidance on how improvement can be achieved, so formative drafts also need meaningful feedback.
questions.source_excerpt: Provide clear feedback of formative and summative work with clear guidance on how improvement can be achieved;

questions.question: A lecturer writes a new contextualised essay each term and invites drafts for formative feedback, but always uses a written essay as the only assessment method. Which plagiarism-minimising measure in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy is still missing?
options: Producing contextualised assessments in each term
Requesting draft submissions for formative feedback
Applying different methods, such as an oral element
Setting an invigilated, timed examination in every unit
questions.explanation: The lecturer already contextualises assessments each term and requests drafts, but the policy also lists applying different assessment methods, including built-in oral elements such as presentations or debates.
questions.source_excerpt: Reducing the risk of students submitting work that is not their own, through the use of a built-in oral element in units ... Frequently designing new assessments and applying different assessment methods.

questions.question: Under the Professional Standards section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, which of these expectations is stated as applying to staff as well as to students?
options: Arriving to their classes on time
Notifying absence with mitigation
Harvard-referencing sourced material
Being told to raise concerns promptly
questions.explanation: The policy states that staff and students arrive to class on time; notifying non-attendance, referencing assessed work and being informed to raise concerns promptly are stated for students.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are encouraged and expected to attend all classes and as in the workplace staff must be informed of a non-attendance with mitigation; ... Staff and students arrive to class on time;

questions.question: A student has an ongoing health condition that affects their learning but is not a diagnosed specific learning need. Under the Student Support section of the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies?
options: Support is limited to students with a formally diagnosed specific learning need
Support is arranged only once a Mitigating Circumstances claim has been upheld
Other on-going needs which affect learning are also to be appropriately supported
The student is referred to the External Examiner, who decides on any adjustments
questions.explanation: The Student Support section covers students with specific learning needs or with other on-going needs which affect their learning, who are to be appropriately supported.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with specific learning needs or with other on-going needs which affect their learning are appropriately supported;

questions.question: While giving formative feedback on a student's draft, a tutor suggests the student runs two revised versions through Turnitin for similarity reports before making the final submission. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies?
options: Drafts are exempt from the Turnitin limit, so the reports can be obtained while formative feedback continues
Two reports are fine, as only the final report is ever used to judge an Academic Concern or Offence
Tutors should not review drafts before final submission, so the student should rely on Turnitin alone
Formative feedback on drafts is fine, but only one similarity report is available before final submission
questions.explanation: Tutors request drafts for formative feedback, but students can obtain only one similarity report prior to the final submission; the final-report rule does not lift that limit.
questions.source_excerpt: Tutors request students to present draft assignment submissions for formative feedback. ... Students can obtain one similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment.

questions.question: A student repeats one core unit and one optional/specialist unit and fails both. Under the reassessment guidance in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, which outcome correctly applies?
options: Both may be replaced by different units, with full attendance and payment of the relevant fees
The optional unit may be replaced by a different unit; the core unit may instead be compensated
The core unit may be replaced by a different unit; the optional unit may instead be compensated
Neither may be replaced or compensated, so the student cannot go on to achieve the qualification
questions.explanation: A failed repeated optional/specialist unit may be replaced by a different unit (with full attendance and fee), but a failed repeated core unit cannot be replaced, although compensation may be granted.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student repeats an optional/specialist unit and does not achieve a pass, the student may be allowed to complete a different unit ... if a student repeats a core unit and does not achieve a pass that cannot be replaced with a different unit, but the student may be granted a compensation.

questions.question: A new Assessor asks how the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy quality-assures assessment decisions, including those of the Assessment and Progression Board (APB), before they are confirmed. Which description matches the policy?
options: Every paper is internally verified; APB decisions are approved by the External Examiner, then verified by the Academic Board
A prescribed sample is verified by the External Examiner; the Internal Verifier then approves the APB's decisions
A prescribed sample is internally verified; the Academic Board verifies APB decisions, then the External Examiner approves them
A prescribed sample is internally verified; APB decisions are verified by the External Examiner, then approved by the Academic Board
questions.explanation: A prescribed sample of summative papers must be internally verified, and all APB decisions must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval.
questions.source_excerpt: A prescribed sample of summative assessment papers must be internally verified using the correct form and procedure; ... All assessment decisions by the Assessment and Progression Board must be verified by the External Examiner and forwarded to the Academic Board for approval

questions.question: A student repeats a core unit and does not achieve a pass. The programme team propose granting compensation on their own judgement. Under the reassessment guidance in the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies?
options: Compensation may be granted, but the APB must follow the compensation regulation in the Pearson BTEC guide
Compensation is not available; the student must instead complete a different unit with full attendance and fees
The programme team may grant it, as compensating a failed core unit is left to the team's academic judgement
The Academic Board may grant it directly, without applying any awarding body's compensation rules
questions.explanation: A failed repeated core unit cannot be replaced with a different unit, but compensation may be granted; when it is, the APB must follow the compensation regulation in the Pearson BTEC Centre Guide.
questions.source_excerpt: if a student repeats a core unit and does not achieve a pass that cannot be replaced with a different unit, but the student may be granted a compensation. In respect of compensation being granted, the APB must follow the compensation regulation stated in the Pearson BTEC Centre Guide to Quality Assurance and Assessment

questions.question: A colleague argues that a reasonable adjustment for a disabled student would breach the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy's aim that assessment must not advantage any group or individual. What does the policy actually provide?
options: Reasonable adjustments are limited to formative tasks, so that summative assessment stays identical for every student
Reasonable adjustments need the External Examiner's prior confirmation that they give the student no advantage
Reasonable adjustments are to be made available to students with disabilities and additional needs
Reasonable adjustments follow only from an upheld Mitigating Circumstances claim, not a disability
questions.explanation: Alongside the aim that assessment does not advantage or disadvantage any group, the Assessment section expressly requires reasonable adjustments to be made available to students with disabilities and additional needs.
questions.source_excerpt: Assessment methodology is valid, reliable and does not advantage or ... disadvantage any group of learners or individuals; ... Reasonable adjustments are made available to students with disabilities and additional needs.

questions.question: While giving formative feedback, a tutor sees a student's pre-submission Turnitin similarity report showing extensive unreferenced matching text. The report on the revised final submission is clean. Under the Learning, Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy, what applies to the earlier report?
options: It can support an Academic Offence finding, as any report showing unreferenced matching text is valid evidence
It cannot support an Offence finding, but it can still be used on its own to record an Academic Concern against them
It can be used, provided the tutor refers it under the Academic Misconduct Policy within 3 weeks of the deadline
It cannot be used to find misconduct, as only the final report determines any Academic Concern or Offence
questions.explanation: Students may obtain one similarity report before final submission, but only the final report is used to determine whether an Academic Concern or Offence has been committed.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can obtain one similarity report prior to the final submission for each assessment. ... Only the final report will be used to determine if any Academic Concern or Offence has been committed, in line with the Academic Misconduct Policy.

policies.title: Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy

questions.question: You are a Personal Tutor. In week 3 of the semester you find that a tutee has not submitted any assignments and is at risk of non-completion. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, what must you do?
options: Add an intervention note to their ILP and report the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM by week 6 of the semester
Record the concern and report it to the Assessment and Progression Board once the semester's results are confirmed
Ask Registry to start withdrawing the student on academic grounds straight away, citing their current RBA score
Log the concern on the student's SMS profile and report it to Student Services and the Academic Board by week 10
questions.explanation: The policy requires Personal Tutors to include an intervention note in the ILP and report the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM on or before the 6th week of the current semester.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors will include an intervention note in the ILP and report the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM on or before the 6th week of the current semester;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what minimum attendance rate per semester must a student meet (absent valid reasons) to avoid being defined as at risk of non-continuation or non-completion?
options: 50% in a semester
75% in a semester
60% in a semester
80% in a semester
questions.explanation: The policy defines students at risk of non-continuation or non-completion as including those not meeting the minimum attendance threshold of 60% in a semester without valid reasons of absence.
questions.source_excerpt: Not meeting the minimum threshold of attendance rate (i.e., minimum 60 % in a semester) without valid reasons of absence and/or;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which of the following is NOT one of the criteria defining a student at risk of non-continuation or non-completion?
options: Attendance below the minimum threshold in a semester without valid reasons for absence
Not submitting assignments, or failing to reach the pass mark on them
Not meeting the awarding body's credit requirements to progress to the next academic year
Coming from a lower socio-economic background or a low-income household
questions.explanation: Lower socio-economic background is listed under the definition of students at risk of non-progression, not non-continuation or non-completion; the other three are the non-continuation/non-completion criteria.
questions.source_excerpt: Students facing the risk of non-progression are defined by the OfS as including but not limited to: 5.4.1.1. Students who are from lower socio-economic backgrounds, including low-income households or areas with historically low participation in higher education;

questions.question: A tutee tells you a family crisis has affected their recent assessments and they want to make a mitigating circumstances claim. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, what is your role as their Personal Tutor?
options: Decide the mitigating circumstances claim yourself, then inform the module leader and Course Coordinator
Refer the student, as appropriate, to the relevant department within the College
Tell the student to raise it through the End of Term Survey so it can be reviewed centrally
Extend the assessment deadline yourself and record the new date on their IALP
questions.explanation: The policy makes Personal Tutors responsible for referring students, as appropriate, to other departments, citing mitigating circumstances claims as an example.
questions.source_excerpt: Referring students, as appropriate, to other departments within the College. Such referrals may relate, for example, to mitigating circumstances claims, disability, and emotional support;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, where must a Personal Tutor maintain a log of their contacts with students?
options: In the student's End of Term Survey record
In the Assessment and Progression Board minutes
In the RBA Scheme report
On the Personal Tutor Tracking Sheet
questions.explanation: One of the Personal Tutor's responsibilities is maintaining a log of contacts with students on the "Personal Tutor Tracking Sheet".
questions.source_excerpt: Maintaining a log of contacts with students on the "Personal Tutor Tracking Sheet" and developing Individual Assessment Learning Plans (IALP) together with students;

questions.question: A new tutee asks when they can see you one-to-one during term. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what should you tell them?
options: One-to-one meetings are held during the induction programme and afterwards on request via Student Services
They may book one one-to-one meeting per semester by contacting their Course Coordinator
Every teaching week has a timetabled session for a one-to-one meeting with their tutor
One-to-one meetings are arranged once the RBA Scheme has flagged the student as at risk
questions.explanation: The policy states all timetables include a session allocated for each teaching week in which students can attend a one-to-one meeting with their personal tutor.
questions.source_excerpt: All timetables include a session allocated for each teaching week, in which students can attend a one-to-one meeting with their individual personal tutor;

questions.question: According to the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what are students' Risk-Based Approach (RBA) scores based on?
options: Their module marks for the year and the feedback ratings given by their Personal Tutor
Their attendance percentage and the units completed compared with the units required
Their End of Term Survey responses and the notes on their Personal Tutor Tracking Sheet
Their entry qualifications and the number of assignments they have submitted late
questions.explanation: The policy states RBA scores are based on attendance percentage and on how many units a student has completed compared with how many they were required to complete across the academic year.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will receive RBA scores which are based on their attendance percentage, and on how many units they have completed in comparison to how many they were required to complete, across the academic year;

questions.question: According to the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, who supervises the College's Personal Tutors?
options: The Director of Student Services for each campus
The Academic Board at its termly meetings
The Quality Assurance Department's tutoring lead
The Course Coordinators for each programme
questions.explanation: The policy states that Personal Tutors are supervised by the Course Coordinators for each programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors are supervised by the Course Coordinators for each of the programme;

questions.question: According to the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which of the following is an intervention Personal Tutors can use to reduce a student's risk of non-progression?
options: Automatically enrolling the student onto a postgraduate course at the College on completion
Reducing the credit requirements the student must meet to progress to the next year
Reaching out to the Alumni Association to find LCC alumni willing to give advice or guidance
Guaranteeing the student a paid work placement through the College's employers
questions.explanation: The policy lists reaching out to the Alumni Association to identify LCC alumni willing to provide advice or guidance as a non-progression intervention.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors can reach out to the Alumni Association to identify if any LCC Alumni would be willing to provide any advice or guidance for students at the College;

questions.question: An applicant to LCC wants to claim credit for learning completed on a previous course. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, what is the Personal Tutor's role?
options: Guiding the applicant through the process of applying for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
Awarding the credit directly after reviewing the applicant's transcripts and module descriptors
Redirecting the applicant to the awarding body, as RPL claims fall outside the College's remit
Advising that prior learning cannot be considered until the applicant has fully enrolled
questions.explanation: The policy lists guiding applicants and students through the process of making applications for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) as a Personal Tutor responsibility.
questions.source_excerpt: Guiding applicants and students through the process of making applications for the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, besides identifying students at risk, what else is the Risk-Based Approach (RBA) Scheme used for?
options: Setting the tuition fee levels charged for each programme in the following academic year
Measuring the performance of each Personal Tutor against an RBA target score
Allocating applicants to programmes and study modes at the point of admission
Deciding which students qualify for College bursaries based on their RBA scores
questions.explanation: The policy states the RBA Scheme will also be used to measure the performance of each Personal Tutor, with each Personal Tutor receiving an RBA target score.
questions.source_excerpt: This scheme will further be used to measure the performance of each Personal Tutor at the College, with each Personal Tutor receiving a RBA target score.

questions.question: One of your personal tutees is studying on a Health and Social Care programme. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, what additional responsibility do you have specifically for students on these programmes?
options: Monitoring the progression of the student's work experience
Approving the student's clinical practice timesheets every week
Verifying the student's DBS check renewal each semester
Reporting the student's placement hours directly to the awarding body
questions.explanation: The policy states that for students on Health and Social Care programmes, Personal Tutors should ensure they monitor the progression of work experience.
questions.source_excerpt: With respect to students studying on Health and Social Care programmes Personal Tutors should ensure that they monitor the progression of work experience;

questions.question: According to the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what type of support does the personal tutoring system provide to help students achieve their potential?
options: Academic support only, with pastoral matters referred to Student Services
Both academic and pastoral support within the study environment
Pastoral support only, with academic matters left to module lecturers
Careers and financial support, with academic matters left to lecturers
questions.explanation: The policy states that the personal tutoring system provides both academic and pastoral support to help students achieve their potential within the study environment.
questions.source_excerpt: The personal tutoring system provides both academic and pastoral support to help students achieve their potential within the study environment.

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, who acts as each student's designated Personal Tutor?
options: A professional services adviser with training in student wellbeing
A student ambassador from a later year of the same programme
An external mentor appointed by the awarding body for the programme
An academic member of staff who has training in mentorship
questions.explanation: The policy states that every student has access to a designated Personal Tutor, who is an academic with training in mentorship.
questions.source_excerpt: All students have access to a designated Personal Tutor, who is an academic with training in mentorship;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what is the minimum number of personal tutors the College has for each programme?
options: One per programme
Two per programme
Three per programme
Four per programme
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College has a minimum of two personal tutors per programme, with more recruited if student numbers rise to a certain threshold.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has a minimum of two personal tutors per programme

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, who has oversight of the effectiveness of the College's personal tutoring system?
options: The Head of Quality Assurance and Academic Standards (HoQAS)
The Head of Student Services and Wellbeing (HoSSW)
The Head of Programmes & Academic Monitoring (HoPAM)
The Director of Learning, Teaching and Enhancement
questions.explanation: The policy gives the Head of Programmes & Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) oversight of the effectiveness of the personal tutoring system.
questions.source_excerpt: The Head of Programmes & Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) will have an oversight of the effectiveness of the personal tutoring system.

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which of these is listed as a Personal Tutor responsibility towards prospective students?
options: Issuing conditional and unconditional offers to prospective students
Checking prospective students' identity and immigration documents
Agreeing tuition fee payment plans with prospective students
Conducting academic interviews for prospective students
questions.explanation: Conducting academic interviews for prospective students is listed among the Personal Tutor's roles and responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: Conducting academic interviews for prospective students.

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, against what does a Personal Tutor monitor and record each student's progress?
options: The student's Individual Assessment Learning Plan (IALP)
The awarding body's unit specifications and grading criteria
The programme specification and module handbook for the course
The attendance register kept by the Course Coordinator
questions.explanation: One of the Personal Tutor's responsibilities is monitoring and recording individual student progress against the IALP.
questions.source_excerpt: Monitoring and recording individual student progress against the IALP;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what are students advised to do so that they can maintain contact with their Personal Tutor?
options: Email their Course Coordinator if their contact details change
Register a contact number with the Student Services helpdesk
Keep the contact details on their SMS student profile up to date
Submit a change-of-details form to the Registry each term
questions.explanation: Students are advised to provide updated contact details on their student profile on the Student Management System (SMS) so they can maintain contact with their Personal Tutor.
questions.source_excerpt: To maintain contact with their Personal Tutor, students are advised to provide updated contact details on their student profile on the Student Management System (SMS);

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, how can students give feedback on the performance of their Personal Tutor?
options: By completing the Graduate Outcomes Survey
By completing the College's End of Term Survey
By adding comments to the Personal Tutor Tracking Sheet
By completing the annual RBA feedback questionnaire
questions.explanation: The policy states that students can provide feedback on their Personal Tutor's performance by completing the End of Term Survey.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can provide feedback on the performance of their respective Personal Tutor by completing the End of Term Survey.

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, why are care-experienced students, estranged students and young carers identified as being at risk of non-progression?
options: They are more likely to have joined with credit awarded through RPL
They are classed as overseas students for fee and visa purposes
They have previously been withdrawn from study on academic grounds
They lack traditional support networks, such as financial safety networks
questions.explanation: The policy groups care-experienced students, estranged students and young carers as students who lack traditional support networks, often including secure financial safety networks.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who lack traditional support networks, these include careexperienced students, estranged students, and young carers. These students often lack secure financial safety networks and professional networks

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which survey should Personal Tutors encourage students to take part in, so the College can identify practices that helped students progress to further study or employment?
options: The Graduate Outcomes Survey organised by HESA
The National Student Survey organised by the OfS
The Destinations Review run by the Alumni Association
The Employability Skills Audit run by the awarding body
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors should encourage students to take part in the Graduate Outcomes Survey, organised by HESA, so the College can identify practices that helped students progress after their studies.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors should encourage students to participate in the Graduate Outcomes Survey, which is organised by the Higher Education ... Statistical Agency (HESA), allowing for the College to identify practises that helped students progress to further study or employment after the completion of their studies at the College.

questions.question: According to the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, in which decision may a student's Risk-Based Approach (RBA) score be considered?
options: Calculating the student's final award classification
Deciding whether the student qualifies for a fee refund
Withdrawing the student from study on academic grounds
Allocating the student a Personal Tutor at induction
questions.explanation: The policy states that a student's RBA score may be considered when withdrawing a student on academic grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: A student's RBA score may be considered when withdrawing a student on academic grounds;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, to which body does the Course Coordinator provide an update on actions for students at risk of non-continuation or non-completion?
options: The Academic Standards Committee
The Assessment and Progression Board
The Quality and Enhancement Committee
The Student Experience and Welfare Committee
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Course Coordinator will notify the actions for students at risk of non-continuation or non-completion and provide an update to the Assessment and Progression Board.
questions.source_excerpt: The Course Coordinator will notify the actions for students at risk of non-continuation or noncompletion, and provide an update to the Assessment and Progression Board.

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which example of support does the policy give for Personal Tutors helping students understand the requirements of assignment briefs?
options: Providing English language advice
Proofreading students' draft work
Granting assignment deadline extensions
Pre-marking drafts against the criteria
questions.explanation: The policy lists assisting students in understanding assignment brief requirements and providing support, such as English language advice, as a Personal Tutor responsibility.
questions.source_excerpt: Assisting students in understanding the requirements of the assignment briefs and providing support, such as English language advice;

questions.question: A new lecturer asks why every LCC student is given a named Personal Tutor. According to the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which College commitment does this arrangement support?
options: Meeting the awarding body's minimum staff-to-student ratio on every programme it validates
Supporting greater access to education for those who might otherwise not realise their potential
Reducing the College's reliance on external counselling and student welfare services
Achieving the attendance targets set for each programme under the Risk-Based Approach (RBA) Scheme
questions.explanation: The policy's aim is to give every student named Personal Tutors in order to comply with the College's commitment to supporting greater access to education for students who might otherwise not realise their full potential.
questions.source_excerpt: The aim of this policy is to provide every student with an opportunity to seek academic advice, support and guidance from named individual Personal Tutors, in order to comply with London Churchill College's (LLC) commitment to supporting greater opportunities for access to education for students who might otherwise not realise their full potential;

questions.question: You are running an introductory personal tutorial during induction week. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what are these introductory tutorials intended to do?
options: Agree each student's IALP targets and record a baseline RBA score for the academic year
Check students' entry qualifications and confirm any credit to be awarded through RPL
Introduce students to their tutor early and ease their move from prospective to current student
Allocate students to their modules and book a one-to-one slot for every teaching week
questions.explanation: Introductory personal tutorials are part of induction so that students meet their tutor as early as possible and to help a smooth transition from "prospective" to "current" student status.
questions.source_excerpt: Introductory personal tutorials are included as part of the induction programme to introduce students to their tutor as early as possible and to help facilitate a smooth transition from "prospective" to "current" student status;

questions.question: Mid-semester, a tutee's results suggest they are at risk of academic failure. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what does the policy say about how often they should meet their Personal Tutor?
options: They should keep to the standard weekly slot so that every tutee receives equal time
They should pause tutorials until the Course Coordinator has reviewed their case
They are encouraged to meet their tutor more regularly to improve their performance
They should meet their tutor once more, at semester end, to review their final results
questions.explanation: The policy states that students deemed at risk of academic failure are encouraged to meet their personal tutors more regularly to improve their academic performance.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who are deemed to be at risk of academic failure are encouraged to meet their personal tutors more regularly to improve their academic performance;

questions.question: Student numbers on one LCC programme have risen sharply. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what does the policy provide for the number of personal tutors on that programme?
options: Existing tutors take larger caseloads, as the number of tutors is fixed at two per programme
More tutors may be recruited once numbers reach a certain threshold, above the minimum of two
The additional students are allocated to Student Services advisers until the next academic year
The Course Coordinator acts as Personal Tutor for any students above the usual caseload
questions.explanation: The policy sets a minimum of two personal tutors per programme, with the possibility of recruiting more if student numbers increase to a certain threshold.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has a minimum of two personal tutors per programme, with the possibility of more personal tutors being recruited if student numbers increase to a certain threshold in a programme;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, how are responsibilities for personal tutoring divided between the Course Coordinators and the Head of Programmes & Academic Monitoring (HoPAM)?
options: The HoPAM supervises Personal Tutors; Course Coordinators oversee the system's effectiveness
Course Coordinators allocate tutees; the HoPAM sets each Personal Tutor's weekly timetable
Both jointly supervise Personal Tutors, while the Academic Board reviews overall effectiveness
Course Coordinators supervise Personal Tutors; the HoPAM oversees the system's effectiveness
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors are supervised by the Course Coordinators for each programme, while the HoPAM has oversight of the effectiveness of the personal tutoring system.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors are supervised by the Course Coordinators for each of the programme; ... The Head of Programmes & Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) will have an oversight of the effectiveness of the personal tutoring system.

questions.question: A tutee is struggling to balance deadlines across several modules and has stopped taking part in College activities. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which Personal Tutor responsibility applies?
options: Providing cross-module guidance and support, and encouraging full participation in College life
Referring them to each module leader, as tutors advise only on the modules they teach
Recording the concern for the End of Term Survey so that it can be reviewed centrally
Reporting them to the HoPAM as being at risk of termination for insufficient progress
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors provide cross-module guidance and support so students can progress, and encourage their full participation in all that the College has to offer.
questions.source_excerpt: Providing cross-module guidance and support to allow students to progress through their studies and encouraging their full participation in all that the College has to offer;

questions.question: A new Personal Tutor plans to write each tutee's Individual Assessment Learning Plan (IALP) alone and email it to them. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, how should IALPs be developed and used?
options: By the Course Coordinator, with the tutor adding comments at the end of each semester
By the tutor alone, then approved by the HoPAM before being shared with the student
By the student alone, then signed off by the tutor at their next one-to-one meeting
Together with the student, with the tutor then monitoring and recording progress against it
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors develop IALPs together with students and then monitor and record each student's progress against the IALP.
questions.source_excerpt: developing Individual Assessment Learning Plans (IALP) together with students; 3.5. Monitoring and recording individual student progress against the IALP;

questions.question: One of your tutees has been identified as "at risk of termination" for insufficient progress. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what is your responsibility as their Personal Tutor?
options: Work with other departments to monitor and support the student
Stop the student's tutorials until a termination decision is made
Issue the student a final written warning on the College's behalf
Transfer the student to a different tutor to give them a fresh start
questions.explanation: The policy makes Personal Tutors responsible for working with other departments to monitor and support students identified as "at risk of termination" for insufficient progress.
questions.source_excerpt: Working with other departments to monitor and support students who have been ... identified as "at risk of termination" for insufficient progress;

questions.question: A tutee tells you they skip personal tutorials because they already attend every lecture. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what is expected of students?
options: Tutorials are optional provided their attendance stays above the 60% threshold
They should attend all tutorial sessions and actively take part in all lectures
They need attend only the introductory tutorials held in the induction programme
They must attend tutorials only once the RBA Scheme has flagged them as at risk
questions.explanation: Students should ensure they attend all tutorial sessions and are active participants in all lectures and learning and teaching events.
questions.source_excerpt: Students should ensure that they attend all tutorial sessions and should be an active participant in all lectures and learning and teaching events;

questions.question: A tutee has started a full-time job that is cutting into their study time. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, what is the student expected to do?
options: Record the change in the End of Term Survey when the term finishes
Inform the Assessment and Progression Board before their next exam
Wait for their tutor to raise it at the next weekly one-to-one slot
Inform their Personal Tutor promptly of the relevant change
questions.explanation: Students are expected to inform their Personal Tutor promptly of any relevant changes in their educational or personal circumstances.
questions.source_excerpt: It is expected that students will inform their Personal Tutor promptly of any relevant changes in their educational or personal circumstances;
