questions.question: A tutee's attendance this semester is 52% with no valid reasons for absence, but all their assignments are submitted and passed. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, how are they defined?
options: Not at risk, as the attendance criterion only applies alongside missed assignments
Not at risk, as the minimum attendance threshold is 50% in a semester
At risk of non-continuation or non-completion, being below the 60% minimum
At risk of non-progression, as defined by the OfS for low-attendance students
questions.explanation: The criteria are joined by "and/or", so attendance below the 60% minimum without valid reasons is enough on its own to define a student as at risk of non-continuation or non-completion.
questions.source_excerpt: Students facing the risk of non-continuation or non-completion are defined as: 5.2.1.1. Not meeting the minimum threshold of attendance rate (i.e., minimum 60 % in a semester) without valid reasons of absence and/or;

questions.question: A tutee failed to submit two assignments last semester but has submitted all work so far this semester. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy's definition, are they at risk of non-continuation or non-completion?
options: No, because only non-submission in the current semester counts towards the definition
Yes, because non-submission in the current or previous semesters falls within the definition
No, because non-submission counts only if their attendance is also below the 60% minimum
Only if the Assessment and Progression Board confirms that the missed work was not mitigated
questions.explanation: The definition covers students not submitting assignments in the current or previous semesters, so last semester's non-submission still places the tutee within it.
questions.source_excerpt: Not submitting assignments in the current or previous semesters or unable to achieve pass mark on submitted assignments and/or;

questions.question: A tutee is a mature student who meets every attendance and assessment requirement. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which risk definition may still apply to them?
options: Non-continuation, because mature students are listed alongside the attendance criteria
Non-completion, because RBA scores are automatically lowered for mature students
None, as the policy's risk definitions relate only to attendance and assessment results
Non-progression, because the OfS definition includes mature students as a group
questions.explanation: The OfS-based definition of students at risk of non-progression includes students with a specific personal or protected characteristic, which explicitly includes mature students.
questions.source_excerpt: Students facing the risk of non-progression are defined by the OfS as including but not limited to: ... Students who are characterised or identify with a specific personal or protected characteristic. This includes mature students,

questions.question: A final-year tutee from a low-income household wants help presenting their skills to employers. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy's interventions for students at risk of non-progression, what can you offer?
options: Advice and skills around CV writing and job applications
A guaranteed interview with one of the College's employer partners
Writing and submitting their job applications on their behalf
A reference from the Alumni Association confirming their grades
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors can offer advice and skills around CV writing and job applications so students can articulate their technical proficiency and professional skills.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can be offered advice and skills around CV writing and job applications by Personal Tutors to articulate their technical proficiency and professional skills to see where students meet graduate level standards for future work or further study;

questions.question: A colleague thinks the Risk-Based Approach (RBA) Scheme only monitors students in their final year. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, over what period does it monitor student progress?
options: Only in semesters where the student's attendance falls below 60%
From the first Assessment and Progression Board to the final award
Continuously, from the start of their studies until they leave the College
At the end of each academic year, once all unit results are confirmed
questions.explanation: The RBA Scheme identifies students at risk of non-continuation or non-completion by monitoring their progress continuously from the start of their studies until they leave the College.
questions.source_excerpt: The purpose of this scheme is to identify students who are at risk of noncontinuation or non-completion by monitoring student progress continuously from the start of their studies until they leave the College;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which sequence correctly describes how a student at risk of non-continuation or non-completion is escalated?
options: Tutor adds an ILP intervention note and reports it; the Course Coordinator updates the Assessment and Progression Board
Tutor emails the student a formal written warning; the Academic Board then reviews the case at its next scheduled meeting
The RBA Scheme flags the student; the HoPAM then notifies the student directly and informs the awarding body
Tutor records it on the Tracking Sheet; Student Services decides on withdrawal after the semester ends
questions.explanation: The Personal Tutor includes an intervention note in the ILP and reports the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM; the Course Coordinator then notifies the actions and updates the Assessment and Progression Board.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors will include an intervention note in the ILP and report the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM on or before the 6th week of the current semester; ... The Course Coordinator will notify the actions for students at risk of non-continuation or noncompletion, and provide an update to the Assessment and Progression Board.

questions.question: A tutee's attendance this semester is 55% because of a documented hospital stay, which the College has accepted as a valid reason for absence. All their assignments are submitted and passed. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, does the attendance criterion place them at risk of non-continuation or non-completion?
options: Yes, because any attendance below 60% in a semester meets the definition regardless of reason
No, because the 60% threshold applies only where absence is without valid reasons
Yes, but only once their RBA score has been reviewed by the Course Coordinator
No, because the attendance threshold for a semester is set at 50%, not 60%
questions.explanation: The attendance criterion is not meeting the 60% minimum in a semester without valid reasons of absence, so a shortfall caused by documented valid reasons does not meet it.
questions.source_excerpt: Not meeting the minimum threshold of attendance rate (i.e., minimum 60 % in a semester) without valid reasons of absence and/or;

questions.question: A tutee attends 90% of sessions and has passed every submitted assignment, but will not meet the awarding body's credit requirements to move into the next academic year. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which risk definition applies?
options: Non-progression, as the OfS defines it by a student's inability to move into the next year
None, as their attendance and assignment results both meet the policy's thresholds
Non-progression, but only if they also come from a lower socio-economic background
Non-continuation or non-completion, as the credit criterion is part of that definition
questions.explanation: Not meeting the awarding body's credit requirements to progress to the following academic year is one of the non-continuation or non-completion criteria; the non-progression definition concerns OfS-listed student groups.
questions.source_excerpt: Students facing the risk of non-continuation or non-completion are defined as: ... Not meeting the credit requirements of the awarding body to progress from the current to the following academic year.

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which of these tutees falls within the definition of a student at risk of non-continuation or non-completion?
options: One with 85% attendance who submits every assignment but fails to reach the pass mark
One with 70% attendance who submitted every assignment late but passed them all
One who is a young carer, with 92% attendance and all assignments passed so far
One from a low-income household who has met every attendance and credit requirement
questions.explanation: Being unable to achieve the pass mark on submitted assignments is a non-continuation or non-completion criterion even with good attendance; young carers and low-income students appear only in the non-progression definition.
questions.source_excerpt: Not submitting assignments in the current or previous semesters or unable to achieve pass mark on submitted assignments and/or;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which of the following is not one of the interventions Personal Tutors can enact for a student at risk of non-continuation or non-completion?
options: Updating the student's Individual Assessment and Learning Plan (ILP)
Including an intervention note in the ILP and reporting the risk
Recommending withdrawal on academic grounds based on the RBA score
Offering the student additional support, if it is required
questions.explanation: The listed interventions are updating the ILP, adding an intervention note and reporting the risk, and offering additional support if required; the RBA score is only something that may be considered when withdrawing a student.
questions.source_excerpt: The Personal Tutor will update the respective Individual Assessment and Learning Plan (ILP); ... Personal Tutors will include an intervention note in the ILP and report the risk ... As a part of the intervention process the Personal Tutor will offer additional support, if required.

questions.question: In week 5, a Personal Tutor adds an intervention note to an at-risk tutee's ILP and reports the risk to the HoPAM, but not to the Course Coordinator. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, has the reporting requirement been met?
options: No, as the report must go to the Course Coordinator, who alone escalates it to the HoPAM
No, as the report must go jointly to the Assessment and Progression Board
Yes, as the risk may go to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM by the 6th week
No, as reports are only accepted after the semester's final attendance data is available
questions.explanation: The policy requires the risk to be reported to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM on or before the 6th week, so reporting to the HoPAM alone in week 5 meets it.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors will include an intervention note in the ILP and report the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM on or before the 6th week of the current semester;

questions.question: A colleague says the Risk-Based Approach (RBA) Scheme exists to identify students at risk of non-progression, such as young carers. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, what is the scheme's stated purpose?
options: Identifying students at risk of non-continuation or non-completion by monitoring progress
Identifying students at risk of non-progression using the OfS characteristics listed
Identifying students eligible for RPL credit by comparing units completed with those required
Identifying applicants likely to withdraw before enrolment, using academic interviews
questions.explanation: The RBA Scheme's stated purpose is to identify students at risk of non-continuation or non-completion by monitoring their progress continuously; non-progression risk is defined separately by OfS groups.
questions.source_excerpt: The purpose of this scheme is to identify students who are at risk of noncontinuation or non-completion by monitoring student progress continuously from the start of their studies until they leave the College;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which two mechanisms bear on how a Personal Tutor's performance is assessed?
options: Graduate Outcomes Survey results and a HoPAM audit of each tutor's Tracking Sheet
Assessment and Progression Board reviews and the IALP completion rate of each tutee
Termly lesson observations by the Course Coordinator and the National Student Survey
Student feedback in the End of Term Survey and an RBA target score per tutor
questions.explanation: Students give feedback on their Personal Tutor's performance through the End of Term Survey, and the RBA Scheme measures each tutor's performance against an RBA target score.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can provide feedback on the performance of their respective Personal Tutor by completing the End of Term Survey. ... This scheme will further be used to measure the performance of each Personal Tutor at the College, with each Personal Tutor receiving a RBA target score.

questions.question: A tutee has a very low Risk-Based Approach (RBA) score and a colleague says the policy requires the student to be withdrawn. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, what is the correct position?
options: Withdrawal is mandatory once a student's RBA score falls below their tutor's RBA target
The score may be considered when a withdrawal on academic grounds is decided
RBA scores are used only to measure tutors, so they play no part in withdrawal decisions
The student must first be referred to HESA, which decides on withdrawal using the RBA score
questions.explanation: The policy says only that a student's RBA score may be considered when withdrawing a student on academic grounds; it does not make withdrawal mandatory.
questions.source_excerpt: A student's RBA score may be considered when withdrawing a student on academic grounds;

questions.question: A tutee discloses a disability and also says they cannot understand what an assignment brief requires. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which combination of actions falls within your role as their Personal Tutor?
options: Assess their disability yourself and rewrite the brief in simpler terms for the whole cohort
Grant reasonable adjustments yourself and refer the brief to the module's external examiner
Record both issues on the End of Term Survey so the Course Coordinator can act on them
Refer them, as appropriate, to the relevant department and help them understand the brief
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors assist students in understanding assignment brief requirements and refer students, as appropriate, to other departments, with disability given as an example.
questions.source_excerpt: Assisting students in understanding the requirements of the assignment briefs and providing support, such as English language advice; ... Referring students, as appropriate, to other departments within the College. Such referrals may relate, for example, to mitigating circumstances claims, disability, and emotional support;

questions.question: A second-year student who is already enrolled asks their Personal Tutor about claiming Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL). Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, what applies?
options: The tutor guides both applicants and current students through the RPL application process
RPL guidance is for applicants only, so the tutor must redirect them to the awarding body
The tutor decides the claim and records any credit awarded on the student's IALP
RPL cannot be claimed after enrolment, so the tutor should decline the request outright
questions.explanation: The policy makes Personal Tutors responsible for guiding both applicants and students through the process of making RPL applications.
questions.source_excerpt: Guiding applicants and students through the process of making applications for the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which pair of Personal Tutor responsibilities can involve people who have not yet enrolled at the College?
options: Maintaining the Tracking Sheet log and developing each person's IALP with them
Monitoring work experience and reporting risk to the HoPAM by the 6th week
Conducting academic interviews and guiding applicants through RPL applications
Issuing offers of study and verifying entry qualifications for each applicant
questions.explanation: The policy lists conducting academic interviews for prospective students and guiding applicants through RPL applications as Personal Tutor responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: Guiding applicants and students through the process of making applications for the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) ... Conducting academic interviews for prospective students.

questions.question: A Personal Tutor cannot reach a tutee who moved house and got a new phone number weeks ago without telling anyone. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which student responsibilities has the tutee failed to meet?
options: Registering with Student Services and completing the End of Term Survey on time
Updating contact details on their SMS profile and promptly informing their tutor of changes
Attending the induction tutorials and agreeing a new IALP with the Course Coordinator
Notifying the Assessment and Progression Board and the Alumni Association in writing
questions.explanation: Students are advised to keep their contact details updated on their SMS profile and are expected to inform their Personal Tutor promptly of relevant changes in their circumstances.
questions.source_excerpt: To maintain contact with their Personal Tutor, students are advised to provide updated contact details on their student profile on the Student Management System (SMS); ... It is expected that students will inform their Personal Tutor promptly of any relevant changes in their educational or personal circumstances;

questions.question: A colleague argues that a tutee cannot be treated as at risk of non-progression unless they belong to one of the groups the Personal Tutoring Policy lists. What is the position under the policy?
options: Correct, as only the four listed groups are recognised by the OfS for non-progression
Correct, unless the Course Coordinator adds the student to the RBA Scheme's at-risk list
Incorrect, as non-progression risk is judged solely on the student's current RBA score
Incorrect, as the OfS definition includes, but is not limited to, the listed groups
questions.explanation: The policy states that students at risk of non-progression are defined by the OfS as including but not limited to the listed groups, so the list is not exhaustive.
questions.source_excerpt: Students facing the risk of non-progression are defined by the OfS as including but not limited to:

questions.question: A programme needs another designated Personal Tutor. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which candidate matches how the policy describes a Personal Tutor?
options: An academic on the programme who has completed training in mentorship
A Student Services wellbeing adviser who has completed mentorship training
A newly appointed lecturer who has not yet received any mentorship training
A final-year student on the programme who has been trained as a peer mentor
questions.explanation: The policy describes each designated Personal Tutor as an academic with training in mentorship, so both conditions must be met.
questions.source_excerpt: All students have access to a designated Personal Tutor, who is an academic with training in mentorship;

questions.question: A new Personal Tutor believes that identifying at-risk students is the job of the Risk-Based Approach (RBA) Scheme, not theirs. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, what is their responsibility?
options: To intervene only after the RBA Scheme has formally flagged a student as being at risk
To identify non-progression risk only, as the RBA Scheme covers all other types of case
To identify and intervene in any case of non-continuation, non-completion or non-progression
To pass all concerns to the Course Coordinator, who identifies and intervenes in every case
questions.explanation: The policy makes Personal Tutors responsible for identifying and intervening in any case where students are at risk of non-continuation, non-completion or non-progression.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors are responsible for identifying and intervening in any case where students are at risk of non-continuation, non-completion or nonprogression.

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which intervention is correctly matched to the type of student risk it is listed under?
options: Updating the student's ILP: risk of non-progression
Contacting the Alumni Association: risk of non-progression
Encouraging the Graduate Outcomes Survey: risk of non-completion
Reporting the risk to the HoPAM by week 6: risk of non-progression
questions.explanation: Reaching out to the Alumni Association is listed among the interventions for students at risk of non-progression; ILP updates and week 6 reporting are non-continuation or non-completion interventions, and the Graduate Outcomes Survey is a non-progression one.
questions.source_excerpt: Interventions for Students at Risk of Non-Progression; ... Personal Tutors can reach out to the Alumni Association to identify if any LCC Alumni would be willing to provide any advice or guidance for students at the College;

questions.question: Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, which pair of roles does the policy give to the Head of Programmes & Academic Monitoring (HoPAM)?
options: Supervising Personal Tutors and updating the Assessment and Progression Board
Conducting academic interviews and approving Recognition of Prior Learning claims
Supervising Personal Tutors and running the End of Term Survey on tutor performance
Overseeing the tutoring system's effectiveness and receiving tutors' at-risk reports
questions.explanation: The HoPAM has oversight of the effectiveness of the personal tutoring system and is one of those to whom Personal Tutors report risk; supervising tutors and updating the Assessment and Progression Board fall to Course Coordinators.
questions.source_excerpt: The Head of Programmes & Academic Monitoring (HoPAM) will have an oversight of the effectiveness of the personal tutoring system. ... report the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM on or before the 6th week of the current semester;

questions.question: A tutee raises a personal matter that is affecting their studies, and their Personal Tutor replies that tutoring covers academic issues only. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, why is this response wrong?
options: Tutoring gives academic and pastoral support, and tutors may refer students for emotional support
Tutors must provide counselling themselves, as their referrals are limited to disability matters
Personal matters must go straight to the HoPAM, who personally oversees all pastoral casework
Personal matters are recorded in the End of Term Survey, which each tutor must then action
questions.explanation: The personal tutoring system provides both academic and pastoral support, and tutors refer students, as appropriate, to other departments, including for emotional support.
questions.source_excerpt: The personal tutoring system provides both academic and pastoral support to help students achieve their potential within the study environment. ... Referring students, as appropriate, to other departments within the College. Such referrals may relate, for example, to mitigating circumstances claims, disability, and emotional support;

questions.question: A final-term tutee from an area with historically low participation in higher education is unsure what to do after graduating. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which non-progression intervention fits?
options: Arranging a Graduate Outcomes Survey interview with HESA before they complete the course
Enrolling them in the Alumni Association so that alumni can guarantee them employment
Offering to meet near the end of their studies to discuss their post-study plans
Referring them to the Course Coordinator, who sets their post-study plan on the IALP
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors can offer to meet students towards the end of their studies to discuss their possible plans for when they complete their studies.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors can offer to meet with students towards the end of their studies at the College to discuss what possible plans they have for when they complete their studies;

questions.question: A final-term tutee meets every attendance and assessment requirement but attended a non-selective school and left with low GCSE and A-Level grades. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which pair of interventions is listed for their type of risk?
options: Updating their ILP, then reporting the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM by the 6th week of the semester
Adding an intervention note to their ILP and offering them additional support, if that support is required
Advice on CV writing and job applications, and encouraging them to take part in the Graduate Outcomes Survey
Referring them to the Assessment and Progression Board and setting them an individual RBA target score to meet
questions.explanation: Students from non-selective schools with lower school-level grades fall within the non-progression definition, and CV and job application advice and encouraging the Graduate Outcomes Survey are listed non-progression interventions; ILP updates, intervention notes, week 6 reporting and additional support are listed for non-continuation or non-completion.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who come from non-selective schools who demonstrate lower grades at school level (e.g. GCSE's, A-Levels etc.). ... Students can be offered advice and skills around CV writing and job applications by Personal Tutors ... Personal Tutors should encourage students to participate in the Graduate Outcomes Survey

questions.question: In week 4, you find that a Health and Social Care tutee has failed to reach the pass mark on both assignments submitted so far, and their work experience has stalled. Under the Personal Tutoring Policy, which course of action fits your role?
options: Refer both issues to the Course Coordinator, who is solely responsible for at-risk students on Health and Social Care programmes
Monitor their work experience, add an ILP intervention note and report the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM by week 6
Monitor their work experience only, as failed work places a student at risk only when attendance is also below the 60% minimum
Report the stalled work experience to the awarding body, and leave the failed work until the student's RBA score has been issued
questions.explanation: Tutors monitor the progression of work experience for Health and Social Care students, and failing to reach the pass mark on submitted assignments is on its own a non-continuation or non-completion criterion, so the tutor adds an ILP intervention note and reports the risk on or before week 6.
questions.source_excerpt: With respect to students studying on Health and Social Care programmes Personal Tutors should ensure that they monitor the progression of work experience; ... unable to achieve pass mark on submitted assignments and/or; ... Personal Tutors will include an intervention note in the ILP and report the risk to the Course Coordinator and/or HoPAM on or before the 6th week of the current semester;

questions.question: A tutee who is estranged from their family finished the semester with 50% attendance and no valid reasons for absence. Under the Personal Tutoring and Enabling Student Development Policy, how is their risk defined?
options: At risk of non-continuation or non-completion and also of non-progression, as both definitions are met
At risk of non-progression only, as estranged students are assessed under the OfS definition instead
At risk of non-continuation or non-completion only, as a student can fall within just one definition
Not yet at risk, as risk is only defined once their RBA score is reviewed at the end of the year
questions.explanation: Attendance below the 60% minimum without valid reasons meets the non-continuation or non-completion definition, and estranged students are listed in the non-progression definition, so both apply.
questions.source_excerpt: Not meeting the minimum threshold of attendance rate (i.e., minimum 60 % in a semester) without valid reasons of absence and/or; ... Students who lack traditional support networks, these include careexperienced students, estranged students, and young carers.

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, what must all programmes delivered by LCC be benchmarked to in order to gain approval?
options: The entry requirements and fee levels of comparable programmes at other London colleges
The College's own internal grading scale and achievement data from previous cohorts
The relevant national qualifications framework and relevant Subject Benchmark Statements
The awarding body's recruitment targets and the College's annual financial plan
questions.explanation: The policy states that all programmes delivered by LCC, whether awarded by Pearson or other accrediting bodies, must be benchmarked to the relevant national qualifications framework and relevant Subject Benchmark Statements to gain approval.
questions.source_excerpt: All programmes delivered by LCC - whether awarded by Pearson or other accrediting bodies - shall be benchmarked to the relevant national qualifications framework and relevant Subject Benchmark Statements in order to gain approval.

questions.question: A member of the professional services team has an idea for a new programme and asks you whether they are allowed to propose it. What does the Programme Design and Development Policy say?
options: Proposals must come from a Programme Leader, so they would need to persuade one to adopt the idea and submit it on their behalf
Any LCC stakeholder can propose it via the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, for formal submission to the PEG
They should submit it directly to Academic Board, which decides whether a Programme Development Team can be formed
New programme proposals are reserved for the awarding body, so the idea must be forwarded to Pearson for consideration
questions.explanation: The policy states that any LCC stakeholder can propose a new programme and submit it to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring, who formally submits it to the PEG.
questions.source_excerpt: Any LCC stakeholder can propose a new programme and submit it to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring for formal submission to the PEG.

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, who leads the Programme Development Team that takes a new Programme through the formal steps of the procedure?
options: The Registrar
The Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring
The Programme Leader designate
The Chair of the Principal's Executive Group (PEG)
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Development team is led by the Programme Leader designate, with Module Leaders, Tutors and Support Staff present and PEG members providing management oversight.
questions.source_excerpt: The Development team will be led by the Programme Leader designate with Module Leaders, Tutors and Support Staff present and further supported by PEG members providing management oversight.

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, whom must the Programme Development Team consult during the development stages of a new Programme?
options: The Office for Students, the College's internal auditors, the Registrar and the Head of Admissions
Employers, student representatives, relevant external advisors and the Head of Student Engagement
Prospective applicants, local secondary schools, competitor colleges and the College's Finance and Marketing teams
Alumni, parents of current students, the Marketing team and the Head of Human Resources
questions.explanation: The policy requires the team to consult employers, student representatives, relevant external advisors and the Head of Student Engagement in the development stages.
questions.source_excerpt: The team will consult employers, student representatives, relevant external advisors and the Head of Student Engagement in the development stages.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Programme Design and Development Policy as documentation the Programme Development Team must prepare for a new Programme?
options: A rationale and market justification setting out the case for the Programme
Mapping against the QAA Subject Benchmark Statement (as relevant)
Proposed staff training for implementing quality assurance of the Programme's delivery
Confirmation that the awarding body has already approved the Programme
questions.explanation: The policy's documentation list includes rationale and market justification, QAA Subject Benchmark mapping and proposed staff training for quality assurance; awarding body approval is not listed, as approved documents are only forwarded to the awarding body after the Internal Approval Panel Event.
questions.source_excerpt: The team will ensure that the following documentation will comprise: ... Rationale and Market justification ... Mapping against the QAA Subject Benchmark Statement (as relevant) ... Propose staff training for implementing the quality assurance of the Programme delivery

questions.question: You are helping to organise an Internal Approval Panel Event to be held on 24 May. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what is the latest date by which the panel should receive the Programme Proposal documentation?
options: 3 May (at least three weeks before the event)
17 May (at least one week before the event)
10 May (at least two weeks before the event)
24 April (at least one month before the event)
questions.explanation: The policy requires the Programme Proposal documentation to be received by the panel at least three weeks before the event, so for a 24 May event the latest date is 3 May.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will organise an Internal Approval Panel Event ... and ensure that documentation of the Programme Proposal is received by the panel at least three weeks before the event.

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, which groups must the Internal Approval Panel include, with their input also recorded through the Programme Development Form?
options: Finance and Marketing team representatives
Student Representatives and Externals
Prospective applicants and their sponsors
Admissions and recruitment staff
questions.explanation: The policy states the Approval Panel will include Student Representatives and Externals, and that their input should be recorded through the Programme Development Form.
questions.source_excerpt: It will include Student Representatives and Externals and their input should also be recorded through the Programme Development Form.

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, which of the following is one of the essential requirements a Programme must meet at the Internal Approval Panel stage?
options: The College has (or can obtain) the resources to deliver the Programme and support students
The Programme has already recruited a minimum viable cohort of students before approval is sought
The Programme can be delivered by existing staff without recruiting any additional members of staff
The Programme's fees are set below those charged by competitors
questions.explanation: One of the essential requirements is that the College has, or can obtain, the resources to deliver the Programme and provide all necessary support to students.
questions.source_excerpt: The college has (or can obtain) the resources to deliver the Programme and to provide all necessary support to the students.

questions.question: At an Internal Approval Panel Event, a panel member asks how a proposed Level 5 Programme addresses progression. According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, what should such a Programme be aligned to do?
options: Guarantee graduates direct employment without further study
Qualify the student for a Level 7 postgraduate programme in any subject
Qualify the student for a Level 6 programme in any subject area
Qualify the student for a Level 6 programme in a similar subject
questions.explanation: Progression routes must be taken into account, and the policy gives the example that a Level 5 Programme should qualify the student for a Level 6 programme in a similar subject.
questions.source_excerpt: Possible progression routes must be taken into account and the Programme aligned to suit these. For example, a Level 5 Programme should qualify the student for a Level 6 in a similar subject.

questions.question: A Programme Development Team wants Academic Board sign-off before the Internal Approval Panel Event to speed things up. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, when should Academic Board sign-off be sought?
options: At the very start, before the proposal is first discussed and agreed at the PEG meeting
Once all other stages are complete and conditions have been met to the panel's satisfaction
Before the Internal Approval Panel Event, so the panel can rely on Academic Board's endorsement
Immediately after the Programme Development Team has been formed and its membership confirmed
questions.explanation: The policy states that Academic Board sign-off is sought only once all other stages of development are complete and conditions have been met to the satisfaction of the panel.
questions.source_excerpt: Sign-off from Academic Board will be sought once all other stages of the development have been completed and conditions met to the satisfaction of the panel.

questions.question: Monitoring and review of an existing programme leads to a proposed Major Modification. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, how should this be handled?
options: The Module Leader reviews and updates the affected module, and the rest of the programme is left unchanged
The Programme Leader approves the change directly and reports it to Academic Board at the next annual review
The College reconsiders the whole programme through the Programme Design and Development Policy
It is reclassified as a Minor Modification provided the student representatives on the programme agree
questions.explanation: The policy states that in the event of a Major Modification the College reconsiders the whole programme through the Programme Design and Development Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Modification Policy distinguishes between Major and Minor modifications. In the event of a Major Modification, the College reconsiders the whole programme through the Programme Design and Development Policy.

questions.question: For Pearson provision, what does the Programme Design and Development Policy say is the purpose of LCC's internal programme design processes?
options: To complement Pearson's processes without duplicating work, tailoring content and assessment to LCC's student body
To take the place of Pearson's processes, so that LCC makes the design, content and assessment decisions itself
To repeat Pearson's checks in full as an independent verification of its programme content and assessment
To allow LCC to design and award Pearson qualifications without any further involvement from Pearson
questions.explanation: The policy states that, for Pearson provision, internal processes complement Pearson's without duplicating work, ensuring content and assessment are determined carefully to suit LCC's student body.
questions.source_excerpt: For Pearson provision, internal processes for programme design exist to complement those of Pearson without duplicating work and that ensure programme content (including pathway selection) and assessment processes are determined carefully to suit LCC's student body

questions.question: The Programme Design and Development Policy includes specific guidance for introducing which new programmes, for which responsibility for programme design and development is shared with Pearson?
options: New Level 3 foundation diploma programmes
New Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes
New Level 7 postgraduate certificate programmes
New degree apprenticeship programmes
questions.explanation: The policy includes specific guidance for introducing new HND programmes, for which responsibilities for programme design and development are shared with Pearson.
questions.source_excerpt: It includes specific guidance for the introduction of new HND programmes to the College's provision, for which responsibilities for programme design and development are shared with Pearson

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, what kind of Programme offer does LCC provide in line with its strategy and mission?
options: A select number of Programmes meeting the community's requirements, designed to maximise employability
A broad range of Programmes across all subject areas, designed to maximise student recruitment
A small number of research-led Programmes, designed to maximise progression to postgraduate study
Only Programmes that LCC awards itself, designed to reduce reliance on external awarding bodies
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC offers a select number of Programmes to meet the requirements of the community, designed to maximise employability.
questions.source_excerpt: In line with its strategy and mission, London Churchill College (LCC) offers a select number of Programmes to meet the requirements of the community and that are designed to maximise employability.

questions.question: For validated programmes, which externals does the Programme Design and Development Policy say are included to ensure Programmes give students knowledge and experience relevant to their chosen sector?
options: Recruitment agents, alumni and prospective students
Local authorities, funding bodies and school teachers
External examiners, employers and practitioners
Competitor colleges, sponsors and parents of students
questions.explanation: For validated programmes, the policy names external examiners, employers and practitioners as the externals included to keep Programmes relevant to students' chosen sector.
questions.source_excerpt: Externals, such as external examiners, employers and practitioners, are included to ensure Programmes provide students with knowledge and experience that is relevant within their chosen sector.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, whose approval will LCC seek for all new programmes?
options: The Office for Students (OfS)
The College's Finance Committee
The College's Quality Committee
The College's Academic Board
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC will seek the approval of Academic Board for all new programmes.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will seek the approval of Academic Board for all new programmes.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, to whose attention should the Programme Leader bring proposals for new Programmes?
options: The Chair of the PEG
The College Registrar
The Chair of Academic Board
The Head of Student Engagement
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Programme Leader should bring proposals for new Programmes to the attention of the Chair of the PEG.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader should bring proposals for new Programmes to the attention of the Chair of the PEG.

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, to whom does the Programme Development Team report regularly, providing a Draft Programme Development Form for comment?
options: The Registrar and the Head of Student Engagement
The awarding body and the College's panel of external examiners
The Principal's Executive Group (PEG) and Academic Board
The Board of Directors and the College's Finance team
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Programme Development Team reports regularly to the PEG and Academic Board, providing them with a Draft Programme Development Form for comment.
questions.source_excerpt: It will report regularly to PEG and Academic Board, providing them with a Draft Programme Development Form for comment.

questions.question: What does the Programme Design and Development Policy state is the primary function of the Programme Development Team?
options: To give final approval to the Programme
To set the tuition fees for the Programme
To recruit the first cohort of students
To continuously add value to the Programme
questions.explanation: The policy states that the primary function of the Programme Development Team is to continuously add value to the Programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Their primary function is to continuously add value to the Programme.

questions.question: Alongside staff CVs, what staffing documentation must the Programme Development Team prepare under the Programme Design and Development Policy?
options: A signed workload agreement from every tutor who will teach on the Programme
A plan to recruit any additional members of staff that may be required
Proof that every tutor already holds a Level 7 teaching qualification
A salary budget for the Programme approved by the College's Finance team
questions.explanation: The required documentation includes staff CVs and a plan for the recruitment of any additional members of staff that may be required.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff CV's, and a plan for the recruitment of any additional members of staff that may be required.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, who organises the Internal Approval Panel Event?
options: The Programme Leader designate, in consultation with the Module Leaders
The Head of Student Engagement, in consultation with student representatives
The Registrar, in consultation with the PEG or an Awarding Body representative
The Chair of Academic Board, in consultation with the external examiners
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Registrar organises the Internal Approval Panel Event, in consultation with the PEG or a representative of an Awarding Body if required.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will organise an Internal Approval Panel Event in consultation with the PEG or a representative of an Awarding Body (if required)

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, who chairs the Internal Approval Panel?
options: A member of the Principal's Executive Group (PEG)
An external examiner appointed by the awarding body
The Programme Leader designate for the Programme
A student representative elected by the student body
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Approval Panel will be chaired by a member of the PEG.
questions.source_excerpt: The Approval Panel will be chaired by a member of the PEG.

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, which Programmes are expected to meet the essential requirements checked before the approval stage?
options: New Programmes only, as current ones are reviewed through annual monitoring instead
New Programmes as well as current ones, against a pre-determined set of criteria
Only Programmes that are undergoing a Major Modification under the Modification Policy
Only Programmes awarded by LCC itself, as Pearson checks its own HND Programmes
questions.explanation: The policy states that all Programmes are tested against a pre-determined set of criteria, and that new Programmes, as well as current ones, are expected to meet the essential requirements.
questions.source_excerpt: All Programmes are tested against a pre-determined set of criteria to determine if the Programme can go forward to the approval stage. New Programmes, as well as current ones, are expected to meet the following essential requirements

questions.question: Where a programme is awarded by Pearson or another validating body, what does the Programme Design and Development Policy say happens to the documents approved at the Internal Approval Panel Event?
options: They are archived by the Registrar
They are forwarded to the awarding body
They are sent to the Office for Students
They are published on the College website
questions.explanation: Where the programme is awarded by Pearson or another validating body, the documents approved at the Internal Approval Panel Event are forwarded to the awarding body.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the programme is awarded by Pearson, or another validating body, the documents approved at the Internal Approval Panel Event will be forwarded to the awarding body.

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, how often is the policy itself reviewed?
options: At least every two years, or when awarding body regulations change significantly
At least annually, or whenever Academic Board approves a new Programme for delivery
At least every three years, or whenever the PEG formally requests a review of it
Only when the awarding body publishes a new centre guide to quality assurance
questions.explanation: The policy is reviewed at least every two years, or whenever significant changes occur within awarding body regulations and regulatory frameworks.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Design and Development Policy is approved by Academic Board and reviewed at least every two years or whenever significant changes occur within awarding body regulations and regulatory frameworks

questions.question: According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, when is the Programme Development Form to be used?
options: For new programmes and for any minor modification to a single module
Only for new HND programmes whose design is shared with Pearson
Only during annual monitoring and review of existing programmes
For new programmes and for a major modification to an existing programme
questions.explanation: The Programme Development Form is to be used for the development of new programmes and in the event of a major modification to an existing programme.
questions.source_excerpt: This form is to be used for the development of new programmes, as well as in the event of a major modification to an existing programme

questions.question: A colleague believes the Programme Design and Development Policy applies only to Pearson HND programmes. Which statement correctly describes the scope of the policy?
options: It covers only programmes awarded by LCC, as Pearson designs and develops its HND programmes on its own
It covers new HND programmes, whose design is shared with Pearson, and any programmes awarded by LCC
It covers only Pearson HNDs, as programmes awarded by LCC follow the Programme Modification Policy
It covers programmes of accrediting bodies other than Pearson, but not programmes awarded by LCC
questions.explanation: The policy includes guidance for introducing new HND programmes, whose design and development responsibilities are shared with Pearson, as well as any programmes awarded by LCC.
questions.source_excerpt: It includes specific guidance for the introduction of new HND programmes to the College's provision, for which responsibilities for programme design and development are shared with Pearson, as well as any programmes which are awarded by LCC.

questions.question: LCC is introducing a Pearson HND and must decide which pathways to offer. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, how should pathway selection be approached?
options: It is left entirely to Pearson, as pathway selection falls outside LCC's internal design processes
Pathways are selected to mirror those offered by competitor colleges in the local area
The Registrar selects the pathways using the previous year's enrolment figures
It is determined carefully through internal processes to suit LCC's student body
questions.explanation: For Pearson provision, LCC's internal design processes ensure programme content, including pathway selection, is determined carefully to suit LCC's student body.
questions.source_excerpt: For Pearson provision, internal processes for programme design exist to complement those of Pearson without duplicating work and that ensure programme content (including pathway selection) and assessment processes are determined carefully to suit LCC's student body

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what happens to a programme once it has been approved, and what purpose does this serve?
options: It is subject to monitoring and review, which can identify modifications to enhance it
It is fixed for the whole validated period, with changes permitted only at revalidation
It is reviewed by the awarding body alone, which decides on any changes that are needed
It is re-approved by Academic Board every year before each new student intake begins
questions.explanation: Following approval, programmes are subject to monitoring and review, which can help identify where modifications could be made to enhance a programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Following approval, programmes are subject to monitoring and review. This can help to identify where modifications could be made to enhance a programme.

questions.question: A Programme Leader has an outline for a new Programme and wants the formal development and approval process to begin. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what must happen before the process commences?
options: Academic Board must approve a draft Programme Development Form for it
The Registrar must schedule an Internal Approval Panel Event for it
It must be discussed and agreed at the Principal's Executive Group (PEG)
The awarding body must confirm that it will validate the Programme
questions.explanation: The policy states that the process to develop and approve a Programme commences following discussion and agreement at the PEG.
questions.source_excerpt: The process to develop and approve the Programme commences following discussion and agreement at the Principal's Executive Group (PEG).

questions.question: When the Principal's Executive Group (PEG) discusses a proposal for a new Programme, what does the Programme Design and Development Policy say the PEG will decide?
options: Which Module Leaders and Tutors will teach the Programme in its first year
How the introduction of the Programme fits in with the institutional Strategic Plan
Which external awarding body will validate the Programme and approve its assessments
What tuition fee the College will charge students who enrol on the Programme
questions.explanation: At the PEG stage, the policy states that the PEG will decide how the introduction of the Programme fits in with the institutional Strategic Plan.
questions.source_excerpt: The PEG will decide how the introduction of the Programme fits in with the institutional Strategic Plan.

questions.question: A new Programme will be awarded by an external Awarding Body that wishes to take part in its development. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, how can this be accommodated?
options: The development team will include members of the Awarding Body, if required
The Awarding Body will take over from the Programme Leader designate as team lead
The Awarding Body may comment only once Academic Board has signed off the Programme
An Awarding Body member will chair the Internal Approval Panel instead of a PEG member
questions.explanation: The development team is led by the Programme Leader designate and, if required, will include members of the Awarding Body.
questions.source_excerpt: A Programme Leader designate, and development team will be formed that will then take on the responsibility of taking the Programme through the formal steps of the procedure through the completion of the Programme Development Form. If required, the team will include members of the Awarding Body.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what role do members of the Principal's Executive Group (PEG) play in a Programme Development Team?
options: They lead the team and complete the Programme Development Form themselves
They formally approve the Programme on behalf of Academic Board
They act as the team's external advisors on employer and market demand
They support the team by providing management oversight
questions.explanation: The team is led by the Programme Leader designate and is further supported by PEG members, who provide management oversight.
questions.source_excerpt: The Development team will be led by the Programme Leader designate with Module Leaders, Tutors and Support Staff present and further supported by PEG members providing management oversight.

questions.question: At the Internal Approval Panel stage, Programmes are tested against a pre-determined set of criteria. According to the Programme Design and Development Policy, what is the purpose of this testing?
options: To set the grading criteria and weighting used in the Programme's assessments
To decide how the Programme fits the institutional Strategic Plan
To determine whether the Programme can go forward to the approval stage
To confirm the Programme's tuition fees and its first-year recruitment targets
questions.explanation: The policy states that all Programmes are tested against a pre-determined set of criteria to determine whether the Programme can go forward to the approval stage.
questions.source_excerpt: All Programmes are tested against a pre-determined set of criteria to determine if the Programme can go forward to the approval stage.

questions.question: A Programme Development Team is compiling the documentation for a new Programme. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, which two forms of consultation evidence must that documentation include?
options: Evidence of consultation with competitor colleges and with local schools
Evidence of employer consultation and evidence of student consultation
Evidence of consultation with alumni and with the parents of applicants
Evidence of consultation with the Office for Students and with Pearson
questions.explanation: The required documentation list includes both evidence of employer consultation and evidence of student consultation.
questions.source_excerpt: The team will ensure that the following documentation will comprise: ... Evidence of employer consultation ... Evidence of student consultation

questions.question: At an Internal Approval Panel Event, a proposed Programme shows strong applicant interest, but there is little demand in the job sector for its graduates. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what follows?
options: It falls short of an essential requirement, as job-sector demand for graduates is one of the criteria
It meets the criteria, as strong applicant interest on its own shows the required market demand
It meets the criteria if the awarding body agrees to validate it despite the weak job-sector demand
It must instead be re-submitted to the PEG as a Major Modification of an existing programme
questions.explanation: Market demand for the Programme and demand in the job sector for its graduates are separate essential requirements, so weak job-sector demand means the Programme falls short of one.
questions.source_excerpt: New Programmes, as well as current ones, are expected to meet the following essential requirements: ... Market demand for the Programme ... Demand in the job sector for graduates of the Programme.

questions.question: A proposed Programme needs specialist equipment the College does not yet own, but a funded plan to obtain it is in place. How does this sit with the resources requirement in the Programme Design and Development Policy?
options: It cannot meet it, as every resource must already be in place before the panel meets
It can meet it only if Academic Board first agrees to waive the resources requirement
It can meet it only if the awarding body agrees to supply the equipment itself
It can meet it, as the College must have, or be able to obtain, the resources
questions.explanation: The essential requirement is that the College has, or can obtain, the resources to deliver the Programme, so a funded plan to obtain the equipment can satisfy it.
questions.source_excerpt: The college has (or can obtain) the resources to deliver the Programme and to provide all necessary support to the students.

questions.question: When Academic Board sign-off is sought for a new Programme, what does the Programme Design and Development Policy say should be included?
options: Written confirmation from the awarding body that it has already validated and approved the Programme
A confirmed enrolment list and timetable for the Programme's first cohort of students
Evidence of how the Programme met the scrutiny criteria, with input from externals and students
Signed employment contracts for every additional member of staff to be recruited
questions.explanation: The policy states that Academic Board sign-off should include evidence of how the Programme met the scrutiny criteria, including evidence of input from externals and students.
questions.source_excerpt: Sign-off from Academic Board will be sought once all other stages of the development have been completed and conditions met to the satisfaction of the panel. This should include evidence demonstrating how the Programme has met the scrutiny criteria, including evidence of input from externals and students.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, which sequence correctly reflects the main stages for developing and approving a new Programme?
options: PEG agreement; development team work; Internal Approval Panel Event; Academic Board sign-off
Development team work; Academic Board sign-off; PEG agreement; Internal Approval Panel Event
PEG agreement; Internal Approval Panel Event; development team work; Academic Board sign-off
Academic Board sign-off; PEG agreement; development team work; Internal Approval Panel Event
questions.explanation: The process commences after PEG agreement, the development team then takes the Programme through the procedure, the Internal Approval Panel Event follows, and Academic Board sign-off is sought once all other stages are complete.
questions.source_excerpt: The process to develop and approve the Programme commences following discussion and agreement at the Principal's Executive Group (PEG). ... A Programme Leader designate, and development team will be formed ... Sign-off from Academic Board will be sought once all other stages of the development have been completed and conditions met to the satisfaction of the panel.

questions.question: Pearson makes significant changes to its regulations one year after the Programme Design and Development Policy was last reviewed. Under the policy, what should happen?
options: The review waits until two years have passed since the policy was last reviewed
The policy should be reviewed now, without waiting for the two-year point
Only Programmes approved during that year need to be re-examined by the PEG
Pearson's new regulations replace the policy until its next scheduled review
questions.explanation: The policy is reviewed at least every two years or whenever significant changes occur within awarding body regulations, so a significant Pearson change triggers a review.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Design and Development Policy is approved by Academic Board and reviewed at least every two years or whenever significant changes occur within awarding body regulations and regulatory frameworks

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, who should normally complete the sections of the Programme Development Form, and when?
options: The Registrar, once the Internal Approval Panel Event has been scheduled
The panel chair, after the Internal Approval Panel Event has taken place
The Academic Board secretary, when sign-off for the Programme is sought
The proposer, as the Programme is taken through the formal stages of design
questions.explanation: The form states that its sections should normally be completed by the proposer as the Programme is taken through the formal stages of design.
questions.source_excerpt: The sections of this form should normally be completed by the proposer, as the Programme is taken through the formal stages of design.

questions.question: A proposed Programme will make use of guest lecturers. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what does the Programme Development Form ask the proposer to indicate about them?
options: Their CVs and signed agreements covering the whole of the validated period
Their fees and the budget line that will fund each of their sessions
The extent and effect of their contributions, and any future plans to use them
Their academic qualifications and the modules that each of them will assess
questions.explanation: The Resources section of the form asks for the extent and effect of guest lecturers' contributions and details of any future plans to use guest lecturers.
questions.source_excerpt: Where use will be made of guest lecturers, please indicate the extent and effect of their contributions to the programme. Please include details of any future plans to use guest lecturers on this programme.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what should be attached when the proposer gives an account of consultation in the Programme Development Form?
options: Relevant committee and programme development team minutes
Signed letters of support from every employer consulted on the proposal
The full set of raw responses from student surveys
The external examiner's most recent annual report
questions.explanation: The consultation section of the form asks for an account of consultation across the College, with external advisors and current students, with relevant committee and programme development team minutes attached.
questions.source_excerpt: An account of how the proposal has been subject to consultation, across the College, with external advisors and current students (relevant committee and programme development team minutes to be attached).

questions.question: A programme LCC will deliver is awarded by an accrediting body other than Pearson. A colleague says benchmarking against Subject Benchmark Statements applies only to LCC-awarded programmes. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what is correct?
options: Only LCC-awarded programmes need benchmarking, so the accrediting body's own standards are applied instead
It must be benchmarked to the relevant national qualifications framework and Subject Benchmark Statements
Only Pearson HNDs need benchmarking, as Pearson shares design and development responsibility with LCC
Benchmarking is left to the accrediting body, and LCC relies on that body's confirmation that it is done
questions.explanation: The policy applies benchmarking to all programmes delivered by LCC, whether awarded by Pearson or other accrediting bodies, as a condition of gaining approval.
questions.source_excerpt: All programmes delivered by LCC - whether awarded by Pearson or other accrediting bodies - shall be benchmarked to the relevant national qualifications framework and relevant Subject Benchmark Statements in order to gain approval.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, which statement correctly distinguishes how a Programme Leader and another LCC stakeholder each bring forward a proposal for a new Programme?
options: Programme Leader: to the Chair of the PEG. Other stakeholder: to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring for submission to the PEG
Programme Leader: to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring. Other stakeholder: to the Chair of the PEG for formal submission
Programme Leader: to the Chair of Academic Board. Other stakeholder: to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring for the PEG
Programme Leader: to the Chair of the PEG. Other stakeholder: to the Registrar, who formally submits it to Academic Board
questions.explanation: A Programme Leader brings proposals to the attention of the Chair of the PEG, while any LCC stakeholder submits a proposal to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring for formal submission to the PEG.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader should bring proposals for new Programmes to the attention of the Chair of the PEG. ... Any LCC stakeholder can propose a new programme and submit it to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring for formal submission to the PEG.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, which of the following is named as someone the Programme Development Team consults in the development stages, rather than as one of those present in the team led by the Programme Leader designate?
options: The Programme's Module Leaders
The Programme's Support Staff
The Head of Student Engagement
The Programme's Tutors
questions.explanation: Module Leaders, Tutors and Support Staff are present in the team; the Head of Student Engagement is listed with employers, student representatives and external advisors as someone the team consults.
questions.source_excerpt: The Development team will be led by the Programme Leader designate with Module Leaders, Tutors and Support Staff present ... The team will consult employers, student representatives, relevant external advisors and the Head of Student Engagement in the development stages.

questions.question: Two weeks before an Internal Approval Panel Event, the panel has still not received the Programme Proposal documentation. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, whose responsibility was it to ensure receipt, and by when?
options: The Programme Leader designate's, at least three weeks before the event
The Registrar's, at least two weeks before the event
The Chair of the PEG's, at least one month before the event
The Registrar's, at least three weeks before the event
questions.explanation: The Registrar organises the event and must ensure the panel receives the Programme Proposal documentation at least three weeks beforehand, so this deadline has already been missed.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will organise an Internal Approval Panel Event in consultation with the PEG or a representative of an Awarding Body (if required) and ensure that documentation of the Programme Proposal is received by the panel at least three weeks before the event.

questions.question: Which of these proposed Internal Approval Panels for a new Programme would comply with the Programme Design and Development Policy?
options: Chaired by the Programme Leader designate, with Student Representatives and Externals included
Chaired by a PEG member, with Student Representatives and Externals included
Chaired by a PEG member, with internal staff only and externals consulted after the event
Chaired by an external examiner, with Student Representatives included as observers
questions.explanation: The panel must be chaired by a member of the PEG and must include Student Representatives and Externals, whose input is recorded through the Programme Development Form.
questions.source_excerpt: The Approval Panel will be chaired by a member of the PEG. It will include Student Representatives and Externals and their input should also be recorded through the Programme Development Form.

questions.question: At an Internal Approval Panel Event, the College can deliver a proposed Programme's teaching but cannot provide the support its students would need. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, how does this sit with the essential requirements?
options: It meets the resources requirement, which concerns only the resources needed to deliver the teaching
It meets the resources requirement, as student support needs are reviewed later through monitoring and review
It falls short of the resources requirement, which also covers providing all necessary student support
It falls short of the market demand requirement, as students are unlikely to enrol on the Programme
questions.explanation: The resources requirement is that the College has, or can obtain, the resources both to deliver the Programme and to provide all necessary support to the students.
questions.source_excerpt: The college has (or can obtain) the resources to deliver the Programme and to provide all necessary support to the students.

questions.question: An Internal Approval Panel approves a new Programme subject to conditions, and the team wants Academic Board sign-off while some of the conditions are still outstanding. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what applies?
options: Sign-off waits until the conditions have been met to the satisfaction of the panel
Sign-off can go ahead, as conditions are dealt with once Academic Board has signed off
Sign-off can go ahead if the Chair of the PEG agrees to waive the outstanding conditions
Sign-off waits until the awarding body confirms that the conditions have been met
questions.explanation: Academic Board sign-off is sought only once all other stages are complete and conditions have been met to the satisfaction of the panel, not the PEG Chair or the awarding body.
questions.source_excerpt: Sign-off from Academic Board will be sought once all other stages of the development have been completed and conditions met to the satisfaction of the panel.

questions.question: Monitoring and review identifies a Major Modification to an existing programme. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what is reconsidered, and which form is used?
options: Only the modified modules are reconsidered, using the Programme Development Form
The whole programme is reconsidered, using the Programme Development Form
The whole programme is reconsidered by the awarding body, without a Programme Development Form
Only the modified modules are reconsidered, and are recorded in the annual monitoring report
questions.explanation: A Major Modification means the College reconsiders the whole programme through this policy, and the Programme Development Form is to be used for a major modification as well as for new programmes.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of a Major Modification, the College reconsiders the whole programme through the Programme Design and Development Policy. ... This form is to be used for the development of new programmes, as well as in the event of a major modification to an existing programme

questions.question: A significant change occurs in a regulatory framework that affects LCC, although no awarding body has changed its regulations. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what should happen to the policy itself?
options: It should be reviewed, taking into account any Programmes that were approved or proposed
It waits for the two-year point, as no awarding body has changed its own regulations
It should be reviewed, taking into account only Programmes that have already been approved
It is suspended until the awarding bodies have updated their regulations to match the change
questions.explanation: The policy is reviewed at least every two years or whenever significant changes occur within awarding body regulations and regulatory frameworks, taking approved or proposed Programmes into account.
questions.source_excerpt: reviewed at least every two years or whenever significant changes occur within awarding body regulations and regulatory frameworks, taking any Programmes that were approved or proposed into account.

questions.question: A proposer completing the Programme Development Form needs to explain how the new Programme can be differentiated from competitors. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, where in the form does this belong?
options: Purposes and Objectives, alongside the knowledge and skills that students can acquire
Strategic Fit, alongside the rationale, community needs and evidence of market demand
Consultation and External Reference Points, alongside the analysis of employer feedback
Resources, alongside the summary of the physical and financial resources required
questions.explanation: The Strategic Fit section asks for comment on the rationale for the programme, including community needs, evidence of market demand and how it can be differentiated from competitors.
questions.source_excerpt: STRATEGIC FIT ... Comment on the rationale for the programme, including how it meets the needs of the community, evidence of market demand and how the programme can be differentiated from competitors.

questions.question: A programme with established employer links is going through revalidation. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what does the Programme Development Form ask the proposer to provide about those employers?
options: A list of the employers who have agreed to recruit graduates of the programme
Confirmation that each employer will offer work placements in the next validated period
Analysis of their feedback for the validated period and details of revalidation consultation
Employers' ratings of individual tutors collected over the course of the validated period
questions.explanation: Where there are employer links, the form asks for analysis of employer feedback for the validated period and details of consultation in the revalidation process.
questions.source_excerpt: Where there are employer links, please provide analysis of employer feedback for the validated period, and details of consultation in the revalidation process.

questions.question: The Delivery section of the Programme Development Form asks for an evaluation of teaching methods and assessment strategy. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, who carries out that evaluation, and against what is the programme mapped?
options: The designate programme team; the College's Learning Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy
The Internal Approval Panel; the College's Learning Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy
The designate programme team; the awarding body's assessment regulations and grading scale
The Head of Student Engagement; the results of the College's annual student survey
questions.explanation: The Delivery section calls for evaluation by the designate programme team, including how the programme has been mapped against the College's Learning Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy.
questions.source_excerpt: DELIVERY Evaluation by the designate programme team of the effectiveness of the teaching methods and assessment strategy including details of how the programme has been mapped against the College's Learning Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy.

questions.question: A proposer's Resources section of the Programme Development Form summarises the physical resources a new Programme will need but says nothing about funding. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what should be added?
options: Quotations from at least three suppliers for each resource
Finance Committee sign-off for the full cost of each resource
Confirmation that the awarding body will fund the resources
An account of how the financial resources are to be secured
questions.explanation: The Resources section asks for a summary of physical resources that includes an account of how the financial resources are to be secured.
