questions.source_excerpt: RESOURCES Summary of the physical resources which are available or will be required to support the programme, including an account on how the financial resources are to be secured.

questions.question: A proposed Programme includes work placements. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what does the Programme Development Form ask to be evaluated in relation to those placements?
options: Each placement provider's insurance and health and safety certificates
The number of placements secured for each student before approval
The arrangements for student guidance, support and advice related to them
The rate at which placement providers have hired previous students
questions.explanation: The form asks for evaluation of the arrangements for student guidance, support and advice systems, including those related to work placements where applicable.
questions.source_excerpt: Evaluation of the arrangements for student guidance, support and advice systems, including those related to work placements where applicable.

questions.question: A programme being revalidated must also satisfy the requirements of a professional body. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what does the Programme Development Form ask the proposer to comment on?
options: Whether the professional body has agreed to chair the Internal Approval Panel
How the programme's assessment will be transferred to that body's regulations
Whether the professional body has approved the programme's fees and entry criteria
The extent to which the programme continues to meet that body's requirements
questions.explanation: Where applicable, the form asks for comment on the extent to which the programme continues to meet the requirements of professional, statutory or regulatory bodies.
questions.source_excerpt: Where applicable, comment on the extent to which the programme continues to meet the requirements of professional, statutory or regulatory bodies.

questions.question: In the Resources section of a Programme Development Form, a proposer lists staff publications but does not link them to the new Programme. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what does the form actually ask for?
options: Evidence that each member of staff holds a doctorate in the relevant subject area
Details of how staff research or professional activity informs the curriculum
The number of hours of research time allocated to each member of staff
A list of each staff member's publications over the last five academic years
questions.explanation: The Resources section asks for details of how the research or professional activity of staff informs the curriculum, not simply a list of their outputs.
questions.source_excerpt: Details of how the research/professional activity of staff informs the curriculum.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, how are students involved across the development and approval of a new Programme?
options: Through Student Representatives on the approval panel, but not consulted in development
Consulted in development, but the approval panel is limited to PEG members and externals
Consulted in development, represented on the panel, and their input evidenced at sign-off
Through module evaluations collected in annual monitoring, once the Programme is approved
questions.explanation: Student representatives are consulted during development, the approval panel includes Student Representatives, and Academic Board sign-off should include evidence of input from students.
questions.source_excerpt: The team will consult employers, student representatives, relevant external advisors and the Head of Student Engagement in the development stages. ... It will include Student Representatives and Externals ... including evidence of input from externals and students.

questions.question: A new colleague believes the PEG gives final approval to new Programmes and that the Registrar chairs the Internal Approval Panel. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, which correction is accurate?
options: Academic Board gives sign-off; the Registrar both organises the panel event and chairs the Internal Approval Panel
The PEG gives final approval, as the colleague says; the Internal Approval Panel is chaired by a member of the PEG
Academic Board gives sign-off; the Registrar organises the panel event, which a member of the PEG chairs
Academic Board gives sign-off; the Programme Leader designate organises and chairs the panel event
questions.explanation: LCC seeks Academic Board approval for all new programmes; the Registrar organises the Internal Approval Panel Event, but the panel itself is chaired by a member of the PEG.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will seek the approval of Academic Board for all new programmes. ... The Registrar will organise an Internal Approval Panel Event ... The Approval Panel will be chaired by a member of the PEG.

questions.question: During development, the Programme Development Team gives Academic Board a Draft Programme Development Form and Academic Board comments favourably. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, does this amount to Academic Board sign-off?
options: Yes; favourable comments on the draft form count as sign-off, so the Internal Approval Panel Event is not needed
Yes, provided the PEG has also commented favourably on the same Draft Programme Development Form
No; sign-off for the Programme is given by the PEG once the Internal Approval Panel Event has been held
No; the draft is for comment, and sign-off is sought once all other stages are complete and conditions met
questions.explanation: The team gives the PEG and Academic Board a Draft Programme Development Form for comment; Academic Board sign-off is sought only once all other stages are complete and conditions are met to the panel's satisfaction.
questions.source_excerpt: It will report regularly to PEG and Academic Board, providing them with a Draft Programme Development Form for comment. ... Sign-off from Academic Board will be sought once all other stages of the development have been completed and conditions met to the satisfaction of the panel.

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, which of the following steps in developing a new Programme would not comply with the procedure?
options: A tutor sends a proposal to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring for formal submission to the PEG
The team's documentation includes staff CVs but no plan to recruit the two extra tutors the Programme needs
The team gives the PEG and Academic Board a Draft Programme Development Form for comment
The Registrar consults the PEG when organising the Internal Approval Panel Event for the Programme
questions.explanation: The team's documentation must include staff CVs and a plan for recruiting any additional staff that may be required; the other steps are all provided for in the procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Any LCC stakeholder can propose a new programme and submit it to the Head of Programmes and Academic Monitoring for formal submission to the PEG. ... Staff CV's, and a plan for the recruitment of any additional members of staff that may be required.

questions.question: For a new Pearson HND, a colleague suggests skipping the Internal Approval Panel Event because design responsibility is shared with Pearson. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what is correct?
options: The event is still held, and the documents approved at it are then forwarded to Pearson
The event is skipped, as Pearson's own approval of the HND takes the place of the internal panel
The event is held only if Academic Board specifically asks for one for Pearson provision
The event is skipped, and the HND goes straight to Academic Board for sign-off instead
questions.explanation: All Programmes are tested at the Internal Approval Panel stage, and where Pearson awards the programme the documents approved at the event are forwarded to Pearson.
questions.source_excerpt: All Programmes are tested against a pre-determined set of criteria to determine if the Programme can go forward to the approval stage. ... Where the programme is awarded by Pearson, or another validating body, the documents approved at the Internal Approval Panel Event will be forwarded to the awarding body.

questions.question: A proposer wants to use the Programme Development Form to evaluate the curriculum in light of developments in the subject area and QAA Subject Benchmark Statements. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, which section is this?
options: Delivery, alongside the mapping of the programme against the College's Learning Teaching & Assessment Policy and Strategy
Purposes and Objectives, alongside the knowledge and skills that students can acquire through the programme
Strategic Fit, alongside the background, history and philosophy of the programme and its rationale
Consultation and External Reference Points, alongside professional, statutory or regulatory body requirements
questions.explanation: The Consultation and External Reference Points section asks for evaluation of the curriculum against subject and professional developments, such as QAA Subject Benchmark Statements, alongside comment on professional, statutory or regulatory body requirements.
questions.source_excerpt: CONSULTATION AND EXTERNAL REFERENCE POINTS ... Where applicable, comment on the extent to which the programme continues to meet the requirements of professional, statutory or regulatory bodies. ... Evaluation of the curriculum in light of developments in the subject area and professional practice (e.g. QAA Subject Benchmark Statements (SBS) or other equivalent professional references).

questions.question: At an Internal Approval Panel Event, a panel member argues that strategic fit was settled when the PEG agreed the proposal, so it need not be tested again. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what is correct?
options: Strategic fit is not re-tested, as the PEG's earlier decision on the Strategic Plan is binding on the panel
Strategic fit is tested only if the awarding body asks the Registrar to add it to the panel's criteria
Strategic fit is not re-tested, as the panel's essential requirements cover only demand, progression and resources
It is still tested, as operating within the College's strategy and mission is an essential requirement
questions.explanation: The PEG decides how the Programme fits the Strategic Plan, but the panel's essential requirements also include that the Programme operates within the College's overall strategy and mission.
questions.source_excerpt: The PEG will decide how the introduction of the Programme fits in with the institutional Strategic Plan. ... New Programmes, as well as current ones, are expected to meet the following essential requirements: ... It operates within the College's overall strategy and mission

questions.question: The Programme Design and Development Policy sets out different arrangements for Pearson provision and for validated programmes. Which statement correctly matches each type of provision to its arrangement?
options: Pearson: LCC's internal processes replace all of Pearson's design work. Validated: input and support from staff and students, with externals included
Pearson: internal processes complement Pearson's without duplicating work. Validated: design is left to the validating body, without staff input
Pearson: Pearson alone decides content, pathways and assessment. Validated: externals are excluded so that only staff and students lead the design
Pearson: internal processes complement Pearson's without duplicating work. Validated: staff and student input and support, with externals included
questions.explanation: For Pearson provision, internal design processes complement Pearson's without duplicating work; for validated programmes, staff and students give input and support, and externals such as external examiners, employers and practitioners are included.
questions.source_excerpt: For Pearson provision, internal processes for programme design exist to complement those of Pearson without duplicating work ... For validated programmes, arrangements are in place to allow for input and support from staff and students. Externals, such as external examiners, employers and practitioners, are included

questions.question: Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, which item is listed in the documentation the Programme Development Team prepares, but is not one of the essential requirements tested at the Internal Approval Panel stage?
options: Demand in the job sector for graduates of the Programme
The entry criteria that applicants to the Programme must meet
Alignment of the Programme to possible progression routes
Operating within the College's overall strategy and mission
questions.explanation: Entry criteria appear in the development team's documentation list but not among the panel's essential requirements, whereas job-sector demand, progression routes and fit with strategy and mission are all essential requirements.
questions.source_excerpt: The team will ensure that the following documentation will comprise: ... Entry criteria ... New Programmes, as well as current ones, are expected to meet the following essential requirements ... Market demand for the Programme ... Possible progression routes ... Demand in the job sector for graduates of the Programme ... It operates within the College's overall strategy and mission

questions.question: While planning the Internal Approval Panel for a new validated programme, a colleague says an employer cannot be one of the panel's Externals, as employers are only consulted by the development team. Under the Programme Design and Development Policy, what is correct?
options: The colleague is wrong: the policy names employers, with external examiners and practitioners, as examples of the Externals it includes
The colleague is right: the panel's Externals must be external examiners, and employers contribute only through the consultation evidence
The colleague is right: employers may attend only as observers, as panel membership is limited to PEG members and College staff
The colleague is wrong, but an employer's input on the panel is not recorded, as only Student Representatives' input goes on the form
questions.explanation: The policy gives employers, alongside external examiners and practitioners, as examples of Externals, and the Internal Approval Panel includes Student Representatives and Externals, whose input is recorded through the Programme Development Form.
questions.source_excerpt: Externals, such as external examiners, employers and practitioners, are included to ensure Programmes provide students with knowledge and experience that is relevant within their chosen sector. ... It will include Student Representatives and Externals and their input should also be recorded through the Programme Development Form.

questions.question: For a new programme awarded by Pearson, which statement correctly describes where the Programme Design and Development Policy provides for awarding body involvement in development and approval?
options: A representative of the awarding body chairs the Internal Approval Panel where required, and the awarding body then gives sign-off in place of Academic Board
The awarding body leads the development team and completes the Programme Development Form in place of the Programme Leader designate
Its members on the development team and consultation on organising the panel event, each if required, then receipt of the documents approved there
None until Academic Board has signed the programme off, after which Academic Board's decision is sent on to the awarding body for validation
questions.explanation: The development team will include members of the Awarding Body if required, the Registrar may organise the panel event in consultation with an Awarding Body representative if required, and the documents approved at the event are forwarded to the awarding body.
questions.source_excerpt: If required, the team will include members of the Awarding Body. ... The Registrar will organise an Internal Approval Panel Event in consultation with the PEG or a representative of an Awarding Body (if required) ... Where the programme is awarded by Pearson, or another validating body, the documents approved at the Internal Approval Panel Event will be forwarded to the awarding body.

questions.question: According to the Programme Modification Policy, who decides whether a modification should be treated as minor or major where there is uncertainty about which process to follow?
options: The Principal's Executive Group (PEG)
The Programme Leader proposing the change
The Quality Assurance Department
The Quality Enhancement Steering Committee (QESC)
questions.explanation: The policy states that where there is uncertainty over which process applies, the Principal's Executive Group determines whether the modification is minor or major.
questions.source_excerpt: Where there is uncertainty as to which process to follow, the Principal's Executive Group shall determine whether the modification should be treated as minor or major.

questions.question: Over several years, a programme has had a series of minor unit replacements that together now amount to more than 30% of the programme's units. Under the Programme Modification Policy, how should this be treated?
options: As minor, because each individual change was approved as minor
As a major modification requiring a higher level of approval
As an awarding body change handled outside the policy
As minor, provided the External Examiner raises no concerns
questions.explanation: The policy treats cumulative minor changes that accumulate to more than 30% of the programme's units as a major modification requiring a higher level of approval and consultation.
questions.source_excerpt: Attention will be paid to cumulative changes which, although minor in themselves, result over time in major changes which require a higher level of approval and consultation. ... multiple minor modifications that accumulate to more than 30% of the programme's units

questions.question: According to the Programme Modification Policy, how must a major modification be progressed?
options: Through the Programme Minor Modification Form, with PEG sign-off as the final approval stage
Directly by the Academic Board, without further consultation with students or staff
Through the Programme Design and Development Policy, completing the Programme Development Form
By the Quality Assurance Department updating the programme records and the programme specification
questions.explanation: Major modifications require the programme to be reconsidered through the Programme Design and Development Policy, and the Programme Development Form must be completed.
questions.source_excerpt: Major modifications require the programme to be reconsidered through the Programme Design and Development Policy. ... The Programme Development Form must be completed;

questions.question: A proposal to move a programme's teaching to a different building reaches PEG, but no student group and accessibility impact has been assessed. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what should happen?
options: PEG may approve it, provided the impact assessment is completed before the end of the current academic year
PEG must not approve it until the impact is assessed, students consulted where appropriate and protections in place
PEG may approve it if the Programme Leader confirms in writing that a small number of students will be affected
PEG should approve it and ask QESC to complete the impact assessment as part of its subsequent internal review
questions.explanation: PEG, QESC and Academic Board must not approve changes to teaching location unless the student group and accessibility impact has been assessed, students consulted where appropriate and protective measures are in place.
questions.source_excerpt: PEG, QESC and Academic Board must not approve any modification involving changes to mode of study, teaching location, facilities or delivery arrangements unless they are satisfied that the student group and accessibility impact has been assessed, affected students have been consulted where appropriate, and reasonable measures are in place to protect student interests;

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, what is the correct approval route for a minor modification proposal?
options: PEG, then internal review by QESC, then final approval by the Academic Board
QESC, then internal review by PEG, then final approval by the Academic Board
Academic Board, then internal review by QESC, then final approval by PEG
PEG, then internal review by the Academic Board, then final approval by QESC
questions.explanation: The proposal goes to PEG first; if accepted, it is reviewed internally by QESC and then submitted to the Academic Board for final approval.
questions.source_excerpt: The proposal, together with supporting documentation, should be submitted to the Principal's Executive Group (PEG). If accepted by PEG, the proposal will be reviewed internally by the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee (QESC) and then submitted for final approval by the Academic Board;

questions.question: A building used for a programme becomes unavailable at short notice and teaching must move immediately, before an impact assessment can be completed. What does the Programme Modification Policy require?
options: Suspend teaching until a full impact assessment has been completed and approved by PEG
Proceed with the move and skip the impact assessment, as urgent operational changes are exempt from it
Implement interim measures and complete the impact assessment as soon as reasonably practicable
Wait for formal Academic Board approval of the new location before taking any interim action
questions.explanation: Measures should normally be applied before a change, but where urgent operational circumstances require immediate action the College implements interim measures and completes the impact assessment as soon as reasonably practicable.
questions.source_excerpt: These measures must be applied before any change is implemented wherever possible. Where urgent operational circumstances require immediate action, the College will implement interim measures and complete the impact assessment as soon as reasonably practicable.

questions.question: According to the Programme Modification Policy, whose consent will be sought where a modification may materially affect their programme, learning experience or contractual expectations?
options: The awarding body and the External Examiner, on behalf of students
Existing students, with consultation with applicants where relevant
Student representatives on the Academic Board, on behalf of all students
Applicants, as existing students have already accepted their contract terms
questions.explanation: The policy states that the consent of existing students, and consultation with applicants where relevant, will be sought where a change may materially affect them.
questions.source_excerpt: The consent of existing students, and consultation with applicants where relevant, will be sought in respect of programme modifications where the change may materially affect their programme, learning experience or contractual expectations;

questions.question: A Programme Leader is proposing a minor modification that changes a module's timetable and may affect students with caring responsibilities. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what must be done?
options: Reclassify it as a major modification and complete the Programme Development Form
Nothing further, as minor modifications are exempt from the impact assessment requirements
Ask affected students to raise any concerns through the Complaints Policy
Complete the Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment section of the form
questions.explanation: Where a minor modification may affect a specific group of students or timetable accessibility, the Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment section of the form must be completed.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a minor modification may affect a specific group of students, accessibility arrangements, reasonable adjustments, timetable accessibility, facilities or mode of study, the Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment section of the form must be completed.

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, which of the following is NOT given as an example of a major modification?
options: Changing the qualification title or award
Closing the course
Making material changes to teaching location or facilities
Swapping modules between years
questions.explanation: Swapping modules between years is listed as an example of a minor modification; title/award changes, course closure and material changes to location or facilities are listed as major.
questions.source_excerpt: Examples of minor modifications may include replacing up to 30% of the programme's units, making changes to assessment methods, swapping modules between years or updating learning resources ... changes to qualification title or award, substantial changes to mode of study, material changes to teaching location or facilities, course closure

questions.question: A module tutor wants to change the assessment method in one module. Under the Programme Modification Policy, who should make the minor modification proposal using the Programme Minor Modification Form?
options: The Programme Leader
The module tutor
The Quality Assurance Department
The External Examiner
questions.explanation: The policy states that proposals to make minor modifications should come from the Programme Leader and be made using the Programme Minor Modification Form.
questions.source_excerpt: Proposals to make minor modifications to a programme should come from the Programme Leader. These should be made using the Programme Minor Modification Form;

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, when students are informed of an approved change, which options open to them should be explained where applicable?
options: Transfer, continuation, complaint or withdrawal rights
Continuation on the modified programme, with no alternative options
An appeal to the awarding body, which must be lodged before the change
An automatic full refund of tuition fees
questions.explanation: Students must be told about approved changes and any options open to them, including transfer, continuation, complaint or withdrawal rights where applicable.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will be informed clearly and in a timely manner about approved changes, the reasons for those changes, the expected impact, the support available and any options open to them, including transfer, continuation, complaint or withdrawal rights where applicable;

questions.question: A Programme Leader is planning a minor modification to update the learning resources in one module. Under the Programme Modification Policy, who must be consulted?
options: The External Examiner and the awarding body, rather than staff or students
Staff, with students consulted later if the change becomes a major modification
Staff and students, with external input sought where PEG deems it necessary
Employers and applicants, with students told once the change has been approved
questions.explanation: For minor modifications, consultation must include staff and students, and external input such as from the External Examiner is sought where the Principal's Executive Group deems it necessary.
questions.source_excerpt: Consultation must include staff and students. External input, such as from the External Examiner, must be sought where it is deemed necessary by the Principal's Executive Group;

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, on what basis will the Academic Board formally sign off programme modifications?
options: Provided a majority of current students have voted in favour of the change in a formal ballot
Provided the External Examiner has countersigned the form and confirmed academic standards
Provided they comply with awarding body requirements and student interests have been protected
Provided the change has already been piloted for one academic term and evaluated by QESC
questions.explanation: The Academic Board signs off modifications provided they comply with awarding body requirements and the College is satisfied that student interests have been protected.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic Board will formally sign off modifications, provided that these comply with awarding body requirements and the College is satisfied that student interests have been protected;

questions.question: An awarding body changes a programme in a way that would count as a minor modification under the College's criteria. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what should the College do?
options: Implement it directly, as the awarding body's own approval replaces the College's internal processes
Consider it through this policy and, where necessary, the Programme Design and Development Policy
Refer it straight to the Academic Board for sign-off, bypassing the PEG and QESC review stages
Log it with the Quality Assurance Department and adopt it without College consultation or review
questions.explanation: Awarding body changes that qualify as minor or major modifications are considered through the Programme Modification Policy and, where necessary, the Programme Design and Development Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of a change being made to a programme by the awarding body that would qualify as either a minor or major modification according to the College's criteria, the College will consider the modification through this Programme Modification Policy and, where necessary, the Programme Design and Development Policy;

questions.question: According to the Programme Modification Policy, how should revised programme documentation be submitted with the Programme Minor Modification Form?
options: As a clean final copy signed off by the Programme Leader
As a brief summary sent to Quality Assurance after approval
As a PDF of the newly added sections
As revised versions marked with track changes
questions.explanation: The policy requires revised versions of programme documentation to be submitted with the form and marked with track changes.
questions.source_excerpt: Revised versions of programme documentation must be submitted with the form. These should be marked with track changes;

questions.question: According to the aims of the Programme Modification Policy, in what way should it be possible to introduce enhancements to a programme?
options: Only when the awarding body requires it
Immediately, with approval sought afterwards
In a timely and controlled manner
Only at the point of annual revalidation
questions.explanation: One of the policy's aims is that there are no unnecessary barriers to enhancing a programme and that enhancements can be introduced in a timely and controlled manner.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy ensures that there are no unnecessary barriers to making modifications to enhance a programme and that it is possible to introduce enhancements in a timely and controlled manner;

questions.question: According to the Programme Modification Policy, through which College mechanism can LCC identify where changes to enhance a programme may be made?
options: Its annual monitoring processes
Its termly timetabling review
Its admissions and enrolment reviews
Its annual staff appraisal cycle
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College can identify where changes to enhance a programme may be made through LCC's annual monitoring processes.
questions.source_excerpt: Through LCC's annual monitoring processes, the College can identify where changes to enhance a programme may be made.

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, to what must all programmes delivered by LCC, whether awarded by Pearson or other accrediting bodies, be benchmarked?
options: The College's Strategic Plan and its annual student recruitment targets
The awarding body's grading criteria and National Student Survey results
Comparable programmes offered by other London colleges and universities
The relevant national qualifications framework and Subject Benchmark Statements
questions.explanation: All LCC programmes, whatever the awarding body, must be benchmarked to the relevant national qualifications framework and Subject Benchmark Statements.
questions.source_excerpt: All programmes delivered by LCC, whether awarded by Pearson or other accrediting bodies, shall be benchmarked to the relevant national qualifications framework and Subject Benchmark Statements;

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, changes connected to course fees or other related charges must be considered in accordance with which documents?
options: The Admissions Policy, Financial Regulations and Enhancement Action Plan
The Terms and Conditions, Tuition Fee and Refund Policy and Student Protection Plan
The Complaints Policy and Procedure, the Equality and Diversity Policy and the Strategic Plan
The awarding body's fee schedule and the Programme Design and Development Policy
questions.explanation: The policy states that changes connected to course fees or related charges must be considered in accordance with the Terms and Conditions, Tuition Fee and Refund Policy and Student Protection Plan.
questions.source_excerpt: changes connected to course fees or other related charges, which must be considered in accordance with the Terms and Conditions, Tuition Fee and Refund Policy and Student Protection Plan.

questions.question: According to the Programme Modification Policy, which of the following must any proposed programme modification identify?
options: The projected cost savings for the College as a whole
The names of all staff who support the proposal
The period of time to which the change applies
The marketing campaign planned for new applicants
questions.explanation: Every proposed modification must identify, among other things, the period of time to which the change applies; cost savings, supporters' names and marketing plans are not required.
questions.source_excerpt: Any proposed modification must identify the valid reason for the change, the students and applicants affected, the period of time to which the change applies, the consultation undertaken, the measures proposed to protect students and any equality or accessibility implications.

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, up to what proportion of a programme's units may be replaced as an example of a minor modification?
options: Up to 10%
Up to 20%
Up to 50%
Up to 30%
questions.explanation: The policy gives replacing up to 30% of the programme's units as an example of a minor modification, provided the cumulative effect does not materially alter the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Examples of minor modifications may include replacing up to 30% of the programme's units, making changes to assessment methods, swapping modules between years or updating learning resources

questions.question: How does the Programme Modification Policy describe major modifications?
options: More extensive changes that go to the heart of the educational experience
Changes to a single module that do not affect the programme's learning outcomes
Any change requested by students through the annual programme feedback survey
Routine updates to reading lists and learning resources made during the year
questions.explanation: The policy describes major modifications as more extensive changes that go to the heart of the educational experience; changes usually confined to a single module or a few linked modules are minor.
questions.source_excerpt: Major modifications are more extensive changes and go to the heart of the educational experience.

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, who must be consulted as part of the design process for a major modification?
options: Staff only, with students told after approval
Students, staff and external stakeholders
Staff and students, with externals only if PEG decides
The awarding body only
questions.explanation: For major modifications, students, staff and external stakeholders must all be consulted as part of the design process.
questions.source_excerpt: Students, staff and external stakeholders must be consulted as part of the design process.

questions.question: Where a modification may change mode of study, teaching location or facilities, what does the Programme Modification Policy require the College to record?
options: Only the approval date and the name of the approving committee
Staff workload hours and the costs incurred in making the change
Individual student attendance before and after the change
Decisions, mitigations, communications and any residual risks
questions.explanation: The measures for such modifications include recording decisions, mitigations, communications and any residual risks.
questions.source_excerpt: g) recording decisions, mitigations, communications and any residual risks.

questions.question: When an awarding body or partner organisation modifies its provision, what does the Programme Modification Policy say the College must continue to ensure in all cases?
options: That the awarding body's changes are adopted in full within the same academic term
That affected students are offered an automatic transfer to another suitable programme
That its teaching, resources, facilities and student support remain suitable for the programme
That the External Examiner has approved the change before it is communicated to students
questions.explanation: In all cases the College must ensure that its learning, teaching and assessment strategy, staff, learning resources, facilities and student support remain suitable to deliver the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: In all cases, the College must continue to ensure that its learning, teaching and assessment strategy, teaching staff, learning resources, facilities and student support arrangements remain suitable to deliver the programme;

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, who will ensure that revised documentation for an approved minor modification is communicated to all relevant departments?
options: The Programme Leader
The Chair of PEG
The Quality Assurance Department
The Academic Board Secretary
questions.explanation: The policy makes the Programme Leader responsible for ensuring revised documentation is communicated to all relevant departments.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader will ensure that revised documentation is communicated to all relevant departments.

questions.question: According to the Programme Modification Policy, where a modification may materially affect students or applicants, what must the communication plan identify?
options: Only the date of the change and the name of the committee that approved it
Who will be informed, when and how, the support available and any options open to them
The staff who proposed the change and the results of the internal vote on it
A summary of every objection raised by students and staff during the consultation
questions.explanation: The communication plan must identify who will be informed, when, the method of communication, the support available and any options available to them.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a modification may materially affect students or applicants, the communication plan must identify who will be informed, when they will be informed, the method of communication, the support available and any options available to them.

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, where must a Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment and its supporting evidence be retained?
options: In each student's personal file
With the External Examiner report
On the College's public website
With the modification record
questions.explanation: The assessment and any supporting evidence must be retained with the modification record and made available to PEG, QESC, Academic Board and relevant committees as required.
questions.source_excerpt: The assessment and any supporting evidence must be retained with the modification record and made available to PEG, QESC, Academic Board and relevant governance committees as required.

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, to whose attention should a Programme Leader or other stakeholder bring proposals for programme modification?
options: The Chair of the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee
The Head of the Quality Assurance Department
The Chair of the Principal's Executive Group
The Secretary to the Academic Board
questions.explanation: The policy states that proposals for programme modification should be brought to the attention of the Chair of PEG (the Principal's Executive Group).
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader or other stakeholder should bring proposals for programme modification to the attention of the Chair of PEG.

questions.question: According to the Programme Modification Policy, where is good practice identified in the modification process added so that it can be shared with other departments?
options: The institutional Enhancement Action Plan
The institutional risk register
The Programme Minor Modification Form
The College's Access and Participation Plan
questions.explanation: Good practice identified in the modification process is added to the institutional Enhancement Action Plan so it can be disseminated to other departments.
questions.source_excerpt: Good practice identified in the process is added to the institutional Enhancement Action Plan so that it can be disseminated to other departments.

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, which department maintains the records of programme modifications, including their rationale, consultation and approval route?
options: The Registry and Admissions Department
The Quality Assurance Department
The Human Resources Department
The Marketing and Communications Department
questions.explanation: The Quality Assurance Department maintains records of programme modifications, including the rationale, consultation, approval route and related measures.
questions.source_excerpt: The Quality Assurance Department will maintain records of programme modifications, including ... the rationale, consultation, approval route, impact assessment, communication plan and any measures taken to protect affected students;

questions.question: Under the Programme Modification Policy, how will any complaints arising from programme modifications be considered?
options: Under the Adverse Occurrence Policy
Under the Academic Appeals Procedure
Under the awarding body's complaints process
Under the Complaints Policy and Procedure
questions.explanation: Complaints arising from programme modifications are considered under the College's Complaints Policy and Procedure and used to inform policy review.
questions.source_excerpt: Any complaints arising from programme modifications will be considered under the Complaints Policy and Procedure and used to inform policy review and continuous improvement.

questions.question: When completing the consultation section of the Programme Minor Modification Form, what must a proposer do if consultation has not taken place?
options: Leave the section blank and ask PEG to arrange the consultation at a later date
Delay the proposal until a full student survey has been completed and analysed
Explain why, and set out the alternative arrangements used to protect student interests
Obtain the External Examiner's written approval to proceed without consultation
questions.explanation: The form requires the proposer to explain why consultation has not taken place and set out the alternative arrangements used to protect student interests.
questions.source_excerpt: Where consultation has not taken place, explain why and set out the alternative arrangements used to protect student interests.

questions.question: A Programme Leader proposes moving a full-time programme to blended delivery. Under the Programme Modification Policy, when should the proposal set out measures to address the needs of specific student groups, including accessibility needs?
options: After implementation, as part of the first annual monitoring report on the change
Only once an affected student has raised a concern under the Complaints Policy
In the proposal itself, before approval is granted wherever possible
After Academic Board sign-off, within the communication and mitigation plan
questions.explanation: Where changes are proposed to mode of study, the proposal must expressly set out measures for specific student groups, including accessibility needs, before approval is granted wherever possible.
questions.source_excerpt: Where changes are proposed to mode of study, teaching location or facilities, the proposal must expressly set out measures to address the needs of specific student groups, including accessibility needs, before approval is granted wherever possible.

questions.question: A Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment for a move to online teaching finds that students with digital access needs may be adversely affected. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what must the assessment then set out?
options: The measures to be taken to mitigate that impact, such as assistive technology
A statement that the benefit to other students outweighs the impact on this group
A recommendation that the affected students transfer to a different programme
A referral of the affected students to the Complaints Policy and Procedure
questions.explanation: The assessment must set out the measures that will be taken to mitigate any adverse impact, which may include assistive technology, additional support or other reasonable adjustments.
questions.source_excerpt: The assessment must set out the measures that will be taken to mitigate any adverse impact. This may include consultation, accessible alternative arrangements, timetable adjustments, assistive technology, alternative facilities, additional academic support

questions.question: A proposal would rewrite the intended outcomes of most modules in a programme, but would not replace any units. Under the Programme Modification Policy, how should the proposal be classified?
options: As minor, because the 30% unit-replacement threshold has not been reached
As major, because it affects learning outcomes across numerous modules
As minor, provided the External Examiner confirms standards are unaffected
As outside the policy, because learning outcomes are set by the awarding body
questions.explanation: Minor modifications usually affect a single module or a few linked modules, whereas major modifications generally affect programme learning outcomes or numerous modules, so this change is major even though no units are replaced.
questions.source_excerpt: Minor modifications usually affect a single module or a small number of linked modules ... Major modifications generally affect the overall programme aims and learning outcomes or numerous modules across the programme;

questions.question: A minor modification changing one module's assessment method has just received final approval. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what should happen to the programme handbook and offer information?
options: They stay unchanged until the programme is next revalidated by the awarding body
They are updated for new applicants only, as current students keep the old version
They are updated only if a student or applicant asks for the latest information
They are updated to reflect the change, and must be accurate, clear and accessible
questions.explanation: Programme handbooks, offer information and other affected public information are updated to reflect approved changes, and the information must be accurate, clear, accessible and consistent with the Terms and Conditions.
questions.source_excerpt: The College website, programme handbooks, offer information, marketing material and any other affected public information will be updated to reflect approved changes. Information must be accurate, clear, accessible and consistent with the Terms and Conditions and other relevant policies;

questions.question: A Programme Leader has an idea for modifying a programme. Under the Programme Modification Policy, at what point does the process to modify and approve the programme commence?
options: Following discussion and agreement at the Principal's Executive Group
Once QESC has reviewed a first draft of the Minor Modification Form
Once the External Examiner has endorsed the idea in an annual report
Following a formal vote of the programme's students at a course meeting
questions.explanation: The process to modify and approve a programme commences following discussion and agreement at PEG, which decides how the modification fits with the Strategic Plan, regulatory obligations and operational capacity.
questions.source_excerpt: The process to modify and approve the programme commences following discussion and agreement at the Principal's Executive Group.

questions.question: After a programme modification is implemented, the team realises that some avoidable problems arose during the process. Under the Programme Modification Policy, where are lessons learned from the modification process discussed?
options: At QESC, as part of its internal review of the next modification proposal
At the Academic Board, which records them in its annual quality report
At PEG, so as to reduce the likelihood of avoidable issues recurring
With the awarding body, during its next periodic review of the provision
questions.explanation: To promote continuous improvement, lessons learned from the modification process are discussed at PEG so as to reduce the likelihood of avoidable issues recurring.
questions.source_excerpt: To promote continuous improvement, any lessons learned from the modification process are discussed at PEG so as to reduce the likelihood of avoidable issues recurring.

questions.question: A change of teaching location planned for next year will affect current students and applicants holding offers. Under the Programme Modification Policy's measures for such changes, who should be consulted?
options: Current students only, since applicants are not yet enrolled at the College
Affected students and, where appropriate, applicants and student representatives
Student representatives only, who respond on behalf of all affected students
The awarding body and External Examiner, who then inform students and applicants
questions.explanation: For changes to teaching location, the College's measures include consulting affected students and, where appropriate, applicants and student representatives.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a programme modification involves, or may result in, changes to mode of study, teaching location, facilities, delivery arrangements or access to support services, the College will take specific and proportionate measures ... b) consulting affected students and, where appropriate, applicants and student representatives;

questions.question: A programme is moving to online delivery and some students may struggle to continue their studies without extra help. Which measure does the Programme Modification Policy include for such a change to mode of study?
options: A full refund of tuition fees where a student finds online study too difficult
Deferring the change until every student confirms they can study online
Referring the students to the awarding body for individual support plans
Additional academic, pastoral, administrative or technical support where necessary
questions.explanation: The measures for changes to mode of study include providing additional academic, pastoral, administrative or technical support where necessary to enable continuation of study.
questions.source_excerpt: f) providing additional academic, pastoral, administrative or technical support where necessary to enable continuation of study;

questions.question: A partner organisation changes a programme's mode of study from face-to-face to online. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what will the College do in response?
options: Assess the impact on students and applicants and put proportionate protective measures in place
Adopt the change as notified, as partner-driven changes fall outside the College's policy
Notify students once the change takes effect, as no impact assessment is needed for it
Ask the partner to defer the change until all current students have completed their studies
questions.explanation: Where a partner-driven change affects mode of study, the College will assess the impact on students and applicants, consult affected students where appropriate and put proportionate measures in place to protect student interests.
questions.source_excerpt: Where an awarding body or partner-driven change affects qualifications to be awarded, course content, mode of study, teaching location, facilities or accessibility, the College will assess the impact on students and applicants, consult affected students where appropriate, and put in place proportionate measures to protect student interests.

questions.question: A fall in student numbers means that a programme's timetable and module structure need to change. Under the Programme Modification Policy, can a programme modification be proposed for this reason?
options: No, modifications may be proposed only to enhance a programme's academic content
No, falling student numbers can be addressed only by closing the programme
Yes, changes required because of student numbers are a listed circumstance
Yes, but only after the awarding body has formally instructed the College to act
questions.explanation: The circumstances in which modifications may be proposed include changes required because of student numbers, staffing, timetabling or other operational considerations.
questions.source_excerpt: Programme modifications may be proposed in circumstances including, but not limited to: ... f) changes required because of student numbers, staffing, timetabling, estate, health and safety, technology, adverse occurrence, business continuity or other operational considerations;

questions.question: When the Programme Modification Policy is reviewed annually, the review considers whether modifications had a disproportionate impact on particular student groups. What does it also consider about the mitigation measures?
options: Whether they cost less than the arrangements they replaced
Whether they were timely, accessible and effective
Whether the awarding body approved them in advance
Whether student representatives requested them first
questions.explanation: The annual review considers whether modifications had a disproportionate impact on particular student groups and whether mitigation measures were timely, accessible and effective.
questions.source_excerpt: The annual review of this policy will include consideration of whether modifications have had a disproportionate impact on particular student groups, including disabled students and students requiring reasonable adjustments, and whether mitigation measures were timely, accessible and effective;

questions.question: An employer suggests updating a module to reflect current industry practice. Under the Programme Modification Policy, how should this suggestion be treated?
options: Set aside, as changes may be identified only through annual monitoring processes
Passed to the awarding body, which alone decides on changes suggested by employers
Held back until the External Examiner has endorsed it in their annual report
Considered as an opportunity for change arising from engagement with employers
questions.explanation: Besides annual monitoring, opportunities for change may be identified through engagement with employers and other stakeholders, and employer input is a listed reason for proposing modifications.
questions.source_excerpt: Through LCC's annual monitoring processes, the College can identify where changes to enhance a programme may be made. Opportunities for change may also be identified through engagement with students, staff, external examiners, employers, professional bodies, awarding bodies, partner organisations and other stakeholders;

questions.question: A lecturer argues that, because the Programme Modification Policy aims to remove unnecessary barriers to enhancement, a small change to one module's assessment method can be made informally. What does the policy require?
options: Enhancement must be timely and controlled, so the Programme Minor Modification Form must still be completed
An informal change is acceptable provided it is reported to PEG at the end of the academic year
An informal change is acceptable provided the External Examiner confirms that academic standards are unaffected
Only changes spanning several linked modules need to follow the formal minor modification route
questions.explanation: The aim is to allow enhancement in a timely and controlled manner; changing assessment methods is an example of a minor modification, for which the Programme Minor Modification Form must be completed.
questions.source_excerpt: it is possible to introduce enhancements in a timely and controlled manner; ... Examples of minor modifications may include ... making changes to assessment methods ... The Programme Minor Modification Form must be completed;

questions.question: A Programme Leader plans a minor modification that will not materially affect students' programme, learning experience or contractual expectations. What does the Programme Modification Policy require regarding students?
options: No student involvement, as students take part only where a change materially affects them
Students must be consulted, and their consent is sought where a change may materially affect them
The written consent of every existing student must be obtained before PEG considers the proposal
Students are told once the Academic Board has approved the change, without prior consultation
questions.explanation: For a minor modification, consultation must include staff and students; the consent of existing students is sought where a change may materially affect their programme, learning experience or contractual expectations.
questions.source_excerpt: The consent of existing students, and consultation with applicants where relevant, will be sought in respect of programme modifications where the change may materially affect their programme, learning experience or contractual expectations; ... Consultation must include staff and students.

questions.question: After a programme moves to blended delivery, a student with a specific learning difficulty needs adjustments to both teaching delivery and assessment arrangements. Under the Programme Modification Policy, how should this be handled?
options: Adjust teaching delivery only, as assessment arrangements fall outside the modification measures
Refer the student to the Complaints Policy and Procedure, which governs requests for adjustments
Make reasonable adjustments to both, in line with the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy
Defer any adjustments until the awarding body has formally approved the programme's move to blended delivery
questions.explanation: The measures for mode-of-study changes include reasonable adjustments to teaching delivery and assessment arrangements, implemented in accordance with the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy and the Equality and Diversity Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Reasonable adjustments will be considered and implemented where required, in accordance with the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy and the Equality and Diversity Policy; ... implementing reasonable adjustments where required, including adjustments to ... teaching delivery, timetabling, facilities, assessment arrangements or support services;

questions.question: A manager says a proposed programme change cannot go forward because its reason does not appear among the circumstances listed in the Programme Modification Policy. Is the manager correct?
options: Yes, modifications may be proposed only in the circumstances that are expressly listed in the policy
Yes, unless PEG first grants a formal exemption allowing an unlisted reason to be relied upon
No, an unlisted reason is acceptable and the proposal need not state any reason for the change
No, the list is not exhaustive, but the proposal must still identify a valid reason for the change
questions.explanation: The circumstances are listed as 'including, but not limited to', so the list is not exhaustive, but every proposal must still identify the valid reason for the change.
questions.source_excerpt: Programme modifications may be proposed in circumstances including, but not limited to: ... Any proposed modification must identify the valid reason for the change,

questions.question: A proposal would replace 20% of a programme's units, but the change would materially alter the student experience. How should it be treated under the Programme Modification Policy?
options: As a major modification, because it materially alters the student experience
As a minor modification, because fewer than 30% of the programme's units are replaced
As a minor modification, provided the Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment is completed
As an awarding body matter, since the choice of units is set by the awarding body alone
questions.explanation: Replacing up to 30% of units is a minor example only where the effect does not materially alter the programme or student experience; changes that materially alter the student experience are listed as major.
questions.source_excerpt: Examples of minor modifications may include replacing up to 30% of the programme's units ... provided that the cumulative effect does not materially alter the programme or student experience; ... course closure or changes that materially alter the student experience;

questions.question: The consultation plan for a major modification covers students, staff and external stakeholders but says nothing about accessibility. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what must the consultation also include where relevant?
options: A ballot of current students, with the change going ahead only if a majority agree
Consideration of affected student groups, accessibility needs and reasonable adjustments
An accessibility audit of the College's facilities carried out by the awarding body
Written confirmation from each disabled student that they accept the proposed change in full
questions.explanation: For major modifications, consultation with students, staff and external stakeholders must include consideration of affected student groups, accessibility needs and reasonable adjustments where relevant.
questions.source_excerpt: Students, staff and external stakeholders must be consulted as part of the design process. The consultation must include consideration of affected student groups, accessibility needs and reasonable adjustments where relevant.

questions.question: A move of teaching to a new campus is planned for next year and is not urgent. The team proposes to make the move first and complete the accessibility and impact measures afterwards. Under the Programme Modification Policy, when must those measures be applied?
options: As soon as reasonably practicable after the move, as that is the rule for any change of location
Whenever PEG decides, as PEG may waive the measures for moves that are planned well in advance
Before the move wherever possible; later completion is reserved for urgent operational cases
During the first term at the new campus, once students' actual experience of it can be assessed
questions.explanation: The measures must be applied before any change is implemented wherever possible; completing the impact assessment afterwards is for urgent operational circumstances requiring immediate action, which a planned move is not.
questions.source_excerpt: These measures must be applied before any change is implemented wherever possible. Where urgent operational circumstances require immediate action, the College will implement interim measures and complete the impact assessment as soon as reasonably practicable.

questions.question: Where a programme modification may change mode of study, teaching location or facilities, which of the following is NOT one of the measures the Programme Modification Policy says the College will take?
options: Identifying students who may be disproportionately affected, including disabled students
Assessing the accessibility, equality and student protection impacts of the change
Recording decisions, mitigations, communications and any residual risks
Obtaining the written consent of every applicant before the change is approved
questions.explanation: The measures include identifying affected students, assessing impacts and recording decisions and risks; applicants are consulted where appropriate, but the policy does not require every applicant's written consent.
questions.source_excerpt: a) identifying students who may be disproportionately affected, including disabled students and students requiring reasonable adjustments; ... b) consulting affected students and, where appropriate, applicants and student representatives; ... g) recording decisions, mitigations, communications and any residual risks.

questions.question: An awarding body describes its revision to a programme as minor, but the revision replaces 40% of the programme's units. Under the Programme Modification Policy, how should the College handle it?
options: Classify it by the College's own criteria as major and reconsider it through the Programme Design and Development Policy
Accept the awarding body's classification and process the change using the Programme Minor Modification Form
Implement it without internal review, as changes made by an awarding body fall outside the College's own policy
Refer it to QESC for approval as minor, because the awarding body has already validated the revised programme
questions.explanation: Awarding body changes are classified according to the College's criteria; replacing more than 30% of units is a major modification, which requires reconsideration through the Programme Design and Development Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event of a change being made to a programme by the awarding body that would qualify as either a minor or major modification according to the College's criteria, the College will consider the modification through this Programme Modification Policy and, where necessary, the Programme Design and Development Policy; ... Examples include replacing more than 30% of the programme's units,

questions.question: PEG does not accept a Programme Leader's minor modification proposal. The Programme Leader then wants to send it straight to QESC and the Academic Board. What does the Programme Modification Policy allow?
options: Submission to QESC, as QESC's internal review is independent of the PEG decision
No onward submission, as QESC review follows only if PEG accepts it
Direct submission to the Academic Board, which may overrule the PEG decision
Resubmission to QESC once the External Examiner has endorsed the proposal
questions.explanation: Under the minor modification procedure, the proposal is reviewed by QESC and then submitted to the Academic Board only if accepted by PEG, so there is no route around a PEG decision not to accept it.
questions.source_excerpt: The proposal, together with supporting documentation, should be submitted to the Principal's Executive Group (PEG). If accepted by PEG, the proposal will be reviewed internally by the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee (QESC) and then submitted for final approval by the Academic Board;

questions.question: An email to students about an approved change sets out what is changing, the support available and the options open to them. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what else must students be told?
options: The minutes of the PEG meeting at which the change was agreed
The names of the staff who proposed and approved the change
The reasons for the change and its expected impact on them
The External Examiner's written opinion on the change
questions.explanation: Students must be informed about approved changes, the reasons for them, the expected impact, the support available and their options; this email omits the reasons and the expected impact.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will be informed clearly and in a timely manner about approved changes, the reasons for those changes, the expected impact, the support available and any options open to them,

questions.question: A proposal would change only a programme's assessment arrangements, replacing in-person exams with timed online tests; mode of study, location and facilities stay the same. Is a Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment required under the Programme Modification Policy?
options: No, it is required only for changes to mode of study, teaching location or facilities
No, as assessment changes are minor modifications and need no impact assessment
Only if a student with reasonable adjustments complains after the change is made
Yes, it is required for any proposed modification that may affect assessment arrangements
questions.explanation: The assessment must be completed for any proposed modification that may affect assessment arrangements, not only for changes to mode of study, teaching location or facilities.
questions.source_excerpt: A Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment must be completed for any proposed modification that may affect mode of study, teaching location, facilities, delivery arrangements, support services, assessment arrangements or the student experience of particular groups;

questions.question: A Student Group and Accessibility Impact Assessment for a move to a more distant campus finds that commuting students will be disproportionately affected. Which mitigation does the Programme Modification Policy expressly list that fits this impact?
options: Travel-related support for affected students
A partial refund of tuition fees for the year
Exemption from the College's attendance monitoring
Priority transfer to another provider's programme
questions.explanation: The assessment must consider commuting students and set out mitigation measures, which the policy says may include travel-related support; fee refunds, attendance exemptions and transfers to other providers are not listed.
questions.source_excerpt: The assessment must consider whether any students may be disproportionately affected, including ... commuting students ... The assessment must set out the measures that will be taken to mitigate any adverse impact. This may include ... travel-related support

questions.question: An impact assessment for moving a programme to evening teaching considers disabled students only, yet the change would disproportionately affect students who work evening shifts, a group the Programme Modification Policy does not name. Must the assessment consider them?
options: No, only the student groups expressly named in the policy need to be considered
Yes, the assessment must also consider any other relevant student group affected
No, students' work commitments are personal matters outside the assessment's scope
Yes, but only once those students have raised a formal complaint about the change
questions.explanation: The assessment must consider whether any students may be disproportionately affected, including the named groups and any other relevant student group, so it is not limited to groups the policy names.
questions.source_excerpt: The assessment must consider whether any students may be disproportionately affected, including disabled students, ... students with protected characteristics and any other relevant student group;

questions.question: A proposed modification is educationally sound, but it is unclear whether the College has the staffing capacity to deliver it. Under the Programme Modification Policy, which body decides how the modification fits with the College's operational capacity?
options: QESC, during its internal review once PEG has accepted the proposal
The Academic Board, at the point it formally signs off the modification
PEG, which also decides how it fits with the institutional Strategic Plan
The Quality Assurance Department, when it records the approval route
questions.explanation: PEG decides how a modification fits with the institutional Strategic Plan, regulatory obligations, student protection responsibilities and operational capacity; QESC review, Academic Board sign-off and QA record-keeping are separate roles.
questions.source_excerpt: PEG will decide how the modification fits with the institutional Strategic Plan, regulatory obligations, student protection responsibilities and operational capacity;

questions.question: A Student Services manager identifies a minor change that would improve a programme. Under the Programme Modification Policy, how should the change be taken forward?
options: The manager completes the Minor Modification Form and submits it directly to QESC for review
The manager cannot raise it, as only Programme Leaders may bring modification ideas to PEG
The manager sends it to the Academic Board, which then refers it on to PEG for initial agreement
The manager raises it with the Chair of PEG; the formal proposal comes from the Programme Leader
questions.explanation: Any stakeholder, not only a Programme Leader, should bring modification proposals to the attention of the Chair of PEG, while the formal minor modification proposal should come from the Programme Leader using the Programme Minor Modification Form.
questions.source_excerpt: Proposals to make minor modifications to a programme should come from the Programme Leader. These should be made using the Programme Minor Modification Form; ... The Programme Leader or other stakeholder should bring proposals for programme modification to the attention of the Chair of PEG.

questions.question: A completed modification revealed an avoidable delay in consulting students and also an effective way of engaging applicants. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what happens to each?
options: The delay is discussed at PEG; the approach enters the Enhancement Action Plan
Both are reviewed by QESC and then reported to the Academic Board at the end of the year
The delay is added to the Enhancement Action Plan; the approach is discussed at PEG
Both are logged in the institutional risk register and reviewed in annual monitoring
questions.explanation: Lessons learned from the modification process are discussed at PEG to reduce the likelihood of avoidable issues recurring, while good practice is added to the institutional Enhancement Action Plan to be disseminated to other departments.
questions.source_excerpt: To promote continuous improvement, any lessons learned from the modification process are discussed at PEG so as to reduce the likelihood of avoidable issues recurring. Good practice identified in the process is added to the institutional Enhancement Action Plan so that it can be disseminated to other departments.

questions.question: Over a year, several separate modifications led to complaints from part-time students about timetabling. Under the Programme Modification Policy, how should these complaints and the modification records be used?
options: They are handled under the Adverse Occurrence Policy, as timetabling changes are operational
Complaints go through the Complaints Policy and Procedure; records are reviewed for recurring issues
The complaints are passed to the awarding body, which decides whether the modifications are reversed
The records are archived unchanged, as they are kept only as evidence that approval was given
questions.explanation: Complaints arising from modifications are considered under the Complaints Policy and Procedure and used to inform policy review, and modification records are reviewed to identify recurring issues and equality or accessibility impacts.
questions.source_excerpt: Modification records will be reviewed to identify recurring issues, equality or accessibility impacts, student protection risks and opportunities for enhancement; ... Any complaints arising from programme modifications will be considered under the Complaints Policy and Procedure and used to inform policy review and continuous improvement.

questions.question: Teaching will move next term to the only available building, which lacks step-free access, and some affected students use wheelchairs. What does the Programme Modification Policy require of the alternative location and arrangements?
options: Nothing specific, as accessibility is looked at only once students raise concerns
Affected students should normally interrupt their studies until a new building is found
They must be accessible, inclusive and suitable for affected students where reasonably practicable
Affected students should be referred to the Complaints Policy and Procedure to request another venue
questions.explanation: Alternative delivery arrangements, locations and facilities must be accessible, inclusive and suitable for affected students wherever reasonably practicable.
questions.source_excerpt: Alternative delivery arrangements, locations, facilities, timetables or support arrangements must be accessible, inclusive and suitable for affected students wherever reasonably practicable;

questions.question: PEG has accepted a minor modification moving a module's practical sessions to different facilities. During QESC's internal review it emerges that affected students were not consulted, although consultation was appropriate. Under the Programme Modification Policy, what should QESC do?
options: Approve it, as PEG's acceptance means the consultation point has already been settled
Forward it to the Academic Board, which may approve it on condition students are consulted later
Approve it, as consultation with students is required only for major modifications
Not approve it unless satisfied that affected students have been consulted where appropriate
questions.explanation: The bar on approving changes to facilities without assessment, consultation and protective measures applies to PEG, QESC and the Academic Board alike, so PEG's acceptance does not relieve QESC of being satisfied that affected students were consulted where appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: PEG, QESC and Academic Board must not approve any modification involving changes to mode of study, teaching location, facilities or delivery arrangements unless they are satisfied that the student group and accessibility impact has been assessed, affected students have been consulted where appropriate, and reasonable measures are in place to protect student interests;

questions.question: A Programme Leader consulted staff and students on a proposed change, but not external stakeholders, because PEG has not deemed external input necessary. Under the Programme Modification Policy, in which case is it acceptable not to consult external stakeholders?
options: If it is a minor modification, since for a major one externals must always be consulted
If it is a major modification, since external input is sought only where PEG deems it necessary
In either case, provided the External Examiner is sent the revised documentation after approval
In neither case, as every modification needs external stakeholder consultation
