questions.explanation: For a minor modification, consultation must include staff and students, with external input sought where PEG deems it necessary; for a major modification, students, staff and external stakeholders must all be consulted as part of the design process.
questions.source_excerpt: Consultation must include staff and students. External input, such as from the External Examiner, must be sought where it is deemed necessary by the Principal's Executive Group; ... Students, staff and external stakeholders must be consulted as part of the design process.

questions.question: PEG has accepted a minor modification and QESC has completed its internal review; the Academic Board meets next month. Marketing wants to update the College website and offer information now. Under the Programme Modification Policy, when should they be updated?
options: Now, as QESC's internal review completes the approval process for a minor modification
After the Academic Board's final approval, as public information reflects approved changes
Now, as PEG's acceptance was the approval and QESC's internal review is advisory only
Only once the External Examiner has confirmed the change in their next annual report to the College
questions.explanation: A minor modification accepted by PEG and reviewed by QESC still goes to the Academic Board for final approval, and public information such as the website and offer information is updated to reflect approved changes.
questions.source_excerpt: If accepted by PEG, the proposal will be reviewed internally by the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee (QESC) and then submitted for final approval by the Academic Board; ... The College website, programme handbooks, offer information, marketing material and any other affected public information will be updated to reflect approved changes.

policies.title: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Policy and Procedure

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, a current student asks to apply for RPL for a module they began studying three weeks ago. What is the correct position?
options: RPL cannot be applied for, because the student has already commenced the module concerned
RPL can be applied for at any point before the module's final assessment is submitted
RPL can be applied for, provided the Personal Tutor approves it as a late application
RPL can be applied for as long as the student has not yet received a grade for the module
questions.explanation: RPL applications may be made during the programme only if the student has not yet commenced the module concerned; this student has already started the module, so RPL cannot be applied for.
questions.source_excerpt: Applications for RPL should ideally be made before the start of the Programme, but can also be made during the Programme, as long as the student has not yet commenced the module for which s/he wishes to apply;

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, who is responsible for identifying prospective or existing students who might be eligible for RPL and informing them of the opportunities available?
options: Programme Leaders
Personal Tutors
The Admissions department
Module Leaders
questions.explanation: The policy gives Personal Tutors responsibility for identifying potentially eligible students and telling them about RPL opportunities.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors are responsible for identifying prospective or existing students who might be eligible for RPL and informing them of opportunities available;

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, who formally assesses an RPL claim?
options: The Personal Tutor who guided the applicant through assembling the portfolio
The Admissions department that handled the applicant's initial enquiry
The External Examiner appointed for the programme on which RPL is claimed
The Programme Leader for the course against which RPL is being claimed
questions.explanation: All RPL claims are formally assessed by the Programme Leader for the course against which RPL is claimed (who may delegate to a Module Leader where subject expertise is needed).
questions.source_excerpt: All RPL claims will be formally assessed by the Programme Leader for the course against which RPL is being claimed.

questions.question: According to the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Policy, what is the maximum permissible credit value for an RPL claim?
options: One quarter of the total credit value of the relevant programme
One third of the total credit value of the relevant programme
Half of the total credit value of the relevant programme
Two thirds of the total credit value of the relevant programme
questions.explanation: The RPL Policy caps any RPL claim at half of the total credit value of the relevant programme.
questions.source_excerpt: The maximum permissible credit value for an RPL claim is half of the total credit value of the relevant programme;

questions.question: A prospective student who has not yet joined a programme contacts you about applying for RPL but has no personal tutor. What does the RPL Policy say they should do?
options: Send their portfolio directly to the Programme Leader of their chosen programme for assessment
Wait until enrolment, when a personal tutor will be assigned and can arrange an RPL meeting
Contact the admissions department and arrange to meet a personal tutor of their chosen programme
Apply directly to the Assessment and Progression Board, which decides pre-enrolment RPL claims
questions.explanation: Prospective students without an assigned personal tutor should contact the admissions department and arrange to meet a personal tutor of their chosen programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Prospective students who have not yet been assigned a personal tutor, as they may not yet have joined the programme, should contact the admissions department and arrange to meet with a personal tutor of their chosen programme.

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, for which of the following is RPL NOT applicable?
options: Work-based learning gained before admission
Modules the student has not yet commenced
Pearson Higher National QCF to RQF transfers
External assessment and set assignments
questions.explanation: The policy explicitly states that RPL is not applicable for external assessment and set assignments; the other options are all covered by RPL under the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: RPL is not applicable for external assessment and set assignments.

questions.question: A student shows you a draft RPL application describing years of job duties at great length, with lots of general information. Under the RPL Policy, what guidance should they be given?
options: Add further general background so the assessor understands the full experience
Base it on what was learned and how it was used, including only relevant details
Keep the detail, as credit is awarded for the experience itself rather than learning
Replace the narrative with a CV listing every role held and its duration
questions.explanation: The policy says applications should be based on what was learned, not the experience itself, and contain only relevant details, as vast amounts of general information make it harder for the assessor.
questions.source_excerpt: The application should be based on what was learned, not on the experience itself. It should only contain relevant details, without excessive amounts of writing (vast amounts of general information will make it harder for the assessor to see that the necessary learning has been covered);

questions.question: As a Personal Tutor in an RPL information and advice session, you compare a student's past learning with the programme's learning outcomes. Under the RPL Policy, what is the purpose at this stage?
options: To make a provisional RPL decision for the Board to approve
To award interim credit until the portfolio is formally assessed
Only to help the student decide whether they wish to pursue RPL
To assess the student's portfolio on the Programme Leader's behalf
questions.explanation: The policy states that at the information and advice stage the comparison is only to help students decide whether they wish to pursue RPL; formal assessment happens later.
questions.source_excerpt: The Personal Tutor works with prospective or current students to compare the past learning and experience against the learning outcomes of the programme. At this stage, this is only to help students to decide if they wish to pursue RPL;

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, how recent should the learning evidenced in an RPL claim normally be?
options: From within the last 5 years
From within the last 2 years
From within the last 3 years
From within the last 10 years
questions.explanation: The policy states the learning should be from within the last 5 years, although older learning may still be relevant in subjects where little change occurs, such as history or maths.
questions.source_excerpt: The learning should be from within the last 5 years. For some subjects, where little change occurs, e.g. history, maths, if the learning is less recent, it may still be relevant to the course;

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, how are RPL decisions proposed by the Programme Leader approved?
options: They are reported to the Assessment and Progression Board, which approves them
They are reported to the Admissions department, which approves them
They are reported to the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee, which approves them
They are approved by the Personal Tutor, who then informs the student
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader reports RPL decisions to LCC's Assessment and Progression Board, which is responsible for approving them.
questions.source_excerpt: RPL decisions are to be reported to LCC's Assessment and Progression Board by the Programme Leader. The Board is responsible for approving decisions proposed by the Programme Leader;

questions.question: An applicant to a Pearson programme wants to make an RPCL claim for a single individual unit. Under the RPL Policy, what is the position?
options: The claim is accepted, provided the unit's learning outcomes are fully mapped to the module
The claim is accepted once the appropriate External Examiner confirms it by Chair's Action
The claim is accepted, as individual units count as certificated learning on Pearson programmes
The claim is not accepted, as individual units are not defined as awards for Pearson programmes
questions.explanation: Individual units are not defined as awards for Pearson programmes, so the policy states RPCL claims on individual units are not accepted.
questions.source_excerpt: Individual units are not defined as awards for Pearson programmes. Therefore any RPCL claim on individual units are not accepted.

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, how long must assessment and internal verification records, along with any additional RPL records, be retained?
options: For one year following certification
For three years following certification
For five years following certification
Until the student completes the module concerned
questions.explanation: The policy requires these records to be retained for a three-year period following certification.
questions.source_excerpt: Assessment and internal verification records, along with any additional RPL records completed, will be retained for a three-year period following certification;

questions.question: Under LCC's RPL Policy, what does the generic term Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) refer to?
options: Recognition of learning from LCC modules that a student failed and now wishes to retake
Recognition of certificated, non-certificated, work-based or experiential learning prior to admission
Recognition of the professional experience itself, measured by the number of years worked
Recognition of formal qualifications only, provided they have already led to credit on the FHEQ
questions.explanation: The policy defines RPL as the generic term for recognising certificated, non-certificated, work-based or experiential learning that occurs prior to admission to a course or stage of a course.
questions.source_excerpt: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) is the generic term used for the recognition of certificated, non-certificated, work-based or experiential learning that occurs prior to admission to a particular course or stage of a course;

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, what does Recognition of Prior Certificated Learning (RPCL) assess and formally acknowledge?
options: Previous Higher Education level learning, e.g. employer-based awards, that has not led to FHEQ credit
Previous learning of any level, provided it has already led to an FHEQ qualification elsewhere
School-level learning from GCSE and A level qualifications that were completed before admission
Previous learning below Higher Education level, where a certificate of attendance is provided
questions.explanation: RPCL covers previous learning, such as employer-based awards, that is at Higher Education level but has not led to credit or qualifications positioned on the FHEQ.
questions.source_excerpt: Recognition of Prior Certificated Learning (RPCL) is the assessment and formal acknowledgement of previous learning, such as that gained through professional development or employer-based awards, which is at Higher Education level but which has not led to the award of credit or qualifications positioned on the Framework for Higher Education Qualifications (FHEQ).

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, what does Recognition of Prior Experiential Learning (RPEL) identify, assess and formally acknowledge?
options: The experience itself, judged by its length and the seniority of the roles held
Attendance at lectures, recorded before the end-of-term assessment of a module
Credit already awarded for qualifications positioned on the FHEQ at other institutions
The learning gained through informal or non-formal experiences, not the experience itself
questions.explanation: RPEL acknowledges the learning gained through informal or non-formal experiences; the policy is explicit that it is not an assessment of the experience itself.
questions.source_excerpt: Recognition of Prior Experiential Learning (RPEL) is the process of identification, assessment and formal acknowledgement of the learning gained through informal or non-formal experiences, not the assessment of the experience itself.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the stated aims of London Churchill College's Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Policy?
options: To enable applicants to receive credit towards the whole of their chosen course
To make RPL processes known only to applicants who ask about them at admission
To reduce duplication of learning, leading to a better overall student experience
To shorten programme duration for all applicants with over five years' work experience
questions.explanation: Among its aims, LCC seeks through RPL to reduce duplication of learning, leading to a better overall student experience.
questions.source_excerpt: Reduce duplication of learning leading to a better overall student experience;

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, who can make determinations in respect of RPL at London Churchill College?
options: Any Admissions officer who has reviewed the applicant's portfolio
Any Personal Tutor, whether or not they have completed RPL training
Senior professional services managers authorised by the Academic Board
Only qualified academics who have completed RPL training
questions.explanation: The policy states that only qualified academics with RPL training can make determinations in respect of RPL at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Only qualified academics with RPL training can make determinations in respect of RPL at the College;

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, who are applicants or students wishing to apply for RPL, or seeking more information about it, advised to meet with?
options: Their Personal Tutor
Their Module Leader
Their Programme Leader
The Head of Quality
questions.explanation: Applicants or students wishing to apply for RPL or seeking additional information are advised to meet with their personal tutor.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants or students wishing to make an application for RPL or seeking additional information are advised to meet with their personal tutor;

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, what should RPL applicants be aware of about the process, compared with completing a module through normal study?
options: It may lower their overall award, as RPL units do not count towards overall grades
It can be time consuming and could become more difficult and complex than normal study
It is available only once the student has attended the first lectures of the module
It could be refused if their learning is over two years old, whatever the subject
questions.explanation: The policy warns that RPL can be time consuming and, depending on previous experience, could become more difficult and complex than completing the module normally.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants should be aware that the process can be time consuming and, depending on their previous experience, could become more difficult and complex than it would be to complete the module through the normal means of attending the lectures and taking the assessment at the end of the term.

questions.question: When using the Application for RPL Form, what does the RPL Policy require applicants to list and explain?
options: All relevant learning outcomes, with a statement for each on how their prior learning qualifies
Every job role held in the last ten years, with the dates and hours worked in each role
The grades they expect for each module, with a justification for each proposed grade
Two referees who can confirm the experience described, with contact details for each
questions.explanation: Applicants must list all the relevant learning outcomes on the Application for RPL Form and provide a statement for each explaining how their prior learning qualifies.
questions.source_excerpt: Using the Application for RPL Form, applicants must list all the relevant learning outcomes and provide statements for each outcome to explain how they believe their prior learning qualifies for RPL;

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, the evidence an applicant chooses to support an RPL claim must be which of the following?
options: Certified, notarised and translated
Original, signed and dated
Brief, official and certificated
Valid, current and reliable
questions.explanation: The applicant decides which evidence to use, and the policy requires that evidence to be valid, current and reliable.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the applicant's responsibility to decide which evidence used, which must be valid, current and reliable.

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, what will be made available to anyone considering applying for RPL, giving them the learning outcomes to map their prior learning to?
options: Programme and Module specifications
Previous applicants' successful portfolios
The External Examiner's annual reports
Minutes of the Assessment and Progression Board
questions.explanation: Programme and Module specifications are made available to anyone considering RPL, and they set out the learning outcomes applicants must map their prior learning to.
questions.source_excerpt: Programme and Module specifications will be made available to anyone considering applications for RPL. The specifications will provide applicants with the Learning Outcomes to which they will be required to map their prior learning.

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, to whom may the Programme Leader delegate the assessment of an RPL claim where specific subject expertise is required?
options: The student's personal tutor
The appropriate External Examiner
The relevant Module Leader
The Quality Assurance department
questions.explanation: The Programme Leader may delegate assessment of an RPL claim to the relevant Module Leader where specific subject expertise is required.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader may delegate the assessment to the relevant Module Leader where specific subject expertise is required;

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, what may be arranged during the assessment of an RPL portfolio to check the applicant's claims to learning?
options: A hearing before an Academic Appeals panel
A visit to the applicant's workplace
A reference check with a past employer
An assessment interview with the applicant
questions.explanation: When assessing a portfolio, an assessment interview may be arranged to check the applicant's claims to learning.
questions.source_excerpt: An assessment interview may be arranged to check claims to learning.

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, what is evidence used for RPL on Pearson programmes subject to?
options: A separate Pearson RPL audit instead of standards verification
Pearson's standards verification, as normal
Re-marking by a second Programme Leader
Pearson's prior approval of each individual RPL decision
questions.explanation: Evidence used for RPL on Pearson programmes is subject to Pearson's standards verification in the normal way.
questions.source_excerpt: Evidence used for RPL on Pearson Programmes will be subject to Pearson's standards verification as normal.

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, where is the guidance provided for a learner who wishes to appeal against an RPL assessment decision?
options: LCC's Complaints Policy and Procedure
Pearson's learner appeals guidance on its website
LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure
The Assessment and Progression Board's appeals procedure
questions.explanation: As with any assessment decision, the guidance for appealing an RPL decision is provided in LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: if a learner wishes to appeal against a decision made in relation to assessment the guidance to follow is provided in LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure.

questions.question: According to the RPL Policy, through which body does London Churchill College monitor its use of RPL?
options: The Assessment and Progression Board
The Quality Enhancement Steering Committee
The Admissions and Recruitment Committee
The Learning and Teaching Quality Committee
questions.explanation: LCC monitors its use of RPL through the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee, which develops and monitors all College policies and procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will monitor its use of RPL through the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee, which is responsible for developing and monitoring all College policies and procedures.

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, what does the College refer to when facilitating RPL for Pearson Higher National students transferring from the QCF to the RQF?
options: The College's internal unit equivalence tables
The FHEQ level descriptors for each unit
The Mapping documents published by Pearson
Pearson's standards verification reports on the programme
questions.explanation: The College facilitates QCF to RQF transfers for Pearson Higher National students with reference to the Mapping documents published by Pearson.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will facilitate RPL for Pearson Higher National students wishing to transfer from the Qualifications and Credit Framework (QCF) to the Regulated Qualifications Framework (RQF), with reference to the Mapping documents published by Pearson.

questions.question: A student on a 240-credit programme hopes an RPL claim will cover 150 credits of their course. Under the RPL Policy, what is the position?
options: The claim may cover 150 credits if every learning outcome is fully mapped and evidenced
The claim cannot exceed 120 credits, half of the programme's total credit value
The claim cannot exceed 80 credits, which is one third of the programme's total credit value
The claim may cover 150 credits, as the credit cap applies only to RPCL and not to RPEL
questions.explanation: The maximum credit value for an RPL claim is half of the programme's total credit value, so 120 of 240 credits is the limit.
questions.source_excerpt: The maximum permissible credit value for an RPL claim is half of the total credit value of the relevant programme;

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy procedure, which sequence correctly shows the main stages an RPL claim passes through after the initial enquiry?
options: Portfolio assembly, advice session with Personal Tutor, Board approval, assessment by Programme Leader
Advice session with Personal Tutor, assessment by Programme Leader, portfolio assembly, Board approval
Advice session with Personal Tutor, portfolio assembly, assessment by Programme Leader, Board approval
Portfolio assembly, assessment by Programme Leader, advice session with Personal Tutor, Board approval
questions.explanation: After the initial enquiry the procedure runs through an information and advice session with the Personal Tutor, assembly of the portfolio, formal assessment by the Programme Leader and approval by the Board.
questions.source_excerpt: Information and Advice Session with Personal Tutor ... Assembly of Portfolio ... All RPL claims will be formally assessed by the Programme Leader for the course against which RPL is being claimed. ... The Board is responsible for approving decisions proposed by the Programme Leader;

questions.question: An RPL decision proposed by a Programme Leader is needed before the Assessment and Progression Board next meets. Under the RPL Policy, how can the decision be confirmed?
options: The Programme Leader's decision applies at once and is noted at the next Board
The Quality Enhancement Steering Committee confirms it on the Board's behalf
The Personal Tutor confirms it, provided the student agrees to it in writing
If the appropriate External Examiner agrees, it may be confirmed by Chair's Action
questions.explanation: Where a decision is needed before the next Board meets, confirmation is sought from the appropriate External Examiner and, if they agree, the decision may be confirmed by Chair's Action.
questions.source_excerpt: In cases where a decision is required before the next Board meets then confirmation will be sought from the appropriate External Examiner and, if s/he is in agreement, the decision may then be confirmed by Chair's Action.

questions.question: A Programme Leader delegates the assessment of an RPL claim to a Module Leader for their subject expertise. Under the RPL Policy, who reports the RPL decision to the Assessment and Progression Board?
options: The Module Leader who carried out the assessment
The Programme Leader for the course concerned
The Personal Tutor who guided the portfolio
The External Examiner for the programme
questions.explanation: Even where assessment is delegated to a Module Leader, RPL decisions are reported to the Assessment and Progression Board by the Programme Leader.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader may delegate the assessment to the relevant Module Leader where specific subject expertise is required; ... RPL decisions are to be reported to LCC's Assessment and Progression Board by the Programme Leader.

questions.question: While assessing an RPL portfolio, the assessor decides that further evidence is needed to support part of the learning claim. What does the RPL Policy say about this?
options: The claim is normally rejected, and a fresh application must be made next term
The Personal Tutor will normally supply the missing evidence for the applicant
The applicant will normally be given the opportunity to produce the evidence
The claim is normally passed to the Board to decide on the evidence already held
questions.explanation: The policy states that where further evidence is required, the applicant will normally be given the opportunity to produce it.
questions.source_excerpt: Where further evidence is required, the opportunity will normally be given to produce this.

questions.question: While assessing an RPL portfolio, a Programme Leader believes a certificate submitted as evidence may not be genuine. Under the RPL Policy, what should happen?
options: It is investigated by the College as suspected academic malpractice
It is referred to the External Examiner, who decides whether the claim proceeds
The certificate is set aside and the rest of the claim is assessed as normal
It is noted for the Board, which decides whether to accept the claim anyway
questions.explanation: The policy requires any instance of suspected academic malpractice arising in RPL assessment to be investigated by the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Any instances of suspected academic malpractice shall be investigated by the College.

questions.question: An RPL applicant's evidence for a maths module comes from learning they completed eight years ago. Under the RPL Policy, what is the position?
options: It is excluded, as all learning must be from within the last 5 years
It may be accepted, but only once the applicant retakes a maths qualification
It may be accepted, but only with a formal exemption from the External Examiner
It may still be relevant, as maths is a subject where little change occurs
questions.explanation: Learning should normally be from within the last 5 years, but for subjects where little change occurs, such as maths, less recent learning may still be relevant.
questions.source_excerpt: The learning should be from within the last 5 years. For some subjects, where little change occurs, e.g. history, maths, if the learning is less recent, it may still be relevant to the course;

questions.question: A student worries that units completed through RPL will stop them achieving a Merit or Distinction overall. What does the RPL Policy say?
options: RPL units are excluded from overall grades, so the overall award is capped at a Pass
RPL units are recorded as a Pass only, so a Merit or Distinction overall is not possible
RPL units count towards overall grades, so will not hinder a Merit or Distinction
RPL units count towards overall grades only where an assessment interview was held
questions.explanation: The policy states that RPL units count towards overall grades and so will not hinder the student from receiving a Merit or Distinction overall.
questions.source_excerpt: RPL units do count towards overall grades, and so will not hinder the student from receiving Merit or Distinction overall;

questions.question: A student's draft RPL application explains what they learned but never says when, where or with whom the learning took place. Which of the policy's application requirements does it fail to meet?
options: Details
Descriptive
Evidence-based
Reflective
questions.explanation: The Descriptive requirement asks applications to clearly describe the context of the learning activities, including when, where and with whom.
questions.source_excerpt: Descriptive: clearly describe the context of the learning activities in terms of when, where, with whom, etc.;

questions.question: A student assembling an RPL portfolio asks their Personal Tutor to choose which evidence to include. Under the RPL Policy, whose decision is this?
options: The applicant's, as the Personal Tutor guides the process but does not choose evidence
The Personal Tutor's, as they guide the applicant through completing the portfolio
The Programme Leader's, as they formally assess the portfolio for the course
The Module Leader's, as they hold the subject expertise for the module concerned
questions.explanation: The Personal Tutor guides the applicant through completing the portfolio, but it is the applicant's responsibility to decide which evidence is used.
questions.source_excerpt: The personal tutor will guide the applicant through the process of completing a portfolio, which will include evidence of their past experience and learning; ... It is the applicant's responsibility to decide which evidence used, which must be valid, current and reliable.

questions.question: An assessor reviewing an RPL portfolio finds a detailed work report showing the applicant held senior responsibilities. Under the RPL Policy, what must the assessor check about this item of evidence?
options: That it shows at least five years of relevant professional experience
That it has been countersigned by the applicant's Personal Tutor
That the applicant's seniority matches the level of the programme
That its learning is appropriate to the award's learning objectives
questions.explanation: Each item of evidence is checked to ensure that the learning is appropriate to the learning objectives of the academic award being sought, not the seniority or length of the experience.
questions.source_excerpt: Checks are made to evaluate each item of evidence to ensure that the learning is appropriate to the learning objectives of the academic award being sought;

questions.question: An RPL claim satisfies LCC's portfolio requirements but does not meet the awarding body's regulations for RPL. Under the RPL Policy, what is the position?
options: It can proceed, as LCC's rules override the awarding body's
It can proceed if the External Examiner agrees and the Chair confirms it
It cannot succeed, as applicants must meet all awarding body RPL regulations
It can proceed if the Programme Leader records the reasons in the portfolio
questions.explanation: The policy requires applicants and students to meet all awarding body regulations for RPL, so meeting LCC's requirements alone is not enough.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants/students must meet all awarding body regulations for RPL;

questions.question: An RPL student's portfolio was assessed in 2023 and they received certification in 2025. Under the RPL Policy, until when must the assessment and internal verification records be kept?
options: Until 2026, three years after the portfolio was assessed
Until 2028, three years after certification
Until 2030, five years after certification
Until 2025, when the student is certified
questions.explanation: Assessment and internal verification records are retained for a three-year period following certification, so certification in 2025 means keeping them until 2028.
questions.source_excerpt: Assessment and internal verification records, along with any additional RPL records completed, will be retained for a three-year period following certification;

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy, which statement correctly divides RPL responsibilities between Personal Tutors and Programme Leaders?
options: Personal Tutors identify eligible students and guide portfolios; Programme Leaders assess portfolios
Programme Leaders identify eligible students and guide portfolios; Personal Tutors assess portfolios
Personal Tutors identify eligible students and assess portfolios; Programme Leaders approve decisions
Programme Leaders identify eligible students; Personal Tutors assess portfolios and approve decisions
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors identify potentially eligible students and guide them through the portfolio, while Programme Leaders assess the RPL portfolio; decisions are approved by the Board.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal Tutors are responsible for identifying prospective or existing students who might be eligible for RPL and informing them of opportunities available; ... Programme Leaders are responsible for the assessment of an applicant's/student's RPL portfolio. ... The personal tutor will guide the applicant through the process of completing a portfolio

questions.question: Under the RPL Policy's definitions, how should these two claims be classified? Applicant A holds an employer-based award at Higher Education level that carries no FHEQ credit; Applicant B learned bookkeeping through years of unpaid voluntary work.
options: A is an RPCL claim; B is an RPEL claim, assessing the learning gained rather than the work itself
A is an RPEL claim, as employer awards are work-based; B is an RPCL claim assessing the work itself
Both are RPCL claims, as each involves learning at a level that is suitable for Higher Education credit
Both are RPEL claims, as neither applicant's learning has yet led to credit positioned on the FHEQ
questions.explanation: RPCL covers Higher Education level learning such as employer-based awards that has not led to FHEQ credit, while RPEL acknowledges the learning gained through informal or non-formal experiences, not the experience itself.
questions.source_excerpt: Recognition of Prior Certificated Learning (RPCL) is the assessment and formal acknowledgement of previous learning, such as that gained through professional development or employer-based awards, which is at Higher Education level ... the learning gained through informal or non-formal experiences, not the assessment of the experience itself.

questions.question: An applicant's professional course was at Higher Education level and has already led to credit positioned on the FHEQ. How does this learning sit against the RPL Policy's definition of RPCL?
options: It is a clear example of RPCL, because it is certificated learning gained at Higher Education level
It falls outside the RPCL definition, which covers HE-level learning that has not led to FHEQ credit
It is treated as RPEL instead, because credit awarded elsewhere counts as a form of non-formal learning
It cannot be recognised in any form, because RPL does not extend to certificated learning at all
questions.explanation: The policy defines RPCL as Higher Education level learning which has not led to credit or qualifications positioned on the FHEQ, so learning already credited on the FHEQ does not meet that definition.
questions.source_excerpt: Recognition of Prior Certificated Learning (RPCL) is the assessment and formal acknowledgement of previous learning ... which is at Higher Education level but which has not led to the award of credit or qualifications positioned on the Framework for Higher Education Qualifications (FHEQ).

questions.question: Midway through a 240-credit programme, a student applies for RPL for 100 credits of modules they have not yet started, plus a 20-credit module they began last month. Under the RPL Policy, what can be considered?
options: All 120 credits, because the total claimed is exactly half of the programme's credit value
None of it, because RPL applications cannot be made once the programme has started
Only the 100 credits of modules not yet commenced; the module already begun is excluded
Only 60 credits, because claims made during the programme are capped at one quarter
questions.explanation: RPL can be applied for during the programme only for modules not yet commenced, so the 20-credit module is excluded; the remaining 100 credits are within the half-credit maximum.
questions.source_excerpt: Applications for RPL should ideally be made before the start of the Programme, but can also be made during the Programme, as long as the student has not yet commenced the module for which s/he wishes to apply; ... The maximum permissible credit value for an RPL claim is half of the total credit value of the relevant programme;

questions.question: A Programme Leader wants to delegate an RPL assessment to a Module Leader who has the necessary subject expertise but has had no RPL training. What does the RPL Policy allow?
options: The delegation stands, as subject expertise is the only condition set for delegating
The delegation stands, provided the Personal Tutor co-signs the Module Leader's decision
The Module Leader may assess, provided the External Examiner later confirms the outcome
The Module Leader cannot make the determination, as only RPL-trained academics may
questions.explanation: Although assessment may be delegated to a Module Leader for subject expertise, only qualified academics with RPL training can make determinations in respect of RPL at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Only qualified academics with RPL training can make determinations in respect of RPL at the College; ... The Programme Leader may delegate the assessment to the relevant Module Leader where specific subject expertise is required;

questions.question: An applicant's transcript from another institution shows a completed unit with the same title as the LCC unit they are claiming RPL for. Under the RPL Policy, what must happen before credit can be given?
options: The learning outcomes met there are carefully mapped against those of the LCC unit
The matching title is confirmed in writing by the other institution's registry
The transcript is accepted as it stands, as the two unit titles are identical
The applicant sits the LCC unit's end-of-term assessment to confirm the match
questions.explanation: The policy requires learning outcomes met in other institutions to be carefully mapped against the learning outcomes of the units claimed; a matching title alone is not enough.
questions.source_excerpt: Checks are carried out to ensure that learning outcomes met in other Institutions are carefully mapped against the learning outcomes for those units for which RPL is applied in order to ensure the integrity of the process at LCC;

questions.question: A Pearson Higher National student moving from the QCF to the RQF wants their completed QCF units recognised. A colleague says individual Pearson units can never be claimed. Under the RPL Policy, what is the position?
options: The colleague is right: individual units are not awards, so no recognition is possible
The College facilitates RPL for this transfer, with reference to Pearson's Mapping documents
The transfer can proceed only as RPCL claims, with each unit treated as a separate award
The student must restart on the RQF, as QCF learning falls outside the scope of RPL
questions.explanation: The bar on individual units applies to RPCL claims; the policy separately commits the College to facilitate RPL for Pearson Higher National students transferring from the QCF to the RQF, using Pearson's Mapping documents.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will facilitate RPL for Pearson Higher National students wishing to transfer from the Qualifications and Credit Framework (QCF) to the Regulated Qualifications Framework (RQF), with reference to the Mapping documents published by Pearson. ... Therefore any RPCL claim on individual units are not accepted.

questions.question: A student with Higher Education level certificated learning asks for RPL on a unit that is assessed through external assessment, well within the half-credit limit. Under the RPL Policy, what is the position?
options: It can be granted as an RPCL claim, because the prior learning is at Higher Education level
It can be granted if the External Examiner agrees and it is confirmed by Chair's Action
It cannot be granted, as RPL is not applicable for external assessment and set assignments
It can be granted, because the claim falls within half of the programme's total credit value
questions.explanation: RPL is not applicable for external assessment and set assignments, whatever the level of the prior learning and even where the claim is within the credit limit.
questions.source_excerpt: RPL is not applicable for external assessment and set assignments.

questions.question: Which of the following is not permitted under the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Policy?
options: Applying for RPL during the programme for a module that has not yet been commenced
Relying on maths learning over five years old, where it is still relevant to the course
Delegating a claim's assessment to the relevant Module Leader for subject expertise
Making an RPCL claim for a single individual unit on a Pearson programme
questions.explanation: Individual units are not defined as awards for Pearson programmes, so RPCL claims on individual units are not accepted; the other three are expressly allowed by the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: can also be made during the Programme, as long as the student has not yet commenced the module for which s/he wishes to apply; ... Individual units are not defined as awards for Pearson programmes. Therefore any RPCL claim on individual units are not accepted.

questions.question: A prospective student with years of informal work experience finds it hard to put their learning into words and assumes College staff cannot help with an RPL portfolio. Under the RPL Policy, what is correct?
options: The College supports eligible prospective students to reflect on and evidence their learning
Staff may not help, as the portfolio must be entirely the applicant's own unaided work
The Programme Leader writes the learning statements, since they will assess the portfolio
Help is available only once a prospective student has enrolled and begun the relevant module
questions.explanation: The College will support eligible prospective students to reflect on their experiences and describe, analyse and evidence their learning, and the personal tutor guides them through the portfolio.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will support eligible prospective students to prepare them to reflect upon their experiences and describe and analyse their learning and evidence the learning gained from those experiences; ... The personal tutor will guide the applicant through the process of completing a portfolio

questions.question: An enrolled student who already has a personal tutor contacts the admissions department to start an RPL application. Under the RPL Policy, where should they be directed?
options: To the admissions team, which handles all RPL enquiries up to the formal assessment
To their own personal tutor; admissions is for those not yet assigned one
To the Programme Leader, who takes RPL enquiries from students already on a programme
To a personal tutor of any programme, as arranged through the admissions department
questions.explanation: Students wishing to apply for RPL are advised to meet their personal tutor; contacting admissions to arrange a personal tutor is the route for prospective students not yet assigned one.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants or students wishing to make an application for RPL or seeking additional information are advised to meet with their personal tutor; ... Prospective students who have not yet been assigned a personal tutor, as they may not yet have joined the programme, should contact the admissions department

questions.question: After an RPL advice session, a Personal Tutor emails a student: 'Your experience clearly covers this module, so you are exempt from it.' Under the RPL Policy, why is this wrong?
options: Only the Admissions department may tell students the outcome of an RPL enquiry
Exemptions may be granted only by the External Examiner, after reviewing the student's evidence
The advice stage only helps the student decide; claims need assessment and Board approval
Personal Tutors may grant exemptions only for modules that the student has commenced
questions.explanation: The advice-stage comparison is only to help students decide whether to pursue RPL; claims are formally assessed by the Programme Leader and decisions approved by the Assessment and Progression Board.
questions.source_excerpt: At this stage, this is only to help students to decide if they wish to pursue RPL; ... All RPL claims will be formally assessed by the Programme Leader for the course against which RPL is being claimed. ... The Board is responsible for approving decisions proposed by the Programme Leader;

questions.question: An RPL applicant's portfolio convincingly maps their prior learning to four of a module's five learning outcomes, but not the fifth. Under the RPL Policy, what is the position?
options: The claim succeeds, as the portfolio demonstrates a clear majority of the learning outcomes
The claim earns four-fifths of the module's credit, in proportion to the outcomes demonstrated
The Personal Tutor may waive the fifth outcome if the applicant's other evidence is strong
The applicant must show how they met every learning outcome of the module, the fifth included
questions.explanation: The applicant is required to demonstrate how they have met each of the learning outcomes of the module claimed, so four out of five is not sufficient.
questions.source_excerpt: The applicant will be required to demonstrate how s/he has met each of the learning outcomes of the module(s) for which an application RPL is made.

questions.question: A registered student holding a relevant Higher Education level certificate says the certificate alone should secure RPL, with no portfolio needed. Under the RPL Policy, what is correct?
options: A portfolio is still required, with the certificate as one item of evidence in it
The certificate is enough for RPCL claims, so a portfolio is needed only for RPEL claims
The certificate is enough, provided the Personal Tutor confirms it relates to the programme
A portfolio is needed only by prospective students, not by students who are already registered
questions.explanation: Prospective and registered students must demonstrate their knowledge and learning, and how it took place, through a portfolio; certificates are one type of evidence within it.
questions.source_excerpt: Prospective and registered students wishing to claim RPL are required to demonstrate knowledge and learning and how that learning has taken place. This is completed through the creation of a portfolio; ... include evidence of the learning referred to, including certificates, transcripts,

questions.question: Which draft RPL application meets all three of the RPL Policy's application requirements: descriptive, details and evidence-based?
options: States when, where and with whom it was learned, and lists at length every duty held, backed by training certificates
States when, where and with whom it was learned, explains what was learned and how it was used, and attaches training records
Explains what was learned and how it was used, backed by a transcript, but gives no context for when or where it was learned
States when, where and with whom it was learned, and explains what was learned and how it was used, without any evidence
questions.explanation: Applications must describe the context of the learning, detail what was learned and how it was used rather than the experience itself, and include evidence such as training documentation.
questions.source_excerpt: Descriptive: clearly describe the context of the learning activities in terms of when, where, with whom, etc.; ... Details: regarding what was learned and how that learning was used. The application should be based on what was learned, not on the experience itself. ... Evidence-based: include evidence of the learning referred to, including certificates, transcripts, reports, documentation from training courses

questions.question: An assessor accepts most of an RPL portfolio but doubts whether the evidence fully substantiates one aspect of the claimed learning. Which step does the RPL Policy allow the assessor to take?
options: Reject the whole claim, as a portfolio cannot be added to once it is submitted
Ask the Personal Tutor to vouch for that aspect of the claimant's learning instead
Ask the claimant to undertake an assessment exercise to substantiate that aspect
Refer that aspect to the External Examiner to assess on the College's behalf
questions.explanation: Assessors may ask the claimant to undertake an assessment exercise to substantiate aspects of the learning claims, and further evidence can normally be produced.
questions.source_excerpt: Assessors might ask the claimant to undertake an assessment exercise to substantiate aspects of the learning claims. Where further evidence is required, the opportunity will normally be given to produce this.

questions.question: To save time, an assessor proposes to judge an RPL portfolio on its overall impression, without reviewing each document individually. Under the RPL Policy, what is required instead?
options: A sample of the evidence is checked, with the rest confirmed by the Personal Tutor
Only certificated evidence is examined, as experiential evidence cannot be verified
The overall impression is enough, provided the External Examiner later agrees with it
Each item of evidence is checked to ensure its learning fits the award's learning objectives
questions.explanation: The policy requires checks evaluating each item of evidence to ensure the learning is appropriate to the learning objectives of the academic award being sought.
questions.source_excerpt: Checks are made to evaluate each item of evidence to ensure that the learning is appropriate to the learning objectives of the academic award being sought;

questions.question: An RPL decision is needed before the Assessment and Progression Board next meets, but the appropriate External Examiner does not agree with the Programme Leader's proposal. Under the RPL Policy, what follows?
options: It cannot be confirmed by Chair's Action, which needs the External Examiner's agreement
The Chair may still confirm it by Chair's Action, as the External Examiner only advises
The Programme Leader's proposal takes effect, and the disagreement is noted at the Board
The Quality Enhancement Steering Committee settles it in place of the Board and the Chair
questions.explanation: A decision needed before the next Board may be confirmed by Chair's Action only if the appropriate External Examiner is in agreement.
questions.source_excerpt: In cases where a decision is required before the next Board meets then confirmation will be sought from the appropriate External Examiner and, if s/he is in agreement, the decision may then be confirmed by Chair's Action.

questions.question: A colleague suggests the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee should approve each individual RPL decision. Under the RPL Policy, how are that Committee's and the Assessment and Progression Board's roles actually divided?
options: The Committee approves Programme Leaders' proposed decisions; the Board monitors RPL use
The Board approves Programme Leaders' proposed decisions; the Committee monitors RPL use
The Committee approves decisions made by Chair's Action; the Board approves all others
The Board approves RPEL decisions; the Committee approves RPCL decisions and monitors use
questions.explanation: The Assessment and Progression Board approves RPL decisions proposed by the Programme Leader, while the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee monitors the College's use of RPL.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board is responsible for approving decisions proposed by the Programme Leader; ... LCC will monitor its use of RPL through the Quality Enhancement Steering Committee, which is responsible for developing and monitoring all College policies and procedures.

questions.question: The Assessment and Progression Board has approved an RPL decision on a Pearson programme. A colleague says the RPL evidence no longer needs Pearson's standards verification. Under the RPL Policy, what is correct?
options: It is no longer subject to external checks, as the Board's approval is final
It is verified by Pearson only if the External Examiner objected to the decision
It is still subject to Pearson's standards verification in the normal way
It is verified by Pearson only for RPCL claims, and not for RPEL claims
questions.explanation: Board approval does not remove external checks: evidence used for RPL on Pearson programmes is subject to Pearson's standards verification as normal.
questions.source_excerpt: Evidence used for RPL on Pearson Programmes will be subject to Pearson's standards verification as normal.

questions.question: A student disagrees with an RPL decision that was confirmed by Chair's Action before the Board met. Under the RPL Policy, what route should the student follow?
options: None, as decisions confirmed by Chair's Action are final and cannot then be appealed
Ask the External Examiner who agreed the decision to reconsider and reverse it
Resubmit the same portfolio to the Personal Tutor for a fresh formal assessment
Follow LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure, as for any assessment decision
questions.explanation: As with any assessment decision, a learner who wishes to appeal an RPL decision follows the guidance in LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: As with any assessment decision, if a learner wishes to appeal against a decision made in relation to assessment the guidance to follow is provided in LCC's Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure.

questions.question: A fully RPL-trained Personal Tutor has guided a student's RPL portfolio and offers to formally assess it as well, arguing that only trained academics may make RPL determinations. Under the RPL Policy, what is the position?
options: The Personal Tutor may assess it, as RPL training is the only condition set for making RPL determinations
The Module Leader must assess it, as Programme Leaders may not assess claims that tutors have guided
The Programme Leader formally assesses it, and may delegate the assessment to the relevant Module Leader
The Personal Tutor may assess RPEL claims, but RPCL claims must always be assessed by the Programme Leader
questions.explanation: RPL training is a precondition for making determinations, but formal assessment of every RPL claim rests with the Programme Leader, who may delegate it to the relevant Module Leader where specific subject expertise is required.
questions.source_excerpt: Programme Leaders are responsible for the assessment of an applicant's/student's RPL portfolio. ... All RPL claims will be formally assessed by the Programme Leader for the course against which RPL is being claimed. The Programme Leader may delegate the assessment to the relevant Module Leader where specific subject expertise is required;

questions.question: An RPEL applicant holds no certificates or transcripts. A colleague says the claim cannot proceed without them, but the applicant has an article they published recently and videos, made last year, of training they delivered. Under the RPL Policy, what is correct?
options: The colleague is wrong: publications and multimedia sources can be evidence, if valid, current and reliable
The colleague is right: an RPEL claim needs at least one certificate, with any other items only as support
The colleague is wrong, but only an employer's reference can stand in for certificates in an RPEL claim
The colleague is right: without certificates, the claim has to be resubmitted as an RPCL claim instead
questions.explanation: The policy lists publications and multimedia sources among acceptable evidence alongside certificates and transcripts; the applicant chooses the evidence, which must be valid, current and reliable.
questions.source_excerpt: include evidence of the learning referred to, including certificates, transcripts, reports, documentation from training courses, publications, multimedia sources, etc. ... It is the applicant's responsibility to decide which evidence used, which must be valid, current and reliable.

questions.question: A Programme Leader delegates an RPL assessment to the relevant Module Leader, and the resulting decision is needed before the Assessment and Progression Board next meets. Under the RPL Policy, which sequence is correct?
options: Module Leader assesses; Module Leader reports it to the Board; External Examiner confirms by Chair's Action
Module Leader assesses; External Examiner proposes the decision; Programme Leader confirms by Chair's Action
Programme Leader assesses; Module Leader proposes the decision; Personal Tutor agrees; confirmed by Chair's Action
Module Leader assesses; Programme Leader proposes; External Examiner agrees; confirmed by Chair's Action
questions.explanation: A delegated assessment is still reported and proposed by the Programme Leader; where a decision is needed before the Board meets, the External Examiner's agreement is sought and the decision may then be confirmed by Chair's Action.
questions.source_excerpt: The Programme Leader may delegate the assessment to the relevant Module Leader where specific subject expertise is required; ... The Board is responsible for approving decisions proposed by the Programme Leader; ... confirmation will be sought from the appropriate External Examiner and, if s/he is in agreement, the decision may then be confirmed by Chair's Action.

questions.question: An applicant's only evidence for a digital marketing module is a course they completed seven years ago, in a field where practice has changed a great deal since. How does the RPL Policy's guidance on the recency of learning apply?
options: It meets the guidance, as the 5-year expectation applies only to experiential and not certificated learning
It is outside the 5-year expectation, and the allowance for older learning is for subjects with little change
It is outside the 5-year expectation, but can be used if the External Examiner grants a formal exemption
It meets the guidance, as older learning can be relevant in any subject if the evidence is valid and reliable
questions.explanation: Learning should be from within the last 5 years; the allowance for less recent learning applies to subjects where little change occurs, such as history or maths, which does not describe this field.
questions.source_excerpt: The learning should be from within the last 5 years. For some subjects, where little change occurs, e.g. history, maths, if the learning is less recent, it may still be relevant to the course;

questions.question: At the start of your class, a student without a Support Agreement Plan asks verbally if they may audio record the lecture. Under the Recording Lectures Policy, how should consent be obtained?
options: Advise them to email you in advance of the class to seek written consent
Give verbal consent there and then, as this is sufficient for audio
Tell them to obtain consent from Student Services rather than from you
Let them record now and confirm consent by email after the class
questions.explanation: The policy permits audio recording only with the lecturer's written consent, sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class.
questions.source_excerpt: The College permits the audio recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer, which should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class.

questions.question: A student whose Support Agreement Plan permits recording teaching sessions as a reasonable adjustment for a disability starts recording your lecture without asking you. Under the Recording Lectures Policy, what is the position?
options: They must stop and email you for written consent before recording again
They must obtain written consent from the Head of Department instead
They do not need to ask individual academics for permission to record
They may audio record freely but need your written consent for video
questions.explanation: Students given permission to record through their Support Agreement Plan as a reasonable adjustment do not need to ask individual academics for permission to audio or video record.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with special needs who have been given permission through their Support Agreement Plan to record lectures or other formal teaching sessions as a reasonable adjustment on a disability do not need to ask for permission to audio or video record from individual academics.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, who owns the intellectual property in recorded lecture sessions?
options: London Churchill College, as the provider
The student who made the recording
The awarding body for the programme
The lecturer who delivered the session
questions.explanation: The policy states that recorded lecture sessions are the intellectual property of the lecturer, and students may use them only for personal use.
questions.source_excerpt: Recorded lecture sessions are the intellectual property of the lecturer. Students must not share, reproduce, or upload them in the public domain. Recorded materials are only permitted for personal use.

questions.question: You are planning a session with high levels of spoken interaction between students, and a student emails asking to record it. Which statement reflects the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: You may refuse, explaining that some students may not wish their voices or opinions recorded
You must allow it, as lecturers may refuse consent for video recording but not for audio recording
You must refer it to the Programme Leader, as lecturers do not make the final decision on recording
You must allow it, provided the student confirms in writing it is for personal study use
questions.explanation: Lecturers have the final decision on whether a lecture can be audio or video recorded, and the policy gives high levels of spoken interaction as an example where the lecturer is likely to refuse, with reasons provided, because some students will not wish their voices or opinions recorded.
questions.source_excerpt: Lecturers have the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded ... Reasons will be provided as to why permission to record a lecture might be denied, for example, in cases where high levels of spoken interaction are expected ... the lecturer is likely to refuse to allow recording on grounds that some students will not wish to have their voices or opinions recorded.

questions.question: A student has your written consent to video record your lecture, but another student in the class objects to being filmed. What does the Recording Lectures Policy require?
options: Recording continues, as the lecturer's written consent takes precedence
Recording continues, provided the footage is kept for personal use only
The College has a duty to abide by the objecting student's wishes
The objecting student must submit a formal complaint to stop filming
questions.explanation: The policy recognises that other participants may object to being filmed and states that the College has a duty to abide by their wishes.
questions.source_excerpt: With respect to video recording, other participants in the class may object to being filmed. The College has a duty to abide by their wishes.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, what will any unauthorised distribution of a lecture recording by a student, such as uploading it to YouTube, be subject to?
options: Disciplinary action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
An automatic fail in the module concerned under the Assessment and Progression Regulations
An informal reminder from the lecturer, as recordings fall outside formal College procedures
Investigation for plagiarism under the Academic Misconduct Policy and Procedure
questions.explanation: Recordings must not be uploaded online, and the policy states any unauthorised distribution is subject to disciplinary action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Any unauthorised distribution of such a recording will be subject to disciplinary action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure. ... Recordings of lectures delivered in the College (i.e.: YouTube) should not be uploaded online.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, where should the video camera be placed when a student has consent to video record a classroom lecture?
options: At the back of the room, capturing the whole class
In a position which captures solely the lecturer
Wherever the student chooses, provided it is visible
Facing the audience so discussion is recorded
questions.explanation: The policy states the camera should be positioned to capture solely the lecturer; anyone else captured must give their permission.
questions.source_excerpt: The video camera should be placed in a position which captures solely the lecturer. Should other individuals be captured in the video recording, their permission will need to be obtained.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, can recordings of live online sessions be used as a replacement for lecture attendance or for intended staff presence in the lecture room?
options: They may replace lecture attendance, but not intended staff presence
They replace neither lecture attendance nor intended staff presence
They may replace intended staff presence, but not lecture attendance
They may replace both, where the Programme Leader approves
questions.explanation: The policy states that recordings are not a replacement for lecture attendance and may not be used as a replacement for intended staff presence in the lecture room.
questions.source_excerpt: Recordings are not a replacement for lecture attendance. In addition, it may not be used as a replacement for intended staff presence in the lecture room.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, which of the following is NOT an expectation placed on students who record lectures?
options: Use the recording only for personal use in the context of their studies
Store the recording in a secure place for the duration of their studies
Delete or destroy the recording once it has served its purpose as a study aid
Send a copy of the recording to the lecturer for approval before using it
questions.explanation: The policy expects personal use only, secure storage for the duration of studies and deletion once the recording has served its purpose; it does not require copies to be sent to the lecturer.
questions.source_excerpt: Use made of a recorded lecture must only be for personal use in the context of a student's studies. ... Recordings of lectures should be stored in a secure place for the duration of studies. ... All recordings of lectures or other formal teaching sessions should be deleted or destroyed after they have served their purpose as a study aid.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, for how long is a recorded lecture retained under the College Data Retention Schedule?
options: 6 months
12 months
24 months
36 months
questions.explanation: The policy states that a recorded lecture is retained for a 12-month period in line with the College Data Retention Schedule.
questions.source_excerpt: A recorded lecture is retained for a 12-month period in accordance with the College Data Retention Schedule.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, by whom may lecture sessions be recorded in the circumstances the policy sets out?
options: Only by the College's IT and media services team
Only by lecturers, using College-approved equipment
Either by the College or by the students
Only by students with a Support Agreement Plan
questions.explanation: The policy's aims state that it sets out the circumstances in which lecture sessions may be recorded either by the College or by the students.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy sets out the circumstances in which any lecture sessions may be recorded either by the College or the students

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, which sessions are expressly included in its coverage of classroom-based learning?
options: Examinations, vivas and induction sessions
Seminars, tutorials and public lectures
Staff meetings and committee meetings
Open days and applicant interviews
questions.explanation: The policy covers lectures recorded in classroom-based learning, expressly including seminars, tutorials and public lectures.
questions.source_excerpt: The policy covers the lectures recorded in classroom-based learning including the seminars, tutorials, and public lectures.

questions.question: Apart from classroom-based learning, which learning formats does the Recording Lectures Policy state that it covers?
options: No other format; it covers classroom-based learning only
Work placements and employer-based training only
Student-led study groups held outside timetabled hours
Blended learning and any other distance learning format
questions.explanation: The policy states that, as well as classroom-based learning, it covers any recording for blended learning or any other distance learning format.
questions.source_excerpt: Furthermore, it covers any recording for blended learning or any other distance learning format.

questions.question: Under the Recording Lectures Policy, on what basis does the College permit a student to video record a classroom lecture?
options: With the written consent of the lecturer
Only with a Support Agreement Plan in place
With the Programme Leader's written approval
Video recording is not permitted, only audio
questions.explanation: The College permits the video recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer.
questions.source_excerpt: The College also permits the video recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer

questions.question: Under the Recording Lectures Policy, what must happen if individuals other than the lecturer are captured in a student's video recording of a lecture?
options: Their faces must be blurred before it is viewed
Their permission will need to be obtained
The lecturer must delete the recording immediately
The student must report it to the Programme Leader
questions.explanation: The policy states that should other individuals be captured in the video recording, their permission will need to be obtained.
questions.source_excerpt: Should other individuals be captured in the video recording, their permission will need to be obtained.

questions.question: Under the Recording Lectures Policy, through which document may a student with special needs be given permission to record lectures as a reasonable adjustment?
options: Their Individual Learning Plan
Their Personal Development Plan
Their Support Agreement Plan
Their Reasonable Adjustment Record
questions.explanation: Students with special needs may be given permission to record lectures as a reasonable adjustment through their Support Agreement Plan.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with special needs who have been given permission through their Support Agreement Plan to record lectures or other formal teaching sessions as a reasonable adjustment on a disability

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, recorded lecture materials are only permitted for which kind of use?
options: Cohort-wide use
Public use
Teaching use
Personal use
questions.explanation: The policy states that recorded materials are only permitted for personal use and must not be shared, reproduced or uploaded in the public domain.
questions.source_excerpt: Students must not share, reproduce, or upload them in the public domain. Recorded materials are only permitted for personal use.

questions.question: Under the Recording Lectures Policy, who retains copyright on work and other intellectual property that an external visiting lecturer generates?
options: The visiting lecturer, or their employer as appropriate
London Churchill College, as the hosting institution
The students who recorded the visiting lecture session
The awarding body that validates the programme
questions.explanation: External visiting lecturers, or their employer as appropriate, retain copyright on work and any other intellectual property rights they generate.
questions.source_excerpt: External visiting lecturers (or their employer as appropriate) retain copyright on work and any other intellectual property rights they generate

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, to which students will the College provide recordings of live online sessions?
options: Students who missed the session through authorised absence
Students enrolled in blended learning taught programmes
Students with a Support Agreement Plan, on request
All students on classroom-based programmes, on request
questions.explanation: The College will provide recordings of live online sessions to students enrolled in blended learning taught programmes.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will provide recordings of live online sessions to students who are enrolled in blended learning taught programmes.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, why are recordings of live online sessions produced for students on blended learning programmes?
options: To provide evidence of attendance for monitoring purposes
To allow students to catch up instead of attending live
To aid the students' learning through reflections
To support the observation of teaching quality
questions.explanation: The policy states that these recordings are produced to aid the students' learning through reflections; they are not a replacement for attendance.
questions.source_excerpt: These recordings will be produced to aid the students' learning through reflections.

questions.question: Under the Recording Lectures Policy, who has the right to make the final decision on whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded?
options: The Programme Leader
The Academic Board
The Head of Department
The lecturer concerned
questions.explanation: The policy gives lecturers the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded.
questions.source_excerpt: Lecturers have the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded

questions.question: The Recording Lectures Policy recognises that permission to record a lecture might be denied. What does it state will be provided in that respect?
options: Reasons as to why permission might be denied
An official College recording of the lecture instead
A written transcript of the lecture for the student
A right of appeal to the Academic Board
questions.explanation: The policy states that reasons will be provided as to why permission to record a lecture might be denied.
questions.source_excerpt: Reasons will be provided as to why permission to record a lecture might be denied

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, how should students keep their recordings of lectures?
options: On the College's shared drive, for staff access
In a secure place for the duration of their studies
On the virtual learning environment for their cohort
With the lecturer, who releases copies on request
questions.explanation: The policy expects recordings of lectures to be stored in a secure place for the duration of studies.
questions.source_excerpt: Recordings of lectures should be stored in a secure place for the duration of studies.

questions.question: According to the Recording Lectures Policy, when should recordings of lectures or other formal teaching sessions be deleted or destroyed?
options: At the end of the module in which they were made
Immediately after the next assessment deadline
After they have served their purpose as a study aid
Only when the lecturer formally requests deletion
questions.explanation: All recordings of lectures or other formal teaching sessions should be deleted or destroyed after they have served their purpose as a study aid.
questions.source_excerpt: All recordings of lectures or other formal teaching sessions should be deleted or destroyed ... after they have served their purpose as a study aid.

questions.question: A student emails asking to audio record your small-group tutorial rather than a lecture. Does the Recording Lectures Policy apply to this request?
options: No; it applies only to timetabled lectures, so tutorials are handled informally
Yes; its coverage of classroom-based learning includes seminars and tutorials
No; tutorials fall under it only when they are delivered through blended learning
Yes, but only where the tutorial is also open to the public as a public lecture
