questions.explanation: The policy covers lectures recorded in classroom-based learning, including seminars, tutorials and public lectures, so the usual consent process applies to a tutorial.
questions.source_excerpt: The policy covers the lectures recorded in classroom-based learning including the seminars, tutorials, and public lectures.

questions.question: Under the Recording Lectures Policy, how does the consent a student needs to video record a classroom lecture compare with the consent needed to audio record it?
options: Video needs the lecturer's written consent, but verbal consent is enough for audio
Video also needs Programme Leader approval; audio needs only the lecturer's consent
It is the same: the lecturer's written consent, sought by email before the class
Audio needs no consent at all, but video needs the lecturer's written consent
questions.explanation: Both audio and video recording are permitted with the written consent of the lecturer, sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class.
questions.source_excerpt: The College permits the audio recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer, which should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class. ... The College also permits the video recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer, which should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class.

questions.question: A student has your emailed written consent to video record your lecture and plans to set the camera up to film the whole class discussion. What does the Recording Lectures Policy require?
options: Nothing further, as your written consent covers everyone else present in the room
The student must instead ask the College to make an official recording
Filming the whole class is fine if the footage is kept for personal use only
The camera should capture solely you; anyone else filmed must give permission
questions.explanation: The camera should be placed to capture solely the lecturer, and if other individuals are captured in the recording, their permission will need to be obtained.
questions.source_excerpt: The video camera should be placed in a position which captures solely the lecturer. Should other individuals be captured in the video recording, their permission will need to be obtained.

questions.question: A lecturer proposes playing last term's recording of a session in the lecture room instead of attending the timetabled session in person. What does the Recording Lectures Policy say?
options: Recordings may not be used as a replacement for intended staff presence
This is allowed while the recording is within its 12-month retention period
This is allowed where the students have agreed in writing to the arrangement
This is allowed for blended learning sessions, but not for classroom sessions
questions.explanation: The policy states that recordings are not a replacement for lecture attendance and may not be used as a replacement for intended staff presence in the lecture room.
questions.source_excerpt: Recordings are not a replacement for lecture attendance. In addition, it may not be used as a replacement for intended staff presence in the lecture room.

questions.question: A blended learning student misses a live online session, watches the College's recording later and asks to be counted as having attended. Which response reflects the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: Yes, as recordings are provided so that students can catch up on missed sessions
No, as recordings are not a replacement for lecture attendance
Yes, provided they watched the full recording within the same week
Yes, if their Support Agreement Plan allows recording as an adjustment
questions.explanation: Recordings of live online sessions are produced to aid learning through reflection, and the policy states that they are not a replacement for lecture attendance.
questions.source_excerpt: These recordings will be produced to aid the students' learning through reflections. ... Recordings are not a replacement for lecture attendance.

questions.question: Which statement correctly summarises how the Recording Lectures Policy treats the College's recordings of live online sessions on blended learning taught programmes?
options: Provided to any student on request and retained until the end of their studies
Provided only to students who were absent and deleted once modules are assessed
Provided to enrolled students to aid reflection and retained for 12 months
Provided to enrolled students in place of attendance and retained for 24 months
questions.explanation: The College provides recordings of live online sessions to students enrolled on blended learning programmes to aid learning through reflection, and a recorded lecture is retained for 12 months under the Data Retention Schedule.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will provide recordings of live online sessions to students who are enrolled in blended learning taught programmes. ... These recordings will be produced to aid the students' learning through reflections. ... A recorded lecture is retained for a 12-month period in accordance with the College Data Retention Schedule.

questions.question: Under the Recording Lectures Policy, how does the retention of a College lecture recording differ from the way students should keep their own lecture recordings?
options: Both are kept for a 12-month period under the College Data Retention Schedule
The College keeps its recording until graduation; students keep theirs 12 months
Both must be deleted as soon as the relevant module has been assessed
The College keeps its copy 12 months; students store theirs securely while studying
questions.explanation: A recorded lecture is retained for 12 months under the College Data Retention Schedule, whereas students should store their recordings in a secure place for the duration of their studies.
questions.source_excerpt: A recorded lecture is retained for a 12-month period in accordance with the College Data Retention Schedule. ... Recordings of lectures should be stored in a secure place for the duration of studies.

questions.question: A newly appointed lecturer asks how the Recording Lectures Policy expects them to handle student requests to record their lectures. Which statement is accurate?
options: The lecturer makes the final decision, though consent is not often refused
Consent should usually be refused unless the student has a Support Agreement Plan
Consent must always be granted to any student who emails before the class
Consent may be refused only with the Programme Leader's written approval
questions.explanation: Lecturers have the right to make the final decision on whether a particular lecture can be recorded, but the policy notes that consent to record is not often refused.
questions.source_excerpt: Lecturers have the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded, but consent to record is not often refused.

questions.question: A student completing their final module asks whether they may keep all their lecture recordings indefinitely for future reference. What does the Recording Lectures Policy expect?
options: They may keep them indefinitely, provided they are stored in a secure place
They may keep them for 12 months after completing, in line with data retention
They should delete or destroy them once they have served their purpose as a study aid
They must return them to the lecturer, who then decides whether they may be kept
questions.explanation: Students should store recordings securely for the duration of their studies, and all recordings should be deleted or destroyed after they have served their purpose as a study aid.
questions.source_excerpt: Recordings of lectures should be stored in a secure place for the duration of studies. ... All recordings of lectures or other formal teaching sessions should be deleted or destroyed ... after they have served their purpose as a study aid.

questions.question: A student who recorded your lecture with your written consent wants to replay it at home while preparing their own coursework. Is this permitted under the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: Only if they email you again for consent each time they replay it
Only once the College's 12-month retention period has ended
No; recordings may only be replayed on College premises
Yes; personal use in the context of their studies is allowed
questions.explanation: The policy requires that a recorded lecture is used only for personal use in the context of the student's studies, which covers replaying it to prepare their own coursework.
questions.source_excerpt: Use made of a recorded lecture must only be for personal use in the context of a student's studies.

questions.question: You learn that a student privately sent your recorded lecture to a friend at another university, without uploading it online. How does the Recording Lectures Policy treat this?
options: As unauthorised distribution, subject to disciplinary action for the student
As acceptable, since only uploading recordings to the public domain is prohibited
As acceptable, provided the friend uses it only for their own personal study
As a copyright matter for the lecturer to pursue outside College procedures
questions.explanation: A recorded lecture may only be used for the student's own personal use in their studies, and any unauthorised distribution is subject to disciplinary action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Use made of a recorded lecture must only be for personal use in the context of a student's studies. Any unauthorised distribution of such a recording will be subject to disciplinary action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.

questions.question: An external visiting lecturer employed by a consultancy firm, which owns the work its staff generate, delivers a recorded session at the College. Under the Recording Lectures Policy, who retains copyright?
options: London Churchill College, as the session was recorded on its premises
The consultancy firm, as the visiting lecturer's employer
The students who recorded it, for their personal study use
The College lecturer who organised and hosted the session
questions.explanation: External visiting lecturers, or their employer as appropriate, retain copyright on work and any other intellectual property rights they generate.
questions.source_excerpt: External visiting lecturers (or their employer as appropriate) retain copyright on work and any other intellectual property rights they generate

questions.question: The College plans to record a public lecture held on campus for later use. Does the Recording Lectures Policy apply to this recording?
options: No; it governs only the recordings that students make of their own classes
No; public lectures are outside its scope, as they are not programme teaching
Yes; it covers recordings by the College or students, including public lectures
Only if the public lecture forms part of a blended learning taught programme
questions.explanation: The policy sets out when lecture sessions may be recorded either by the College or the students, and its coverage of classroom-based learning includes public lectures.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy sets out the circumstances in which any lecture sessions may be recorded either by the College or the students ... The policy covers the lectures recorded in classroom-based learning including the seminars, tutorials, and public lectures.

questions.question: Last week you gave a student written consent to record your lecture. For this week's lecture you decide recording is not appropriate. What does the Recording Lectures Policy allow?
options: You may refuse, as you decide whether a particular lecture is recorded, giving reasons
You cannot refuse, as consent once given applies to the rest of the module's lectures
You may refuse only if the Programme Leader agrees to withdraw your consent
You may refuse video recording this week, but audio recording must continue
questions.explanation: Lecturers have the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be recorded, and reasons will be provided where permission is denied.
questions.source_excerpt: Lecturers have the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded ... Reasons will be provided as to why permission to record a lecture might be denied

questions.question: A student who recorded your lecture with consent plans to type up a full transcript of it and post the transcript on a public study forum. What does the Recording Lectures Policy say?
options: This is permitted, as a transcript is not itself a recording of the lecture session
This is permitted if the transcript credits you as the lecturer and owner
This is permitted once the recording has served its purpose as a study aid
It must not be reproduced or uploaded in the public domain; use is personal only
questions.explanation: Recorded lecture sessions are the lecturer's intellectual property; students must not share, reproduce or upload them in the public domain, and may use them only for personal use.
questions.source_excerpt: Recorded lecture sessions are the intellectual property of the lecturer. Students must not share, reproduce, or upload them in the public domain. Recorded materials are only permitted for personal use.

questions.question: A student whose Support Agreement Plan permits recording as a reasonable adjustment sets up a camera to video record your seminar, and a classmate objects to being filmed. Under the Recording Lectures Policy, what is the position?
options: The plan overrides the objection, because recording is an agreed reasonable adjustment
The student must first email you for written consent before any filming can continue
The plan only removes the need to ask academics; the College must abide by the objection
The classmate must submit a formal complaint before the College can consider stopping the filming
questions.explanation: A Support Agreement Plan removes only the need to ask individual academics for permission; where other participants object to being filmed, the College has a duty to abide by their wishes.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with special needs who have been given permission through their Support Agreement Plan ... do not need to ask for permission to audio or video record from individual academics. ... other participants in the class may object to being filmed. The College has a duty to abide by their wishes.

questions.question: A student emailed you two days before class asking for consent to audio record your lecture. You have not replied, and the student starts recording, saying you did not refuse. What is the position under the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: Without your written consent, they may not record it
They may record, as they sought consent in advance by email
They may record, as consent to record is not often refused
They must wait for the Programme Leader to confirm the request instead
questions.explanation: Audio recording is permitted only with the lecturer's written consent; emailing a request in advance is how consent is sought, but an unanswered request is not written consent.
questions.source_excerpt: The College permits the audio recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer, which should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class.

questions.question: A student emailed in advance and received your written consent to audio record next week's lecture. On the day, they set up a video camera pointed solely at you. What does the Recording Lectures Policy require?
options: Nothing further, as the camera is positioned to capture solely the lecturer
Nothing further, as written consent to record a lecture covers any format
The verbal agreement of the other students present before filming starts
Your written consent to video recording as well, sought by email before the class
questions.explanation: The policy permits audio and video recording as separate matters, each with the lecturer's written consent sought by email in advance, so consent to audio record does not extend to video.
questions.source_excerpt: The College permits the audio recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer ... The College also permits the video recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer, which should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class.

questions.question: A student recorded a guest session at the College with the external visiting lecturer's consent and argues that, as the College does not own the copyright, they may upload it to YouTube. What does the Recording Lectures Policy say?
options: They may upload it if they credit the visiting lecturer as the copyright holder
Recordings of lectures delivered in the College should not be uploaded online
They may upload it, as the College's upload rules cover only College-owned work
They may upload it after the College's 12-month retention period has ended
questions.explanation: Although visiting lecturers or their employer retain copyright, the policy states that recordings of lectures delivered in the College should not be uploaded online, regardless of who owns the work.
questions.source_excerpt: External visiting lecturers (or their employer as appropriate) retain copyright on work and any other intellectual property rights they generate ... Recordings of lectures delivered in the College (i.e.: YouTube) should not be uploaded online.

questions.question: A blended learning student downloads the College's recording of a live online session and posts it on a public social media page. How does the Recording Lectures Policy treat this?
options: As acceptable, since only recordings that students make themselves are restricted
As a matter for IT Services only, since the College itself produced the recording
As unauthorised distribution, which is subject to disciplinary action
As acceptable once the College's 12-month retention period for it has expired
questions.explanation: The College provides these recordings to blended learning students, but any recorded lecture may only be used personally for study, and unauthorised distribution is subject to disciplinary action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will provide recordings of live online sessions to students who are enrolled in blended learning taught programmes. ... Use made of a recorded lecture must only be for personal use in the context of a student's studies. Any unauthorised distribution of such a recording will be subject to disciplinary action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.

questions.question: Fourteen months after a live online session, a blended learning student asks for the College's recording of it to revise. What does the Recording Lectures Policy indicate about its availability?
options: A recorded lecture is retained for 12 months, so it is beyond that period
Recordings are kept for the duration of studies, so it must still be held
It must be provided, as blended students are entitled to all recordings
It may be released only with the written consent of the lecturer concerned
questions.explanation: A recorded lecture is retained for a 12-month period under the College Data Retention Schedule; storing recordings for the duration of studies is an expectation on students for their own copies, not the College's retention period.
questions.source_excerpt: A recorded lecture is retained for a 12-month period in accordance with the College Data Retention Schedule.

questions.question: A classroom-based student says that, because blended learning students receive College recordings of live online sessions, they are entitled to College recordings of your classroom lectures. What is the correct position under the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: They are right, as the College provides recordings to all enrolled students
They are right, if a Support Agreement Plan lists recording as an adjustment
Recordings of classroom lectures are released at the Programme Leader's discretion
That provision is for blended learning students; they may seek your written consent
questions.explanation: The College's provision of recordings of live online sessions is for students enrolled in blended learning taught programmes; in classroom settings, students may record with the lecturer's written consent sought by email in advance.
questions.source_excerpt: The College permits the audio recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer, which should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class. ... The College will provide recordings of live online sessions to students who are enrolled in blended learning taught programmes.

questions.question: A student whose Support Agreement Plan permits recording lectures as a reasonable adjustment wants to share their recordings of your lectures with a study partner. What is the position under the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: Sharing is allowed, as the recordings form part of an agreed reasonable adjustment
No; the plan removes only the need to ask permission, and use must stay personal
Sharing is allowed if the study partner also has a Support Agreement Plan
Sharing is allowed once the student has passed the module the lectures belong to
questions.explanation: A Support Agreement Plan only removes the need to ask individual academics for permission to record; students must not share recorded lectures, which are permitted for personal use only.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with special needs who have been given permission through their Support Agreement Plan to record lectures ... do not need to ask for permission to audio or video record from individual academics. ... Students must not share, reproduce, or upload them in the public domain. Recorded materials are only permitted for personal use.

questions.question: A colleague refused a student's request to record one of their lectures and gave the student no reason for the refusal. Which part of this is inconsistent with the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: Giving no reason, as reasons will be provided if permission to record is denied
Deciding personally, as the final decision rests with the Programme Leader
Refusing audio recording, as lecturers may refuse only video recording
Refusing at all, as the policy states consent to record is never refused
questions.explanation: Lecturers have the final decision on whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded, but the policy states that reasons will be provided where permission to record is denied.
questions.source_excerpt: Lecturers have the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded, but consent to record is not often refused. ... Reasons will be provided as to why permission to record a lecture might be denied

questions.question: You refuse a request to record your debate-style seminar, where high levels of student discussion are expected. The student offers to record audio only so that nobody is filmed. What does the Recording Lectures Policy support?
options: You must now agree, as refusal applies to video recording but not to audio
You may still refuse, but only once a student in the class formally objects
You must refer the revised request to the Programme Leader, who makes the final decision
You may still refuse, as some students may not wish their voices or opinions recorded
questions.explanation: The policy's example of likely refusal concerns students not wishing their voices or opinions recorded, which audio recording still captures, and the lecturer makes the final decision on audio or video recording.
questions.source_excerpt: Lecturers have the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded ... in cases where high levels of spoken interaction are expected to take place between students during the lecture, the lecturer is likely to refuse to allow recording on grounds that some students will not wish to have their voices or opinions recorded.

questions.question: A student with your written consent to record plans to upload the recording to YouTube as an unlisted video, purely so they can revise from it on their phone. What does the Recording Lectures Policy say?
options: This is fine, as personal use in the context of studies is permitted
This is fine if the student password-protects the video and shares the link with no one
It should not be uploaded online, even though it is for their personal use
It may be uploaded only after the College's 12-month retention period ends
questions.explanation: Although recordings may be used for personal study, the policy separately states that recordings of lectures delivered in the College, such as on YouTube, should not be uploaded online.
questions.source_excerpt: Use made of a recorded lecture must only be for personal use in the context of a student's studies. ... Recordings of lectures delivered in the College (i.e.: YouTube) should not be uploaded online.

questions.question: A student has finished a module but will draw on its recorded lectures for a final-year project. They ask whether they must delete the recordings now. What does the Recording Lectures Policy expect?
options: Delete them now, as recordings must be destroyed at the end of each module
Hand them to the lecturer, who will keep them until the project is complete
Keep them for no more than 12 months, in line with the Data Retention Schedule
Keep them securely until they have served their purpose as a study aid
questions.explanation: Students should store recordings in a secure place for the duration of their studies and delete them once they have served their purpose as a study aid, which has not yet happened here.
questions.source_excerpt: Recordings of lectures should be stored in a secure place for the duration of studies. ... All recordings of lectures or other formal teaching sessions should be deleted or destroyed ... after they have served their purpose as a study aid.

questions.question: A part-time student plans to rewatch your recorded lecture on their own to prepare a presentation for their employer that is unrelated to their course. Under the Recording Lectures Policy, is this permitted?
options: No; use must be personal and in the context of the student's own studies
Yes; the use is personal, as nobody else will see or hear the recording
Only if the Programme Leader first gives written approval for the work use
Yes, provided the student credits you as the lecturer who delivered it
questions.explanation: Use of a recorded lecture must be personal use in the context of the student's studies; preparing work for an employer unrelated to their course falls outside that, even if no one else sees the recording.
questions.source_excerpt: Use made of a recorded lecture must only be for personal use in the context of a student's studies.

questions.question: How does the Recording Lectures Policy treat intellectual property in recorded sessions delivered by College lecturers compared with sessions delivered by external visiting lecturers?
options: The College owns both, as all of the recordings are made on College premises
The College owns College lecturers' sessions; visiting lecturers keep theirs
Lecturers own their sessions; visiting lecturers or their employer retain theirs
The recording student owns both, as the maker of the recording for study
questions.explanation: Recorded lecture sessions are the intellectual property of the lecturer, while external visiting lecturers, or their employer as appropriate, retain copyright and other intellectual property they generate.
questions.source_excerpt: Recorded lecture sessions are the intellectual property of the lecturer. ... External visiting lecturers (or their employer as appropriate) retain copyright on work and any other intellectual property rights they generate

questions.question: A student wants to video record one of your classroom lectures. Which sequence of steps follows the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: Set the camera to film the class, then ask you for verbal consent at the start
Email you in advance for written consent, then position the camera solely on you
Ask classmates for permission, then email you after the class for your consent
Obtain Programme Leader approval, then record the whole session for later sharing
questions.explanation: Written consent for video recording should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class, and the camera should then be placed to capture solely the lecturer.
questions.source_excerpt: The College also permits the video recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer, which should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class. The video camera should be placed in a position which captures solely the lecturer.

questions.question: A student who recorded your lecture with your written consent claims that, as they made the recording, they own it and may sell copies to next year's cohort. What does the Recording Lectures Policy say?
options: They own it, but may sell copies only to students on the same programme
They own it jointly with the College, so the College must approve any sale
The College owns it, so copies may be sold only through the College
It is your intellectual property and must not be reproduced
questions.explanation: Consent to record does not transfer ownership: recorded lecture sessions are the lecturer's intellectual property, and students must not share or reproduce them, as they are for personal use only.
questions.source_excerpt: Recorded lecture sessions are the intellectual property of the lecturer. Students must not share, reproduce, or upload them in the public domain. Recorded materials are only permitted for personal use.

questions.question: A student emails the programme administrator, rather than the lecturer, asking for consent to audio record a lecture, and the administrator replies agreeing. What is the position under the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: Consent is valid, as it was given in writing before the class took place
Consent is valid for audio recording, but video would need the lecturer
Consent is not valid; written consent must come from the lecturer, who decides
Consent is not valid until the Head of Department countersigns the reply
questions.explanation: Audio recording requires the written consent of the lecturer, sought by emailing the lecturer, and it is the lecturer who has the right to make the final decision on recording.
questions.source_excerpt: The College permits the audio recording of lectures with the written consent of the lecturer, which should be sought by emailing the lecturer in advance of the class. ... Lecturers have the right to make the final decision as to whether a particular lecture can be audio or video recorded

questions.question: A student has your written consent to video record your lecture. Which of their planned actions is consistent with the Recording Lectures Policy?
options: Filming the whole room, then blurring classmates' faces before watching it back
Aiming the camera solely at you and storing the file securely during their studies
Uploading the file to a private online folder shared only with their study group
Keeping the file permanently after finishing the course, as they made the recording
questions.explanation: The camera should capture solely the lecturer and recordings should be stored securely for the duration of studies; recordings are for personal use only, should not be uploaded online, and should be deleted once they have served their purpose as a study aid.
questions.source_excerpt: The video camera should be placed in a position which captures solely the lecturer. ... Recorded materials are only permitted for personal use. ... Recordings of lectures should be stored in a secure place for the duration of studies. ... All recordings of lectures or other formal teaching sessions should be deleted or destroyed

questions.question: A student with your written consent places the video camera to capture solely you, but during a group activity you move among the students and several of them appear in the footage. What does the Recording Lectures Policy require?
options: Nothing further, as the camera was set up to capture solely the lecturer
The permission of the students captured in the footage will need to be obtained
Nothing further, since your written consent covers those appearing alongside you
The footage must be handed to the College to be retained for its 12-month period
questions.explanation: Correct camera placement does not remove the separate requirement that, should other individuals be captured in the video recording, their permission will need to be obtained.
questions.source_excerpt: The video camera should be placed in a position which captures solely the lecturer. Should other individuals be captured in the video recording, their permission will need to be obtained.

questions.question: According to the Work Experience Policy, before which type of work experience placement is a DBS check mandatory for students and staff?
options: Any placement that is expected to last longer than three months
Any unpaid placement with a charity or voluntary organisation
Any placement taking place in a health and care setting
Any placement that the College has arranged directly
questions.explanation: The policy states that a DBS check is mandatory for students and staff before starting a work experience placement in any health and care setting.
questions.source_excerpt: A DBS check is mandatory for the students and staff before commencing work experience placement in any health and care setting.

questions.question: According to the Work Experience Policy, whose responsibility is it to arrange a student's work experience as part of their programme?
options: The Work-based Learning Team, on the student's behalf
The Programme Leader, through the College's employer partnerships
The student's Personal Tutor, at one-to-one meetings
The student themselves, with support from the College
questions.explanation: The College supports students to access opportunities, but the policy is explicit that arranging work experience is the students' responsibility.
questions.source_excerpt: The College provides support to students to access fieldwork, work experience and work-based learning opportunities ... It is the responsibility of the students to arrange their work experience as part of their programme.

questions.question: A student has not completed their required work experience by the time their programme ends. Under the Work Experience Policy, how long do they have to complete it?
options: Until the end of the following academic semester
One year after the end of their programme
Six months after the end of their programme
Two years after the end of their programme
questions.explanation: The policy gives students who are late completing work experience one year after the end of their programme to complete it.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who are late with completion of work experience have one year to complete after the end of their programme.

questions.question: You are a Personal Tutor. In a one-to-one meeting, your tutee tells you they are having problems progressing with their work experience. Under the Work Experience Policy, what should you do?
options: Refer the issue to the WBL Coordinator for action
Contact the employer yourself and end the placement
Report the matter directly to the Academic Board
Log it and raise it at the next SEG semester meeting
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors check work experience progress at one-to-one meetings and must refer issues to the WBL Coordinator for action.
questions.source_excerpt: Check student progress in their work experience at weekly one-to-one meetings and refer issues to the WBL coordinator for action.

questions.question: You are accompanying LCC students on a work placement hosted by an external institution. Under the Work Experience Policy, whose policies and regulations must you and the students comply with during the placement?
options: The College's policies and regulations, which override the host's
The host institution's policies and regulations, in place of the College's
Both the College's and the host institution's policies and regulations
The Work Experience Handbook terms, instead of either institution's rules
questions.explanation: The policy requires LCC students and staff on work placement to comply with the policies and regulations of both the College and the host institution.
questions.source_excerpt: During work-placement LCC students and staff must comply with the policies and regulations of the college and the institution where the work-placement is taking place.

questions.question: According to the Work Experience Policy, how is a student's progress assessed while they are on a work placement?
options: A placement supervisor monitors and contributes to continuous assessment, and a College tutor/assessor also assesses them
The employer sets a practical test in the final week, and the result is sent to the Programme Leader as the grade
Assessment is deferred until the placement ends, when the Programme Leader marks the completed PLAD portfolio
An Admissions Officer visits the workplace each month and grades their practice against the programme's intended learning outcomes
questions.explanation: Each student is assigned a placement supervisor who monitors and contributes to continuous assessment, and a College tutor/assessor also assesses them during practice on placement.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will be assigned a placement supervisor in each setting who will monitor and contribute to the continuous assessment of their progress. Additionally, a tutor/assessor from the College will assess students during their practice on placement.

questions.question: A student on a programme where work experience is not a mandatory requirement asks whether the College recommends finding a placement anyway. What is the College's position under the Work Experience Policy?
options: It leaves the decision to the student where work experience is not a mandatory programme requirement
It advises all students to find work experience, whether or not their programme requires it
It discourages optional placements so students can focus on their assessed coursework
It asks all students to defer optional placements until their mandatory modules are passed
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College advises all students to find work experience, on programmes where it is mandatory and on those where it is not.
questions.source_excerpt: The College advises all students to find work experience on programmes where it is a mandatory requirement as well as those where it is not.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, what are students required to complete at induction in relation to work experience?
options: A Work Experience Information Form (WEIF) showing their current work experience status and whether they are seeking it
A Practice Learning, Assessment and Development (PLAD) portfolio setting out their placement goals and target hours
A declaration form confirming the link between their intended placement and the curriculum, countersigned by their tutor
A Work Experience Handbook agreement, countersigned by the Programme Leader before their placement search begins
questions.explanation: At induction the College requires students to complete a Work Experience Information Form (WEIF) identifying their current work experience status and whether they are seeking work experience.
questions.source_excerpt: The College discusses the importance and scope of work experience at induction and requires students to complete a Work Experience Information Form (WEIF) identifying their current work experience status and if they are seeking work experience;

questions.question: According to the Work Experience Policy, what does the College expect of employers who provide work experience to students?
options: To grade the student's PLAD portfolio and forward the marked copy to the Programme Leader
To hold weekly meetings with the student and send the College a weekly written progress report
To upload the student's signed Work Experience Handbook to the VLE once the placement is complete
To monitor students, hold monthly meetings and give written comments on their performance at the end
questions.explanation: The policy expects employers to monitor students, have monthly meetings and make written comments on their performance at the end of the work experience.
questions.source_excerpt: The College expects employers to monitor students, have monthly meetings and to make written comments about their performance at the end of their work experience;

questions.question: You are an Admissions Officer. During recruitment, an applicant mentions they currently work part-time for a local retail company. Under the Work Experience Policy, what should you do?
options: Tell them the College will find and arrange a suitable placement for them once they have completed induction
Inform them of the programme's work experience requirements and note the organisation they work with
Leave their current job off the record until they declare it on the WEIF at induction
Ask them to begin their PLAD portfolio now so that hours in their current job count towards it
questions.explanation: At the recruitment stage Admissions Officers inform students about the programme's work experience requirements and note the organisation they work with, and current work status is noted in the application documentation.
questions.source_excerpt: At the recruitment stage, students are asked about their current work status and this is noted in their application documentation; ... Inform students about the work experience requirements of the programme at the recruitment stage and note the organisation they are working with if appropriate.

questions.question: According to the Work Experience Policy, when do students submit their Practice Learning, Assessment and Development (PLAD) portfolio?
options: At induction, before they begin looking for a placement
At each monthly meeting held with their employer
Once they have completed their work experience placement
At the end of every semester, to the Student Engagement Group
questions.explanation: The policy states that students complete the PLAD portfolio, which records reflective activities and time in work experience roles, and submit it once they have completed their work experience.
questions.source_excerpt: Students complete a Practice Learning, Assessment and Development (PLAD) portfolio that includes reflective activities and expectations and time undertaken in work experience roles. Students complete the PLAD portfolio and submit on completion of their work experience;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, who must sign the Work Experience Handbook that a student completes?
options: The student's Personal Tutor
The Programme Leader for their course
The Head of Student Engagement
The student's employer or supervisor
questions.explanation: Among the students' responsibilities, the policy states that the Work Experience Handbook is signed by their employer or supervisor.
questions.source_excerpt: Students complete a Work Experience Handbook, and this is signed by their employer or supervisor;

questions.question: The introduction to the Work Experience Policy names two forms of work experience that London Churchill College students undertake. Which two does it name?
options: Job shadowing and industry mentoring schemes
Work-integrated learning and work-based learning
Apprenticeships and sandwich-year placements
Summer internships and graduate trainee schemes
questions.explanation: The introduction states that students undertake a variety of work experience, including work-integrated learning and work-based learning.
questions.source_excerpt: Students undertake a variety of work experience including work-integrated learning and work-based learning.

questions.question: According to its stated aim, the Work Experience Policy identifies responsibilities for which parties?
options: The College, students and the awarding body
Students, employers and the Students' Union
The College, employers and local authorities
The College, students and employers
questions.explanation: The aim section states that the policy identifies responsibilities for the College, students and employers.
questions.source_excerpt: The Policy sets out arrangements for and integration of work experience and voluntary work-based learning into our programmes and identifies responsibilities for the College, students and employers.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, which statement about payment for work experience is correct?
options: It must be unpaid for the hours to count towards the programme
It must be paid at no less than the National Minimum Wage
It may be paid or unpaid, and includes real work environments
It may be paid only where the College arranged the placement
questions.explanation: The policy states that work experience may be paid or unpaid, and that it includes work-integrated learning, work-based learning and real work environments.
questions.source_excerpt: Work experience may be paid or unpaid. It includes work-integrated learning, work-based learning and real work environments.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, where does the College add details of student work experience so that they can be monitored?
options: In the central Student Management System (SMS)
In the Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) course area
In each student's PLAD portfolio, held by their tutor
In the Programme Handbook for the student's course
questions.explanation: The College adds details of student work experience into a central Student Management System (SMS), which is monitored by the Work-based Learning Coordinator.
questions.source_excerpt: The College adds details of student work experience into a central Student Management System (SMS) which is monitored by the Work-based Learning Coordinator.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, which employers does the College contact to confirm their suitability?
options: Employers in health and care settings only
Employers that offer unpaid placements
All employers providing work experience
Employers the College itself has arranged
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College contacts all employers providing work experience to confirm their suitability, and should plan workplace visits where appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: The College contacts all employers providing work experience to confirm their suitability.

questions.question: According to the Work Experience Policy, besides relevant professional experience and knowledge of a particular industry, what can a work experience placement give students?
options: Professional body membership
A professional licence
Potential references
Module exemptions
questions.explanation: The policy supports staff encouraging students to take a placement to gain relevant professional experience, knowledge of a particular industry and potential references.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is supportive of staff encourgaing their students to undertake a work expereince placement to gain relevena professional expereince and knowledge of a particualr industry as well as protential references.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, what do students sign to confirm that they have completed their work experience?
options: A declaration form, which also confirms the link to the curriculum
A Work Experience Information Form (WEIF), countersigned by the WBL Team
A placement attendance register held by their Personal Tutor
A final contract of employment issued by the host organisation
questions.explanation: Students sign a declaration form confirming completion of their work experience and its link to the curriculum, and also complete a brief reflective survey.
questions.source_excerpt: Students sign a declaration form confirming completion of their work experience and the link to the curriculum. They also complete a brief survey reflecting on their experiences.

questions.question: The Work Experience Policy gives examples of others, besides the provider, towards whom students on work experience may have additional responsibilities. Which examples does it give?
options: The provider's shareholders and board of directors
Customers, other employees and the public
The awarding body and the Office for Students
Their classmates and the Students' Union
questions.explanation: The policy notes that students on work experience may have additional responsibilities towards providers and to others such as customers, other employees and the public.
questions.source_excerpt: Students undertaking work experience may have additional responsibilities towards the providers and to others such as their customers, other employees and the public;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, what does LCC offer to employers who provide work experience for its students?
options: A contribution towards the student's placement wages
Free places for their staff on LCC short courses
A reduced rate for advertising their job vacancies
Mentoring, to help them in working with students
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC offers mentoring to employers to help them in working with students.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC offers mentoring to employers to help them in working with students;

questions.question: The Work Experience Policy says employers can contact the College to discuss issues arising from a placement. Which examples of such issues does it give?
options: Pay rates or working hours agreed with the student
Visa status or the tuition fees owed to the College
Safeguarding or the student's attendance on placement
Travel costs or the uniform the student must wear
questions.explanation: The policy states that employers can contact the College to discuss any issues arising from the placement, giving safeguarding and attendance as examples.
questions.source_excerpt: Employers can contact the College to discuss any issues such as safeguarding or attendance arising from the placement;

questions.question: According to the Work Experience Policy, where does the College publish statements informing students of their work experience commitments on their programmes?
options: In the Programme Handbook, on the website and in the VLE
In the student's offer letter and enrolment contract
In a placement agreement signed with each employer
In the end of term surveys and the SMS student portal
questions.explanation: The College informs students of their work experience commitments through statements in the Programme Handbook, on the website and in the VLE, as well as at induction and at the start of the application process.
questions.source_excerpt: The College informs students of their commitments to work experience on their programmes through statements in the Programme Handbook information on the Web site and in the VLE, in the induction and at the start of the application process;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, how often as a minimum does the Student Engagement Group (SEG) meet to monitor student work experience?
options: Once a fortnight
Once a semester
Once a month
Once a week
questions.explanation: The Student Engagement Group meets at least once a semester to monitor student work experience and other practice activities.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Engagement Group (SEG) meets minimum once a semester to monitor student work experience and other practice activities and reports to PEG;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, who provides the Academic Board with an annual report evaluating the effectiveness of the College's work experience arrangements?
options: The Head of Student Engagement
The Work-based Learning Coordinator
Each Programme Leader for their course
The Head of Admissions and Recruitment
questions.explanation: The Head of Student Engagement is responsible for giving the Academic Board an annual report evaluating the effectiveness of the College's work experience arrangements.
questions.source_excerpt: The Head of Student Engagement is responsible for providing the Academic Board with an annual report evaluating the effectiveness of the work experience arrangements of the College

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, which role uploads the work experience handbooks to the VLE?
options: The Head of Data and Information Technology
Admissions Officers
Personal Tutors
Academic staff / WBL Administrator
questions.explanation: Under Roles and Responsibilities, the Academic staff / WBL Administrator uploads the handbooks to the VLE and provides information about work experience requirements.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic staff / WBL Administrator ... Uploads the handbooks to the VLE;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, how often do Personal Tutors check their students' progress in work experience?
options: At monthly one-to-one meetings
At weekly one-to-one meetings
At the end of each teaching semester
Only when the employer reports a concern
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors check student progress in work experience at weekly one-to-one meetings and refer any issues to the WBL Coordinator for action.
questions.source_excerpt: Check student progress in their work experience at weekly one-to-one meetings and refer issues to the WBL coordinator for action.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, which role is responsible for all data security, reports on student activity and management information, including end of term surveys?
options: The Work-based Learning (WBL) Coordinator
The Academic staff / WBL Administrator
The Programme Leader for each programme
The Head of Data and Information Technology
questions.explanation: The Head of Data and Information Technology is responsible for all data security, reports on student activity and management information, including end of term surveys.
questions.source_excerpt: Head of Data and Information Technology 11.8.1. Responsible for all data security, reports on student activity and management information for review and action, including end of term surveys.

questions.question: The College has arranged a work experience placement for a student with a local provider. Under the Work Experience Policy, what must the College ensure in relation to this provider?
options: That the provider agrees to offer students paid placements only
That the provider takes on the College's insurance liability for students
That risks are assessed and proportionate safeguards are in place
That the provider joins the College's formal employer partnership scheme
questions.explanation: For work experience providers arranged by the College, the policy requires that risks are assessed and that appropriate and proportionate safeguards are in place.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that risks associated with work experience providers arranged by the College are assessed and that appropriate and proportionate safeguards are in place;

questions.question: The College is carrying out due diligence on a work experience provider. Under the Work Experience Policy, what does the College take reasonable steps to ensure about the learning experiences offered?
options: That they are relevant, valid and related to programme outcomes
That they are approved in advance by the Student Engagement Group
That they lead to a recognised professional licence for the student
That they are paid and meet the minimum hours set by the awarding body
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College undertakes due diligence with providers and takes reasonable steps to ensure learning experiences are relevant, valid and related to the outcomes of the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: The College undertakes due diligence with providers and takes reasonable steps to ensure that learning experiences are relevant, valid and related to the outcomes of the programme.

questions.question: A member of staff is due to support LCC students on a work experience placement in a care home. Under the Work Experience Policy, what must happen before the placement starts?
options: Only the students need a DBS check, as staff are covered by the College
The care home must carry out its own induction in place of a DBS check
A DBS check is needed only if the placement lasts longer than one month
The staff member and the students must each have a DBS check
questions.explanation: A DBS check is mandatory for both students and staff before commencing a work experience placement in any health and care setting, which includes a care home.
questions.source_excerpt: A DBS check is mandatory for the students and staff before commencing work experience placement in any health and care setting.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, which sequence correctly describes when a student completes their work experience paperwork, from the start of their programme to the end of their placement?
options: PLAD portfolio at induction, then the WEIF, then the declaration form on completion
WEIF at induction, then the PLAD portfolio and the declaration form on completion
Declaration form at induction, then the WEIF, then the PLAD portfolio on completion
WEIF at induction, then the declaration form before placement, then the PLAD on completion
questions.explanation: Students complete the WEIF at induction; on completion of their work experience they submit the PLAD portfolio and sign a declaration form confirming that completion.
questions.source_excerpt: at induction and requires students to complete a Work Experience Information Form (WEIF) ... Students complete the PLAD portfolio and submit on completion of their work experience; ... Students sign a declaration form confirming completion of their work experience

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy procedure, which of the following takes place at student induction rather than at the recruitment stage?
options: Students are asked about their current work status, noted in their application documentation
The College discusses the scope of work experience and students complete a WEIF
Admissions Officers note the organisation the student is working with, if appropriate
Students sign a declaration form linking their planned placement to the curriculum
questions.explanation: At recruitment students are asked about their current work status; at induction the College discusses the importance and scope of work experience and students complete a Work Experience Information Form (WEIF).
questions.source_excerpt: At the recruitment stage, students are asked about their current work status and this is noted in their application documentation; ... The College discusses the importance and scope of work experience at induction and requires students to complete a Work Experience Information Form (WEIF)

questions.question: A student has found their own work experience placement with an employer that is new to the College. Under the Work Experience Policy, what should the College do?
options: Contact the employer to confirm its suitability and plan a workplace visit where appropriate
Take no action, as students who arrange their own placements are responsible for suitability
Ask the Academic Board to approve the employer before the student is allowed to start
Require the employer to sign a formal partnership agreement with the College first
questions.explanation: The College contacts all employers providing work experience to confirm their suitability, including those found by students, and should plan to visit workplace settings where appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: The College contacts all employers providing work experience to confirm their suitability. The College should plan to visit workplace settings where appropriate;

questions.question: The Work Experience Policy aims to help students reflect on their work experience. Which document that students complete includes reflective activities and the time undertaken in work experience roles?
options: The Work Experience Information Form (WEIF) completed at induction
The declaration form signed to confirm the link to the curriculum
The application documentation completed at the recruitment stage
The Practice Learning, Assessment and Development (PLAD) portfolio
questions.explanation: The PLAD portfolio includes reflective activities and expectations and the time undertaken in work experience roles, supporting the policy's aim of helping students reflect on their work experience.
questions.source_excerpt: helping students reflect on their work experience and their professional and personal development ... Students complete a Practice Learning, Assessment and Development (PLAD) portfolio that includes reflective activities and expectations and time undertaken in work experience roles.

questions.question: Monitoring of the Student Management System (SMS) shows that a student is behind in their work experience activities. Under the Work Experience Policy, how is this acted on?
options: Through a formal warning letter issued by the Academic Board
Through a written report sent to the student's employer
Through in-class visits and follow-up emails, calls and meetings
Through suspension from classes until the placement resumes
questions.explanation: The WBL role that monitors the SMS acts when students are behind in work experience activities through in-class visits and follow-up emails, calls and meetings.
questions.source_excerpt: Monitors the SMS and acts when students are behind in work experience activities through in class visits and follow-up emails, calls and meetings;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, which of the following is listed as a responsibility of employers rather than of students?
options: Finding suitable work experience and/or work-based learning
Meeting the norms and expectations for professional conduct in the field
Complying with all statutory requirements with work experience students
Completing a Work Experience Handbook and having it signed off
questions.explanation: Employers are responsible for the health, safety and welfare of their employees and should comply with all statutory requirements with work experience students; the other options are listed as student responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: Employers are responsible for the health, safety and welfare of their employees and should comply with all statutory requirements with work experience students;

questions.question: A partner organisation has offered new opportunities to LCC students. Under the Work Experience Policy, how does the College inform students of opportunities available with partners and third parties?
options: Through the awarding body's national placement listings shared at each induction
Through tutor contact and dissemination by the WBL Team, staff members and posters
Through a termly bulletin from the Academic Board, emailed to all students
Through the Head of Data and IT's end of term surveys and management reports
questions.explanation: The College informs students of opportunities with partners and third parties through tutor contact and dissemination through the Work based Learning Team, staff members and posters.
questions.source_excerpt: The College informs students of opportunities available with partners and third parties through tutor contact and dissemination through the Work based Learning Team, staff members and posters.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, who attends the monthly meetings the College arranges to monitor the status of student work experience and action any enhancements?
options: The Academic Board, PEG and the Head of Data and Information Technology
Employers, placement supervisors and the College's Admissions Officers
Students, their employers and elected student representatives
The WBL Coordinator, Head of Student Engagement, Programme Leader and tutors
questions.explanation: The College arranges monthly meetings with the WBL Coordinator, Head of Student Engagement, Programme Leader and tutors to monitor student work experience and action enhancements.
questions.source_excerpt: The College arranges monthly meetings with the WBL Coordinator, Head of Student Engagement, Programme Leader and tutors to monitor the status of student work experience, to identify areas for enhancement and action any enhancements;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, how do the Student Engagement Group (SEG) and the Head of Student Engagement each report on work experience?
options: SEG reports to PEG; the Head of Student Engagement gives the Academic Board an annual report
SEG reports to the Academic Board; the Head of Student Engagement reports monthly to PEG
SEG reports to the Head of Student Engagement, who sends PEG a report each semester
SEG reports to the Board of Directors; the Head of Student Engagement reports to PEG
questions.explanation: The SEG monitors student work experience and reports to PEG, while the Head of Student Engagement provides the Academic Board with an annual report on the effectiveness of the arrangements.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Engagement Group (SEG) meets minimum once a semester to monitor student work experience and other practice activities and reports to PEG; ... The Head of Student Engagement is responsible for providing the Academic Board with an annual report

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, when does the College review the risks associated with work experience arranged by the College and by students?
options: Only after an employer reports a safeguarding concern to the College
Only for placements that take place in health and care settings
On a periodic basis or as part of the programme review
Only at each student's end-of-placement review, using the PLAD portfolio
questions.explanation: The College reviews the risks associated with work experience arranged by both the College and students on a periodic basis or as part of the programme review.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will review the risks associated with work experience arranged by both the College and by students on a periodic basis or as part of the programme review.

questions.question: A colleague notices out-of-date work experience data in the Student Management System (SMS). Under the Work Experience Policy, which role is responsible for updating and quality control of data in the SMS?
options: The Head of Data and Information Technology
The Work based Learning Manager
The Academic staff / WBL Administrator
The student's Personal Tutor
questions.explanation: Under Roles and Responsibilities, the Work based Learning Manager is responsible for updating and quality control of data in the SMS.
questions.source_excerpt: Work based Learning Manager 11.2.1. Is responsible for bringing in work experience activity in and around the curriculum; 11.2.2. Is Responsible for updating and quality control of data in the SMS;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, what is the role of Programme Leaders in the running of work experience?
options: Signing each student's Work Experience Handbook in place of the employer or supervisor
Carrying out DBS checks on students before any health and care placement begins
Writing the end-of-placement comments on each student's performance for the employer
Supporting the WBL Coordinator and Head of Student Engagement and managing academic content
questions.explanation: Programme Leaders support the WBL Coordinator and the Head of Student Engagement in the smooth running of work experience in the curriculum and manage academic related content.
questions.source_excerpt: Provide support for the WBL Coordinator and the Head of Student ... Engagement in the smooth running of work experience in the curriculum and ... manage academic related content.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, Admissions Officers tell students about work experience requirements at the recruitment stage. Which role provides information about work experience requirements during the programme?
options: Academic staff / WBL Administrator
The Head of Data and Information Technology
The student's placement supervisor
The Student Engagement Group (SEG)
questions.explanation: The Academic staff / WBL Administrator uploads the handbooks to the VLE and provides information about work experience requirements during the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic staff / WBL Administrator 11.5.1. Uploads the handbooks to the VLE; 11.5.2. Provides information about work experience requirements during the ... programme.

questions.question: A lecturer is explaining to their class why the College supports work experience. Which reason is given in the Purpose of Work Experience section of the Work Experience Policy?
options: It helps the College to meet its graduate employment targets
It develops the skills and attitudes needed to succeed in the workplace
It replaces taught sessions on the practical modules of the programme they study
It lets students gain academic credit for their prior employment
questions.explanation: The Purpose section states that the College supports and encourages students' development of the skills and attitudes required to succeed in the workplace.
questions.source_excerpt: The College supports and encourages all student's development of necessary skills and attitues that are required to succeed in the workplace.

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, after tracking the take-up of work experience, how does the College contact students to make sure their work experience takes place successfully?
options: Through automated reminders sent from the SMS to students and their employers
Through written notices issued by Admissions Officers at the end of each term
Through a placement review panel convened by the Academic Board at the end of every semester
Through email and face-to-face meetings with personal tutors and/or the WBL Team
questions.explanation: The College tracks take-up of work experience and contacts students through email and face-to-face meetings with personal tutors and/or the Work based Learning Team.
questions.source_excerpt: The College tracks the take-up of work experience among students and contacts students to ensure work experience takes place successfully through email and face-to-face meetings with personal tutors and/or the Work based Learning Team;

questions.question: A student has arranged their own work experience placement directly with an employer. Under the Work Experience Policy's provisions on risk, which statement is correct for this placement?
options: Only the provider risk assessment applies, since that duty covers every provider a student uses
Neither provision applies, as the risk of a self-arranged placement rests with the student
The periodic risk review applies, as it covers work experience arranged by students too
Both provisions apply, but only where the placement is in a health and care setting
questions.explanation: The duty to assess risks and put safeguards in place is stated for providers arranged by the College, while the periodic risk review expressly covers work experience arranged by both the College and students.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that risks associated with work experience providers arranged by the College are assessed and that appropriate and proportionate safeguards are in place; ... The College will review the risks associated with work experience arranged by both the College and by students on a periodic basis or as part of the programme review.

questions.question: The Head of Student Engagement wants to make a substantial change to the work experience procedure. Under the Work Experience Policy, through which route is approval for such a change sought?
options: The annual report to the Academic Board, which includes approvals sought for substantial changes
The Student Engagement Group's semester report to PEG, which approves changes to procedure
A vote of Programme Leaders, who manage the academic related content of work experience
The Head of Data and IT's end of term survey reports, circulated to the Admissions team
questions.explanation: The Head of Student Engagement's annual report to the Academic Board covers the effectiveness of the arrangements, enhancements made and approvals sought for substantial changes to procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: The Head of Student Engagement is responsible for providing the Academic Board with an annual report evaluating the effectiveness of the work experience arrangements of the College, enhancements made to the process and approvals sought for substantial changes to procedure;

questions.question: Several meetings described in the Work Experience Policy monitor student work experience. Which option matches each of the following meetings to its correct frequency?
options: Tutor one-to-ones monthly; employer meetings with students weekly; SEG at least once a semester
Tutor one-to-ones weekly; employer meetings with students monthly; SEG at least once a semester
Tutor one-to-ones weekly; employer meetings with students fortnightly; SEG at least once a month
Tutor one-to-ones fortnightly; employer meetings with students monthly; SEG at least once a year
questions.explanation: Personal Tutors check progress at weekly one-to-ones, employers are expected to hold monthly meetings with students, and the SEG meets at least once a semester.
questions.source_excerpt: The College expects employers to monitor students, have monthly meetings ... The Student Engagement Group (SEG) meets minimum once a semester to monitor student work experience ... Check student progress in their work experience at weekly one-to-one meetings

questions.question: A student has arranged a paid work experience placement in a care home and plans to apply for a DBS check during their first month there. Under the Work Experience Policy, what is the position?
options: This is acceptable, as a paid placement the student arranged is outside the DBS requirement
This is acceptable, provided the check is complete before the student's first assessment
This is acceptable only if their placement supervisor monitors them closely until it is done
A DBS check is mandatory and must be in place before the student starts the placement
questions.explanation: Work experience may be paid or unpaid, and a DBS check is mandatory before commencing a placement in any health and care setting, so it cannot be deferred into the placement.
questions.source_excerpt: Work experience may be paid or unpaid. ... A DBS check is mandatory for the students and staff before commencing work experience placement in any health and care setting.

questions.question: A student's programme has ended but they still have work experience outstanding. Under the Work Experience Policy, what applies to finishing the work experience and submitting their PLAD portfolio?
options: They have one year after the programme ends to complete, and submit the PLAD portfolio on completion
They must submit the PLAD portfolio by the programme end date, with the missing hours marked incomplete
They have six months after the programme ends, and submit the PLAD portfolio at the next SEG meeting
They have one year to complete, but must submit the PLAD portfolio before the programme end date
questions.explanation: Students who are late have one year after the end of their programme to complete their work experience, and the PLAD portfolio is submitted on completion of the work experience.
questions.source_excerpt: Students complete the PLAD portfolio and submit on completion of their work experience; ... Students who are late with completion of work experience have one year to complete after the end of their programme.

questions.question: Staff are dividing up tasks relating to the Work Experience Handbook. Under the Work Experience Policy, which allocation of handbook tasks between College roles is correct?
options: Personal Tutors upload the handbooks to the VLE; the Programme Leader administers checks on them
The WBL Administrator uploads the handbooks to the VLE; the WBL Manager administers checks on them
The WBL Manager uploads the handbooks to the VLE; Admissions Officers administer checks on them
The Head of Data and IT uploads the handbooks to the VLE; Personal Tutors administer checks on them
questions.explanation: The Academic staff / WBL Administrator uploads the handbooks to the VLE, and the WBL Manager administers checks on and discusses the Work Experience Handbook.
questions.source_excerpt: Work-based Learning (WBL) Manager ... Administers checks and discusses the Work Experience Handbook. ... Academic staff / WBL Administrator ... Uploads the handbooks to the VLE;

questions.question: An applicant says they expected to hear about work experience commitments only after enrolling. Under the Work Experience Policy, at which points does the College inform students of these commitments?
options: At enrolment, when the offer letter sets out the programme's work experience terms and hours
Once a placement is confirmed, through the employer's own workplace induction for new starters
At the end of the first semester, when the SEG reviews each student's placement plans
At the start of the application process, at induction and in published statements
questions.explanation: The College informs students of their work experience commitments through statements in the Programme Handbook, website and VLE, at induction and at the start of the application process.
questions.source_excerpt: The College informs students of their commitments to work experience on their programmes through statements in the Programme Handbook information on the Web site and in the VLE, in the induction and at the start of the application process;

questions.question: A concern is raised about the security of student work experience data, and separately about errors in data held in the SMS. Under the Work Experience Policy, which roles are responsible for each?
options: The WBL Manager for data security; the Head of Data and IT for SMS data quality
The WBL Administrator for data security; Personal Tutors for SMS data quality
The Head of Data and IT for data security; the WBL Manager for SMS data quality
The Programme Leader for data security; Admissions Officers for SMS data quality
questions.explanation: The Head of Data and Information Technology is responsible for all data security, while the Work based Learning Manager is responsible for updating and quality control of data in the SMS.
questions.source_excerpt: Is Responsible for updating and quality control of data in the SMS; ... Responsible for all data security, reports on student activity and management information

questions.question: A programme team proposes letting students progress without meeting the awarding body's progression requirement for the work experience element. Under the Work Experience Policy, what is the position?
options: It may do so if the Head of Student Engagement records the change in the annual report
It may not, as the College must comply with the awarding body progression requirement
