It may do so if the Academic Board, which has oversight of work experience, agrees to it
It may do so if the Student Engagement Group approves the change at its next semester meeting
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College must comply with the awarding body progression requirement for the work experience element, so no internal body, meeting or report can waive it.
questions.source_excerpt: The College must comply with the awarding body progression requirement for the work experience element;

questions.question: A student on a retail work experience placement asks to whom they have responsibilities while on placement. Which answer reflects the Work Experience Policy?
options: To the employer and the College only, as duties to customers and the public rest with the employer
To the employer, the College and the awarding body, but not to the provider's customers
To the College and their own progression only, as the employer is not a party to their programme
To the employer, the College, their own progression and others such as customers and the public
questions.explanation: The College helps students understand their responsibility to the employer, the College and their own progression, and students may have additional responsibilities to others such as customers, other employees and the public.
questions.source_excerpt: The College assists students in understanding their responsibility to the employer, the College and their own progression in relation to their work. ... Students undertaking work experience may have additional responsibilities towards the providers and to others such as their customers, other employees and the public;

questions.question: Under the Work Experience Policy, which statement correctly distinguishes the role of the Head of Student Engagement from that of the Work based Learning Manager?
options: The Head oversees work experience and is responsible for the policy; the Manager brings in activity
The Head brings in activity and contacts external companies; the Manager is responsible for the policy
The Head updates and quality-controls SMS data; the Manager gives the Academic Board an annual report
The Head uploads the handbooks to the VLE; the Manager informs applicants at the recruitment stage
questions.explanation: The Head of Student Engagement has oversight of work experience within the curriculum and is responsible for the policy, while the Work based Learning Manager brings in work experience activity and has contact with external companies.
questions.source_excerpt: Has oversight of work experience within the curriculum and is responsible for the Work Experience Policy. ... Work based Learning Manager 11.2.1. Is responsible for bringing in work experience activity in and around the curriculum;

questions.question: An employer tells the College it is unsure how best to work with its placement student and is also concerned about the student's attendance. Under the Work Experience Policy, what is available to it?
options: It must end the placement and notify the awarding body before any support is offered
It must raise attendance with the student only, as the College offers employers no support
It can discuss the attendance issue with the College, and LCC offers mentoring to employers
It can ask the Student Engagement Group for training, as the SEG handles attendance issues
questions.explanation: Employers can contact the College to discuss issues such as attendance arising from the placement, and LCC offers mentoring to help employers work with students.
questions.source_excerpt: Employers can contact the College to discuss any issues such as safeguarding or attendance arising from the placement; ... LCC offers mentoring to employers to help them in working with students;

questions.question: A student's work experience is split between two different workplace settings. Under the Work Experience Policy, how is their progress monitored and assessed?
options: One placement supervisor is chosen to cover both settings, and the employer grades the PLAD
A placement supervisor is assigned in each setting, and a College tutor/assessor also assesses them
The first setting assigns a supervisor, and the second is overseen by the student's Personal Tutor
A College tutor/assessor replaces placement supervisors whenever more than one setting is used
questions.explanation: Students are assigned a placement supervisor in each setting to monitor and contribute to continuous assessment, and a College tutor/assessor also assesses them during practice on placement.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will be assigned a placement supervisor in each setting who will monitor and contribute to the continuous assessment of their progress. Additionally, a tutor/assessor from the College will assess students during their practice on placement.

questions.question: A student has just finished their work experience placement. Under the Work Experience Policy, which of the following is not one of the tasks they complete at that point?
options: Submitting their completed PLAD portfolio
Signing a declaration confirming the curriculum link
Completing a brief survey reflecting on the experience
Completing a Work Experience Information Form (WEIF)
questions.explanation: The WEIF is completed at induction; on completion students submit the PLAD portfolio, sign a declaration confirming completion and the link to the curriculum, and complete a brief reflective survey.
questions.source_excerpt: at induction and requires students to complete a Work Experience Information Form (WEIF) ... Students complete the PLAD portfolio and submit on completion of their work experience; ... Students sign a declaration form confirming completion of their work experience and the link to the curriculum. They also complete a brief survey reflecting on their experiences.

questions.question: A new tutor asks where details of student work experience are recorded and where student records are kept under the Work Experience Policy. Which answer is correct?
options: Details are logged in the VLE, and records are held by each student's Personal Tutor
Details are logged in each PLAD portfolio, and records are kept by the host employer
Details go into the central SMS, and records are stored securely in the WBL room
Details are logged in the Programme Handbook, and records are held by Admissions Officers
questions.explanation: The College adds details of student work experience into the central Student Management System (SMS), and student records are stored securely in the Work-based Learning room.
questions.source_excerpt: The College adds details of student work experience into a central Student Management System (SMS) which is monitored by the Work-based Learning Coordinator. Student records are stored securely in the Work-based Learning room;

questions.question: The College is building links with an organisation that cannot host placements but could give guest presentations to students. How does this fit the Work Experience Policy's aims for partnerships?
options: It is out of scope, as partnerships exist only to secure placements that students can attend
It is in scope only if the link is formalised, as informal partnerships are not recognised
It is in scope only once the organisation also agrees to host paid work experience placements
It is in scope, as partnerships also support presentations, projects and work-related activities
questions.explanation: The College builds formal and informal partnerships to expand its network for work experience opportunities and for presentations, projects and other work-related activities around the curriculum.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will continue to build formal and informal partnerships with external organisations to expand our network for work experience opportunities and for presentations, projects and other work-related activities in and around the curriculum.

questions.question: A student wants an unpaid voluntary role at a local charity to be treated as work experience. Under the Work Experience Policy, can this kind of arrangement fall within the policy?
options: No, as the policy covers only paid placements with commercial or public sector employers
Yes, as it may be unpaid and the policy covers voluntary work-based learning
Only if the College arranged the placement itself and first assessed the charity's risks
Only if the charity works in a health and care setting that requires a DBS check first
questions.explanation: The policy's aim covers the integration of work experience and voluntary work-based learning into programmes, and it states that work experience may be paid or unpaid.
questions.source_excerpt: The Policy sets out arrangements for and integration of work experience and voluntary work-based learning into our programmes ... Work experience may be paid or unpaid.

questions.question: The College has arranged a work experience placement for a student with an external employer. Under the Work Experience Policy, which statement correctly describes the duties of the employer and of the College for this placement?
options: The employer should comply with all statutory requirements with the student; the College ensures risks are assessed and safeguards are in place
The employer's statutory duties cover its own staff only; the College assumes all statutory duties owed to the student during the placement
The College takes over the employer's statutory duties for the student; risks need assessing only for placements in health and care settings
The employer holds all duties, as the College assesses risks only for placements that students have arranged for themselves
questions.explanation: Employers should comply with all statutory requirements with work experience students, while for providers it has arranged the College ensures risks are assessed and appropriate, proportionate safeguards are in place.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that risks associated with work experience providers arranged by the College are assessed and that appropriate and proportionate safeguards are in place; ... Employers are responsible for the health, safety and welfare of their employees and should comply with all statutory requirements with work experience students;

questions.question: An employer hosting an LCC student on work experience asks which parts of the placement paperwork it is expected to complete. Under the Work Experience Policy, which answer is correct?
options: Signing the declaration form that confirms completion of the placement and its link to the curriculum
Completing the brief reflective survey and submitting the student's PLAD portfolio on completion
Signing the student's Work Experience Handbook and writing comments on their performance at the end
Completing the Work Experience Information Form (WEIF) and countersigning the student's application
questions.explanation: The Work Experience Handbook is signed by the employer or supervisor, and employers are expected to make written comments on the student's performance at the end; the declaration form, survey, PLAD portfolio and WEIF are completed by the student.
questions.source_excerpt: Students complete a Work Experience Handbook, and this is signed by their employer or supervisor; ... The College expects employers to monitor students, have monthly meetings and to make written comments about their performance at the end of their work experience;

questions.question: An LCC student on work experience at an accountancy firm asks what standards they must meet while on the placement. Under the Work Experience Policy, which answer is correct?
options: The College's and the firm's policies and regulations, and professional conduct norms in accountancy
The firm's policies and regulations only, as the College's own regulations are suspended during placements
Both organisations' policies and regulations, but not professional conduct norms, which apply only to qualified staff
The conduct standards in their Work Experience Handbook, which replace both organisations' own policies on placement
questions.explanation: Students on placement must comply with the policies and regulations of both the College and the host, and are responsible for meeting the norms and expectations for professional conduct in their field of work.
questions.source_excerpt: During work-placement LCC students and staff must comply with the policies and regulations of the college and the institution where the work-placement is taking place. ... Students are responsible for meeting the norms and expectations for professional conduct in the field of work or study that they are undertaking;

questions.question: A new student on a programme where work experience is not mandatory has a part-time job, noted in their application at recruitment. At induction they say they are not seeking work experience. Under the Work Experience Policy, what applies?
options: They need not complete a WEIF, as the form is required only on programmes where work experience is a mandatory requirement
They need not complete a WEIF, as their work status is already noted in their application documentation
They must still complete a WEIF identifying their current work experience status and whether they are seeking it
They complete a WEIF only if they later decide to seek a placement, by asking the Work based Learning Team
questions.explanation: At induction the College requires students to complete a WEIF identifying their current work experience status and whether they are seeking work experience; the policy gives no exemption for non-mandatory programmes or for work status already noted at recruitment.
questions.source_excerpt: At the recruitment stage, students are asked about their current work status and this is noted in their application documentation; ... The College discusses the importance and scope of work experience at induction and requires students to complete a Work Experience Information Form (WEIF) identifying their current work experience status and if they are seeking work experience;

questions.question: A student arrives 20 minutes after the start of your lecture. Under the Attendance Policy, how should their attendance be recorded on the register?
options: Present (mark 'P'), as students up to 30 minutes late count as present
Late (mark 'L'), as they arrived between 15 and 30 minutes late
Absent (mark 'A'), as any arrival after the start counts as absence
Authorised Absence (mark 'E'), provided they give you a reason
questions.explanation: The Attendance Policy marks students present only if they are up to 15 minutes late; those arriving between 15 and 30 minutes late are marked Late ('L').
questions.source_excerpt: Students will be marked as present if they are up to 15 minutes late. Students who arrive between 15 and 30 minutes late will be marked as Late (Recorded on register as mark `L').

questions.question: According to the Attendance Policy, when can tutors alter an attendance entry they have recorded on the LCC Online Student Management System?
options: Only on the same day that the class takes place
Only within 48 hours of the class taking place
Only until the end of that teaching week
At any time until the end of the academic term
questions.explanation: To protect the integrity of the attendance record, the policy limits alteration access for all tutors to the same day the class takes place.
questions.source_excerpt: To maintain the integrity of the attendance record, alteration access of any attendance entry is limited to the same day the class takes place, for all tutors.

questions.question: A student disputes an attendance mark you recorded for them last week and asks you to correct it. Under the Attendance Policy, who must you inform?
options: The student's Personal Tutor and the Programme Leader
The Registrar or nominated deputy in Academic Administration
Relevant colleagues in the Monitoring & IT Departments
The Course Coordinator or nominee for that register
questions.explanation: The Attendance Policy requires tutors to inform relevant colleagues in the Monitoring & IT Departments about attendance record disputes or any required rectification.
questions.source_excerpt: In case of attendance record disputes or any required rectification, tutors are required to inform relevant colleagues in the Monitoring & IT Departments.

questions.question: According to the Attendance Policy, what is the impact on student funding when a student is recorded with the register mark 'A' (Absent)?
options: Funding continues and is reviewed at term end
The student course fee loan is released
The student's funding will be withheld
There is no impact if it is entered on time
questions.explanation: The policy's table of register marks states that for 'A' (Absent), student funding will be withheld, which is why timely and accurate attendance marking matters.
questions.source_excerpt: Timely input and updating of attendance marks is critical in ensuring that students receive payment of funds on the expected date. ... A = Absent - Student funding will be withheld;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, what may happen if a student is identified attempting proxy attendance on behalf of a fellow student?
options: The absent student's proxy mark is changed to 'A', with no disciplinary action taken
The student who signed in may face disciplinary action, but the absent student is not penalised
Both students may be issued a First Warning Letter and invited to an Intervention Meeting
Both students may face disciplinary action, including suspension or termination
questions.explanation: The College does not tolerate proxy attendance; if a proxy attempt is identified, both students may face disciplinary action, which may include suspension or termination.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will not tolerate proxy attendance on behalf of fellow students. If any proxy attempt is identified, both students may be subjected to disciplinary action, which may include suspension or termination from the College;

questions.question: A student who is a carer tells you they will regularly need to leave your class early. What should you advise them to do under the Attendance Policy?
options: Raise it with their Personal Tutor, as it may be approved as a reasonable adjustment
Submit a medical certificate via the student portal to cover each early departure
Apply to the College Assessment Board for a formal exemption from attendance requirements
Accept that each early departure is recorded as an absence and counts towards warning letters
questions.explanation: The policy allows leaving early to be approved as a reasonable adjustment case by case, including for carers, and students requiring an adjustment should raise it with their Personal Tutor.
questions.source_excerpt: Some students, due to their disability or wider personal circumstances, may have lateness and/or leaving early approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis; this includes students who are carers. If students require an adjustment, they should raise the matter with their Personal Tutor (PT).

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, an authorised absence (mark 'E') agreed between a student and a member of curriculum staff is usually no longer than how long in any given instance?
options: One teaching day (or the equivalent)
One teaching week (or the equivalent)
Two teaching weeks (or the equivalent)
Three teaching weeks (or the equivalent)
questions.explanation: The policy defines authorised absence as a short-term absence agreed with curriculum staff that is usually no more than one teaching week (or the equivalent) in any given instance.
questions.source_excerpt: Authorised absence is a short-term absence agreed between the student and a member of curriculum staff on the following basis ... c) is usually no more than one teaching week (or the equivalent) in any given instance;

questions.question: According to the Attendance Policy, at what point does a student's absence become a long-term absence?
options: When it exceeds one teaching week
When it exceeds two consecutive teaching weeks
When it exceeds four consecutive teaching weeks
When it exceeds half of the academic term
questions.explanation: The policy states that an absence exceeding two consecutive teaching weeks becomes a long-term absence, and this applies to all forms of long-term absence, including medical.
questions.source_excerpt: If an absence exceeds two consecutive teaching weeks, it will become a long-term absence. This section applies to ALL forms of long-term absence, including long-term medical absence;

questions.question: A continuing student who attended earlier in the term has now been absent for three consecutive teaching weeks. Under the Attendance Policy, what will the College do, where appropriate?
options: Refer the student directly to the College Assessment Board, which will decide on their withdrawal
Issue a Notification of Non-Registration Letter confirming that the student's enrolment is cancelled
Issue a Final Warning Letter and invite them to an Intervention Meeting with the Registrar or deputy
Change the missed register marks to 'E' and agree a return date with the student by email, with no meeting
questions.explanation: For an absence of three consecutive teaching weeks or more, the policy says the College will, where appropriate, issue a Final Warning Letter and invite the student to an Intervention Meeting with the Registrar or nominated deputy.
questions.source_excerpt: If an absence is three consecutive teaching weeks or more, where appropriate, the College will issue the student a Final Warning Letter and the student will be invited for an Intervention Meeting with the Registrar or nominated deputy.

questions.question: According to the Attendance Policy, when is a First Warning Letter issued to a student?
options: At the end of term, to students whose attendance falls below 60%
At the midpoint, to students whose attendance falls below 80%
After a student misses three consecutive timetabled classes
At the midpoint, to students whose attendance falls below 60%
questions.explanation: The Attendance Policy states that the First Warning Letter is issued at the midpoint to students whose attendance falls below 60%.
questions.source_excerpt: The First Warning Letter will be issued at the midpoint to those students whose attendance falls below 60%.

questions.question: A student received a Final Warning Letter but failed to meet a member of the attendance management team or any other authorised person. Under the Attendance Policy, what is the next step?
options: A Notification of Suspension Letter is issued
A Withdrawal Letter is issued straight away
A second Final Warning Letter is issued
A Notification of Non-Registration Letter is issued
questions.explanation: The policy states that a Notification of Suspension Letter is issued to any student who received the final warning letter and failed to meet the attendance management team or another authorised person.
questions.source_excerpt: Notification of Suspension Letter is to be issued to any student who has received the final warning letter and failed to meet one of the members of the attendance management team or any other authorised person.

questions.question: A student submits a medical certificate for a medical absence, but the dates on it have been amended by hand. Under the Attendance Policy, what applies?
options: It can be accepted if the student initials the handwritten amendment
It can be accepted if their Personal Tutor countersigns the amendment
It can be accepted for short-term absences of up to two teaching weeks
It cannot be accepted, as handwritten amendments are not accepted
questions.explanation: The Attendance Policy states that handwritten amendments or annotations on documentation cannot be accepted, and the student is responsible for submitting certificates covering the absence.
questions.source_excerpt: The student is responsible for ensuring medical certificates are submitted to cover the date range of the absence; ... Handwritten amendments or annotations on documentation cannot be accepted.

questions.question: The campus is closed because of severe weather and classes cannot take place. Under the Attendance Policy, how should this be recorded on the affected registers?
options: Centrally recorded as 'H' by the Course Coordinator or nominee
Each tutor marks all students as 'E' (Authorised Absence)
Students are marked 'A' until the closure is confirmed by email
Each tutor marks all students as 'O' (Present Online)
questions.explanation: The policy states that campus closure or significant disruption from events such as adverse weather is centrally recorded on all affected registers as 'H' by the Course Coordinator or nominee.
questions.source_excerpt: Campus or College closure or significant disruption resulting from an event such as adverse weather or industrial action shall be centrally recorded on all affected attendance registers as `H' by the Course Coordinator or nominee;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, when is a Notification of Non-Registration Letter issued to a new starter, warning that their registration/enrolment will be cancelled?
options: After they miss the first week of classes of an academic term
After they miss the first two weeks of classes of an academic term
After they miss the first four weeks of classes of an academic term
After they miss their first assessment deadline of an academic term
questions.explanation: The policy states the Notification of Non-Registration Letter is issued after a new starter has missed the first two weeks of classes/sessions of an academic term.
questions.source_excerpt: Notification of Non-Registration Letter will be issued after a student has missed the first two weeks of classes/sessions of an academic term. This letter will notify the students that registration/enrolment will be cancelled (applies to new starters);

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Attendance Policy as an example of an authorised absence?
options: Jury duty or community service
A medical or dental appointment for a dependent child
A holiday that is not a religious holiday
A court date or driving test that cannot be held outside class time
questions.explanation: The policy's examples of authorised absence include religious holidays 'but not other holidays', while jury duty, community service, dependants' medical appointments and court or driving test appointments are all listed.
questions.source_excerpt: c) Community Service; ... g) Jury duty; h) Medical or dental appointments for self, or a child or adult who is dependent on the student; i) Religious Holidays (but not other holidays); j) To attend an appointment where scope is limited for the student to this schedule outside timetabled classes (e.g., children's hearing, court, driving test

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, student punctuality is recorded on registers. Apart from attendance monitoring, what may the College use this punctuality information for?
options: Setting the dates of the student's fee instalments
Calculating the student's final classification
Allocating the student to seminar or tutorial groups
Providing references when the College is asked for one
questions.explanation: The Attendance Policy states that punctuality recorded on registers may be used when the College is asked to provide references.
questions.source_excerpt: Student punctuality will be recorded on registers and this information may be used when asked to provide references.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, by when are all tutors advised to complete the attendance record procedure for a class?
options: Within five working days of the class
Before the next class
By the end of that week
Within the lecture period
questions.explanation: The policy advises all tutors to complete the attendance record procedure within the lecture period.
questions.source_excerpt: All tutors are advised to complete the attendance record procedure within the lecture period.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, in which circumstances may a student be recorded on the register with the mark 'O' (Present Online)?
options: Only for classes that are delivered online
Whenever they join an on-campus class remotely
When they watch the lecture recording later
When remote study is a reasonable adjustment
questions.explanation: The policy states that the 'O' (Present Online) mark is only recorded for online classes.
questions.source_excerpt: Present Online (Recorded on Register as mark `O'). `O' is only recorded for online classes;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, the College may apply a penalty to a student who is persistently late. What is that penalty equivalent to?
options: 1 absence for every 4 late attendances recorded
1 absence for every 5 late attendances recorded
1 absence for every 8 late attendances recorded
1 absence for every 10 late attendances recorded
questions.explanation: The policy states that a persistently late student may be subject to a penalty equivalent to 1 absence for 8 late attendances recorded.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student is persistently late, the College may subject him/her to a penalty which is equivalent to 1 absence for 8 late attendances recorded;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, if an absent student cannot maintain regular contact with the College, who may keep the College advised on the progress of the absence?
options: Only an advocate appointed by the student in writing
A representative of the student, such as a family member
Only their GP or another registered medical practitioner
No one, as contact must come from the student personally
questions.explanation: The policy says that where the student cannot maintain contact, a representative such as a family member may keep the College advised on the progress of the absence.
questions.source_excerpt: The student, where possible, should engage with the College during periods of absence by maintaining regular contact with relevant staff. Where this is not possible, a representative (e.g., family member) may keep the College advised on the progress of the absence;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, a student who misses a timetabled class with no agreed alternative register mark is marked 'A'. How does the College regard this default mark?
options: As an authorised absence
As a provisional absence
As an unauthorised absence
As a pending medical absence
questions.explanation: The policy states that 'A' is the default mark for non-attendance and is considered by the College to be an unauthorised absence.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will be marked absent if they do not attend a timetabled class and there is no agreed appropriate alternative register mark. This shall be the default mark for non-attendance and considered by the College to be an unauthorised absence;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, how is a student's attendance rate treated from one academic term to the next?
options: It is combined across the whole academic year
It is combined across the whole programme
It is monitored separately and not carried forward
Any shortfall is carried forward to the next term
questions.explanation: The policy states that students are monitored each term separately, and the attendance rate is not carried forward to the next term.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will be monitored each term separately for their attendance, i.e. - attendance rate is not carried forward to the next term.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, who takes the decision to withdraw a student from their programme of study following the suspension stage?
options: The Programme Leader (or nominee)
The College Assessment Board
The attendance management team
The Head of Department
questions.explanation: The policy states that the withdrawal decision will be taken by the College Assessment Board.
questions.source_excerpt: A Withdrawal Letter is to be issued to any student who has received the suspension decision and failed to meet the conditions of return to study ... The withdrawal decision will be taken by the College Assessment Board.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, what details must a medical certificate for a short-term or long-term medical absence include?
options: The student's full name and address
The student's ID number and date of birth
The student's ID number and course code
The student's name and Personal Tutor's signature
questions.explanation: The policy requires appropriate medical certificates for short- and long-term medical absence, and they must include the student's full name and address.
questions.source_excerpt: Short-term and long-term medical absence shall require appropriate medical certificates and must include the student's full name and address;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, how often does the College's dedicated team communicate with students who are absent from their scheduled classes?
options: Weekly, at the end of each teaching week
Only after three consecutive missed classes
At the midpoint of term, by warning letter
Daily, to record the reasons for the absence
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College undertakes daily intervention, with a dedicated team communicating with absentees daily to record the reasons for absence.
questions.source_excerpt: The College undertakes daily intervention for those students who are absent from their scheduled classes. A dedicated team communicates with absentees daily to record the reason(s) for absence

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, how should the notification of an Intervention Meeting be sent to the student?
options: By both email and letter
By email only
By text message and email
By letter to the home address only
questions.explanation: The policy's important actions for intervention state that the notification of the meeting should be sent by both email and letter.
questions.source_excerpt: The notification of the meeting should be sent by both email and letter;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, what must take place if a student is likely to be absent on maternity, paternity or adoption leave for any longer than 3 weeks?
options: A referral to the Assessment Board
A formal suspension of studies
A student progress meeting
Automatic withdrawal from the course
questions.explanation: The policy states that if a student is likely to be absent for any longer than 3 weeks, a student progress meeting must take place.
questions.source_excerpt: While the College wishes to support those students' requiring maternity, paternity, or adoption leave ... If a student is likely to be absent for a period of any longer than 3 weeks, a student progress meeting must take place

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, what is required of students who attend repeat units?
options: They attend only the sessions linked to the failed assessment
They study the complete unit under the standard attendance procedure
They attend at least half of the unit's sessions under a reduced procedure
They follow a lighter attendance procedure agreed with the unit tutor
questions.explanation: The policy states that students attending repeat units must study the complete unit, and the standard attendance procedure must be followed.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who attend repeat units must study the complete unit. For repeat unit attendance, the standard attendance procedure must be followed.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, the College develops and maintains an Individual Assessment and Learning Plan (IALP) through discussion with the student and whom?
options: The Registrar or nominated deputy
The Student Funding department
The College Assessment Board
The student's 'Named Contact'
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College will develop, agree and maintain an IALP through discussion with the student and their 'Named Contact'.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will develop, agree, and maintain an Individual Assessment and Learning Plan (IALP) through discussion with the student and their `Named Contact'.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, how can students monitor their own attendance and achievement?
options: By using the student portal
By emailing Academic Administration
Through their Personal Tutor only
Through termly progress letters
questions.explanation: The policy states that students may monitor their attendance and achievement using the student portal.
questions.source_excerpt: Students may also monitor their attendance and achievement using the student portal;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, what is the impact on student funding of the register mark 'E' (Authorised Absence)?
options: Funding is withheld until the absence has been reviewed
No impact, if entered legitimately at the time of recording
Funding is reduced for each 'E' mark recorded in the term
No impact, if approved by the Registrar within one week
questions.explanation: The policy's table of register marks states that 'E' has no impact on funding if the mark is entered legitimately at the time of recording.
questions.source_excerpt: E = Authorised Absence - No impact if the mark is entered legitimately at the time of recording;

questions.question: The Attendance Policy's Equality Impact Assessment notes that students may self-certify certain absences. Which of the following is one of them?
options: Holidays that are not religious
Long-term medical absences
Antenatal appointments
Shifts at part-time work
questions.explanation: The EIA gives examples of absences students may self-certify: religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments and caring responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, students may self-certify religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, how often does the College monitor student retention and achievement rates with reference to protected characteristics?
options: Twice per academic year, at mid-year and year end
Monthly, alongside the daily intervention reports
Four times per academic year, once each quarter
Three times per academic year, on a termly basis
questions.explanation: The policy states that student retention and achievement rates are monitored three times per academic year (termly) with reference to protected characteristics.
questions.source_excerpt: We also monitor student retention and achievement rates three times per academic year (on a termly basis) with reference to protected characteristics

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, what should the Academic Department do for a student whose attendance has been affected by their disability?
options: Make reasonable adjustments to accommodate an attendance excuse
Exempt the student from all termly attendance monitoring
Record the missed sessions as 'H' on the attendance register
Refer the student to the Assessment Board for an exemption
questions.explanation: The policy's EIA states that the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments to accommodate an attendance excuse for students whose attendance has been affected by disability.
questions.source_excerpt: Similarly, the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments to accommodate attendance excuse for students whose attendance have been affected by his or her disability.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, a student's lateness has been approved as a reasonable adjustment because of their disability, and the arrangement is expected to be more than short-term. What should happen?
options: Their late arrivals are recorded as 'E' and reviewed by the Registrar each term
They upload a medical certificate to the student portal at the start of each term
An IALP is devised and regularly reviewed as part of a learning agreement
The 1 absence per 8 lates penalty is applied only at the end of each academic term
questions.explanation: Lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment case by case, and where the arrangement is more than short-term an Individual Assessment and Learning Plan (IALP) is devised and regularly reviewed as part of a learning agreement.
questions.source_excerpt: Some students, due to their disability or wider personal circumstances, may have lateness and/or leaving early approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis; ... An Individual Assessment and Learning Plan (IALP) will be devised and regularly ... reviewed as part of a learning agreement, should the arrangement be more than short-term.

questions.question: A student arrives 40 minutes after your lecture has started. Under the Attendance Policy, what may you do?
options: Admit them and record them as Late ('L'), like any other late arrival
Refuse them admission at your discretion and record their attendance as absent
Admit them and record them as Present ('P'), provided they stay until the end
Refuse them admission and record the session as 'E' until they give a reason
questions.explanation: The 'L' mark covers arrivals between 15 and 30 minutes late; students over 30 minutes late may be refused admission at the tutor's discretion and recorded as absent.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who arrive between 15 and 30 minutes late will be marked as Late (Recorded on register as mark `L'). Students who are over 30 minutes late may be refused admission to that session at the tutors' discretion and their attendance will be recorded as absent;

questions.question: A student who received a First Warning Letter responds, but gives no documentary evidence to explain their absences. Under the Attendance Policy, what should they receive next?
options: A Notification of Suspension Letter, following the Suspension of Studies Policy
A second First Warning Letter, asking for the evidence within 5 working days
A Withdrawal Letter, as the College Assessment Board will decide on withdrawal
A Final Warning Letter, inviting them to a meeting within 10 working days
questions.explanation: A Final Warning Letter goes to students who received the first warning letter but failed to give an adequate explanation with documentary evidence; it may invite them to meet the attendance management team within 10 working days.
questions.source_excerpt: Final Warning Letter will be sent to students who have already received the first warning letter and have failed to provide adequate explanation/information with documentary evidence. ... b) Invite the student to meet with one of the members of the attendance ... management team or any other authorised person within 10 working days

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, a continuing student's attendance stays poor and they do not engage at any stage. In what order are the letters issued to them?
options: First Warning, Final Warning, Notification of Suspension, then Withdrawal
First Warning, Notification of Suspension, Final Warning, then Withdrawal
Non-Registration, First Warning, Final Warning, then Withdrawal
First Warning, Final Warning, Withdrawal, then Notification of Suspension
questions.explanation: The letters escalate from the First Warning Letter to the Final Warning Letter, then the Notification of Suspension Letter, and finally the Withdrawal Letter; the Non-Registration Letter applies only to new starters.
questions.source_excerpt: The First Warning Letter will be issued at the midpoint ... Final Warning Letter will be sent to students who have already received the first warning letter ... Notification of Suspension Letter is to be issued to any student who has received the final warning letter ... A Withdrawal Letter is to be issued to any student who has received the suspension decision

questions.question: A student asks a member of curriculum staff to agree an authorised absence for a house removal. Under the Attendance Policy, which of these is one of the bases on which it may be agreed?
options: The Registrar has approved the request in writing beforehand
The student's Named Contact confirms the move in writing
The absence will not adversely affect the student's progress
A supporting document is uploaded to the student portal first
questions.explanation: House removal is listed as an example of authorised absence, which is agreed between the student and curriculum staff on the basis that the request is reasonable, will not adversely affect progress, is short and is not excessively frequent.
questions.source_excerpt: Authorised absence is a short-term absence agreed between the student ... and a member of curriculum staff on the following basis : ... a) a reasonable request; b) will not adversely affect progress; ... e) House removal;

questions.question: A student uploads a medical certificate to the student portal covering four days of illness. Under the Attendance Policy, what should then happen?
options: The tutor updates the covered dates to 'E' on the day the certificate arrives
The College processes it within five working days and updates the dates to 'E'
The Registrar reviews it at term end and records the covered dates as 'H'
The College processes it within ten working days and updates the dates to 'M'
questions.explanation: Processing of a medical certificate is completed by the College within ten working days of submission, and the covered dates are updated to 'M' on the register.
questions.source_excerpt: Each instance must be covered by a medical certificate and uploaded to the student portal as evidence to request for an attendance excuse; 4.8.4. Processing shall be completed by the College within ten working days from the date of submission. The attendance mark for the covered dates will be updated to show the value `M' on the attendance register(s);

questions.question: A student's medical certificates cover an absence of two and a half consecutive teaching weeks. Under the Attendance Policy, how is this absence treated?
options: As a short-term medical absence, as each instance has a certificate
As a long-term medical absence, managed with regular dialogue
As an authorised absence ('E') agreed with a member of curriculum staff
As an unauthorised absence ('A') until the Registrar reviews it
questions.explanation: A short-term medical absence is no more than two consecutive teaching weeks; anything longer is a long-term medical absence, which becomes a managed absence requiring regular dialogue.
questions.source_excerpt: A medical absence greater than two consecutive teaching weeks will be considered as a long-term medical absence. This will become a managed absence with the requirement for regular dialogue

questions.question: During a student's long-term absence, which of these responsibilities does the Attendance Policy give to the College rather than to the student or their representative?
options: Arranging for a family member to act as the student's representative
Completing and submitting the agreed work on time
Continuously reviewing the absence and setting work where appropriate
Ensuring medical certificates cover the full date range of the absence
questions.explanation: The College must continuously review the absence, set work where appropriate and maintain communication; engaging, keeping the College informed, submitting agreed work and covering the absence with certificates fall to the student.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the responsibility of the student (or representative) to engage with the College and to keep the College informed of the progress of the absence and, as appropriate, to complete and submit the agreed work on time; ... It is the responsibility of the College to continuously review the absence, set work where appropriate and maintain effective communication throughout the absence;

questions.question: A student returns to College after an absence of two consecutive teaching weeks. Under the Attendance Policy, what should happen?
options: An attainment action plan is agreed, setting out how and when outstanding work is done
A Final Warning Letter is issued and an Intervention Meeting is arranged
A Notification of Suspension Letter is issued pending an Assessment Board decision
The missed classes are re-marked as 'E' retrospectively, with no further action
questions.explanation: For an absence of less than three consecutive teaching weeks where the student has returned, an attainment action plan is developed and agreed; the Final Warning Letter and Intervention Meeting apply at three weeks or more.
questions.source_excerpt: If an absence is less than three consecutive teaching weeks and the student has returned to College, an attainment action plan will be developed and agreed, noting how and when any outstanding work (including assessments) will be achieved and review dates agreed;

questions.question: At an Intervention Meeting held under the Attendance Policy, the student does not agree with the proposed attainment action plan. What happens next?
options: The Registrar issues a Withdrawal Letter within ten working days
The student is issued a Notification of Suspension Letter at once
A second Intervention Meeting is held, this time with the Programme Leader
The Assessment Board makes the final decision on attainment and progression
questions.explanation: Option 2 of the Intervention Meeting outcomes applies: if the student does not agree with the attainment action plan, the Assessment Board makes a final decision on attainment and progression.
questions.source_excerpt: The outcomes of the Intervention Meeting will be either Option 1 or Option 2: ... b) Option 2: If a student does not agree with the attainment action plan, the Assessment Board will make a final decision on attainment and progression.

questions.question: A student last attended class on 3 March, then had a certificated medical absence until 17 March, and has not engaged since. If they are withdrawn, what effective date should the withdrawal letter state under the Attendance Policy?
options: 3 March, the last day on which they physically attended class
The date of the Intervention Meeting at which withdrawal was agreed
17 March, the last day of their certificated medical absence
The date on which the Registrar signs the withdrawal letter
questions.explanation: The effective date of withdrawal is the last date of attendance, and this includes certificated medical absence, so it runs to the end of the certificated period.
questions.source_excerpt: The letter shall include the effective date of withdrawal, which shall be the last date of attendance (including certificated medical absence)

questions.question: A student tells you they will miss two days of classes during term time to observe a religious festival. Under the Attendance Policy, how should the College record this absence?
options: As an Authorised Absence (mark 'E')
As a College closure event (mark 'H')
As an unauthorised absence (mark 'A')
As a self-certified medical absence (mark 'M')
questions.explanation: Although funding cannot be paid for term-time holidays, religious holidays are an exception and should be recorded by the College as an Authorised Absence ('E').
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Loans Company (SLC) Guidance stipulates that the Student Funding department cannot make payments to students for holidays during term time. The exceptions are as follows: a) Religious holidays should be recorded by the College as an Authorised Absence.

questions.question: A student receiving help from College support services is not progressing satisfactorily, and a meeting with the curriculum team is arranged. Under the Attendance Policy, whom should the Programme Leader (or nominee) ask to attend?
options: The Registrar or a nominated deputy
A representative from the support service
The student's 'Named Contact' from their IALP
A member of the attendance management team
questions.explanation: Where a student who is not progressing is supported by College support services, the Programme Leader (or nominee) should ask a representative from that service to attend the meeting with the curriculum team.
questions.source_excerpt: A meeting should take place between the student and the curriculum team to establish reasons for this. If the student is being supported by the College support services, the Programme Leader (or nominee) should ask a representative from the service to attend the meeting.

questions.question: A student attends your class but leaves before the end time. Under the Attendance Policy, which register mark applies and what is its impact on student funding?
options: 'A' (Absent), with the student's funding withheld
'L' (Present but Arrived Late), with funding reduced
'E' (Authorised Absence), with no impact if entered on time
'LE' (Present but Left Early), with no impact on funding
questions.explanation: The register mark 'LE' records that the student was present but left before the end time, and it has no impact on funding.
questions.source_excerpt: LE = Present but Left Early - used to record that the student left before the end time, No impact;

questions.question: The Attendance Policy's Equality Impact Assessment concludes that the policy is not likely to have a negative impact on people who share protected characteristics. What reason does it give?
options: It lowers the warning letter thresholds for students with protected characteristics
It anticipates that personal circumstances may affect attendance and makes allowances
It exempts students with protected characteristics from termly attendance monitoring
It anonymises attendance data before any warning letter is sent to a student
questions.explanation: The EIA reasons that the policy anticipates personal circumstances may affect attendance and makes reasonable allowances, such as self-certifying religious holidays, medical appointments and caring responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not likely that this EIA will have a negative impact on people who share protected characteristics. The reason for this is that the EIA anticipates that personal circumstances may affect attendance and makes reasonable allowances for this.

questions.question: Two students persistently leave your class early: one is a carer whose early leaving is approved as a reasonable adjustment, the other has no legitimate reason. Under the Attendance Policy, which statement is correct?
options: Both are dealt with under the policy's processes, as adjustments cannot cover leaving early
Neither is dealt with, as the 'LE' mark has no impact on student funding
Only the student with no legitimate reason is dealt with under the policy's processes
Both must upload medical certificates to the student portal to excuse each early departure
questions.explanation: Persistent leaving early for no legitimate reason is dealt with under the College's processes, whereas leaving early may be approved as a reasonable adjustment case by case, including for carers.
questions.source_excerpt: Persistent late-coming and/or leaving early, for no legitimate reason, will be dealt with under the College's processes defined in this policy; ... may have lateness and/or leaving early approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis; this includes students who are carers.

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, a student has been recorded as Late ('L') 16 times this term. Which statement correctly describes the position?
options: The College may apply a penalty equal to 4 absences, and funding is withheld for each 'L' mark
No penalty is possible, as an 'L' mark records the student as present with no impact
The College may apply a penalty equal to 2 absences; the 'L' marks themselves have no funding impact
Each 'L' mark must be changed to 'A', so the student's funding is withheld for all 16 sessions
questions.explanation: A persistently late student may be given a penalty equivalent to 1 absence for every 8 late attendances (16 lates equal 2 absences), while the 'L' mark itself has no impact on funding.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student is persistently late, the College may subject him/her to a penalty which is equivalent to 1 absence for 8 late attendances recorded; ... L = Present but Arrived Late - used to record that the student arrived after the start time, No impact;

questions.question: A new first-year student and a returning second-year student each miss the first two weeks of classes of an academic term. Under the Attendance Policy, who is issued a Notification of Non-Registration Letter?
options: Only the new first-year student, as it applies to new starters
Only the returning student, as they are already enrolled on the programme
Both students, as each has missed the first two weeks of classes
Neither student, until three consecutive teaching weeks have been missed
questions.explanation: The Notification of Non-Registration Letter is issued after the first two weeks of classes are missed and applies to new starters, warning that their registration/enrolment will be cancelled.
questions.source_excerpt: Notification of Non-Registration Letter will be issued after a student has missed the first two weeks of classes/sessions of an academic term. This letter will notify the students that registration/enrolment will be cancelled (applies to new starters);

questions.question: A student's attendance was 45% in the first term. At the midpoint of the second term, their attendance for that term is 70%. Under the Attendance Policy, is a First Warning Letter issued at this midpoint?
options: Yes, as the first-term shortfall is carried forward into the second term
Yes, as their combined attendance across both terms is below 60%
No, but a Final Warning Letter is sent, as the first term was below 60%
No, as each term is monitored separately and this term's rate is above 60%
questions.explanation: Attendance is monitored each term separately and the rate is not carried forward, and the First Warning Letter goes only to students below 60% at the midpoint.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will be monitored each term separately for their attendance, i.e. - attendance rate is not carried forward to the next term. ... The First Warning Letter will be issued at the midpoint to those students whose attendance falls below 60%.

questions.question: A student ignored a Final Warning Letter, never met the attendance management team, and has not responded to the Notification of Suspension Letter issued to them. Under the Attendance Policy, which guidelines govern the next step?
options: Those in the Withdrawal of Studies Policy
Those in the Suspension of Studies Policy
Those in the Student Loans Company attendance guidance
Those in the Assessment Board's progression rules
questions.explanation: If no response is received after the Notification of Suspension Letter, the subsequent action follows the Suspension of Studies Policy; the Withdrawal of Studies Policy applies only after a suspension decision and a failure to meet return conditions.
questions.source_excerpt: Notification of Suspension Letter is to be issued to any student who has received the final warning letter and failed to meet one of the members of the attendance management team or any other authorised person. If no response is received from the student, the subsequent action should follow the guidelines set in the Suspension of Studies Policy

questions.question: A suspended student fails to meet the conditions of return to study and is to be withdrawn. Under the Attendance Policy, which statement about the withdrawal decision and letter is correct?
options: The Registrar decides; the Programme Leader emails the signed letter to the student within 10 working days
The attendance management team decides; the Registrar sends the letter to the home address within 5 working days
The College Assessment Board decides; the Registrar signs the letter, sent to the home address within 10 working days
The Registrar decides; the Assessment Board chair signs the letter, sent to the home address within 20 working days
questions.explanation: The withdrawal decision is taken by the College Assessment Board, and the withdrawal letter should be signed by the Registrar and sent to the student's home address within 10 working days.
questions.source_excerpt: A Withdrawal Letter is to be issued to any student who has received the suspension decision and failed to meet the conditions of return to study ... The withdrawal decision will be taken by the College Assessment Board. ... The letter, in the case of withdrawal, should be signed by the Registrar and ... sent to the student's home address within 10 working days.

questions.question: A student asks a member of curriculum staff for an authorised absence for a one-day appointment, their fourth such request in five weeks. Under the Attendance Policy, on which basis could the request be declined?
options: Each request goes beyond the limit of one teaching day in any given instance
Authorised absences are capped at three per term unless the Registrar approves
An authorised absence needs a supporting document uploaded to the student portal
The College deems the frequency of the student's requests to be excessive
questions.explanation: Authorised absence is agreed on the basis that the request is reasonable, will not adversely affect progress, is usually no more than one teaching week and is not requested so often that the College deems it excessive.
questions.source_excerpt: Authorised absence is a short-term absence agreed between the student ... and a member of curriculum staff on the following basis : ... d) the frequency of such requests by the student is not deemed by the College to be excessive.

questions.question: A student is summoned for jury duty lasting three consecutive teaching weeks. Under the Attendance Policy, how is this absence handled?
options: As a long-term absence, managed under the section covering all forms of long-term absence
As an authorised absence ('E') only, as jury duty is a listed example needing no management
As an exceptional event ('H'), as it arises from a legal duty outside the student's control
As a medical absence ('M'), once the student uploads the jury summons to the student portal
questions.explanation: Authorised absence is usually no more than one teaching week; any absence exceeding two consecutive teaching weeks becomes a long-term absence, and that section applies to all forms of long-term absence.
questions.source_excerpt: c) is usually no more than one teaching week (or the equivalent) in any given instance; ... g) Jury duty; ... If an absence exceeds two consecutive teaching weeks, it will become a long-term absence. This section applies to ALL forms of long-term absence

questions.question: A student is ill for eight teaching days, but the medical certificate they upload to the student portal covers only five of them. Under the Attendance Policy, what happens to the register?
options: All eight days are updated to 'M', as the certificate shows one continuous illness
Only the five covered dates become 'M'; the student is responsible for covering the rest
All eight days remain 'A' until the College Assessment Board has reviewed the certificate
The five covered dates become 'M' and the other three are changed to 'E' automatically
questions.explanation: Only the covered dates are updated to 'M' after processing, and the student is responsible for ensuring certificates cover the full date range of the absence.
questions.source_excerpt: The attendance mark for the covered dates will be updated to show the value `M' on the attendance register(s); ... The student is responsible for ensuring medical certificates are submitted to cover the date range of the absence;

questions.question: A student on a long-term absence is studying a unit built on practical skill acquisition and group projects. What does the Attendance Policy say about supporting them through the VLE?
options: VLE support fully replaces the practical sessions, so no effect on progress needs to be considered
Support is likely to be less effective where learning is experiential or group work is significant
VLE support is offered only once the Assessment Board has approved a long-term absence plan
The student must be withdrawn, as practical learning cannot be supported during absence
questions.explanation: The College supports absent students via the VLE and other means, but the policy notes these measures are likely to be less effective where learning is experiential (skill acquisition) or group work is significant.
questions.source_excerpt: The College shall keep the student advised of the work currently being undertaken, facilitate support via the College's Virtual Learning Environment (VLE), as well as any other appropriate means. ... These supportive measures are likely to be less effective when the learning is experiential (i.e., skill acquisition) or where group work plays a significant contributory factor;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, as a student's long-term absence continues, when is it most likely that withdrawal from the course will need to be considered?
options: When the student's progress cannot be sustained or is not being sustained
Once the absence reaches six consecutive teaching weeks, whatever the progress
As soon as the student misses any assessment during the period of absence
When the student's representative stops keeping the College informed
questions.explanation: The policy sets no fixed time limit: the College hopes to support students through absence, but withdrawal is most likely to be considered when progress cannot be sustained or is not being sustained.
questions.source_excerpt: The College would hope to support students through their absence, however, as time progresses, it may become necessary to consider withdrawal from the course. This is most likely to occur when progress cannot be sustained or is not being sustained.

questions.question: A student is absent for two and a half consecutive teaching weeks because of caring responsibilities, then returns to College. Under the Attendance Policy, which statement is correct?
options: It remained a short-term absence, so no action plan is needed now they have returned
It became a long-term absence, so a Final Warning Letter and Intervention Meeting follow
It is recorded as 'H', as caring responsibilities are outside the student's control
It became a long-term absence, and on return an attainment action plan is agreed
questions.explanation: An absence exceeding two consecutive teaching weeks becomes long-term, but where it is under three weeks and the student has returned, an attainment action plan is agreed; the Final Warning Letter and Intervention Meeting apply at three weeks or more.
questions.source_excerpt: If an absence exceeds two consecutive teaching weeks, it will become a long-term absence. ... If an absence is less than three consecutive teaching weeks and the student has returned to College, an attainment action plan will be developed and agreed

questions.question: You are drafting the invitation to an Intervention Meeting for a student absent for four consecutive teaching weeks. Under the Attendance Policy, what must the correspondence make clear?
options: The effective date of withdrawal that applies if the student does not attend the meeting
That the meeting is with the Assessment Board, which will decide on progression
The reason for the meeting and that the student may be accompanied, e.g. by an advocate
That the student must bring medical certificates covering every missed teaching day
questions.explanation: The correspondence should clearly reflect the reason for the meeting and make clear the opportunity to be accompanied; the student is advised that an advocate can accompany them.
questions.source_excerpt: The student will be advised that an advocate can accompany him/her to the meeting. ... The correspondence should clearly reflect the reason for the meeting; ... The opportunity to be accompanied should be made clear;

questions.question: At an Intervention Meeting held under the Attendance Policy, the student agrees the proposed attainment action plan. Which statement describes what follows?
options: Review dates and a return date are agreed, and the outcomes are confirmed by letter
The Assessment Board makes the final decision, and the outcomes are confirmed by email only
Review dates are agreed, and the outcomes are recorded only in the notes of the discussion
A Notification of Suspension Letter is issued until the outstanding work has been completed
questions.explanation: Under Option 1 the attainment action plan is agreed with review dates and a return date, and after the meeting the outcomes should be confirmed by letter.
questions.source_excerpt: Option 1: An attainment action plan is agreed, noting how and when any outstanding work (including assessments) will be achieved, review dates are agreed and the student returns to the College on an agreed date; ... After the meeting, the outcomes should be confirmed by letter;

questions.question: A student tells you she expects the College to give her the same maternity leave conditions as staff, including pay. Under the Attendance Policy, which response is correct?
options: Maternity leave is recorded as 'H', so her student funding continues with no impact
Staff conditions cannot be offered, and there is no statutory entitlement to maternity pay
She receives staff conditions for up to 3 weeks, and then a student progress meeting decides
She may self-certify the leave as antenatal appointments, recorded as 'E' with no impact
questions.explanation: The College cannot offer students the same maternity, paternity or adoption conditions as its staff, and there is no statutory entitlement for students to receive payment for maternity leave.
questions.source_excerpt: While the College wishes to support those students' requiring maternity, ... paternity, or adoption leave, it cannot offer the same conditions as it offers to its staff. There is no statutory entitlement for students to receive payment for maternity leave

questions.question: A student attends every class but is clearly not making every effort to achieve progression in their studies. Under the Attendance Policy, how should this be handled?
options: No action is needed, as the processes are triggered only by attendance below 60%
Through the Students' Behaviour process, as for unacceptable levels of attendance
By referral straight to the Assessment Board for a final decision on progression
Under the College's processes in this policy, which include attending but not progressing
questions.explanation: Where a student is not making every effort to progress, the matter is dealt with under the College's processes in the Attendance Policy, and this expressly includes attending but not progressing.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the student is not making every effort to achieve progression in studies, the matter should be dealt with under the College's processes defined in this policy. This includes attending but not progressing in studies;

questions.question: A student has missed many classes but has obtained lecture notes from College staff and handed in all their assignments. Under the Attendance Policy, how should the academic team treat this?
options: As irrelevant, since engagement is judged only on the register marks
As grounds to re-mark the missed sessions as authorised absence ('E')
As matters to consider when judging whether they are still participating
As usable only once a medical certificate covering the absence is provided
questions.explanation: Academic teams should consider whether students have kept up to date by obtaining lecture notes or materials from staff and handed in assignments, as signs they are continuing to participate in their studies.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic Teams should consider whether students have: ... a) Kept up to date with learning by obtaining lecture notes, online resources or other learning materials from the College staff; ... c) Handed in assignments or classwork;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy's register marks, which mark has no impact on student funding only on condition that it is entered legitimately at the time of recording?
options: 'LE' (Present but Left Early)
'H' (Exceptional Event or class cancelled)
'L' (Present but Arrived Late)
'M' (Absence for Medical reasons)
questions.explanation: 'M' has no impact only if the mark is entered legitimately at the time of recording, whereas 'L', 'LE' and 'H' are listed as having no impact without that condition.
questions.source_excerpt: L = Present but Arrived Late - used to record that the student arrived after the start time, No impact; ... M = Absence for Medical reasons - No impact if the mark is entered legitimately at the time of recording;

questions.question: A class is cancelled at short notice for an unforeseen circumstance. Under the Attendance Policy, which register mark applies and what is its impact on student funding?
options: 'H' for every student, with no impact on their student funding
'E' for every student, with no impact if entered on time
'A' for every student, with funding withheld until rescheduled
'O' for every student, so the course fee loan is released
questions.explanation: The 'H' mark covers exceptional events and classes cancelled for unforeseen circumstances, and it has no impact on student funding.
questions.source_excerpt: H = Exceptional Event that closes a campus or limits normal College activity (e.g., adverse weather, industrial action) or class cancelled for unforeseen circumstance; No impact.

questions.question: The Attendance Policy's Equality Impact Assessment lists absences that students may self-certify. For people with which protected characteristics does it say this should reduce the potential for negative impact?
options: Age, race, and marriage and civil partnership
Religion or belief, disability, and pregnancy and maternity
Gender reassignment, sexual orientation, and age
Race, marriage and civil partnership, and sexual orientation
questions.explanation: Self-certifying religious holidays, medical and antenatal appointments and caring responsibilities should reduce negative impact arising from religion or belief, disability, and pregnancy and maternity.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, students may self-certify religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities. This should reduce the potential for negative impact on people as a result of their religion or belief, disability, and/or pregnancy and maternity;

questions.question: Under the Attendance Policy, which of these communications to a student may be sent by text message alone, without a letter or an email?
options: The notification inviting the student to an Intervention Meeting
A warning notification about the student's attendance for the term
Confirmation of the outcomes agreed at an Intervention Meeting
Notice of their withdrawal, stating the effective date of withdrawal
questions.explanation: Attendance warning notifications may be sent by letter, email or text message or a combination, whereas an Intervention Meeting notice must go by both email and letter, its outcomes must be confirmed by letter, and a withdrawal letter goes to the home address.
questions.source_excerpt: The warning notifications could be sent in the form of a letter, email or text message or a combination; ... The notification of the meeting should be sent by both email and letter; ... After the meeting, the outcomes should be confirmed by letter; ... The letter, in the case of withdrawal, should be signed by the Registrar and sent to the student's home address within 10 working days.

questions.question: A student joins your online class 10 minutes after it starts. Under the Attendance Policy, which register mark should you record for them?
options: 'O' (Present Online), as up to 15 minutes late still counts as present
'L' (Late), as any late arrival to an online class is recorded as Late
'P' (Present On campus), as 'O' is used only for those who join on time
'A' (Absent), unless you choose to admit them at your own discretion
questions.explanation: Students up to 15 minutes late are marked as present, and in an online class the present mark is 'O'; 'L' applies only to arrivals between 15 and 30 minutes late, and tutor discretion to refuse admission applies only after 30 minutes.
questions.source_excerpt: Present Online (Recorded on Register as mark `O'). `O' is only recorded for online classes; ... Students will be marked as present if they are up to 15 minutes late. Students who arrive between 15 and 30 minutes late will be marked as Late (Recorded on register as mark `L').

questions.question: A student plans a one-week family holiday abroad during term time; it is not a religious holiday. Under the Attendance Policy, which statement is correct?
options: It may be agreed as an authorised absence ('E'), as it lasts only one teaching week
Student Funding cannot pay for term-time holidays, and it is not a listed exception
It is recorded centrally as 'H' by the Course Coordinator, with no funding impact
The student may self-certify the holiday under the EIA, so their funding is unaffected
questions.explanation: SLC guidance means Student Funding cannot pay for term-time holidays; religious holidays are an exception recorded as authorised absence, but other holidays are not, and 'H' is only for closures or disruption.
questions.source_excerpt: i) Religious Holidays (but not other holidays); ... The Student Loans Company (SLC) Guidance stipulates that the Student Funding department cannot make payments to students for holidays during term time. The exceptions are as follows: a) Religious holidays should be recorded by the College as an Authorised Absence.

questions.question: A programme is disrupted because of the awarding body, with no fault on the College's part. A student asks you whether LCC will pay them compensation. What does the Student Compensation Policy say?
options: LCC pays the compensation in full at the outset, then recovers the cost from the awarding body
LCC and the awarding body each pay half of the compensation, with LCC handling the claim
The student has no right to compensation from anyone, as the disruption was not LCC's fault
LCC will not pay; the claim lies against the awarding body, but LCC will help the student claim
questions.explanation: Where disruption is caused by the awarding or accreditation body without fault by the College, the College pays no compensation; the student's claim lies against that body, and the College will help them obtain compensation from it.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will not pay out any compensation ... due the cause of awarding body or accreditation body without any fault on the part of the College. In such cases student's claim for compensation lie against the awarding body or accreditation body. However, the College will help and assist affected students so that they receive appropriate compensation from the relevant body;

questions.question: An applicant has accepted a place on an LCC programme but has not yet enrolled. LCC then announces it intends to terminate that programme. Under the Student Compensation Policy, does this count as disruption to continuation of study?
options: Yes, the definition covers a programme on which a student accepted a place but was not enrolled
