No, the definition covers enrolled students alone, so an applicant who has not enrolled is excluded
Yes, provided the applicant has already paid a tuition fee deposit to secure their place at LCC
No, the definition applies once a programme has actually closed, not when LCC merely intends to
questions.explanation: The policy defines disruption to include the College terminating, or intending to terminate, a programme on which a student accepted a place but was not enrolled; no deposit or completed termination is required.
questions.source_excerpt: a) the College either terminated or intends to terminate a programme of study on which a student accepted a place but not was not enrolled as a student or;

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, in which circumstance is the termination of a programme excluded from the definition of disruption to continuation of study?
options: Where fewer than half of the registered students on the programme are affected
Where the College gives registered students at least one full term's written notice of closure
Where all registered students expected to complete by the termination date have done so
Where registered students are offered a transfer onto a similar programme run by the College
questions.explanation: The definition does not include termination of programmes where all registered students who would normally have been expected to complete at the date of termination have done so.
questions.source_excerpt: It does not include changes to or termination of programmes where all registered students who would normally have been expected to complete at the date of termination have done so.

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, which situation is described as an Unavoidable Termination of a programme?
options: The College temporarily discontinues a programme and readjusts it at the end of the academic year
A student can no longer continue their studies because of personal, health or financial circumstances
The College decides to change the teaching timetable, campus or delivery mode of a programme mid-year
An unexpected event forces termination during the year, or too few students enrol for it to be viable
questions.explanation: Unavoidable Termination occurs when an unexpected event compels the College to terminate a programme during an academic year, or when insufficient students enrol to make it viable to run.
questions.source_excerpt: Unavoidable Termination of a programme occurs when an unexpected event or circumstances arise which compel the College to terminate the programme during an academic year or Insufficient students enrolled for the programme to make it viable to run.

questions.question: According to the Student Compensation Policy, what is a Temporary Termination and Adjustment of a Programme (TTAP)?
options: The College discontinues a programme for a time but readjusts it at the end of an academic year
The College suspends a programme for a few weeks and restarts it unchanged within the same term
The awarding body suspends a programme while an accreditation review of the College is carried out
The College terminates a programme part-way through the year because of an unexpected event
questions.explanation: The policy states that TTAP occurs when the College discontinues the programme for a time but readjusts it at the end of an academic year; termination forced by an unexpected event is Unavoidable Termination.
questions.source_excerpt: TTAP occurs when the College contemporarily discontinues the programme but readjusts it at the end of an academic year.

questions.question: According to the Student Compensation Policy, if it is not possible to specify the actual amount of compensation a student is entitled to, what will the College ensure?
options: The student receives a flat-rate payment in place of the actual amount, equal to one term's tuition fees
The student receives an amount set by the awarding body for that programme
The student receives a refund of their enrolment deposit, with no further payment for any other costs
The student receives the actual loss suffered or additional costs incurred due to the disruption
questions.explanation: Where the amount cannot be specified, the College will ensure affected students receive the actual loss suffered or additional costs incurred because of the disruption.
questions.source_excerpt: If it is not possible to specify the actual amount of compensation to which the affected students will be entitled, the College will ensure that affected students receive the actual loss suffered or additional costs incurred because of the disruption of the continuation of study.

questions.question: After a programme termination, a relocating student claims both accommodation costs and travel costs in their compensation package. Under the Student Compensation Policy, what are they entitled to?
options: Either maintenance or accommodation costs, or travel costs, but not both
Both accommodation and travel costs, provided they supply receipts for each
Both types of cost, capped at the combined value of one term's tuition fees
Travel costs alone, as accommodation costs fall outside the compensation package
questions.explanation: The policy states an individual student will receive either maintenance or accommodation costs or travel costs, but not both.
questions.source_excerpt: An individual student will receive (a) either maintenance or accommodation costs or (b) travel costs, but not both;

questions.question: According to the Student Compensation Policy, how will a student's travel costs for increased travelling distance be covered?
options: At 20 pence per mile or actual costs, whichever is higher
At 45 pence per mile, in line with standard mileage rates
At 20 pence per mile or actual costs, whichever is lower
At actual costs in full, with no upper limit applied
questions.explanation: Travel costs cover increased travelling distance at 20 pence per mile or actual costs, whichever is the lower.
questions.source_excerpt: Travel costs will cover increased travelling distance at a rate of 20 pence per mile or actual costs whatever is the lower;

questions.question: A student's compensation claim has been agreed. They ask you when and how the money will be paid. What does the Student Compensation Policy say?
options: Normally within 7 days of agreement, by cheque to the student's address
Normally within 14 days once agreed, paid via bank transfer
Normally at the end of the academic year, by bank transfer
Within 30 days of agreement, in cash from the Finance Office
questions.explanation: Payment will normally be made within 14 days once agreed, via bank transfer.
questions.source_excerpt: Payment will normally be made within 14 days once agreed, via bank transfer.

questions.question: A student on a programme that LCC is terminating holds a bursary and is worried about losing it if they transfer. What does the Student Compensation Policy say about the bursary?
options: It ends when the programme closes, and the student must reapply for new funding
It continues to cover a different programme at LCC or the same programme at another provider
It continues if the student transfers to another programme at LCC, but not to another provider
It is converted into a one-off cash payment that is added to the student's compensation package
questions.explanation: The College will ensure that a bursary or similar funding continues to cover a different programme at the College or the same programme at an alternative provider.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will ensure that a bursary or similar funding awarded to a student, continues to cover funding to a different programme at the College or to the same programme at an alternative provider.

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, when a programme is terminated, what will the College ensure regarding the awards of its registered students?
options: They receive the full final award for the programme, as if they had completed every stage of it
They receive a letter confirming attendance and modules studied, but no formal certificate or diploma
They receive a programme award, such as a certificate or diploma, recognising the stage reached
They receive no award until they complete the same programme at an alternative provider
questions.explanation: The College will ensure all registered students receive the programme award, such as a certificate or diploma, that recognises the stage they have reached.
questions.source_excerpt: b) Ensure that all registered students receive the programme award (e.g. Certificate or diploma) that recognises the stage they have reached;

questions.question: According to the Student Compensation Policy, which of the following is NOT listed as something the compensation package should include?
options: Maintenance or accommodation costs
Study equipment, such as a laptop
Travel costs because of relocation
Additional tuition costs
questions.explanation: The package should include maintenance or accommodation costs, lost time, additional tuition costs and travel costs because of relocation; study equipment such as a laptop is not listed.
questions.source_excerpt: the compensation package referred to above should include: a) Maintenance or accommodation costs; b) Lost time; c) Additional tuition costs; d) Travel costs because of relocation;

questions.question: According to LCC's Student Compensation Policy, why has the College adopted a compensation policy?
options: To refund fees to students who withdraw for personal reasons
To compensate applicants who are not offered a place on their chosen programme
To recompense students if the continuation of their study is disrupted
To pay students' fees when they fail a module and have to repeat it
questions.explanation: The College adopted the policy to recompense students if the continuation of their study is disrupted, recognising that its arrangements to prevent disruption may not always be enough.
questions.source_excerpt: Therefore, the College has adopted a Compensation Policy to recompense the students if the continuation of study is disrupted.

questions.question: The Student Compensation Policy defines disruption to include LCC terminating, or intending to terminate, a programme on which a student enrolled. What further condition does that part of the definition set?
options: The student has been enrolled for at least one full academic year
The programme on which the student enrolled has not been completed
The student has paid their tuition fees for the current year in full
The awarding body has also withdrawn its approval of the programme
questions.explanation: The definition covers the College terminating, or intending to terminate, a programme on which a student enrolled but which has not been completed; no minimum study period or fee payment is required.
questions.source_excerpt: b) the College either terminated or intends to terminate a programme of study on which a student enrolled but the programme has not been completed.

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, how will LCC contact students affected by a disruption to their study, and what will it explain to them?
options: Promptly via their email address, explaining their rights of compensation
By letter to their home address, explaining the College complaints procedure
Through their personal tutor at the next tutorial, explaining transfer options
By text message, directing them to the awarding body's claims process
questions.explanation: The College will contact affected students promptly via their email address and explain their rights of compensation.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will contact affected students promptly via their email address and explain their rights of compensation.

questions.question: The Student Compensation Policy reminds students to check their email regularly so they do not miss contact about a disruption. How often does it recommend they check it?
options: At least once a week
At least twice a week
At least once a fortnight
At least once a day
questions.explanation: Students are reminded to check their email regularly, recommended at least once a day, and to make sure College emails are not treated as junk or spam.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are reminded to check their email regularly (recommended at least once a day) and ensure that emails from the College are not being treated as a junk or spam email.

questions.question: When a programme is affected by a Temporary Termination and Adjustment of a Programme (TTAP), between which options does the Student Compensation Policy say LCC will help students decide?
options: Taking a paid work placement or withdrawing with a full refund of fees
Transferring to a different programme or to a different college or university
Repeating the current year at LCC or switching to online distance learning
Suspending their studies for a year or appealing to the awarding body
questions.explanation: Under TTAP the College will offer students help to decide whether to transfer to a different programme or to a different College or University to complete the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: c) Offer the students help to decide whether to transfer to a different programme or transfer to a different College or University to complete the program;

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, when LCC terminates a programme, what will it offer to pay if a student wants to visit another institution they might transfer to?
options: A fixed allowance of £50 per visit, whatever the distance travelled
The full cost of travel plus one night's hotel accommodation
Reasonable travel costs of the visit to the alternative provider
Nothing, as such visits are made at the student's own expense
questions.explanation: The College will offer to pay reasonable travel costs of a visit to an alternative provider; no fixed allowance or accommodation cost is mentioned.
questions.source_excerpt: d) Offer to pay reasonable travel costs of a visit to an alternative provider;

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, if LCC has to terminate a programme, who does it commit to consulting?
options: The students registered on the programme
Only the elected course representatives
The employers of students on placements
The parents or sponsors of students on the programme
questions.explanation: In both a TTAP and an Unavoidable Termination, the College will consult the students registered on the programme.
questions.source_excerpt: If this situation arises, the College will: a) Consult the students registered on the programme;

questions.question: According to the Student Compensation Policy, when a programme is terminated, at what point is a compensation package offered to an affected student?
options: Only once the student has lodged a formal complaint
Once the student has enrolled with an alternative provider
At the end of the academic year in which the programme closed
After the College has consulted with the student
questions.explanation: A compensation package will be offered after consulting with the student; it does not depend on a complaint, enrolment elsewhere or the end of the academic year.
questions.source_excerpt: e) A compensation package will be offered after consulting with the student incorporating a provision for reimbursement of additional travel and maintenance costs reasonably incurred by students;

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, whose guidance will be consulted while LCC prepares a compensation package for affected students?
options: The Student Loans Company or the Department for Education
The Office for Students or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
Universities UK or the Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education
The Students' Union or the Citizens Advice service
questions.explanation: Guidance produced by either the Office for Students or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator for Higher Education will be consulted during preparation of the Compensation Package.
questions.source_excerpt: Guidance produced by either the Office for Students or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator for Higher Education will be consulted during preparation of the Compensation Package.

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, what is used as the basis when accommodation or maintenance costs cover a student's increased rent?
options: The rent shown on the student's own tenancy agreement, whatever the amount
The average private rent for a one-bedroom flat in the London area
A flat weekly allowance set each year by the College's Finance team
The standard student accommodation rent in the area of the new provider
questions.explanation: Accommodation or maintenance costs cover increased rent based on the standard student accommodation rent in the respective area of the new provider.
questions.source_excerpt: Accommodation or maintenance costs will cover increased rent based on the standard student accommodation rent in the respective area of the new provider.

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, when does LCC reserve the right to claim back maintenance, accommodation or travel costs it has paid to a student?
options: When they were not used or incurred, e.g. the student did not pursue the programme with a new provider
When the student later completes the programme with a new provider and receives the final award
When the awarding body later agrees to reimburse the College for the cost of the disruption
When the new provider charges the student lower tuition fees than LCC charged for the programme
questions.explanation: The College reserves the right to claim back maintenance, accommodation and travel costs that were not used or incurred, for example if the student did not pursue the programme with a new provider.
questions.source_excerpt: The College reserves the right to claim back maintenance or accommodation costs and travel costs which have not been used or incurred if, for example, the student did not pursue the programme with a new provider.

questions.question: Before teaching begins, too few students enrol on an LCC programme for it to be viable to run, so LCC closes it. Under the Student Compensation Policy, how is this disruption classified?
options: Temporary Termination and Adjustment, as it closes before it runs
Outside the policy, because no teaching on the programme had begun
Awarding body disruption, so the claim lies against that body instead
Unavoidable Termination, which covers insufficient enrolment
questions.explanation: Unavoidable Termination includes the case where insufficient students enrol for a programme to make it viable to run; TTAP is a temporary discontinuance that is readjusted at the end of an academic year.
questions.source_excerpt: Unavoidable Termination of a programme occurs when an unexpected event or circumstances arise which compel the College to terminate the programme during an academic year or Insufficient students enrolled for the programme to make it viable to run.

questions.question: LCC decides to stop delivering a programme for the time being, planning to readjust it and bring it back at the end of the academic year. Under the Student Compensation Policy, which type of disruption is this?
options: Unavoidable Termination, because delivery stops during the academic year
Temporary Termination and Adjustment of a Programme (TTAP)
A programme change that falls outside the definition of disruption
A short suspension outside the policy, as the programme will return
questions.explanation: TTAP occurs when the College discontinues a programme for a time but readjusts it at the end of an academic year, and the College's commitments to registered students then apply.
questions.source_excerpt: TTAP occurs when the College contemporarily discontinues the programme but readjusts it at the end of an academic year. If this situation arises, the College will: a) Consult the students registered on the programme;

questions.question: Staff are briefing two groups: students on a programme under TTAP, and students on a programme facing Unavoidable Termination. How do LCC's commitments to the two groups compare under the Student Compensation Policy?
options: Only the Unavoidable Termination group are offered a compensation package
The TTAP group get no programme award, since their programme will resume
Both groups get the same commitments, from consultation to bursary cover
Only the TTAP group are offered help to decide whether to transfer away
questions.explanation: Sections 4.1 and 4.2 list the same six commitments for TTAP and Unavoidable Termination: consultation, a programme award, help to decide on a transfer, visit travel costs, a compensation package and continued bursary funding.
questions.source_excerpt: TTAP occurs when ... If this situation arises, the College will: a) Consult the students registered on the programme; ... Unavoidable Termination of a programme occurs when ... If this situation arises, the College will:

questions.question: After LCC terminates a programme, a student's increased travelling distance to their new provider is 100 miles, and the actual cost of that travel is £15. Under the Student Compensation Policy, how much travel cost is covered?
options: £15.00, the actual travel cost, being the lower of the two figures
£20.00, the mileage-rate figure, being the higher of the two
£17.50, the midpoint of the mileage-rate figure and actual cost
£45.00, applying a standard rate of 45 pence per mile travelled
questions.explanation: Travel costs are covered at 20 pence per mile or actual costs, whichever is lower: 100 miles at 20p is £20, so the lower actual cost of £15 applies.
questions.source_excerpt: Travel costs will cover increased travelling distance at a rate of 20 pence per mile or actual costs whatever is the lower;

questions.question: A student used to travel 8 miles to LCC. After their programme is terminated, they stay at the same address but study at a new provider 20 miles away. Under the Student Compensation Policy, which mileage do travel costs cover?
options: The full 20 miles to the new provider
The combined 28 miles of both routes
The original 8 miles to LCC only
The increased distance of 12 miles
questions.explanation: Travel costs cover increased travelling distance, so only the extra 12 miles (20 minus 8) is covered, at 20 pence per mile or actual costs if lower.
questions.source_excerpt: Travel costs will cover increased travelling distance at a rate of 20 pence per mile or actual costs whatever is the lower;

questions.question: A student submits a compensation claim on 1 March, and LCC agrees the compensation with them on 10 March. Under the Student Compensation Policy, by when should payment normally be made?
options: Within 14 days of 1 March, when the claim was submitted
Within 14 days of the date LCC announced the programme closure
Within 14 days of 10 March, when the compensation was agreed
Within 14 days of the student starting at their new provider
questions.explanation: Payment will normally be made within 14 days once agreed, so the timeframe runs from 10 March, when the compensation was agreed, not from the claim or closure date.
questions.source_excerpt: Payment will normally be made within 14 days once agreed, via bank transfer.

questions.question: After LCC terminates a programme, a student moves to study at a provider in Leeds, and their rent goes up. Under the Student Compensation Policy, what will their accommodation or maintenance costs cover?
options: Their whole new rent in Leeds, as shown on their tenancy agreement
Increased rent, based on standard student accommodation rent in Leeds
Increased rent, based on standard student accommodation rent near LCC
Increased rent, based on the national average rent paid by UK students
questions.explanation: Accommodation or maintenance costs cover increased rent based on the standard student accommodation rent in the area of the new provider, which here is Leeds.
questions.source_excerpt: Accommodation or maintenance costs will cover increased rent based on the standard student accommodation rent in the respective area of the new provider.

questions.question: LCC paid a student accommodation costs to move near a new provider. After two months in their new room, the student stops pursuing the programme there. Under the Student Compensation Policy, what may LCC claim back?
options: All the accommodation costs paid, including rent already incurred
Nothing, as the costs were paid under an agreed compensation package
Only travel costs, as accommodation costs cannot be claimed back
Only the accommodation costs that have not been used or incurred
questions.explanation: The College reserves the right to claim back maintenance or accommodation costs and travel costs which have not been used or incurred; rent the student has already incurred is outside that right.
questions.source_excerpt: The College reserves the right to claim back maintenance or accommodation costs and travel costs which have not been used or incurred if, for example, the student did not pursue the programme with a new provider.

questions.question: A student whose programme LCC has terminated is offered a compensation package after consultation, and asks which of their costs it will reimburse. Under the Student Compensation Policy, what must the package make provision for?
options: Additional travel and maintenance costs reasonably incurred by the student
Any costs the student chooses to claim, provided each is backed by a receipt
Costs the student incurred before the termination was first announced
Tuition fees already paid to LCC for the whole of the programme so far
questions.explanation: The compensation package offered after consulting the student incorporates a provision for reimbursement of additional travel and maintenance costs reasonably incurred by students, not any cost claimed or fees already paid.
questions.source_excerpt: e) A compensation package will be offered after consulting with the student incorporating a provision for reimbursement of additional travel and maintenance costs reasonably incurred by students;

questions.question: LCC withdraws a programme once its last cohort has graduated, and no registered student who was due to finish by then is still studying. A graduate asks if they can claim under the Student Compensation Policy. What is the position?
options: Yes; any termination of a programme the student studied on is covered
Yes, but only for lost time, as the graduate has already got their award
No; a closure after all students due to complete have done so is excluded
No, because any claim lies against the awarding body for that programme
questions.explanation: The definition of disruption does not include termination of programmes where all registered students who would normally have been expected to complete at the date of termination have done so.
questions.source_excerpt: It does not include changes to or termination of programmes where all registered students who would normally have been expected to complete at the date of termination have done so.

questions.question: Two students are affected by the same programme termination, but one must relocate and the other does not. How does the Student Compensation Policy say the content of each compensation package is determined?
options: Each gets an identical standard package, fixed once for the whole programme
The awarding body sets each package, and the College then pays it out
Each package depends on the circumstances and situation of the student
It is limited to the costs each student itemises in a written claim
questions.explanation: The policy states that the compensation package should include its listed elements depending on the circumstances and situation, so its content varies between students rather than being a fixed standard.
questions.source_excerpt: Depending on the circumstances and situation, the compensation package referred to above should include: a) Maintenance or accommodation costs; b) Lost time; c) Additional tuition costs; d) Travel costs because of relocation;

questions.question: After LCC terminates a programme, a student transfers to the same programme at another provider, where finishing it costs more in fees than it would have at LCC. How does the Student Compensation Policy treat that extra cost?
options: It is covered under the package element for additional tuition costs
It falls outside the package, as fees at another provider are its own matter
It is paid only if the student first makes a formal complaint to LCC
It is recovered from the awarding body, as fee levels are set by that body
questions.explanation: Additional tuition costs are one of the elements the compensation package should include, so the extra fees for completing the programme elsewhere fall within it.
questions.source_excerpt: Depending on the circumstances and situation, the compensation package referred to above should include: a) Maintenance or accommodation costs; b) Lost time; c) Additional tuition costs; d) Travel costs because of relocation;

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, which sequence correctly describes how compensation reaches a student after LCC terminates their programme?
options: LCC pays an interim sum within 14 days, then consults the student and agrees a package
LCC consults the student, offers a package, agrees it, then normally pays within 14 days
LCC agrees a package with the awarding body, then pays the student at the end of the year
LCC offers a standard package, pays within 14 days, then consults the student about it
questions.explanation: A compensation package is offered after consulting with the student, and payment is normally made within 14 days once it is agreed, via bank transfer.
questions.source_excerpt: A compensation package will be offered after consulting with the student incorporating a provision for reimbursement of additional travel and maintenance costs reasonably incurred by students; ... Payment will normally be made within 14 days once agreed, via bank transfer.

questions.question: LCC terminates a programme on 30 June. All but one of the registered students expected to complete by that date have done so; the remaining student, also due to finish by then, has a final module outstanding. Is this termination excluded from the definition of disruption in the Student Compensation Policy?
options: Yes, because nearly every student due to complete by then has done so
No, because the exclusion applies only where all of those students have completed
Yes, because a student who misses their expected completion date loses the policy's cover
No, because the exclusion applies only where the awarding body has approved the closure
questions.explanation: The exclusion applies only where all registered students who would normally have been expected to complete at the date of termination have done so; one such student has not, so the termination remains within the definition.
questions.source_excerpt: It does not include changes to or termination of programmes where all registered students who would normally have been expected to complete at the date of termination have done so.

questions.question: A lecturer's two-week illness means several classes are cancelled, but the programme continues as planned. A student asks whether this counts as disruption to continuation of study under LCC's Student Compensation Policy. What is the position?
options: Yes, as any cancelled teaching counts as disruption to continuation of study
Yes, provided the cancelled classes add up to more than one week of teaching
No, as disruption caused by staff absence is for the awarding body to deal with
No, as the policy defines it as LCC terminating, or intending to terminate, a programme
questions.explanation: The policy defines disruption to continuation of study as the College terminating, or intending to terminate, a programme; cancelled classes on a programme that continues do not meet that definition.
questions.source_excerpt: In this Policy a reference to the `continuation of study without disruption' is defined as: a) the College either terminated or intends to terminate a programme of study ... b) the College either terminated or intends to terminate a programme of study on which a student enrolled but the programme has not been completed.

questions.question: An applicant has accepted a place on an LCC programme but has not yet enrolled. Too few students then enrol for the programme to be viable, and LCC closes it. Which statement about this case is correct under the Student Compensation Policy?
options: The applicant is outside the definition as not enrolled; the closure is an Unavoidable Termination
The applicant is within the definition; the closure is a Temporary Termination and Adjustment
The applicant is within the definition; the closure is an Unavoidable Termination
The applicant is outside the policy, as low-enrolment closures are excluded
questions.explanation: Disruption includes LCC terminating a programme on which a student accepted a place but was not enrolled, and insufficient enrolment to make a programme viable is one form of Unavoidable Termination.
questions.source_excerpt: a) the College either terminated or intends to terminate a programme of study on which a student accepted a place but not was not enrolled as a student ... Unavoidable Termination of a programme occurs when ... Insufficient students enrolled for the programme to make it viable to run.

questions.question: An awarding body withdraws approval of an LCC programme because LCC failed to meet the body's requirements, and LCC then terminates the programme. Does the Student Compensation Policy's exclusion for disruption caused by an awarding body apply?
options: No, as it covers only disruption without any fault on LCC's part
Yes, as any withdrawal by an awarding body moves the claim to that body
Yes, but LCC and the awarding body then share the compensation equally
No, as it covers accreditation bodies only and not awarding bodies
questions.explanation: The College will not pay compensation for disruption caused by an awarding or accreditation body without any fault on the part of the College; here LCC was at fault, so the exclusion does not apply.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will not pay out any compensation or this compensation policy will not be operative in respect of disruption of quality study continuously due the cause of awarding body or accreditation body without any fault on the part of the College.

questions.question: In March a flood leaves LCC unable to continue a programme, and LCC terminates it. A student who has completed two years of the programme asks what type of disruption this is and what award they will get. What does the Student Compensation Policy say?
options: A TTAP; they receive a programme award recognising the stage they have reached
An Unavoidable Termination; they receive the full final award for the programme
Outside the policy, as a flood is not LCC's fault; no award is due to the student
An Unavoidable Termination; they receive an award recognising the stage reached
questions.explanation: An unexpected event compelling LCC to terminate a programme during an academic year is an Unavoidable Termination, and LCC will ensure registered students receive a programme award recognising the stage they have reached.
questions.source_excerpt: Unavoidable Termination of a programme occurs when an unexpected event or circumstances arise which compel the College to terminate the programme during an academic year ... b) Ensure that all registered students receive the programme award (e.g. Certificate or diploma) that recognises the stage they have reached;

questions.question: A bursary holder is leaving a programme that LCC has terminated. Which of these moves does the Student Compensation Policy commit LCC to ensuring their bursary or similar funding continues to cover?
options: A different programme at another university
The same programme at another college
A different programme at another college
Any programme elsewhere after a year's break
questions.explanation: The College will ensure a bursary continues to cover a different programme at the College or the same programme at an alternative provider; a different programme at another provider is not included.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will ensure that a bursary or similar funding awarded to a student, continues to cover funding to a different programme at the College or to the same programme at an alternative provider.

questions.question: During an Unavoidable Termination, a student travels to visit a university they are thinking of transferring to. Which commitment in the Student Compensation Policy covers the cost of that visit?
options: Travel costs for increased travelling distance, at 20p per mile or actual cost if lower
Accommodation costs, based on standard student rent near that university
The offer to pay reasonable travel costs of a visit to an alternative provider
Travel costs because of relocation, within the agreed compensation package
questions.explanation: Both TTAP and Unavoidable Termination include an offer to pay reasonable travel costs of a visit to an alternative provider; the 20p-per-mile rate and relocation travel costs belong to the compensation package.
questions.source_excerpt: d) Offer to pay reasonable travel costs of a visit to an alternative provider;

questions.question: When LCC terminates a programme, whether under a TTAP or an Unavoidable Termination, which of these is NOT something the Student Compensation Policy commits LCC to doing?
options: Consulting the students who are registered on the programme
Securing a guaranteed place for each student at an alternative provider
Offering to pay reasonable travel costs of a visit to an alternative provider
Keeping a bursary in place for the same programme at an alternative provider
questions.explanation: LCC commits to consult students, help them decide on a transfer, offer visit travel costs and keep bursaries in place, but the policy does not commit it to securing a guaranteed place at another provider.
questions.source_excerpt: a) Consult the students registered on the programme; ... c) Offer the students help to decide whether to transfer to a different programme or transfer to a different College or University to complete the program; d) Offer to pay reasonable travel costs of a visit to an alternative provider; ... continues to cover funding to a different programme at the College or to the same programme at an alternative provider.

questions.question: After LCC terminates a programme, a manager plans to email every affected student the same fixed compensation package before speaking to any of them. Which requirement of the Student Compensation Policy does this plan overlook?
options: Packages must be approved by the awarding body before being offered to any student
Packages may be offered only once the programme has formally closed at year end
Packages must be sent to each student's home address by post, not by email
Packages are offered after consulting each student, and depend on their circumstances
questions.explanation: A compensation package is offered after consulting with the student, and its content depends on the circumstances and situation, so a fixed package issued before any consultation overlooks both points.
questions.source_excerpt: e) A compensation package will be offered after consulting with the student ... Depending on the circumstances and situation, the compensation package referred to above should include:

questions.question: After LCC terminates a programme, a student relocates to study at a new provider, loses a term and has to pay higher tuition fees there. Under the Student Compensation Policy, which combination can their compensation package include?
options: Lost time, additional tuition, accommodation costs and travel costs together
Additional tuition and accommodation costs only, as lost time is not covered
Lost time, additional tuition, and accommodation or travel costs, but not both
Lost time and travel costs only, as extra tuition fees are not covered
questions.explanation: The package can include lost time, additional tuition costs, and maintenance or accommodation costs or travel costs; an individual student receives either accommodation or maintenance costs or travel costs, not both.
questions.source_excerpt: the compensation package referred to above should include: a) Maintenance or accommodation costs; b) Lost time; c) Additional tuition costs; d) Travel costs because of relocation; ... An individual student will receive (a) either maintenance or accommodation costs or (b) travel costs, but not both;

questions.question: After LCC terminates a programme, a bursary holder moves to a different LCC programme. They need no new accommodation, travel or extra fees, but they lose a term. What does the Student Compensation Policy provide?
options: Their bursary covers the new LCC programme; the package includes lost time
Their bursary ends on the transfer, but the package still includes lost time
Their bursary covers the new LCC programme, but internal moves get no package
Their bursary ends on the transfer, and the package includes all four listed elements
questions.explanation: A bursary continues to cover a different programme at the College, and the package depends on the student's circumstances, so for this student it covers the lost time.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will ensure that a bursary or similar funding awarded to a student, continues to cover funding to a different programme at the College ... Depending on the circumstances and situation, the compensation package referred to above should include: a) Maintenance or accommodation costs; b) Lost time;

questions.question: A student used to travel 10 miles to LCC. After LCC terminates their programme, they travel 40 miles to a new provider, and the actual cost of the extra travel is £7.50. Under the Student Compensation Policy, how much travel cost is covered?
options: £7.50: the actual cost of the extra travel, being the higher figure
£6.00: 20p on the 30 extra miles, being below the actual cost
£8.00: 20p per mile on the whole 40-mile trip to the new provider
£6.75: the midpoint between the mileage figure and the actual cost
questions.explanation: Travel costs cover the increased distance of 30 miles at 20 pence per mile or actual costs, whichever is lower: 30 miles at 20p is £6.00, which is lower than the £7.50 actual cost.
questions.source_excerpt: Travel costs will cover increased travelling distance at a rate of 20 pence per mile or actual costs whatever is the lower;

questions.question: LCC announces that it intends to terminate a programme at the end of next year, and its enrolled students have not yet completed it. What is their position under the Student Compensation Policy now?
options: They fall within the definition, and LCC will email them promptly about compensation rights
They fall within the definition, but LCC informs them only once the programme closes
They are not yet affected, as the definition applies only once a programme closes
They are affected only if the awarding body confirms the closure to them in writing
questions.explanation: The definition covers a programme the College intends to terminate on which students enrolled but have not completed, and the College will contact affected students promptly via email to explain their rights of compensation.
questions.source_excerpt: b) the College either terminated or intends to terminate a programme of study on which a student enrolled but the programme has not been completed. ... The College will contact affected students promptly via their email address and explain their rights of compensation.

questions.question: LCC paid a student a compensation package covering lost time and travel costs. Before starting, the student decides not to pursue the programme with the new provider, so none of the travel takes place. Under the Student Compensation Policy, what may LCC claim back?
options: The whole package, including the payment made for lost time
Nothing, as payment was already made once the package was agreed
The travel costs, as these have not been used or incurred
The lost-time payment only, as the student will no longer lose time
questions.explanation: The College reserves the right to claim back maintenance or accommodation costs and travel costs not used or incurred, for example where the student did not pursue the programme with a new provider; lost time is not covered by that right.
questions.source_excerpt: The College reserves the right to claim back maintenance or accommodation costs and travel costs which have not been used or incurred if, for example, the student did not pursue the programme with a new provider.

questions.question: Under the Student Compensation Policy, in which of these situations does a student's claim for compensation lie against a body other than LCC?
options: Too few students enrol for LCC to make the programme viable to run
An unexpected event compels LCC to terminate a programme mid-year
LCC discontinues a programme for now and readjusts it at the year's end
An accreditation body's decision disrupts study with no fault by LCC
questions.explanation: Where disruption is caused by an awarding or accreditation body without any fault on the College's part, the student's claim lies against that body; insufficient enrolment, unexpected events and TTAP are LCC's own terminations.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will not pay out any compensation ... due the cause of awarding body or accreditation body without any fault on the part of the College. In such cases student's claim for compensation lie against the awarding body or accreditation body.

questions.question: LCC paid a student a year's travel costs in advance to reach a new provider. The student stays on the programme there, but from the second term lives beside the campus with a relative, so no further travel costs are incurred. Under the Student Compensation Policy, what may LCC claim back?
options: The travel costs paid for later terms, as that travel was not incurred
Nothing, as claw-back applies only if the student stops the programme
All the travel costs paid, including the first term's travel already made
Nothing, as compensation paid once agreed cannot later be recovered
questions.explanation: The College reserves the right to claim back travel costs which have not been used or incurred; a student not pursuing the programme is only an example, so unincurred travel costs can be reclaimed even though the student continues.
questions.source_excerpt: The College reserves the right to claim back maintenance or accommodation costs and travel costs which have not been used or incurred if, for example, the student did not pursue the programme with a new provider.

questions.question: LCC terminates a programme mid-year and cannot specify the actual amount of compensation one student is entitled to. Under the Student Compensation Policy, what will LCC ensure the student receives, and whose guidance is consulted in preparing the package?
options: A flat sum equal to one term's fees, consulting Office for Students or Independent Adjudicator guidance
A standard tariff set by the awarding body, consulting Quality Assurance Agency guidance
Their actual loss or extra costs, consulting guidance issued by the programme's awarding body
Their actual loss or extra costs, consulting Office for Students or Independent Adjudicator guidance
questions.explanation: Where the amount cannot be specified, the College will ensure students receive the actual loss suffered or additional costs incurred, and guidance from the Office for Students or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator is consulted in preparing the package.
questions.source_excerpt: If it is not possible to specify the actual amount of compensation to which the affected students will be entitled, the College will ensure that affected students receive the actual loss suffered or additional costs incurred ... Guidance produced by either the Office for Students or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator for Higher Education will be consulted

questions.question: After LCC terminates a programme, a student relocates to Manchester to study at a new provider. They ask for both their increased rent and travel costs because of the relocation. Under the Student Compensation Policy, what can their package provide?
options: Both, with the increased rent based on standard student accommodation rent in Manchester
Both, with the increased rent based on the rent in their own Manchester tenancy agreement
Either increased rent based on standard Manchester student rent, or travel costs, not both
Either increased rent based on their own Manchester tenancy rent, or travel costs, not both
questions.explanation: An individual student receives either maintenance or accommodation costs or travel costs, but not both, and accommodation costs cover increased rent based on the standard student accommodation rent in the new provider's area.
questions.source_excerpt: An individual student will receive (a) either maintenance or accommodation costs or (b) travel costs, but not both; ... Accommodation or maintenance costs will cover increased rent based on the standard student accommodation rent in the respective area of the new provider.

questions.question: A student tells you they are unhappy about a straightforward issue with a College service and asks how to complain. Under the Complaints Policy, what should normally happen first?
options: The student discusses it informally with their personal tutor or another relevant staff member to seek early resolution
The student submits a Stage Two Complaints Form to the Principal so that senior staff are made aware of the issue straight away
The student submits the Complaints Form to the Registrar, who then convenes a Complaints Panel meeting to hear the case
The student refers the matter to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator to obtain an early, independent view of it
questions.explanation: The policy says anyone considering a complaint should first discuss it informally with their personal tutor or another relevant member of staff to seek early resolution, which is designed for straightforward concerns.
questions.source_excerpt: Any student or group of students or applicant who is considering making a complaint should discuss the matter informally in the first instance with their personal tutor or other relevant member of LCC staff, in order to seek early resolution;

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy and Procedure, how does London Churchill College define a complaint?
options: Any concern a student raises about the College, whether or not staff have yet had a chance to look into it and respond
Dissatisfaction with a programme or related service, where the complainant is not satisfied with the College's response
A formal request to review an assessment mark or a progression decision made by a board of examiners
Any written allegation of misconduct or unprofessional behaviour made against a named member of staff or a fellow student
questions.explanation: The policy defines a complaint as an expression of dissatisfaction with a programme or related academic or administrative service, where the complainant has raised the concern with the College and is not satisfied with the response.
questions.source_excerpt: London Churchill College (LCC) defines a complaint as an expression of dissatisfaction concerning the provision of a programme of study or related academic or administrative service, when the complainant has drawn his or her concern to the attention of the College and is not satisfied with the response.

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy and Procedure, how soon after the incident giving rise to it should a complaint normally be received by the College?
options: Within 10 working days after the incident occurred
No later than 20 working days after the incident
No later than three months after the incident
No later than 12 months after the incident
questions.explanation: The policy states that, to be considered, a complaint should normally be received no later than three months after the incident giving rise to it.
questions.source_excerpt: In order to be considered by the College, a complaint should normally be received no later than three months after the incident giving rise to the complaint.

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy, to whom, and within what timeframe, should a formal (Stage One) complaint be submitted after the outcome of early resolution?
options: To the Principal, within 20 working days, using the Stage Two Complaints Form
To the personal tutor, within five working days, by email or by letter
To the Registrar, within 10 working days, using the Complaints Form
To the Academic Board, within three months, using the Complaints Form
questions.explanation: Formal complaints go to the Registrar within 10 working days of the early resolution outcome, using the Complaints Form.
questions.source_excerpt: Formal complaints should be submitted to the Registrar within 10 working days of the outcome of the Early Resolution, using the Complaints Form;

questions.question: As a personal tutor, you have just completed the informal (early resolution) stage of a student's complaint. What does the Complaints Policy require you to give the student?
options: A Completion of Procedures letter confirming that internal procedures are exhausted
A Stage Two Complaints Form so that they can appeal directly to the Principal
Nothing further, as the informal stage is concluded verbally and is not recorded
A written outcome setting out the result of the informal (early resolution) stage
questions.explanation: The policy requires the Personal Tutor or other staff member to provide the student with a written outcome on completion of the informal stage.
questions.source_excerpt: On completion of the informal stage, the Personal Tutor/other staff member should provide the student with a written outcome.

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy, within what timeframe must the outcome of the formal stage (Stage One) be communicated to the student in writing?
options: Within 5 working days
Within 20 working days
Within 28 calendar days
Within 15 working days
questions.explanation: The policy states that the outcome of the formal stage is communicated to the student in writing within 20 working days.
questions.source_excerpt: The outcome of the formal stage shall be communicated to the student in writing within 20 working days.

questions.question: You are a lecturer and a student's formal complaint concerns your conduct. Under the Complaints Policy, how will the Registrar ensure your side of the matter is heard?
options: By asking your line manager to submit a written response to the complaint on your behalf
By waiting until a Complaints Panel is convened before inviting you to give your account
Through the right of reply, by a written statement or a minuted individual interview
By informing you of the complaint once the Stage One outcome has been issued to the student
questions.explanation: Where a complaint is about a staff member or student, the Registrar upholds the right of reply, giving all parties the chance to respond fully through written statements or minuted individual interviews.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the complaint is about a member of staff or a student at LCC, the Registrar will ensure that the principle of `right of reply' is upheld by giving all parties an opportunity to fully respond to the issues raised in the complaint through written statements or by minuted individual interviews

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy, if a student is not satisfied with the Stage One outcome, to whom and by when should they request a Stage Two review?
options: To the Registrar, within 20 working days of the Stage One outcome
To the Chair of the Complaints Panel, within five working days of the outcome
To the Principal, within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
To the Office of the Independent Adjudicator, within 12 months of the outcome
questions.explanation: A dissatisfied complainant may appeal to the Principal using Complaints Form Stage 2, submitted within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: he or she may appeal to the Principal using Complaints Form Stage 2 (Review Stage). The student should submit the form within 10 working days of receiving the outcome of the first Formal Stage.

questions.question: A student asks for a Stage Two review because they have found new evidence. Under the Complaints Policy, when can new evidence be a valid ground for a review?
options: If it came to light after the Stage One outcome was issued, even if the student could have supplied it earlier
If it is material, could not for valid reasons be given earlier, and would significantly affect the outcome
If it has been supplied or formally endorsed in writing by a member of College staff involved in the case
If the Registrar agrees it is relevant, even where it would have made no difference to the Stage One outcome
questions.explanation: New evidence is a valid ground only if it is material, the student was unable for valid reasons to provide it earlier, and it would have significantly affected the Stage One outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: c) new material evidence has emerged which the student or applicant was unable, for valid reasons, to provide earlier in the process which would have significantly affected the outcome of the Stage One complaint

questions.question: A student who has received a Completion of Procedures letter says they will now ask the Office for Students (OfS) to investigate their complaint. What should you tell them, according to the Complaints Policy?
options: The OfS will investigate it, as the College's internal procedures are now complete
They must obtain the Registrar's written permission before contacting the OfS
They must first ask the Principal to reopen Stage Two before the OfS can act
The OfS does not adjudicate individual complaints; external review is only via the OIA
questions.explanation: The policy states that the OfS does not investigate or adjudicate individual complaints and that external review of unresolved complaints is provided solely through the OIA.
questions.source_excerpt: Students should note that the Office for Students does not investigate or adjudicate individual complaints and that external review of unresolved complaints is provided solely through the OIA.

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy, by when must the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA) receive a student's completed complaint?
options: Within 12 months of the date of the Completion of Procedures letter
Within three months of the date of the Completion of Procedures letter
Within 12 months of the incident that gave rise to the original complaint
Within 28 days of the Principal's Stage Two decision letter
questions.explanation: The OIA must receive a completed complaint within 12 months of the date of the COP letter; later submissions are normally considered out of time.
questions.source_excerpt: The OIA must receive a completed complaint within 12 months of the date of the COP letter; complaints submitted after this period will normally be considered out of time.

questions.question: Several students on the same course are affected by the same change to teaching delivery and want to complain together. How does the Complaints Policy allow this to be handled?
options: Each student submits a separate complaint, because group complaints are not accepted under the policy
A collective complaint may be made, with one student as spokesperson if all others agree
The course leader submits a single complaint on the students' behalf and acts as their spokesperson
A group complaint can be considered once each student has received an individual Stage One outcome
questions.explanation: Where an issue affects a number of students, a group or collective complaint may be made, and one student may be nominated as spokesperson if all the others agree.
questions.source_excerpt: Where an issue affects a number of students, a group or collective complaint may be made and one student may be nominated as a spokesperson or liaison point, if all others agree, in order to manage the process more effectively.

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy and Procedure, who is covered by the policy?
options: Students currently registered with the College, but not former students, applicants or the public
Current students and College staff, but not applicants or members of the public
Current and former students of any date, as well as applicants and members of the public
Current and recently registered students, applicants and members of the public
questions.explanation: The policy covers students who are registered or were recently registered within the qualifying period, as well as applicants and members of the public.
questions.source_excerpt: This Policy covers students who are registered with the College or were recently registered on a programme of study delivered by the College within the qualifying period, as well as applicants and members of the public;

questions.question: Having investigated a Stage One complaint, which of the following is NOT one of the decisions open to the Registrar under the Complaints Policy?
options: There is no reasonable justification for the complaint
The complaint should be referred to a Complaints Panel because of its complexity
The complaint should be progressed through other procedures and terminated at this stage
The complaint should be referred directly to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
questions.explanation: The Registrar may decide there is no justification, that other procedures apply, that a Complaints Panel is needed, or that the complaint is justified; referral to the OIA only follows a Completion of Procedures letter.
questions.source_excerpt: the Registrar shall decide whether: a) there is no reasonable justification for the complaint; b) the complaint should be progressed through other procedures in which case the complaint shall be terminated at this stage; c) the complaint should on account of its complexity be referred to a Complaints Panel meeting; d) there is reasonable justification for the complaint.

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy, how is a Complaints Panel made up when the Registrar decides a complaint should be decided by a Panel meeting?
options: An independent staff Chair, two other staff with no prior involvement in the case, and a Minute Taker
The Principal as Chair, together with the student's personal tutor, one other staff member and a Minute Taker
The Registrar as Chair, together with two student representatives from the course and a Minute Taker
An independent Chair, two members of the Academic Board, and the member of staff the complaint concerns
questions.explanation: The Registrar appoints an independent member of staff as Chair, two other staff members with no prior involvement in the case, and a Minute Taker.
questions.source_excerpt: he or she shall appoint an independent member of staff as Chair, together with two other members of staff with no prior involvement in the case and a Minute Taker to minute proceedings;

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy and Procedure, what is complaints data analysed for?
options: To decide which staff should be referred for capability review or for formal disciplinary action
To set the level of compensation payable to students whose complaints are upheld in the year
To identify trends and inform improvements to teaching quality, student experience and outcomes
To rank academic departments by complaint volume for publication in the annual College prospectus
questions.explanation: The policy states that complaints data is analysed to identify trends and inform improvements to teaching quality, student experience, retention and student outcomes.
questions.source_excerpt: Complaints data is analysed to identify trends and inform improvements to teaching quality, ... student experience, retention and student outcomes

questions.question: The Complaints Policy says the College's complaints process is underpinned by core principles from the OIA Good Practice Framework. Which principles does it name?
options: Accessibility, independence, timeliness, proportionality and fairness
Confidentiality, impartiality, consistency, transparency and redress
Openness, accountability, promptness, flexibility and consistency
Accessibility, confidentiality, efficiency, discretion and neutrality
questions.explanation: The policy names accessibility, independence, timeliness, proportionality and fairness as the OIA Good Practice Framework principles underpinning the process.
questions.source_excerpt: The College's complaints process is underpinned by the core principles set out in the OIA's Good Practice Framework, including accessibility, independence, timeliness, proportionality and fairness.

questions.question: Which of the following does the Complaints Policy explicitly list as an example of a matter that students or prospective students may complain about?
options: Concerns about external examiners appointed by the awarding body
Concerns about private landlords used by new students
Concerns about funding decisions made by the Student Loans Company
Concerns about Brand Advocates contracted by the College
questions.explanation: The policy's non-exclusive list of example complaint areas includes concerns about Brand Advocates contracted by the College.
questions.source_excerpt: The examples covered in the below list are non-exclusive. ... g) Concerns about Brand Advocates contracted by the College.

questions.question: What does the Complaints Policy state about students and other stakeholders who make a formal complaint?
options: They may raise only one complaint about the same issue per academic year
They will not be disadvantaged as a result of making the formal complaint
Their complaint is anonymised before it is passed on to the Registrar
They must withdraw any academic appeal on the same matter first
questions.explanation: The policy states that students and other stakeholders will not be disadvantaged as a result of making a formal complaint.
questions.source_excerpt: Students and other stakeholders will not be disadvantaged as a result of making a formal

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy, when may a complainant include another person's personal data in their complaint?
options: Only when that person has given them written permission to do so
Only when the Registrar has confirmed that the data is relevant to the case
Whenever the other person is a student or staff member named in it
Only when the data is limited to the person's name and job or course title
questions.explanation: Complainants must avoid disclosing another person's personal data unless that person has given them written permission to do so.
questions.source_excerpt: Complainants must also avoid disclosing personal data of any other person in the complaint unless they have been given written permission by the person/s to do so.

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy, a complaint made against a fellow student may be investigated in line with which procedure?
options: The Academic Appeals Procedure overseen by the Academic Board
The Fitness to Study Procedure run by Student Services
The Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
The Bullying and Harassment Procedure managed by Human Resources
questions.explanation: The policy states that a complaint against a fellow student may be investigated in line with the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: A complaint made against a fellow student may be investigated in line with Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure;

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy, what may the College do when a complaint is submitted more than three months after the incident it relates to?
options: Reject it, as the three-month limit is applied strictly with no exceptions
Consider it only once the student has obtained written approval from the Principal
Pass it directly to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator as an out-of-time case
Use its discretion to consider it where there are valid reasons for the delay
questions.explanation: The College may exercise discretion to consider late complaints where there are valid reasons for delay, such as health issues, disability or caring responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: The College may exercise discretion to consider complaints submitted outside this timeframe where there are valid reasons for delay, including health issues, disability, caring responsibilities or other exceptional circumstances;

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy, within what timeframe will the Registrar acknowledge receipt of a written formal complaint?
options: Within 10 working days of receipt
Within five working days of receipt
Within three working days of receipt
Within 48 hours of receipt
questions.explanation: As part of the initial evaluation, the Registrar acknowledges receipt of the written complaint within five working days.
questions.source_excerpt: On receipt of a complaint, the Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation to: ... b) acknowledge receipt of the written complaint within five working days;

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy, once all parties agree the Registrar's recommendations for a justified Stage One complaint, who is the matter referred to so that the resolution is implemented?
options: The Head of Quality Assurance
The Chair of the Academic Board
The student's Head of Department
The Principal of the College
questions.explanation: If all parties agree the Registrar's recommendations, the matter is referred to the Principal, who ensures that the resolution is implemented.
questions.source_excerpt: This Registrar shall seek to resolve any justifiable complaint through recommendations and shall, if the recommendations are agreed by all parties, refer the matter to the Principal, who will ensure that the resolution is implemented;

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy, who may accompany a complainant who has been invited to attend a Complaints Panel meeting?
options: A current student or a member of College staff
A solicitor or other legal representative
A family member or a friend from outside the College
An advocate from an external advice service
questions.explanation: The invitation to the Panel informs the complainant of their right to be accompanied by a current student or member of staff.
questions.source_excerpt: informing him/her of the right to be accompanied by a current student/member of staff;

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy, what timeframe is set for issuing the outcome of a Stage Two (Review Stage) to the student?
options: Within 14 days of the decision
Within 20 working days of the decision
Within 28 days of the decision
Within 12 weeks of the decision
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Stage Two outcome is issued to the student within 28 days of the decision.
questions.source_excerpt: Outcome issued to student within 28 days of decision

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy, what does a Completion of Procedures (COP) letter confirm to the student?
options: That their complaint was upheld in full at the Stage Two review
That the College's internal complaints procedures have been exhausted
That the Office for Students has agreed to investigate the complaint
That the complaint is now closed and cannot be taken any further
questions.explanation: The COP letter confirms that the College's internal procedures have been exhausted and explains the right to refer the complaint to the OIA.
questions.source_excerpt: Upon completion of the internal complaints process, the College will issue the student with a Completion of Procedures (COP) letter. This letter confirms that the College's internal procedures have been exhausted

questions.question: The Equality Impact Assessment in the Complaints Policy gives examples of matters that students may self-certify for. Which of the following is one of them?
options: Religious holidays and caring responsibilities
Part-time work shifts and job interviews
Driving tests and pre-booked family holidays
Travel disruption and national transport strikes
questions.explanation: The policy states that students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments and caring responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments and caring responsibilities.

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy, who should make reasonable adjustments for students whose attendance at panel hearings has been affected by their disability?
options: The Registrar's Office
The Student Services team
The Chair of the Complaints Panel
The Academic Department
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments for students whose attendance at panel hearings has been affected by disability.
questions.source_excerpt: Similarly, the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments for students whose attendance at panel hearings or other, has been affected by his or her disability to accommodate attendance at review meetings.

questions.question: According to the Complaints Policy, what happens while the members of a Complaints Panel deliberate and reach their decision?
options: The complainant stays to answer any final questions from the Panel
The Registrar joins the Panel to advise on the likely outcome
All parties in attendance are asked to leave the room
The Minute Taker reads back the evidence to all parties present
questions.explanation: At the end of the Panel meeting, all parties in attendance are asked to leave the room while the Panel members deliberate and reach a decision.
questions.source_excerpt: All parties in attendance are asked to leave the room while the Panel members ... deliberate and reach a decision.

questions.question: Under the monitoring arrangements in the Complaints Policy, how does the College ensure that all complaints data is kept?
options: Anonymised at source and deleted at the end of each academic year
Recorded accurately, verified and maintained with appropriate audit trails
Held only by the Principal and not shared with any College committee
Stored separately by each department and reviewed only upon request
questions.explanation: The policy states that all complaints data is recorded accurately, verified and maintained with appropriate audit trails, supporting reliable reporting.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that all complaints data is recorded accurately, verified and maintained with appropriate audit trails.

questions.question: An applicant wants to complain about how their application for admission to the College was handled. Under the Complaints Policy, how should a complaint from a prospective student be approached?
options: It should adhere to the relevant policy, for instance the Recruitment, Selection and Admission Policy
It cannot be accepted until the applicant has enrolled, as only registered students may complain
It goes straight to a Complaints Panel, as applicants are not able to use the informal stage
It must be referred directly to the OIA, as the College's internal procedures do not cover applicants
questions.explanation: The policy states that a complaint from a prospective student should adhere to the relevant policy, such as the Recruitment, Selection and Admission Policy or the Brand Advocate Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: A complaint from a prospective student should adhere to the relevant policy, for instance the Recruitment, Selection and Admission Policy or Brand Advocate Policy.

questions.question: A student drafting a complaint asks whether to mention a health condition that has nothing to do with the issue. What does the Complaints Policy advise complainants about personal information like this?
options: Include it, as all health information must be declared in full on the Complaints Form
Avoid disclosing it, as unnecessary personal information should not be included
Include it only if a doctor's letter is attached so the Registrar can verify it
Send it to the Registrar separately so that it can be added to the complaint file
questions.explanation: Complainants should avoid disclosing unnecessary personal information, such as medical conditions, unless they feel it is relevant to the issues raised.
questions.source_excerpt: At all stages of the complaints process a complainant should ensure that he or she avoids disclosing unnecessary personal information (e.g. medical conditions etc.) unless s/he feels it is relevant to the issues raised.

questions.question: Complaints suggest that one particular group of students is being disproportionately affected by a change to delivery arrangements. Under the Complaints Policy, what may the College do in response?
options: Pause the delivery change until the OIA has reviewed each of the complaints received
Refer the affected students to the Office for Students for an individual adjudication
Review whether additional support measures or wider remedial action are required
Merge the complaints into one Stage Two review to be heard directly by the Principal
questions.explanation: Where complaints indicate that particular groups may be disproportionately affected by delivery arrangements, the College may review whether additional support measures or wider remedial action are required.
questions.source_excerpt: Where complaints indicate that particular groups of students may be disproportionately affected by institutional decisions, delivery arrangements or support provision, the College may review whether additional support measures or wider remedial action are required.

questions.question: A student's concern relates to a staff member's conduct across several different incidents and will require detailed investigation. How does the Complaints Policy treat a complaint like this?
options: It must first be settled by the personal tutor at the informal stage before anything else
It is passed straight to the Principal for a decision as a Stage Two review of the case
It can only be made jointly with at least one other student affected by the same conduct
It is one of the situations in which the formal complaints process is triggered
questions.explanation: The formal process is triggered where the issues are complex and need detailed investigation, for example where a complaint relates to staff conduct or covers several different incidents.
questions.source_excerpt: The formal complaints process is triggered when: ... j) the issues raised are complex and will require detailed investigation, for example ... where a complaint relates to the conduct of staff members, accessibility concerns, changes to delivery arrangements or covers several different incidents.
