questions.question: A student with a concern declines to discuss it informally with their personal tutor and wants to go straight to a formal complaint. What is the position under the Complaints Policy?
options: The complaint cannot proceed until an informal meeting with the tutor has taken place
The student may initiate the formal process, as declining early resolution triggers it
The student must instead ask the Principal for a Stage Two review of the concern raised
The Registrar must first hold the informal meeting in the personal tutor's place
questions.explanation: The formal process is triggered where the student or applicant declines to engage with early resolution and initiates the formal process.
questions.source_excerpt: The formal complaints process is triggered when: ... h) the student or applicant declines to engage with early resolution and initiates the formal process

questions.question: A student asks what they need to include when submitting a formal (Stage One) complaint. According to the Complaints Policy, what must they ensure?
options: The details are clear and in writing, supporting evidence is provided and the outcome sought is stated
A signed statement from their personal tutor confirms that early resolution was tried and failed
Written consent is obtained from every staff member named and the informal stage minutes are attached
A verbal account is given to the Registrar, who then completes the Complaints Form on their behalf
questions.explanation: At the formal stage students must make the details clear in writing, provide any supporting evidence and clearly express the outcome they are seeking.
questions.source_excerpt: When making a complaint at the formal stage, students will need to ensure that they: ... a) make clear the details of the complaint in writing; b) provide any evidence to support his or her complaint; c) express clearly the outcome being sought

questions.question: A formal complaint reaches the Registrar and is acknowledged a few days later. Under the Complaints Policy, how long should the Registrar's investigation normally last, and from when is it counted?
options: Up to 10 working days from the acknowledgement
Up to 20 working days from the acknowledgement
Up to five working days from the acknowledgement
Up to 10 working days from its receipt
questions.explanation: The Registrar investigates over a period not normally exceeding 10 working days from receipt of the complaint; acknowledgement within five working days is a separate step.
questions.source_excerpt: Having fully investigated the complaint over a period not normally exceeding 10 working days from its receipt, the Registrar shall decide whether:

questions.question: The Registrar has decided that a student's Stage One complaint is not upheld. According to the Complaints Policy, what must the student be informed of?
options: That they may now refer the complaint directly to the OIA under the national scheme
That the matter is closed and no further internal route is open to them
Their right to request a review of Stage One, how to do so and the time limits
That they must attend a Complaints Panel meeting within 21 working days
questions.explanation: If a Stage One complaint is not upheld, the student is told of their right to request a review, with instructions on how to do so and the time limits.
questions.source_excerpt: If the complaint is not upheld, the student will be informed of his/her right to request a review of Stage One, as well as instructions on how to do so and the time limits.

questions.question: A Complaints Panel hearing has been arranged for a student's complaint. Under the Complaints Policy, what must the student be given a minimum of five working days before the hearing?
options: The Panel's draft decision and the recommendations it is minded to make on the case
Details of the Panel's composition, other invitees and the information relevant to the case
The minutes of the Panel members' preliminary private discussion about the complaint
A Completion of Procedures letter explaining how to take the case to the OIA if needed
questions.explanation: The Chair must give the student, at least five working days before the hearing, information on the Panel's composition, other invitees and a copy of the relevant information to be considered.
questions.source_excerpt: d) provide the student or applicant a minimum of five working days before the hearing with information about the composition of the Complaints Panel, other invitees and a copy of the information relevant to his or her case that will be considered.

questions.question: At a Complaints Panel meeting about a complaint against a member of staff, at what point is that staff member invited to present representations or evidence challenging the complaint?
options: After the student has presented their case
Before the student or applicant presents their case
After the student's brief concluding statement
After the Panel members have asked their questions
questions.explanation: In the Panel running order, the student or applicant presents their case first and the staff member or student complained about is then invited to present representations or evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: c) The student or applicant is invited to present his or her case ... d) In instances where a complaint is about a member of staff or student, s/he will be ... invited to present any representations and/or evidence to challenge the complaint;

questions.question: A Complaints Panel has reached its decision on a student's complaint. Under the Complaints Policy, what must the student be told, and by when?
options: The outcome within five working days of the decision, and how to apply to the OIA
The outcome within 28 days of the decision, and that the Panel's decision is final
The outcome within 10 working days of the decision, and how to contact the OfS
The outcome within 20 working days of the decision, and their right to request a review
questions.explanation: After a Panel decision, the student is notified of the outcome within 20 working days and informed of their right to request a review.
questions.source_excerpt: The student or other will be notified of the outcome within 20 working days of the decision being made. The complainant will also be informed of their right to request a review of the decision made.

questions.question: A student requests a Stage Two review, citing a minor procedural slip at Stage One that had no effect on the outcome. Under the Complaints Policy, is this a valid ground for review?
options: Yes, because any departure from the set procedure is a valid ground for a review
Yes, provided the request is made within 28 days of the Stage One outcome letter
No, because the irregularity must be material and have affected the Stage One outcome
No, because procedural issues can be raised only with the OIA and not at the review stage
questions.explanation: A procedural ground for review requires a material procedural irregularity which has affected the outcome of the Stage One complaint.
questions.source_excerpt: A request for a review must be based on the following limited grounds: a) the outcome at Stage One is unreasonable; b) there has been a material procedural irregularity which has affected the outcome of ... the Stage One complaint;

questions.question: A student's Stage One complaint was upheld, but the recommendations made at that stage have not been implemented. What route does the Complaints Policy give the student?
options: Appeal to the Principal using Complaints Form Stage 2
Refer the complaint to the OIA without a COP letter
Ask the personal tutor to reopen the informal stage
Ask the Chair of the Academic Board to enforce the recommendations
questions.explanation: If the recommendations made at the Formal Stage are not implemented, the complainant may appeal to the Principal using Complaints Form Stage 2 (Review Stage).
questions.source_excerpt: If the complainant is not satisfied with the decision at the conclusion of the Formal Stage or if the recommendations made at this stage are not implemented, he or she may appeal to the Principal using Complaints Form Stage 2 (Review Stage).

questions.question: After receiving the written outcome of the informal stage, a student wants to go straight to the Principal for a Stage Two review. What does the Complaints Policy say about this?
options: The Principal may accept it if it is submitted within 10 working days of the informal outcome
The complaint must first have been considered at the formal Stage One before it can be escalated
The Principal may accept it if the personal tutor agrees in writing to the escalation
The Principal must accept it, as a review can follow any written complaint outcome
questions.explanation: A complaint must have been considered at the formal Stage One before it can be escalated to the Stage Two review.
questions.source_excerpt: A complaint must have been considered at the formal Stage One before it can be escalated to the Stage Two review

questions.question: Under the Complaints Policy, once the Principal (or nominee) has acknowledged receipt of a Stage Two review request, what options are open to them?
options: Return it to the personal tutor for informal resolution, or refer it on to a Complaints Panel
Refer it directly to the OIA, or ask the Office for Students to adjudicate the complaint
Send it back to the Registrar for a revised Stage One letter, or refer it to the Academic Board
Dismiss the case with a Stage Two decision letter, or seek to agree alternative recommendations
questions.explanation: At Stage Two the Principal (or nominee) will either dismiss the case with a Stage Two decision letter or seek to negotiate and agree an alternative set of recommendations.
questions.source_excerpt: The Principal (or nominee) shall acknowledge receipt of the complaint within five working days and will: a) either dismiss the case and inform the complainant in writing with a Stage Two ... decision letter or b) seek to negotiate and agree an alternative set of recommendations

questions.question: A disabled student's complaint paperwork is late because of the effects of their disability. How does the equality section of the Complaints Policy say lateness like this may be treated?
options: It cannot be excused, as time limits apply equally to every student
It is excused automatically for all disabled students, without review
It may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis
It can be approved only by the OIA once internal procedures have ended
questions.explanation: The equality section states that, for students with disability, lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis.
questions.source_excerpt: References are made throughout the EIA to ensure that accommodation is made for students with disability. For example, lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis.

questions.question: A manager suggests that the main oversight of complaints at the College is reporting each individual case to the Office for Students. Which statement reflects the oversight arrangements in the Complaints Policy?
options: The Principal reports every upheld complaint to the OfS, which then decides whether the College's remedy was adequate
The Registrar sends the OIA a termly report on all complaints, which the OIA then uses to audit the College's procedure
The Registrar reports annually to the Academic Board and the ARRC on complaints activity, trends, outcomes and themes
Each Complaints Panel Chair reports decisions to the Board of Directors, which then confirms or overturns each outcome
questions.explanation: The Registrar reports annually to the Academic Board and the ARRC on complaints activity, trends, outcomes and significant themes or risks; the OfS does not investigate or adjudicate individual complaints.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will report annually to the Academic Board and the Audit Risk and Renumeration Committee (ARRC) on complaints activity, trends, outcomes and any significant themes or risks identified ... Students should note that the Office for Students does not investigate or adjudicate individual complaints

questions.question: Eight students affected by a change of campus location want to make a collective complaint, but two of them object to the student proposed as spokesperson. What does the Complaints Policy say about that nomination?
options: It cannot go ahead as proposed, as a spokesperson may be nominated only if all the others agree
It can go ahead, as a clear majority of the affected students have agreed to the spokesperson
It can go ahead once the Registrar has approved the nominee as the group's liaison point
It lapses, and the collective complaint must be replaced by eight separate individual complaints
questions.explanation: A group or collective complaint may be made, but one student may be nominated as spokesperson or liaison point only if all the others agree.
questions.source_excerpt: Where an issue affects a number of students, a group or collective complaint may be made and one student may be nominated as a spokesperson or liaison point, if all others agree, in order to manage the process more effectively.

questions.question: A student complains that a member of staff has repeatedly bullied them, for a reason unconnected with race, disability or any other characteristic named in the Complaints Policy. How does the policy's list of example complaint areas apply?
options: It excludes this, as bullying by staff is dealt with solely under the staff disciplinary procedure
It covers this only where the bullying relates to a characteristic protected by equality law
It excludes this, as only matters specifically named in the list may be raised as complaints
It covers bullying by staff or fellow students on any named ground or for any other reason
questions.explanation: The list of examples is non-exclusive and includes any form of harassment or bullying from fellow students or staff on the named grounds, any other personal characteristic, or for any other reason.
questions.source_excerpt: The examples covered in the below list are non-exclusive. ... Any form of harassment or bullying from fellow students, member of staff on grounds of ... other personal characteristic or for any other reason

questions.question: A student drafting a complaint wants to mention a classmate's medical condition, which the student genuinely feels is relevant to the issue. What does the Complaints Policy require before this is included?
options: Nothing more, as personal information may be disclosed whenever the complainant feels it is relevant
Written permission from the classmate, as it is the personal data of another person in the complaint
The Registrar's written agreement that the details are relevant, recorded on the Complaints Form
A letter from a medical professional confirming the condition, attached to the Complaints Form
questions.explanation: Complainants may include their own personal information if they feel it is relevant, but must avoid disclosing another person's personal data unless that person has given written permission.
questions.source_excerpt: a complainant should ensure that he or she avoids disclosing unnecessary personal information (e.g. medical conditions etc.) unless s/he feels it is relevant to the issues raised. Complainants must also avoid disclosing personal data of any other person in the complaint unless they have been given written permission by the person/s to do so.

questions.question: A student who has no disability but does have additional needs asks for an adjustment so that they can take part in the complaints process. What does the Complaints Policy say?
options: Adjustments are limited to students whose disability has been formally assessed by the College
Adjustments are considered only by the OIA once the College's internal procedures are exhausted
Reasonable adjustments may be made where appropriate for those with additional support needs
Adjustments may be made only at the Complaints Panel stage, by the Chair appointed to the hearing
questions.explanation: The College takes reasonable steps to keep complaints procedures accessible and inclusive, including reasonable adjustments where appropriate for disabled students and students with additional support needs.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will take reasonable steps to ensure that complaints procedures are accessible and inclusive, including making reasonable adjustments where appropriate for disabled students and students with additional support needs

questions.question: A student raises a straightforward concern about a library service with a member of professional services staff rather than their personal tutor. Under the Complaints Policy, how may the informal stage be handled?
options: That staff member may seek early resolution and, on completion, should give the student a written outcome
That staff member must redirect the student to their personal tutor, as only tutors handle early resolution
That staff member must pass it to the Registrar, as concerns raised outside tutoring are formal complaints
That staff member may resolve it verbally, as a written outcome is needed only when a tutor handles it
questions.explanation: Early resolution may be sought with the personal tutor or another relevant member of LCC staff, and on completion the Personal Tutor or other staff member should give the student a written outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: discuss the matter informally in the first instance with their personal tutor or other relevant member of LCC staff, in order to seek early resolution; ... On completion of the informal stage, the Personal Tutor/other staff member should provide the student with a written outcome.

questions.question: A formal complaint to the Registrar concerns alleged misconduct by a fellow student, and the Registrar decides it should be progressed under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure. What happens to the complaint under the Complaints Policy?
options: It is paused, and resumes at Stage One once the disciplinary procedure has reached its conclusion
It goes to a Complaints Panel, which decides which of the two procedures should apply to the case
It moves to Stage Two, so that the Principal can confirm its transfer to the disciplinary procedure
It is terminated at this stage of the complaints process, as it is progressed through the other procedure
questions.explanation: A complaint against a fellow student may be investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, and where the Registrar decides a complaint should be progressed through other procedures it is terminated at this stage.
questions.source_excerpt: A complaint made against a fellow student may be investigated in line with Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure; ... the complaint should be progressed through other procedures in which case the ... complaint shall be terminated at this stage;

questions.question: The Registrar is drafting the Stage One outcome letter for a complaint that has been upheld. Besides the decision and any actions to be taken, what should the letter normally explain, according to the Complaints Policy?
options: The reasons for the decision and how to contact the OIA within 12 months
The reasons for the decision and the student's right to request a review
Nothing further, as review rights are explained only if a complaint is not upheld
The names of the Panel members who would hear any review of the decision
questions.explanation: Outcome letters will normally explain the decision, the reasons for it, any actions to be taken and the student's right to request a review; this is not limited to complaints that are not upheld.
questions.source_excerpt: Outcome letters will normally explain the decision reached, the reasons for the decision, any actions to be taken and the student's right to request a review.

questions.question: During a Stage One investigation, the Registrar believes that speaking to the complainant and to a witness would help establish the facts. What does the Complaints Policy allow at this stage?
options: The Registrar must decide on the written evidence alone, as discussions are held only at a Panel meeting
The Registrar may, if necessary, hold discussions with the complainant and other persons to investigate
The Registrar may speak to the complainant, but a witness can be heard only at the Stage Two review
The Registrar may hold discussions only once the Principal has given written approval to do so
questions.explanation: As part of the Stage One evaluation, the Registrar considers the evidence and may, if necessary, hold discussions with the complainant and other persons to fully investigate the complaint.
questions.source_excerpt: On receipt of a complaint, the Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation to: ... c) consider the evidence and, if necessary, hold discussions with the complainant and ... any other persons he or she deems appropriate to fully investigate the complaint.

questions.question: A Complaints Panel Chair sends the complainant the invitation to attend, together with the case papers, three working days before the meeting. Under the Complaints Policy, what is wrong with this?
options: Nothing, as only the case papers are subject to a minimum notice period before the hearing
The invitation should have come from the Registrar, who is responsible for convening the Panel
The invitation and the case papers had to be sent at least 21 working days before the meeting
The invitation and the case papers were both due no later than five working days before it
questions.explanation: The Chair must invite the complainant no later than five working days before the meeting and provide the case information a minimum of five working days before the hearing.
questions.source_excerpt: issue an invitation to the complainant to attend the Panel to present the case (no later ... than five working days before the meeting is due to take place) ... provide the student or applicant a minimum of five working days before the hearing with information about the composition of the Complaints Panel, other invitees and a copy of the information relevant to his or her case

questions.question: At a Complaints Panel meeting, the Panel members have just finished asking their questions of the attendees. Under the Complaints Policy, what are the next two steps, in order?
options: The Chair invites anyone present to ask further questions or add information, then the student makes a brief concluding statement
The student makes a brief concluding statement, and then the staff member complained about gives a final response to it
Anyone accompanying the student is invited to speak, then the Panel deliberates with all parties still in the room
The Panel deliberates in private, and then the Chair calls all parties back into the room to announce its decision
questions.explanation: After the Panel's questions, the Chair invites anyone present to ask further questions or provide further information, and the student or applicant is then invited to make a brief concluding statement.
questions.source_excerpt: the panel members may ask questions of ... any attendees, as they see fit; g) The Chair will invite anyone present to ask further questions or to provide further ... information; h) The student or applicant is then invited to make a brief concluding statement;

questions.question: A Complaints Panel Chair wants to depart from the standard running order for a Panel meeting. Under the Complaints Policy, when is this permitted?
options: Never, as the running order in the policy is fixed for every meeting
Whenever the complainant agrees to the change in advance of the meeting
In exceptional circumstances, under the provision to vary the procedure
Only where the Principal has approved the change in writing beforehand
questions.explanation: The Panel meeting is normally conducted in the set manner, with provision to vary the procedure in exceptional circumstances.
questions.source_excerpt: The Panel meeting shall normally be conducted in the following manner, with the provision to vary the procedure in exceptional circumstances:

questions.question: Which of the following Stage Two review requests is based on one of the limited grounds for review set out in the Complaints Policy?
options: The student had evidence at Stage One but chose not to submit it, and now wishes to rely on it
The student accepts the Stage One outcome but would like a more senior person to confirm it
The student argues that the Stage One outcome is unreasonable on the evidence considered
The student now wants a different remedy from the outcome sought in the Stage One complaint
questions.explanation: Review requests must rest on limited grounds: an unreasonable Stage One outcome, a material procedural irregularity that affected the outcome, or new material evidence that could not for valid reasons be provided earlier.
questions.source_excerpt: A request for a review must be based on the following limited grounds: ... a) the outcome at Stage One is unreasonable;

questions.question: A student's Stage Two request asks the Principal to reinvestigate the whole complaint from the beginning. What does the Complaints Policy say about the scope of the review stage?
options: It will not normally reinvestigate in full, unless that is considered necessary in the interests of fairness
It always reinvestigates in full, since the Principal must reach an independent view of the complaint
It never reinvestigates, and is limited to checking whether the Stage One letter was issued on time
It reinvestigates in full only where the student provides new evidence that was not seen at Stage One
questions.explanation: The review stage will not normally reinvestigate the complaint in full unless this is considered necessary in the interests of fairness.
questions.source_excerpt: The review stage will not normally reinvestigate the complaint in full unless this is considered necessary in the interests of fairness.

questions.question: A Stage Two review request reaches the College while the Principal is on leave. Under the Complaints Policy, who may acknowledge receipt, and within what time?
options: Only the Principal, within 10 working days of returning from leave
The Principal's nominee, within five working days of receipt
The Registrar, within 10 working days of receiving it
The Chair of the Academic Board, within 28 days of receipt
questions.explanation: At Stage Two, the Principal (or nominee) acknowledges receipt of the complaint within five working days.
questions.source_excerpt: The Principal (or nominee) shall acknowledge receipt of the complaint within five working days

questions.question: Once the Registrar has referred a complaint to a Complaints Panel, which pair of time limits in the Complaints Policy applies to the Panel stage?
options: Meeting convened within 10 working days; outcome notified within 28 calendar days of the decision
Meeting convened within 20 working days; outcome notified within 5 working days of the decision
Meeting convened within 28 days; outcome notified within 10 working days of the decision
Meeting convened within 21 working days; outcome notified within 20 working days of the decision
questions.explanation: The Chair convenes the Panel meeting within 21 working days, and the student is notified of the outcome within 20 working days of the decision being made.
questions.source_excerpt: a) convene a meeting within 21 working days of the Complaints Panel; ... The student or other will be notified of the outcome within 20 working days of the decision being made.

questions.question: A student whose Stage One complaint was not upheld asks for a Completion of Procedures letter straight away so that they can go to the OIA. What does the Complaints Policy indicate?
options: The Registrar must issue the COP letter with the Stage One outcome, as the formal stage is now over
A COP letter comes once internal procedures are exhausted, and a Stage Two review is still open to them
The student may go to the OIA without a COP letter if they do so within 12 months of Stage One
The student must ask the Office for Students to issue the COP letter, as it oversees the OIA scheme
questions.explanation: A COP letter is issued upon completion of the internal complaints process and confirms internal procedures are exhausted; a student whose Stage One complaint is not upheld still has the right to request a Stage Two review.
questions.source_excerpt: If the complaint is not upheld, the student will be informed of his/her right to request a review of Stage One ... Upon completion of the internal complaints process, the College will issue the student with a Completion of Procedures (COP) letter. This letter confirms that the College's internal procedures have been exhausted

questions.question: A student asks to self-certify for caring responsibilities that affected their ability to meet a complaints deadline. How does the Equality Impact Assessment in the Complaints Policy regard allowances of this kind?
options: As concessions only for students whose disability has been confirmed by the Academic Department
As exceptions that need the Principal's written approval before any time limit can be relaxed
As arrangements that apply to religious holidays only, and not to caring or medical matters
As reasonable allowances, since personal circumstances may affect a student's ability to appeal
questions.explanation: The EIA anticipates that personal circumstances may affect ability to appeal and makes reasonable allowances, such as self-certification for religious holidays, medical and antenatal appointments and caring responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: the EIA anticipates that personal circumstances may affect ability to appeal and makes reasonable allowances for this. For example, students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments and caring responsibilities.

questions.question: A student complains that the complaints procedure itself was applied incorrectly in their case. Besides dealing with the complaint, what does the monitoring section of the Complaints Policy say about complaints of this kind?
options: They are referred straight to the OIA, as the College cannot review its own procedure
They are left out of complaints data, so that reporting on trends is not distorted
They are reviewed to identify trends, recurring issues and areas for improvement
They are passed to the Office for Students to consider as a possible regulatory breach
questions.explanation: Under the monitoring arrangements, complaints relating to the application or implementation of the procedure are reviewed to identify trends, recurring issues and areas for improvement.
questions.source_excerpt: Complaints relating to the application or implementation of this procedure will be reviewed to identify trends, recurring issues and areas for improvement.

questions.question: A Complaints Panel has decided a student's complaint, and the student is dissatisfied with the decision. Under the Complaints Policy, what route is then open to the student?
options: Request a Stage Two review by the Principal, within 10 working days of the outcome
Ask the Registrar to reconvene the Panel with new members within 21 working days
Refer the complaint straight to the OIA within 12 months of the Panel's decision
Request a second Panel hearing from the Chair within five working days of the outcome
questions.explanation: After a Panel decision the complainant is told of the right to request a review; a dissatisfied complainant appeals to the Principal using Complaints Form Stage 2 within 10 working days of the formal stage outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: The complainant will also be informed of their right to request a review of the decision made. ... he or she may appeal to the Principal using Complaints Form Stage 2 (Review Stage). The student should submit the form within 10 working days of receiving the outcome of the first Formal Stage.

questions.question: The Registrar is setting up a Complaints Panel and proposes the personal tutor who gave the student the written informal-stage outcome as one of the two staff members to sit with the Chair. Is this consistent with the Complaints Policy?
options: Yes, as long as the Chair appointed to lead the Panel is an independent member of staff
Yes, as long as the student agrees in writing to the tutor sitting on the Panel
No, as those two members must be staff with no prior involvement in the case
No, as those two members must be drawn from the Academic Board, not from teaching staff
questions.explanation: The Registrar appoints an independent Chair plus two other members of staff with no prior involvement in the case; a tutor who handled the informal stage has already been involved in it.
questions.source_excerpt: On completion of the informal stage, the Personal Tutor/other staff member should provide the student with a written outcome. ... he or she shall appoint an independent member of staff as Chair, together with two other members of staff with no prior involvement in the case and a Minute Taker to minute proceedings;

questions.question: A student's complaint arose from an incident 14 months ago. The College's internal procedures ended with a Completion of Procedures letter dated nine months ago, and the student now wants to go to the OIA. How does the Complaints Policy treat the timing?
options: Out of time, as more than 12 months have now passed since the incident behind the complaint
In time, provided the OIA receives the completed complaint within 12 months of the COP letter
Out of time, as the OIA applies the same three-month limit from the incident as the College does
In time, but only once the Principal confirms in writing that the College consents to the referral
questions.explanation: The OIA deadline runs from the date of the COP letter, not from the incident: the OIA must receive a completed complaint within 12 months of that date, after which it will normally be out of time.
questions.source_excerpt: The COP letter will include details of how to access the OIA complaints form and will confirm that the OIA must receive a completed complaint within 12 months of the date of the COP letter, after which the complaint will normally be considered out of time.

questions.question: At Stage One, the Registrar finds a complaint about a lecturer justified and proposes recommendations. The student accepts them, but the lecturer does not. Under the Complaints Policy, what is needed before the matter goes to the Principal to implement the resolution?
options: Agreement to the recommendations from all parties, which includes the lecturer concerned
A Complaints Panel decision confirming that the Registrar's recommendations are justified
Nothing further, as agreement is needed only from the complainant and not from the lecturer
Approval of the recommendations by the Academic Board, to which the Registrar reports
questions.explanation: The Registrar refers a justifiable complaint to the Principal for implementation only if the recommendations are agreed by all parties, and a staff member complained about is one of the parties given a right of reply.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the complaint is about a member of staff or a student at LCC, the Registrar will ensure that the principle of `right of reply' is upheld by giving all parties an opportunity to fully respond ... This Registrar shall seek to resolve any justifiable complaint through recommendations and shall, if the recommendations are agreed by all parties, refer the matter to the Principal

questions.question: Under the Data Protection Policy, within what timeframe shall the College report a potential personal data breach to the ICO, where feasible?
options: Within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach
Within 30 calendar days of the breach occurring
Within 21 days of the breach being investigated
Within 7 working days of the DPO being notified
questions.explanation: The policy states the College shall report any potential data breach to the ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, where feasible.
questions.source_excerpt: The College shall report to ICO any potential data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, where feasible.

questions.question: You accidentally email a spreadsheet of student contact details to the wrong external recipient. According to the Data Protection Policy's definition, is this a personal data breach?
options: No, a breach under the policy requires a deliberate act, not a mistake
No, the definition covers lost or stolen devices, not misdirected emails
Not unless the recipient confirms they have opened and read the spreadsheet
Yes, the definition covers accidental unauthorised disclosure of personal data
questions.explanation: A personal data breach includes the accidental or unlawful unauthorised disclosure of personal data, and covers both accidental and deliberate causes.
questions.source_excerpt: A personal data breach means a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. This includes breaches that are the result of both accidental and deliberate causes.

questions.question: You use your own smartphone to access College emails containing student personal data, and you lose it on the train. Under the Data Protection Policy, what must you do?
options: Wait 72 hours to see if the phone is handed in before reporting it
Tell your line manager at your next scheduled one-to-one meeting
Change your passcode remotely and record the loss in your own notes
Report the loss immediately to the Data Protection Officer (DPO)
questions.explanation: The BYOD section requires any staff member who loses a personal device, or believes its personal data may have been breached, to report this immediately to the DPO.
questions.source_excerpt: If any staff member loses a personal device or believes the personal data contained on their device may have been breached, they must report this immediately to the DPO.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, within what timeframe will the College ensure that an individual's request for a copy of their personal information is fulfilled, unless there is a good reason for delay?
options: Within 72 hours of the request
Within 21 calendar days of the request
Within 30 calendar days of the request
Within 40 working days of the request
questions.explanation: Under the right of access, the College will ensure requested personal information is provided within 30 calendar days of the request unless there is a good reason for delay.
questions.source_excerpt: The College aims to comply with requests for access to personal information as quickly as possible but will ensure that it is provided within 30 calendar days unless there is a good reason for delay.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, how should an individual submit a request to exercise any of their data protection rights?
options: In writing to their head of department, on the signed College request form
Directly to the ICO, which will then forward the request to the College
To the Data Protection Officer, who will accept it verbally or in writing
Through their line manager or course tutor, as a signed written statement
questions.explanation: The policy states that requests to exercise individual rights are submitted to the Data Protection Officer and can be made either verbally or in writing.
questions.source_excerpt: Individuals wishing to exercise any of their rights should do so by submitting a request to the Data Protection Officer (Email: dpo@lcc.ac.uk). This can be done either verbally or in writing.

questions.question: You write a handwritten sticky note recording your opinion of an identifiable student's behaviour in class. According to the Data Protection Policy, is this personal data?
options: Yes, opinions about an identifiable individual are included in personal data
No, the policy covers information held electronically, not paper notes
No, opinions are excluded; the definition covers statements of fact
No, a handwritten note becomes personal data once it is scanned or filed
questions.explanation: The policy defines personal data as including any expression of opinion about an identifiable living individual, and lists handwritten notes and sticky notes as examples.
questions.source_excerpt: Any personal information which relates to a living individual who can be identified. This includes any expression of opinion about the individual. ... Emails, file notes, handwritten notes, sticky notes

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, which of the following is an example of special category personal data that needs more protection?
options: An individual's trade union membership
An individual's name and home address
An individual's employment or education history
An individual's date of birth
questions.explanation: The policy lists trade union membership among the examples of special category personal data; name, address, date of birth and employment history are listed only as ordinary personal data.
questions.source_excerpt: Special category personal data is data which the GDPR identifies as more sensitive, and so needs more protection. For example, information about an individual's: ... trade union membership;

questions.question: A former student asks the DPO to erase all their records, including data the College must keep to comply with awarding body regulations. Under the Data Protection Policy, which statement is correct?
options: All records, including awarding body data, must be erased within 72 hours
Everything must be erased within 30 calendar days, as erasure is an absolute right
The awarding body must approve the erasure before the DPO can act on it
Data needed to comply with awarding body regulations does not have to be erased
questions.explanation: The right to erasure is not absolute, and the College complies within 30 calendar days only where the data is not required to comply with awarding body, government or funding body regulations, so such data does not have to be erased.
questions.source_excerpt: Individuals have the right to have personal data erased. The right is not absolute and only applies in certain circumstances. ... The College will comply within 30 calendar days, provided that the ... data is not required in order to comply with awarding body, government or funding body regulations.

questions.question: A student tells you they are unhappy with how the College has used their personal data and asks how to complain. Under the Data Protection Policy, what should you advise?
options: Go straight to the ICO, as the College cannot handle data complaints
Contact the DPO first; if still dissatisfied, refer the matter to the ICO
Write to the Board of Directors, whose decision on the complaint is final
Raise it with their course tutor, who will decide whether to escalate it
questions.explanation: Data-related complaints go to the DPO in the first instance; if the individual remains dissatisfied, they can refer the matter to the ICO.
questions.source_excerpt: Individuals wishing to make a complaint regarding the security of their data, the use of their data or any other data-related issue, should do so by contacting the DPO in the first instance. ... However, if the individual remains dissatisfied with the College's response or if s/he would like to seek advice, the individual can refer the matter to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).

questions.question: A student tells you they no longer want the College to use their personal data for direct marketing. Under the Data Protection Policy, what is their position?
options: They have an absolute right to stop their data being used for direct marketing
They cannot object, as direct marketing forms part of the College's public task
They must first complain to the ICO, which will then instruct the College to stop
They can object to direct marketing if they also withdraw from their course
questions.explanation: The right to object includes an absolute right to stop personal data being used for direct marketing.
questions.source_excerpt: The GDPR gives individuals the right to object to the processing of their personal data in certain circumstances. This includes an absolute right to stop their data being used for direct marketing.

questions.question: A student asks you for a copy of CCTV footage showing themselves in the College foyer. Under the Data Protection Policy, how should this request be handled?
options: Show them the footage at reception straight away, since it is their own image
Explain that CCTV footage is not personal data, so it cannot be requested
Ask them to apply in writing to the DPO and provide Proof of Identification
Ask them to make a verbal request to their course tutor, who can release it
questions.explanation: CCTV footage requests must be made in writing to the Data Protection Officer, and the individual must provide Proof of Identification before being permitted access.
questions.source_excerpt: Requests to access or to obtain a copy of any CCTV footage should be made in writing to the Data Protection Officer. Individuals will be required to provide Proof of Identification before they will be permitted to access the footage.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, for how long will recorded CCTV images normally be retained, unless required for evidential purposes or the investigation of crime?
options: No longer than 72 hours from the time of recording
No longer than 21 days from the date of recording
No longer than 30 calendar days from recording
No longer than 12 months from the date of recording
questions.explanation: The CCTV section states recorded images are retained for no longer than 21 days from the date of recording unless required for evidence, crime investigation or otherwise.
questions.source_excerpt: Recorded images will be retained for no longer than 21 days from the date of recording, unless required for evidential purposes or the investigation of crime or otherwise required.

questions.question: Under the Data Protection Policy, which of the following must be included when the College requests consent from an individual?
options: A pre-ticked box recording agreement unless the individual opts out
Information on how the individual can withdraw consent at any time
A statement that consent, once given, cannot later be withdrawn
A list of all special category data the College already holds on them
questions.explanation: Requests for consent must be unambiguous, involve a clear affirmative action, and include information on how the individual can withdraw consent at any time.
questions.source_excerpt: When seeking consent from an Individual, the College will always ensure that it is unambiguous and that it involves a clear affirmative action by the Individual. Requests for consent shall include: ... Information to the Individual on how to withdraw their consent at any time

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, what is the College's position on consent and enrolment?
options: Consent to direct marketing must be given before enrolment is confirmed
Consent may be made a precondition of enrolment if the DPO approves it
Enrolment may be withdrawn if a student withdraws their consent
Consent shall never be a precondition to enrolment at the College
questions.explanation: The Consent section states plainly that consent shall never be a precondition to enrolment at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Consent shall never be a precondition to enrolment at the College.

questions.question: Under the Data Protection Policy, what are department heads responsible for?
options: Reporting any data breach in their area directly to the ICO within 30 calendar days
Approving every subject access and erasure request relating to their department
Ensuring their staff abide by the policy and reporting potential breaches to the DPO
Monitoring the policy's implementation and reporting to the Principal's Executive Group
questions.explanation: Department heads must ensure their staff abide by the Data Protection Policy and report any potential data breach to the DPO; monitoring implementation is the DPO's role.
questions.source_excerpt: Department heads are responsible for ensuring that their staff abide by the Data Protection Policy and must report to the DPO if any potential Data Breach has occurred.

questions.question: Does the Data Protection Policy set expectations for contractors who process personal information on behalf of the College?
options: No, it applies only to staff directly employed under a College contract
No, contractors follow their own employer's policy and not this one
Yes, contractors are listed alongside staff, students and partner staff
Only where the contractor has access to special category personal data
questions.explanation: The policy's aim states that its expectations apply to all College staff, students, contractors, partnership organisations and partner staff who process personal information on the College's behalf.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy sets out the expectations that all College staff, students, contractors, partnership organisations and partner staff who process or use any personal information on behalf of the College are subject to

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, are individuals who have left the College, or whose application to it was unsuccessful, covered by the policy?
options: Yes, the policy covers all individuals, including both of these groups
No, coverage ends on the date they leave or their application is rejected
Leavers are covered, but data on unsuccessful applicants is excluded
Only for 21 days after they leave or their application is rejected
questions.explanation: The definition of the Individual states that all individuals, including those who have left the College or whose application was unsuccessful, are covered by the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: All Individuals, including those who have left the College or whose application to the College has been unsuccessful, shall be covered by this policy.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, to whom does the College limit access to personal data?
options: Any member of staff working in the same department as the individual
All staff who hold a College network account and email address
Managers at head of department level or above, on request
Only those who require it for legitimate purposes
questions.explanation: The policy states that access to personal data is limited to only those who require it for legitimate purposes.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that access to personal data is limited to only those who require it for legitimate purposes.

questions.question: Under the Data Protection Policy, who is responsible for ensuring the College does not collect information that is not strictly necessary for the purpose for which it is obtained?
options: Each head of department
The Data Protection Officer
The IT department
The Principal's Executive Group
questions.explanation: The policy gives the Data Protection Officer responsibility for ensuring the College does not collect information that is not strictly necessary.
questions.source_excerpt: The Data Protection Officer is responsible for ensuring that the College does not collect information that is not strictly necessary for the purpose for which it is obtained.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, what may follow if a member of staff breaches the policy?
options: Disciplinary action, with any criminal offence reported to the authorities
An informal note on file only, as breaches are treated as training needs
A fine deducted from salary, with the amount set by the Data Protection Officer
A referral to the ICO, which alone decides whether any action can be taken
questions.explanation: A staff breach of the policy may lead to disciplinary action and may also be a criminal offence, in which case it will be reported to the appropriate authorities.
questions.source_excerpt: Any breach of the Policy by a staff member may lead to disciplinary policy and may also be a criminal offence, in which case the matter will be reported as soon as possible to the appropriate authorities.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, in what manner shall all processing of personal data be completed?
options: In a prompt, efficient and consistent manner
In an anonymised, centralised and automated manner
In a lawful, fair and transparent manner
In a cost-effective, timely and documented manner
questions.explanation: The Grounds for Data Processing section states that all processing of personal data shall be lawful, fair and transparent.
questions.source_excerpt: All processing of Personal Data shall be completed in a lawful, fair and transparent manner.

questions.question: Under the Data Protection Policy, when does the College seek an individual's consent before processing their data?
options: Before any processing needed to meet government or funding body regulations
Only when their data is to be shared with a law enforcement agency
Only after processing has begun, within 30 calendar days of it starting
Before processing that cannot be considered part of its public authority duty
questions.explanation: The College seeks consent before any processing that cannot be considered part of its duty as a public authority, such as direct marketing.
questions.source_excerpt: The College seeks the consent of the individual whom the data concerns, before completing any processing that cannot be considered part of its duty as a public authority.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, where can individuals find clear information on how their data is processed, who it is shared with and how long it is stored?
options: In the student handbook issued at the start of each intake
In the Privacy Policy, available on the College website
In the College prospectus sent to every applicant
In the ICO's public register of data controllers
questions.explanation: Under the right to be informed, this information is included in the Privacy Policy, which is available on the College website.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will provide all individuals with clear and concise information about how their data will be processed, the purpose for its collection, who it will be shared with and how long it will be stored for. This information is included in the Privacy Policy, which is available on the College website.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, to which data does the right to data portability apply?
options: Data the College processes with the individual's consent
Data the College processes in its role as a public authority
Special category data only, such as health or religion
All personal data held, including recorded CCTV images
questions.explanation: The right to data portability only applies to data processed with the individual's consent, not to data the College processes as a public authority.
questions.source_excerpt: The right only applies to data that the College is processing with the Individual's consent but does not apply to data that the College processes as a public authority.

questions.question: Under the Data Protection Policy, if the College decides it has grounds to continue processing after an individual objects, what shall it do?
options: Refer the objection to the Board of Directors for a final ruling
Erase the data within 30 calendar days, whatever the grounds
Inform the individual of their right to submit a complaint to the ICO
Ask the individual to confirm the objection in writing to HR
questions.explanation: Where the College determines it has grounds to continue processing, it shall inform the individual of their right to submit a complaint to the ICO.
questions.source_excerpt: If the College determines that it has grounds to continue processing, then it shall inform the Individual of their right to submit a complaint to the ICO.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, which of the following must the College not do when it supplies CCTV footage?
options: Supply it to a law enforcement agency assisting a specific criminal enquiry
Supply it to an insurance company or that company's legal representatives
Supply a copy to the person shown once they give Proof of Identification
Disclose personal data of any other individual who appears in the footage
questions.explanation: When supplying footage the College must not disclose any personal data of another individual, which may involve blurring; the other options are permitted by the CCTV section.
questions.source_excerpt: By supplying the footage, the College must not disclose any personal data of another Individual. This may involve blurring parts of the footage.

questions.question: Under the Data Protection Policy's Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) requirements, when should a personal device used for College work lock?
options: At the end of each working day, via a scheduled setting
Automatically, when inactive for more than a few minutes
Only when it is connected to a public or shared Wi-Fi network
When the IT department sends it a remote lock command
questions.explanation: The BYOD requirements tell staff to set their device to lock automatically when it is inactive for more than a few minutes.
questions.source_excerpt: Set your device to lock automatically when the device is inactive for more than a few minutes.

questions.question: According to the Data Protection Policy, what is the general rule on how long the College may keep personal information about applicants, students or staff?
options: For six years after the individual's last contact with the College
Indefinitely, unless the individual submits a request for erasure
No longer than is required for the purpose for which it is held
For 21 days, the same period that applies to CCTV recordings
questions.explanation: The College is not permitted to keep personal information of applicants, students or staff for longer than is required for its purpose, subject to the Data Retention Schedule.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is not permitted to keep personal information of either applicants, students or staff for longer than is required for its purpose.

questions.question: According to the Data Breaches section of the Data Protection Policy, if a breach is likely to adversely affect individuals' rights and freedoms, when shall those individuals be informed?
options: Within 30 calendar days
After the ICO investigates
At the next policy review
Without undue delay
questions.explanation: The Data Breaches section states that where a breach is likely to adversely affect individuals' rights and freedoms, those individuals shall be informed without undue delay.
questions.source_excerpt: If the breach is likely to adversely affect individuals' rights and freedoms, the individuals concerned shall be informed without undue delay.

questions.question: You record the name and work email address of a named contact at a partner organisation in a College spreadsheet. Under the Data Protection Policy's definitions, is that contact an individual covered by the policy?
options: No, people acting in a business capacity fall outside the policy's definition
Yes, an individual is covered whether in a personal or a business capacity
No, only the College's own students, staff and applicants count as individuals
Only once the partner has signed a data sharing agreement with the College
questions.explanation: The policy defines the Individual as any living individual who is the subject of personal data, whether in a personal or business capacity, so a named business contact is covered.
questions.source_excerpt: Any living individual who is the subject of personal data whether in a personal or business capacity.

questions.question: The College plans to use students' fingerprint scans to confirm their identity at exam entry. How does the Data Protection Policy classify this data?
options: Ordinary personal data, in the same way as a name and address
Not personal data unless it is stored alongside the student's name
Exempt data, because it is collected under the College's public task
Special category personal data, which needs more protection
questions.explanation: Biometrics used for ID purposes are listed as special category personal data, which the GDPR identifies as more sensitive and so needing more protection.
questions.source_excerpt: Special category personal data is data which the GDPR identifies as more sensitive, and so needs more protection. For example, information about an individual's: ... biometrics (where used for ID purposes);

questions.question: A new member of staff asks whether the College needs their separate consent to process the personal information it requires for its statutory obligations. What does the Data Protection Policy say?
options: No, agreeing to this processing is a condition of staff employment at the College
Yes, consent is the College's main lawful ground for processing any staff data
Yes, written consent must be collected before any staff data is processed
No, staff data is covered by separate HR policies and not by this policy
questions.explanation: Under the Public Task ground, it is a condition of staff employment (and of student enrolment) that they agree to the College processing certain personal information as part of its statutory obligations.
questions.source_excerpt: It is a condition of student enrolment and of staff employment that they agree to the College processing certain personal information as part of its statutory obligations.

questions.question: A consent form is being drafted for a joint campaign with a partner organisation that will also rely on the consent collected. Under the Data Protection Policy, which item must the form include?
options: The partner's written promise that it will not pass the data to anyone else
The partner's ICO registration number and its data officer's name
The partner's name, identified as a third-party controller of the data
A declaration that the individual gives up the right to withdraw consent later
questions.explanation: Requests for consent must name any third-party controllers who will rely on the consent, alongside an explanation of why the data is wanted and how consent can be withdrawn.
questions.source_excerpt: Requests for consent shall include: ... the name of any third-party controllers who will rely on the consent;

questions.question: You are taking down applicants' contact details at a College open day. Under the Data Protection Policy, when must these individuals be directed to the College's Privacy Policy?
options: Only if they later ask how their data is being processed
When they enrol, after their application has been accepted
Within 30 calendar days of their details being recorded
At the time when their personal data is being collected
questions.explanation: Under the right to be informed, all individuals will be directed to the Privacy Policy at the time when their personal data is collected.
questions.source_excerpt: All individuals will be directed to the Privacy Policy at the time when their personal data is collected.

questions.question: A student notices their College record shows their home address without the flat number they supplied. Under the Data Protection Policy, which right lets them have the record completed?
options: The right to rectification
The right to data portability
The right to restrict processing
The right of access to their data
questions.explanation: The right to rectification lets individuals have inaccurate personal data rectified, or completed if it is incomplete.
questions.source_excerpt: The GDPR includes a right for individuals to have inaccurate personal data rectified or completed if it is incomplete.

questions.question: The College no longer needs a former student's personal data, but the student asks for it to be kept because they need it to defend a legal claim. Under the Data Protection Policy, which right covers this request?
options: The right to erasure of personal data
The right to data portability
The right to restrict processing
The right to object to processing
questions.explanation: Individuals can ask the College to restrict processing where it no longer needs the data but the individual needs it kept to establish, exercise or defend a legal claim.
questions.source_excerpt: the College no longer needs the personal data, but the individual needs the College to keep it in order to establish, exercise or defend a legal claim

questions.question: A student asks the College to transfer personal data they provided with their consent straight to another organisation. Under the Data Protection Policy's right to data portability, what can they request?
options: That it is first printed and handed to them, so that they can pass it on in person
That it is sent directly to the other controller in a machine-readable format
That the ICO transfers it on behalf of both the College and the other controller
That only a summary is sent, as the original records can never leave the College
questions.explanation: Data portability gives individuals the right to receive their data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and to ask for it to be transmitted directly to another controller.
questions.source_excerpt: The right to data portability gives individuals the right to receive personal data they have provided to a controller in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format. It also gives them the right to request that a controller transmits this data directly to another controller.

questions.question: A student emails the DPO a one-line objection to the College processing their personal data for a purpose other than direct marketing. Under the Data Protection Policy, what is expected of them?
options: Nothing more, as an objection stops all processing within 30 calendar days
They must first take the objection to the ICO before the College can act
They must get written support from their course tutor or a line manager
They must give specific reasons for objecting, based on their own situation
questions.explanation: Outside direct marketing, an individual must give specific reasons for objecting, based on their situation; the College may then continue only if compelling legitimate grounds override their interests.
questions.source_excerpt: An individual must give specific reasons why they object to the processing of their data. These reasons should be based upon their situation.

questions.question: Several outside parties ask the College for CCTV footage of an incident in its building. Under the Data Protection Policy, which of these third-party requesters meets the criteria for access?
options: A legal representative acting on behalf of a prosecution agency
A solicitor acting for a neighbouring business in a civil dispute
A local newspaper reporting on the incident in the public interest
A parent of a student who appears in the recorded footage
questions.explanation: Third-party access to CCTV footage is limited to law enforcement agencies (for a specific criminal enquiry), prosecution agencies and their legal representatives, and insurance companies and their legal representatives.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will provide access to CCTV footage to Third Parties if the requestor satisfies the following criteria ... Prosecution Agencies and their Legal Representatives

questions.question: You are replacing the personal phone you have used for College work. Under the Data Protection Policy's BYOD requirements, what must you do with the College information on the old phone?
options: Hand the old phone to the IT department, who will keep it for 21 days
Transfer it to the new phone and keep the old one locked as a backup
Securely delete all non-published College information from the old phone
Encrypt the old phone and keep it until you leave the College's employment
questions.explanation: When you stop using a device, for example because you have replaced it, the BYOD requirements say you must securely delete all non-published College information from it.
questions.source_excerpt: When you stop using your device (for example because you have replaced it) and when you leave the College's employment, securely delete all (non-published) College information from your device.

questions.question: A colleague says all of a student's personal data must be deleted as soon as they complete their course. Under the Data Protection Policy's data retention rules, is this correct?
options: Yes, the College may keep no personal data once a student's course has ended
No, some is kept longer to comply with statutory or funding body requirements
No, all of it is kept for 21 days and is then securely destroyed by IT staff
Yes, unless the student gives written consent for their data to be retained
questions.explanation: Although personal data may not be kept longer than its purpose requires, some data will be kept longer or in perpetuity to comply with statutory or funding body requirements, under the Data Retention Schedule.
questions.source_excerpt: some data will be kept longer or in perpetuity to comply with statutory or funding body requirements in accordance with the Data Retention Schedule.

questions.question: The DPO finds that one department is repeatedly not following the Data Protection Policy. Under the policy's monitoring arrangements, to whom will the DPO report this?
options: The Board of Directors
The Principal's Executive Group
The Information Commissioner's Office
The Academic Board
questions.explanation: The DPO monitors implementation of the policy and will report to the Principal's Executive Group if the policy is not being followed.
questions.source_excerpt: The DPO is responsible for monitoring the implementation of this policy and will report to the Principal's Executive Group if the policy is not being followed or to bid for further resources.

questions.question: A CCTV camera records a distant, blurred figure crossing the College car park, and no one could be identified from the footage. Under the Data Protection Policy, is this recording personal data?
options: Yes, every CCTV recording made on College premises counts as personal data
No, it is personal data only where an individual can be identified from it
Yes, CCTV footage is listed in the policy as special category personal data
No, CCTV recordings fall under a separate CCTV policy and never under this one
questions.explanation: The policy treats CCTV footage as personal data only where an individual can be identified from it; images showing a recognisable person are covered by the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: CCTV footage if an individual can be identified from the ... CCTV images that show a recognisable person are considered personal data and are therefore covered by this Data Protection Policy.

questions.question: A funding body regulation requires the College to report the ethnic origin of its enrolled students. Under the Data Protection Policy, how should staff treat this data?
options: As special category data, which the College may process to meet funding body regulations
As ordinary personal data, since ethnic origin is not listed as needing extra protection
As special category data that may be processed only after each student gives separate consent
As data the College must never hold, since ethnic origin cannot be collected by a college
questions.explanation: Ethnic origin is special category personal data, and the Public Task section states the College may process such data where it is required to comply with government or funding body regulations, so separate consent is not needed.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, information about an individual's: ... ethnic origin; ... the College may also process some information that is categorised as "special category personal data". This information may be required to comply with certain government or funding body regulations.

questions.question: Out of curiosity, a member of staff opens a student's record that they have no work reason to view, and tells no one. Under the Data Protection Policy, how should this be viewed?
options: Not a breach, because no data was lost, altered or disclosed outside the College
A breach only if the staff member later shares what they saw with another person
Not a breach, because staff with system access may view any record they can open
A breach, since access is limited to legitimate purposes; discipline may follow
questions.explanation: Access to personal data is limited to those who need it for legitimate purposes, unauthorised access is part of the breach definition whether accidental or deliberate, and a staff breach may lead to disciplinary action.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that access to personal data is limited to only those who require it for legitimate purposes. ... Any breach of the Policy by a staff member may lead to disciplinary policy ... unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. This includes breaches that are the result of both accidental and deliberate causes.

questions.question: A draft online enrolment form has a pre-ticked box agreeing to marketing emails, and students cannot submit the form unless it stays ticked. Under the Data Protection Policy, what is wrong with this design?
options: Nothing, as marketing emails form part of the College's public authority duty
Only that the box must start unticked; it may still be required for enrolment
Consent needs clear affirmative action and can never be required for enrolment
Nothing, provided a link to the Privacy Policy is shown right beside the ticked box
questions.explanation: Consent must be unambiguous and involve a clear affirmative action, which a pre-ticked box is not, and consent shall never be a precondition to enrolment.
questions.source_excerpt: When seeking consent from an Individual, the College will always ensure that it is unambiguous and that it involves a clear affirmative action by the Individual. ... Consent shall never be a precondition to enrolment at the College.

questions.question: A department wants to use enrolled students' contact details to send them promotional emails about other short courses. Under the Data Protection Policy, what is needed first?
options: Nothing more, as agreeing to data processing was a condition of their enrolment
Their consent, as direct marketing is outside the College's public authority duty
Written approval from the ICO, which regulates all marketing sent to students
Sign-off from the head of department, who ensures staff abide by the policy
questions.explanation: Enrolment covers processing for the College's statutory obligations; processing outside its public authority duty, such as direct marketing, needs the individual's consent first.
questions.source_excerpt: The College seeks the consent of the individual whom the data concerns, before completing any processing that cannot be considered part of its duty as a public authority. This may include the consent to receive Direct Marketing.

questions.question: A student phones the DPO asking for a copy of their student record and for CCTV footage showing them in the library. Under the Data Protection Policy, which statement is correct?
options: Both requests are valid by phone, since any right may be exercised verbally
Neither request is valid until the student puts it in writing to the DPO
The footage request may be verbal, but the record request must be in writing
The record request may be verbal, but the footage request must be in writing
questions.explanation: Requests to exercise individual rights can be made verbally or in writing, but requests for CCTV footage should be made in writing to the DPO, with Proof of Identification.
questions.source_excerpt: Individuals wishing to exercise any of their rights should do so by submitting a request to the Data Protection Officer (Email: dpo@lcc.ac.uk). This can be done either verbally or in writing. ... Requests to access or to obtain a copy of any CCTV footage should be made in writing to the Data Protection Officer.

questions.question: The College discovers it has processed a student's personal data unlawfully. The student opposes erasure but wants the data's use limited. Under the Data Protection Policy, which option is available to them?
options: Ask the College to restrict processing, which the policy allows when erasure is opposed
Nothing, since the policy requires unlawfully processed data to be erased in every case
Ask for data portability, which obliges the College to stop using the data
Ask for rectification, which covers any data that has been processed unlawfully
questions.explanation: One of the listed grounds for restricting processing is that the data has been unlawfully processed and the individual opposes erasure and requests restriction instead.
questions.source_excerpt: Individuals have the right to request that the College restricts the processing of their personal data in the following circumstances: ... the data has been unlawfully processed and the individual opposes ... erasure and requests restriction instead

questions.question: A member of staff has objected to the College processing their data, and the College is still considering whether its legitimate grounds override theirs. Under the Data Protection Policy, what may the individual request meanwhile?
options: That the College transmits the data to another controller while it decides
That the ICO takes over the decision on whether the processing can continue
That the College restricts processing of their data while it considers this
That the data is erased at once, since any objection stops processing outright
questions.explanation: The right to restrict processing applies where the individual has objected and the College is considering whether its legitimate grounds override those of the individual.
questions.source_excerpt: the individual has objected to the College processing their data and the ... College is considering whether it has legitimate grounds that override those of ... the individual.

questions.question: A student asks for a machine-readable copy of both their marketing preferences, given with consent, and the attendance records the College keeps as a public authority. Under the Data Protection Policy, what does the right to data portability cover?
options: Both sets of data, as portability covers all personal data the student provided
The attendance records only, as data held as a public authority must be portable
Neither set, as portability applies only to special category personal data
The marketing preferences only, as portability covers consent-based processing
questions.explanation: Data portability applies only to data the College processes with the individual's consent, not to data it processes as a public authority.
questions.source_excerpt: The right only applies to data that the College is processing with the Individual's consent but does not apply to data that the College processes as a public authority.
