questions.question: CCTV footage of a theft on College premises is needed for a police investigation expected to last several weeks. Under the Data Protection Policy, what happens to the usual CCTV retention limit?
options: It still applies, so the footage must be deleted 21 days after recording
It does not apply where footage is needed to investigate a crime
It is extended to 30 calendar days, in line with the deadline for access requests
It can be lifted only if everyone shown in the footage gives written consent
questions.explanation: Recorded images are kept for no longer than 21 days unless required for evidential purposes or the investigation of crime, so this footage can be kept longer.
questions.source_excerpt: Recorded images will be retained for no longer than 21 days from the date of recording, unless required for evidential purposes or the investigation of crime or otherwise required.

questions.question: Police request CCTV footage that would assist a specific criminal enquiry. The footage also shows several students with no link to the incident. Under the Data Protection Policy, how should the College respond?
options: Refuse, as footage showing students can be released only with their consent
Supply the footage unedited, as law enforcement requests are exempt from the policy
Supply it without disclosing the other students' personal data, e.g. by blurring
Supply it only after each student shown has made a written request to the DPO
questions.explanation: Law enforcement agencies meet the third-party criteria where the images would assist a specific criminal enquiry, but the College must not disclose other individuals' personal data, which may involve blurring.
questions.source_excerpt: Law enforcement agencies (where the images recorded would assist in a specific criminal enquiry) ... By supplying the footage, the College must not disclose any personal data of another Individual. This may involve blurring parts of the footage.

questions.question: An external examiner will review student work containing personal data on their own laptop. Under the Data Protection Policy, do the Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) protection requirements extend to them?
options: No, the BYOD requirements apply only to staff employed under a College contract
Yes, they include visitors such as external examiners given access to personal data
No, external examiners are bound only by their own institution's data policies
Only if the IT department has first installed College software on the examiner's own laptop
questions.explanation: The BYOD section states that its protection requirement includes visitors, such as external examiners or reviewers, who might receive access to personal data.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff wishing to use their own device for College work must ensure that any personal data of the College that is stored on their device is appropriately protected. This includes visitors (such as external examiners or reviewers) who might receive access to personal data.

questions.question: Under the Data Protection Policy's Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) requirements, which of the following is not permitted for a member of staff using their own phone for College work?
options: Letting a household member use the phone through a separate account with its own passcode
Using a PIN number as the phone's passcode, choosing a strong one wherever possible
Asking the IT department for help to meet the BYOD requirements set out in the policy
Telling a trusted family member the passcode so they can use the phone in an emergency
questions.explanation: The BYOD requirements say never to share the passcode with anyone; a PIN is an accepted passcode, household use is allowed with an additional account passcode, and staff may seek IT help.
questions.source_excerpt: Set and use a passcode (e.g. pin number or password) to access your device. Whenever possible, use a strong passcode. Do not share the passcode with anyone.

questions.question: A colleague says that because the personal phone they use for College work has a strong passcode, encrypting it is unnecessary. Under the Data Protection Policy's BYOD requirements, why is this wrong?
options: Encryption blocks access even if the storage chips are moved to another device
Encryption lets the DPO recover the College data if the device is lost or stolen
Encryption removes the need to report a lost device to the DPO straight away
Encryption lets household members share the device without an extra passcode
questions.explanation: Encryption is a separate BYOD requirement, intended to prevent access even if someone extracts the storage chips or disks and puts them in another device.
questions.source_excerpt: Encrypt the device (to prevent access even if someone extracts the storage chips or disks and houses them in another device)

questions.question: You are clearing a cabinet of old applicant files. Some are no longer needed for their purpose; others must be kept for funding body requirements under the Data Retention Schedule. Under the Data Protection Policy, what should you do?
options: Keep all of the files in perpetuity, as applicant records are exempt from retention limits
Destroy all of the files, as applicant data can never be kept once admissions close
Keep those the Schedule requires and securely destroy the rest in line with best practice
Scan all of the files, then put the paper originals in the general office recycling
questions.explanation: Personal data may not be kept longer than its purpose requires, except where the Data Retention Schedule requires it for statutory or funding body reasons, and destroyed data must be destroyed securely in line with best practice.
questions.source_excerpt: some data will be kept longer or in perpetuity to comply with statutory or funding body requirements in accordance with the Data Retention Schedule. ... When data held in accordance with this policy is destroyed, it must be destroyed securely in accordance with best practice at the time of destruction.

questions.question: A department head learns that a team member has emailed a class list to the wrong external address. Under the Data Protection Policy, what should the department head do, and what deadline applies to reporting it to the ICO?
options: Report it to the DPO; the College should tell the ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware
Report it directly to the ICO; the College then has 30 calendar days to inform the students
Log it within the department; the ICO is told only if a student complains within 21 days
Report it to the Principal's Executive Group, which tells the ICO within 7 working days
questions.explanation: Department heads must report any potential data breach to the DPO, and the College reports potential breaches to the ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware, where feasible.
questions.source_excerpt: Department heads are responsible for ensuring that their staff abide by the Data Protection Policy and must report to the DPO if any potential Data Breach has occurred. ... The College shall report to ICO any potential data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, where feasible.

questions.question: A student has made no complaint but wants to speak to someone outside the College about how the College uses their data. Under the Data Protection Policy, can they contact the ICO?
options: No, the ICO can be contacted only after the DPO has given a final response
No, only the College itself may refer data protection matters to the ICO
Yes, an individual may refer a matter to the ICO to seek advice
Only if the DPO first gives written permission for the matter to go to the ICO
questions.explanation: Besides remaining dissatisfied with the College's response, an individual who would like to seek advice can refer the matter to the ICO.
questions.source_excerpt: However, if the individual remains dissatisfied with the College's response or if s/he would like to seek advice, the individual can refer the matter to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).

questions.question: A department's course feedback form asks students for their religion and home address, although neither is needed for the feedback. Under the Data Protection Policy, what is the problem?
options: None, provided the form links to the Privacy Policy at the point of collection
None, provided the answers are deleted within 21 days of the form being returned
Only the religion question is a problem, as a home address is not personal data
It collects information that is not strictly necessary for the purpose
questions.explanation: The DPO must ensure the College does not collect information that is not strictly necessary for the purpose for which it is obtained; a home address is ordinary personal data and religion is special category data.
questions.source_excerpt: The Data Protection Officer is responsible for ensuring that the College does not collect information that is not strictly necessary for the purpose for which it is obtained.

questions.question: An applicant whose application to the College was unsuccessful asks the DPO for a copy of the personal information the College holds about them. Under the Data Protection Policy, how should the request be treated?
options: As outside the policy, which covers only currently enrolled students and employed staff members
As a valid request, to be met within 30 calendar days unless there is good reason for delay
As invalid, since the data of unsuccessful applicants is automatically deleted after 21 days
As valid only if the applicant reapplies to the College and is then accepted onto a course
questions.explanation: The policy covers all individuals, including unsuccessful applicants, and access requests are met within 30 calendar days unless there is a good reason for delay.
questions.source_excerpt: All Individuals, including those who have left the College or whose application to the College has been unsuccessful, shall be covered by this policy. ... will ensure that it is provided within 30 calendar days unless there is a good reason for delay.

questions.question: A Brand Advocate who promotes College courses asks whether data protection forms part of what they have agreed to. Under the Data Protection Policy, what is correct?
options: Yes, their agreement's Terms and Conditions include Data Protection
No, data protection duties apply only to College employees, not Brand Advocates
Only after they attend a breach briefing that the DPO runs following an incident
Yes, but they are bound only by ICO rules and not by any agreement with the College
questions.explanation: The Brand Advocate agreement's Terms and Conditions include Data Protection, and the workshops held during each admission intake act as a refresher on them.
questions.source_excerpt: These are also used as a refresher session for the Terms and Conditions of the Brand Advocate agreement, which include Data Protection.

questions.question: A student objects to receiving direct marketing and, giving specific reasons based on their situation, to a separate non-marketing use of their data. The College believes it has compelling legitimate grounds for both. Under the Data Protection Policy, what is correct?
options: It must stop the direct marketing; the other use may continue if its grounds override
It may continue both, as compelling legitimate grounds override any kind of objection
It must stop both, as an objection supported by specific reasons ends all processing
It may keep the direct marketing but must pause the other use until the ICO decides
questions.explanation: The right to object includes an absolute right to stop direct marketing, whereas for other processing the College may continue if compelling legitimate grounds override the individual's interests, rights and freedoms.
questions.source_excerpt: This includes an absolute right to stop their data being used for direct marketing. ... An individual must give specific reasons why they object to the processing of their data. ... In these circumstances the College may continue processing if there are compelling legitimate grounds for the processing, which override the interests, rights and freedoms of the individual.

questions.question: The police ask the College for all CCTV footage from the past fortnight to analyse general crime trends in the neighbourhood; no particular incident is being investigated. Under the Data Protection Policy, does this request meet the criteria for third-party access to CCTV footage?
options: Yes, as all of the footage requested is still within the 21-day retention period
No, as only prosecution agencies and insurers, not the police, may be given footage
No, as police access applies where the images would assist a specific criminal enquiry
Yes, once the officers apply in writing to the DPO and provide Proof of Identification
questions.explanation: Law enforcement agencies meet the third-party criteria only where the recorded images would assist in a specific criminal enquiry, so a general request does not qualify; the 21-day limit and the writing and ID rule do not create an entitlement.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will provide access to CCTV footage to Third Parties if the requestor satisfies the following criteria ... Law enforcement agencies (where the images recorded would assist in a specific criminal enquiry)

questions.question: An applicant wants to enrol but refuses to agree to the College processing the personal information it needs for its statutory obligations, and also refuses consent to direct marketing. Under the Data Protection Policy, what is correct?
options: Agreeing to the statutory processing is a condition of enrolment; marketing consent is not
Neither refusal can affect enrolment, because consent can never be a precondition to it
Marketing consent is a condition of enrolment; the statutory processing needs no agreement
Both are conditions of enrolment, so the applicant cannot enrol while refusing either one
questions.explanation: Agreeing to the College processing certain personal information for its statutory obligations is a condition of student enrolment, whereas consent, such as to direct marketing, shall never be a precondition to enrolment.
questions.source_excerpt: It is a condition of student enrolment and of staff employment that they agree to the College processing certain personal information as part of its statutory obligations. ... Consent shall never be a precondition to enrolment at the College.

questions.question: According to the Equality and Diversity Policy, to whom does the policy apply?
options: Permanent full-time staff and enrolled students, with visitors and contractors falling outside its scope
Academic staff and students, but not professional services staff, visitors or on-site contractors
All staff with a contract of employment (full-time and part-time), students, visitors and contractors
Students and applicants, with staff covered separately under the College's HR policy framework
questions.explanation: The scope section states the policy applies to all staff with a contract of employment (full-time and part-time), all students, visitors and contractors working at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy applies to all members of London Churchill College, including: ... All members of staff in possession of a contract of employment including full-time and part time staff. ... All London Churchill College students. ... London Churchill College visitors. ... Contractors working at London Churchill College.

questions.question: An hourly paid lecturer tells you they need a reasonable adjustment at work because of a health condition. What does the Equality and Diversity Policy say about this?
options: Reasonable adjustment covers permanent staff, so hourly paid lecturers cannot be offered one
They should request it from the Academic Department, which approves staff and student adjustments
They should apply through Student Support under the Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy
Reasonable adjustment applies to them, and they should seek advice from the HR department
questions.explanation: The policy states reasonable adjustment applies to both permanent and hourly paid staff, and that staff requiring it should seek advice from the HR department.
questions.source_excerpt: Reasonable adjustment also applies to members of staff, both permanent and hourly paid. Staff requiring reasonable adjustment should seek advice from the HR department.

questions.question: The Equality and Diversity Policy lists the grounds on which no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor or member of staff should be treated unfavourably. Which of the following is included in that list?
options: Being an ex-offender
Prior academic attainment
Length of service
Choice of study mode
questions.explanation: Alongside the legally protected characteristics, the policy explicitly lists trade union activity, social class and being an ex-offender.
questions.source_excerpt: The College seeks to take every step to ensure that no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, disability, ... trade union activity, social class or being an ex-offender.

questions.question: A new student has declared a disability during enrolment. According to the Equality and Diversity Policy, what should happen next?
options: The student is contacted and invited to meet to discuss the additional support the College can provide
No action is taken until the student submits a formal written request for additional learning support
The student is automatically exempted from attendance and punctuality requirements for the year
The student is referred to an external agency for a needs assessment before any support is discussed
questions.explanation: The policy states that students with declared disabilities are contacted and invited to meet and discuss the additional support the College can provide.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with declared disabilities are contacted and invited to meet and discuss the additional support that the College can provide them.

questions.question: According to the Equality and Diversity Policy, how are learning opportunities made equally accessible to all students?
options: By providing separate specialist classes and learning materials for any student who declares a disability
By inclusive design wherever possible and reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary
By individual adjustments alone, agreed once the student has submitted a formal written request
By reducing assessment requirements and extending deadlines for any student who declares a disability
questions.explanation: The policy states learning opportunities are made equally accessible through inclusive design wherever possible and reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are offered learning opportunities that are equally accessible to them, by means of inclusive design wherever possible and by means of reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary.

questions.question: A colleague believes their request for flexible working was handled unfavourably because of pregnancy and maternity. Which statement correctly reflects the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: The policy's staff protections are limited to recruitment and selection, so flexible working falls outside it
Pregnancy and maternity is listed as a protected ground for students, but not for members of staff
The College's opposition to unlawful discrimination expressly includes requests for flexible working
Flexible working is excluded, as the policy covers pay, promotion and dismissal but not working patterns
questions.explanation: The policy protects members of staff from unfavourable treatment on grounds including pregnancy and maternity, and its opposition to unlawful discrimination expressly includes requests for flexible working.
questions.source_excerpt: no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, ... The College seeks to oppose and avoid all forms of unlawful discrimination. This includes pay and benefits, ... leave for parents, requests for flexible working,

questions.question: A student's disability has affected their attendance at a panel hearing. Under the Equality and Diversity Policy, who should make reasonable adjustments to accommodate their attendance at review meetings?
options: The HR department
The Academic Department
The Quality Assurance Department
The Admissions team
questions.explanation: The policy states the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments for students whose attendance at panel hearings has been affected by disability.
questions.source_excerpt: Similarly, the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments for students whose attendance at panel hearings or other, has been affected by his or her disability to accommodate attendance at review meetings.

questions.question: According to the Equality and Diversity Policy, how may lateness by a student with a disability be treated?
options: Lateness is recorded as unauthorised, with disability considered at a later review
Students with a disability are automatically exempt from lateness rules
Lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis
Lateness may be approved as an adjustment after three late arrivals in a term
questions.explanation: The policy gives lateness as an example of accommodation for students with disabilities, approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis.
questions.source_excerpt: References are made throughout the EIA to ensure that accommodation is made for students with disabilities. For example, lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis.

questions.question: According to the Equality and Diversity Policy, what does the College monitor with reference to protected characteristics so it can act on potential equality and diversity issues?
options: Staff sickness absence rates
Student retention and achievement rates
Student attendance at social and enrichment events
Applicants' previous school examination results
questions.explanation: The monitoring section states the College monitors student retention and achievement rates with reference to protected characteristics and takes action on potential issues.
questions.source_excerpt: We also monitor student retention and achievement rates with reference to protected characteristics and take action to address potential diversity and equality issues.

questions.question: A student explains she could not meet a requirement because she had an antenatal appointment. According to the Equality and Diversity Policy's impact assessment, how is this kind of circumstance allowed for?
options: It is allowed for once a hospital or midwife letter has been supplied as supporting evidence
No allowance applies, as antenatal appointments are treated as unauthorised absence
An allowance applies once she applies for a formal interruption of study
Students may self-certify for antenatal appointments as a reasonable allowance
questions.explanation: The impact assessment makes reasonable allowances for personal circumstances, stating that students may self-certify for antenatal appointments, among other things.
questions.source_excerpt: the EIA anticipates that personal circumstances may affect ability to appeal and makes reasonable allowances for this. For example, students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities.

questions.question: According to the Equality and Diversity Policy, what kind of environment does London Churchill College strive to create in delivering and administering its programmes?
options: An educational environment in which all students and staff are treated equally by one another and can work free of any form of discrimination
A learning environment in which students are protected from discrimination by staff, with staff conduct handled under HR policies alone
A competitive academic environment in which students are selected and progressed solely on merit and on their prior attainment
A working environment in which staff are treated equally, with the treatment of students set out only in the Student Code of Conduct
questions.explanation: The Aim section states the College strives to create an educational environment in which all students and staff are treated equally by one another and can work free of any form of discrimination.
questions.source_excerpt: In delivering and administering its programmes, London Churchill College strives to create an educational environment in which all students and staff are treated equally by one another and can work free of any form of discrimination

questions.question: The Equality and Diversity Policy says the College has put procedures in place to ensure students are protected in all aspects of education. Which aspects does it name as included?
options: Accommodation, catering, and extra-curricular enrichment activities
Timetabling, library access, and graduation and awards ceremonies
Recruitment and selection, teaching, and assessment procedures
Fee payment, bursary awards, and student finance applications
questions.explanation: The Aim section names recruitment and selection, teaching, and assessment procedures as aspects of education in which students are protected.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has put procedures in place to ensure that students are protected in all aspects of education including recruitment and selection, teaching, and assessment procedures.

questions.question: Under the Equality and Diversity Policy, the College seeks to ensure that no one in certain named groups is treated unfavourably. Apart from students, visitors and staff, which groups are named?
options: Alumni and former members of staff
Prospective students and applicants
Students' parents, guardians and sponsors
Staff employed by the College's awarding bodies
questions.explanation: The policy names prospective students and applicants, alongside students, visitors and members of staff, as people who should not be treated unfavourably.
questions.source_excerpt: The College seeks to take every step to ensure that no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably

questions.question: The Equality and Diversity Policy states that the College seeks to oppose and avoid all forms of unlawful discrimination. Which of these employment matters does it expressly say this includes?
options: Allocating office and desk space
Approving staff travel and expense claims
Setting annual teaching timetables
Dealing with grievances and discipline
questions.explanation: The policy expressly lists dealing with grievances and discipline among the employment matters covered by its opposition to unlawful discrimination, alongside pay, dismissal, redundancy and promotion.
questions.source_excerpt: The College seeks to oppose and avoid all forms of unlawful discrimination. This includes pay and benefits, terms, and conditions of employment, dealing with grievances and discipline, dismissal, redundancy,

questions.question: How does the Equality and Diversity Policy say the College actively seeks to tackle any form of harassment, bullying or intimidation?
options: By applying a zero-tolerance rule of exclusion for anyone reported
By requiring all students and staff to complete annual anti-bullying training
By promoting an environment that champions the values of dignity for all
By appointing a named harassment officer within each academic department
questions.explanation: The policy states the College tackles harassment, bullying or intimidation by promoting an environment that champions the values of dignity for all.
questions.source_excerpt: The College actively seeks to tackle any form of harassment, bullying or intimidation through promoting an environment that champions the values of dignity for all.

questions.question: The Equality and Diversity Policy commits the College to abiding by current legislation in discharging its duties. In what manner does it say those duties are discharged?
options: In a fair and transparent manner
In a confidential and proportionate manner
In a timely and cost-effective manner
In a discreet and consistent manner
questions.explanation: The policy states the College is committed to abiding by current legislation in discharging its duties in a fair and transparent manner.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is committed to abiding by current legislation in discharging its duties in a fair and transparent manner.

questions.question: According to the commitments in the Equality and Diversity Policy, why does London Churchill College encourage equality, diversity and inclusion in the College?
options: Because they are a condition of its awarding body partnerships
Because they are required under its student funding arrangements
Because they improve its position in national league tables
Because they are good practice and make business sense
questions.explanation: The first commitment is to encourage equality, diversity and inclusion because they are good practice and make business sense.
questions.source_excerpt: Encourage equality, diversity, and inclusion in the College as they are good practice and make business sense.

questions.question: The Equality and Diversity Policy commits the College to promoting dignity and respect for all. What does it say will be recognised and valued in all staff and students?
options: Their academic achievements and awards
Their individual differences and contributions
Their length of service and seniority level
Their attendance, punctuality and engagement
questions.explanation: The second commitment describes a College where individual differences and the contributions of all staff and students are recognised and valued.
questions.source_excerpt: promoting dignity and respect for all, and where individual differences and the contributions of all staff and students are recognise and valued.

questions.question: The Equality and Diversity Policy directs readers to another document for further information on inclusive design and individual adjustments for students. Which document is it?
options: Inclusive Learning and Individual Adjustments Procedure
Disability Access and Learning Support Code of Practice
Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy
Student Wellbeing and Adjustments Strategy
questions.explanation: The Reasonable Adjustments section states that further information can be read in the Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are offered learning opportunities that are equally accessible to them, by means of inclusive design wherever possible and by means of reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary. ... Further information on this can be read in Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy.

questions.question: The Equality Impact Assessment in the Equality and Diversity Policy states that equitable procedure is a relevant factor in which of the following?
options: Student attainment
Staff promotion
Course validation
Tuition fee setting
questions.explanation: The Equitable Procedure part of the impact assessment states that equitable procedure is a relevant factor in student attainment.
questions.source_excerpt: Equitable procedure is a relevant factor in student attainment.

questions.question: According to the Equality and Diversity Policy, what does the College recognise that its process and procedures for equality and diversity will be at all times?
options: Reviewed each year by the Academic Board and published on the College website
Confidential, managed by the HR department, and available to staff on request
Administered centrally by Quality Assurance and applied on a case-by-case basis
Comprehensive, easy to access and use, and available to all without discrimination
questions.explanation: The policy states the College recognises that its equality and diversity process and procedures will at all times be comprehensive, easy to access and use, and available to all without discrimination.
questions.source_excerpt: The College recognises that at all times the process and procedures for equality and diversity will be comprehensive, easy to access and use and available to all without discrimination.

questions.question: The Equality and Diversity Policy's impact assessment says gender is also relevant to student self-certification. What reason does it give?
options: Female students are more likely than male students to attend medical appointments
More female students than male students are primarily responsible for childcare
More male than female students are in paid work alongside their studies
Female students are more likely than male students to need to interrupt their study
questions.explanation: The impact assessment states gender is relevant to self-certification because more female students than male students are primarily responsible for childcare.
questions.source_excerpt: Gender is also relevant in terms of self-certification, as it is known that more female students than male students are primarily responsible for childcare.

questions.question: According to the impact assessment in the Equality and Diversity Policy, what does the EIA anticipate that personal circumstances may affect, and so make reasonable allowances for?
options: Students' eligibility for funding
Students' choice of programme
Students' ability to appeal
Students' ability to enrol on time
questions.explanation: The impact assessment anticipates that personal circumstances may affect ability to appeal and makes reasonable allowances for this.
questions.source_excerpt: the EIA anticipates that personal circumstances may affect ability to appeal and makes reasonable allowances for this.

questions.question: What conclusion does the impact assessment in the Equality and Diversity Policy reach about negative impact on people who share protected characteristics?
options: It is not likely to have a negative impact on them
It is likely to have a negative impact that is justified
It will have a negative impact on disabled students only
Its impact cannot be judged until monitoring data is held
questions.explanation: The impact assessment concludes that it is not likely that the EIA will have a negative impact on people who share protected characteristics.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not likely that this EIA will have a negative impact on people who share protected characteristics.

questions.question: The impact assessment in the Equality and Diversity Policy says allowing students to self-certify should reduce the potential for negative impact linked to certain characteristics. Which are named?
options: Age, race, sex, and sexual orientation
Social class, being an ex-offender, and trade union activity
Marriage and civil partnership, and gender reassignment
Religion or belief, disability, and pregnancy and maternity
questions.explanation: The impact assessment states self-certification should reduce the potential for negative impact on people as a result of their religion or belief, disability, and/or pregnancy and maternity.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities. This should reduce the potential for negative impact on ... people as a result of their religion or belief, disability, and/or pregnancy and maternity

questions.question: According to the monitoring section of the Equality and Diversity Policy, which of the following will be monitored?
options: Staff attendance at equality and diversity training
Any complaints about the implementation of the process
The number of reasonable adjustments approved each year
Student satisfaction survey results for each programme
questions.explanation: The monitoring section states that any complaints about the implementation of the process will be monitored.
questions.source_excerpt: Any complaints about the implementation of this process will be monitored.

questions.question: In the Equality Impact Assessment section of the Equality and Diversity Policy, what does it mean for a policy, procedure or decision to be equality 'neutral'?
options: It applies only to staff and not to students or to visitors
It can be approved without completing an impact assessment
It will not have a differential impact on any equality group
It has a positive impact on every protected characteristic
questions.explanation: The impact assessment describes equality 'neutral' as meaning the policy, procedure or decision will not have a differential impact on any equality group.
questions.source_excerpt: Or is it clear at this stage that it will be equality "neutral"? will not have a differential impact on any equality group/s?

questions.question: A student makes derogatory remarks about the religion of an electrician contracted to work on the College premises. Does the Equality and Diversity Policy apply to this situation?
options: No, the policy's scope is limited to staff and students, so contractors are covered only by their employer's policy
Yes, the policy applies to all London Churchill College students and to contractors working at the College
Only if the electrician is directly employed by the College on a full-time or part-time contract of employment
Only once the contractor has completed the College's site induction and signed its staff code of conduct
questions.explanation: The scope section states the policy applies to all London Churchill College students and to contractors working at the College, so both people in this situation are within it.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy applies to all members of London Churchill College, including: ... All London Churchill College students. ... Contractors working at London Churchill College.

questions.question: A part-time administrator with a contract of employment believes she was passed over for a training opportunity because of her age. How does the Equality and Diversity Policy apply?
options: It does not apply, as the policy covers full-time staff and part-time staff are dealt with under separate HR terms
It applies to her, but training falls outside the employment matters listed in its anti-discrimination statement
It applies only to recruitment, so training decisions for existing staff are handled under the appraisal process
It covers part-time staff with a contract of employment, and its opposition to unlawful discrimination includes training
questions.explanation: The scope covers staff with a contract of employment, full-time and part-time, and the College's opposition to unlawful discrimination, including on grounds of age, expressly includes training and development opportunities.
questions.source_excerpt: All members of staff in possession of a contract of employment including full-time and part time staff. ... no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, ... This includes pay and benefits, ... promotion, training, or other development opportunities.

questions.question: A lecturer believes she was selected for redundancy because of her trade union activity. Which statement reflects the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: Trade union activity is a listed ground, and redundancy is expressly covered by the policy
Trade union activity is listed only for students, so it gives no protection in staff redundancy decisions
Redundancy is a business decision and falls outside the employment matters the policy expressly lists
The policy covers only characteristics protected by the Equality Act, so union activity is outside it
questions.explanation: Trade union activity is one of the grounds on which no member of staff should be treated unfavourably, and the College's opposition to unlawful discrimination expressly includes redundancy.
questions.source_excerpt: no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, ... trade union activity, social class or being an ex-offender. The College seeks to oppose and avoid all forms of unlawful discrimination. This includes pay and benefits, ... dismissal, redundancy,

questions.question: A student believes their coursework was marked down because of their social class. Under the Equality and Diversity Policy, is this something the College's equality procedures are meant to protect against?
options: No, social class is not one of the grounds the policy lists, as it is not a protected characteristic in law
No, the College's student protections cover recruitment and selection, with marking left to academic judgement
Yes, social class is a listed ground, and the procedures protect students in assessment as well as teaching
Only if the student can first show the marking also breached the College's published assessment regulations
questions.explanation: The policy lists social class among the grounds on which no student should be treated unfavourably, and the College's procedures protect students in all aspects of education, including assessment.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has put procedures in place to ensure that students are protected in all aspects of education including recruitment and selection, teaching, and assessment procedures. ... no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, ... social class or being an ex-offender.

questions.question: A member of staff in a civil partnership is told that a staff benefit is available only to married colleagues. Which statement reflects the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: Marriage and civil partnership is listed only in relation to leave for parents, not to pay and benefits
Marriage and civil partnership is a listed ground, and pay and benefits are expressly covered
Staff benefits are set by contract, so they fall outside the matters the policy covers
Civil partners are covered for recruitment decisions, but benefits are handled under the pay policy
questions.explanation: Marriage and civil partnership is a ground on which no member of staff should be treated unfavourably, and the College's opposition to unlawful discrimination expressly includes pay and benefits.
questions.source_excerpt: no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, ... The College seeks to oppose and avoid all forms of unlawful discrimination. This includes pay and benefits,

questions.question: A manager tells a new colleague that the College's belief in equal opportunities, as set out in the Equality and Diversity Policy, concerns students only. Which statement correctly reflects the policy?
options: Equal opportunities are for everyone involved with the institution, so that students gain the best from their education
Equal opportunities are for enrolled and prospective students, so that they gain the best from their education
Equal opportunities are for staff, with students covered separately under the College's Student Charter
Equal opportunities are for permanent staff and students, with hourly paid staff covered by their contracts
questions.explanation: The policy states the College strongly believes in equal opportunities for everyone involved with the institution, in order for students to gain the best from their education.
questions.source_excerpt: The College strongly believes in equal opportunities for everyone involved with the institution in order for students to gain the best from their education.

questions.question: A member of staff is treated less favourably after supporting a colleague's discrimination complaint. How do the commitments in the Equality and Diversity Policy address victimisation?
options: Victimisation is not named, as the commitments cover bullying and harassment of students only
The College commits to freeing students from victimisation, with staff matters left to HR procedures
Victimisation is dealt with under the grievance procedure and falls outside the policy's commitments
The College commits to making the College free from victimisation, alongside bullying and harassment
questions.explanation: The College's commitments include making the College free from bullying, harassment, victimisation and unlawful discrimination, with the contributions of all staff and students recognised and valued.
questions.source_excerpt: Making the College free from bullying, harassment, victimisation and unlawful discrimination, promoting dignity and respect for all, and where individual differences and the contributions of all staff and students are recognise and valued.

questions.question: Lateness has been approved as a reasonable adjustment for one disabled student. A colleague says it must now be approved for every disabled student in the same group. What does the Equality and Diversity Policy say?
options: The colleague is right, as one approval sets the rule for every disabled student in the group
Lateness can be approved only by the HR department, so the first approval must be withdrawn
The colleague is wrong, as lateness may be approved as an adjustment on a case-by-case basis
No approval is needed, as students with a disability are automatically exempt from lateness rules
questions.explanation: The impact assessment states that lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis, so one approval does not set a rule for other students.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis.

questions.question: A manager is completing the 'Equality Neutral' part of an Equality Impact Assessment under the Equality and Diversity Policy. Which question does that part begin by asking?
options: How much will this cost to implement and to monitor each year?
Who will benefit from this (students/staff/stakeholders)?
Which department will own and review this policy or decision?
Has this been discussed with student and staff representatives?
questions.explanation: The 'Equality Neutral' part of the impact assessment opens by asking who will benefit (students, staff or stakeholders), before asking about positive impact on people who share protected characteristics.
questions.source_excerpt: Equality `Neutral' ... Who will benefit from this (students/staff/stakeholders)? Is there likely to be a positive impact on people who share protected characteristics, and if so, how?

questions.question: While completing the 'Protected Characteristics' part of an Equality Impact Assessment under the Equality and Diversity Policy, a manager finds an adverse impact is likely on people who share a protected characteristic. What does the assessment then ask?
options: The cost of removing the adverse impact and the budget holder responsible for it
The date by which the procedure will be withdrawn until it is revised
The senior manager accountable for approving the decision despite the impact
Who may be affected by the adverse impact, and why they may be affected
questions.explanation: The 'Protected Characteristics' part asks whether an adverse impact is likely and, if so, who may be affected and why.
questions.source_excerpt: Is there likely to be an adverse impact on people who share protected characteristics? If so, who may be affected and why?

questions.question: Four students each missed a requirement for different reasons. According to the impact assessment in the Equality and Diversity Policy, which reason is named as an example of something students may self-certify for?
options: Attending an interview for a part-time weekend job
Being summoned for jury service by a court
Caring responsibilities for a family member
Travel disruption on the way to College
questions.explanation: The impact assessment gives religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments and caring responsibilities as examples of what students may self-certify for.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities.

questions.question: A department proposes that its equality and diversity procedure be available only to students who request a copy in writing from the Registry. Which principle in the Equality and Diversity Policy does this conflict with?
options: That equality procedures will be reviewed and reissued by the Academic Board each year
That the procedures will be easy to access and use, and available to all without discrimination
That every procedure is published in the Student Handbook before the start of each term
That requests for College documents are answered by the Registry within ten working days
questions.explanation: The policy recognises that its equality and diversity process and procedures will at all times be comprehensive, easy to access and use and available to all without discrimination, which a request-only arrangement undermines.
questions.source_excerpt: The College recognises that at all times the process and procedures for equality and diversity will be comprehensive, easy to access and use and available to all without discrimination.

questions.question: Monitoring shows that students who share a particular protected characteristic have lower retention rates than other students. According to the Equality and Diversity Policy, what does the College do?
options: Records the finding, acting only if a student later makes a formal complaint
Refers the data to the Academic Board for review at the end of the year
Publishes the data and asks the affected group to propose changes
Takes action to address potential diversity and equality issues
questions.explanation: The monitoring section states the College monitors retention and achievement with reference to protected characteristics and takes action to address potential diversity and equality issues.
questions.source_excerpt: We also monitor student retention and achievement rates with reference to protected characteristics and take action to address potential diversity and equality issues.

questions.question: A lecturer plans to leave a new module's design unchanged and deal with accessibility only through individual adjustments when students ask. How does this fit the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: It falls short: the policy uses inclusive design wherever possible and individual adjustments wherever necessary
It fits: the policy relies on individual adjustments requested in writing by the students who need them
It fits: inclusive design is required only for the assessment of students with declared disabilities
It falls short: the policy requires separate specialist classes and materials for every student who declares a disability
questions.explanation: The policy makes learning accessible through inclusive design wherever possible and reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary, so relying only on adjustments on request falls short.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are offered learning opportunities that are equally accessible to them, by means of inclusive design wherever possible and by means of reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary.

questions.question: A student is treated unfavourably by another student because of their race. A colleague says the Equality and Diversity Policy only governs how the College itself treats students. Which statement reflects the policy's aim?
options: Its aim is that students and staff are treated equally by one another, so conduct between students is within it
Its aim covers decisions the College makes as an institution, with conduct between students left outside it
Its aim covers how staff treat students, with conduct between students dealt with under separate disciplinary rules
Its aim covers conduct between students only when it takes place during teaching or assessment procedures
questions.explanation: The Aim section describes an environment in which all students and staff are treated equally by one another and can work free of any form of discrimination, so treatment between students is within it.
questions.source_excerpt: London Churchill College strives to create an educational environment in which all students and staff are treated equally by one another and can work free of any form of discrimination

questions.question: An enrolment administrator says the Equality and Diversity Policy's aim concerns teaching and does not reach administrative processes. How does the wording of the policy's aim answer this?
options: The aim applies to teaching staff, with administrative processes governed by HR procedures
The aim reaches administration only where a process forms part of student recruitment
The College pursues the aim in administering its programmes as well as in delivering them
The aim reaches administration only once an impact assessment has been completed for it
questions.explanation: The Aim section opens 'In delivering and administering its programmes', so the College's aim of equal treatment free of discrimination applies to administration as well as delivery.
questions.source_excerpt: In delivering and administering its programmes, London Churchill College strives to create an educational environment in which all students and staff are treated equally by one another

questions.question: An admissions interviewer rejects an applicant because of their sexual orientation, arguing that the Equality and Diversity Policy protects only enrolled students. Which statement reflects the policy?
options: Applicants gain protection only once they accept an offer and complete enrolment at the College
Applicants are named in the policy, and students are protected in recruitment and selection
Recruitment and selection is covered for staff posts, with student admissions outside the policy
Sexual orientation is a listed ground for staff and students, but it does not extend to applicants
questions.explanation: The policy names prospective students and applicants among those who must not be treated unfavourably on grounds including sexual orientation, and its procedures protect students in recruitment and selection.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has put procedures in place to ensure that students are protected in all aspects of education including recruitment and selection, teaching, and assessment procedures. ... no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, ... sexual orientation,

questions.question: Several circumstances are mentioned in different parts of the Equality and Diversity Policy. Which of these is not one of the grounds on which the College seeks to ensure no one is treated unfavourably?
options: Being an ex-offender
Trade union activity
Marriage and civil partnership
Caring responsibilities
questions.explanation: Caring responsibilities appear in the impact assessment as something students may self-certify for, but they are not in the list of grounds, which does include trade union activity, marriage and civil partnership and being an ex-offender.
questions.source_excerpt: is treated unfavorably of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, trade union activity, social class or being an ex-offender. ... students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities.

questions.question: A candidate for an administrator post is rejected at interview because of their religion. The manager says the Equality and Diversity Policy does not apply as the candidate holds no contract of employment yet. Which statement is correct?
options: The policy covers applicants and selection for employment, and religion or belief is a listed ground
The manager is right, as the policy protects staff only once they hold a contract of employment
The policy covers job candidates only where the post is academic rather than professional services
The policy covers selection for employment, but religion or belief is listed as a ground for students only
questions.explanation: The policy names applicants among those who must not be treated unfavourably on grounds including religion or belief, and its opposition to unlawful discrimination expressly includes selection for employment.
questions.source_excerpt: no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, ... religion or belief, ... This includes pay and benefits, ... selection for employment, promotion, training, or other development opportunities.

questions.question: A male member of staff is refused a type of leave for parents that is routinely granted to female colleagues in the same circumstances. Which statement reflects the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: Leave for parents is covered only under pregnancy and maternity, so the protection applies to mothers alone
Leave entitlements are contractual terms set by HR, and so they sit outside the matters the policy lists
Sex is a listed ground, and leave for parents is expressly within the College's opposition to discrimination
Leave for parents is covered for students with caring responsibilities, but not for members of staff
questions.explanation: Sex is one of the grounds on which no member of staff should be treated unfavourably, and the College's opposition to unlawful discrimination expressly includes terms and conditions of employment and leave for parents.
questions.source_excerpt: no prospective student, applicant, student, visitor, or member of staff is treated unfavorably of age, ... sex, ... The College seeks to oppose and avoid all forms of unlawful discrimination. This includes pay and benefits, terms, and conditions of employment, ... leave for parents,

questions.question: A guest speaker visiting the College is intimidated by a group of students after a talk. A colleague says the Equality and Diversity Policy is irrelevant because the speaker is neither staff nor a student. Which statement is correct?
options: The colleague is right, as the policy's scope is limited to staff with contracts and enrolled students
Visitors are within the policy's scope, and the College actively seeks to tackle any form of intimidation
Visitors are covered only while taking part in teaching, so a talk outside teaching falls outside it
Visitors are covered only where a contractor employs them to work on the College premises
questions.explanation: The scope section states the policy applies to London Churchill College visitors, and the College actively seeks to tackle any form of harassment, bullying or intimidation.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy applies to all members of London Churchill College, including: ... London Churchill College visitors. ... The College actively seeks to tackle any form of harassment, bullying or intimidation through promoting an environment that champions the values of dignity for all.

questions.question: A manager tells a team that the College supports equality and diversity only because the law requires it. Which statement from the Equality and Diversity Policy shows this view is incomplete?
options: The College applies the Equality Act 2010 alone and treats any further commitment as optional practice
The College goes beyond legislation only where its awarding bodies require it as a partnership condition
The College commits to legislation for staff matters and to good practice for student matters only
The College also encourages equality, diversity and inclusion as good practice that makes business sense
questions.explanation: Besides committing to abide by current legislation, the College commits to encourage equality, diversity and inclusion because they are good practice and make business sense.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is committed to abiding by current legislation in discharging its duties in a fair and transparent manner. ... Encourage equality, diversity, and inclusion in the College as they are good practice and make business sense.

questions.question: On the same day, a permanent administrator and a student each ask you about reasonable adjustments. Which pairing of routes matches the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: The administrator seeks advice from HR; for students, detail is in the Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy
Both seek advice from the HR department, which the policy names as the route for staff and students alike
The administrator follows the Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy; the student seeks HR advice
Both go to the Academic Department, which the policy names as making all reasonable adjustments at the College
questions.explanation: The policy points to the Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy for further information on student adjustments, while staff requiring reasonable adjustment should seek advice from the HR department.
questions.source_excerpt: Further information on this can be read in Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy. Reasonable adjustment also applies to members of staff, both permanent and hourly paid. Staff requiring reasonable adjustment should seek advice from the HR department.

questions.question: A student who has not declared a disability is finding a module's learning materials hard to access. Which statement reflects the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: No support is available until a disability is formally declared, as adjustments are limited to declared disabilities
The student is referred to HR, which handles adjustments for any condition a student has not yet declared
Accessible learning is for all students, through inclusive design and reasonable individual adjustments where necessary
The student is exempt from the module's assessment requirements until a disability has been formally declared
questions.explanation: All students are offered equally accessible learning opportunities through inclusive design wherever possible and reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary; the invitation to meet is an additional step for declared disabilities.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are offered learning opportunities that are equally accessible to them, by means of inclusive design wherever possible and by means of reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary.

questions.question: A member of staff is repeatedly bullied by a colleague for reasons unconnected with any of the grounds listed in the Equality and Diversity Policy. Which statement reflects the policy?
options: The policy is limited to unfavourable treatment on its listed grounds, so the bullying falls outside it
The College seeks to tackle any form of bullying and commits to a College free from bullying
The policy covers bullying of students, with bullying between members of staff left outside its scope
The policy covers bullying only where it is also victimisation for supporting a discrimination complaint
questions.explanation: The policy states the College actively seeks to tackle any form of harassment, bullying or intimidation, and commits to making the College free from bullying, so it is not limited to the listed grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: The College actively seeks to tackle any form of harassment, bullying or intimidation ... Making the College free from bullying, harassment, victimisation and unlawful discrimination

questions.question: A manager completing an Equality Impact Assessment under the Equality and Diversity Policy expects a new procedure to benefit students who share a protected characteristic. Which part of the assessment asks about this?
options: The 'Protected Characteristics' part, which asks if a positive impact is likely and how
The 'Equitable Procedure' part, which asks who will benefit and how benefit is measured
The 'Monitoring' part, which asks what positive impact is expected for each characteristic
The 'Equality Neutral' part, which asks if a positive impact is likely and how
questions.explanation: The 'Equality Neutral' part asks who will benefit and whether a positive impact on people who share protected characteristics is likely and how; the 'Protected Characteristics' part asks about adverse impact.
questions.source_excerpt: Equality `Neutral' ... Who will benefit from this (students/staff/stakeholders)? Is there likely to be a positive impact on people who share protected characteristics, and if so, how? ... Is there likely to be an adverse impact on people who share protected characteristics?

questions.question: A manager assumes the Equality Impact Assessment set out in the Equality and Diversity Policy is only for new written policies. According to the policy, what is the assessment applied to?
options: New written policies only, before they are approved
Decisions affecting staff pay and benefits only
The policy, procedure or decision being considered
Student-facing procedures only, not staff decisions
questions.explanation: The assessment is framed around the 'policy/procedure/decision' being considered, so it is not limited to new written policies.
questions.source_excerpt: Name of policy/procedure/decision: ... This section sets out the requirements in relation to diversity procedures impact from an equality perspective and protected characteristics by posing the following questions and issues of the policy/procedure/decision being considered

questions.question: A student with a disability is often late because of their condition and also misses one session for a hospital appointment. Which response matches the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: Both may be self-certified, as the policy treats disability-related lateness as a medical appointment
Both are approved automatically, as students with a disability are exempt from attendance rules
The lateness is approved by HR after an assessment; the appointment needs a letter from the hospital
Lateness may be approved as an adjustment case by case; the appointment may be self-certified
questions.explanation: The policy states lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis, and separately that students may self-certify for medical appointments.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, ... For example, lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis.

questions.question: According to the monitoring part of the Equality and Diversity Policy, which of the following is not something the College states that it monitors?
options: Complaints about implementation of the process
Student retention rates by protected characteristic
Staff promotion rates by protected characteristic
Student achievement rates by protected characteristic
questions.explanation: The monitoring part covers complaints about implementation and student retention and achievement rates by protected characteristic; it does not mention staff promotion rates.
questions.source_excerpt: Any complaints about the implementation of this process will be monitored. We also monitor student retention and achievement rates with reference to protected characteristics

questions.question: A manager asks how the Equality and Diversity Policy connects fair procedures with how well students do. Which statement reflects the policy?
options: Equitable procedure is relevant to student attainment, and achievement is monitored by protected characteristic
Attainment depends on entry qualifications, so achievement is monitored by programme rather than by characteristic
Equitable procedure is a factor in staff retention, while student attainment is left to academic judgement
Attainment is outside the impact assessment, which considers only students' access to the appeals process
questions.explanation: The impact assessment states equitable procedure is a relevant factor in student attainment, and the monitoring part states achievement rates are monitored with reference to protected characteristics.
questions.source_excerpt: Equitable procedure is a relevant factor in student attainment. ... We also monitor student retention and achievement rates with reference to protected characteristics

questions.question: A student declares a disability at enrolment and later cannot attend a panel hearing because of it. Which sequence matches the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: They must first request a meeting in writing; HR then adjusts the arrangements for the review meeting
They are invited to discuss support; the Academic Department should accommodate review meetings
They are referred for an external needs assessment; the missed hearing is recorded as non-attendance
They are contacted by HR to agree support; the review meeting then goes ahead in the student's absence
questions.explanation: Students with declared disabilities are contacted and invited to meet to discuss support, and the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments to accommodate attendance at review meetings where disability has affected attendance at panel hearings.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with declared disabilities are contacted and invited to meet and discuss the additional support that the College can provide them. ... the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments for students whose attendance at panel hearings or other, has been affected by his or her disability to accommodate attendance at review meetings.

questions.question: A male student who is the main carer for his young child asks to self-certify an absence caused by caring responsibilities. A colleague says the Equality and Diversity Policy ties this to female students. Which statement is correct?
options: Students may self-certify for caring responsibilities; the childcare point explains why gender is relevant
The colleague is right, as the policy links self-certification for childcare to female students only
He may self-certify only once the Academic Department approves the absence as a reasonable adjustment
Caring responsibilities may be self-certified only where the student has also declared a disability at enrolment
questions.explanation: The impact assessment lets students self-certify for caring responsibilities; it mentions that more female than male students are primarily responsible for childcare only to explain why gender is relevant to self-certification, not to restrict who may use it.
questions.source_excerpt: students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities. ... Gender is also relevant in terms of self-certification, as it is known that more female students than male students are primarily responsible for childcare.

questions.question: A manager's Equality Impact Assessment finds a new procedure is not likely to have a negative impact on people who share protected characteristics, so the manager plans to skip monitoring. Which statement reflects the Equality and Diversity Policy?
options: Monitoring is needed only where the Protected Characteristics part finds that an adverse impact is likely
A procedure unlikely to have a negative impact counts as equality 'neutral' and needs no further questions
Monitoring is limited to retention and achievement rates, which the College already tracks for every procedure
The assessment still asks what action will be taken to ensure the procedure's impact is monitored
questions.explanation: The assessment's requirements are set by posing all of its questions, including what action will be taken to monitor the procedure's impact; the policy's own assessment finds no likely negative impact yet still monitors complaints and student outcomes.
questions.source_excerpt: This section sets out the requirements in relation to diversity procedures impact from an ... It is not likely that this EIA will have a negative impact on people who share protected characteristics. ... What action will you take to ensure that you are monitoring the impact ... Any complaints about the implementation of this process will be

questions.question: A student says that a disabled classmate's approved lateness breaks the Equality and Diversity Policy's aim that all students are treated equally. Which statement reflects the policy?
options: Equal treatment means identical rules, so the lateness must be recorded as unauthorised like anyone else's
The policy seeks equally accessible learning through reasonable individual adjustments, and lateness may be one
Lateness may be approved only through self-certification, which the classmate may also use for any reason
Lateness adjustments are for staff on HR advice, so approving one for a student departs from the policy
questions.explanation: Equal access is achieved through inclusive design and reasonable individual adjustments where necessary, and the policy states that lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment for a student with a disability on a case-by-case basis.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are offered learning opportunities that are equally accessible to them, by means of inclusive design wherever possible and by means of reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary. ... lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis.

policies.title: Learning Resource Centre and IT Using Policy

questions.question: A member of staff uses a College computer to share material promoting a non-violent extremist cause, saying it is harmless because it is not violent. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is the position?
options: It is permitted, as the IT restriction covers violent extremism and terrorism but not non-violent causes
It is permitted, as the Prevent restriction on IT use applies to students rather than staff
It is forbidden if the material reaches students, but permitted if it is shared among staff
It is forbidden, as IT systems must not be used to promote violent or non-violent extremism
questions.explanation: In line with the Prevent Duty, the Guide forbids both staff and students from using the IT systems for the instigation, promotion, planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism, for any reason.
questions.source_excerpt: The College recognises its duty of care to students and its responsibility to comply with the Prevent Duty guide. It is therefore forbidden for staff and students to use the IT systems for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation, or terrorism in the name of ideology or belief or any other reason.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, how much of a work may be copied using the copyright exception for education?
options: Up to 10% of a work in any 12-month period across the College
Up to 5% of a work in any 12-month period across the College
Up to 5% of a work per lecturer in each academic term
Up to one full chapter of a work per course in each year
questions.explanation: The Copyright section states that the copyright exception for education can be used to copy up to 5% of a work in any 12-month period across the College.
questions.source_excerpt: This copyright exception for education can be used to copy up to 5% of a work in any 12-month period across the College.

questions.question: A lecturer wants to display some webpages and quotes on a projector during a class. According to the copyright section of the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: Written permission must first be obtained from each copyright owner
It requires the College to have purchased the source material beforehand
It is not allowed, as the exception covers printed handouts only
It is an example of fair use and needs no additional permissions
questions.explanation: The Guide gives a teacher displaying webpages or quotes on a projector as an example of fair use that does not need additional permissions.
questions.source_excerpt: Minor acts of copying are permitted for teaching purposes, as long as the use is considered fair and reasonable. An example of fair use would be a teacher displaying ... webpages or quotes on a projector without the need to seek additional permissions.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what may happen to photocopies made in excess of the copyright limits?
options: They can be confiscated, as each user must personally comply with the law
They may be kept if the user pays double the standard per-page charge
They may be kept, as the College alone is responsible for copyright compliance
They must be handed to the LRC to be added to the reference collection
questions.explanation: The Guide states that each user must personally comply with the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 and that photocopies made in excess of the limits can be confiscated.
questions.source_excerpt: The College's photocopying services are offered in accordance with the provisions of the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988. Each user must personally comply with the law. All photocopies made in excess of the limits can be confiscated;

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which of the following is NOT one of the four factors for deciding whether use of a copyrighted work is fair?
options: The purpose and character of the use, including whether it is commercial
The nature of the copyrighted work being used
The number of students who will receive a copy of the material
The effect of the use on the potential market for or value of the work
questions.explanation: The four factors listed are the purpose and character of the use, the nature of the work, the amount used, and the effect on the market or value; the number of recipients is not one of them.
questions.source_excerpt: There are four factors to consider when determining whether your use is a fair one. 1. The purpose and character of the use, including whether such use is of a commercial nature ... 2. The nature of the copyrighted work; 3. The amount and substantially of the portion used ... 4. The effect of the use upon the potential market for or value of the copyrighted work.

questions.question: A student has taken a book out of the LRC without checking it out and has damaged it. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what may follow?
options: An automatic, permanent exclusion from the College and from all of its programmes of study
A late charge of 10p per day until the book is replaced, with no disciplinary action taken
Action under the Student Code of Conduct, including LRC suspension and loss of VLE access
Referral to the police for prosecution under the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988
questions.explanation: Damaging materials or taking them without checking them out may lead to action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, with penalties including suspension from the LRC and withdrawal of VLE access.
questions.source_excerpt: materials or taking materials from our LRC without checking them out first.
