Failure to do so may result in action being taken against you in accordance with the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure , with penalties including suspension from the LRC and the withdrawal of permission to access our VLE;

questions.question: A student who has returned all borrowed materials undamaged is leaving their course before completion and asks whether they can reclaim their library membership deposit. What does the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide say?
options: No, a refund is available to students who transfer to another LCC course, not to leavers
No, leaving before completion means the deposit is automatically forfeited
Yes, but a claim can be made no earlier than three months after the date they leave
Yes, the deposit can be reclaimed when a student leaves the course before completion
questions.explanation: The Guide states the deposit can be reclaimed after completion of the programme or when the student leaves the course, should this occur before completion; forfeiture is linked only to damage or loss of materials.
questions.source_excerpt: Deposit can be reclaimed after the completion of the programme or when the student leaves the course, should this occur before completion.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what must all students wear when using LRC facilities?
options: A visitor lanyard, collected from the LRC desk each time they use the facilities
Their college ID card when borrowing or returning materials, but not otherwise
Their college ID card, at all times while they are using the LRC facilities
A library membership badge confirming that their £10 deposit has been paid
questions.explanation: In the interest of safety and security, the Guide requires all students using the LRC facilities to wear their college ID card, not only when borrowing.
questions.source_excerpt: In the interest of safety and security, all students using the LRC facilities must wear their college ID card;

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what does the College ask of LRC users regarding food and drink?
options: They may drink from sealed bottles, but must not eat any food at the study tables
They should refrain from eating or drinking in the LRCs or when working on a College computer
They may eat in the LRC, provided no food or materials are left behind on study tables
They should avoid food and drink at College computers but may eat elsewhere in the LRC
questions.explanation: Recognising that some foods may be offensive to others, the Guide asks users to refrain from eating or drinking in the LRCs or when working on a College computer.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC recognises that different cultures have different approaches to food and manners and that some foods may be offensive to others, particularly in respect of smells and or materials left on study tables. Therefore, we ask that you refrain from eating or drinking in our LRCs, or when you are working on one of the College's computers;

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what are the borrowing limits for library members?
options: Up to 2 materials for 1 week
Up to 3 materials for 2 weeks
Up to 2 materials for 2 weeks
Up to 5 materials for 1 week
questions.explanation: The Library Service section states that members can borrow up to 2 materials for 1 week.
questions.source_excerpt: Members can borrow up to 2 materials for 1 week.

questions.question: A student has completed their course and still has unused printing credit. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, by when must they claim the remaining balance?
options: Within three months of the course completion date
Within one month of the course completion date
Within twelve months of the course completion date
It cannot be claimed, as unused credit is forfeited at completion
questions.explanation: The Guide states that any remaining balance must be claimed within three months of the course completion date (or date of withdrawal/termination).
questions.source_excerpt: Top-up credit should be used before the programme completion date. Any remaining balance must be claimed within three months of the course completion date or date of course withdrawal/termination.

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what does a student need to pay to register for library membership?
options: A £10 annual membership fee, charged at registration and not refunded on completion
Nothing for registration itself, but a £10 refundable deposit is required
Nothing at all, as no fee or deposit is needed from students already enrolled at LCC
Nothing for registration itself, but a £5 refundable deposit is required
questions.explanation: The Library Service section states that membership registration is free but requires a £10 deposit, which is refunded once the student's programme is successfully completed.
questions.source_excerpt: A membership is required to hire out books or any study materials from the library. Registration for membership is free but will require a ... deposit, that will be refunded to the student once their programme is successfully completed.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, to whom does the Guide apply?
options: All students and staff members who use the services of the Learning Resource Centre
Students only, as staff use of the LRC is covered by the separate staff IT policy
Registered library members only, whether they are students or members of staff
LRC and IT staff only, as the people responsible for delivering the services
questions.explanation: The Introduction states that the Guide applies to all students and staff members who use the services of the LRC, not only to students or registered members.
questions.source_excerpt: This Guide is applicable to all students and staff members using the services of the Learning Resource Centre (LRC);

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, where does the College provide a Learning Resource Centre (LRC)?
options: At the main campus only, with the other sites served by the digital library
On every campus, each fully equipped with a quiet, comfortable space to work
At the two largest campuses, with other sites sharing an online booking system
At the head office only, with materials sent to other campuses on request
questions.explanation: The Guide states that the College provides an LRC on every campus, each fully equipped with a quiet, comfortable space for students to work.
questions.source_excerpt: The College provides an LRC on every campus. Each LRC is fully equipped and has a quiet, comfortable space for students to work.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what does the College's Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) hold for the Units delivered?
options: Assessment marks, attendance records and tutor feedback for each individual student
Past examination papers and model answers approved by the external examiner
Lecture notes, assignment briefings and any additional material lecturers provide
Reading lists and loan records for every item borrowed from the LRC collection
questions.explanation: The Guide states that the VLE holds lecture notes, assignment briefings and any additional material that lecturers provide for the Units delivered.
questions.source_excerpt: On our VLE are lecture notes, assignment briefings and any additional material that lecturers provide in respect of the Units delivered.

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, can students access the College's VLE when they are off-campus?
options: No, only from computers located in the College's LRCs
Yes, but only during the library's opening hours
Only after LRC staff approve a written access request
Yes, providing they have the proper log-in details
questions.explanation: The Guide states that students can access the College's VLE off-campus, providing they have the proper log-in details.
questions.source_excerpt: In addition, students can access the College's VLE off-campus, providing you have the proper log-in details.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, as well as helping students find information for their assignments, what can LRC staff help them learn?
options: How to reference the information they have found
How to submit work through the plagiarism checker
How to appeal the mark given for an assignment
How to request an extension to a submission deadline
questions.explanation: The Guide states that LRC staff can help students learn how to reference the information they have found.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC ensures that LRC staff members are always available during open times to help you develop the skills required to find the information needed to complete your assignments ... In addition, they can help you to learn how to reference the information you have found.

questions.question: The Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide says LRC resources must be used in line with licensing and legislative provisions. What does 'use' include here?
options: Borrowing hard copy items, but not copying digital content
The copying, storing, amending and transmission of information
Only reading information on College computers while on campus
Only accessing third-party digital libraries such as JSTOR
questions.explanation: The Guide defines use of LRC resources as including the copying, storing, amending and transmission of information.
questions.source_excerpt: LRC's resources must be used only in accordance with appropriate licensing and legislative provisions, library circulation procedures and borrowing limits. Use includes the copying, storing, amending and transmission of information;

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what happens to students who act in a way that infringes copyright or intellectual property laws?
options: They receive an informal warning from the librarian with no further action
They forfeit their £10 library deposit, with no further action being taken
Action is taken under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
The matter is referred to the Academic Appeals Panel for a final decision
questions.explanation: The Guide states that action will be taken under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure against students who infringe copyright or intellectual property laws.
questions.source_excerpt: Students must ensure that they do not act in a way that infringes copyright or intellectual property laws. Action will be taken under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure against students who do so.

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, when is the library open?
options: Monday to Friday, 9.00am to 5.00pm
Monday to Saturday, 9.30am to 5.15pm
Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 6.15pm
Monday to Friday, 9.30am to 5.15pm
questions.explanation: The Guide for Library and IT Services states that the library is open Monday to Friday, 9.30am to 5.15pm.
questions.source_excerpt: The library is open from Monday to Friday, 9.30am to 5.15pm.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what password does a student use to log into a College computer?
options: Their date of birth, in DDMMYYYY format
Their student ID number without the LCC prefix
A temporary code issued by LRC staff at induction
Their surname followed by their year of entry
questions.explanation: The Guide states that the password for logging into a College computer is the student's date of birth in DDMMYYYY format.
questions.source_excerpt: Logging into a Computer Your username is your full student ID number starting with "LCC". Your password will be your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format.

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is a student's password for logging into the Student Portal?
options: A one-time code sent by the IT team at enrolment each year
The one they set up when filling in the LCC Admission Form
A temporary password issued by LRC staff at their induction
The password sent to them when they accepted their offer
questions.explanation: The Guide states that the Student Portal password is the one the student set up when filling in the LCC Admission Form.
questions.source_excerpt: Logging into your Student Portal Your username is your full student ID number starting with "LCC", and your password is the one you set up when filling in the LCC Admission Form.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, how can a student reset their Moodle password?
options: By emailing the librarian from their College account
By asking their lecturer to reset it at the next class
By using the 'forget password' option on Moodle
By completing a reset form at the LRC help desk
questions.explanation: The Guide states that students can reset their Moodle password by using the 'forget password' option.
questions.source_excerpt: You can reset your password by using `forget password' option.

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is charged for borrowed materials kept past their return date?
options: 20p per day
50p per week
£1 per day
10p per day
questions.explanation: The Library Service section states that there is a charge of 10p per day for materials exceeding the return date.
questions.source_excerpt: There will be a charge of 10p per day for materials exceeding the return date.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, when can library members renew materials they have borrowed?
options: Before the return date expires, depending on the availability of resources
Only after the return date, once any late charges have been paid in full
At any time, as loans renew automatically unless an item is reported lost
Only once per term, and only with written approval from the librarian
questions.explanation: The Guide states that, depending on the availability of resources, members can renew the borrowing before the return date expires.
questions.source_excerpt: Depending on the availability of resources, members can renew the borrowing before the ... return date expires.

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, where is the access link to the JSTOR digital library found?
options: On the College's public website
On the student portal site
In the LRC induction handbook
In the enrolment welcome email
questions.explanation: The Digital Library Service section states that the access link to JSTOR is on the student portal site.
questions.source_excerpt: The access link to JSTOR is on the student portal site.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, how much does printing and photocopying cost?
options: 2p a page
10p a page
5p a page
15p a page
questions.explanation: The Topping-Up section states that printing and photocopying costs 5p a page.
questions.source_excerpt: Printing & photocopying costs 5p a page.

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, where can students top up their printing credit?
options: At the LRC desk, in cash only
Through the Moodle site
At the photocopier panel by card
On their Student Portal account
questions.explanation: The Guide states that students can top up their printing credit on their Student Portal account.
questions.source_excerpt: You can top up your printing credit on your Student Portal account.

questions.question: According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, on what condition are minor acts of copying permitted for teaching purposes?
options: That the use is considered fair and reasonable
That written permission is first obtained from the author
That the original work is no longer commercially available
That the copying is carried out by a member of LRC staff
questions.explanation: The Copyright section states that minor acts of copying are permitted for teaching purposes as long as the use is considered fair and reasonable.
questions.source_excerpt: Minor acts of copying are permitted for teaching purposes, as long as the use is considered fair and reasonable.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what may lead to a student forfeiting their £10 library membership deposit?
options: Leaving their course before the programme has been completed
Damage to or loss of any of the library's study materials
Returning borrowed materials after the return date has passed
Not wearing their college ID card while using the LRC facilities
questions.explanation: The Library Service section states that damage or loss of any of the study materials may result in the student forfeiting the deposit.
questions.source_excerpt: Damage or loss of any of the study materials may result in the student forfeiting the ... deposit.

questions.question: A student asks a member of staff where to find the access links for the BIBLIU and JSTOR digital libraries. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is the correct answer?
options: BIBLIU is linked from the student portal site, and JSTOR from the Moodle site
Both are linked from the Moodle site, once library membership is registered
BIBLIU is linked from the Moodle site, and JSTOR from the student portal
Both are linked from the student portal, using the Admission Form password
questions.explanation: The Digital Library Service section states that the BIBLIU access link is on the Moodle site and the JSTOR access link is on the student portal site; all students have access without needing library membership.
questions.source_excerpt: All the College's students have access to third-party digital library services such as BIBLIU and JSTOR. The access link to BIBLIU is on the Moodle site. The access link to JSTOR is on the student portal site.

questions.question: A new student asks how the passwords differ for College computers, Moodle and the Student Portal. According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: Computers and Moodle use the date of birth (DDMMYYYY); the Portal uses the password set on the Admission Form
Computers and the Portal use the date of birth (DDMMYYYY); Moodle uses the password set on the Admission Form
All three use the date of birth (DDMMYYYY) as the password until the student chooses to reset it
Moodle and the Portal use the password set on the Admission Form; computers use the date of birth (DDMMYYYY)
questions.explanation: The Guide gives the date of birth in DDMMYYYY format as the password for both College computers and Moodle, while the Student Portal password is the one set up on the LCC Admission Form.
questions.source_excerpt: Logging into a Computer Your username is your full student ID number starting with "LCC". Your password will be your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format. ... your password is the one you set up when filling in the LCC Admission Form. ... Logging into Moodle Your Moodle username is your full student ID number starting with "LCC". Your password will be your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format.

questions.question: A student asks how to print a document in the LRC. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is the correct sequence?
options: Touch the ID card on the photocopier panel first, then log into a computer and send the print command
Email the document to the librarian, who then releases it at the photocopier for the student to collect in person
Send the print command from the Student Portal, then type the student ID number into the photocopier
Log into a computer with their ID, send the print command, then touch the photocopier panel with their ID card
questions.explanation: The Guide says to log into any computer with your ID, send the print command using the papercut option, and then touch the photocopier panel with your ID card.
questions.source_excerpt: Printing: For printing log into any computer with your ID and send the print command (papercut option) of the document you wish. Then touch the photocopier panel with your ID card.

questions.question: Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which of these LRC services does a student obtain by asking the librarian, rather than by using their ID card at the photocopier?
options: Photocopying a document
Scanning a document
Printing a document
Topping up printing credit
questions.explanation: Photocopying and printing are done by touching the ID card on the photocopier panel and credit is topped up on the Student Portal, whereas for scanning students are asked to see the librarian.
questions.source_excerpt: Photocopying: Simply touch your ID card on the panel of the photocopier and follow the on-screen instruction. ... Scanning Please ask the librarian for scanning service.

questions.question: A new student has not yet topped up the credit on their ID card. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, how many pages can they print or photocopy using only their starting credit?
options: 10 pages
5 pages
20 pages
50 pages
questions.explanation: Everyone starts with £1 credit on their ID card and printing or photocopying costs 5p a page, so the starting credit covers 20 pages.
questions.source_excerpt: Printing & photocopying costs 5p a page. Everyone starts off with ... credit already on their ID card.

questions.question: A library member returns one borrowed book five days after its return date. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what charge applies?
options: 50p, at 10p for each day past the return date
25p, at 5p for each day past the return date
£1, at 20p for each day past the return date
£10, as the whole membership deposit is forfeited
questions.explanation: The Guide sets a charge of 10p per day for materials kept past the return date, so five days late costs 50p; forfeiting the deposit relates to damage or loss, not late return.
questions.source_excerpt: There will be a charge of 10p per day for materials exceeding the return date.

questions.question: A library member's book passed its return date two days ago, and they now ask to renew it. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: Renewal is provided for only before the return date expires, and the late days cost 10p each
They may renew it now, and the late charge is cancelled once the renewal has been recorded
They may renew it at any point within seven days of the return date without any late charge
They must forfeit their library deposit before they are allowed to renew or borrow any item
questions.explanation: Members can renew before the return date expires (subject to availability), and materials exceeding the return date are charged at 10p per day.
questions.source_excerpt: There will be a charge of 10p per day for materials exceeding the return date. 5. Depending on the availability of resources, members can renew the borrowing before the ... return date expires.

questions.question: A student who has not registered for library membership wants to take a textbook home from the LRC. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is required first?
options: Showing their college ID card at the desk, as every enrolled student is automatically a member
Written approval from their lecturer confirming that the textbook is needed for their Unit
Registering for library membership, which is free but requires a refundable deposit
Nothing, provided they return the textbook within 1 week and pay 10p a day if it is late
questions.explanation: Membership is required to hire out books or study materials; registration is free but requires a deposit that is refunded once the programme is successfully completed.
questions.source_excerpt: A membership is required to hire out books or any study materials from the library. Registration for membership is free but will require a ... deposit, that will be refunded to the student once their programme is successfully completed.

questions.question: A student is drinking coffee while working on a College computer in a classroom outside the LRC. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is the position?
options: It is acceptable, as the food and drink request applies only inside the LRCs
It is acceptable for drinks, as the request is aimed only at food smells
It is acceptable, provided nothing is left behind on the desk afterwards
They are asked to refrain, as the request covers working on College computers
questions.explanation: The Guide asks users to refrain from eating or drinking in the LRCs or when working on one of the College's computers, so it applies at a College computer outside the LRC too.
questions.source_excerpt: Therefore, we ask that you refrain from eating or drinking in our LRCs, or when you are working on one of the College's computers;

questions.question: A lecturer plans to copy 8% of a textbook for a class under the copyright exception for education. According to the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: It is within the exception, which allows up to 10% of a work for teaching purposes
It exceeds the exception, which allows up to 5% of a work in any 12-month period
It is within the exception, provided the copying is for non-profit educational use
It is within the exception, provided each student receives only a single copy
questions.explanation: The copyright exception for education covers up to 5% of a work in any 12-month period across the College, so 8% exceeds it.
questions.source_excerpt: Minor acts of copying are permitted for teaching purposes, as long as the use is considered fair and reasonable. ... This copyright exception for education can be used to copy up to 5% of a work in any 12-month period across the College.

questions.question: When judging whether copying is fair use, a lecturer asks whether the copies could reduce sales of the book. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which of the four factors is this?
options: The effect of the use upon the potential market for or value of the work
The purpose and character of the use, including any commercial nature
The amount and substantiality of the portion used relative to the whole
The nature of the copyrighted work that is being copied for the class
questions.explanation: Whether copies could reduce sales goes to the fourth factor: the effect of the use upon the potential market for or value of the copyrighted work.
questions.source_excerpt: There are four factors to consider when determining whether your use is a fair one. ... 4. The effect of the use upon the potential market for or value of the copyrighted ... work.

questions.question: A student tells LRC staff they would find it easier to study at a library closer to home. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, how can LRC staff help?
options: They cannot advise on external libraries, so the student must email the librarian
They can transfer the student's library membership and deposit to a local library
They can only direct the student to the College's digital libraries such as JSTOR
They can recommend local libraries and suggest other places to find information
questions.explanation: The Guide states that LRC staff can recommend local libraries and suggest other places to find information, or a site closer to home, and invites students to ask.
questions.source_excerpt: We can also recommend local libraries for you to use and suggest other places to go to find the information you need, or perhaps to visit a site closer to home. Just ask one of our LRC staff members for details.

questions.question: The Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide says LRC staff are always available during open times. At which of these times can a student expect LRC staff to be available?
options: Saturday at 11.00am
Monday at 9.00am
Wednesday at 4.30pm
Friday at 5.30pm
questions.explanation: LRC staff are available during open times, and the library is open Monday to Friday, 9.30am to 5.15pm; only Wednesday at 4.30pm falls within those hours.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC ensures that LRC staff members are always available during open times ... The library is open from Monday to Friday, 9.30am to 5.15pm.

questions.question: A student keeps the only copy of their assignment on a College computer in the LRC. What does the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide strongly advise students to do?
options: Ask LRC staff to save a copy of their work to the College network drive
Email a copy of each assignment to the librarian before submission
Leave it on the LRC computer, as IT backs up every College machine
Keep a back-up of all their work on a storage device or online facility
questions.explanation: The Guide strongly advises students to keep a back-up of all their work on a storage device or online facility.
questions.source_excerpt: Important Students are strongly advised to keep a back-up of all their work on a storage device or online facility.

questions.question: A student downloads articles from a licensed LRC resource and emails them to friends at another college. How does the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide treat this?
options: It is outside the Guide, which covers only borrowing hard copy materials from the LRC
It is use of LRC resources, so it must comply with licensing and legislative provisions
It is outside the Guide, as its rules cover copying and storing but not transmission
It is permitted, as the licensing rules apply only while the student is on campus
questions.explanation: Use of LRC resources includes the copying, storing, amending and transmission of information, and must be in accordance with appropriate licensing and legislative provisions.
questions.source_excerpt: LRC's resources must be used only in accordance with appropriate licensing and legislative provisions, library circulation procedures and borrowing limits. Use includes the copying, storing, amending and transmission of information;

questions.question: A newly appointed member of professional services staff, who does not teach, asks whether the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide applies to them and whether they can use the VLE. Which answer is correct?
options: It applies only to students, though staff may use the VLE if a lecturer sponsors their access
It applies to them, but VLE access is limited to the lecturers who deliver the College's Units
It applies to staff using LRC services, and all staff members have access to the College's VLE
It applies only to academic staff, so they fall outside both the Guide and the VLE access rules
questions.explanation: The Guide applies to all students and staff members using LRC services, and all students and staff members have access to the VLE, not only lecturers.
questions.source_excerpt: This Guide is applicable to all students and staff members using the services of the Learning Resource Centre (LRC); ... All students and staff members have access to our VLE, which provides valuable information regarding every Unit delivered in the College.

questions.question: A student uses an LRC computer to plan an act of radicalisation that is never carried out, and claims it had nothing to do with ideology or belief. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is the position?
options: It is forbidden, as the ban covers planning, whether for ideology, belief or any other reason
It is outside the ban, which applies only once an act of radicalisation is actually executed
It is outside the ban, which covers only acts in the name of an ideology or a religious belief
It is outside the ban, as the Prevent restriction on IT systems binds staff but not students
questions.explanation: The Prevent-based rule forbids staff and students from using the IT systems for the instigation, promotion, planning or execution of radicalisation, in the name of ideology or belief or any other reason.
questions.source_excerpt: It is therefore forbidden for staff and students to use the IT systems for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation, or terrorism in the name of ideology or belief or any other reason.

questions.question: In its Expectations of Students section, which expectation does the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide expressly extend to staff as well as to students?
options: Wearing a college ID card while using the LRC facilities, in the interest of safety and security
Respecting other students by refraining from making any undue noise in the library
Not damaging LRC materials or removing them from the LRC without checking them out first
Not using the College's IT systems for extremism, radicalisation or terrorism
questions.explanation: Only the Prevent-related prohibition expressly names staff and students; the ID card rule is stated for all students, and the noise and materials requests are addressed to students.
questions.source_excerpt: In the interest of safety and security, all students using the LRC facilities must wear their college ID card; ... It is therefore forbidden for staff and students to use the IT systems for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation, or terrorism

questions.question: A student in the LRC says their snack has no smell and they will leave nothing on the study table, so the food request's concerns do not apply. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is the position?
options: They may eat it, as the request is aimed only at foods that might be offensive to others
They are still asked to refrain, as the request covers all eating and drinking in the LRCs
They may eat it, provided no food or other materials are left behind on the study table
They may eat it away from the computers, as the request applies only at the College's computers
questions.explanation: The concerns about smells and materials left on tables explain the rule, but the request itself is to refrain from eating or drinking in the LRCs, with no exception for odourless food.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC recognises that different cultures have different approaches to food and manners and that some foods may be offensive to others, particularly in respect of smells and or materials left on study tables. Therefore, we ask that you refrain from eating or drinking in our LRCs

questions.question: Both damaging LRC materials and infringing copyright can lead to action under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure. Which specific penalties does the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide name, and for which breach?
options: LRC suspension and withdrawal of VLE access, named for infringing copyright laws
A 10p daily fine and a written warning from the librarian, named for both types of breach
LRC suspension and withdrawal of VLE access, named for damaging or taking materials
Withdrawal of VLE access alone, with no LRC suspension, named for both types of breach
questions.explanation: Penalties including suspension from the LRC and withdrawal of VLE access are named for damaging or taking materials; for copyright infringement the Guide states only that action will be taken under the Code.
questions.source_excerpt: Failure to do so may result in action being taken against you in accordance with the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure , with penalties including suspension from the LRC and the withdrawal of permission to access our VLE; ... Action will be taken under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure against students who do so.

questions.question: Two lecturers in different departments each plan to copy 4% of the same textbook for teaching within the same 12-month period. Under the copyright exception for education in the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: Both are within the exception, as the 5% limit applies to each lecturer separately
Both are within the exception, as the 5% limit applies to each department separately
Both are within the exception, as the 5% limit resets at the start of each term
Together they exceed the exception, as the 5% limit applies across the College
questions.explanation: The exception allows up to 5% of a work in any 12-month period across the College, so two 4% copies of the same work in that period total 8% and exceed it.
questions.source_excerpt: This copyright exception for education can be used to copy up to 5% of a work in any 12-month period across the College.

questions.question: A lecturer plans to copy 3% of a book for a class, but it is the key chapter that most readers buy the book for. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: It is automatically fair, as copying within the 5% limit needs no further consideration
Staying within 5% is not enough; the use must be fair, and the substantiality of the portion counts
It is barred outright, as the exception excludes the most important chapter of any work
It needs the publisher's written permission first, as all chapter copying for teaching does
questions.explanation: Minor copying for teaching is permitted only where the use is fair and reasonable, and the amount and substantiality of the portion used is one of the four factors for judging fairness.
questions.source_excerpt: Minor acts of copying are permitted for teaching purposes, as long as the use is considered fair and reasonable. ... There are four factors to consider when determining whether your use is a fair one. ... The amount and substantially of the portion used in relation to the copyrighted ... work as a whole

questions.question: A library member has two books on loan, both due tomorrow. They want to borrow a third book today and renew the two they have. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: A third book is within the limit, and all three loans can then be renewed automatically
A third book is allowed once a further deposit is paid, and renewal needs no availability check
A third book exceeds the 2-item limit; the two may be renewed before they are due, if resources allow
A third book is refused, and the two books can be renewed only after the return date has passed
questions.explanation: Members can borrow up to 2 materials for 1 week, and can renew before the return date expires depending on the availability of resources.
questions.source_excerpt: Members can borrow up to 2 materials for 1 week. ... Depending on the availability of resources, members can renew the borrowing before the ... return date expires.

questions.question: A student successfully completes their programme but lost one borrowed library book earlier in the year. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what may happen to their library membership deposit?
options: It may be forfeited, as loss of any study materials can result in forfeiting the deposit
It must be refunded in full, as the only refund condition is completing the programme successfully
It must be refunded, less a 10p daily charge counted from the date the lost book was due back
It may be held for three months, in line with the claim period for unused printing credit
questions.explanation: Although the deposit is refunded on successful completion, the Guide states that damage or loss of any study materials may result in the student forfeiting it.
questions.source_excerpt: Registration for membership is free but will require a ... deposit, that will be refunded to the student once their programme is successfully completed. Damage or loss of any of the study materials may result in the student forfeiting the ... deposit.

questions.question: A student leaving their course before completion, with all library items returned undamaged, asks about their library deposit and unused printing credit. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: Both must be claimed within three months of the date the student leaves the course
The deposit is forfeited on leaving early, but credit can be claimed within three months
Neither can be reclaimed, as both are refunded only on successful programme completion
Both can be reclaimed, and the Guide sets a three-month claim limit only for the credit
questions.explanation: The deposit can be reclaimed when a student leaves before completion, while the three-month claim limit is stated only for the remaining printing credit balance.
questions.source_excerpt: Deposit can be reclaimed after the completion of the programme or when the student leaves the course, should this occur before completion. ... Any remaining balance must be claimed within three months of the course completion date or date of course withdrawal/termination.

questions.question: A student asks whether they can keep printing with their remaining top-up credit for a few months after their programme ends. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: Credit may be used for up to three months after completion, after which any remaining balance lapses
Credit should be used before completion; any remaining balance must be claimed within three months
Credit may be used until the next academic year begins, when any remaining balance is then refunded
Credit may be used at any time after completion, as a topped-up balance never expires once it is paid
questions.explanation: Top-up credit should be used before the programme completion date; the three-month period is for claiming any remaining balance, not for continuing to print.
questions.source_excerpt: Top-up credit should be used before the programme completion date. Any remaining balance must be claimed within three months of the course completion date or date of course withdrawal/termination.

questions.question: A new student who has not yet printed, photocopied or topped up needs to print a 30-page document. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is the minimum top-up needed, and where is it made?
options: £1.50, topped up on their Student Portal account
50p, topped up on their Student Portal account
50p, paid to the librarian at the LRC desk
£1, topped up at the photocopier panel
questions.explanation: 30 pages at 5p a page costs £1.50; everyone starts with £1 credit, so a 50p top-up is needed, made on the Student Portal account.
questions.source_excerpt: Printing & photocopying costs 5p a page. Everyone starts off with ... credit already on their ID card. You can top up your printing credit on your Student Portal account.

questions.question: A student wants to photocopy a page from a book and then print an essay in the LRC. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which of these tasks requires them to log into a computer first?
options: Only printing, as photocopying needs just the ID card on the photocopier panel
Only photocopying, as printing is sent straight from the student's Student Portal
Both tasks, as each is released only after logging in with the student's ID
Neither task, as both are carried out by asking the librarian at the LRC desk
questions.explanation: Photocopying needs only the ID card touched on the photocopier panel, whereas printing requires logging into a computer to send the print command before touching the panel.
questions.source_excerpt: Photocopying: Simply touch your ID card on the panel of the photocopier and follow the on-screen instruction. Printing: For printing log into any computer with your ID and send the print command (papercut option) of the document you wish. Then touch the photocopier panel with your ID card.

questions.question: A student tries to log into a College computer using their ID number without the LCC prefix and the password they set on the LCC Admission Form. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, what is wrong?
options: Only the username, as the Admission Form password is the correct one for College computers
Only the password, as the ID number without the LCC prefix is the correct username on College computers
Neither, as College computers accept any of the student's College usernames and passwords
Both: the username is the full ID starting LCC and the password is the DDMMYYYY date of birth
questions.explanation: For College computers the username is the full student ID starting with LCC and the password is the date of birth in DDMMYYYY format; the Admission Form password is for the Student Portal.
questions.source_excerpt: Logging into a Computer Your username is your full student ID number starting with "LCC". Your password will be your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format.

questions.question: A student who has not registered for library membership asks how to reach the BIBLIU digital library. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: They must first register for library membership and pay the refundable deposit
They can, but only once LRC staff have approved a digital library access request
They can, as all students have access, using the link on the Moodle site
They can, as all students have access, using a link emailed by the librarian on request
questions.explanation: Membership is needed to hire out books or study materials, but all students have access to digital library services such as BIBLIU, whose access link is on the Moodle site.
questions.source_excerpt: All the College's students have access to third-party digital library services such as BIBLIU and JSTOR. The access link to BIBLIU is on the Moodle site.

questions.question: A student asks LRC staff for help finding information for a personal development interest unrelated to any assignment. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which is correct?
options: LRC staff support only information searches that are needed for assessed assignments
LRC staff help develop skills to find information for assignments or personal development
LRC staff may help only outside open times, by an appointment booked on the Student Portal
LRC staff must refer the student to a local library, as the LRC supports coursework only
questions.explanation: LRC staff are available during open times to help students develop the skills to find information for their assignments or to further their own personal development.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC ensures that LRC staff members are always available during open times to help you develop the skills required to find the information needed to complete your assignments or to further your own personal development.

questions.question: A student wants to use the JSTOR digital library. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which route and log-in details are correct?
options: Log into the Student Portal with the full LCC ID and Admission Form password, then use the JSTOR link
Log into Moodle with the full LCC ID and date of birth password, then use the JSTOR link there
Log into the Student Portal with the full LCC ID and date of birth password, then use the JSTOR link
Log into a College computer, as JSTOR is available only on the intranet at each LRC site
questions.explanation: The JSTOR access link is on the student portal, and the Portal is accessed with the full LCC student ID and the password set up on the LCC Admission Form.
questions.source_excerpt: The College offers the digital library services (e.g., JSTOR) that students can access through the Student Portal; ... Logging into your Student Portal Your username is your full student ID number starting with "LCC", and your password is the one you set up when filling in the LCC Admission Form. ... The access link to JSTOR is on the student portal site.

questions.question: A library member returns one borrowed book four days late and another book damaged. Under the Learning Resource Centre and IT Services Guide, which consequences may follow?
options: A 20p charge for the late book at 5p per day, and possible forfeiture of the deposit
Forfeiture of the deposit for both books, with no separate daily charge
A 40p charge for the late book, with no consequence for the damaged book
A 40p charge for the late book, and possible forfeiture of the deposit for the damage
questions.explanation: Late materials are charged at 10p per day, so four days costs 40p, and damage to study materials may result in the student forfeiting the deposit.
questions.source_excerpt: Damage or loss of any of the study materials may result in the student forfeiting the ... deposit. ... There will be a charge of 10p per day for materials exceeding the return date.

policies.title: Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy

questions.question: During an open day, a visiting parent asks a member of staff whether they may use the College's prayer/multi-faith room. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, how should the staff member respond?
options: Allow it, as the room is open to visitors of any faith on College open days
Allow it once the parent has signed in at reception as a visitor
Explain that the room is for the use of LCC students and staff only
Allow it, provided a member of staff accompanies the parent throughout
questions.explanation: The policy restricts the prayer/multi-faith room to students and staff of LCC only, so visitors such as parents are not permitted to use it.
questions.source_excerpt: The prayer/multi-faith room is for the use of students and staff of the LCC only

questions.question: A student society asks to use the prayer/multi-faith room to host a talk by a visiting speaker on their faith. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, how should you respond?
options: Agree, provided the visiting speaker has been vetted and approved by the Prevent Lead
Decline, as the room is for individual prayer only, not speakers' events
Agree, provided the talk is open to students and staff of all faiths
Agree, provided it is booked outside the regular agreed prayer times
questions.explanation: The policy states the room is available for individual prayer only and is not available for teaching or any form of speakers' event other than prayer.
questions.source_excerpt: It is available for individual prayer only; 2.4.It is not available for teaching or any other form of speakers' event other than prayer

questions.question: You are the Facilities Manager and notice an unusual occurrence in the corridor right beside the Prayer and Faith Room. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what must you do?
options: Log it and raise it at the next annual policy review
Report it directly to the Board of Directors
Report it to the PEG within 24 hours of the incident
Report it to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible
questions.explanation: The policy requires the Facilities Manager to report any unusual occurrence within or around the proximity of the Prayer and Faith Room to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible.
questions.source_excerpt: The Facilities Manager is required to report any unusual occurrence within or around the proximity of the Prayer and Faith Room to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, if the Prevent Lead believes after investigation that the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy, when must they inform members of the Principal Executive Group (PEG)?
options: Within 24 hours of confirming findings
Within 48 hours of confirming findings
Within 5 working days of the concern being raised
At the next scheduled PEG meeting
questions.explanation: The policy states the Prevent Lead must inform PEG members within 24 hours of confirming findings where they believe the College is at risk.
questions.source_excerpt: If the Prevent Lead, following investigation, believe the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy, they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members within 24 hours of confirming findings

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what must the Prevent Lead do when concerns are presented by the Facilities Manager?
options: Refer them straight to the police and take no further internal action
Fully investigate them and provide a report showing the action taken
Pass them to the PEG for a decision without investigating them first
Log them and review them with the Facilities Manager at the annual review
questions.explanation: The policy requires the Prevent Lead to fully investigate concerns presented by the Facilities Manager and to provide a report demonstrating the action taken as a result of the referral.
questions.source_excerpt: The Prevent Lead is required under the terms of the Policy to fully investigate any concerns presented by the Facilities Manager; 5.4.The Prevent Lead is responsible for providing a report demonstrating the action taken as a result of the referral

questions.question: Two faith groups both need the prayer/multi-faith room at overlapping times each week. According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, how should the space be shared?
options: By giving priority to whichever group booked the room first each week
By giving the larger group priority and moving the other group to a classroom
By having the Facilities Manager set fixed slots without consulting the groups
By consulting all user groups, agreeing timings and communicating clearly
questions.explanation: The policy says that where different faith groups need the room at different times, the space should be shared by consulting all user groups, agreeing timings and ensuring clear communication.
questions.source_excerpt: the space should be shared by consulting with all the user groups, i.e., agreement of timings, and making sure the communications are clear.

questions.question: A student asks whether they can put up a poster promoting their faith society's events inside the prayer/multi-faith room. What does the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy advise?
options: It is strongly recommended not to display such materials in the room
Posters are permitted if every faith is given equal display space in the room
It is recommended that posters are first approved by the Facilities Manager
Posters are permitted for up to one week before the society's event
questions.explanation: The policy strongly recommends that no faith-related posters or promotional materials are displayed within the room.
questions.source_excerpt: It is strongly recommended not to display any faith-related posters or promotional materials within the room

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which rule applies to anyone using the prayer/multi-faith room?
options: Shoes are not permitted inside the room, to preserve its significance
Users must book a slot with the Prevent Lead in advance of each visit
Users must sign in with the Facilities Manager before entering the room
The room is reserved for use outside timetabled teaching hours
questions.explanation: The policy states that shoes are not permitted within the room in order to preserve its significance; it sets no booking, sign-in or teaching-hours rule.
questions.source_excerpt: In addition, shoes are not permitted within the room to preserve the significance

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, who has ongoing responsibility for the delivery of the policy?
options: The Prevent Lead
The Facilities Manager
The multi-faith management group
The Principal Executive Group (PEG)
questions.explanation: The Monitoring and Review Procedure states that the Facilities Manager has an ongoing responsibility for delivering the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: The Facilities Manager has an ongoing responsibility for the delivery of this policy

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what applies to any religious scripture stored in the prayer/multi-faith room's bookshelf or any other location?
options: It must be removed by users at the end of each day
It may be kept there if donated by a recognised faith body
It is subject to review by the management team
It must be catalogued and approved by the Prevent Lead
questions.explanation: The policy states that any religious scripture stored in the bookshelf or elsewhere is subject to review by the management team.
questions.source_excerpt: Any religious scripture stored in the bookshelf or any other location is subject to review by the management team.

questions.question: The Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy was produced in response to the development of which other College policy?
options: The LCC Equality Policy
The LCC Prevent Policy
The LCC Welfare Policy
The LCC Estates Policy
questions.explanation: The introduction states that the policy was produced in response to the development of the LCC Prevent Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy has been produced in response to the development of the LCC Prevent Policy

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, to whom does the policy apply?
options: Students who are registered members of a recognised College faith society
Staff and students who hold a regular weekly prayer booking with the College
The Facilities Manager and members of the multi-faith management group only
All staff and students wishing to make use of the multi-faith facilities provided
questions.explanation: The introduction states that the policy applies to all staff and students wishing to make use of the multi-faith facilities provided.
questions.source_excerpt: It is applicable to all staff and students wishing to make use of the multi-faith facilities provided.

questions.question: Which statement about faith and the prayer/multi-faith room is correct under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy?
options: Its use is not restricted to any one particular faith
It is reserved for faiths with a student society
It is reserved for faiths approved by the Prevent Lead
It is allocated termly to the faith with most users
questions.explanation: The user guidance states that the room is a multi-faith room and is not restricted to any one particular faith.
questions.source_excerpt: The room is a multi-faith room and is not restricted to any one particular faith

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what type of prayer is the prayer/multi-faith room available for?
options: Group prayer at set times
Society-led prayer only
Individual prayer only
Individual and group prayer
questions.explanation: The user guidance states that the room is available for individual prayer only.
questions.source_excerpt: It is available for individual prayer only

questions.question: What does the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy say about using the prayer/multi-faith room for teaching?
options: It is available for teaching when no prayer is taking place
It is not available for teaching, only for prayer
It is available for faith-related teaching only
It is available for teaching once booked with the Facilities Manager
questions.explanation: The user guidance states that the room is not available for teaching or any form of speakers' event other than prayer.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not available for teaching or any other form of speakers' event other than prayer

questions.question: What does the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy advise users about food and drink in the prayer/multi-faith room?
options: Users are advised to avoid consuming food and drink whilst inside
Food and drink may be consumed if users clean up afterwards
Only drinks in sealed containers may be brought into the room
Food may be consumed only as part of a religious observance
questions.explanation: The policy describes the rooms as clean areas and advises users to avoid the consumption of food and drink whilst inside.
questions.source_excerpt: The prayer/multi-faith room are clean areas and users are advised to avoid the consumption of food and drink whilst inside.

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what situation may require the prayer/multi-faith room to be shared between users?
options: Teaching staff needing the room when classrooms are overbooked
Visitors requesting the room during College open days
Societies needing the room for their speaker events
Different faith groups requiring the room at different times
questions.explanation: The policy anticipates different faith groups requiring the room at different times; teaching, visitors and speaker events are not permitted uses of the room at all.
questions.source_excerpt: Sharing space with different faith groups who may require the room at different times

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, who will ensure they are aware of, and make provision for, different expressions of religious etiquette?
options: The Prevent Lead
The Principal Executive Group (PEG)
The multi-faith management group
The College Oversight Board
questions.explanation: The Etiquette section states that the multi-faith management group will ensure it is aware of and makes provision for different expressions of religious etiquette.
questions.source_excerpt: Different faith groups and cultures may have different expressions of religious etiquette ... The multi-faith management group will ensure to be aware of and make provision for such cases.

questions.question: Which of the following does the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy give as an example of religious etiquette that may differ between faith groups?
options: Limiting conversation in the space
Covering the head before entering
Facing a set direction to pray
Bringing a personal prayer mat
questions.explanation: The Etiquette section gives removal of shoes, limiting conversation in the space and keeping the space clean as examples of religious etiquette.
questions.source_excerpt: Different faith groups and cultures may have different expressions of religious etiquette, i.e., removal of shoes, limiting conversation in space, or the necessity for the space to be kept clean.

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which unusual occurrences is the Facilities Manager required to report?
options: Those taking place inside the Prayer and Faith Room itself, but not nearby
Any within or around the proximity of the Prayer and Faith Room
Those that a student or member of staff has reported to them in writing
Those that happen during agreed prayer timings
questions.explanation: The policy requires the Facilities Manager to report any unusual occurrence within or around the proximity of the Prayer and Faith Room.
questions.source_excerpt: The Facilities Manager is required to report any unusual occurrence within or around the proximity of the Prayer and Faith Room

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, who is required to fully investigate any concerns presented by the Facilities Manager?
options: The multi-faith management group
The College's Board of Directors
The College Oversight Board
The College's Prevent Lead
questions.explanation: The Monitoring and Review Procedure states that the Prevent Lead is required to fully investigate any concerns presented by the Facilities Manager.
questions.source_excerpt: The Prevent Lead is required under the terms of the Policy to fully investigate any concerns presented by the Facilities Manager

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, whom must the Prevent Lead inform if, following investigation, they believe the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy?
options: The Facilities Manager and the multi-faith management group
The Designated Safeguarding Lead and the Students' Union
Members of the Principal Executive Group (PEG)
The Office for Students and the local authority Prevent team
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Prevent Lead must inform Principal Executive Group (PEG) members if they believe the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: If the Prevent Lead, following investigation, believe the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy, they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what will the Principal Executive Group (PEG) do about a Prevent risk to the College reported to it by the Prevent Lead?
options: Take no action until the Board of Directors has approved a response
Take any action it deems necessary to mitigate the risk to the College
Act only on written recommendations made by the Facilities Manager
Wait until the next policy review before taking any action on the risk
questions.explanation: The policy states that the PEG will take any action it deems necessary to mitigate the risk to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: The PEG will take any action it deems necessary to mitigate the risk to the College

questions.question: According to the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, to whom does the PEG report any concern or unusual occurrence coming forward under the Prevent Policy?
options: The College Oversight Board and the Board of Directors
The Office for Students and the local Prevent coordinator
The Facilities Manager and the multi-faith management group
The Academic Board and the Quality Assurance Board
questions.explanation: The policy states that the PEG will report any concern or unusual occurrence under the Prevent Policy to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.
questions.source_excerpt: The PEG will report any concern or unusual occurrence coming forward under the Prevent Policy to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what must the report provided by the Prevent Lead following a referral demonstrate?
options: The number of students using the room
The agreed prayer timings for each group
The scripture held on the room's bookshelf
The action taken as a result of the referral
questions.explanation: The policy makes the Prevent Lead responsible for providing a report demonstrating the action taken as a result of the referral.
questions.source_excerpt: The Prevent Lead is responsible for providing a report demonstrating the action taken as a result of the referral

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, how quickly must the Facilities Manager report an unusual occurrence in or near the Prayer and Faith Room?
options: Within five working days
By the end of the term
As soon as possible
At the next policy review
questions.explanation: The policy requires the Facilities Manager to report any unusual occurrence within or around the room as soon as possible.
questions.source_excerpt: The Facilities Manager is required to report any unusual occurrence within or around the proximity of the Prayer and Faith Room to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, in what order is an unusual occurrence near the Prayer and Faith Room escalated where the Prevent Lead confirms a risk to the College?
options: Facilities Manager → Prevent Lead → PEG → College Oversight Board and Board of Directors
Facilities Manager → PEG → Prevent Lead → College Oversight Board and Board of Directors
Prevent Lead → Facilities Manager → PEG → College Oversight Board and Board of Directors
Facilities Manager → Prevent Lead → Board of Directors → PEG and College Oversight Board
questions.explanation: The Facilities Manager reports to the Prevent Lead, who informs PEG members if they believe the College is at risk; the PEG then reports to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.
questions.source_excerpt: report any unusual occurrence within or around the proximity of the Prayer and Faith Room to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible ... they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members ... The PEG will report any concern or unusual occurrence coming forward under the Prevent Policy to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.

questions.question: A student enters the prayer/multi-faith room wearing shoes and carrying a hot drink. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which statement correctly reflects the user guidance?
options: Shoes may be kept on if clean, but drinks are banned inside under any circumstances
Both are acceptable, provided the student leaves the room clean after praying
Shoes are not permitted inside, and users are advised to avoid drinking there
Drinks are fine if sealed, and shoes need removing only during actual prayer
questions.explanation: The policy says shoes are not permitted within the room, while users are advised to avoid consuming food and drink whilst inside.
questions.source_excerpt: users are advised to avoid the consumption of food and drink whilst inside. In addition, shoes are not permitted within the room to preserve the significance

questions.question: A student leaves copies of a religious text on a windowsill in the prayer/multi-faith room rather than on the bookshelf. How does the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy treat this scripture?
options: It is exempt from review, as only scripture on the bookshelf is reviewed
It is subject to review by the management team, wherever it is stored
It must be reported to the Prevent Lead as an unusual occurrence
It must be moved to the bookshelf and logged by the Facilities Manager
questions.explanation: The policy makes any religious scripture stored in the bookshelf or any other location subject to review by the management team, so its location does not matter.
questions.source_excerpt: Any religious scripture stored in the bookshelf or any other location is subject to review by the management team.

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what condition must be met before the Prevent Lead is required to inform members of the Principal Executive Group (PEG)?
options: The Facilities Manager must have reported the occurrence in writing
The concern must have been raised by at least two members of staff
The multi-faith management group must have endorsed the referral
After investigating, the Prevent Lead must believe the College is at risk
questions.explanation: The duty to inform PEG members arises only where the Prevent Lead, following investigation, believes the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: If the Prevent Lead, following investigation, believe the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy, they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members within 24 hours of confirming findings

questions.question: Which pairing of role and responsibility is correct under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy?
options: Prevent Lead – reports unusual occurrences near the room to the Facilities Manager
Multi-faith management group – informs PEG members of confirmed Prevent risks
College Oversight Board – takes any action needed to mitigate the risk
Facilities Manager – has ongoing responsibility for delivering the policy
questions.explanation: The Facilities Manager has ongoing responsibility for delivering the policy; it is the Facilities Manager who reports to the Prevent Lead, the Prevent Lead who informs PEG, and the PEG that mitigates the risk.
questions.source_excerpt: The Facilities Manager has an ongoing responsibility for the delivery of this policy

questions.question: Faith groups using the prayer/multi-faith room observe different etiquette, such as limiting conversation in the space. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what is expected of the multi-faith management group?
options: To apply one standard of etiquette, based on the group with the most users
To be aware of such differences and make provision for them
To refer each differing practice to the Prevent Lead for review
To limit use of the room to groups sharing the same etiquette
questions.explanation: The Etiquette section says the multi-faith management group will ensure it is aware of and makes provision for different expressions of religious etiquette.
questions.source_excerpt: Different faith groups and cultures may have different expressions of religious etiquette, i.e., removal of shoes, limiting conversation in space ... The multi-faith management group will ensure to be aware of and make provision for such cases.

questions.question: The Prevent Lead has investigated a concern about the prayer/multi-faith room and confirmed findings that the College is at risk. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, who takes action to mitigate the risk to the College?
options: The Facilities Manager, as the person responsible for delivering the policy
The multi-faith management group, after consulting all the user groups
The PEG, once its members have been informed by the Prevent Lead
The Board of Directors, on receiving the Prevent Lead's report directly
questions.explanation: The Prevent Lead must inform PEG members of a confirmed risk, and the PEG will then take any action it deems necessary to mitigate the risk to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members within 24 hours of confirming findings; 5.6.The PEG will take any action it deems necessary to mitigate the risk to the College

questions.question: A faith group asks for the prayer/multi-faith room to be reserved exclusively for its own members. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, how should this request be handled?
options: Decline, as the room is not restricted to any one faith
Grant it, if the group has the most regular users of the room
Grant it, once the request is approved by the Prevent Lead
Grant it, provided the group keeps the room clean and tidy
questions.explanation: The policy states the room is a multi-faith room that is not restricted to any one particular faith, so it cannot be reserved for one group's exclusive use.
questions.source_excerpt: The room is a multi-faith room and is not restricted to any one particular faith

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which timeframes apply to the Facilities Manager reporting an unusual occurrence and to the Prevent Lead informing PEG of a confirmed risk?
options: Facilities Manager: within 24 hours; Prevent Lead to PEG: as soon as possible
Facilities Manager: as soon as possible; Prevent Lead to PEG: within 24 hours of confirming findings
Facilities Manager: within 24 hours; Prevent Lead to PEG: within 48 hours of confirming findings
Facilities Manager: as soon as possible; Prevent Lead to PEG: within 5 working days of confirming findings
questions.explanation: The Facilities Manager must report to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible, and the Prevent Lead must inform PEG members within 24 hours of confirming findings.
questions.source_excerpt: to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible ... they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members within 24 hours of confirming findings

questions.question: A lecturer whose classroom has been double-booked asks to run a one-hour seminar in the prayer/multi-faith room while nobody is praying. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what is the correct response?
options: Agree, as the room may be used for teaching whenever it is empty
Agree, provided the Facilities Manager approves the booking first
Agree, provided shoes are removed and no food or drink is taken in
Decline, as the room is not available for teaching or speakers' events
questions.explanation: The policy states the room is not available for teaching or any other form of speakers' event other than prayer, regardless of whether it is in use.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not available for teaching or any other form of speakers' event other than prayer

questions.question: The PEG has taken action to mitigate a Prevent risk arising from the prayer/multi-faith room and considers the matter resolved. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what should happen next?
options: The PEG reports it to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors
Nothing further, as resolved concerns do not need to be reported
The Facilities Manager records it for the next annual policy review
The Prevent Lead reopens the investigation to confirm the outcome
questions.explanation: The PEG will report any concern or unusual occurrence coming forward under the Prevent Policy to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors, including one it has resolved.
questions.source_excerpt: The PEG will take any action it deems necessary to mitigate the risk to the College; 5.7.The PEG will report any concern or unusual occurrence coming forward under the Prevent Policy to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.

questions.question: The Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy notes that removal of shoes is part of some faiths' etiquette. How does its user guidance treat shoes in the prayer/multi-faith room?
options: Shoes must be removed only by users whose faith requires it
Removing shoes is recommended, but it is left to each user's choice
Shoes are not permitted within the room, whatever the user's faith
Shoes must be removed only during agreed group prayer timings
questions.explanation: Although the Etiquette section lists removal of shoes as one faith practice, the user guidance states that shoes are not permitted within the room, which applies to all users.
questions.source_excerpt: shoes are not permitted within the room to preserve the significance ... Different faith groups and cultures may have different expressions of religious etiquette, i.e., removal of shoes

questions.question: After fully investigating a concern referred by the Facilities Manager, the Prevent Lead concludes the College is not at risk under the Prevent Policy. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which of the Prevent Lead's duties still applies?
options: Informing PEG members within 24 hours of confirming the investigation's findings
Providing a report demonstrating the action taken on the referral
Reporting the concern to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors
Asking the multi-faith management group to re-investigate the concern
questions.explanation: The Prevent Lead must always provide a report demonstrating the action taken on the referral; informing PEG is required only where the Prevent Lead believes the College is at risk.
questions.source_excerpt: The Prevent Lead is responsible for providing a report demonstrating the action taken as a result of the referral; ... If the Prevent Lead, following investigation, believe the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy, they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members
