questions.question: A member of staff wants to use the prayer/multi-faith room for individual prayer during a break, but a colleague says the room is for students only. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, who is right?
options: The staff member, as the room is for the use of LCC students and staff
The colleague, as staff may use the room only outside term time
The colleague, as staff must first be approved by the Prevent Lead
The staff member, but only with the Facilities Manager's written consent
questions.explanation: The policy states the prayer/multi-faith room is for the use of students and staff of LCC, and it is available for individual prayer.
questions.source_excerpt: The prayer/multi-faith room is for the use of students and staff of the LCC only; 2.2.The room is a multi-faith room and is not restricted to any one particular faith; 2.3.It is available for individual prayer only

questions.question: The Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy words some of its user guidance as advice or a recommendation and some as a firm rule. Which of the following is stated as a firm rule rather than advice?
options: Food is not to be eaten inside the room
Drinks are not to be consumed inside the room
Shoes are not to be worn inside the room
Faith-related posters are not to be displayed in the room
questions.explanation: Shoes are 'not permitted' within the room, whereas users are only 'advised to avoid' food and drink, and it is 'strongly recommended' not to display faith-related posters.
questions.source_excerpt: users are advised to avoid the consumption of food and drink whilst inside. In addition, shoes are not permitted within the room to preserve the significance; 2.6.It is strongly recommended not to display any faith-related posters or promotional materials within the room

questions.question: An LCC student asks to bring a friend who studies at another university into the prayer/multi-faith room so that they can pray there together. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what is the correct response?
options: Allow it, provided the LCC student stays with the friend for the whole visit
Decline, as the room is for LCC students and staff only, and for individual prayer
Allow it, provided the friend shares the same faith as the LCC student
Allow it, once the friend has signed in with the Facilities Manager as a guest
questions.explanation: The room is for the use of LCC students and staff only, so the friend cannot use it, and it is available for individual prayer only, not for praying together.
questions.source_excerpt: The prayer/multi-faith room is for the use of students and staff of the LCC only ... It is available for individual prayer only

questions.question: Three faith groups use the prayer/multi-faith room. Timings are agreed with the two larger groups only and are then clearly circulated to everyone. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what has been missed?
options: Consulting all the user groups, including the smaller one, when agreeing timings
Having the agreed timings approved by the Prevent Lead before they are circulated
Having the agreed timings ratified by the Principal Executive Group (PEG)
Giving the smaller group first priority, as the room serves every faith
questions.explanation: The policy says the space should be shared by consulting with all the user groups when agreeing timings; clear communication alone does not make up for leaving a group out.
questions.source_excerpt: the space should be shared by consulting with all the user groups, i.e., agreement of timings, and making sure the communications are clear.

questions.question: Timings for the prayer/multi-faith room were agreed after consulting every user group, but the timetable was never circulated and users keep arriving at clashing times. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which element of sharing the space has not been met?
options: Obtaining the Prevent Lead's approval for the timetable
Consulting with all the user groups before agreeing timings
Making sure communications about agreed timings are clear
Having the PEG ratify the timings before they take effect
questions.explanation: Sharing the space requires consulting all user groups, agreeing timings and making sure the communications are clear; here only the clear communication was missing.
questions.source_excerpt: in such cases the space should be shared by consulting with all the user groups, i.e., agreement of timings, and making sure the communications are clear.

questions.question: A new faith group whose etiquette includes limiting conversation starts using the prayer/multi-faith room, which another group also needs at similar times. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, how should this be handled?
options: The Facilities Manager sets one etiquette standard for all users and allocates prayer slots without any consultation
Timings are agreed by consulting all user groups, and the multi-faith management group makes provision for the etiquette
The Prevent Lead reviews the new group's practices and approves them before it may use the room at all
The group with the most regular users decides both the prayer timings and the etiquette that applies to everyone in the room
questions.explanation: Sharing is handled by consulting all user groups and agreeing timings, and the multi-faith management group makes provision for different expressions of religious etiquette.
questions.source_excerpt: in such cases the space should be shared by consulting with all the user groups, i.e., agreement of timings ... The multi-faith management group will ensure to be aware of and make provision for such cases.

questions.question: Some faith groups regard it as necessary for the prayer space to be kept clean. Which provision in the user guidance of the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy reflects this?
options: Each faith group must clean the room at the end of its agreed timing
Users are advised to avoid food and drink, as the room is a clean area
Users must sign a cleanliness agreement with the Facilities Manager
Scripture may be kept only on the bookshelf so the room stays tidy
questions.explanation: The user guidance describes the room as a clean area and advises users to avoid consuming food and drink inside, which matches the etiquette of keeping the space clean.
questions.source_excerpt: The prayer/multi-faith room are clean areas and users are advised to avoid the consumption of food and drink whilst inside. ... the necessity for the space to be kept clean.

questions.question: The Facilities Manager reports an unusual occurrence near the Prayer and Faith Room on a Monday. The Prevent Lead investigates and, at 4pm that Friday, confirms findings that the College is at risk. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, by when must PEG members be informed?
options: By Tuesday, 24 hours after the Facilities Manager's report was received
At the next scheduled PEG meeting after the Prevent Lead's report
By 4pm on Saturday, 24 hours after the findings were confirmed
By the following Friday, five working days after confirming findings
questions.explanation: The 24-hour deadline runs from confirming findings, not from the original report, so PEG members must be told by 4pm on Saturday.
questions.source_excerpt: If the Prevent Lead, following investigation, believe the College is at risk under the Prevent Policy, they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members within 24 hours of confirming findings

questions.question: The Facilities Manager sees something unusual just outside the Prayer and Faith Room but is unsure whether it is a Prevent concern, so plans to look into it personally before telling anyone. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what should happen?
options: The Facilities Manager investigates first, as they are responsible for delivering the policy
The Facilities Manager reports it to PEG within 24 hours, once they judge that a risk exists
The Facilities Manager asks the multi-faith management group to assess it before any report
The Facilities Manager reports it to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible, who investigates it
questions.explanation: The Facilities Manager must report any unusual occurrence around the room to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible; investigating is the Prevent Lead's responsibility.
questions.source_excerpt: The Facilities Manager is required to report any unusual occurrence within or around the proximity of the Prayer and Faith Room to the Prevent Lead as soon as possible; 5.3.The Prevent Lead is required under the terms of the Policy to fully investigate any concerns presented by the Facilities Manager

questions.question: After confirming findings that the College is at risk, the Prevent Lead sends their report straight to the Board of Directors and takes no other step. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which required step has been missed?
options: Informing PEG members within 24 hours of confirming the findings
Informing the Facilities Manager within 24 hours of the findings
Referring the findings to the multi-faith management group for review
Obtaining the College Oversight Board's approval of the findings
questions.explanation: The Prevent Lead must inform PEG members within 24 hours of confirming findings; it is then the PEG that reports to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.
questions.source_excerpt: they must inform Principal Eexcutive Group (PEG) members within 24 hours of confirming findings ... The PEG will report any concern or unusual occurrence coming forward under the Prevent Policy to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.

questions.question: Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which of the following is not a responsibility of the Prevent Lead?
options: Fully investigating any concerns that are presented by the Facilities Manager
Providing a report demonstrating the action taken on the referral
Informing PEG members of a confirmed risk within 24 hours
Reporting concerns to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors
questions.explanation: Reporting concerns to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors is the PEG's role; the other three duties belong to the Prevent Lead.
questions.source_excerpt: The Prevent Lead is required under the terms of the Policy to fully investigate any concerns presented by the Facilities Manager ... The PEG will report any concern or unusual occurrence coming forward under the Prevent Policy to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.

questions.question: After investigating a referral from the Facilities Manager, the Prevent Lead asks the Facilities Manager to write the report on the outcome, since they deliver the policy. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what is the correct position?
options: The Facilities Manager writes it, as they have ongoing responsibility for delivering the policy
The Prevent Lead provides it, and it must demonstrate the action taken as a result of the referral
PEG writes it once informed, as it decides what action is needed to mitigate the risk
No report is needed unless the Prevent Lead's findings show that the College is at risk
questions.explanation: Although the Facilities Manager delivers the policy, the Prevent Lead is responsible for providing the report demonstrating the action taken as a result of the referral.
questions.source_excerpt: The Facilities Manager has an ongoing responsibility for the delivery of this policy ... The Prevent Lead is responsible for providing a report demonstrating the action taken as a result of the referral

questions.question: The library is full, so a student asks to use the empty prayer/multi-faith room for quiet individual revision, pointing out that this is neither teaching nor a speakers' event. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what is the correct response?
options: Allow it, as only teaching and speakers' events are excluded from the room
Allow it, provided the student removes their shoes and avoids eating inside
Decline, as the room is available for individual prayer only
Allow it, provided the revision falls outside the agreed prayer timings
questions.explanation: The room is available for individual prayer only, so other individual uses such as revision are not permitted even when they are not teaching or speakers' events.
questions.source_excerpt: It is available for individual prayer only; 2.4.It is not available for teaching or any other form of speakers' event other than prayer

questions.question: The Facilities Manager presents the Prevent Lead with a concern about the Prayer and Faith Room that the Prevent Lead considers minor. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, what must the Prevent Lead do?
options: Close it without investigation and note it for the next policy review
Pass it to PEG to decide whether any investigation is needed at all
Return it to the Facilities Manager to gather more evidence first
Fully investigate it, whatever its apparent seriousness
questions.explanation: The Prevent Lead is required to fully investigate any concerns presented by the Facilities Manager, however minor they seem.
questions.source_excerpt: The Prevent Lead is required under the terms of the Policy to fully investigate any concerns presented by the Facilities Manager

questions.question: A faith group argues that, because the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy expects clear communications when the prayer/multi-faith room is shared, it should put up a poster promoting its events inside the room. What is the correct position?
options: Clear communication of timings is expected, but promotional faith posters in the room are strongly recommended against
The poster is required, as the policy makes clear communications mandatory for every user group sharing the room
The poster may be displayed once the Facilities Manager has approved its content and wording in writing beforehand
Communications about agreed timings are optional for user groups, but all posters in the room are banned outright by the policy
questions.explanation: The sharing section expects clear communication of agreed timings, but the user guidance strongly recommends against displaying faith-related posters or promotional materials in the room.
questions.source_excerpt: making sure the communications are clear. ... It is strongly recommended not to display any faith-related posters or promotional materials within the room

questions.question: Which of these people is using the prayer/multi-faith room in line with all of the user guidance in the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy?
options: A student's visiting parent who removes their shoes, prays individually and eats nothing inside
An LCC staff member who prays individually but keeps their shoes on because the floor is cold
An LCC student who removes their shoes and gives a short talk on prayer to other students
An LCC student who removes their shoes, prays individually and avoids eating or drinking inside
questions.explanation: Only the LCC student meets every point: the room is for LCC students and staff, for individual prayer only, shoes are not permitted and food and drink should be avoided.
questions.source_excerpt: The prayer/multi-faith room is for the use of students and staff of the LCC only ... It is available for individual prayer only; 2.4.It is not available for teaching or any other form of speakers' event other than prayer ... shoes are not permitted within the room

questions.question: Once PEG members have been informed by the Prevent Lead of a confirmed risk, which matter does the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy leave to the PEG's own judgement?
options: What action is necessary to mitigate the risk to the College
Whether to report the concern to the Oversight Board and Board of Directors
Whether the Prevent Lead must still provide a report on the action taken
Whether the Prevent Lead was required to inform it within 24 hours
questions.explanation: The PEG will take any action it deems necessary to mitigate the risk, but the policy fixes that it will report to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.
questions.source_excerpt: The PEG will take any action it deems necessary to mitigate the risk to the College; 5.7.The PEG will report any concern or unusual occurrence coming forward under the Prevent Policy to the College Oversight Board and Board of Directors.

questions.question: A user of the prayer/multi-faith room tells a student chatting quietly there that the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy forbids all conversation in the room. How does the policy actually treat limiting conversation?
options: As a firm user-guidance rule forbidding conversation, stated in the same terms as the rule that shoes are not permitted
As user-guidance advice to avoid conversation, worded in the same way as the advice to avoid food and drink inside
As a limit on conversation that applies only during the timings agreed by consulting all the user groups
As an example of differing faith-group etiquette, for which the multi-faith management group makes provision
questions.explanation: Limiting conversation appears only in the Etiquette section as an expression of etiquette that some faith groups may have, for the multi-faith management group to make provision for; the user guidance contains no rule or advice on conversation.
questions.source_excerpt: Different faith groups and cultures may have different expressions of religious etiquette, i.e., removal of shoes, limiting conversation in space, or the necessity for the space to be kept clean. The multi-faith management group will ensure to be aware of and make provision for such cases.

questions.question: A faith society pins leaflets promoting its events on the prayer/multi-faith room wall and leaves its scripture on the bookshelf, arguing that as the room is not restricted to any one faith, nothing it brings can be limited. Under the Management of Prayer and Multi-Faith Facilities Policy, which statement is correct?
options: Both must be approved by the Prevent Lead, as any faith material in the room is a possible Prevent concern
The society is right, as in a multi-faith room neither the leaflets nor the scripture falls under any user-guidance provision
Displaying the leaflets is strongly recommended against, and the scripture is subject to management team review
The leaflets may stay if the Facilities Manager approves them, and the scripture must be kept on the bookshelf only
questions.explanation: The policy strongly recommends against displaying faith-related posters or promotional materials in the room, and makes any religious scripture stored there subject to review by the management team.
questions.source_excerpt: It is strongly recommended not to display any faith-related posters or promotional materials within the room; 2.7.Any religious scripture stored in the bookshelf or any other location is subject to review by the management team.

questions.question: You are a tutor marking an assignment and know that the student has submitted a mitigating circumstances claim. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, how must you mark the work?
options: Mark it as presented, taking no account of the mitigating circumstances.
Apply a small uplift to the mark to reflect the circumstances the student has reported.
Mark it leniently and record the claim in your feedback.
Mark it against a reduced set of assessment criteria agreed with the Registrar.
questions.explanation: The policy requires tutors to mark all work as presented, with no account taken of mitigating circumstances at the marking stage.
questions.source_excerpt: All student work must be marked by tutors as presented with no account taken of mitigating circumstances at this stage.

questions.question: According to the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, by when must a mitigating circumstances claim normally be submitted?
options: On or before the assessment deadline.
Within 14 working days after the assessment deadline.
Within five weeks of the assessment results being published.
Before any appeal is heard.
questions.explanation: The policy requires all claims to be submitted on or before the assessment deadline unless there are compelling grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: All claims must be submitted on or before the assessment deadline unless there are compelling grounds.

questions.question: A student had compelling grounds for missing the normal deadline for a mitigating circumstances claim. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what is the latest point by which they must submit the claim?
options: Within 48 hours of returning to the College after the absence.
Within 14 working days of the assessment results being released.
At least one week before the Assessment and Progression Board meeting.
At least four weeks before the Assessment and Progression Board meeting.
questions.explanation: Students with compelling grounds must submit their claim at least one week before the Assessment and Progression Board meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with compelling grounds must submit the claim at least one week before the Assessment and Progression Board meeting.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, where must a student's mitigating circumstances claim be submitted in the first instance?
options: To the module tutor who set the affected assessment.
To the College reception, care of the Registrar.
To the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board.
To the Appeal Panel through the Student Portal.
questions.explanation: The procedure requires claims to be submitted to the College reception, care of the Registrar, in the first instance.
questions.source_excerpt: The claims must be submitted to the College reception c/o the Registrar in the first instance.

questions.question: A student wants to support a mitigating circumstances claim with a scanned copy of a hospital letter. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what evidence is normally required?
options: The scanned copy, provided it is emailed directly to the Registrar.
Independent documentary evidence in its original form.
A photocopy of the letter certified as a true copy by their tutor.
A detailed personal statement written and signed by the student.
questions.explanation: The policy normally requires independent documentary evidence in its original form and states that photocopies or scanned copies will not be accepted.
questions.source_excerpt: Independent documentary evidence in its original form shall normally be required. Photocopies or scanned copies of evidence will not be accepted.

questions.question: How does the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure define mitigating circumstances?
options: Unexpected, significantly disruptive events beyond the student's control that could not reasonably be predicted.
Any difficulty a student reports during the assessment period, whether or not it could reasonably have been foreseen.
Circumstances the student could have predicted but which still caused them significant stress close to an assessment deadline.
Long-term conditions or disabilities that the student disclosed to the College at the point of enrolment.
questions.explanation: The policy defines mitigating circumstances as unexpected, significantly disruptive and beyond the student's control, and not reasonably predictable or able to be accommodated by the student.
questions.source_excerpt: Circumstances that are unexpected, significantly disruptive and beyond the control of the student, which could not be reasonably predicted or accommodated by the student, and which affects the student's ability to meet assessment deadlines or impairs the performance of the student in assessment.

questions.question: According to the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, how are a student's on-going conditions and other disabilities dealt with?
options: They are treated as mitigating circumstances automatically, without evidence.
They must be declared again on a Mitigating Circumstances Claim Form each term.
They are considered under the Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy.
They are referred straight to the Appeal Panel for a decision.
questions.explanation: The policy states that on-going conditions and other disabilities fall outside its scope and are considered under the Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: On-going conditions and other disabilities are considered under the "Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy" and thus do not fall within the confines of this policy.

questions.question: A student tells you they have been unwell, their assignment is only half finished and the deadline is tomorrow. They intend to make a mitigating circumstances claim. What does the Mitigating Circumstances Policy advise them to do with the work?
options: Hold the work back until the Assessment and Progression Board has decided on the claim.
Submit nothing, as a lodged claim itself removes the need to hand in the assignment.
Send the draft to the tutor to be marked with the circumstances in mind.
Make every effort to submit it by the deadline, even if it is incomplete.
questions.explanation: The policy advises students to make every effort to submit work by the deadline even if incomplete, or at the earliest opportunity on their return.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are advised that they must make every effort to submit work by the deadline even if it is incomplete

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, if the Board accepts that a student failed to submit coursework due to illness or another valid cause, what may it offer?
options: A resubmission within two weeks, with the mark capped at a pass.
An automatic pass for the module based on earlier grades.
Another chance to submit, up to an additional five weeks, without penalty.
A resubmission up to ten weeks later, with the standard late penalty applied.
questions.explanation: For coursework, the Board may offer another opportunity to submit by an agreed date up to an additional five weeks, as if for the first time and without penalty.
questions.source_excerpt: Course work: To offer the student another opportunity to submit the work by a date agreed by the Board up to an additional five weeks, as if for the first time and without penalty.

questions.question: According to the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, within what timeframe will a student normally be notified of the outcome of their claim?
options: Within five working days of submitting the claim.
Within 28 calendar days of the Assessment and Progression Board meeting.
At the end of the academic year, together with the student's final results.
Within approximately 14 working days of submitting the claim.
questions.explanation: The policy states the student will be notified of the outcome within approximately 14 working days of submitting the claim.
questions.source_excerpt: The student will be notified of the outcome within approximately 14 working days of the submission of the claim.

questions.question: After failing an exam, a student asks whether they can appeal the result on the grounds of a family bereavement before the exam, which they could reasonably have reported at the time but chose not to. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy, can they?
options: Yes, provided the bereavement is reported to the Registrar within 14 working days of the result.
No, as they could reasonably have reported it to the College in advance.
Yes, if their module tutor supports the appeal in writing.
Yes, because a close family bereavement overrides the normal claim deadlines.
questions.explanation: The policy states that students cannot appeal on the grounds of mitigating circumstances they could reasonably have reported to the College in advance.
questions.source_excerpt: Students cannot appeal against their results on the grounds of mitigating circumstances if they could reasonably have reported them to the College in advance.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, which of the following is one of the only two grounds on which a student may appeal a decision of the Assessment and Progression Board?
options: The student disagrees with the academic judgement of the markers.
The student believes the mark awarded is lower than their effort and attendance deserved.
The student was unaware of the deadline for submitting a mitigating circumstances claim.
An administrative error or procedural irregularity that casts doubt on the result.
questions.explanation: Appeals are allowed only on two grounds: previously unknown mitigating circumstances, or an administrative error or procedural irregularity that causes doubt as to whether the result might have been different.
questions.source_excerpt: Students have the right to appeal against a decision of the Assessment and Progression Board but only on these two grounds: ... there was an administrative error or procedural irregularity or other inadequacy in the conduct of the assessors or processing of marks or grades of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different

questions.question: According to the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, its aim is to be explicit, transparent and accessible for all students so that the policy, procedures and processes for claims are what?
options: Discretionary, binding and final.
Proportionate, flexible and swift.
Equitable, valid and reliable.
Standardised, automatic and uniform.
questions.explanation: The aim states the policy is explicit, transparent and accessible so that the policy, procedures and processes are equitable, valid and reliable.
questions.source_excerpt: The aim of the mitigating circumstances policy is that it is set out to be explicit, transparent, and accessible in relation to the mitigating circumstances claim for all students to ensure that the policy, procedures, and processes are equitable, valid, and reliable.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, how must applications for mitigating circumstances be held and disclosed?
options: On the student's file, open to all academic staff who teach on the course.
Securely, disclosed only to those who need access and have a right to see it.
By the module tutor, shared with the full course team for moderation.
In the Student Portal, where the student's personal tutor can view them.
questions.explanation: The policy requires all applications to be held securely and disclosed only to those who need access to the information and have a right to see it.
questions.source_excerpt: All applications for mitigating circumstances are held securely and disclosed only to those who need access to the information and have a right to see it.

questions.question: The Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure makes clear the limits of the decisions an examination board or assessment panel may make. Which of these does it give as an example?
options: Whether new assessment attempts may be allowed.
Whether misconduct penalties may be lifted.
Whether assessment weightings may be altered.
Whether a student may transfer to another course.
questions.explanation: The policy gives whether marks may be changed, new assessment attempts allowed or fails disregarded as examples of the limits of the board's decisions.
questions.source_excerpt: The policy and procedures make clear the limits of the range of decisions which may be made by the examination board/assessment panel, for example whether marks may be changed, new assessment attempts allowed or fails disregarded.

questions.question: Under the definition in the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, when does a medical operation count as a mitigating circumstance?
options: When it was booked before the term began.
When it is carried out in an NHS hospital.
When it needs more than one night in hospital.
When the operation is an emergency.
questions.explanation: The definition lists a medical operation as a mitigating circumstance only if it is an emergency.
questions.source_excerpt: Serious personal injury, medical condition or mental health condition or medical operation (if an emergency) preventing attendance, completion of assessment or submission of work.

questions.question: The Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure includes unexpected caring responsibilities caused by a close relative's sudden serious illness. What evidence does it specify for this circumstance?
options: A signed statement from the relative.
Evidence from a medical practitioner.
Confirmation from a local social worker.
A letter from the student's personal tutor.
questions.explanation: The definition states that unexpected caring responsibilities must be supported with evidence from a medical practitioner.
questions.source_excerpt: Unexpected caring responsibilities caused by sudden serious illness or worsening of on-going medical condition to child, partner, or close relative, with evidence from a medical practitioner.

questions.question: The Mitigating Circumstances Claim Form is available on the College website, Virtual Learning platform and Student Portal. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, where can a student get a hardcopy?
options: From the College reception office.
From the College library desk.
From the Student Support office.
From the Examinations office.
questions.explanation: The policy states that, in addition to the online versions, a student can access the hardcopy of the form from the reception office.
questions.source_excerpt: The form and its related guidance are available on the College website, Virtual Learning platform and Student Portal. Additionally, a student can access the hardcopy from the reception office.

questions.question: According to the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what must a student provide alongside the completed Mitigating Circumstances Claim Form to initiate a claim?
options: A supporting letter from their module tutor.
Their attendance record for the affected module.
A copy of the assessment brief they missed.
Documents in evidence to support the claim.
questions.explanation: To initiate a claim, the student must complete the Claim Form and provide documents in evidence to support it.
questions.source_excerpt: To initiate a mitigating claim a student must complete the Mitigating Circumstances Claim Form and provide documents in evidence to support their claim.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, who conducts the initial assessment of the mitigating circumstances claims that are received?
options: The student's module tutor.
The Appeal Panel.
The College Registrar.
The Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board.
questions.explanation: The College Registrar conducts the initial assessment of claims and informs students in writing where claims are not allowable.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Registrar will conduct an initial assessment of claims received and will inform those students in writing where claims are not allowable in accordance with the Guidance.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, after the initial assessment, with whom does the College Registrar arrange a meeting to consider a mitigating circumstances claim?
options: The Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board.
The Chair of the Academic Board and the module leader.
The student's personal tutor and the Head of Student Support.
The Head of Quality Assurance.
questions.explanation: The Registrar arranges a meeting with the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board to consider the claim.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Registrar will then arrange a meeting with the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board to consider the mitigating circumstances claim.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, if mitigating circumstances stop a student submitting work by the deadline, when must they submit it after returning to the College?
options: Only after the Assessment and Progression Board has approved the claim.
At the earliest opportunity, even if the work is incomplete.
On a date agreed with the module tutor, once the work is complete.
At the next assessment point, together with any referred work.
questions.explanation: Students must submit work at the earliest opportunity on their return to the College, even if it is incomplete as a result of the circumstances.
questions.source_excerpt: or they must submit work at the earliest opportunity on their return to the College, even if as a result of the mitigating circumstance, it is incomplete.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, whose responsibility is it to inform the College of circumstances that may have affected a student's assessment?
options: The module tutor's, by flagging it on the mark sheet.
The personal tutor's, by emailing the College Registrar.
The Student Support team's, by referring it to the Board.
The student's, by submitting a Mitigating Circumstances Form.
questions.explanation: It is the student's responsibility to inform the College by submitting a Mitigating Circumstances Form by the stipulated deadline.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the student's responsibility to inform the College of any circumstances that they consider may have affected their assessment by submitting a Mitigating Circumstances Form by the stipulated deadline.

questions.question: According to the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, how must any translation into English of a student's supporting evidence be provided?
options: By the student, signed as a true translation.
By a bilingual member of College staff.
By using an authorised translator.
By the student's personal tutor or sponsor.
questions.explanation: Evidence must be presented in English, with any translations provided using an authorised translator.
questions.source_excerpt: Evidence must be presented in English, with any translations provided using an authorised translator.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, if the Board accepts that illness or another valid cause affected a student's examination, what would the student normally be allowed?
options: A mark calculated from their coursework in the same module.
Either an examination re-sit or a unit re-take opportunity.
An aggregated pass based on results in their other units.
A viva with the module tutor in place of the examination.
questions.explanation: For examinations, the student would normally be allowed either an examination re-sit or a unit re-take opportunity.
questions.source_excerpt: Examinations: The student would normally be allowed either an examination re-sit or unit re-take opportunity.

questions.question: According to the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, on what condition can further referrals be considered with mitigating circumstances?
options: The original claim is resubmitted with the tutor's endorsement.
The student has passed at least half of the module's assessments.
A new claim is submitted together with relevant documentary evidence.
The Chair of the Board agrees to carry the first claim forward.
questions.explanation: Further referrals can only be considered with mitigating circumstances if a new claim is submitted together with relevant documentary evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: Further referrals can only be considered with mitigating circumstances provided that a new claim is submitted together with relevant documentary evidence.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, a student appealing on the ground of mitigating circumstances the assessors were not aware of must support the request with what?
options: New medical certificates or other acceptable documentary evidence.
The original claim form and a statement from their module tutor.
A personal statement explaining why the circumstances were withheld.
Written confirmation from the Registrar that the claim arrived late.
questions.explanation: On this ground, the request must be supported by new medical certificates or other documentary evidence acceptable to the Appeal Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: their existed mitigating circumstances affecting the student's performance of which the assessors were not aware ... the candidate's request must be supported by new medical certificates or other documentary evidence acceptable to the Appeal Panel

questions.question: According to the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, which policy should a student refer to if they wish to challenge a decision of the Assessment and Progression Board?
options: The Student Complaints Policy and Procedure.
The Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy.
The Academic Misconduct Policy.
The LCC Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure.
questions.explanation: To appeal against a decision, students should refer to the LCC Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: To appeal against a decision, students should refer to the LCC Academic Appeals Policy and Procedure which is available on the College website and via the student portal.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, the College Registrar and the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board have agreed recommendations on a claim. What happens to those recommendations next?
options: They go to the module tutor, who adjusts the student's mark to reflect them.
They are sent to the Appeal Panel, which confirms or overturns each one.
They are endorsed as final decisions by the Assessment and Progression Board.
They are issued straight to the student by the Registrar as the final outcome.
questions.explanation: The Registrar and the Chair agree recommendations of final decisions, which are then endorsed by the Assessment and Progression Board.
questions.source_excerpt: They will agree on recommendations of final decisions to be endorsed by the Assessment and Progression Board. ... Decisions are endorsed by the Assessment and Progression Board.

questions.question: When the College Registrar meets the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board to consider a claim, what must they determine under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure?
options: Whether the circumstances were material to performance in the assessment and whether there is sufficient evidence they occurred.
Whether the student's attendance was satisfactory and whether the affected work was still handed in by the original deadline.
Whether the tutor's original mark was accurate and whether the student has already made any earlier claims that academic year.
Whether the claim form was countersigned by a tutor and whether the student has a declared disability on their record.
questions.explanation: At the meeting they determine whether the circumstances were material to the student's performance in the assessment and whether there is sufficient evidence that they occurred.
questions.source_excerpt: They will determine whether the mitigating circumstances were material to the student's performance in the assessment in question and whether there is sufficient evidence to warrant accepting that the mitigating circumstances occurred.

questions.question: During the initial assessment, the College Registrar finds that a student's claim is not allowable in accordance with the Guidance. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what must the Registrar do?
options: Pass the claim to the Chair of the Board, who makes the final decision on it.
Return the claim to the module tutor to reflect in the mark awarded.
Keep the claim on file until the student lodges an appeal against it.
Inform the student in writing that the claim is not allowable.
questions.explanation: Where claims are not allowable in accordance with the Guidance, the Registrar informs those students in writing.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Registrar will conduct an initial assessment of claims received and will inform those students in writing where claims are not allowable in accordance with the Guidance.

questions.question: A student with compelling grounds missed the assessment deadline and now wishes to submit a mitigating circumstances claim. The Assessment and Progression Board meets in ten days. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, can they still submit it?
options: No, because every claim must be made on or before the assessment deadline.
Yes, provided it is submitted at least one week before the Board meeting.
No, because late claims must be made within five working days of the deadline.
Yes, but it will be treated as an appeal and passed to the Appeal Panel.
questions.explanation: Claims are normally due by the assessment deadline, but a student with compelling grounds may submit up to at least one week before the Board meeting, which ten days allows.
questions.source_excerpt: All claims must be submitted on or before the assessment deadline unless there are compelling grounds. Students with compelling grounds must submit the claim at least one week before the Assessment and Progression Board meeting.

questions.question: The Assessment and Progression Board accepts a student's claim for missed coursework. The module tutor suggests allowing the student eight weeks to resubmit. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what applies?
options: The tutor may set the date, as long as it falls before the next Board meeting.
The tutor's eight weeks stands, with the standard late penalty applied.
The Board agrees the date, which can be no more than an additional five weeks.
The Registrar sets the date, which can be up to an additional ten weeks.
questions.explanation: For coursework, the new submission date is agreed by the Board and can be up to an additional five weeks, so eight weeks is not permitted.
questions.source_excerpt: Course work: To offer the student another opportunity to submit the work by a date agreed by the Board up to an additional five weeks, as if for the first time and without penalty.

questions.question: A student sat an examination while seriously ill and still achieved a pass mark. The Board is satisfied the illness affected their performance. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, can a re-sit or re-take be offered?
options: No, because re-sits are available only to students who failed the examination.
Yes, as the opportunity can be granted irrespective of the mark obtained.
No, because sitting the exam means the student declared themselves fit to sit.
Yes, but only if the mark is no more than five per cent above the pass mark.
questions.explanation: Where the student undertook the examination, a re-sit or re-take opportunity can be granted irrespective of the mark obtained.
questions.source_excerpt: Examinations: The student would normally be allowed either an examination re-sit or unit re-take opportunity. This opportunity can be granted irrespective of the mark obtained if the student had undertaken the examination.

questions.question: A student wants to appeal a Board decision on the ground of mitigating circumstances the assessors were not aware of. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what else must be true of those circumstances?
options: They could not reasonably have been presented to the assessors beforehand.
They first arose after the Board had already taken its decision.
The student's module tutor was told about them informally at the time.
They were described in full on the student's original claim form.
questions.explanation: This appeal ground covers circumstances the assessors were not aware of and which could not reasonably have been presented to them.
questions.source_excerpt: their existed mitigating circumstances affecting the student's performance of which the assessors were not aware when their decision was taken, and which could not reasonably have been presented to the assessors

questions.question: After a Board decision, a student finds a minor administrative error in how their marks were processed, but it could not have changed their result. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, can they appeal on the administrative error ground?
options: Yes, as any administrative error is enough on its own to support an appeal.
Yes, if they report it to the Registrar within 14 working days of the result.
No, as only errors made by the tutor during marking can be appealed.
No, as the error must cast doubt on whether the result might have differed.
questions.explanation: The administrative error ground applies only where the error is of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different.
questions.source_excerpt: there was an administrative error or procedural irregularity or other inadequacy in the conduct of the assessors or processing of marks or grades of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different had there not been such an error.

questions.question: A student's mitigating circumstances claim says they missed a deadline because of a family holiday booked several months earlier. Under the definition in the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, why would this not qualify?
options: Holidays count only when supported by the original booking documents.
It could reasonably have been predicted or accommodated by the student.
Holidays are covered only when the student is abroad for over four weeks.
The claim should have gone to the module tutor rather than the Registrar.
questions.explanation: Mitigating circumstances must be unexpected and not reasonably predictable or accommodated by the student; a holiday booked months ahead fails that test.
questions.source_excerpt: Circumstances that are unexpected, significantly disruptive and beyond the control of the student, which could not be reasonably predicted or accommodated by the student

questions.question: A student's home is badly damaged by fire the night before an exam. A fire is not one of the examples listed in the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure. Can it still be considered as a mitigating circumstance?
options: No, only the listed injury, bereavement and caring circumstances can be considered.
No, because damage to property is handled through the complaints procedure.
Yes, as the list is not exhaustive and it can qualify if it meets the definition.
Yes, but only if the Registrar and the tutor both countersign the claim form.
questions.explanation: The listed examples are included but not limited to, so any circumstance meeting the definition (unexpected, significantly disruptive, beyond the student's control) can be considered.
questions.source_excerpt: Circumstances that are unexpected, significantly disruptive and beyond the control of the student ... These will include, but not be limited to:

questions.question: A student's partner has an on-going medical condition that suddenly worsens, leaving the student with unexpected caring responsibilities during an assessment period. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, can this be a mitigating circumstance?
options: No, because only the student's own illness is recognised as mitigation.
No, because caring responsibilities count only when they relate to a child.
Yes, if the student's personal tutor confirms the caring role in writing.
Yes, as a worsening of a partner's on-going condition is expressly covered.
questions.explanation: The definition includes unexpected caring responsibilities caused by the worsening of an on-going medical condition of a child, partner or close relative, with evidence from a medical practitioner.
questions.source_excerpt: Unexpected caring responsibilities caused by sudden serious illness or worsening of on-going medical condition to child, partner, or close relative, with evidence from a medical practitioner.

questions.question: A student's close friend dies suddenly a week before a coursework deadline. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, can this bereavement be a mitigating circumstance?
options: Yes, as bereavement of a friend is expressly included.
No, as bereavement only counts for a close family member or partner.
No, unless the friend was the student's registered next of kin.
Yes, but only if the funeral falls on the day of the deadline.
questions.explanation: The definition expressly includes bereavement of a close family member, partner or friend.
questions.source_excerpt: Bereavement of a close family member, partner, or friend.

questions.question: A colleague who has no role in a student's claim asks you to show them the student's mitigating circumstances application. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what should you do?
options: Show it, as any member of College staff may view applications on request.
Show it, but only once the Board has endorsed a final decision on the claim.
Decline, as access is limited to those who need it and have a right to it.
Show a summary, provided the student's name and ID are removed first.
questions.explanation: Applications are held securely and disclosed only to those who need access to the information and have a right to see it.
questions.source_excerpt: All applications for mitigating circumstances are held securely and disclosed only to those who need access to the information and have a right to see it.

questions.question: A student submits an original medical certificate written in Bengali, with an English translation prepared by their brother. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what is still needed for this evidence?
options: An English translation provided using an authorised translator.
Nothing further, as the certificate itself is an original document.
A signed declaration from the brother that his translation is accurate.
A scanned copy of the certificate emailed to the Registrar as well.
questions.explanation: Evidence must be presented in English, and any translation must be provided using an authorised translator, not a family member.
questions.source_excerpt: Independent documentary evidence in its original form shall normally be required. ... Evidence must be presented in English, with any translations provided using an authorised translator.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, which sequence correctly describes how a mitigating circumstances claim is handled once the student has submitted it?
options: Registrar's initial assessment; Registrar meets Board Chair; Board endorses decision; student told in writing.
Tutor marks the work with mitigation; Registrar reviews claim; Appeal Panel endorses; student told in writing.
Board Chair's initial assessment; Registrar endorses decision; tutor adjusts the mark; student told by email.
Registrar's initial assessment; Board endorses decision; tutor meets student; Appeal Panel confirms outcome.
questions.explanation: The Registrar makes an initial assessment, then meets the Board Chair to agree recommendations; the Board endorses the decisions and the student is informed in writing.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Registrar will conduct an initial assessment of claims received ... The College Registrar will then arrange a meeting with the Chair of the Assessment and Progression Board ... Decisions are endorsed by the Assessment and Progression Board. ... Students are informed of the decision of the Assessment and Progression Board in writing

questions.question: A student submitted their coursework on time, but a sudden illness badly affected its quality. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, can the Board still apply its mitigation options?
options: No, the options apply only where a student has failed to submit work.
No, because an on-time submission shows the student was fit to be assessed.
Yes, but only after the student has lodged a formal academic appeal.
Yes, if satisfied the poor performance was due to illness or other valid cause.
questions.explanation: The Board's options apply where it is satisfied that a failure to submit or poor performance in a module assessment was due to illness or other valid cause.
questions.source_excerpt: If the Board is satisfied that a student's failure to submit work or poor performance in a module assessment was due to illness or other valid cause, they may choose to implement the following options:

questions.question: A student who has submitted a mitigating circumstances claim asks how they will find out whether it has been accepted. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what should staff tell them?
options: Their tutor will tell them in person at the first tutorial after the Board meets.
An adjusted mark will appear on the Student Portal without any separate notice.
They will be told in writing, normally within about 14 working days of the claim.
They will hear the outcome at the Board meeting, which they are required to attend.
questions.explanation: Students are informed of the Board's decision in writing, and are notified of the outcome within approximately 14 working days of submitting the claim.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are informed of the decision of the Assessment and Progression Board in writing within the prescribed timeline. ... The student will be notified of the outcome within approximately 14 working days of the submission of the claim.

questions.question: Which of these situations would not be dealt with under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure itself?
options: A student's long-standing disability that affects their work in every assessment across the year.
Caring for a partner whose on-going medical condition suddenly worsens during the exam period.
An emergency operation the day before a coursework deadline that prevents the work being submitted.
The sudden death of a close friend a week before the student's scheduled examination.
questions.explanation: On-going conditions and other disabilities are considered under the Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy and fall outside this policy; the other situations are listed examples of mitigating circumstances.
questions.source_excerpt: On-going conditions and other disabilities are considered under the "Student Support and Reasonable Adjustments Policy" and thus do not fall within the confines of this policy.

questions.question: A student with compelling grounds plans to lodge a late mitigating circumstances claim and asks whether they can also hold back their coursework until then. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what should staff advise?
options: Yes; the compelling-grounds allowance covers the work too, up to one week before the Board meets.
Yes; the work is not due until the Board has decided the claim and set a new submission date.
No; the claim and the finished work must both be handed in together on the original deadline.
No; they must make every effort to submit the work by the deadline, even if it is incomplete.
questions.explanation: The compelling-grounds allowance applies to the claim only; students must make every effort to submit work by the deadline even if incomplete, or at the earliest opportunity on their return.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with compelling grounds must submit the claim at least one week before the Assessment and Progression Board meeting. ... Students are advised that they must make every effort to submit work by the deadline even if it is incomplete

questions.question: After the Assessment and Progression Board accepts a claim for a missed examination, the student asks for the five extra weeks they have heard about so they can sit it later. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what should staff explain?
options: The five-week period covers exams too, so the student may pick any exam date that falls within that window.
An accepted exam claim leads only to an adjusted mark, so no further attempt at the exam is available.
The five-week period is for coursework; for an exam they would normally be allowed a re-sit or unit re-take.
The Board cannot offer a new attempt itself, so the student must ask the Appeal Panel to set a new exam date.
questions.explanation: The additional period of up to five weeks is the coursework option; for examinations the Board would normally allow either an examination re-sit or a unit re-take opportunity.
questions.source_excerpt: Course work: To offer the student another opportunity to submit the work by a date agreed by the Board up to an additional five weeks, as if for the first time and without penalty. ... Examinations: The student would normally be allowed either an examination re-sit or unit re-take opportunity.

questions.question: A student claims illness and supports it with an original, signed letter in English written by their sister, who looked after them. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what is the weakness in this evidence?
options: It should have been scanned and emailed in, rather than handed in as a paper original.
It is not independent documentary evidence, which is normally required.
It must be countersigned by the student's module tutor before it can be considered.
It needs a certified translation, as all evidence must pass through an authorised translator.
questions.explanation: The policy normally requires independent documentary evidence in its original form; a letter from the student's own sister is not independent.
questions.source_excerpt: Independent documentary evidence in its original form shall normally be required.

questions.question: A student provides original evidence of a close relative's death, which happened two weeks after they had completed and submitted the assessment in question. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, which test does this claim fail?
options: Bereavement qualifies only where the person who died was a parent, child or spouse.
Evidence of a death must be submitted as a scanned copy rather than as an original.
Bereavement claims must be lodged with the module tutor within 48 hours of the death.
The circumstances were not material to the student's performance in that assessment.
questions.explanation: The Registrar and Chair must determine whether the circumstances were material to performance in the assessment in question; a death after submission could not have affected it.
questions.source_excerpt: They will determine whether the mitigating circumstances were material to the student's performance in the assessment in question

questions.question: Before marking, a module tutor asks the Registrar for the details of a student's mitigating circumstances claim so they can bear them in mind. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, how should the Registrar respond?
options: Decline, as work is marked as presented and access is limited to those who need it.
Share them, since the tutor must reflect accepted claims in the marks they award.
Share only the outcome, so the tutor can apply the agreed adjustment to the mark.
Decline for now, then pass the full claim to the tutor for re-marking after the Board.
questions.explanation: Tutors mark all work as presented with no account taken of mitigating circumstances, and applications are disclosed only to those who need access and have a right to see them.
questions.source_excerpt: All applications for mitigating circumstances are held securely and disclosed only to those who need access to the information and have a right to see it. ... All student work must be marked by tutors as presented with no account taken of mitigating circumstances at this stage.

questions.question: A student claims unexpected caring duties after their mother's sudden serious illness abroad, and supplies a scanned letter in Urdu from her doctor. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what would normally make this evidence acceptable?
options: Nothing more, as a letter from a medical practitioner is all a caring claim requires.
A statement from the mother herself confirming the care, in place of the doctor's letter.
The original letter, with an English translation provided by an authorised translator.
A covering note from the student's tutor confirming that the scan is a faithful copy.
questions.explanation: Evidence must normally be the original, as scanned copies are not accepted, and be presented in English, with any translation provided using an authorised translator.
questions.source_excerpt: Independent documentary evidence in its original form shall normally be required. Photocopies or scanned copies of evidence will not be accepted. Evidence must be presented in English, with any translations provided using an authorised translator.

questions.question: A student returns after an emergency operation and hands in incomplete coursework, with a mitigating circumstances claim already lodged. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, how is the work handled?
options: The tutor marks only the completed sections and scales the mark up to reflect the claim.
It is marked as presented; the Board considers the claim and any further opportunity.
It is held unmarked until the Board decides the claim, then marked in light of the outcome.
It is returned for the student to finish, as incomplete work cannot be accepted with a claim.
questions.explanation: Work submitted on return, even if incomplete, is marked as presented with no account taken of the circumstances; the Board then decides whether to offer, for example, another opportunity to submit.
questions.source_excerpt: they must submit work at the earliest opportunity on their return to the College, even if as a result of the mitigating circumstance, it is incomplete. ... All student work must be marked by tutors as presented with no account taken of mitigating circumstances at this stage.

questions.question: Which of these practices by an assessment board would conflict with the principles of the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure?
options: Recording the outcome of every mitigating circumstances claim that it considers.
Endorsing the final decisions recommended by the Registrar and the Board Chair.
Restricting access to claim files to those who need it and have a right to see it.
Exercising discretion differently on comparable claims, without any explanation.
questions.explanation: Decisions and any exercise of discretion must be made consistently, and all decisions transparently and fairly; the other practices are required by the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: The decision for mitigating circumstances applications and any exercise of discretion are made in a consistent manner by individual boards/panels. ... All decisions related to the mitigating circumstances claims are to be made transparently and fairly.

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, which of these appeals falls within the ground of mitigating circumstances that were unknown to the assessors?
options: A student was in intensive care throughout the claim period and now has new hospital certificates.
A student re-presents the illness the Board already considered and rejected, with the same GP letter.
A student chose to keep a family illness private before the Board met but now wants it considered.
A student could not have told the assessors about a crisis, but can offer no documentary evidence.
questions.explanation: This ground covers circumstances the assessors did not know of and which could not reasonably have been presented to them, supported by new medical certificates or other acceptable documentary evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: their existed mitigating circumstances affecting the student's performance of which the assessors were not aware when their decision was taken, and which could not reasonably have been presented to the assessors if resting on this ground, the candidate's request must be supported by new medical certificates or other documentary evidence acceptable to the Appeal Panel

questions.question: The Board accepted a student's coursework claim and set a resubmission date three weeks away. The student wants to appeal because they had hoped for the full five weeks. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, is this a valid appeal?
options: Yes; every accepted coursework claim is entitled to exactly five additional weeks.
Yes; students may appeal any Board decision that they consider unduly harsh.
No; appeals are allowed only on the two grounds that the policy sets out.
No; resubmission dates can be challenged only through a fresh claim to the Registrar.
questions.explanation: The Board may agree a date up to an additional five weeks, and appeals are limited to unknown mitigating circumstances or an administrative error or irregularity casting doubt on the result.
questions.source_excerpt: To offer the student another opportunity to submit the work by a date agreed by the Board up to an additional five weeks ... Students have the right to appeal against a decision of the Assessment and Progression Board but only on these two grounds:

questions.question: The Assessment and Progression Board's record wrongly shows a student's accepted claim as rejected, so no resubmission was offered. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what route is open to the student?
options: Appeal on the ground of mitigating circumstances unknown to the assessors, with new medical evidence.
Appeal on the ground of an administrative error or procedural irregularity that casts doubt on the result.
No appeal is possible, as the Board's recorded outcome is final and only the Registrar can change it.
No appeal is needed; they resubmit the same claim as a further referral with the original evidence.
questions.explanation: A recording error that led to no resubmission being offered is an administrative error or procedural irregularity of a kind that casts doubt on whether the result might have been different.
questions.source_excerpt: The Mitigating Circumstances claims outcomes are recorded by the Assessment and Progression Board. ... there was an administrative error or procedural irregularity or other inadequacy in the conduct of the assessors or processing of marks or grades of such a nature as to cause doubt as to whether the result might have been different had there not been such an error.

questions.question: A tutor knew informally that a student was very unwell before an exam, but the student never submitted a Mitigating Circumstances Form. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, can the tutor's knowledge stand in for a claim?
options: Yes, if the tutor confirms the illness to the Registrar in writing before the Board meets.
Yes, as the tutor's awareness means the College was informed before the examination.
No, but the tutor may reflect the illness in the exam mark in place of a formal claim.
No, as the student must inform the College by submitting the form by the stipulated deadline.
questions.explanation: It is the student's responsibility to inform the College by submitting a Mitigating Circumstances Form by the stipulated deadline, and tutors mark work as presented.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the student's responsibility to inform the College of any circumstances that they consider may have affected their assessment by submitting a Mitigating Circumstances Form by the stipulated deadline.

questions.question: A student granted a re-sit through an accepted claim falls ill again and fails the re-sit. They ask the Registrar to apply their original claim to it. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what is required?
options: Nothing further, as an accepted claim carries forward to any later referral in that unit.
A formal appeal to the Appeal Panel, as a second claim on the same unit is not allowed.
A new claim, submitted together with relevant documentary evidence of the new illness.
A note from the tutor confirming the illness, attached to the student's original claim.
questions.explanation: Further referrals can only be considered with mitigating circumstances if a new claim is submitted together with relevant documentary evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: Further referrals can only be considered with mitigating circumstances provided that a new claim is submitted together with relevant documentary evidence.

questions.question: After meeting the Board Chair, the Registrar emails a student that their claim has been accepted and closed, before the Assessment and Progression Board has met. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, what is wrong with this?
options: Nothing, as the Registrar and Chair jointly make the final decision on each claim.
It is only a recommendation until the Assessment and Progression Board endorses it.
The Chair, not the Registrar, is responsible for telling the student the outcome.
Outcomes can be released only once the student's tutor has adjusted the mark.
questions.explanation: The Registrar and Chair agree recommendations of final decisions to be endorsed by the Board, and students are informed of the Board's decision.
questions.source_excerpt: They will agree on recommendations of final decisions to be endorsed by the Assessment and Progression Board. ... Decisions are endorsed by the Assessment and Progression Board. ... Students are informed of the decision of the Assessment and Progression Board in writing within the prescribed timeline.

questions.question: Two days before a coursework deadline, a student tells you their father has died. Which advice follows the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure?
options: Lodge the claim form with original evidence at reception by the deadline, and still try to submit the work.
Concentrate on the funeral, then appeal the result afterwards with a copy of the death certificate.
Ask the tutor to take the bereavement into account when marking, as a parent's death needs no form.
Email a scan of the death certificate to the tutor, who can extend the deadline by five weeks.
questions.explanation: Claims go to reception c/o the Registrar with original evidence by the assessment deadline, and students must still make every effort to submit work, even if incomplete.
questions.source_excerpt: The claims must be submitted to the College reception c/o the Registrar in the first instance. ... All claims must be submitted on or before the assessment deadline unless there are compelling grounds. ... they must make every effort to submit work by the deadline even if it is incomplete

questions.question: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, which of these caring situations can be claimed as a mitigating circumstance?
options: Looking after children during a school half-term that was known about well in advance.
Caring for a child suddenly taken seriously ill, with evidence from a medical practitioner.
Caring for a partner after a sudden illness, backed only by the partner's own statement.
Helping a close relative with a house move that was planned several months in advance.
questions.explanation: The policy covers unexpected caring responsibilities caused by a child's, partner's or close relative's sudden serious illness, with evidence from a medical practitioner.
questions.source_excerpt: Unexpected caring responsibilities caused by sudden serious illness or worsening of on-going medical condition to child, partner, or close relative, with evidence from a medical practitioner.

questions.question: A student was ill during an exam but did not submit a mitigating circumstances claim by the assessment deadline, and has no compelling grounds for the delay. The Board meets in a fortnight. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, can the claim still be made?
options: Yes, as any claim received at least one week before the Board meeting is still considered.
Yes, provided the student's module tutor confirms the illness to the Registrar in writing.
No, as any late claim must be lodged within five working days of the examination taking place.
No, as without compelling grounds it had to be submitted on or before the assessment deadline.
questions.explanation: Claims are due on or before the assessment deadline; the later route of at least one week before the Board meeting is open only to students with compelling grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: All claims must be submitted on or before the assessment deadline unless there are compelling grounds. Students with compelling grounds must submit the claim at least one week before the Assessment and Progression Board meeting.

questions.question: The Board rejected a student's illness claim for lack of evidence. The student has since obtained a detailed hospital report on that same illness and wants to appeal on the ground of circumstances unknown to the assessors. Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy and Procedure, does this fit that ground?
options: Yes, as new medical certificates or other new evidence are all that this ground requires.
No, as the assessors were already aware of that illness at the time their decision was taken.
Yes, if the hospital report reaches the Registrar at least one week before the Appeal Panel meets.
No, as new evidence of an illness can only be considered through a further referral claim.
questions.explanation: This ground covers only circumstances the assessors were not aware of when they decided; new documentary evidence is an additional requirement, and here the Board already knew of the illness.
questions.source_excerpt: their existed mitigating circumstances affecting the student's performance of which the assessors were not aware when their decision was taken, and which could not reasonably have been presented to the assessors if resting on this ground, the candidate's request must be supported by new medical certificates or other documentary evidence acceptable to the Appeal Panel

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, if a member of staff is concerned about a student or a colleague, who must they contact?
options: Their line manager, who decides whether to escalate it
The Registrar, who then informs the PSG
The Head of Quality Assurance or nominated other
The Metropolitan Police, before telling anyone at College
questions.explanation: The referral procedure states that anyone concerned about a staff member or student must contact the Head of Quality Assurance or nominated other, who then liaises with internal and external contacts.
questions.source_excerpt: If any staff or students are concerned about a staff member or student, they must contact Head of Quality Assurance or nominated other.

questions.question: A student's remarks in class leave you unsure whether they amount to a Prevent concern. Under the Prevent Policy, what should you do?
options: Make a referral without delay, directly to the Chair or a member of the PSG
Wait until you have gathered firm evidence before making a formal referral
Question the student privately first to establish the facts yourself
