Note it down and raise it at the next scheduled Prevent Steering Group meeting
questions.explanation: The Prevent Policy says that in cases of doubt or concern, referrals should be made without delay and directly to the Chair or a member of the Prevent Steering Group.
questions.source_excerpt: In cases of doubt or concern referrals should be made without delay and directly to the Chair or member of the PSG.

questions.question: In addition to vocal or active opposition to fundamental British values, what does the Prevent Policy's definition of extremism expressly include?
options: Organising a lawful protest against government policy
Calls for the death of members of the armed forces
Holding strong religious or political convictions
Refusing to attend Prevent awareness training
questions.explanation: The policy's definition of extremism covers opposition to fundamental British values and also includes calls for the death of members of the armed forces, whether in the UK or overseas.
questions.source_excerpt: Extremism: the Prevent strategy (2011) defines extremism as vocal or active opposition to fundamental British values ... It also includes the call for the death of members of our armed forces, whether in this country or overseas;

questions.question: A lecturer wants to research extremism-related materials to prepare a new module. What does the Prevent Policy require them to do?
options: Nothing, since academic research is exempt from the Prevent Policy
Obtain written approval from the Metropolitan Police before starting
Register the module with the local FE/HE Prevent Co-ordinator for approval
Refer the proposed activity to the Prevent Steering Group for advice
questions.explanation: Under the section on internet and electronic communication, staff or students who seek to research sensitive or extremism-related materials must refer the proposed activity to the Prevent Steering Group (PSG) for advice.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff or students who seek to research sensitive or extremism-related materials, must refer proposed activity to the PSG for advice;

questions.question: A student discloses information to a College support service that raises a Prevent concern. What does the Prevent Policy say about sharing that information?
options: It can lawfully be disclosed to bodies such as Channel, the police or social services
It must stay within the support service, as those discussions are held in strict confidence
It can be passed to the student's family, but not to the police, Channel or social services
It cannot leave the College, although other internal College services may be informed
questions.explanation: Although support services maintain confidentiality, the policy states that, in accordance with the law, such information can be disclosed to bodies within or outside the College, including the Prevent Co-ordinator, Channel, the police or social services.
questions.source_excerpt: In accordance with the law, such information can be disclosed to bodies within or outside the College, including the Prevent Co-ordinator, `Channel', the police or social services.

questions.question: A student group asks to seat men and women separately at a guest lecture it is organising. What is the position under the Prevent Policy?
options: It is permitted if the speaker requests it on religious grounds
It is not permitted on College premises, but may go ahead off-site
It is not permitted, as the College upholds equality legislation
It is permitted if every attendee agrees to the arrangement when booking
questions.explanation: The policy states that, in upholding equality legislation, gender segregation such as seating men and women separately is not permitted at lectures and other events, whether or not held on College premises.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures that it upholds equality legislation considering that gender segregation, such as ... seating men and women separately at an event, is not permitted. These events include academic meetings, speaking events, lectures ... whether or not held on College premises.

questions.question: Under the Prevent Policy, using the College's SMS, IT systems or social media to instigate, promote or plan which of the following is prohibited?
options: Violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation or terrorism
Violent extremism, as non-violent extremist views are not covered
Terrorism offences, with extremism and radicalisation not covered
Extremist activity in working hours, with out-of-hours use exempt
questions.explanation: The policy prohibits staff, students and third parties from using College systems for the instigation, promotion, planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation or terrorism.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not permitted for any member staff, students or third partice to use the College's Student Management System (SMS), IT and social media ... for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation or terrorism in the name of ideology or belief.

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, what is the aim of the interventions into which people at risk of being drawn into terrorism are referred?
options: To gather evidence for a criminal prosecution
To decide whether the person should be excluded
To divert vulnerable people from radicalisation
To impose sanctions on those holding extremist views
questions.explanation: The policy defines Prevent as including the identification and referral of those at risk into appropriate interventions, which aim to divert vulnerable people from radicalisation.
questions.source_excerpt: Prevent includes but is not confined to the identification and referral of those at risk of being drawn into terrorism into appropriate interventions. These interventions aim to divert vulnerable people from radicalisation;

questions.question: Students stage an organised protest aimed at stopping an approved guest speaker from being heard. How does the Prevent Policy say the College may respond?
options: Take no action, since protest is protected under the Freedom of Speech Policy
Refer the students to the Metropolitan Police under the Prevent referral procedure
Cancel the event, since a protest overrides an approved speaker booking
Use disciplinary processes under the Student Code of Conduct as appropriate
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure allows disciplinary processes to be used as appropriate for protests or systematic activity aimed at preventing freedom of speech.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure describes the conduct expected and required by the College and use disciplinary processes as appropriate in event of actions of protest or systematic activity, which are aimed at preventing the freedom of speech.

questions.question: You are organising a College-branded event with an external speaker at a hired venue off-site. Under the Prevent Policy, which rules apply?
options: None, as off-site events fall outside the scope of the Prevent Policy
The same criteria set out in the External Speakers and Events Policy
The hired venue's own rules on speakers, bookings and security checks
The local FE/HE Prevent Co-ordinator's separate off-site approval rules
questions.explanation: The Prevent Policy states that off-site events which are College or Student body branded are subject to the same criteria outlined in the External Speakers and Events Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Events held off-site which are College or Student body branded are subject to the same criteria outlined in the External Speakers and Events Policy;

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, what are placement providers and providers of work-related settings expected to do?
options: Follow the Student Code of Conduct and leave any reporting of concerns to the student
Follow their professional body's guidelines, with no need to report to the College
Follow the External Speakers and Events Policy and seek PSG approval for each placement
Follow the CONTEST strategy and report concerns to the College and relevant external bodies
questions.explanation: Under the Partnership section, placement and work-related setting providers are expected to follow the government's counter-terrorism strategy, CONTEST, and report concerns to the College and relevant external bodies.
questions.source_excerpt: Placement and providers of work-related settings are expected to follow the governments' counter-terrorism strategy, `CONTEST' and report any concerns to the College and relevant external bodies;

questions.question: Prevent training is provided to all College staff. According to the Prevent Policy, which of the following is one of the things the training will enable staff to do?
options: Investigate concerns themselves and gather evidence before making any referral
Understand the referral procedure and what to do with the information they have
Decide on appropriate disciplinary sanctions for students who express extremist views
Identify which faith groups and societies on campus should be monitored most closely
questions.explanation: The policy states that training is provided to all College staff and will enable attendees to understand the referral procedure and what to do with the information they have; it does not ask staff to investigate, sanction or target particular faith groups.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff training is provided to all College staff. ... The training will enable attendees to: Identify the risks and signals of extremism and potential affiliation with terrorism; Understanding their duties and responsibilities in relation to Prevent; Understand the referral procedure and what actions to take with the information they have;

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, what is the aim of the national Prevent Strategy?
options: To identify and prosecute people in the UK who express extremist political or religious opinions
To reduce the threat to the UK from terrorism by stopping people becoming terrorists or supporting terrorism
To monitor the membership and activities of faith groups and religious societies on UK campuses
To limit debate on controversial political subjects in UK colleges in order to protect students
questions.explanation: The Purpose section states that the aim of the Prevent Strategy is to reduce the threat to the UK from terrorism by stopping people becoming terrorists or supporting terrorism.
questions.source_excerpt: The aim of the Prevent Strategy is to reduce the threat to the UK from terrorism by stopping people becoming terrorists or supporting terrorism.

questions.question: Which of the following is named in the Prevent Policy's list of fundamental British values?
options: National unity
Economic self-reliance
Respect for the Crown
Individual liberty
questions.explanation: The policy names democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs as fundamental British values.
questions.source_excerpt: vocal or active opposition to fundamental British values, including democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs.

questions.question: According to the principles set out in the Prevent Policy, what does the policy establish for the operation of Prevent-related activity?
options: A single point of contact
A Prevent lead in each team
An anonymous reporting line
A rota of duty managers
questions.explanation: The Principles section states that the policy gives clear guidance on the referral procedure and establishes a single point of contact for the operation of Prevent-related activity.
questions.source_excerpt: It provides clear guidance of the referral procedure and establishes a single point of contact for operation of Prevent related activity;

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, which body monitors the activities of the Prevent Risk Register and the Corporate Risk Register?
options: The local FE/HE Prevent Co-ordinator
The College's Human Resources team
The Principal's Executive Group (PEG)
The Registrar and Executive Assistant
questions.explanation: The Risk Register section states that the Principal's Executive Group (PEG) monitors the activities of the Prevent Risk Register and the Corporate Risk Register.
questions.source_excerpt: The Principal's Executive Group (PEG) monitors activities of the Prevent Risk Register and Corporate Risk Register

questions.question: Which risk does the Prevent Policy identify under 'ICT factors' in the College's Prevent risk assessment?
options: Hackers attacking the College's Student Management System from overseas
Staff sharing student records with outside agencies without consent
Students or staff accessing extreme material on College systems
Students recording lectures on personal devices without permission
questions.explanation: The risk assessment lists ICT factors as students or staff accessing extreme material on College systems.
questions.source_excerpt: ICT Factors Students or staff accessing extreme material on College systems.

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, who chairs the Prevent Steering Group (PSG)?
options: The Principal
The Head of Quality Assurance
The Human Resource Officer
The Registrar
questions.explanation: The PSG is chaired by the Principal; the Head of Quality Assurance is a member and the Registrar provides administrative support.
questions.source_excerpt: It is chaired by the Principal and includes the Head of Quality Assurance and Senior Quality Assurance Officer.

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, what are the College's brand ambassadors and student recruitment agents expected to do?
options: Screen every applicant against a Prevent watch list before recruiting them
Refer any concerns straight to the police without first informing the College
Complete Prevent accreditation from the PSG before each new student intake
Follow the College's Prevent practices and report any concerns to the College
questions.explanation: Under the Partnership section, brand ambassadors and agents involved in student recruitment are expected to follow the College's Prevent practices and report any concerns to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: In respect of student recruitment all brand ambassadors / agents are expected to follow the College's Prevent practices to meet the Prevent agenda and report any concerns to the College;

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, which staff are prioritised for Prevent training?
options: Staff who have been employed by the College for less than a year
Key staff and stakeholders who will benefit most directly
Staff who have previously made a referral to the Head of Quality Assurance
Staff working in the College's IT and information systems teams
questions.explanation: Training is provided to all College staff, and key College staff and stakeholders who will benefit most directly from Prevent training are prioritised.
questions.source_excerpt: Key College staff and stakeholders who will benefit most directly from Prevent training are prioritised.

questions.question: Which external agencies does the Prevent Policy's referral procedure name as possible contacts for liaison about a concern?
options: The local Prevent Coordinator and the Metropolitan Police
The Office for Students and the Home Office Prevent team
UK Visas and Immigration and the London borough council
The Charity Commission and the Department for Education
questions.explanation: The referral procedure states that the Head of Quality Assurance liaises with appropriate external agencies, which might include the local Prevent Coordinator and the Metropolitan Police.
questions.source_excerpt: The Head of Quality Assurance will liaise with relevant internal contacts and also liaise with appropriate external agencies. This might include: the local Prevent Coordinator and Metropolitan Police.

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, to whom may the PSG refer specific concerns about a member of staff?
options: The staff member's line manager
The Board of Directors
The Human Resource Officer
The head of their department
questions.explanation: The referral procedure states that specific concerns about staff may be referred by the PSG to the Human Resource Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: Specific concerns about staff may be referred by the PSG to Human Resource Officer;

questions.question: Under the Prevent Policy, what does the College reserve the right to do about material on its sites that encourages extremism or terrorism?
options: Issue a financial penalty to the person who brought the material onto site
Ask students or staff to remove all or any such electronic or physical material
Publish the names of those responsible to all students and staff on the VLE
Send the material to the Home Office before speaking to the person concerned
questions.explanation: The College reserves the right to ask students or staff to remove from its sites all or any electronic or physical material encouraging engagement with extremism, radicalisation or terrorism.
questions.source_excerpt: The College reserves the right to ask students or members of staff to remove from the College's sites, all or any electronic or physical material encouraging engagement with violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation or terrorism related activities;

questions.question: In relation to external speakers and events, what does the Prevent Policy say the College is committed to?
options: Hosting only speakers who have first been vetted by the Metropolitan Police
Restricting debate on sensitive political subjects to academic staff only
Banning any speaker whose views conflict with the College's stated values
Free intellectual enquiry, free expression and freedom of speech within the law
questions.explanation: The Events section states that the College is committed to principles of free intellectual enquiry, free expression and freedom of speech within the law.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is committed to principles of free intellectual enquiry, free expression and freedom of speech within the law

questions.question: Under the Prevent Policy, which College document should staff consult for further information on the support available to students in relation to Prevent?
options: The Student Welfare Policy
The Student Code of Conduct
The Information Security Policy
The Privacy Notice for Students
questions.explanation: The policy states that further information on the welfare available to students in relation to Prevent can be found in the Student Welfare Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Further information on the Welfare available to students in relation to Prevent can be found in the Student Welfare Policy.

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, what do the College's support services offer staff and students?
options: Legal representation in any police inquiry relating to terrorism
An anonymous line for reporting concerns directly to Channel
A promise that nothing disclosed is ever shared outside the service
A secure environment to discuss sensitive issues in confidence
questions.explanation: The policy states that College support services offer a secure environment for individuals to discuss sensitive issues in confidence, although information can lawfully be disclosed where required.
questions.source_excerpt: The College provides a number of support services to staff and students which offer ... a secure environment for individuals to discuss sensitive issues in confidence.

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, where are College students expected to adhere to the Prevent Policy and other College policies?
options: On College sites, not on placement
Whether they are on or off-site
In class, but not on social media
At College events, not privately
questions.explanation: The Student Body section states that College students are expected to adhere to the Prevent Policy and other policies whether on or off-site.
questions.source_excerpt: College students are expected to adhere to the Prevent Policy and other policies whether on or off-site.

questions.question: According to the Prevent Policy, how are all Prevent-related policies and procedures made available to students?
options: In the prospectus
On noticeboards
Through the VLE
By Registry email
questions.explanation: The policy states that all Prevent-related policies and procedures are made available to all students through the VLE.
questions.source_excerpt: all Prevent-related policies and procedures are made available to all students through the VLE.

questions.question: How does the Prevent Policy define radicalisation?
options: The expression of strong political or religious views that differ from those held by the majority of the population
The act of joining an organisation that has been proscribed by the Home Secretary under the Terrorism Act 2000
The process by which a person comes to support terrorism and extremist ideologies associated with terrorist groups
The recruitment of students into campus societies that campaign against government policy and foreign conflicts
questions.explanation: The Terms section defines radicalisation as the process by which a person comes to support terrorism and extremist ideologies associated with terrorist groups.
questions.source_excerpt: Radicalisation refers to the process by which a person comes to support terrorism and extremist ideologies associated with terrorist groups;

questions.question: Under the Prevent Policy, how is progress on the Prevent Risk Assessment and Action Plan reported to the Principal's Executive Group (PEG)?
options: Regularly, by the PSG Chair or a nominated other
Annually, by the Board of Directors after its own review
By the local Prevent Co-ordinator on the College's behalf
Only after a referral, by the Head of Quality Assurance
questions.explanation: The Prevent Steering Group reports to PEG, and regular reporting of progress on the Risk Assessment and Action Plan is made to PEG by the Chair or a nominated other.
questions.source_excerpt: A Prevent Steering Group (PSG) has been established as an ad hoc group reporting to the Principal's Executive Group (PEG) ... Regular reporting of progress on the Risk Assessment and Action Plan is made to PEG by the Chair or nominated other.

questions.question: A colleague suggests the College's Prevent procedures should concentrate on students from one particular religion. How does this fit with the Prevent Policy?
options: It fits, if the Prevent Risk Register rates that religion as a higher risk
It does not, because the Prevent Policy covers staff rather than students
It does not, as the College's policies are not directed at any specific religion
It fits, as long as the local Prevent Co-ordinator agrees the approach first
questions.explanation: As a Relevant Higher Education Body, the College's Prevent policies and procedures are not directed at any specific religion, religious group or set of beliefs.
questions.source_excerpt: As a `Relevant Higher Education Body', the College has policies and procedures in place which are not directed at any specific religion, religious group or at the proponents of any other set of beliefs.

questions.question: A lecturer plans a seminar in which students critically debate what 'fundamental British values' mean. What does the Prevent Policy say about these values?
options: They must be taught as settled principles not open to classroom debate
They may be debated only once the PSG has approved the seminar in writing
They may be discussed only by staff who have completed Prevent training
They are rightly the subject of debate and consideration in Colleges
questions.explanation: The College adopts the definition of extremism while recognising that these values and concepts are rightly the subject of debate and consideration in universities and Colleges.
questions.source_excerpt: The College adopts this definition for purposes of implementing guidelines, recognising that these are values and concepts which are rightly the subject of debate and consideration in universities and Colleges;

questions.question: A member of staff has a Prevent concern about a colleague. Under the Prevent Policy, which sequence correctly describes how that concern can progress?
options: They report it to the Human Resource Officer, who decides whether the PSG needs to know
They contact the Head of Quality Assurance, and the PSG may refer it to the HR Officer
They tell the colleague's line manager, who passes it to the local Prevent Coordinator
They report it to the Metropolitan Police, who then notify the Head of Quality Assurance
questions.explanation: Concerns must first go to the Head of Quality Assurance or nominated other; specific concerns about staff may then be referred by the PSG to the Human Resource Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: If any staff or students are concerned about a staff member or student, they must contact Head of Quality Assurance or nominated other. ... Specific concerns about staff may be referred by the PSG to Human Resource Officer;

questions.question: Under the Prevent Policy, the extensive Prevent duty training that staff gain is meant to reflect what?
options: Their length of service, with longer-serving staff trained in more depth
The nature of their work and function in addressing Prevent issues
Their grade, with only senior managers receiving extensive training
The number of Prevent referrals they have previously made to the PSG
questions.explanation: The training is intended to give attendees extensive training on the Prevent duty that reflects the nature of their work and function in addressing Prevent issues.
questions.source_excerpt: Gain extensive training in relation to Prevent duty to reflect the nature of their work and function in respect of addressing Prevent issues.

questions.question: A professional body that accredits a College programme already has its own Prevent guidelines. According to the Prevent Policy, what is it expected to do in addition?
options: Raise any concerns it has with the College
Adopt the College's Prevent practices instead
Seek PSG sign-off before each College visit
Report concerns only to its own regulator
questions.explanation: The policy anticipates that professional bodies have their own guidelines and duties, but in addition expects them to raise any concerns with the College.
questions.source_excerpt: In engaging with professional bodies we anticipate that they have guidelines and duties in place with which they expect to adhere, but in addition they are expected to raise any concerns with the College;

questions.question: A student asks whether the College might monitor their use of its IT systems. Under the Prevent Policy, which policy advises on the steps the College may take to monitor or intercept communications?
options: The Student Welfare Policy
The Safeguarding and Security Policy
The Freedom of Speech Policy and Code of Practice
The External Speaker and Events Policy
questions.explanation: The Prevent Policy states that the Safeguarding and Security Policy advises staff and students of the consequences of accessing inappropriate material and the steps the College may take to monitor and/or intercept communications.
questions.source_excerpt: Safeguarding and Security Policy advises staff and students of consequences of accessing inappropriate material and the steps the College may take to monitor and/or intercept communications.

questions.question: A visiting contractor uses the College's IT network and social media to promote non-violent extremism. Does the Prevent Policy's ban on this misuse of College IT apply to them?
options: No, it covers only enrolled students and directly employed staff
No, contractors fall under their own employer's IT policy instead
Only if they were booked through the External Speaker process
Yes, it applies to third parties as well as to staff and students
questions.explanation: The prohibition on using College systems to instigate, promote or plan violent or non-violent extremism applies to staff, students and third parties.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not permitted for any member staff, students or third partice to use the College's Student Management System (SMS), IT and social media or other elements of the information management systems or processes for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism

questions.question: A student society is planning a religious event with an external speaker. Which of the following is correct under the Prevent Policy?
options: The External Speaker and Events Policy applies, and religious and community contacts can advise
It is exempt from the External Speaker and Events Policy because it is a religious event
It needs approval from the local Prevent Co-ordinator instead of the College's own process
It may be held only in the College's prayer rooms, under the Multi-faith Facilities Policy
questions.explanation: Religious events and Student body activity are subject to the External Speaker and Events Policy, and religious and community contacts can offer advice in relation to religious events.
questions.source_excerpt: External speakers and events, including academic guest lectures, Student body activity, commercial external visitors and/or religious events are subject to the External Speaker and Events Policy ... Religious and community contacts can offer advice in relation to religious events

questions.question: Someone deliberately and seriously disrupts a College electronic system. Under the terrorism definition in the Prevent Policy, what else must be true for this to count as terrorism?
options: It must also involve violence against a person or damage to property, because disrupting an electronic system is not enough on its own
It must be carried out by a member of an organisation that the Home Secretary has proscribed under the Terrorism Act 2000
It must aim to influence the government, intimidate the public and advance a political, religious, racial or ideological cause
It must take place within the UK and result in a criminal conviction before the Prevent Policy can be applied to it
questions.explanation: The definition covers actions aimed at seriously disrupting an electronic system, provided the use or threat is designed to influence the government, intimidate the public and advance a political, religious, racial or ideological cause.
questions.source_excerpt: the action involves violence against a person, property, endangers a person's life, creates a serious risk to the health or safety of the public or aims to seriously interfere with or disrupt an electronic system. The use or threat must be designed to influence the government, intimidate the public and must be made for the purposes of advancing a political, religious, racial or ideological cause;

questions.question: A student repeatedly and vocally opposes democracy and the rule of law but never uses or calls for violence. How does the Prevent Policy classify this behaviour?
options: As a form of non-violent extremism
As radicalisation rather than extremism
As terrorism under the Terrorism Act
As a welfare issue, not extremism
questions.explanation: Vocal opposition to fundamental British values such as democracy and the rule of law is extremism, and extremism not accompanied by violence is defined as non-violent extremism.
questions.source_excerpt: Extremism: the Prevent strategy (2011) defines extremism as vocal or active opposition to fundamental British values, including democracy, the rule of law ... Non-violent extremism is extremism, which is not accompanied by violence;

questions.question: During a student society debate, a speaker promotes ideas that could draw listeners towards terrorism. What does the Prevent Policy say about ideas of this kind?
options: They must be left unchallenged to protect free speech
Only the police may respond to them, not the College
There is a need to challenge them, not ignore them
They may be challenged only after a PSG referral
questions.explanation: The Principles section sets out expectations of the student body and makes clear the need to challenge extremist ideas which risk drawing people into terrorism.
questions.source_excerpt: The policy sets out expectations of the student body and its connected activities in delivering the Prevent Duty and makes clear the need to challenge extremist ideas which risk drawing people into terrorism;

questions.question: A guest speaker at a College event calls for the death of British soldiers serving overseas but says nothing about democracy or other British values. How does this fit the Prevent Policy's definition of extremism?
options: It is not extremism, as the definition covers only calls concerning armed forces based in the UK
It is not extremism unless it is accompanied by vocal opposition to democracy or the rule of law
It is extremism, as calls for the death of armed forces members count whether in the UK or overseas
It is extremism only if the speaker belongs to a group proscribed under the Terrorism Act 2000
questions.explanation: The policy's definition of extremism includes calls for the death of members of the armed forces, whether in this country or overseas, in addition to opposition to fundamental British values.
questions.source_excerpt: It also includes the call for the death of members of our armed forces, whether in this country or overseas;

questions.question: A colleague says that, under the Prevent Policy, 'Prevent' means nothing more than spotting people at risk and referring them on. How does the policy's own definition of prevention respond to this?
options: Prevent includes identifying and referring those at risk into interventions, but is not confined to it
Prevent covers identification only, with all referrals being handled by the police and by Channel
Prevent covers referral only, with identifying risk left to the local Prevent Co-ordinator to do
Prevent is confined to monitoring College IT systems for staff or students accessing extreme material
questions.explanation: The Terms section defines prevention as reducing or eliminating the risk of individuals becoming involved in terrorism, and says Prevent includes but is not confined to identifying and referring those at risk into interventions.
questions.source_excerpt: Prevention in the context of this document, means reducing or eliminating the risk of individuals becoming involved in terrorism. Prevent includes but is not confined to the identification and referral of those at risk of being drawn into terrorism into appropriate interventions.

questions.question: The Prevent Policy's Terms section defines several closely related terms. Which pairing of term and definition matches the policy?
options: Radicalisation: coming to hold political or religious views that differ from the majority
Safeguarding: protecting vulnerable groups from crime and abuse, but not from being drawn into terrorism
Non-violent extremism: extremism that involves no call for the death of armed forces members
Prevention: reducing or eliminating the risk of individuals becoming involved in terrorism
questions.explanation: The policy defines prevention as reducing or eliminating the risk of individuals becoming involved in terrorism. Radicalisation is coming to support terrorism and related extremist ideologies, safeguarding includes protection from being drawn into terrorist-related activity, and non-violent extremism is extremism not accompanied by violence.
questions.source_excerpt: Non-violent extremism is extremism, which is not accompanied by violence; ... Radicalisation refers to the process by which a person comes to support terrorism ... Prevention in the context of this document, means reducing or eliminating the risk of individuals becoming involved in terrorism. ... Safeguarding is the process of protecting vulnerable groups ... from being drawn into terrorist-related activity.

questions.question: Under the Prevent Policy, where are the main point of contact, authorised officer and information-sharing approaches in relation to Prevent determined?
options: By PEG, through its links with local Prevent Co-ordinators
Within the Prevent Steering Group (PSG)
By the Board of Directors
By the Head of Quality Assurance's nominated other
questions.explanation: The Partnership section states that the main point of contact, authorised officer and information-sharing approaches are determined within the PSG, even though PEG leads on strengthening links with local Prevent Co-ordinators.
questions.source_excerpt: The main point of contact, authorised officer and information sharing approaches in relation to Prevent is determined within the PSG.

questions.question: Tracing the Prevent Policy's governance chain for the Prevent Risk Assessment and Action Plan, which description of the reporting lines is correct?
options: The PSG reports straight to the Board of Directors, which then briefs PEG and the College Oversight Board
PEG reports to the PSG, which then reports progress on to the Board of Directors and College Oversight Board
The PSG reports to the Prevent HE/FE Co-ordinator, who then reports its progress on to PEG and the Board
The PSG reports to PEG; mitigating actions go on to the Board of Directors and College Oversight Board
questions.explanation: The PSG is an ad hoc group reporting to PEG; PEG monitors the risk registers, and actions to mitigate risks are considered regularly and reported to the Board of Directors and College Oversight Board.
questions.source_excerpt: actions taken to mitigate risks described in the Risk ... Assessment and Action Plan are considered on a regular basis and reported to the Board of Directors and College Oversight Board; ... A Prevent Steering Group (PSG) has been established as an ad hoc group reporting to the Principal's Executive Group (PEG)

questions.question: Students on a College-organised HE-related activity elsewhere in London are exposed to extremist views during the trip. Under which avenue of radicalisation does the Prevent Policy's risk assessment place this risk?
options: External factors
College sites
ICT factors
Partnership and placements
questions.explanation: Although the activity is College-organised, the risk assessment lists exposure to extremist views on College or HE-related activities in London under external factors; the College sites category covers materials on or around College sites.
questions.source_excerpt: External Factors Students / staff being exposed to extremist views whilst at College, or on College / HE related activities in London;

questions.question: The Prevent Policy names the people who chair, sit on or give administrative support to the Prevent Steering Group. Which of these roles is not one of them?
options: The Registrar
The Senior Quality Assurance Officer
The Executive Assistant
The Human Resource Officer
questions.explanation: The PSG is chaired by the Principal, includes the Head of Quality Assurance and Senior Quality Assurance Officer, and is supported by the Registrar and Executive Assistant; the Human Resource Officer is named only as someone to whom the PSG may refer concerns about staff.
questions.source_excerpt: It is chaired by the Principal and includes the Head of Quality Assurance and Senior Quality Assurance Officer. It receives administrative support from the Registrar and the Executive Assistant.

questions.question: A new manager believes the Prevent HE/FE Co-ordinator reviews and monitors LCC's Prevent Risk Assessment and Action Plan. How does the Prevent Policy actually allocate this responsibility?
options: The Co-ordinator reviews and monitors it, with the PSG acting only in an advisory role
The Board of Directors reviews and monitors it, with advice from PEG
The PSG reviews and monitors it, with advice from the Prevent HE/FE Co-ordinator
The Head of Quality Assurance reviews it alone and then reports it to the Co-ordinator
questions.explanation: The Action Plan section states that the Risk Assessment and Action Plan is reviewed and monitored by the PSG, with the Prevent HE/FE Co-ordinator providing advice.
questions.source_excerpt: The group is responsible for overseeing the Risk Assessment and Action Plan to address threats and mitigate risks. The Risk Assessment and Action Plan is reviewed and monitored by the PSG with advice from the Prevent HE/FE Co-ordinator.

questions.question: Under the Partnership section of the Prevent Policy, which group is expected to report concerns to relevant external bodies as well as to the College?
options: Brand ambassadors and agents involved in student recruitment
Providers of placements and work-related settings
Professional bodies with their own guidelines and duties
Religious and community contacts advising on events
questions.explanation: Placement and work-related setting providers are expected to follow CONTEST and report concerns to the College and relevant external bodies; agents and professional bodies are expected to report or raise concerns with the College.
questions.source_excerpt: In respect of student recruitment all brand ambassadors / agents are expected to follow the College's Prevent practices to meet the Prevent agenda and report any concerns to the College; ... Placement and providers of work-related settings are expected to follow the governments' counter-terrorism strategy, `CONTEST' and report any concerns to the College and relevant external bodies;

questions.question: A part-time administrator in a non-key role and a newly elected Student Representative both ask whether they will receive Prevent training. What does the Prevent Policy provide?
options: Neither will: Prevent training is limited to key staff and stakeholders, and students are not given any Prevent training
Both will: all College staff are trained, with key staff prioritised, and Student Representatives get awareness training
Only the administrator will, because Prevent training is provided to all College staff but never to any students
Only the Student Representative will, because staff training is restricted to key College staff and stakeholders
questions.explanation: Staff training is provided to all College staff, with key staff and stakeholders prioritised, and the College separately provides Prevent awareness training for Student Representatives.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff training is provided to all College staff. Key College staff and stakeholders who will benefit most directly from Prevent training are prioritised. ... The College provides Prevent awareness training for the Student Representatives

questions.question: One student plans to use College IT to research extremist propaganda for a dissertation; another uses College social media to promote a non-violent extremist cause. How does the Prevent Policy treat the two cases?
options: Research must go to the PSG for advice; the promotion is not permitted
Both are banned outright on College systems, whatever the reason or purpose
Both are allowed, since the College is committed to free intellectual enquiry
The research needs police approval, and the promotion needs PSG approval first
questions.explanation: Using College IT or social media to promote violent or non-violent extremism is not permitted, whereas anyone seeking to research sensitive or extremism-related materials must refer the proposed activity to the PSG for advice.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not permitted for any member staff, students or third partice to use the College's Student Management System (SMS), IT and social media ... for the instigation, promotion or planning or execution of violent or non-violent extremism ... Staff or students who seek to research sensitive or extremism-related materials, must refer proposed activity to the PSG for advice;

questions.question: Which College policy does the Prevent Policy say sets out expectations on the use, transmission or receipt of obscene, unlawful or indecent material and makes specific mention of the Prevent duty?
options: The Safeguarding and Security Policy
The Student Code of Conduct
The External Speaker and Events Policy
The Information Security Policy
questions.explanation: The Prevent Policy attributes these expectations, and the specific mention of the Prevent duty, to the Information Security Policy; the Safeguarding and Security Policy covers the consequences of accessing inappropriate material and monitoring.
questions.source_excerpt: The College's Information Security Policy clearly states expectation of use, transmission or receipt of obscene, unlawful or indecent images or material, and makes specific mention of the Prevent duty.

questions.question: A commercial company asks to send an external presenter to run a session for students on a College campus. Under the Prevent Policy, how should this visit be handled?
options: It is outside the External Speaker and Events Policy, which covers only academic and religious events
It needs sign-off only from the local Prevent Co-ordinator, as the presenter is not College staff
It is subject to the External Speaker and Events Policy, including its booking and referral procedures
It falls under the Information Security Policy, since commercial visitors may use College IT
questions.explanation: Commercial external visitors are expressly listed among the speakers and events subject to the External Speaker and Events Policy, which sets out the booking process and the referral/escalation procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: External speakers and events, including academic guest lectures, Student body activity, commercial external visitors and/or religious events are subject to the External Speaker and Events Policy which clearly outlines the process for booking such events and speakers and also the procedures for referral / escalation;

questions.question: HR organises a staff-only meeting in a College room and a manager proposes seating men and women separately. What is the position under the Prevent Policy?
options: It is not permitted, because the ban covers meetings attended by employees of the College
It is permitted, provided the meeting is internal and not advertised as a speaking event
It is permitted, because the segregation ban applies only to events for students or the public
It is permitted if it is agreed in advance with both the Human Resource Officer and the PSG
questions.explanation: Gender segregation is not permitted, and the events covered include meetings organised for and attended by employees of the College, whether or not held on College premises.
questions.source_excerpt: seating men and women separately at an event, is not permitted. These events include academic meetings, speaking events, lectures or meetings organised for and attended by students, members of the public or employees of the College, whether or not held on College premises.

questions.question: A College support adviser learns about a student group engaged only in lawful activity and assumes nothing about the group could ever be shared outside the service. How does the Prevent Policy treat this assumption?
options: It is correct, because information about lawful activity must always stay within the support service
It is wrong only where the students have given written consent for the information to be shared
It is correct unless the group's activity becomes unlawful and has already been reported to the police
It is wrong, as in accordance with the law it can be disclosed to bodies within or outside the College
questions.explanation: The policy recognises that support services' work may result in disclosure of information about individuals or groups engaged in lawful activity, and that in accordance with the law this can be disclosed to bodies within or outside the College.
questions.source_excerpt: the nature of the work undertaken by some College support services, may result in the disclosure of specific information about an individual or a group of individuals engaged in lawful activity. In accordance with the law, such information can be disclosed to bodies within or outside the College

questions.question: A person emails the College threatening to attack a government building, but never acts on the threat. How does the Prevent Policy's definition of terrorism treat a threat like this?
options: It cannot amount to terrorism, as the definition applies only once violent action has been taken
It falls outside the definition, as a threat not carried out counts only as non-violent extremism
It can amount to terrorism only if the threat comes from a member of a proscribed group
It can amount to terrorism, as the definition covers the threat of such action as well as its use
questions.explanation: The definition of terrorism covers the use or threat of action involving violence against a person or property or endangering life, so a threat that is never carried out can still qualify where the required purposes are present.
questions.source_excerpt: Section 1 of the Terrorism Act (2000) defines terrorism as the use or threat of action where the action involves violence against a person, property, endangers a person's life ... The use or threat must be designed to influence the government, intimidate the public and must be made for the purposes of advancing a political, religious, racial or ideological cause;

questions.question: A staff member pins up a leaflet in a shared College office encouraging non-violent extremism and argues that, as it urges no violence, the College cannot act. What does the Prevent Policy allow?
options: Nothing, as the removal power applies only to material that encourages violence
Asking them to remove it, as the power covers non-violent extremism too
Asking for its removal only if the leaflet was displayed in a student area
Asking for its removal only once the police have confirmed it is unlawful material
questions.explanation: The College reserves the right to ask staff or students to remove from its sites any electronic or physical material encouraging engagement with violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation or terrorism.
questions.source_excerpt: The College reserves the right to ask students or members of staff to remove from the College's sites, all or any electronic or physical material encouraging engagement with violent or non-violent extremism, radicalisation or terrorism related activities;

questions.question: The Prevent Policy refers staff to several other College documents. Which pairing of document and what the Prevent Policy says it covers is correct?
options: Information Security Policy: the steps the College may take to monitor or intercept communications
Freedom of Speech Policy and Code of Practice: the process for booking external speakers and events
Privacy Notice for Students: behaviour expectations and the activities permitted on College sites
Student Welfare Policy: the rules on using the College's prayer rooms and multi-faith facilities
questions.explanation: The Prevent Policy says the Student Code of Conduct and the Privacy Notice for Students set out behaviour expectations and activities permitted on College sites. Monitoring sits with the Safeguarding and Security Policy, bookings with the External Speaker and Events Policy, and prayer rooms with the Management of Prayer and Multi-faith Facilities Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure and Privacy Notice for Students clearly enunciate behaviour expectation and activities which are permitted on College sites;...Safeguarding and Security Policy advises staff and students of consequences of accessing inappropriate material and the steps the College may take to monitor and/or intercept communications

questions.question: A student society plans a Student body-branded religious talk in a hired hall off-site, and the speaker asks for men and women to be seated separately. Which statement matches the Prevent Policy?
options: Separate seating is not permitted, but the event falls outside the External Speakers and Events Policy as it is off-site
The External Speakers and Events Policy criteria apply, and seating men and women separately is not permitted
The External Speakers and Events Policy criteria apply, but separate seating is allowed as the hall is off-site
Neither rule applies, as religious events are overseen by religious and community contacts rather than the College
questions.explanation: Off-site events that are College or Student body branded are subject to the same External Speakers and Events Policy criteria, and religious events are expressly covered. Seating men and women separately is not permitted at such events, whether or not they are held on College premises.
questions.source_excerpt: Events held off-site which are College or Student body branded are subject to the same criteria outlined in the External Speakers and Events Policy;...seating men and women separately at an event, is not permitted. These events include academic meetings, speaking events, lectures or meetings organised for and attended by students...whether or not held on College premises.

questions.question: In a seminar, one student argues that the meaning of 'the rule of law' is contested and should be debated; another repeatedly campaigns for followers of one faith to be driven out of the College. Under the Prevent Policy, which is extremism?
options: Both, since each student is openly questioning one of the fundamental British values
Only the first, since arguing that the rule of law is contested is vocal opposition to it
Neither, since the policy's definition of extremism requires violence or a call for violence
Only the second, as it is active opposition to tolerance of different faiths and beliefs
questions.explanation: The policy defines extremism as vocal or active opposition to fundamental British values, including mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs. It also recognises these values as rightly the subject of debate in Colleges, so debating their meaning is not extremism.
questions.source_excerpt: The legislation defines extremism as `vocal or active opposition to fundamental British values, including democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs...recognising that these are values and concepts which are rightly the subject of debate and consideration in universities and Colleges;

questions.question: A criminal gang threatens to sabotage a busy railway line unless a company pays it a ransom; its only aim is money. How does the Prevent Policy's definition of terrorism apply to this threat?
options: It is not terrorism, as the threat is not made to advance a political, religious, racial or ideological cause
It is terrorism, as any threat that endangers public safety meets the definition whatever its purpose
It is terrorism, as the definition requires only that the threat is designed to intimidate the public
It is not terrorism yet, but it would become terrorism once the railway line was actually sabotaged
questions.explanation: The definition requires the use or threat to be designed to influence the government, intimidate the public and advance a political, religious, racial or ideological cause. A threat made purely for money lacks that purpose, whether or not it is carried out.
questions.source_excerpt: defines terrorism as the use or threat of action where the action involves violence against a person, property, endangers a person's life, creates a serious risk to the health or safety of the public...The use or threat must be designed to influence the government, intimidate the public and must be made for the purposes of advancing a political, religious, racial or ideological cause;

policies.title: Reasonable Adjustment and Special Needs Policy

questions.question: While marking coursework, you notice signs that a student may have an undiagnosed learning difficulty that seems to be disadvantaging them. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what should you do?
options: Refer the student directly to an outside assessment centre yourself for a formal diagnosis.
Adjust the student's marks to compensate for the difficulty you have noticed in their work.
Refer the student to the Registrar, who can refer them for an official assessment if they wish.
Take no action unless the student has already declared a disability on their College application form.
questions.explanation: The policy's staff guidelines state that staff who notice signs of potential learning difficulties should refer the student to the Registrar, who can refer the student for an official assessment if the student wishes.
questions.source_excerpt: Should staff notice any signs of potential learning difficulties amongst students that may be disadvantaging to them, they should refer the student to the Registrar. If the student wishes to, the Registrar can refer the student for an official assessment.

questions.question: A colleague asks you to forward a student's GP letter, provided as evidence of their disability, so the whole teaching team is aware. The student has not agreed to this. What does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy require?
options: Forward it, as all teaching staff on the programme are entitled to see a student's disability evidence.
Do not share it, as such evidence is confidential and not shared without student consent.
Forward it once the student's name and ID number have been removed, as anonymised evidence may be shared.
Share it with the Programme Leader, who can then decide which other staff may see it.
questions.explanation: Under the policy's confidentiality guideline, any evidence students provide to support their needs is treated as confidential and must not be shared without the student's consent.
questions.source_excerpt: Any evidence provided by students to support their needs will be treated as confidential and not be shared without student consent.

questions.question: You are marking an assignment from a student who has agreed reasonable adjustments for a learning difficulty. According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how should you mark it?
options: Against the same criteria as other students, as their support is given in advance of assessment.
Using a lower pass threshold, set by the Programme Leader to reflect the student's learning difficulty.
By adding compensatory marks to make up for the disadvantage caused by the difficulty.
Using the separate, simplified marking criteria recorded in the student's Support Agreement Plan.
questions.explanation: The policy explains that students with learning difficulties are supported in advance of assessment, so adjustment in marking is limited to ensuring all students are marked against the same criteria.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with learning difficulties are supported in advance of assessment (their reasonable adjustments). These adjustments `level the playing field' and therefore the need to adjust in marking is limited to ensuring that all students are marked against the same criteria.

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what happens to students who have declared a disability on their application form?
options: They are invited to a confidential one-to-one session with the Registrar to discuss reasonable adjustments.
They are automatically registered for Disabled Students' Allowances by the College Admissions Office.
Their disability details are circulated to all of their tutors and the Library before the course begins.
They are asked to discuss their needs with their Programme Leader during the first class of the course.
questions.explanation: The policy states that all students who declare disabilities on their application forms are contacted and invited to a confidential one-to-one session with the Registrar to discuss reasonable adjustments.
questions.source_excerpt: All students who have declared disabilities on their application forms are contacted and invited to meet the Registrar for a confidential one-to-one session to discuss the reasonable adjustments that the College can make for them;

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what will the College do if a student has declared a disability but has not been formally diagnosed?
options: Decline to consider any adjustments until the student has arranged and paid for a private diagnosis.
Ask the student's Programme Leader to carry out a diagnostic assessment during class time.
Put the requested adjustments in place straight away, without requiring any assessment or evidence.
Refer the student to an outside centre for an assessment, whose report informs the support given.
questions.explanation: Where a student has declared a disability but has not been formally diagnosed, the policy says the College will refer the student to an outside centre for an assessment, and the report allows the College to accommodate their needs.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student has declared a disability, but has not been formally diagnosed, then the College will refer the student to an outside centre for an assessment. The assessment report allows the College to accommodate significant needs of the student

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, who is responsible for implementing a student's Support Agreement Plan (SAP)?
options: The Student Welfare Officer, in consultation with the Admissions Officer and the Head of Library Services.
The Programme Leader, in consultation with the Academic Administration Office.
The Registrar, in consultation with the Head of Program and Monitoring and the Programme Manager.
The Academic Board, in consultation with the student's personal tutor and the Registrar.
questions.explanation: The policy gives the Registrar responsibility for implementing the SAP, in consultation with the Head of Program and Monitoring (HoPAM) and the Programme Manager (PM).
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar has responsibility for the implementation of the student Support Agreement Plan (SAP) in consultation with the Head of Program and Monitoring (HoPAM) and Programme Manager (PM);

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, at what point is a student's Support Agreement Plan (SAP) completed by the Registrar together with the student?
options: After the student's first set of assessment results has been published.
Once evidence of the student's difficulties has been received.
Before the student has submitted their application form to the College.
At the end of the first term, following a review by the Academic Board.
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Agreement is completed by the Registrar together with the student once evidence of the difficulties has been received.
questions.source_excerpt: The Agreement will be completed by the Registrar together with the student once evidence of the difficulties has been received;

questions.question: Midway through the course, a student with a signed Support Agreement Plan tells you their condition has changed and they now need different support. What does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy say?
options: The Agreement is fixed for the whole course and cannot be changed once it is signed.
The Agreement stays as signed until the next academic year, when the Registrar reviews all plans.
The student must reapply through the admissions process and submit new evidence to change the Agreement.
The Agreement can be reviewed at any time during the course if support needs change.
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Support Agreement Plan can be reviewed at any time during the course should the student's support needs change.
questions.source_excerpt: The Agreement can be reviewed at any time during the course, should the student's support need change.

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how does the College ensure that learning opportunities are equally accessible to all students?
options: Through inclusive design wherever possible and reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary.
Through separate teaching groups arranged for all students who have declared a disability.
Through individual adjustments that are put in place after a student has failed an assessment.
Through external DSA funding, which replaces the need for the College to make adjustments.
questions.explanation: The policy commits the College to offering equally accessible learning opportunities by inclusive design wherever possible and by reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are offered learning opportunities that are equally accessible to them, by means of inclusive design wherever possible and by means of reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary;

questions.question: A prospective applicant with a disability contacts you before enrolling and asks whether they can discuss possible support. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what can they do?
options: Nothing yet, as support is not discussed with applicants until they have enrolled and attended induction.
Arrange to meet the Registrar before enrolment to discuss adjustments, including for admission.
Apply for DSA first, as support cannot be discussed with the College until DSA funding is approved.
Wait for the Student Welfare Officer to contact them at the end of their first term.
questions.explanation: The policy allows applicants to arrange to meet the Registrar prior to enrolment to discuss reasonable adjustments for their studies and adjustments to support them during the admission stage.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants for programmes offered by LCC can arrange to meet with the Registrar prior to enrolment. This allows applicants to discuss the reasonable adjustments that could be put into place for them should they join the College as a student, as well as adjustments that can support them during the admission stage;

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which of the following is NOT listed as something a student's evidence letter or report should contain?
options: The likely duration of the student's disability, whether temporary or permanent.
Any prescribed medication and the impact of any possible side effects.
The specific adjustments the College must put in place for the student.
An indication of how the condition might affect the student's studies.
questions.explanation: The policy lists the nature of the disability, its likely duration, day-to-day effects, likely effect on studies, prescribed medication and side effects, and coping strategies; the specific adjustments the College must make are not among the listed items.
questions.source_excerpt: The letter/report should contain the following: ... The likely duration (temporary or permanent); ... An indication of how the condition might affect their studies; ... Any prescribed medication and the impact of any possible side effects;

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, who processes a student's application for Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA)?
options: The College Registrar, as part of drawing up the student's Support Agreement Plan.
The Academic Board, through its termly review of student support.
The Admissions Officer, once the applicant has been offered a place at the College.
The funding body, which the policy identifies as Student Finance England.
questions.explanation: The policy states that DSA applications are processed by the funding body, Student Finance England, not by the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Applications will be processed by the funding body, i.e., Student Finance England.

questions.question: The Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy is designed to enable all students to develop their academic, personal and professional potential. What else does the policy state it is designed to eliminate?
options: Any need for students to provide disability evidence
Arbitrary and unnecessary barriers to learning
Separate assessment deadlines for disabled students
The cost of specialist equipment for disabled students
questions.explanation: The policy's objectives state that it is designed to enable all students to develop their potential and to eliminate arbitrary and unnecessary barriers to learning.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy is designed to enable all students to develop their academic, personal, and professional potential, regardless of any disability or difficulties they may have and to eliminate arbitrary and unnecessary barriers to learning.

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how are prospective students encouraged to provide information about a disability?
options: Through a mandatory medical questionnaire sent out with every offer letter from the College
Through a phone call from the Registrar to every applicant before an offer is made
Through a disability disclosure session held for all new students during the first week of induction
Through a positive statement in the prospectus, on the website and in other College publicity
questions.explanation: The policy states that prospective students are encouraged to share information about a disability by a positive statement in the College prospectus, on the website and in other College publicity.
questions.source_excerpt: Prospective students are encouraged to provide information about a disability, by including a positive statement in the College prospectus, on the website and in any other College publicity where appropriate;

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what does the College provide to enable staff to identify any special needs of the students they teach or interact with?
options: Ongoing staff development training
A one-off workshop at induction
Access to all students' DSA reports
A guidance leaflet from the Library
questions.explanation: The policy commits the College to providing ongoing staff development training so that staff can identify the special needs of students they teach or interact with.
questions.source_excerpt: Provision of ongoing staff development training by the College to enable staff to identify any special needs of students they teach and/or interact with, in learning contexts;

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what does the College use to record, and inform its departments of, the adjustments agreed with a student who has an externally assessed disability?
options: The student's DSA Needs Assessment Report
The student's original application form
A confidential Support Agreement Plan (SAP)
A shared staff disability spreadsheet
questions.explanation: For students with externally assessed disabilities, the policy says the College uses a confidential Support Agreement Plan to record the agreed adjustments and inform departments of them.
questions.source_excerpt: For students with externally assessed disabilities, the College will use a confidential Support Agreement Plan to record and inform departments within the College of the adjustments that have been agreed with the student;

questions.question: The Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy says reasonable adjustments are implemented for students with declared disabilities. What does it say is available to those who believe they may have a disability?
options: Automatic extra exam time
Advice and guidance
A DSA award
Exemption from assessments
questions.explanation: The policy states that advice and guidance are available to those who believe they may have a disability, while reasonable adjustments are implemented for declared disabilities.
questions.source_excerpt: Reasonable adjustments are implemented for students with declared disabilities; advice and guidance are available to those who believe they may have a disability;

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what adjustment can applicants with disabilities such as dyslexia request for an English language examination required for admission, and on what condition?
options: Exemption from the examination, if the Registrar approves it
A lower pass mark, if dyslexia was declared on the application form
A deferred examination date, if the Admissions Officer agrees
Additional time, if they have supporting evidence
questions.explanation: The policy states that applicants with disabilities such as dyslexia can request adjustments, including additional time, for the English language examination if they have supporting evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: some applicants may be required to undergo an English language examination to gain admission to the College. Applicants with disabilities, such as dyslexia, can request adjustments including additional time, if they have supporting evidence.

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, by whom is the available Special Needs support promoted to all students during programme induction?
options: The Student Welfare Officer
The Programme Leader
The Registrar
The Head of Program and Monitoring
questions.explanation: The policy states that the available Special Needs support is promoted to all students during programme induction by the Student Welfare Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: Promote the available Special Needs' support during the programme induction, to all students by the Student Welfare Officer.

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, where an applicant is offered a place, what is the Admissions Officer required to encourage them to do?
options: Wait until after their first assessment before requesting any adjustments or support
Arrange adjustments directly with their Programme Leader rather than the Registrar
Begin arranging any necessary adjustments and support for their studies as soon as possible
Apply for Disabled Students' Allowances before they are allowed to enrol at the College
questions.explanation: The policy requires the Admissions Officer to encourage candidates who are offered a place to begin arranging any necessary adjustments and support as soon as possible.
questions.source_excerpt: Where applicants are offered a place, the Admission's Officer is required to: ... Encourage candidates to begin the process of arranging any necessary adjustments and support for their studies as soon as possible;

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what does the College require a student to provide if they wish to apply for adjustments?
options: A written recommendation from their Programme Leader
Confirmation of an approved DSA award
A signed Support Agreement Plan
Evidence that relates to their disability
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College requires students to provide evidence of their disabilities if they wish to apply for adjustments.
questions.source_excerpt: The College requires students to provide evidence of their disabilities if the student wishes to apply for adjustments;

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which of the following is listed as a need that an outside centre's assessment report can allow the College to accommodate?
options: Exemption from all coursework submission deadlines
One-to-one tutorials and assertiveness training
A reduced pass mark for all assessed modules
Automatic resits without any capping of marks
questions.explanation: The policy lists one-to-one tutorials, assertiveness training and permission for technology-assisted learning among the needs the assessment report allows the College to accommodate.
questions.source_excerpt: The assessment report allows the College to accommodate significant needs of the student, including but not limited to one-to-one tutorials, assertiveness training, permission for technology-assisted learning

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which of the following is given as an example of acceptable evidence of a student's disability?
options: A letter from a GP or a specialist
A signed self-declaration from the student
A reference from the student's former tutor
A written statement from a family member
questions.explanation: The policy gives a letter from a GP or specialist, or a recent DSA Needs Assessment Report, as examples of evidence that relates to a student's disability.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are required to provide evidence that specifically relates to their disability. For example, a letter from a GP or specialist or a recent Needs Assessment Report for a Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA).

questions.question: According to the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which of the following is listed as an example of the extra costs that Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA) can pay for?
options: Tuition fees for the student's programme
Everyday living costs such as food and rent
Specialist equipment and non-medical helpers
Private medical treatment for the condition
questions.explanation: The policy states that DSA pays for extra costs incurred as a direct result of a disability, including specialist equipment, non-medical helpers and related expenses such as photocopying.
questions.source_excerpt: DSA pays for extra costs that students may incur in attending their programme as a direct result of their disability, including but not limited to specialist equipment, non-medical helpers, and other related expenses

questions.question: What does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy say about repaying Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA) received by students?
options: They must be repaid in full once the student's course has ended
They are repaid from future earnings, in the same way as tuition loans
They must be repaid only if the student withdraws from the course early
They do not, at present, have to be repaid by those receiving them
questions.explanation: The policy states that students who receive DSA are, at the present time, not required to repay the benefits received.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who receive such loans are, at the present time, not required to repay the benefits received;

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, depending on the agreed adjustments, a signed Support Agreement Plan may include instructions to which of the following?
options: Student Finance England, the Admissions Officer and the Academic Board
The Programme Leader, the Academic Administration Office and the Library
The student's GP, the outside assessment centre and the Registrar
The Student Welfare Officer, the Finance Office and IT Services
questions.explanation: The policy states that the signed agreement may include instructions to the Programme Leader, Academic Administration Office and Library, depending on the agreed adjustments.
questions.source_excerpt: The signed agreement may include instructions to the Programme Leader, Academic Administration Office and Library, depending on the agreed adjustments;
