questions.question: According to the staff guidelines in the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what does the policy say about learning difficulties that students are unaware of?
options: They are always identified at enrolment through the application form
They are identified by the Library during study skills sessions
They could become evident in the work the student produces
They do not need to be considered unless the student declares them
questions.explanation: The staff guidelines note that students may have learning difficulties they are unaware of, which could become evident in their work.
questions.source_excerpt: Students may have learning difficulties that they are unaware of, which could become evident in their work;

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how often does the Registrar provide the Academic Board with a report summarising any issues about additional support or reasonable adjustments for students?
options: Once a term
Once a year
Once a month
Every two years
questions.explanation: The policy makes the Registrar responsible for giving the Academic Board a termly report summarising issues about additional support or reasonable adjustments.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar is responsible for providing the Academic Board with a termly report summarising any issues regarding the additional support or reasonable adjustments that are provided to students;

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which sequence correctly describes how a student's Support Agreement Plan (SAP) is put in place?
options: The Registrar drafts and signs the SAP, the student receives a copy, and evidence of the difficulties is collected later
The student completes the SAP alone, the Programme Leader signs it, and the Registrar then requests supporting evidence
Evidence is received, the Registrar and student complete the SAP, the student agrees it, both sign it and the student gets a copy
Evidence is received, the Academic Board approves the SAP, and the Registrar signs it without needing the student's agreement
questions.explanation: The policy says the Registrar completes the Agreement with the student once evidence is received; once the student agrees its content, both sign it, and the student receives a copy.
questions.source_excerpt: The Agreement will be completed by the Registrar together with the student once evidence of the difficulties has been received; ... Once the student has agreed the content of the agreement, it will be signed by the Registrar and the student; ... The student will also receive a copy of the agreement;

questions.question: A student applying for adjustments offers a recent Needs Assessment Report prepared for their Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA) as evidence. How does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy treat this?
options: It is an acceptable example of evidence that specifically relates to the student's disability.
It is not accepted, as only a letter from the student's own GP counts as evidence of a disability.
It is accepted only once Student Finance England has confirmed its contents directly to the Registrar.
It is not accepted, as DSA reports belong to the funding body and cannot be relied on by the College.
questions.explanation: The policy gives a recent Needs Assessment Report for DSA, alongside a letter from a GP or specialist, as an example of evidence that specifically relates to a student's disability.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are required to provide evidence that specifically relates to their disability. For example, a letter from a GP or specialist or a recent Needs Assessment Report for a Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA).

questions.question: A student with a formal diagnosis of dyslexia, declared on their application, now wishes to apply for adjustments. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what must happen?
options: The College must refer them to an outside centre for assessment, as every student needs one before adjustments.
They must provide evidence relating to their disability, such as a letter from a GP or specialist.
Nothing further is needed, as declaring dyslexia on the application form is enough to apply for adjustments.
Their Programme Leader must first confirm the diagnosis by observing them in class for a full term.
questions.explanation: The policy requires students who wish to apply for adjustments to provide evidence of their disability, such as a GP or specialist letter; referral to an outside centre is for students who have not been formally diagnosed.
questions.source_excerpt: The College requires students to provide evidence of their disabilities if the student wishes to apply for adjustments; ... If a student has declared a disability, but has not been formally diagnosed, then the College will refer the student to an outside centre for an assessment.

questions.question: A student declared a disability on their application but has never been formally diagnosed. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which route leads to their Support Agreement Plan (SAP)?
options: The Registrar completes the SAP straight away, and a formal diagnosis is sought only if the student fails an assessment.
The student applies to Student Finance England for a diagnosis, and the SAP is drawn up once DSA funding is awarded.
The Programme Leader assesses the student in class and signs the SAP once the difficulty is confirmed in their work.
The College refers them to an outside centre for assessment, and the Registrar completes the SAP with them once evidence is received.
questions.explanation: For a declared but undiagnosed disability, the College refers the student to an outside centre for assessment, and the SAP is completed by the Registrar with the student once evidence has been received.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student has declared a disability, but has not been formally diagnosed, then the College will refer the student to an outside centre for an assessment. ... The Agreement will be completed by the Registrar together with the student once evidence of the difficulties has been received;

questions.question: A student with a long-term medical condition, rather than a disability or learning difficulty, asks whether Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA) could apply to them. What does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy say?
options: They are not eligible, as DSA funding is limited to students who have a physical disability.
They are not eligible, as DSA funding is limited to specific learning difficulties such as dyslexia.
They may be eligible, as DSA can fund students with a long-term medical condition as well as a disability.
They may be eligible, but only if their long-term medical condition was first assessed by an outside centre.
questions.explanation: The policy states that students with a disability, specific learning difficulty or long-term medical condition may be eligible for DSA funding.
questions.source_excerpt: If students have a disability, specific learning difficulty or long-term medical condition, they may be eligible for funding from the Disabled Student Allowances (DSA);

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how are enrolment-stage duties shared between the Admissions Officer and the Student Welfare Officer once an applicant is offered a place?
options: The Student Welfare Officer meets offer-holders to agree adjustments, and the Admissions Officer then signs their SAP.
The Admissions Officer encourages early arrangement of adjustments; the Student Welfare Officer promotes support at induction.
The Admissions Officer completes the Support Agreement Plan; the Student Welfare Officer signs it with the student at induction.
The Admissions Officer collects disability evidence; the Student Welfare Officer then forwards it to all of the student's tutors.
questions.explanation: At enrolment, the Admissions Officer encourages candidates offered a place to begin arranging adjustments as soon as possible, and the Student Welfare Officer promotes Special Needs support to all students at induction.
questions.source_excerpt: Where applicants are offered a place, the Admission's Officer is required to: ... Encourage candidates to begin the process of arranging any necessary adjustments and support for their studies as soon as possible; ... Promote the available Special Needs' support during the programme induction, to all students by the Student Welfare Officer.

questions.question: Under the Monitoring and Enhancement section of the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which statement correctly describes the Registrar's responsibilities?
options: Keep a confidential record of disabled students, monitor the adjustments made, and report termly to the Academic Board.
Keep a record of disabled students that is open to all staff, and report annually to the Board of Directors on adjustments.
Keep a confidential record of disabled students, and report monthly to the Student Welfare Officer on DSA claims.
Monitor DSA payments made by Student Finance England, and report termly to each student's Programme Leader.
questions.explanation: The Registrar maintains a confidential record of disabled students, monitors the adjustments made for them, and provides the Academic Board with a termly report on support and adjustment issues.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar is responsible for maintaining a confidential record of disabled students and monitoring the adjustments the College makes for them; ... The Registrar is responsible for providing the Academic Board with a termly report summarising any issues regarding the additional support or reasonable adjustments that are provided to students;

questions.question: After a tutor refers a student with possible learning difficulties to the Registrar, the student says they do not want an official assessment. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what applies?
options: The Registrar must refer the student for an official assessment, unless the tutor withdraws the original concern.
The tutor should apply adjusted marking to the student's work until the student agrees to an official assessment.
The Registrar can refer the student for an official assessment only if the student wishes to be referred.
The tutor should refer the student to Student Finance England for a DSA needs assessment instead of the Registrar.
questions.explanation: The staff guidelines say staff refer the student to the Registrar, who can refer the student for an official assessment if the student wishes to.
questions.source_excerpt: Should staff notice any signs of potential learning difficulties amongst students that may be disadvantaging to them, they should refer the student to the Registrar. If the student wishes to, the Registrar can refer the student for an official assessment.

questions.question: A colleague believes the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy only covers students with a formally declared disability. Which statement correctly describes the policy's scope?
options: It covers only students who declared a disability on their application form and then provided evidence at the enrolment stage.
It covers students with disabilities and learning difficulties, so they can participate on the same basis as others.
It covers only students who have been awarded Disabled Students' Allowances by Student Finance England.
It covers only students whose disability was assessed by an outside centre before they joined the College.
questions.explanation: The policy's objectives describe the steps the College takes so that students with disabilities and learning difficulties can participate on the same basis as other students.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy describes the steps taken by the College to ensure students with disabilities and learning difficulties can participate on the same basis as other students.

questions.question: A specialist's letter describes the nature of a student's condition and how it affects them day to day. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which other detail should the letter also contain?
options: The student's previous examination results and academic transcript.
The grade adjustments the College should apply when marking their work.
Confirmation that the student has already applied for DSA funding.
Any coping strategies the student uses to manage their disability.
questions.explanation: Besides the nature of the disability and its day-to-day effects, the policy says the letter or report should include any other coping strategies the student uses to manage their disability.
questions.source_excerpt: The letter/report should contain the following: ... The nature of the disability; ... A brief account of how the condition affects the student on a day-to-day basis; ... Any other coping strategies they use to manage their disability.

questions.question: An applicant with dyslexia must pass an English language examination to be admitted and wants to discuss support before enrolling. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what is available?
options: A meeting with the Registrar before enrolment, and extra exam time if they have supporting evidence.
A meeting with the Registrar only after enrolment, and full exemption from the English examination.
A meeting with the Student Welfare Officer at induction, and extra exam time without any evidence.
No support until they enrol, when the Admissions Officer may waive the English examination entirely.
questions.explanation: Applicants can arrange to meet the Registrar before enrolment to discuss adjustments, and applicants with disabilities such as dyslexia can request additional time for the English examination if they have supporting evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants for programmes offered by LCC can arrange to meet with the Registrar prior to enrolment. ... Applicants with disabilities, such as dyslexia, can request adjustments including additional time, if they have supporting evidence.

questions.question: An outside centre's assessment report for a student recommends using a digital recording device in lectures. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how can the College respond?
options: It can permit recording only once Student Finance England has awarded the student DSA funding to pay for the device.
It can accommodate the need, as the report allows permission for technology-assisted learning such as recording devices.
It cannot act on the report until a second outside centre has confirmed the recommendation in writing.
It can act on the report only once the Academic Board has approved it at its next termly review meeting.
questions.explanation: The policy says the outside centre's assessment report allows the College to accommodate significant needs, including permission for technology-assisted learning through digital recording devices.
questions.source_excerpt: The assessment report allows the College to accommodate significant needs of the student, including but not limited to one-to-one tutorials, assertiveness training, permission for technology-assisted learning through use of digital recording devices, mind-mapping software, and other peripherals.

questions.question: A student applying for adjustments provides a specialist's letter stating that their condition is expected to be temporary. A colleague says temporary conditions cannot be evidenced. What does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy indicate?
options: The colleague is right, as evidence is accepted only where a specialist confirms that the disability is permanent.
The colleague is right, as a temporary condition must be evidenced by a DSA Needs Assessment Report instead.
The letter can be accepted only once an outside centre has separately confirmed that the condition is temporary.
The letter should state the likely duration, which the policy lists as temporary or permanent.
questions.explanation: The policy lists the likely duration, temporary or permanent, among the contents an evidence letter or report should include, so a temporary condition can be evidenced.
questions.source_excerpt: The letter/report should contain the following: ... The likely duration (temporary or permanent);

questions.question: A student has given the Registrar a specialist's letter about their disability and also wants to apply for Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA). Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how are these two matters handled?
options: The Registrar completes the Support Agreement Plan with the student; Student Finance England processes the DSA application.
The Registrar processes the DSA application and then completes the Support Agreement Plan once the funding is confirmed.
Student Finance England completes the Support Agreement Plan; the Registrar processes the DSA application for the student.
The Support Agreement Plan cannot be completed until Student Finance England has approved the student's DSA application.
questions.explanation: The Support Agreement Plan is completed by the Registrar with the student once evidence has been received, while DSA applications are processed by the funding body, Student Finance England.
questions.source_excerpt: Applications will be processed by the funding body, i.e., Student Finance England. ... The Agreement will be completed by the Registrar together with the student once evidence of the difficulties has been received;

questions.question: A student with a specific learning difficulty asks you about Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA). Which statement is fully consistent with the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy?
options: They may be eligible; the Registrar processes the application; at present the allowance does not need to be repaid.
They may be eligible; Student Finance England processes the application; it must be repaid once the course ends.
They may be eligible; Student Finance England processes the application; at present it does not need to be repaid.
They are not eligible, as DSA is limited to physical disabilities; Student Finance England would process any application.
questions.explanation: The policy says students with a specific learning difficulty may be eligible for DSA, applications are processed by Student Finance England, and recipients are at present not required to repay it.
questions.source_excerpt: If students have a disability, specific learning difficulty or long-term medical condition, they may be eligible for funding from the Disabled Student Allowances (DSA); ... Applications will be processed by the funding body, i.e., Student Finance England. ... Students who receive such loans are, at the present time, not required to repay the benefits received;

questions.question: The Registrar and a student have drafted the student's Support Agreement Plan, but the student does not yet agree with part of its content. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what is the position?
options: The Registrar can sign it alone and implement it, as the Registrar is responsible for its implementation.
The Registrar and the Head of Program and Monitoring can sign it in place of the student and send them a copy.
The Programme Leader settles the disputed content, and the plan is then signed by the Registrar and Programme Leader.
It is signed by the Registrar and the student once the student has agreed its content, and the student gets a copy.
questions.explanation: The policy says the agreement is signed by the Registrar and the student once the student has agreed its content, and the student also receives a copy.
questions.source_excerpt: Once the student has agreed the content of the agreement, it will be signed by the Registrar and the student; ... The student will also receive a copy of the agreement;

questions.question: A student's agreed adjustments concern only Library services. A colleague insists the signed Support Agreement Plan must instruct every department named in the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy. Which statement is correct?
options: It must always include instructions to the Programme Leader, the Academic Administration Office and the Library.
Its instructions to the Programme Leader, Academic Administration Office or Library depend on the adjustments agreed.
It may include instructions only to the Programme Leader, as the Library is always instructed separately by the Registrar.
It cannot include instructions to any department, as the plan is kept confidential between the student and the Registrar.
questions.explanation: The policy says the signed agreement may include instructions to the Programme Leader, Academic Administration Office and Library depending on the agreed adjustments, and the plan is used to inform departments of agreed adjustments.
questions.source_excerpt: the College will use a confidential Support Agreement Plan to record and inform departments within the College of the adjustments that have been agreed with the student; ... The signed agreement may include instructions to the Programme Leader, Academic Administration Office and Library, depending on the agreed adjustments;

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, Student A believes they may have a disability but has not declared one; Student B has declared a disability but has no formal diagnosis; Student C has declared one and provided a specialist's letter. Which pairing is correct?
options: A: referral to an outside centre for assessment; B: advice and guidance; C: Support Agreement Plan with the Registrar.
A: advice and guidance; B: referral to an outside centre for assessment; C: Support Agreement Plan with the Registrar.
A: advice and guidance; B: Support Agreement Plan with the Registrar; C: referral to an outside centre for assessment.
A: Support Agreement Plan with the Registrar; B: advice and guidance; C: referral to an outside centre for assessment.
questions.explanation: Advice and guidance are available to those who believe they may have a disability, a declared but undiagnosed student is referred to an outside centre, and the Registrar completes the Support Agreement Plan once evidence is received.
questions.source_excerpt: advice and guidance are available to those who believe they may have a disability; ... If a student has declared a disability, but has not been formally diagnosed, then the College will refer the student to an outside centre for an assessment. ... The Agreement will be completed by the Registrar together with the student once evidence of the difficulties has been received;

questions.question: An applicant with a disability other than dyslexia must pass an English language examination to be admitted. They have supporting evidence and want an adjustment other than extra time. What does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy say?
options: Adjustments to the examination are open only to applicants with dyslexia, and only in the form of additional time.
They can request adjustments, as the provision covers disabilities such as dyslexia and adjustments including extra time.
They can request additional time only; any other adjustment must wait until they enrol and agree a Support Agreement Plan.
Adjustments to admission examinations are not offered; the applicant must instead apply for DSA to fund their support.
questions.explanation: The policy lets applicants with disabilities, such as dyslexia, request adjustments including additional time if they have supporting evidence, so it is not limited to dyslexia or to extra time.
questions.source_excerpt: some applicants may be required to undergo an English language examination to gain admission to the College. Applicants with disabilities, such as dyslexia, can request adjustments including additional time, if they have supporting evidence.

questions.question: An outside centre's assessment report recommends a form of support that is not named in the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy's list of examples. What does the policy say about that list?
options: It is a complete list, so only the named forms of support, such as one-to-one tutorials, can be accommodated.
It covers only technology-assisted learning, so any other recommendation must be referred to the Academic Board.
It says the report allows the College to accommodate needs including, but not limited to, the listed examples.
It applies only to students with DSA funding, who may get support beyond the list once their funding is confirmed.
questions.explanation: The policy states that the assessment report allows the College to accommodate significant needs including but not limited to the listed examples, so the list is not exhaustive.
questions.source_excerpt: The assessment report allows the College to accommodate significant needs of the student, including but not limited to one-to-one tutorials, assertiveness training, permission for technology-assisted learning through use of digital recording devices, mind-mapping software, and other peripherals.

questions.question: A student asks the Registrar to share their specialist's letter with their Programme Leader so the Programme Leader understands their needs. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, can this be done?
options: Yes, as the policy prevents such evidence being shared only where the student has not given their consent.
No, as disability evidence may never leave the Registrar's confidential record, even when the student consents.
No, as the only route for informing a Programme Leader is the Registrar's termly report to the Academic Board.
Yes, but only once all personal and medical details have been removed so that the student cannot be identified.
questions.explanation: The policy treats evidence as confidential and bars sharing it without the student's consent; here the student is asking for it to be shared.
questions.source_excerpt: Any evidence provided by students to support their needs will be treated as confidential and not be shared without student consent.

questions.question: A student's support needs change a few weeks before an exam, and their tutor suggests allowing for this when marking instead of changing their Support Agreement Plan. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, what is the correct approach?
options: The tutor's approach is correct, as a signed plan cannot be changed until the start of the next academic year.
The tutor's approach is correct, provided the Registrar records the allowance in the termly Academic Board report.
The plan stays unchanged, and the student must reapply through admissions with new evidence before the exam.
The plan can be reviewed at any time, so support is in place in advance; marking stays against the same criteria.
questions.explanation: The College plans adjustments in advance and the Agreement can be reviewed at any time if needs change, while marking is limited to ensuring all students are marked against the same criteria.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will plan all necessary adjustments in advance. The Agreement can be reviewed at any time during the course, should the student's support need change; ... the need to adjust in marking is limited to ensuring that all students are marked against the same criteria.

questions.question: A colleague proposes that, to protect confidentiality, Special Needs support should be promoted at programme induction only to students who declared a disability. What does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy provide?
options: The Student Welfare Officer promotes it to all students at induction; declared students are invited to a Registrar one-to-one.
The Registrar promotes it only to declared students, during a confidential one-to-one session held at programme induction.
The Admissions Officer promotes it only to declared students, at the point when their offer of a place is made.
The Student Welfare Officer promotes it only to declared students, because disability information is kept confidential.
questions.explanation: The Student Welfare Officer promotes Special Needs support to all students at induction, while students who declared a disability are separately invited to a confidential one-to-one with the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: Promote the available Special Needs' support during the programme induction, to all students by the Student Welfare Officer. ... All students who have declared disabilities on their application forms are contacted and invited to meet the Registrar for a confidential one-to-one session

questions.question: The Library asks the Registrar for a full list of disabled students so it can plan its services. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how should the Library learn of adjustments that affect it?
options: Through the Registrar's record of disabled students, which the policy says is shared with all College departments.
Through a student's Support Agreement Plan, which may instruct the Library; the Registrar's record is kept confidential.
Through the Student Welfare Officer's list of the students who attended the Special Needs briefing at induction.
Through the Academic Board, which circulates the Registrar's termly report naming each student and their adjustments.
questions.explanation: The Registrar keeps a confidential record of disabled students, and agreed adjustments reach departments such as the Library through instructions in the signed Support Agreement Plan.
questions.source_excerpt: The signed agreement may include instructions to the Programme Leader, Academic Administration Office and Library, depending on the agreed adjustments; ... The Registrar is responsible for maintaining a confidential record of disabled students

questions.question: Student A declared a disability on their application but has no formal diagnosis. Student B declared nothing, but a tutor has noticed signs of a learning difficulty. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how does the route to assessment differ?
options: A: the College will refer them to an outside centre; B: the tutor refers them to the Registrar, who can refer B if B wishes.
A: the tutor refers them to the Registrar; B: the College will refer them to an outside centre, whether or not B wishes.
A and B: both are referred for assessment by Student Finance England as part of an application for DSA funding.
A and B: neither can be assessed until the Registrar has completed a Support Agreement Plan with each student.
questions.explanation: A declared but undiagnosed student is referred by the College to an outside centre, whereas staff refer a student showing signs of a learning difficulty to the Registrar, who can refer them for assessment if the student wishes.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student has declared a disability, but has not been formally diagnosed, then the College will refer the student to an outside centre for an assessment. ... they should refer the student to the Registrar. If the student wishes to, the Registrar can refer the student for an official assessment.

questions.question: Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, which statement correctly distinguishes the Programme Manager's role from the Programme Leader's role in relation to a student's Support Agreement Plan?
options: The Programme Leader is consulted on implementing it; the Programme Manager may receive instructions in the signed plan.
The Programme Manager signs the plan with the student; the Programme Leader implements it once it has been signed.
The Programme Manager is consulted on implementing it; the Programme Leader may receive instructions in the signed plan.
The Programme Manager completes the plan with the student; the Programme Leader keeps the confidential record of it.
questions.explanation: The Registrar implements the plan in consultation with the Head of Program and Monitoring and the Programme Manager, and the signed agreement may include instructions to the Programme Leader.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar has responsibility for the implementation of the student Support Agreement Plan (SAP) in consultation with the Head of Program and Monitoring (HoPAM) and Programme Manager (PM); ... The signed agreement may include instructions to the Programme Leader, Academic Administration Office and Library, depending on the agreed adjustments;

questions.question: Two students receiving Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA) ask about printing costs. One needs extra printing because of their disability; the other's is ordinary course printing unrelated to any disability. What does the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy indicate?
options: DSA can cover both, as the policy lists photocopying and printer cartridges among the costs that it pays for.
DSA can cover neither, as it pays only for specialist equipment and non-medical helpers, not for consumables.
DSA can cover the first, as it pays for extra costs incurred as a direct result of the student's disability.
DSA can cover both, provided the Registrar records the printing costs in each student's Support Agreement Plan.
questions.explanation: The policy says DSA pays for extra costs students incur as a direct result of their disability, including related expenses such as photocopying and printer cartridges, which fits only the first student.
questions.source_excerpt: DSA pays for extra costs that students may incur in attending their programme as a direct result of their disability, including but not limited to specialist equipment, non-medical helpers, and other related expenses, i.e., photocopying and printer cartridges.

questions.question: A module leader designing new teaching materials plans to make them accessible only when a student requests an individual adjustment. How does this fit the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy?
options: It fits, as accessibility is provided solely through the individual adjustments recorded in each Support Agreement Plan.
It fits, as teaching materials only need to be made accessible once Disabled Students' Allowances have been awarded.
It falls short, as the policy requires the Registrar to approve all new teaching materials before they are used.
It falls short, as the policy expects inclusive design wherever possible, with individual adjustments where necessary.
questions.explanation: The policy offers equally accessible learning by inclusive design wherever possible and by reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary, so relying only on individual requests falls short.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are offered learning opportunities that are equally accessible to them, by means of inclusive design wherever possible and by means of reasonable individual adjustments wherever necessary;

questions.question: Which of these sets consists only of items that the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy expressly describes as confidential?
options: The Registrar's one-to-one session, the Support Agreement Plan and the Registrar's record of disabled students.
The Registrar's one-to-one session, the Support Agreement Plan and the termly report to the Academic Board.
The Support Agreement Plan, the induction briefing on Special Needs support and students' disability evidence.
The application form declaration, the termly Academic Board report and the Registrar's record of disabled students.
questions.explanation: The policy describes the Registrar's one-to-one session, the Support Agreement Plan and the Registrar's record of disabled students as confidential; the termly report, induction briefing and application declaration are not so described.
questions.source_excerpt: invited to meet the Registrar for a confidential one-to-one session ... the College will use a confidential Support Agreement Plan ... The Registrar is responsible for maintaining a confidential record of disabled students

questions.question: A student says an adjustment that their signed Support Agreement Plan instructs the Academic Administration Office to provide is not happening. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, who holds responsibility for the plan's implementation?
options: The Academic Administration Office, as the instruction in the signed plan makes that office responsible for implementing it.
The Head of Program and Monitoring, as the policy gives that role responsibility for monitoring the adjustments made.
The Academic Board, as it receives the Registrar's termly report on issues with the reasonable adjustments provided.
The Registrar, who is responsible for implementing the plan and for monitoring the adjustments that the College makes.
questions.explanation: The Registrar is responsible for implementing the Support Agreement Plan, consulting the Head of Program and Monitoring and the Programme Manager, and for monitoring the adjustments made; departments named in the plan receive instructions but are not given that responsibility.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar has responsibility for the implementation of the student Support Agreement Plan (SAP) in consultation with the Head of Program and Monitoring (HoPAM) and Programme Manager (PM); ... The Registrar is responsible for maintaining a confidential record of disabled students and monitoring the adjustments the College makes for them;

questions.question: Which set lists only roles that the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy gives to the Registrar?
options: Promoting Special Needs support at induction, keeping a confidential record of disabled students, and referring students for official assessment if they wish
Meeting applicants before enrolment, processing Disabled Students' Allowances applications, and referring students for official assessment if they wish
Meeting applicants before enrolment, keeping a confidential record of disabled students, and reporting termly to the Academic Board
Promoting Special Needs support at induction, processing Disabled Students' Allowances applications, and reporting termly to the Academic Board
questions.explanation: The Registrar meets applicants before enrolment, keeps a confidential record of disabled students and reports termly to the Academic Board. Promoting support at induction is the Student Welfare Officer's role, and DSA applications are processed by Student Finance England.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants for programmes offered by LCC can arrange to meet with the Registrar prior to enrolment. ... The Registrar is responsible for maintaining a confidential record of disabled students ... The Registrar is responsible for providing the Academic Board with a termly report

questions.question: A student applying for adjustments submits a GP letter confirming they are registered with the practice and fit to study, but it says nothing about their disability. Under the Reasonable Adjustments and Special Needs Policy, how should the letter be treated?
options: As sufficient, as the policy names a letter from a GP as acceptable evidence regardless of what the letter says.
As sufficient, once the Registrar has countersigned it during the student's confidential one-to-one session.
As insufficient, as the policy accepts only a recent DSA Needs Assessment Report as evidence of a disability.
As insufficient, as the evidence must specifically relate to the disability and set out matters such as its nature.
questions.explanation: A GP letter is only an example of acceptable evidence: the policy requires evidence that specifically relates to the student's disability, and the letter should set out matters such as the nature of the disability.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are required to provide evidence that specifically relates to their disability. For example, a letter from a GP or specialist or a recent Needs Assessment Report for a Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA). The letter/report should contain the following: ... The nature of the disability;

questions.question: A student tells you about sexual misconduct they experienced at the College several months ago. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, what is the immediate priority upon this disclosure?
options: Establishing whether the disclosure is too old to be considered
Contacting the alleged perpetrator to hear their side first
Collecting written evidence before any support can be offered
The safety and welfare of the student making the disclosure
questions.explanation: The policy states that on disclosure of any sexual misconduct, whether current or historic, the immediate priority is the safety and welfare of the disclosing party.
questions.source_excerpt: The College recognises that the immediate priority upon disclosure of any experience of sexual misconduct, whether current or historic, is the safety and welfare of the disclosing party;

questions.question: You witness an incident of sexual harassment on an LCC campus but were not directly affected. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, which dedicated channel can you use to notify the College?
options: None, as witnesses are not permitted to report incidents
A confidential letter addressed to the College's Board of Directors
A dedicated comments section in the end-of-module survey
The College's dedicated email address, harassment@lcc.ac.uk
questions.explanation: The policy provides the College's dedicated email address, harassment@lcc.ac.uk, for students, staff and external parties, and this expressly includes witnesses to an incident on an LCC campus.
questions.source_excerpt: Students, staff and external parties can also notify the Colllege of incidents through a dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk. This includes being a witness to an incident on an LCC campus, or involving a member of the LCC community.

questions.question: A colleague tells you they have been sexually harassed by another staff member and wants to make a complaint. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, besides the Incident Report Form, who can staff make a complaint to?
options: The Registry team or the Student Engagement department
The HR Manager or HR Officer, who will advise on how to proceed
Any member of the Academic Board, who will decide the outcome
The Quality Assurance Department, who will log and close the case
questions.explanation: The policy states that staff and external stakeholders may additionally make a complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer, who will advise on how to proceed, following the process in the Staff Handbook.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff and external stakeholders may additionally make a complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer, who will advise on how to proceed. All reporting should be conducted according to the process within the Staff Handbook.

questions.question: According to the Sexual Harassment Policy, who is responsible for receiving and sensitively handling harassment or sexual misconduct disclosures from students?
options: The student's personal tutor or programme leader, whichever of them they approach first
Appropriately trained members of the Registry team and Student Engagement department
The Quality Assurance Department, which logs and investigates each student disclosure
The HR Officer, who manages and operationalises disclosures made by students
questions.explanation: The Responsibilities section assigns the receiving and sensitive handling of student disclosures to appropriately trained members of the Registry team and Student Engagement department; the HR Officer's role is limited to staff incidents.
questions.source_excerpt: The appropriately trained members of the Registry team and Student Engagement department are responsible for receiving and sensitively handling any harassment or sexual misconduct disclosure from students;

questions.question: A colleague regularly talks in detail about their own sex life in front of others at work. How does the Sexual Harassment Policy treat this behaviour?
options: It is not covered, as it does not involve comments about another person
It is treated as harassment when students are present, but not among colleagues
It is a conduct matter for line managers rather than a form of sexual harassment
It is listed in the policy as a behaviour that can constitute sexual harassment
questions.explanation: The policy's list of behaviours that can constitute sexual harassment expressly includes discussing your own sex life.
questions.source_excerpt: Sexual harassment can be defined from a wide range of behaviours, including but not limited to: ... Discussing your own sex life

questions.question: According to LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy and Protocol, how will any sexual harassment, including misconduct and gender-based violence, that occurs at the College be handled?
options: On a case-by-case basis, with minor incidents handled locally by managers
Through a verbal then written warning before any formal sanction is applied
With a zero-tolerance approach, whatever form the sexual harassment takes
After the police have secured a criminal conviction against the individual
questions.explanation: The policy's introduction states that the College is committed to handling any form of sexual harassment, including misconduct and gender-based violence, with a zero-tolerance approach.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is committed to ensuring that any form of sexual harassment, including misconduct and gender-based violence, which may occur at the College is handled with a zero-tolerance approach.

questions.question: The Sexual Harassment Policy adopts the OfS Condition E6 definition of sexual misconduct. Which of the following matches that definition?
options: Unwanted conduct of a sexual nature, including but not limited to sexual harassment, sexual assault and rape
Conduct of a sexual nature that has resulted in a criminal conviction under the Sexual Offences Act 2003
Repeated conduct of a sexual nature that continues after the recipient has clearly and formally asked for it to stop
Physical contact of a sexual nature, with verbal, written and online behaviour falling outside the definition
questions.explanation: The policy cites OfS Condition E6, which defines sexual misconduct as unwanted conduct of a sexual nature including, but not limited to, sexual harassment, sexual assault and rape.
questions.source_excerpt: sexual misconduct is defined as an unwanted conduct of a sexual nature and includes, but is not limited to: ... Sexual harassment; ... Sexual assault; and ... Rape.

questions.question: A student is alleged to have committed sexual misconduct against another student. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, how will the allegation be investigated?
options: Under the Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, as set out in the Staff Handbook
By referral to the police, with the College suspending any internal action until they conclude
Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, which can lead to expulsion
Through informal mediation between the two students, with sanctions capped at a written warning
questions.explanation: The policy states that any sexual misconduct by students will be investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, and sanctions can include expulsion.
questions.source_excerpt: Any sexual misconduct will be investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure and sanctions applied under this procedure can include expulsion from the College.

questions.question: According to the Reporting Channel section of the Sexual Harassment Policy, how may students or staff who have been affected make a complaint?
options: Via the Incident Report Form on the dedicated College support webpage
By completing a paper complaint form available from the campus reception desk
By raising it at the next scheduled staff or student representative meeting
By writing to the Academic Board and asking it to open a formal investigation
questions.explanation: The policy states that affected students or staff may make a complaint via the Incident Report Form, found on the dedicated College harassment and sexual misconduct support webpage.
questions.source_excerpt: Students or staff who have been affected by may make a complaint via the Incident Report Form, which can be found on the dedicated College webpage on https://lcc.ac.uk/harassment-and-sexual-misconduct-support/

questions.question: A student's harassment concern has not been resolved at the informal stage. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, what should the student be encouraged to do?
options: Wait for the Board of Directors to review the case and issue a decision at its next scheduled meeting
Raise the matter with the HR Officer as a formal grievance, following the procedures set out in the Staff Handbook
Make a formal complaint under the College Complaints Policy or Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
Accept the informal outcome, as the Student Code of Conduct provides no further complaint stage for students
questions.explanation: The Formal Complaints section says students whose case is not resolved informally are encouraged to make a formal complaint under the College Complaints Policy or the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: If any case is not resolved in the informal stage, students are encouraged to make a formal complaint in accordance with the College Complaints Policy or Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.

questions.question: According to the Sexual Harassment Policy, which policy must all staff adhere to as part of their expected behaviour?
options: The Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, published on the Student Portal
The Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, in the Staff Handbook
The College Complaints Policy and Procedure, available on the College website
The Equality and Diversity Charter for staff, displayed on each College campus
questions.explanation: Under Expected Behaviour of Staff, all staff must adhere to the College's Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, which is included in the Staff Handbook; the Student Code of Conduct applies to students.
questions.source_excerpt: All staff must adhere to the College's Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, which is included in the Staff Handbook.

questions.question: Under the Responsibilities section of the Sexual Harassment Policy, what are staff and students required to disclose to the College?
options: Criminal convictions acquired during their employment or study at the College
Any personal or romantic relationship with another member of the College community
Any previous complaint or allegation made against them at another institution
Any social media accounts they use to contact students or colleagues at the College
questions.explanation: The policy requires staff and students to disclose criminal convictions acquired during their employment or study at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff and students are required to disclose criminal convictions acquired during employment or study at the College;

questions.question: According to the College Statement in the Sexual Harassment Policy, who can experience sexual misconduct and violence?
options: Mainly students under 18 and adults at risk, whom the College treats as a priority
Students and staff on campus, as off-campus incidents fall under other procedures
Any individual, regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, age, faith or other status
People in a working or study relationship where one party holds authority over the other
questions.explanation: The College Statement says sexual misconduct and violence can be experienced by any individual, regardless of characteristics such as sex, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability or faith.
questions.source_excerpt: Regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, relationship status, age, disability, faith, ethnicity, nationality and/or economic status, sexual misconduct and violence can be experienced by any individual.

questions.question: The College Statement in the Sexual Harassment Policy says any reporting of sexual misconduct will be taken seriously. How else does it say such reporting will be treated?
options: It will be treated with dignity and respect
It will be kept anonymous for the person reporting
It will take priority over all other College complaints
It will receive a written outcome within ten working days
questions.explanation: The College Statement commits the College to ensuring that any reporting of sexual misconduct is taken seriously and treated with dignity and respect.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will ensure that any reporting of sexual misconduct is taken seriously and treated with dignity and respect;

questions.question: According to the College Statement in the Sexual Harassment Policy, who is expected to take responsibility for building and maintaining an inclusive, equal, positive and safe cultural environment for all?
options: Senior managers and heads of department, on behalf of their teams
The HR team and the Student Engagement department
Staff who hold designated wellbeing or safeguarding roles
All members of the College, whatever their role
questions.explanation: The College Statement says the College expects all its members to take responsibility for building and maintaining an inclusive, equal, positive and safe cultural environment.
questions.source_excerpt: The College expects that all its members will take responsibility for building and maintaining an inclusive, equal, positive and safe cultural environment for all.

questions.question: What does the Sexual Harassment Policy state about sexual harassment under the Equality Act 2010?
options: Only sexual harassment that is repeated is unlawful
Any form of sexual harassment is unlawful
It is unlawful only where it involves physical contact
It is unlawful only between an employer and an employee
questions.explanation: The Definitions section states that under the Equality Act 2010 any form of sexual harassment is unlawful.
questions.source_excerpt: Under the Equality Act 2010, any form of sexual harassment is unlawful.

questions.question: The Sexual Harassment Policy lists behaviours that can constitute sexual harassment. How does the policy describe the scope of this list?
options: An exhaustive list, with any conduct not listed handled under other policies
The most serious behaviours only, each of which leads to automatic dismissal or expulsion
A wide range of behaviours, including but not limited to those it lists
Behaviours that count only when they take place on College premises
questions.explanation: The policy says sexual harassment can be defined from a wide range of behaviours, including but not limited to those listed, so the list is not exhaustive.
questions.source_excerpt: Sexual harassment can be defined from a wide range of behaviours, including but not limited to:

questions.question: Does the Sexual Harassment Policy's list of behaviours that can constitute sexual harassment include conduct online or by message?
options: Yes, including sexual posts or contact on social media and explicit emails or texts
No, as online conduct is dealt with under the College's IT Acceptable Use Policy
Only where the messages include images, as written messages alone are not listed
Only where the online contact continues after the recipient has asked for it to stop
questions.explanation: The list expressly includes making inappropriate sexual posts or contact on social media and sending sexually explicit emails or text messages, with no restriction to College systems.
questions.source_excerpt: Making inappropriate sexual posts or contact on social media ... Sending sexually explicit emails or text messages

questions.question: Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, besides actively promoting a culture of zero tolerance towards sexual misconduct, what does the College recognise it must ensure?
options: That every allegation is referred to the police before any College action is taken
That all staff complete annual accredited training on handling disclosures
That anyone accused of sexual misconduct is suspended until the case concludes
That arrangements are in place to support all staff and students who experience it
questions.explanation: The Policy section says the College must actively promote a zero-tolerance culture and ensure there are arrangements in place to support all staff and students who experience sexual misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: The College recognises that it must actively promote a culture of zero tolerance with regard to any form of sexual misconduct and ensure that there are arrangements in place to support all staff and students who experience it;

questions.question: What does the Sexual Harassment Policy commit the College to providing to its stakeholders to address sexual misconduct?
options: An annual published report of all cases and their outcomes
Clear and transparent information, with clear signposting
A named independent advocate for every person who reports
Free specialist legal advice for anyone who makes a complaint
questions.explanation: The Policy section states that the College will provide clear and transparent information to its stakeholders to address sexual misconduct, with clear signposting.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will provide clearand transparent information to its stakeholders to address sexual misconduct with clear signposting;

questions.question: According to the Policy section of the Sexual Harassment Policy, what will the College do regarding any individual who has committed sexual misconduct?
options: Hold them accountable, which may include major disciplinary action such as expulsion
Refer them to the police and limit any College action to a formal written warning
Offer mediation with the affected person before any sanction is considered
Transfer them to another campus or team while keeping the matter confidential
questions.explanation: The policy states the College will hold accountable any individual who has committed sexual misconduct, which may include major disciplinary action, including expulsion.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will hold accountable any individual who has committed sexual misconduct. This may include facing major disciplinary action, including expulsion.

questions.question: According to the Sexual Harassment Policy, the Student Code of Conduct sets out expected student behaviour towards which people?
options: Other students only, as conduct towards staff is covered by the Staff Handbook
Teaching staff and fellow students, but only while on College premises
Other students, staff, Principals, Directors, managers, contractors and visitors
Students and staff within the same programme, including placement supervisors
questions.explanation: The policy says the Student Code of Conduct represents expected student behaviour towards other students, members of staff, Principals, Directors, managers, contractors and other visitors to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: This code represents the expected behaviour from students towards to other students, members of staff, Principals, Directors, managers, contractors, or other visitors to the College;

questions.question: According to the Responsibilities section of the Sexual Harassment Policy, who is responsible for oversight of any matters arising under the policy?
options: The Academic Board of the College
The College's Board of Directors
The Head of Student Engagement
The HR Manager and HR Officer
questions.explanation: The Responsibilities section assigns oversight of any matters arising under the Sexual Harassment Policy and Protocol to the Board of Directors.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board of Directors is responsible for oversight of any matters arising under the Sexual Harassment Policy and Protocol;

questions.question: Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, who can notify the College of incidents through the dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk?
options: Staff only; students use the Incident Report Form
Students only; staff report to the HR Officer
Students and staff, but not external parties
Students, staff and external parties
questions.explanation: The Reporting Channel section states that students, staff and external parties can all notify the College of incidents through harassment@lcc.ac.uk.
questions.source_excerpt: Students, staff and external parties can also notify the Colllege of incidents through a dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk.

questions.question: According to the Sexual Harassment Policy, where are the College Complaints Policy and the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure made available?
options: On the College website and the Student Portal
In the Staff Handbook and on the staff intranet
Only on request from the Registry team or Student Engagement
On noticeboards in each campus reception area
questions.explanation: The Formal Complaints section states that these procedures are available on the website and Student Portal.
questions.source_excerpt: students are encouraged to make a formal complaint in accordance with the College Complaints Policy or Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure. These procedures are available on the website and Student Portal.

questions.question: Under the Formal Complaints section of the Sexual Harassment Policy, to whom should a member of staff make a formal complaint?
options: The Board of Directors, via the Quality Assurance Department
The HR Officer, following the procedures in the Staff Handbook
The Registry team, under the College Complaints Policy
Their line manager, who decides whether to escalate it
questions.explanation: The Formal Complaints section states that staff should make a formal complaint to the HR Officer, with procedures outlined in the Staff Handbook.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff should make a formal complaint to the HR Officer. Procedures are outlined in the Staff Handbook.

questions.question: A line manager tells a new colleague that LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy is a student policy that does not concern staff. According to the policy's Introduction, whose harassment-free experience does the College recognise as significant?
options: Students' study experience, as staff conduct falls outside this policy
Students' study experience and that of external visitors to campus
The work and study experience of both College staff and students
Students and the academic staff who directly teach or supervise them
questions.explanation: The Introduction states that the College recognises the significance of a harassment-free work and study experience for the College staff and students, so the policy concerns staff as well as students.
questions.source_excerpt: London Churchill College (LCC) recognises the significance of a harassment-free work and study experience for the College staff and students.

questions.question: A student hesitates to report sexual misconduct because the person responsible is their partner, and fears the College will treat it as a private matter. What does the College Statement in the Sexual Harassment Policy say?
options: Incidents between partners are private and are referred to external relationship services
Incidents between partners are considered only where both are enrolled on the same course
A report is considered only if the relationship has ended before the report is made
Anyone can experience it regardless of relationship status, and reports are taken seriously
questions.explanation: The College Statement says sexual misconduct can be experienced by any individual regardless of characteristics including relationship status, and that any reporting will be taken seriously and treated with dignity and respect.
questions.source_excerpt: Regardless of sex, gender, sexual orientation, relationship status, age, disability, faith, ethnicity, nationality and/or economic status, sexual misconduct and violence can be experienced by any individual. The College will ensure that any reporting of sexual misconduct is taken seriously and treated with dignity and respect;

questions.question: A manager argues that an incident reported to them cannot be sexual misconduct because it is not sexual harassment, sexual assault or rape. Under the OfS E6 definition used in the Sexual Harassment Policy, is the manager right?
options: Yes; the definition is limited to those three named forms of unwanted sexual conduct
No; it covers unwanted conduct of a sexual nature and is not limited to those three
Yes, unless the incident has also been reported to the police as a suspected offence
No, but only where the conduct took place on an LCC campus during teaching hours
questions.explanation: The OfS E6 definition in the policy describes sexual misconduct as unwanted conduct of a sexual nature that includes, but is not limited to, sexual harassment, sexual assault and rape.
questions.source_excerpt: defined as an unwanted conduct of a sexual nature and includes, but is not limited to: ... Sexual harassment; ... Sexual assault; and ... Rape.

questions.question: A student tells you another student has been stalking them. A colleague says stalking is a police matter that falls outside the Sexual Harassment Policy. How does the policy's list of sexual harassment behaviours treat stalking?
options: It excludes stalking, which is dealt with only by the police under criminal law
It covers stalking only where a member of staff, not a student, is responsible
It lists criminal behaviour, including stalking, among its harassing behaviours
It covers stalking only once a criminal conviction has been obtained in court
questions.explanation: The list of behaviours that can constitute sexual harassment expressly includes criminal behaviour such as sexual assault, stalking, grooming and indecent exposure, so stalking is within the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Sexual harassment can be defined from a wide range of behaviours, including but not limited to: ... Criminal behaviour, including sexual assault, stalking, grooming, indecent exposure and sending offensive communications

questions.question: The Sexual Harassment Policy notes that any form of sexual harassment is unlawful under the Equality Act 2010. What further position does the College maintain about such an act?
options: That it must be reported to the police before any College action
That it is unlawful only when repeated after a warning has been given
That it becomes a College matter only once a formal complaint is made
That it violates the dignity of the affected individual
questions.explanation: The Definitions section links the Equality Act 2010 position with the College's own view that an act of sexual harassment violates the dignity of the affected individual.
questions.source_excerpt: Under the Equality Act 2010, any form of sexual harassment is unlawful. It defines an individual who engages in an inappropriate conduct of sexual nature with another individual. The College maintains such an act violates the dignity of the affected individual;

questions.question: A senior manager at LCC is found to have committed sexual misconduct. A colleague assumes the Sexual Harassment Policy's accountability commitment applies only to students, since it mentions expulsion. What does the policy say?
options: The College will hold accountable any individual who has committed sexual misconduct
Accountability applies to students only, with staff dealt with through annual appraisal
Senior managers are referred to the Board of Directors for handling outside this policy
Staff are held accountable only where a criminal conviction has already been obtained
questions.explanation: The Policy section says the College will hold accountable any individual who has committed sexual misconduct, which may include major disciplinary action; the commitment is not limited to students.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will hold accountable any individual who has committed sexual misconduct. This may include facing major disciplinary action, including expulsion.

questions.question: A member of staff who experienced sexual misconduct from a student asks whether the College's support arrangements extend to staff. What does the Policy section of the Sexual Harassment Policy say?
options: Support arrangements are for students, and staff are referred to an external helpline
Arrangements must be in place to support all staff and students who experience it
Staff receive support only after making a formal complaint to the HR Officer
Staff receive support only once the student is found responsible under the Code
questions.explanation: The Policy section says the College must ensure there are arrangements in place to support all staff and students who experience sexual misconduct, with no precondition of a formal complaint or finding.
questions.source_excerpt: The College recognises that it must actively promote a culture of zero tolerance with regard to any form of sexual misconduct and ensure that there are arrangements in place to support all staff and students who experience it;

questions.question: A student makes sexual comments to a contractor carrying out maintenance on campus. According to the Sexual Harassment Policy, which code sets out the behaviour expected of the student towards the contractor?
options: The contractor's own employer's code, as contractors are outside the College community
The Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, which also covers contractors
None, as the Student Code covers conduct towards students and teaching staff only
The Student Code of Conduct, which covers behaviour towards contractors and visitors
questions.explanation: The policy says the Student Code of Conduct represents the expected behaviour of students towards other students, staff, Principals, Directors, managers, contractors and other visitors to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: The College requires all students to follow the Student Code of Conduct. This code represents the expected behaviour from students towards to other students, members of staff, Principals, Directors, managers, contractors, or other visitors to the College;

questions.question: A member of staff is accused of making sexual comments to a student. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, which document sets the standard of behaviour that the member of staff must adhere to?
options: The Student Code of Conduct, because the person affected is a student
The College Complaints Policy, once the student has made a complaint
The Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, in the Staff Handbook
The Academic Board's terms of reference, which govern teaching staff conduct
questions.explanation: Under Expected Behaviour of Staff, all staff must adhere to the Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff in the Staff Handbook; the Student Code of Conduct sets expected behaviour for students, not staff.
questions.source_excerpt: All staff must adhere to the College's Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, which is included in the Staff Handbook.

questions.question: A student at LCC receives a criminal conviction partway through their course, for an offence unrelated to sexual misconduct. What does the Responsibilities section of the Sexual Harassment Policy require?
options: They must disclose it, as the duty covers criminal convictions acquired during study
No disclosure is needed, as the duty applies only to convictions for sexual offences
No disclosure is needed, as the duty applies to staff rather than to enrolled students
Disclosure is needed only if the College asks about convictions at re-enrolment
questions.explanation: The Responsibilities section requires staff and students to disclose criminal convictions acquired during employment or study at the College, without limiting this to sexual offences.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff and students are required to disclose criminal convictions acquired during employment or study at the College;

questions.question: A member of professional services staff discloses that a colleague has sexually harassed them. Under the Responsibilities section of the Sexual Harassment Policy, who is responsible for managing and operationalising this disclosure?
options: The Board of Directors, which decides all staff cases directly
The HR Officer, who holds responsibility for staff incidents
Trained members of the Registry team and Student Engagement
Their line manager, who then decides whether to inform HR
questions.explanation: The Responsibilities section states that for staff incidents the responsibility lies with the HR Officer to manage and operationalise any disclosure; Registry and Student Engagement handle student disclosures.
questions.source_excerpt: For staff incidents the responsibility lies with the HR Officer to manage and operationalise any disclosure.

questions.question: A visiting external stakeholder is sexually harassed during a meeting at LCC. Under the Reporting Channel section of the Sexual Harassment Policy, which routes are expressly open to them?
options: A complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer, or an email to harassment@lcc.ac.uk
A formal complaint under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
A written complaint to the Board of Directors via the Quality Assurance Department
The Incident Report Form only, as the email address is for students and staff
questions.explanation: The Reporting Channel section lets external stakeholders complain to the HR Manager or HR Officer, and lets external parties notify the College through harassment@lcc.ac.uk.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff and external stakeholders may additionally make a complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer, who will advise on how to proceed. ... Students, staff and external parties can also notify the Colllege of incidents through a dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk.

questions.question: A member of staff witnesses one LCC student sexually harassing another at an off-campus social event. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, can the staff member notify the College through harassment@lcc.ac.uk?
options: No, as witnesses may use the email only for incidents on an LCC campus
No, as off-campus incidents must go through the Incident Report Form
Yes, but only once the harassed student has given written consent
Yes, as the email covers incidents involving members of the LCC community
questions.explanation: The dedicated email address covers being a witness to an incident on an LCC campus or one involving a member of the LCC community, so an off-campus incident between LCC students can be reported.
questions.source_excerpt: Students, staff and external parties can also notify the Colllege of incidents through a dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk. This includes being a witness to an incident on an LCC campus, or involving a member of the LCC community.

questions.question: A student who has been sexually harassed does not want to use the Incident Report Form. Under the Reporting Channel section of the Sexual Harassment Policy, which other route is expressly available to students?
options: Complaining to the HR Manager, who will advise the student on how to proceed
Notifying the College through the dedicated address harassment@lcc.ac.uk
Writing to the Board of Directors, which investigates all student reports
Posting it anonymously through the Student Portal's module feedback page
questions.explanation: Besides the Incident Report Form, students can notify the College through harassment@lcc.ac.uk; the route to the HR Manager or HR Officer is given to staff and external stakeholders.
questions.source_excerpt: Students or staff who have been affected by may make a complaint via the Incident Report Form ... Students, staff and external parties can also notify the Colllege of incidents through a dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk.

questions.question: A member of staff wants to report sexual harassment to HR and may later need to make a formal complaint. According to the Sexual Harassment Policy, where are the processes for both of these set out?
options: On the Student Portal, alongside the College Complaints Policy
On the harassment and sexual misconduct support webpage alone
In the Staff Handbook, for reporting and formal complaints alike
In the Board of Directors' terms of reference for this policy
questions.explanation: The policy says all staff reporting should follow the process in the Staff Handbook, and that the procedures for a staff formal complaint to the HR Officer are also outlined in the Staff Handbook.
questions.source_excerpt: All reporting should be conducted according to the process within the Staff Handbook. ... Staff should make a formal complaint to the HR Officer. Procedures are outlined in the Staff Handbook.

questions.question: A manager decides to overlook a colleague's first jokes with sexual innuendo, saying LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy lets minor first incidents pass. What does the policy say?
options: Jokes are not on the list of behaviours, so they fall outside the policy unless they are repeated
Such jokes are a listed behaviour, and any form of sexual harassment is met with zero tolerance
Zero tolerance applies only to criminal behaviour, such as sexual assault or stalking
A first incident may be overlooked where the colleague apologises and does not repeat it
questions.explanation: The policy lists inappropriate comments or jokes with sexual innuendos as sexual harassment, and the Introduction commits the College to handling any form of sexual harassment with a zero-tolerance approach.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is committed to ensuring that any form of sexual harassment, including misconduct and gender-based violence, which may occur at the College is handled with a zero-tolerance approach. ... Making inappropriate comments or jokes with sexual innuendos

questions.question: A head of department says a safe culture at LCC is the job of HR and Student Engagement, delivered through one annual awareness week. How does the College Statement in the Sexual Harassment Policy describe this?
options: HR and Student Engagement hold sole responsibility, supported by an annual awareness campaign
Line managers hold responsibility for their own teams, with tutors responsible for students
Staff in designated safeguarding roles hold responsibility, with others encouraged to assist
It is promoted through an embedded approach, with all members expected to take responsibility
questions.explanation: The College Statement commits the College to an inclusive, positive and safe cultural environment through an embedded approach, and expects all its members to take responsibility for building and maintaining it.
questions.source_excerpt: The College is committed to promoting and ensuring, through an embedded approach, an inclusive, positive and safe cultural environment for all members of its community; ... The College expects that all its members will take responsibility for building and maintaining an inclusive, equal, positive and safe cultural environment for all.

questions.question: A colleague claims LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy deals only with verbal and online harassment, leaving gender-based violence, sexual assault and rape to other procedures. Which statement shows why this is wrong?
options: Zero tolerance extends to gender-based violence, and sexual misconduct includes sexual assault and rape
