It covers gender-based violence on campus, and sexual assault or rape once a conviction is obtained
It covers sexual assault and rape between students only, leaving staff incidents to the police
It covers gender-based violence only where it forms part of a pattern of predatory behaviour
questions.explanation: The Introduction applies the zero-tolerance approach to any form of sexual harassment including misconduct and gender-based violence, and the definition of sexual misconduct used in the policy includes sexual assault and rape.
questions.source_excerpt: any form of sexual harassment, including misconduct and gender-based violence, which may occur at the College is handled with a zero-tolerance approach. ... defined as an unwanted conduct of a sexual nature and includes, but is not limited to: ... Sexual assault; and ... Rape.

questions.question: A member of professional services staff is upset by sexually explicit posters a colleague has put up in their shared office, although the posters are not aimed at anyone. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, which statement is correct?
options: Posters not aimed at a particular person are not harassment, so it is a workplace matter
It is a listed behaviour, but only students, not staff, may use the Incident Report Form
Such posters are a listed behaviour; the colleague may use the Incident Report Form
It counts as harassment only if the posters depict the colleague who is upset by them
questions.explanation: Displaying graphic pictures, posters or photos of a sexual nature is on the policy's list of harassment behaviours with no requirement that they target anyone, and affected staff may make a complaint via the Incident Report Form.
questions.source_excerpt: Displaying graphic pictures, posters or photos of a sexual nature ... Students or staff who have been affected by may make a complaint via the Incident Report Form

questions.question: A student posts sexual comments on social media about an employer's representative who visited LCC to give a careers talk. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, how is the student's conduct dealt with?
options: It falls outside the policy, as online comments about people outside the College are not covered
It is passed to the HR Officer, who manages incidents where the person affected is not a student
It is dealt with under the Personal Harassment Policy, which governs conduct towards visitors
It is a listed behaviour, investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
questions.explanation: Inappropriate sexual posts on social media are a listed harassment behaviour; the Student Code of Conduct covers students' behaviour towards visitors, and student sexual misconduct is investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Making inappropriate sexual posts or contact on social media ... This code represents the expected behaviour from students towards to other students, members of staff, Principals, Directors, managers, contractors, or other visitors to the College; ... Any sexual misconduct will be investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure

questions.question: A student alleges sexual harassment by a classmate, and the matter is not resolved at the informal stage. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, which pairing of procedures is correct?
options: Classmate investigated under the College Complaints Policy; complainant complains to the HR Officer
Classmate investigated under the Personal Harassment Policy; complainant uses the Complaints Policy only
Classmate investigated under the Student Code procedure; complainant may use it or the Complaints Policy
Classmate investigated under the Student Code procedure; complainant complains to the Board of Directors
questions.explanation: Student sexual misconduct is investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, while a student whose case is not resolved informally is encouraged to complain formally under the College Complaints Policy or that same procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Any sexual misconduct will be investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure ... If any case is not resolved in the informal stage, students are encouraged to make a formal complaint in accordance with the College Complaints Policy or Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.

questions.question: The Responsibilities section of LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy sets out a duty to disclose criminal convictions. Which of these convictions falls within that duty?
options: One a student received at school, before they applied to study at LCC
One a member of staff receives during their second year of working at LCC
One a former employee receives two years after leaving the College
One a contractor's worker receives while carrying out repairs on campus
questions.explanation: The duty applies to staff and students, and to criminal convictions acquired during their employment or study at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff and students are required to disclose criminal convictions acquired during employment or study at the College;

questions.question: A student wants to disclose sexual harassment by another student. A colleague says the Board of Directors handles every case because it oversees the Sexual Harassment Policy. Under the policy's Responsibilities section, which is correct?
options: The Board of Directors handles it directly, and trained Registry staff then oversee the outcome
The HR Officer handles it, and the Board of Directors reviews the outcome as part of its oversight
The Academic Board handles it, and Student Engagement oversees any follow-up support offered
Trained Registry and Student Engagement staff handle it, and the Board of Directors has oversight
questions.explanation: Trained members of the Registry team and Student Engagement department receive and sensitively handle student disclosures, while the Board of Directors is responsible for oversight of matters arising under the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: The Board of Directors is responsible for oversight of any matters arising under the Sexual Harassment Policy and Protocol; ... The appropriately trained members of the Registry team and Student Engagement department are responsible for receiving and sensitively handling any harassment or sexual misconduct disclosure from students;

questions.question: A lecturer discloses that a student has been sending them sexually explicit text messages. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, which statement is correct?
options: The HR Officer manages the disclosure, and the student is investigated under the Student Code procedure
Registry and Student Engagement manage the disclosure, because the person accused is a student
The HR Officer manages the disclosure, and the student is investigated under the Personal Harassment Policy
The Board of Directors manages the disclosure, and the student is investigated under the Student Code procedure
questions.explanation: A lecturer's disclosure is a staff incident, which the HR Officer manages and operationalises; the student's sexual misconduct is investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Sending sexually explicit emails or text messages ... Any sexual misconduct will be investigated under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure ... For staff incidents the responsibility lies with the HR Officer to manage and operationalise any disclosure.

questions.question: A member of staff affected by sexual harassment asks which routes the Reporting Channel section of LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy makes available to them. Which answer is correct?
options: The Incident Report Form or harassment@lcc.ac.uk only, as HR handles formal complaints alone
A complaint to the HR Officer only, as the form and email address are provided for students
The Incident Report Form, a complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer, or harassment@lcc.ac.uk
A complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer only, with the form reserved for affected students
questions.explanation: Affected staff may use the Incident Report Form, may additionally complain to the HR Manager or HR Officer, and can also notify the College through harassment@lcc.ac.uk.
questions.source_excerpt: Students or staff who have been affected by may make a complaint via the Incident Report Form ... Staff and external stakeholders may additionally make a complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer ... Students, staff and external parties can also notify the Colllege of incidents through a dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk.

questions.question: A lecturer reported sexual harassment to the HR Manager, who advised them on how to proceed. The matter is unresolved and they now want to make a formal complaint. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, what should they do?
options: Make it to the HR Manager, as the person who received the original report
Make it to the HR Officer, following the Staff Handbook procedures
Make it under the College Complaints Policy, published on the College website
Make it to the Board of Directors, which has oversight of matters under the policy
questions.explanation: The HR Manager or HR Officer can receive and advise on a staff report, but the Formal Complaints section says staff should make a formal complaint to the HR Officer, following the Staff Handbook procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff and external stakeholders may additionally make a complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer, who will advise on how to proceed. ... Staff should make a formal complaint to the HR Officer. Procedures are outlined in the Staff Handbook.

questions.question: At an LCC open day, a student and a member of staff each make sexual comments to a visitor. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, which standard of behaviour applies to each of them?
options: Both are bound by the Student Code of Conduct, as it covers behaviour towards visitors
Both are bound by the Personal Harassment Policy, as the visitor is not a student
Student: the Personal Harassment Policy; staff member: the Student Code of Conduct
Student: the Student Code of Conduct; staff member: the Personal Harassment Policy
questions.explanation: The Student Code of Conduct sets students' expected behaviour, including towards visitors, while all staff must adhere to the Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff in the Staff Handbook.
questions.source_excerpt: This code represents the expected behaviour from students towards to other students, members of staff, Principals, Directors, managers, contractors, or other visitors to the College; ... All staff must adhere to the College's Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, which is included in the Staff Handbook.

questions.question: A student affected by sexual harassment asks where to find the Incident Report Form and, if the matter is not resolved informally, the formal complaint procedures. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, what should you tell them?
options: The form is on the dedicated College support webpage; the procedures are on the website and Student Portal
The form is on the Student Portal; the procedures are in the Staff Handbook, available from the HR Officer
The form is available from Registry on request; the procedures are displayed on campus noticeboards
The form and the procedures are both available only on request from the Student Engagement department
questions.explanation: The Incident Report Form is on the dedicated College harassment and sexual misconduct support webpage, and the College Complaints Policy and Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure are available on the website and Student Portal.
questions.source_excerpt: the Incident Report Form, which can be found on the dedicated College webpage on https://lcc.ac.uk/harassment-and-sexual-misconduct-support/ ... students are encouraged to make a formal complaint in accordance with the College Complaints Policy or Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure. These procedures are available on the website and Student Portal.

questions.question: A visiting speaker witnesses one guest sexually harassing another at an event on an LCC campus; neither guest is part of the LCC community. Under the Sexual Harassment Policy, can the speaker report it to harassment@lcc.ac.uk?
options: No; the email address covers only incidents that involve a member of the LCC community
No; external parties must instead complain to the HR Manager or HR Officer
Yes; external parties may use it, and it covers witnessing an incident on an LCC campus
Yes, but only once one of the guests involved has confirmed the incident in writing
questions.explanation: The dedicated email address is open to external parties and covers being a witness to an incident on an LCC campus, or one involving a member of the LCC community, so either condition is enough.
questions.source_excerpt: Students, staff and external parties can also notify the Colllege of incidents through a dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk. This includes being a witness to an incident on an LCC campus, or involving a member of the LCC community.

questions.question: A student says a lecturer's hug after a tutorial was unwelcome; the lecturer says it was friendly and the student did not object at the time. How does LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy treat this?
options: It is outside the policy, because the student did not object when the hug happened
It is covered only if the hug was repeated, as a single hug is not listed
It is covered only if the unwelcome hug came with sexual comments or gestures
Unwelcome hugging is listed as a behaviour that can constitute sexual harassment
questions.explanation: Unwelcome touching, hugging, massaging or kissing is on the policy's list of behaviours that can constitute sexual harassment, with no condition about objecting at the time, repetition or accompanying comments.
questions.source_excerpt: Sexual harassment can be defined from a wide range of behaviours, including but not limited to: ... Unwelcome touching, hugging, massaging or kissing

questions.question: Which of these is not a role that LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy gives to the HR Officer?
options: Managing and operationalising any disclosure arising from a staff incident
Receiving formal complaints from staff, under Staff Handbook procedures
Receiving and sensitively handling disclosures made by students
Advising staff and external stakeholders who complain on how to proceed
questions.explanation: The HR Officer manages staff disclosures, receives staff formal complaints and advises complainants, but student disclosures are received and handled by trained Registry and Student Engagement staff.
questions.source_excerpt: Registry team and Student Engagement department are responsible for receiving and sensitively handling any harassment or sexual misconduct disclosure from students; ... HR Officer to manage and operationalise any disclosure. ... HR Manager or HR Officer, who will advise on how to proceed. ... Staff should make a formal complaint to the HR Officer.

questions.question: A new member of staff is repeatedly asked intrusive questions about their sex life by a senior colleague, and wants to speak to HR before deciding on a formal complaint. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, which is correct?
options: It is listed, and the HR Manager or HR Officer will advise them on how to proceed
Questions alone are not a listed behaviour, so HR can offer them only informal advice
It is a listed behaviour, but staff must use the Incident Report Form before approaching HR
It is a listed behaviour, but HR can be approached only once a formal complaint is lodged
questions.explanation: Asking intrusive questions about a person's private or sex life is a listed harassment behaviour, and staff may additionally complain to the HR Manager or HR Officer, who will advise on how to proceed.
questions.source_excerpt: Asking intrusive questions about a person's private or sex life ... Staff and external stakeholders may additionally make a complaint to the HR Manager or HR Officer, who will advise on how to proceed.

questions.question: A member of staff tells HR that a colleague sexually assaulted them at a College event two years ago, and asks whether it is now too late to raise it. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, which statement is correct?
options: Historic disclosures go to trained Registry and Student Engagement staff, who assess them first
Only current incidents fall under the policy, so HR may signpost them to outside support only
The HR Officer manages it as a staff incident, and the discloser's safety and welfare comes first
Historic incidents are referred to the Board of Directors, which decides whether they can proceed
questions.explanation: The immediate priority on disclosure of sexual misconduct, whether current or historic, is the safety and welfare of the disclosing party, and responsibility for staff incidents lies with the HR Officer.
questions.source_excerpt: the immediate priority upon disclosure of any experience of sexual misconduct, whether current or historic, is the safety and welfare of the disclosing party ... For staff incidents the responsibility lies with the HR Officer to manage and operationalise any disclosure.

questions.question: On separate occasions during a careers fair on an LCC campus, a visiting exhibitor makes sexual comments to a student and to a member of staff, and each later discloses it. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, who is responsible for handling each disclosure?
options: Student: trained Registry and Student Engagement staff; staff member: the HR Officer
Student: the HR Officer; staff member: trained Registry and Student Engagement staff
Both: the HR Officer, as the person responsible is an external visitor, not a student
Both: the Board of Directors, as it has oversight of all matters arising under the policy
questions.explanation: Trained Registry and Student Engagement staff receive and handle disclosures from students, whoever is responsible, while the HR Officer manages disclosures from staff incidents; the Board of Directors has oversight only.
questions.source_excerpt: The appropriately trained members of the Registry team and Student Engagement department are responsible for receiving and sensitively handling any harassment or sexual misconduct disclosure from students; ... For staff incidents the responsibility lies with the HR Officer to manage and operationalise any disclosure.

questions.question: A lecturer offers a student a better grade in return for sexual favours, and the student wants to report it. Under LCC's Sexual Harassment Policy, which answer correctly gives the standard the lecturer must adhere to and the reporting routes expressly open to the student?
options: Lecturer: the Student Code of Conduct; student: the Incident Report Form or harassment@lcc.ac.uk
Lecturer: the Personal Harassment Policy; student: the Incident Report Form or harassment@lcc.ac.uk
Lecturer: the Personal Harassment Policy; student: a complaint to the HR Manager only, as staff are involved
Not covered; an offer of this kind counts as harassment only if it is made in writing or repeated
questions.explanation: Making promises in return for sexual favours is a listed behaviour; staff must adhere to the Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff, and students may use the Incident Report Form or the harassment@lcc.ac.uk address.
questions.source_excerpt: Making promises in return for sexual favours ... All staff must adhere to the College's Personal Harassment Policy and Procedure for staff ... Students or staff who have been affected by may make a complaint via the Incident Report Form ... Students, staff and external parties can also notify the Colllege of incidents through a dedicated email address harassment@lcc.ac.uk.

questions.question: A student sends a friend request to your personal Facebook account asking for help with an assignment. Under the Social Media Policy, what is the correct approach?
options: Accept it, but only if your privacy settings restrict what the student can see
Accept it, but keep conversations strictly limited to coursework
Do not use your personal account; engage only via the College's platform
Accept it once your line manager has given written approval for the contact
questions.explanation: Staff are prohibited from using personal social media accounts to interact with students and should engage with them only through the College's social media platform for educational purposes.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff are prohibited from utilizing their personal social media accounts to interact with students. However, they are encouraged to engage with students exclusively through the College's social media platform for educational purposes.

questions.question: A new member of staff's personal LinkedIn profile identifies London Churchill College as their employer. Under the Social Media Policy, what should the profile include?
options: The official College logo, to confirm their employment at LCC
A link to the College's official social media channels, as required for all staff
Their line manager's name and email as the contact for any College-related queries
A disclaimer that the views expressed are their own, not the College's
questions.explanation: Where a private account identifies the College, it must be made clear that its views do not represent the College, using an appropriate disclaimer.
questions.source_excerpt: In cases where private social media account/s identify the College, it must be made clear that the views expressed on or through that account does not represent the view of the College. Such account/s should include an appropriate disclaimer

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, what should staff members assume about anything they post on social media platforms?
options: It will be public and permanent, regardless of the privacy settings applied
It will stay private provided the account's privacy settings are set to friends only
It only becomes a concern where the College is explicitly named or tagged in the post
It can be permanently erased by the IT department on request
questions.explanation: The policy tells staff to assume anything posted will be public and permanent whatever the privacy settings applied, and that a link to their College role is easily made even if LCC is not mentioned.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff members should assume anything posted on any social media platforms will be public and permanent, regardless of the privacy settings applied. Whether the College has been explicitly mentioned or not, it can often be easy to make the connection between the individual and their role within the College;

questions.question: You want to post photos from a College event that show students on the College's social media. Under the Social Media Policy, what must happen before you post them?
options: Nothing further is needed, provided the students are not tagged or named in the post
Consent can be sought after posting, if a student objects
The students' personal tutors must be informed in writing before the photos go live
Consent must be obtained in advance by completing the consent form
questions.explanation: Consent must be obtained in advance of posting pictures of people related to the College; for students, this is done by completing the consent form.
questions.source_excerpt: Consent must be obtained in advance of posting pictures on social media which has pictures of people that relate to the College i.e., if it is a student, the College requires to get consent by completing the consent form;

questions.question: You come across content on an LCC-related social media page that appears offensive and possibly unlawful. Under the Social Media Policy, where should this be directed as the initial point of contact?
options: The Quality Assurance department, which owns and enforces the policy
The IT department, which will escalate it to the appropriate team
Your line manager, who will decide whether it should be reported
The Registry team, by emailing the details to registry@lcc.ac.uk
questions.explanation: Although Quality Assurance and Student Engagement own the policy, anything inappropriate, offensive or breaking laws goes to the IT department first, which then escalates it.
questions.source_excerpt: The Quality Assurance and Student Engagement departments are responsible for the policy, however anything that is deemed as inappropriate, offensive, or breaking laws should be directed to the IT department as an initial point of contact. These will then be escalated to the appropriate team;

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, what responsibility do staff and students have if they use the LCC name on social media?
options: A legal responsibility to represent LCC accurately and fairly
A duty to tag the College's official account in every post they make
A requirement to have every post approved by HR before it is published
No responsibility if the post is on a personal account
questions.explanation: The policy states that anyone using the LCC name has a legal responsibility to represent LCC accurately and fairly and to uphold its integrity.
questions.source_excerpt: Students and staff can use social media and note that if they use LCC name they have a legal responsibility to represent LCC accurately and fairly and are expected to uphold the integrity of LCC.

questions.question: A member of staff receives abusive messages through a social media account. Under the Social Media Policy, what are they required to do before referring to the Complaints Policy and Procedure?
options: Delete the messages so that the abuse cannot spread any further
Reply to the sender and ask them to stop the messages immediately
Close the social media account on which the messages were received
Screenshot the evidence of the abuse or harassment that they received
questions.explanation: The policy requires anyone receiving abuse or harassment via social media to screenshot the evidence before referring to the Complaints Policy and Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Should you receive abuse or harassment through social media accounts, you are required to: ... Screenshot the evidence prior to referring to the Complaints Policy and Procedure.

questions.question: A colleague is accused of copyright infringement over material they shared in the course of their employment. Under the Social Media Policy, who should they contact in the first instance?
options: The IT department, for further advice and assistance with the case
The Data Protection Officer, by emailing the full details to dpo@lcc.ac.uk
Their line manager or the HR department, for investigation and support
The copyright holder directly, to negotiate a settlement themselves
questions.explanation: Staff accused of copyright infringement in the course of their employment must contact their line manager or HR in the first instance; the matter is then investigated and support provided. Referral to IT applies to student cases.
questions.source_excerpt: If members of staff are accused of copyright infringement in the course of their employment, they are either required to contact their line manager or HR in the first instance.

questions.question: Under the Social Media Policy, if a staff member's social media content brings the College into disrepute or breaches the standards of conduct required of staff, which department may address it?
options: The Registry team
The HR department
The Student Engagement team
The Admissions team
questions.explanation: The policy states such content may be addressed through the relevant department, namely HR.
questions.source_excerpt: Any content that brings the College into disrepute or that breaches the standards of conduct required of staff, may be addressed through the relevant department, i.e., HR;

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, when may social media be used as a learning or teaching tool?
options: Whenever the lecturer judges it will benefit the students
Once every student in the group has agreed to join the platform
Only if and once it has been approved by the College
Only on platforms that the students already use personally
questions.explanation: The policy states social media should only be used as a learning or teaching tool if and once approved by the College, and this applies to any College-related posts.
questions.source_excerpt: Social media should only be used either as a learning or a teaching tool, if and once approved by the College This applies to any College related posts;

questions.question: You use a College-approved social media platform for a module, but one student does not wish to create an account on it. Under the Social Media Policy, what must you do?
options: Provide the same content in a different format or on an alternative site
Explain that creating an account is a mandatory requirement of the module
Ask a classmate to forward the platform content to the student privately
Refer the student to IT support so they can be helped to set up an account
questions.explanation: Staff must ensure the same information and content are available in a different format or on an alternative site best suited to the student.
questions.source_excerpt: Should a student not have access to or wish not to create an account on the social media platform for learning purposes, College staff must ensure that the same information and content are available in a different format or on an alternative site, best suited to the student/s;

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, what must staff do before using the LCC logo in social media content such as videos, images or posters?
options: Edit the logo so that it fits the platform's image format and colours
Seek approval prior to using the College logo in any such content
Add a personal disclaimer directly beneath the logo in each post
Register the content with the Data Protection Officer before posting
questions.explanation: Staff should use the College logo on social media content for brand recognition, but must seek approval before using it; the logo must also not be edited or modified.
questions.source_excerpt: The College logo should be used by members of staff for any content i.e., video, images, events, or posters, that are used for social media purposes to ensure brand recognition and avoid any copyright issues (members of staff will have to seek approval prior to the use of the LCC logo).

questions.question: A student asks you how to withdraw their GDPR consent and have their images deleted from the College's social media. Under the Social Media Policy, who can they contact?
options: Their personal tutor, who will have the posts removed
Either the Data Protection Officer or the Student Engagement Team
The IT department, which holds the social media sign-in details
The HR department, which stores all signed student consent forms
questions.explanation: Students can withdraw GDPR consent at any time by contacting the Data Protection Officer (dpo@lcc.ac.uk) or the Student Engagement Team and requesting data deletion.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can withdraw their GDPR consent by contacting the Data Protection Officer: dpo@lcc.ac.uk or by contacting the Student Engagement Team and request their data deletion from the social media at any time;

questions.question: According to the freedom of speech section of the Social Media Policy, where is the line drawn for views expressed on social media?
options: Views must be consistent with the College's official position on the matter
Controversial views may only be shared on private accounts, not College ones
Any view is acceptable if the account carries a disclaimer
Views others may disagree with are fine, but not hate speech or violence
questions.explanation: LCC supports freedom of speech, including views others may disagree with, but those views must not cross over into hate speech or violence.
questions.source_excerpt: we are legally allowed to articulate views which other may or may not disagree, however these viewpoints must not crossover into a hate speech or violence;

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy and Guideline, which social media platforms does the policy apply to?
options: The platforms named in the policy, such as Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn
All official College channels listed in section 12
All social media platform use, whether listed in the policy or not
Platforms that have been approved by the College for learning and teaching
questions.explanation: The policy says the platforms it names are only examples and that it applies to all social media platform use, whether listed in the policy or not.
questions.source_excerpt: these are only a few examples that will be updated periodically; however, this policy applies to all social media platform use, whether listed in this policy and guideline or not;

questions.question: How does the Social Media Policy and Guideline define social media for its purposes?
options: Any website or app accessed by staff or students using a College device or network
Interactive online media that lets parties communicate instantly or share data in a public forum
Online platforms that the College has formally approved for teaching, learning and marketing
Commercial platforms that show advertising alongside content posted by their registered users
questions.explanation: The policy defines social media as interactive online media which allows parties to communicate instantly with one another or to share data in a public forum.
questions.source_excerpt: For the purpose of this policy, social media is defined as a form of interactive online media which allows parties to communicate instantly with one another or to share data in a public forum;

questions.question: Which of the following does the Social Media Policy give as an example of personal communications on social media?
options: Posts published through the College's official Instagram account
Updates shared on the College's Facebook main page or Alumni page
Personal staff profile pages on the College's official website
Private Facebook or LinkedIn accounts, or personal blogs
questions.explanation: The policy states that personal communications on social media include private accounts on platforms such as Facebook or LinkedIn, or personal blogs; the other options are official College channels or pages.
questions.source_excerpt: Personal communications on social media include, private accounts on social media platforms such as on, Facebook, LinkedIn, or personal blogs;

questions.question: Which of the following does the Social Media Policy list as an example of confidential material that must not be posted online without permission?
options: Promotion of College events and services
Lawful views that others may disagree with
Details of complaints and/or legal proceedings
Event photos posted with students' GDPR consent
questions.explanation: Details of complaints and/or legal proceedings are listed as confidential material, alongside trade secrets, confidential research data and personal information about another individual; the other options are uses the policy permits.
questions.source_excerpt: Confidential material can include personal confidential information about an individual or information which is confidential for profession reasons, including: ... Details of complaints and/ or legal proceedings.

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, what does 'hate speech' include?
options: Speech, or its endorsement, that is derogatory towards a group based on a protected classification
Any post that publicly criticises the College, its staff or its students, even where the post is lawful
Any view that other users disagree with or that they report to the platform as offensive
Speech posted anonymously or from an account that cannot be linked to a named individual
questions.explanation: The policy defines hate speech as any speech, or endorsement or promotion of speech, that is derogatory towards a group of people based on a protected classification such as race, religion or disability.
questions.source_excerpt: "Hate speech" includes any speech - or endorsement or promotion of speech that is derogatory towards a group of people based on a protected classification;

questions.question: Under the Social Media Policy, who reserves the right to remove user-generated content or comments, for the safety of students and staff?
options: The Head of Quality Assurance and Student Engagement
The Head of Data and Information Technology
The Student Engagement and Welfare Officer
The Data Protection Officer
questions.explanation: The Head of Data and Information Technology (HoDIT) reserves the right to remove any user-generated content or comments in accordance with the policy, for the safety of students and staff.
questions.source_excerpt: The Head of Data and Information Technology (HoDIT) reserves the right to remove any user- generated content or comments in accordance with this policy, for the safety of the students and staff;

questions.question: Under the Social Media Policy, what must staff and students read and agree to before accessing, posting on or browsing social media?
options: A usage agreement countersigned by their line manager
A GDPR consent form covering each post they intend to publish
The privacy settings guidance issued by the IT support team
The terms and conditions set by the platform or website itself
questions.explanation: Staff and students must read and agree to the terms and conditions of the social media platform or website before accessing, posting and browsing.
questions.source_excerpt: Students and staff must ensure to read and agree to the terms and conditions of the social media platform/website prior accessing, posting, and browsing;

questions.question: Under the Social Media Policy, staff must not post or share discriminatory content, or content that contravenes which College policy?
options: The Equality and Diversity Policy
The Freedom of Speech Policy and Code of Practice
The Data Protection Policy
The Complaints Policy and Procedure
questions.explanation: Staff must not post or share discriminatory content or content which contravenes the College's Equality and Diversity Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff must not post or share content that causes hatred, promotes, or advocates radicalisation, terrorism, or posts that discriminates on the grounds of race, gender, disability, age, marital status, sex, pollical or religious belief or, which contravenes the College's Equality and Diversity Policy;

questions.question: Under the Social Media Policy, a student who feels harassed via social media should report it through the Complaints Policy and Procedure. Which team can they also email their concerns to?
options: The IT support team
The Quality Assurance team
The Registry team
The Admissions team
questions.explanation: Students who feel attacked or harassed via social media should report it through the Complaints Policy and Procedure and can also email the Registry team at registry@lcc.ac.uk.
questions.source_excerpt: Should a student feel attacked or harassed by a fellow student or member of staff via social media, please ensure to report it through the Complaints Policy and Procedure. Additionally, you can email your concerns to the Registry team: registry@lcc.ac.uk.

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, what must happen after an incident of abuse or harassment through social media has been dealt with?
options: The affected social media account must be closed by the IT department
The team that led on it reports back to the relevant department
The collected screenshots are passed to the Data Protection Officer
The incident is summarised in a post on the College's official channels
questions.explanation: After the incident, the team which leads on it must report back to the relevant department so that up-to-date information on all outcomes is held.
questions.source_excerpt: It is necessary that after the incident, the team which leads on it reports back to the relevant department, to ensure we have up-to-date information of all outcomes;

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, how often are LCC's social media accounts monitored by Student Engagement?
options: Daily
Monthly
Biweekly
Once a term
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC's social media accounts are carefully monitored by Student Engagement biweekly.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC's social media accounts are carefully monitored by the Student Engagement, biweekly;

questions.question: The Social Media Policy restricts how the College name, logo and images may be displayed on personal, departmental or organisational sites. Which use does it prohibit?
options: Use in posts that share College news and success with staff and students
Use on a site whose owner has added a personal views disclaimer
Use on professional networking sites such as LinkedIn
Use that promotes a product, cause, political party or candidate
questions.explanation: The College name, logo or other College images may not be displayed on personal, departmental or organisational sites in a manner that promotes a product, cause, political party or candidate.
questions.source_excerpt: The College name, logo or any other College images or iconography may not be displayed on any personal, departmental, or organisational sites in a manner that promotes a product, cause, political party, or candidate.

questions.question: Under the Social Media Policy, who should a student accused of copyright infringement contact for academic-related instances?
options: Their personal tutor or lecturer
The Data Protection Officer
The Registry team via registry@lcc.ac.uk
The Student Engagement and Welfare Officer
questions.explanation: Students accused of copyright infringement must contact their personal tutor or lecturer for academic-related instances; cases may then be referred to the IT department.
questions.source_excerpt: If students are accused of copyright infringement, they must ensure to contact either their personal tutor or lecturer for academic-related instances.

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, what is required for every publication request on the College's social media channels?
options: Approval by the PIMG prior to publishing
Review by Student Engagement after posting
Consent from the Data Protection Officer
Sign-off by the HR department in advance
questions.explanation: The policy states that all publication requests require approval by the PIMG prior to publishing.
questions.source_excerpt: All publication requests require approval by the PIMG prior to publishing;

questions.question: According to the Social Media Policy, how is access to the sign-in details for the College's social media accounts controlled?
options: Available to all Student Engagement staff, with no further approval
Held only by the Head of Data and Information Technology personally
Restricted to 2-3 members of staff, subject to IT department approval
Shared with any staff member whose line manager has approved access
questions.explanation: Access to social media sign-in details is restricted to 2-3 members of staff and is subject to approval by the IT department.
questions.source_excerpt: Access to social media sign-in details is restricted to 2-3 members of staff and is subject to approval by the IT department.

questions.question: A lecturer plans to set up a new social media account to share course-related content with students. Under the Social Media Policy, what should they do about the account's intended content?
options: Register the account with the Data Protection Officer before any content is posted
Seek advice on the intended content from their line manager or a member of staff
Obtain written consent from every student who will follow or join the account
Rely on the biweekly Student Engagement monitoring to review content once posted
questions.explanation: Staff who establish a social media account or presence for work or education-related content should seek advice on intended content from their line manager or a member of staff.
questions.source_excerpt: All staff and students who establish a social media account or presence for work or education-related content/activities should seek advice on intended content from their line manager or a member of staff;

questions.question: A member of staff wants to mention on social media that a colleague is off work because of a medical condition. The colleague has not given permission. How does the Social Media Policy treat this?
options: As acceptable if it is posted on a personal account rather than a College channel
As acceptable if it is shared only within a closed or private online group
As a potential breach of data protection and of College privacy rules
As a concern only if the colleague later makes a complaint about the post
questions.explanation: Posting confidential material online without permission is potentially a breach of data protection and College privacy rules, and personal information such as someone's medical history is confidential material.
questions.source_excerpt: Posting confidentiality material online without permission is potentially a breach of data protection as well as college privacy rules. ... Personal information about another individual (such as information about their medical history, or sexuality)

questions.question: A student gave GDPR consent at the start of her course, and her photos have been on the College's social media for months. She now wants them removed. Under the Social Media Policy, can she withdraw her consent?
options: Yes; she can withdraw her consent and request data deletion at any time
No; consent cannot be withdrawn for posts that are already published
Only within 12 months of the date on which she signed the consent form
Only before the images have been shared on the College's public channels
questions.explanation: Students can withdraw their GDPR consent and request deletion of their data from social media at any time, via the Data Protection Officer or the Student Engagement Team.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can withdraw their GDPR consent by contacting the Data Protection Officer: dpo@lcc.ac.uk or by contacting the Student Engagement Team and request their data deletion from the social media at any time;

questions.question: A comment on a College social media page uses no slurs but implies a threat of harassment towards a student. How does the Social Media Policy treat this comment?
options: As lawful expression, because no derogatory language has been used
As a concern only if the threat is stated explicitly rather than implied
As acceptable unless the student belongs to a protected class of people
As covered by the College's zero tolerance of implied threats of harassment
questions.explanation: The College has zero tolerance for expressed or implied threats of harassment, so an implied threat is covered even without derogatory language.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has zero tolerance for racism, bigotry, misogyny, expressed or implied threats of harassment, physical harm, or hate speech;

questions.question: A member of staff posts comments as a representative of the College on an external industry forum that the College does not run. Does the Social Media Policy apply to these postings?
options: No; it covers only postings made on the College's own sites and channels
Yes; it covers postings as a College representative on non-institutional sites
No; it covers only accounts whose sign-in details have been approved by IT
Only if the forum has first been approved by the PIMG for College use
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all social media postings on a College site or made as a representative of the College on a non-institutional site.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy applies to all social media postings on college site or as a representative of the College on a non-institutional site.

questions.question: A student posts content on social media that damages the reputation of a member of staff. Under the Social Media Policy, what may the College do with this content?
options: Use it as evidence for potential disciplinary measures, as deemed appropriate
Nothing, as content on a student's personal account is outside the policy
Refer it to the Data Protection Officer so that it is deleted under GDPR
Pass it only to the staff member's line manager to resolve informally
questions.explanation: Where a student damages the reputation of the College or another student or staff member, the College reserves the right to use this as evidence for potential disciplinary measures.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event that a student damages the reputation of the College or another student/staff member, the College reserves the right to utilise this as evidence for potential disciplinary measures, as deemed appropriate.

questions.question: A member of staff uses their personal account to post a belittling comment aimed at a colleague, arguing that the Social Media Policy only covers College accounts. Are they right?
options: Yes; personal accounts are covered only when the College is named in a post
Yes; posts on personal accounts are covered only if made in working hours
No; personal accounts must not be used to abuse or intimidate colleagues
No, but only because the colleague works in the same department as them
questions.explanation: When posting on a personal account, staff must not use social media to verbally abuse or intimidate work colleagues, students or other users, and respect should be shown at all times.
questions.source_excerpt: When positing on a personal account, social media should not be used to verbally abuse or intimidate work colleagues or students, or other users; respect should be shown at all times;

questions.question: A student accidentally posts sensitive College information in a public social media group. According to the Social Media Policy, what could this lead to?
options: No penalties, because the disclosure was accidental rather than intentional
Penalties for the student only, as the College is not liable for their posts
Penalties for the College only, as students cannot be held personally liable
Significant legal and financial penalties for both the College and the student
questions.explanation: Posting sensitive or confidential information, whether accidentally or intentionally, may breach information security and could result in significant legal and financial penalties for the College and the student.
questions.source_excerpt: should students post sensitive or confidential information, be it accidentally or intentionally, it may lead to breach of information security which could result in significant, legal, and financial penalties for the College and the student;

questions.question: A student tells you they are being harassed through social media and has screenshotted the evidence. Which contacts does the Social Media Policy list for students in this situation?
options: Their Personal Tutor, the Registry Team or the Student Engagement Team
The page administrators or the PIMG, which approves publications
The Data Protection Officer or the Head of Data and Information Technology
Their line manager or the HR department, in the first instance
questions.explanation: Students receiving abuse or harassment via social media can contact their Personal Tutor, the Registry Team or the Student Engagement Team; staff contact the relevant department.
questions.source_excerpt: You can either contact the Personal Tutor (students), Registry Team: Registry@lcc.ac.uk or the Student Engagement Team (Student Engagement and Welfare Officer or Manger);

questions.question: During monitoring, a comment on one of LCC's social media accounts is deemed inappropriate. According to the Social Media Policy, what happens next?
options: The comment is left in place until the next biweekly monitoring review
The account owner decides alone, without involving any other teams
The relevant teams discuss it and a course of action is then taken
The account is closed and new sign-in details are issued by IT
questions.explanation: Where comments are deemed inappropriate, discussions take place between the relevant teams and a course of action is taken.
questions.source_excerpt: Should a situation arise where a comment/s are deemed as inappropriate, discussions will take place between the relevant teams and a course of action will be taken.

questions.question: Page administrators notice a rise in audience interactions on one of the College's social media channels. Under the Social Media Policy, who do they share this information with?
options: The HR department, to review the conduct of the users who commented
The IT department, which approves access to the channel's sign-in details
The Data Protection Officer, to log the interactions under GDPR
The Student Engagement team, for analysis and response as needed
questions.explanation: Page administrators and the Welfare Officer monitor audience interactions and share this information with the Student Engagement team for analysis and response as needed.
questions.source_excerpt: Page administrators and the Welfare Officer monitor audience interactions with the social media channels when possible and share this information with the Student Engagement team for analysis and response as needed;

questions.question: A department wants to recolour the College logo to match the theme of its own social media page. Under the Social Media Policy, is this permitted?
options: Yes, provided approval is sought before the recoloured logo is used
No; the College logo should not be edited or modified in any way
Yes, if the recoloured logo is used only on the department's own pages
No, unless the College's full name appears beside the recoloured logo
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College logo should not be edited or modified; approval to use the logo does not extend to altering it.
questions.source_excerpt: The College logo should not be edited or modified;

questions.question: A member of staff accused of copyright infringement says they did not know the image they posted was protected. According to the Social Media Policy, does this help their case?
options: No; ignorance is no defence under copyright law
Yes, provided the image was removed once the owner complained
Yes, if the post was made in the course of their employment
Only if they report the matter to HR within five working days
questions.explanation: The policy notes that ignorance is no defence under copyright law, so not knowing the image was protected does not excuse the infringement.
questions.source_excerpt: It should be noted that ignorance is no defence under copyright law,

questions.question: A student accused of copyright infringement has contacted their lecturer about an academic-related instance. Under the Social Media Policy, where may the case then be referred for further advice?
options: The HR department, which handles all copyright allegations
The IT department, for further advice and assistance
The Registry team, for recording on the student's file
The Data Protection Officer, for a formal investigation
questions.explanation: Students accused of copyright infringement contact their personal tutor or lecturer for academic-related instances, and cases may be referred to the IT department for further advice and assistance.
questions.source_excerpt: If students are accused of copyright infringement, they must ensure to contact either their personal tutor or lecturer for academic-related instances. Cases may be referred to the IT department, who will offer further advice and assistance;

questions.question: A departmental manager wants help setting up an effective social media channel and, separately, has spotted an offensive post on an existing LCC page. Under the Social Media Policy, who should they contact about each?
options: Quality Assurance for the set-up help; the Student Engagement team as first contact for the post
The Data Protection Officer for the set-up help; HR as first contact for the post
The PIMG for the set-up help; the Registry team as first contact for the post
The IT support team for the set-up help; the IT department as first contact for the post
questions.explanation: Queries such as help setting up effective channels go to the IT support team, and anything inappropriate or offensive goes to the IT department as the initial point of contact, even though Quality Assurance and Student Engagement own the policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Should there be any concerns or queries i.e., assistance with setting up effective social media channels, please contact the IT support team; ... anything that is deemed as inappropriate, offensive, or breaking laws should be directed to the IT department as an initial point of contact.

questions.question: A member of staff is accused of copyright infringement over images used in a private business they run outside their College role. What does the Social Media Policy say about the help the College can offer?
options: The College will negotiate with the copyright holder for them, as it does for all staff
It may not be able to offer further help, as the case is outside its usual course of business
The IT department may take over the case, as it handles all copyright claims against staff
HR will give full support, provided they did not know the images were protected
questions.explanation: The College may not be able to offer further assistance where copyright allegations relate to instances outside the scope of its usual course of business; ignorance is also no defence under copyright law.
questions.source_excerpt: It should be noted that ignorance is no defence under copyright law, hence the College may not be able to offer further assistance, should allegations of copyright infringement refer to instances that fall outside of the scope of the College's usual course of business.

questions.question: A lecturer and one of their students both receive abusive messages from the same social media account. After screenshotting the evidence, who does the Social Media Policy say each of them should contact?
options: Both should contact HR, which handles all social media abuse involving College members
Lecturer: their Personal Tutor or Registry; student: the relevant department
Student: Personal Tutor, Registry or Student Engagement; lecturer: the relevant department
Both should contact the Data Protection Officer, as the messages involve their personal data
questions.explanation: Students can contact their Personal Tutor, the Registry Team or the Student Engagement Team, whereas members of staff contact the relevant department.
questions.source_excerpt: Screenshot the evidence prior to referring to the Complaints Policy and Procedure. ... You can either contact the Personal Tutor (students), Registry Team: Registry@lcc.ac.uk or the Student Engagement Team (Student Engagement and Welfare Officer or Manger); ... Contact the relevant department (members of staff);

questions.question: A member of staff's personal account carries the disclaimer 'Views expressed here are my own and do not reflect the views of London Churchill College'. They share a post advocating radicalisation. How does the Social Media Policy treat this?
options: As permitted, because the disclaimer shows the views are not the College's own
As permitted, provided the account does not display the College name or logo
As prohibited: staff must not post or share content advocating radicalisation
As a matter for the platform, since the policy covers only College-run channels
questions.explanation: A disclaimer only makes clear that a private account's views are not the College's; staff must still not post or share content that promotes or advocates radicalisation or terrorism.
questions.source_excerpt: Staff must not post or share content that causes hatred, promotes, or advocates radicalisation, terrorism,

questions.question: A member of staff posts content on a private account that never mentions LCC but breaches the standards of conduct required of staff. They argue the College cannot act. Under the Social Media Policy, which statement is correct?
options: The College cannot act, because it was not explicitly mentioned in the post
The link to their role is easily made, and HR may address the conduct breach
The College can act only if a student complains under the Complaints Policy
The College can act only if the account was set to public when they posted
questions.explanation: Staff should assume posts are public and permanent, and a connection to their College role is easily made whether or not the College is mentioned; content breaching staff conduct standards may be addressed through HR.
questions.source_excerpt: Whether the College has been explicitly mentioned or not, it can often be easy to make the connection between the individual and their role within the College; ... Any content that brings the College into disrepute or that breaches the standards of conduct required of staff, may be addressed through the relevant department, i.e., HR;

questions.question: To get help with a system error, a member of staff posts a screenshot showing a student's full name and student ID on an external discussion forum, without the student's permission. How does the Social Media Policy treat this?
options: As prohibited, because the student has not given their permission
As permitted, because the post was made for a legitimate work-related purpose
As permitted, provided the post is deleted once the system error has been fixed
As permitted, if the IT department has approved staff use of that forum
questions.explanation: Staff and students are prohibited from sharing anyone's personal identification information on external social media sites without their permission, which could damage LCC's reputation and even lead to lawsuits.
questions.source_excerpt: Students and staff are prohibited from sharing anyone's personal identification information on external social media sites without their permission. This can cause damage to LCC's reputation and relationship which could even result in lawsuits;

questions.question: After a staff away day, a lecturer wants to post group photos of their colleagues on their own personal social media account. Under the Social Media Policy, what applies?
options: No consent is needed, since consent is required only for photos in which students appear
Consent is needed only if the photos are posted on an official College channel
Consent must be obtained in advance, as the photos show people relating to the College
Consent can be assumed unless a colleague later asks for the photos to be removed
questions.explanation: Consent must be obtained in advance of posting pictures of people that relate to the College; the consent form is the specific route for students, but the requirement is not limited to them.
questions.source_excerpt: Consent must be obtained in advance of posting pictures on social media which has pictures of people that relate to the College i.e., if it is a student, the College requires to get consent by completing the consent form;

questions.question: A lecturer's lawful post on a College site sparks debate, and some colleagues ask for it to be removed simply because they disagree with it. What does the Social Media Policy say about this?
options: It must be removed, since posts on College sites must reflect the College's view
It must be removed once a colleague reports it to the IT department as offensive
It may stay only if the lecturer adds a disclaimer that the views are their own
The policy is not intended to limit lawful free speech, even if others disagree
questions.explanation: Views others may disagree with can lawfully be expressed, provided they do not cross into hate speech or violence, and nothing in the policy is intended to limit freedom of speech within the law.
questions.source_excerpt: we are legally allowed to articulate views which other may or may not disagree, ... Nothing in the social media policy and guideline is intended to have the effect of limiting the freedom of speech within the law.

questions.question: A colleague argues that a derogatory post about a group of people cannot be hate speech under the Social Media Policy, because the group's characteristic is not on the policy's list. Why is this reasoning flawed?
options: The policy's list of protected classifications is non-exhaustive
Hate speech also covers derogatory posts aimed at a single individual
Any post reported by a reader as offensive is treated as hate speech
The list covers staff only; HR holds a wider list covering students
questions.explanation: Hate speech is speech derogatory towards a group based on a protected classification, and the policy expressly describes its list of classifications as non-exhaustive.
questions.source_excerpt: "Hate speech" includes any speech - or endorsement or promotion of speech that is derogatory towards a group of people based on a protected classification; a list of non-exhaustive of what this may include:

questions.question: A member of staff did not write a post that dehumanises a religious group, but reshared it with an approving comment. How does the Social Media Policy treat the reshare?
options: As outside the policy, because they were not the original author of the post
As acceptable, provided the original author's name remains clearly visible
As hate speech, which includes endorsing or promoting such speech
As a matter for the platform alone, as reshares fall under its own terms
questions.explanation: Hate speech includes the endorsement or promotion of speech derogatory towards a group based on a protected classification, and speech that dehumanises a protected class is hate speech.
questions.source_excerpt: "Hate speech" includes any speech - or endorsement or promotion of speech that is derogatory towards a group of people based on a protected classification; ... Speech that dehumanises or promotes violence against a protected class of people is hate speech.

questions.question: A student ambassador is asked to post about an upcoming open event on behalf of the College. Under the Social Media Policy, which rule governs these College-related posts?
options: They may post freely, provided a personal disclaimer is added to each post
They need approval only from their personal tutor before posting
They should post only if and once the College has approved the use
They may post, as student posts fall outside the rules for College use
questions.explanation: Students posting on behalf of the College are directed to the learning and teaching provisions, which say social media should be used only if and once approved by the College, and that this applies to any College-related posts.
questions.source_excerpt: Students that post on behalf of the College should refer to section 5 of the policy; ... Social media should only be used either as a learning or a teaching tool, if and once approved by the College This applies to any College related posts;

questions.question: A member of staff whose access to the College's social media sign-in details has been approved by IT wants to publish an urgent update straight away. What does the Social Media Policy still require?
options: Nothing further, as IT approval of access also covers publishing
PIMG approval of the publication request before publishing
A review of the post by Student Engagement at its next biweekly check
GDPR consent from the Data Protection Officer before the post goes live
questions.explanation: Access to sign-in details is a separate control approved by IT; all publication requests still require PIMG approval before publishing.
questions.source_excerpt: All publication requests require approval by the PIMG prior to publishing; ... Access to social media sign-in details is restricted to 2-3 members of staff and is subject to approval by the IT department.

questions.question: A member of staff's personal blog backs a local election candidate. They want to add the College logo, alongside a disclaimer that the views are their own. Under the Social Media Policy, is this allowed?
options: Yes; the disclaimer makes clear that the blog does not represent the College
Yes, provided they seek approval before using the College logo on the blog
No, unless the blog posts are also shared on the College's official channels
No; the logo may not be shown on personal sites in a way that promotes a candidate
questions.explanation: The College name, logo and images may not be displayed on personal sites in a manner that promotes a political party or candidate; neither a disclaimer nor logo approval changes this.
questions.source_excerpt: The College name, logo or any other College images or iconography may not be displayed on any personal, departmental, or organisational sites in a manner that promotes a product, cause, political party, or candidate.

questions.question: In separate cases, a member of staff is accused of copyright infringement in the course of their employment, and a student is accused in an academic-related instance. Under the Social Media Policy, whom should each contact first?
options: Both should contact the IT department, which advises on all copyright cases
Staff member: line manager or HR; student: their personal tutor or lecturer
Staff member: the IT department; student: the Registry team
Staff member: the Data Protection Officer; student: Student Engagement
questions.explanation: Staff contact their line manager or HR in the first instance, while students contact their personal tutor or lecturer for academic-related instances; student cases may then be referred to IT.
questions.source_excerpt: If students are accused of copyright infringement, they must ensure to contact either their personal tutor or lecturer for academic-related instances. ... If members of staff are accused of copyright infringement in the course of their employment, they are either required to contact their line manager or HR in the first instance.

questions.question: The College plans to share, on its YouTube channel, a video of students presenting their projects; no still photos are involved. Under the Social Media Policy, is GDPR consent from the students needed?
options: Yes; GDPR consent covers pictures, videos or any form of media
No; GDPR consent is required only for still photographs of students
No, provided the students are not named in the video's title or caption
Only if the video will stay on the channel for more than twelve months
questions.explanation: GDPR consent is obtained from students when sharing any pictures, videos or any form of media on the LCC public domain, not just photographs.
questions.source_excerpt: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) consent will be obtained from students when sharing any pictures, videos, or any form of media on the LCC public domain;

questions.question: A module team has College approval to use a social media platform for teaching. Under the Social Media Policy, which terms must staff and students observe before accessing the platform?
options: Only the platform's terms, as College approval replaces the College's own terms
Only the College's terms, as these override any terms set by the platform
The platform's terms and the Freedom of Speech Code of Practice only
Both the platform's terms and conditions and the College's terms on its use
questions.explanation: Staff and students must read and agree to the platform's own terms and conditions and must also abide by the College's terms and conditions on social media use before accessing it.
questions.source_excerpt: Students and staff must ensure to read and agree to the terms and conditions of the social media platform/website prior accessing, posting, and browsing; ... Students and staff must also ensure that they abide by the College's terms and conditions relating to the use of social media in this context prior to accessing any social media platforms;

questions.question: A student reports harassment received through social media, and the Student Engagement team leads on the case. Which sequence follows the Social Media Policy?
options: The student screenshots the evidence before referring it; afterwards the lead team reports back to the relevant department
The student deletes the messages and reports them; the lead team then posts a public update on the College's channels
The lead team gathers the screenshots itself, then passes the whole case to the Data Protection Officer to close
The student reports it to the platform only; the lead team gets involved only if the platform takes no action
questions.explanation: The person receiving abuse screenshots the evidence before referring to the Complaints Policy and Procedure, and after the incident the team that led on it reports back to the relevant department.
questions.source_excerpt: Screenshot the evidence prior to referring to the Complaints Policy and Procedure. ... It is necessary that after the incident, the team which leads on it reports back to the relevant department, to ensure we have up-to-date information of all outcomes;

questions.question: A student cannot access the College-approved platform used for a module and asks the lecturer to send the materials from the lecturer's own personal WhatsApp account. Under the Social Media Policy, what should the lecturer do?
options: Send them from the personal account, as a reasonable adjustment for the student
Make the same content available in another format or on an alternative site
Seek their line manager's approval, then send them from the personal account
Explain that the student must create an account to access the materials
questions.explanation: Staff must make the same content available in a different format or on an alternative site, and must not use personal social media accounts to interact with students.
questions.source_excerpt: College staff must ensure that the same information and content are available in a different format or on an alternative site, best suited to the student/s; ... Staff are prohibited from utilizing their personal social media accounts to interact with students.

questions.question: A lecturer wants to teach using a newly launched platform that the Social Media Policy does not name, arguing that the policy therefore does not apply. Which statement is correct?
options: The policy covers only the platforms it names until its list is next updated
The policy applies only once IT has added the platform to its approved list
The policy applies, but approval is needed only if the platform is used for marketing
The policy covers all social media use, so College approval is needed first
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all social media platform use whether listed or not, and social media may be used as a learning or teaching tool only if and once approved by the College.
questions.source_excerpt: this policy applies to all social media platform use, whether listed in this policy and guideline or not; ... Social media should only be used either as a learning or a teaching tool, if and once approved by the College

questions.question: A researcher plans to post a summary of confidential research data on LinkedIn to attract collaborators, without permission. The summary contains no personal information about anyone. How does the Social Media Policy treat this?
options: As a potential breach, since research data can be confidential material
As acceptable, since research data is confidential only when it identifies individuals
As acceptable, provided the profile carries a disclaimer that the views are their own
As acceptable, if the post is deleted once suitable collaborators have made contact
questions.explanation: Confidential material is not limited to personal information: it includes information confidential for professional reasons, such as confidential research data, and posting it online without permission is potentially a breach of data protection and College privacy rules.
questions.source_excerpt: Posting confidentiality material online without permission is potentially a breach of data protection as well as college privacy rules. Confidential material can include personal confidential information about an individual or information which is confidential for profession reasons, including: ... Confidential research data

questions.question: A student's posts damage the College's reputation, and separately a member of staff posts content that brings the College into disrepute. Under the Social Media Policy, how may each case be dealt with?
options: Student: recorded by the Registry team; staff: referred to the Data Protection Officer
Student: used as evidence for potential disciplinary measures; staff: addressed through HR
Student: reviewed by the PIMG; staff: dealt with by the Welfare Officer
Student: dealt with by their personal tutor alone; staff: referred to Quality Assurance
questions.explanation: Where a student damages the College's reputation, the College may use this as evidence for potential disciplinary measures; staff content that brings the College into disrepute may be addressed through HR.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event that a student damages the reputation of the College or another student/staff member, the College reserves the right to utilise this as evidence for potential disciplinary measures, as deemed appropriate. ... Any content that brings the College into disrepute or that breaches the standards of conduct required of staff, may be addressed through the relevant department, i.e., HR;

questions.question: A member of staff designing an event poster for the College's Instagram plans to leave the logo off so they need not seek approval. Under the Social Media Policy, which approach is correct?
options: Leave the logo off, as approval is needed only when the logo appears in content
Use a simplified version of the logo, which needs no approval as it is not the official one
Include the unaltered logo, having sought approval before using it on the poster
Include the logo without approval, as the poster is for an official College channel
questions.explanation: Staff should use the College logo on social media content such as posters for brand recognition, must seek approval before using it, and must not edit or modify it.
questions.source_excerpt: The College logo should not be edited or modified; ... The College logo should be used by members of staff for any content i.e., video, images, events, or posters, that are used for social media purposes to ensure brand recognition and avoid any copyright issues (members of staff will have to seek approval prior to the use of the LCC logo).

questions.question: A lecturer wants to post a third-party diagram on a College-approved teaching page, arguing that copyright is the College's concern because it approved the platform. Under the Social Media Policy, where does responsibility for using the diagram lawfully lie?
options: With the College, as its approval of the platform covers all material posted on it
With the IT department, which clears copyright on approved platforms
With the PIMG, whose approval of a publication confirms that copyright is cleared
With the lecturer, which may involve ensuring permission has been granted
