questions.explanation: It is the responsibility of both staff and students to make legitimate use of third-party material, which may involve ensuring the copyright holder's permission has been granted; approval of the platform does not shift this.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the responsibility of both members of staff and students to make legitimate use of any third-party material; this may involve ensuring permission has been granted to avoid interfering with any of the exclusive rights of the copyright holder;

policies.title: Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure

questions.question: A student comes to you with a complaint about another student's behaviour that falls under the Student Code of Conduct. What does the Preliminary Enquiry stage of the procedure require you to do?
options: Investigate the complaint yourself and gather the witness statements
Refer the matter verbally to the student's personal tutor
Refer the matter in writing to a Registry member of staff
Forward the complaint to the Deputy Vice-Principal to convene a panel
questions.explanation: Any staff member receiving an initial complaint must refer it in writing to a Registry member of staff, who then decides whether it falls under the procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Any staff member receiving an initial complaint under this code should refer the matter in writing to a Registry member of staff. The Registry member of staff will consider whether the complaint falls under this procedure;

questions.question: A student in your class has shown some low-level anti-social behaviour in lessons. Under the Early Intervention section of the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, what are staff encouraged to do?
options: Refer the student immediately to the Serious Cases Triage Panel for review
Issue the student with a formal written warning within 5 working days
Address it informally to promote positive behaviour, without formal action
Report it in writing to the Principal so a misconduct panel can be convened
questions.explanation: Staff are encouraged to deal with apparently petty incidents such as low-level anti-social behaviour through informal means to promote positive behaviour, without escalating to formal action; formal procedures apply only where this is ineffective, insufficient or inappropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC members of staff are encouraged to address apparently petty incidents, for instance, low-level anti-social behaviour or unauthorised absences, through informal means to promote positive behaviour among students that adheres to policies and regulations, without an escalation to formal action.

questions.question: According to the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, where can behaviour amounting to student misconduct take place?
options: On College premises or at official College events, but not in students' private lives
On College premises or elsewhere, whether or not engaged in College-related activity
Anywhere, provided the student is engaged in College-related activity at the time
On College premises during term time, whether or not classes are running that day
questions.explanation: The policy states that misconduct could take place on College premises or elsewhere, whether or not the student is engaged in College-related activity.
questions.source_excerpt: Such behaviour could take place on College premises or elsewhere, and whilst engaged in College related activity or not;

questions.question: An allegation of sexual misconduct is made against a student, who apologises and says it was a misunderstanding. Under the Student Code of Conduct, can it be dealt with through the informal Minor Misconduct process?
options: Yes, because the student has shown sincere regret and contrition about the incident
No, informal resolution will not normally be appropriate for sexual misconduct
Yes, provided no material loss or damage was caused and no one has suffered
Yes, if the Registrar believes informal guidance is likely to resolve the situation
questions.explanation: The Minor Misconduct section states that informal resolution will not normally be appropriate for an allegation of sexual misconduct, which is also listed as serious or repeated misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: With respect to an allegation of sexual misconduct informal resolution will not normally be appropriate;

questions.question: Pending a disciplinary hearing, a student has been told not to contact a particular individual. You learn they have contacted that person. How does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure treat this?
options: As a minor matter to be handled informally by staff through early intervention
As having no disciplinary consequence, because the restriction is not itself a penalty
As a matter for automatic referral to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
As a serious disciplinary offence for failing to comply with the restriction
questions.explanation: The College may impose restrictions short of suspension, such as not contacting a particular individual, and failure to comply with such a restriction constitutes a serious disciplinary offence.
questions.source_excerpt: The College may impose other actions short of suspension, such as a requirement that a student does not visit a particular campus or building, or that they do not contact a particular individual. Failure to comply with such a restriction or a suspension would constitute a serious disciplinary offence;

questions.question: Under the investigation principles of the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, who bears the burden of proof and what standard of proof applies?
options: The student; the balance of probabilities
The College; the balance of probabilities
The College; beyond reasonable doubt
The complainant; beyond reasonable doubt
questions.explanation: The burden of proof falls on the College and the standard of proof is the balance of probabilities, meaning it is more likely than not that the event happened.
questions.source_excerpt: The `burden of proof' (defined as determining whose responsibility it is to prove an issue) falls upon the College, whilst the `standard of proof' to be employed during investigations shall be the `balance of probabilities' (defined as it being more likely than not that a particular event happened);

questions.question: According to the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, what is the role of the Serious Cases Triage Panel (SCTP)?
options: To hear student appeals against a misconduct panel's findings and decide the final outcome
To decide the final penalty once the Registrar's formal investigation has fully concluded
To make urgent safeguarding or precautionary decisions, pending a formal investigation
To resolve minor misconduct informally through guidance meetings with the students involved
questions.explanation: Serious misconduct cases are normally referred first to the SCTP, which makes urgent decisions on safeguarding or precautionary measures (e.g. no-contact orders, suspension) based on prima facie evidence, pending a formal investigation.
questions.source_excerpt: the case will normally be referred in the first instance to the Serious Cases Triage Panel (SCTP) to make urgent decisions that may concern safeguarding action or precautionary measures such as no-contact orders or suspension of students from campus, based on prima facie evidence, pending a formal investigation.

questions.question: While investigating a disciplinary matter under the Student Code of Conduct, you notice the student appears to show signs of mental health difficulties. What may you do under the policy?
options: Consult the Principal, then suspend the investigation and refer the student to Student Support Services
Continue the investigation but refer the case straight to a misconduct panel for a quicker decision
Close the case at once and delete the record of the matter from the student's disciplinary file
Pause the investigation until the student supplies a formal medical diagnosis from their own GP
questions.explanation: The Health matters section allows an investigating staff member, after consulting the Principal, to suspend their investigation and refer the student to the College's Student Support Services.
questions.source_excerpt: If it appears to an investigating staff member that a student involved in a disciplinary matter is affected by signs of mental health difficulties, or psychological or emotional disorder, they may, after consulting with the Principal, suspend their investigation and refer the student to the College's Student Support Services;

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, what does LCC do where criminal proceedings against a student are ongoing?
options: Awaits the outcome of those proceedings before commencing its own investigation
Runs its own investigation in parallel and shares its findings with the police
Closes the disciplinary case permanently, leaving the matter to the criminal proceedings
Lets the court hearing the case decide any College penalty on the College's behalf
questions.explanation: Where a criminal offence appears to have been committed the College refers it to the police, and where criminal proceedings are ongoing LCC waits for their outcome before starting its own investigation.
questions.source_excerpt: Where it appears that a criminal offence has been committed, the College will refer the matter to the police. In instances where criminal proceedings against a student are ongoing, LCC will await the outcome of those proceedings before commencing its own investigation;

questions.question: A student called to a misconduct panel hearing asks you whether they can bring a solicitor to represent them. What does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure say?
options: Yes, students may be represented by any legal practitioner of their choice
Yes, provided the College is also legally represented at the same hearing
Not normally; they may instead be represented by a fellow LCC student
No, students must attend alone and may not be represented by anyone
questions.explanation: Students may be represented by a fellow LCC student, but neither the College nor the student is normally permitted representation by a legal practitioner.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are entitled to be represented by one of their fellow LCC students in meetings or hearings. Neither the College nor the student will in normal circumstances be permitted representation in meetings or hearings by a legal practitioner;

questions.question: According to the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, which of the following is listed as a situation that can constitute serious or repeated misconduct?
options: Any material loss or damage is minor and can be repaired quickly and inexpensively
Informal guidance to the student is likely to resolve the situation
No one has suffered because of the incident and the student is sorry
The student has been absent without authorisation on repeated occasions
questions.explanation: Repeated unauthorised absence by the student is listed among the situations that can constitute serious or repeated misconduct; the other options are elements of minor misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: Serious or repeated misconduct can include the following situations: ... Previous misconduct has been repeated despite warnings Repeated unauthorised absence from the student

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, what may happen if a misconduct complaint proves to be without substance and was made for frivolous, malicious or vexatious reasons?
options: The complaint is closed and the College can take no further action on it
The matter is automatically referred to the police for criminal investigation
The complainant is referred to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
The College may consider disciplinary action against the complainant
questions.explanation: The policy says that where a complaint is without substance and made for frivolous, malicious or vexatious reasons, the College may consider disciplinary action against the complainant.
questions.source_excerpt: However, if it becomes apparent that a complaint is without substance and, on the balance of probabilities, has been made for frivolous, malicious or vexatious reasons then the College may consider disciplinary action against the person who made the complaint;

questions.question: A student tells you they want to appeal against a misconduct panel's decision. Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, how and when must they do this?
options: In writing to the Principal (or nominee) within 10 working days of being notified in writing
In writing to the Registrar (or nominee) within 5 working days of the misconduct panel hearing
Verbally to the Deputy Vice-Principal within 20 working days of receiving notice of the decision
Directly to the OIA, in writing, within 10 working days of the misconduct panel hearing
questions.explanation: Appeals are lodged in writing to the Principal (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving written notification of the disciplinary decision, setting out the grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: A student may lodge an appeal against the decision of the misconduct panel's findings by writing to the Principal (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the written notification of the disciplinary decision, setting out the grounds for appeal;

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid ground for appeal under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure?
options: A procedural error that had a material effect upon the panel's decision
Bias on the part of the misconduct panel
The severity of the penalty was unreasonable and disproportionate
Evidence the student already had but chose not to present to the panel
questions.explanation: New evidence is a ground for appeal only if it could not have been made available to the misconduct panel at the time; procedural error, bias and a disproportionate penalty are all listed grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: The following alone shall constitute grounds for appeal: ... That new and relevant material evidence or information has emerged, which could not have been made available for consideration at the time of the misconduct panel

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, what happens once the Principal (or nominee) has decided a student's disciplinary appeal?
options: The student may lodge a second internal appeal with the Board of Directors, whose decision is then final
It is the final internal stage; the student receives a Completion of Procedures letter and may approach the OIA
The Registrar reviews the case file and then confirms or varies the appeal outcome within 10 working days
The student may appeal again to the Deputy Vice-Principal, who then issues the College's final decision
questions.explanation: The appeal is the final internal stage: the student receives a Completion of Procedures letter within 5 working days, and a dissatisfied student may then approach the OIA.
questions.source_excerpt: This appeal is the final internal stage for the College, and the student will be issued with a Completion of Procedures letter within 5 working days of the decision, presenting the outcome with reasons. ... If students remain dissatisfied with the decision they may approach the independent review body for Higher Education cases, the OIA, if they have exhausted a provider's internal procedures.

questions.question: How does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure define student misconduct?
options: Behaviour that interferes with the proper functioning of the College, or could harm individuals or its reputation
Behaviour that leads to a criminal conviction or police caution while the student is registered at the College
Behaviour in breach of assessment rules, which is dealt with under the College's separate academic regulations
Behaviour on College premises that a member of staff has reported in writing to a Registry member of staff
questions.explanation: The policy defines misconduct as behaviour that interferes with the proper functioning of the College, its activities or its people, or that has the potential to harm individuals or damage the reputation of the College or the student body.
questions.source_excerpt: Misconduct is behaviour which interferes with the proper functioning of the College and its activities, or those who work and study in the College, or which has the potential to harm individuals, or damage the reputation of the College or the student body.

questions.question: How does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure define sexual misconduct?
options: Conduct of a sexual nature, but only where it has resulted in a criminal charge or a conviction
Any conduct of a sexual nature between a student and a member of staff employed by the College
Unwanted conduct of a sexual nature, including sexual harassment, sexual assault and rape
Sexual conduct that has been reported to the police and took place on College premises or at events
questions.explanation: The policy defines sexual misconduct as unwanted conduct of a sexual nature, including but not limited to sexual harassment, sexual assault and rape.
questions.source_excerpt: sexual misconduct is defined as unwanted conduct of a sexual nature and includes, but is not limited to: Sexual harassment; Sexual assault; and Rape.

questions.question: Which of the following does the Student Code of Conduct list as an example of non-academic misconduct relating to alcohol or drugs?
options: Drinking alcohol off campus on the evening before a timetabled class the following morning
Attending classes or entering any other learning environment whilst under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Failing to tell the Registry about prescribed medication or drugs before attending timetabled classes
Declining to attend a College alcohol and drugs awareness session when a member of staff asks them to
questions.explanation: Attending classes or entering any other learning environment whilst under the influence of alcohol or drugs is listed as an example of non-academic misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: Attending classes or entering any other learning environment whilst under the influence of alcohol or drugs;

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct, what may the College be obliged to do if a student on a course leading to a professional qualification is found guilty of certain types of misconduct?
options: Refer the case to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator for an independent review
Suspend the student from all professional placements until the course ends
Report the finding to the Office for Students under its harassment and misconduct rules
Disclose the matter to the professional body concerned with that qualification
questions.explanation: For students on courses leading to a professional qualification, the College may be under an obligation to disclose certain misconduct findings to the professional body concerned.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a student on a course leading to a professional qualification is found guilty of certain types of misconduct, the College may be under an obligation to disclose the matter to the professional body concerned.

questions.question: If a student's health difficulty, disorder or disability appears to have contributed to alleged misconduct, what will the Principal do under the Student Code of Conduct?
options: Refer the case straight to a misconduct panel and ask it to reduce any penalty it decides to apply
Consult Student Support Services professionals on whether the behaviour may be managed rather than punished
Close the disciplinary case and remove every reference to the alleged misconduct from the student's file
Require the student to obtain an independent medical assessment before any penalty can be applied
questions.explanation: Where a health difficulty, disorder or disability has or is contributing to alleged misconduct, the Principal consults the appropriate Student Support Services professionals to decide whether and how the behaviour may be managed rather than punished.
questions.source_excerpt: If it appears that a student's health difficulty, disorder or disability has or is contributing to alleged misconduct, the Principal will consult with the appropriate professionals within the Student Support Services to determine whether and how the student's behaviour may be managed, rather than punished.

questions.question: At the Preliminary Enquiry stage of the Student Code of Conduct, who determines whether an incident is potentially minor or potentially serious or repetitive misconduct?
options: The staff member who first received the complaint from the student
The Serious Cases Triage Panel, before any evidence is gathered
The Registry member of staff to whom the complaint was referred
The Deputy Vice-Principal, as the chair of the misconduct panel
questions.explanation: The Registry member of staff gathers relevant evidence and determines whether the incident is potentially minor, or potentially serious or repetitive misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registry member of staff will determine whether the incident is potentially minor in nature, or whether it is an example of potentially serious or repetitive misconduct;

questions.question: According to the Student Code of Conduct, how should a temporary suspension imposed while a disciplinary hearing is pending be understood?
options: As the most serious penalty the College can apply, short of permanent dismissal
As a sanction that stays on the student's record for their studies
As a formal written warning that the misconduct panel will later confirm or remove
As a measure to protect the College community, not as a sanction or penalty
questions.explanation: Suspension in this context is not a sanction or penalty; it is imposed to protect the College community, its members or its reputation, or to allow an investigation to proceed unimpeded.
questions.source_excerpt: Suspension in this context is not a sanction or penalty but is imposed to protect the College community or members of that community, or the College's reputation, pending a criminal trial or disciplinary hearing, or to allow an investigation to be carried out unimpeded.

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, how does a student's acquittal or conviction in criminal proceedings affect the College's own procedure?
options: The College may act regardless of the outcome, as it is not bound by the prosecution
An acquittal ends the College's case, as it must follow the finding reached by the court
Only a conviction allows the College to begin disciplinary action under the procedure
The court's sentence automatically replaces any penalty the College would otherwise apply
questions.explanation: The College may act under the procedure irrespective of an acquittal or conviction and is not bound by the outcome of a criminal prosecution, although it may consider any court penalty at its discretion.
questions.source_excerpt: The College may act against a student under this procedure irrespective of the student's acquittal or conviction in criminal proceedings. LCC is not bound by the outcome of any criminal prosecution when making its own determinations under this procedure.

questions.question: Under the Minor Misconduct process of the Student Code of Conduct, when should the meeting with the student normally take place?
options: Within 5 working days of the incident being reported
Within 20 working days of the incident taking place
Within 7 working days of receiving the student's written reply
Within 10 working days of the incident being reported
questions.explanation: The Minor Misconduct meeting should normally occur within 10 working days of the incident being reported.
questions.source_excerpt: The meeting should normally occur within 10 working days of the incident being reported;

questions.question: Under the Minor Misconduct process of the Student Code of Conduct, what may happen if the student fails to attend the meeting about the alleged incident?
options: The case is escalated automatically to a misconduct panel
The allegation is dismissed as not proven on the evidence
The investigation may continue in the student's absence
The meeting must be rearranged with fresh written notice
questions.explanation: If the student fails to attend, the investigation may continue in their absence.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the student fails to attend the interview, the investigation may continue in their absence;

questions.question: When a student is told they are being investigated for serious or repeated misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct, what is the minimum period they will normally be given to supply a written reply?
options: 5 working days
10 working days
7 working days
15 working days
questions.explanation: The student may produce a written reply with supporting evidence and will normally be given a deadline of not less than 10 working days to supply it.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar will inform the student that s/he is investigating the matter, and the student may produce a written reply to the allegation of misconduct and any supporting evidence or information, including witness statements. A deadline of not less than 10 working days will normally be given to the student to supply a reply;

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, who normally chairs a misconduct panel?
options: The Deputy Vice-Principal (or nominee)
The Registrar who carried out the investigation
The Principal (or nominee)
The chair of the Serious Cases Triage Panel
questions.explanation: The Deputy Vice-Principal (or nominee) normally chairs the misconduct panel, with two other independent members of staff and a minute taker.
questions.source_excerpt: The Deputy Vice-Principal (or nominee) will normally chair the misconduct panel with two other independent members of staff, and a further minute taker to record notes of the proceedings;

questions.question: Where a misconduct panel imposes a written warning under the Student Code of Conduct, how long does the warning remain on the student's record?
options: For 12 months from the date of the panel's decision
Until the end of the current academic year only
Permanently, including after the student has left
For a period determined by the Principal
questions.explanation: The penalties section states that a written warning remains on the student's record for a period determined by the Principal.
questions.source_excerpt: A written warning to the student, to remain on their record for a period determined by the Principal

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct, what may the Principal (or nominee) do if a student's disciplinary appeal is submitted after the 10 working day deadline?
options: Forward the late appeal to the OIA, which then decides whether it can be accepted
Determine that the appeal is out of time and issue a Completion of Procedures letter
Refer the late appeal back to the original misconduct panel for it to reconsider
Extend the deadline by a further 10 working days so the grounds can be completed
questions.explanation: Where an appeal is submitted outside the 10 working day deadline, the Principal (or nominee) may determine that it is out of time and issue a Completion of Procedures letter.
questions.source_excerpt: In instances where the student has submitted his/her appeal outside of the 10 working days deadline above, the Principal (or nominee) may determine that the appeal is out of time and issue a Completion of Procedures letter;

questions.question: According to the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, what is the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA)?
options: The College's internal appeal panel chaired by the Principal
The panel that makes urgent safeguarding decisions on cases
The independent review body for Higher Education cases
The body that sets the College's student conduct rules
questions.explanation: The OIA is the independent review body for Higher Education cases, which students may approach once they have exhausted the College's internal procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: If students remain dissatisfied with the decision they may approach the independent review body for Higher Education cases, the OIA, if they have exhausted a provider's internal procedures.

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct, if the Principal (or nominee) upholds a student's disciplinary appeal, to whom may the case be referred back for consideration?
options: A freshly constituted misconduct panel
The same misconduct panel that heard it
The Serious Cases Triage Panel
The Office of the Independent Adjudicator
questions.explanation: If an appeal is upheld, one of the actions the Principal (or nominee) may take is to refer the case back to a freshly constituted misconduct panel for consideration.
questions.source_excerpt: If upheld, the Principal (or nominee) may take one or more of the following actions: ... Refer the case back to a freshly constituted misconduct panel for consideration

questions.question: During an argument, a student recklessly knocks another student's laptop off a desk and damages it, without intending to. How does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure treat this?
options: It is not misconduct, since the damage was accidental rather than intentional
It is misconduct, as damage to others' property counts if intentional or reckless
It is misconduct only where the damaged property belongs to the College itself
It is a private dispute between two students, outside the Code of Conduct
questions.explanation: Theft, damage to or defacement of the property of other members and users of the College is listed as non-academic misconduct whether caused intentionally or recklessly.
questions.source_excerpt: Theft, damage to or defacement of College property, or the property of other members and users of the College or third parties, whether caused intentionally or recklessly;

questions.question: A member of staff reasonably asks a student on College premises for their name and student number, and the student refuses to give them. How does the Student Code of Conduct treat this refusal?
options: As the student's right, since personal details need never be given to staff
As an academic offence, dealt with under the College's separate regulations
As a listed example of what might constitute non-academic misconduct
As misconduct only if the student is also suspected of another listed offence
questions.explanation: Failure to disclose a student's name, student number or other relevant details to a staff member, when it is reasonable to give them, is listed as an example of non-academic misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: A non-exhaustive list of examples of what might constitute non-academic misconduct are: ... Failure to disclose a student's name, student's number, or other relevant details to a staff member of the College, when it is reasonable that such information be given;

questions.question: A student on a course leading to a professional qualification is found guilty of misconduct so serious it might stop them completing professional placements. What may the College need to do under the Student Code of Conduct?
options: Terminate their registration on the course, or counsel them towards another path of study
Pass the case to the professional body, which then decides the College's own penalty
Postpone any penalty until the professional body decides whether to register them
Refer the finding to the OIA, which then decides whether the student may remain on the course
questions.explanation: Where an offence is so serious that it might prevent professional registration or completion of placements, the College may need to terminate the student's registration on the course or counsel them to consider another path of study.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the offence is so serious that it might prevent the student registering with the professional body or completing professional placements, it may be necessary for the College to terminate the student's registration on the course or to counsel the student to consider another path of study.

questions.question: You have had several informal conversations with a student about repeated unauthorised absences, but they have had no effect. What does the Early Intervention section of the Student Code of Conduct say happens next?
options: Staff must keep using informal means until the end of the academic year
The case is closed, as unauthorised absence is not a disciplinary matter
The student's tutor issues a formal written warning without further process
The formal procedures apply, as the informal discussions have been ineffective
questions.explanation: Staff are encouraged to address petty incidents such as unauthorised absences informally, but where such discussions are ineffective, insufficient or inappropriate the formal procedures apply.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC members of staff are encouraged to address apparently petty incidents, for instance, low-level anti-social behaviour or unauthorised absences, through informal means ... Where such discussions with students are ineffective, insufficient, or inappropriate, the formal procedures below will apply.

questions.question: A serious misconduct allegation is received. A colleague says no precautionary measure, such as a no-contact order, can be taken until the facts are proven on the balance of probabilities. Is that right under the Student Code of Conduct?
options: Yes; a misconduct panel must first uphold the allegation before any such measure
No; the SCTP can decide urgent precautionary measures on prima facie evidence
Yes; the balance of probabilities must be met before a no-contact order is made
No; precautionary measures may be imposed only after a referral to the police
questions.explanation: Serious cases are normally referred first to the Serious Cases Triage Panel, which makes urgent decisions on precautionary measures such as no-contact orders based on prima facie evidence, pending a formal investigation.
questions.source_excerpt: the case will normally be referred in the first instance to the Serious Cases Triage Panel (SCTP) to make urgent decisions that may concern safeguarding action or precautionary measures such as no-contact orders or suspension of students from campus, based on prima facie evidence, pending a formal investigation.

questions.question: Under the investigation principles of the Student Code of Conduct, in which kind of case will the College temporarily suspend a student until a determination has been reached under the procedure?
options: Where the student has missed the informal meeting held under the Minor Misconduct process
Where the student has lodged an appeal against the misconduct panel's decision
Where the alleged misconduct leads to safeguarding or related concerns for other stakeholders
Where the student has received a verbal warning for a first minor incident of misconduct
questions.explanation: Temporary suspension pending a determination occurs where the alleged misconduct is of such a nature as to lead to safeguarding or related concerns for LCC's other stakeholders, to whom the College owes a duty of care.
questions.source_excerpt: The College retains the right in some cases where appropriate to temporarily suspend a student for a period until a determination has been arrived at under this procedure. Such suspensions will occur in instances where the alleged misconduct is of such a nature as to lead to safeguarding or related concerns of LCC's other stakeholders

questions.question: While messing about, a student damages a classroom chair, which can be repaired quickly and inexpensively. No one was hurt and the student shows sincere regret. How does the Student Code of Conduct indicate this should be dealt with?
options: Through the informal process used for incidents deemed to be minor in nature
Through a misconduct panel, as any damage to College property is serious
Through referral to the Serious Cases Triage Panel for precautionary measures
Through referral to the police, as damage to property is a criminal offence
questions.explanation: An informal process is used for minor incidents, and minor misconduct includes cases where any loss or damage is minor and can be repaired quickly and inexpensively, no one has suffered and the student shows sincere regret.
questions.source_excerpt: An informal process will be used to deal with those incidents that are deemed to be minor in nature; Minor Misconduct could constitute an incident which contains one of the following elements: ... Any material loss or damage is minor and can be repaired quickly and inexpensively

questions.question: A student is being invited to a meeting under the Minor Misconduct process of the Student Code of Conduct. What minimum notice must they receive, and who may accompany them?
options: At least 5 working days' notice; a solicitor or other legal practitioner
At least 10 working days' notice; a parent, guardian or other family member
At least 7 working days' notice; any member of staff they choose to bring
At least 7 working days' notice; a fellow student or student representative
questions.explanation: The student receives a minimum of 7 working days' notice of the meeting and is reminded that they may be accompanied by a fellow student or student representative.
questions.source_excerpt: The student will receive a minimum of 7 working days' notice of the meeting and be reminded that they may be accompanied by a fellow student/ student representative;

questions.question: After a Minor Misconduct meeting, the Registrar finds that the misconduct occurred and gives the student a verbal warning. Under the Student Code of Conduct, what must accompany the warning, and when?
options: A Completion of Procedures letter, issued within 5 working days of the meeting
A written summary of the verbal warning, issued within 10 working days of it being reported
A written summary of the verbal warning, issued within 5 working days of the meeting
A misconduct panel date, given at least 7 working days before the panel sits
questions.explanation: Where minor misconduct is found, the verbal warning is accompanied by a written summary issued within 5 working days of the meeting.
questions.source_excerpt: Issue a verbal warning to the student expressing that his/her conduct is unacceptable, accompanied by a written summary of the verbal warning to be issued within 5 working days of the meeting

questions.question: A student is found in possession of illegal drugs on College premises. Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, which disciplinary route does this situation fall within?
options: Serious or Repeated Misconduct, with a misconduct panel convened
Early Intervention, with staff addressing the matter informally
Minor Misconduct, with an informal meeting led by the Registrar
The College's separate regulations for dealing with academic offences
questions.explanation: Possession of illegal drugs or substances is listed as serious or repeated misconduct, and where misconduct is serious and/or repeated a misconduct panel is convened.
questions.source_excerpt: Serious or repeated misconduct can include the following situations: ... Possession of illegal drugs or substances ... Where the alleged misconduct is serious and / or repeated, a misconduct panel will be convened

questions.question: At a misconduct panel hearing under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, who presents the evidence from the Registrar's investigation to the panel?
options: The Registrar, who then questions the student about the allegation
The complainant, supported by the witnesses who gave statements
The minute taker, reading aloud from the investigation case file
One of the panel members, before the student is invited to respond
questions.explanation: One of the panel members presents the evidence from the Registrar's investigation; the Deputy Vice-Principal then invites the student (or representative) to present their evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: The evidence from the Registrar's investigation will be presented to the panel by one of the panel members; The Deputy Vice-Principal shall then invite the student (or representative) to present any evidence or information in support of his/her case.

questions.question: After considering all the evidence in private, a misconduct panel under the Student Code of Conduct concludes that it is not more likely than not that the student committed the alleged misconduct. Which determination should the panel make?
options: Uphold the allegation in part and decide a reduced penalty
Dismiss the alleged misconduct, so no penalty is decided
Refer the case to the Serious Cases Triage Panel to decide
Adjourn until the student supplies further written evidence
questions.explanation: The standard of proof is the balance of probabilities (more likely than not); an allegation not proven to that standard is dismissed, and a penalty is decided only where an allegation is upheld.
questions.source_excerpt: the `standard of proof' to be employed during investigations shall be the `balance of probabilities' (defined as it being more likely than not that a particular event happened); ... To dismiss the alleged misconduct, because either there is no case to answer or the allegation has not been proven on the balance of probabilities

questions.question: On appeal, the Principal (or nominee) quashes a misconduct panel's decision and determines that no further action be taken. Under the Student Code of Conduct, what happens to references to the misconduct?
options: They stay on the student's file for the rest of their period of study
They stay on the student's record for a period set by the Principal
They are all removed from the student's file by the College
They are sent to the OIA, which decides whether they should be kept
questions.explanation: If the appeal is upheld and the panel's decision is quashed with no further action, any references to the misconduct are removed from the student's file.
questions.source_excerpt: Quash the decision of the misconduct panel and determine that no further action be taken. Any references to the misconduct will be removed from the student's file

questions.question: When the Principal (or nominee) considers a student's disciplinary appeal that has valid grounds, whose advice may they seek under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure?
options: Other staff members who have had no prior involvement in the case
The misconduct panel members who made the original decision on the case
The Registrar who carried out the original investigation into the allegation
The legal practitioner the student has chosen to act on their behalf
questions.explanation: Where an appeal has valid grounds, the Principal (or nominee) reviews the case file and may seek the advice of other members of staff who have not had prior involvement in the case.
questions.source_excerpt: Where the appeal has valid grounds, the Principal (or nominee) will consider the appeal, review the case file, and may seek the advice of other members of staff who have not had prior involvement in the case;

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, a student repeatedly taunts a classmate because they wrongly believe the classmate follows a particular religion; in fact the classmate does not. How is this behaviour treated?
options: It may be misconduct, as the Code covers harassment on grounds of perceived religion or for any other reason
It cannot be misconduct, because the classmate does not in fact follow the religion the student assumed
It may be misconduct, but only once the classmate makes a formal written complaint to a Registry member of staff
It may be dealt with only under the Freedom of Speech policy, since the remarks concern religious belief
questions.explanation: The Code lists harassment or bullying on grounds of a perceived characteristic, including religion, or for any other reason, so the classmate's actual beliefs do not matter.
questions.source_excerpt: Harassment or bullying in any form of any student, member of staff, Principal, director, manager, contractor, or other visitor to the College on grounds of their perceived race, nationality, gender, transgender status, disability, sexual orientation, religion, belief, age, other personal characteristic or for any other reason

questions.question: At an off-campus social evening organised and run by student representatives, a student is found carrying a knife intended for use as a weapon. How does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure treat this?
options: As outside the Code, because the event was off campus and was not organised by members of College staff
As misconduct, because the Code covers such possession at an event under the control of student representatives
As misconduct only if the knife was actually produced or used to threaten or injure another person present
As a matter solely for the police, which the College has no power to consider under its own procedure
questions.explanation: Criminal conduct, including possession of implements intended for use as weapons, is listed as misconduct on College premises or at an event under the control of the College or student representatives.
questions.source_excerpt: Conduct which constitutes a criminal offence, including possession of offensive weapons, possession of implements that are intended for use as weapons and possession of illegal substances on College premises or at an event under the control of the College or student representatives

questions.question: A misconduct complaint against a student is not upheld, but the complainant clearly raised it genuinely and in good faith. Under the Student Code of Conduct, may the College consider disciplinary action against the complainant?
options: Yes; any complaint that is not upheld is automatically treated by the College as having been made vexatiously
Yes, if the student who was complained about asks the Registrar in writing to take action against the complainant
No; that is for complaints without substance made for frivolous, malicious or vexatious reasons
No; people who make complaints are protected from any disciplinary action in all circumstances under the Code
questions.explanation: Action against a complainant may be considered only where the complaint is without substance and, on the balance of probabilities, was made for frivolous, malicious or vexatious reasons; a genuine complaint made in good faith does not meet that test.
questions.source_excerpt: if it becomes apparent that a complaint is without substance and, on the balance of probabilities, has been made for frivolous, malicious or vexatious reasons then the College may consider disciplinary action against the person who made the complaint

questions.question: As a penalty after a misconduct panel, a student is excluded from the College library for a fixed period, but keeps entering it despite reminders. How does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure treat this?
options: As no new disciplinary matter, since the student has already been penalised once for the original misconduct
As an appeal for the Principal to decide, since the student is in effect disputing the penalty imposed
As a petty incident for informal early intervention only, since entering a library harms no one directly
As further misconduct: persistent failure to comply with penalties is listed as serious or repeated misconduct
questions.explanation: Failure to comply with a previously imposed penalty is itself listed as non-academic misconduct, and persistent failure to comply with disciplinary penalties is listed among the situations that can constitute serious or repeated misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: Failure to comply with a previously imposed penalty under the disciplinary procedures. ... Persistent failure to comply with disciplinary penalties applied under this procedure ... Exclusion from a particular section of the College's premises or facilities for a fixed or indefinite period

questions.question: After consulting the Principal, an investigator suspends a disciplinary investigation because the student shows signs of mental health difficulties. A colleague says the student is therefore suspended from the College. Is that right under the Student Code of Conduct?
options: No; it is the investigation that is suspended, and the student is referred to Student Support Services
Yes; suspending the investigation on health grounds also suspends the student until they have recovered
Yes; the student is barred from campus until the Serious Cases Triage Panel has reviewed their case
No; an investigation cannot be paused for health reasons, so the case simply continues as normal
questions.explanation: The health provision allows the investigator, after consulting the Principal, to suspend the investigation and refer the student to Student Support Services; it does not suspend the student.
questions.source_excerpt: they may, after consulting with the Principal, suspend their investigation and refer the student to the College's Student Support Services

questions.question: A student tells you another student has threatened them with violence. You are inclined to have a quiet informal word with the other student rather than report it. What does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure expect?
options: An informal word first, with the formal procedure used only if a second threat is later reported by the same student
Informal means are for apparently petty incidents; this threat should be referred in writing to Registry
Informal handling of any first incident, provided the student apologises to the person they threatened
A verbal referral to the Deputy Vice-Principal, who then convenes a misconduct panel to hear the case
questions.explanation: Early intervention is for apparently petty incidents; where informal discussion is inappropriate the formal procedures apply, and a complaint must be referred in writing to a Registry member of staff.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC members of staff are encouraged to address apparently petty incidents ... Where such discussions with students are ineffective, insufficient, or inappropriate, the formal procedures below will apply. ... Any staff member receiving an initial complaint under this code should refer the matter in writing to a Registry member of staff.

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, which sequence correctly reflects the Preliminary Enquiry stage once a staff member has received an initial complaint?
options: Registry gathers witness statements; staff member confirms scope; SCTP decides minor or serious
Written referral to the Principal; minor or serious decided; evidence gathered only if a panel sits
Written referral to Registry; scope checked; evidence gathered; minor or serious decided
Verbal report to Registry; student sends a written reply; Registry then decides the complaint's scope
questions.explanation: The complaint is referred in writing to Registry, which considers whether it falls under the procedure, arranges the gathering of evidence and then determines whether it is potentially minor or serious.
questions.source_excerpt: refer the matter in writing to a Registry member of staff. The Registry member of staff will consider whether the complaint falls under this procedure; ... the Registry Member of Staff will arrange for the gathering of any relevant evidence, including statements from witnesses. The Registry member of staff will determine whether the incident is potentially minor in nature

questions.question: A student has been charged with a criminal offence against another student and the trial is pending. Under the Student Code of Conduct, which approach is open to the College in the meantime?
options: Begin its own investigation at once, but take no protective steps until the trial has ended
Take no action of any kind, including protective steps, until the trial has concluded and the court has reached its verdict
Hold a misconduct panel now and apply a penalty, which the court must then take into account
Await the outcome before investigating, while it may suspend the student to protect the community
questions.explanation: LCC awaits the outcome of ongoing criminal proceedings before starting its own investigation, but it may impose a suspension, which is not a penalty, to protect the College community pending a criminal trial.
questions.source_excerpt: Suspension in this context is not a sanction or penalty but is imposed to protect the College community or members of that community, or the College's reputation, pending a criminal trial or disciplinary hearing ... In instances where criminal proceedings against a student are ongoing, LCC will await the outcome of those proceedings before commencing its own investigation

questions.question: A student facing a misconduct panel under the Student Code of Conduct asks to be represented by a friend who graduated from LCC last year and is not a lawyer. What does the policy provide?
options: The friend may attend, as any former LCC student may represent a current student at a panel
The friend does not qualify: the right is to a representative from within the current LCC student body
The friend does not qualify, as only a member of College staff may represent a student at a panel
The friend may attend, as only legal practitioners are excluded from representing students
questions.explanation: Students may be represented by a fellow LCC student, and before a misconduct panel they are reminded of their right to a representative from within the current LCC student body, so a graduate does not qualify.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are entitled to be represented by one of their fellow LCC students in meetings or hearings. ... The student shall be reminded of their right to be a representative from within the current LCC student body.

questions.question: In an exceptional disciplinary case, following the standard steps of the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure would be unfair to the student. What does the policy allow the College to do?
options: Vary the procedure it follows at any stage, in the interests of fairness
Vary the procedure, but only before a misconduct panel has been convened
Vary the procedure, but only with the student's written consent to each change
Pass the case to the OIA, which then sets a bespoke procedure for the College
questions.explanation: In exceptional cases the College reserves the right to vary its procedure at any stage in the interests of fairness; no consent or stage limit is set.
questions.source_excerpt: In exceptional cases, the College reserves the right to vary the procedure it follows at any stage in the interests of fairness.

questions.question: A minor misconduct incident is reported. To hold the meeting within the normal timeframe in the Student Code of Conduct while still giving the student the minimum notice required, what is the latest point by which the invitation should be sent?
options: 3 working days after the incident is reported
5 working days after the incident is reported
7 working days after the incident is reported
10 working days after the incident is reported
questions.explanation: The meeting should normally occur within 10 working days of the report and the student must receive at least 7 working days' notice, so the invitation must go out within 3 working days.
questions.source_excerpt: The meeting should normally occur within 10 working days of the incident being reported; ... The student will receive a minimum of 7 working days' notice of the meeting

questions.question: A student who received a verbal warning under the Minor Misconduct process of the Student Code of Conduct then repeats the same misconduct. The new incident is itself minor in nature. Which route does the policy indicate?
options: A second informal meeting with the Registrar, as each minor incident is judged separately on its own merits
Early intervention by the student's tutor, as informal means should always be tried again first
A formal written warning from the Registrar, issued without any further meeting or procedure
The Serious or Repeated Misconduct procedure, as the student was told any repetition would invoke it
questions.explanation: Students warned under the minor process are told any repetition will invoke the Serious or Repeated Misconduct procedure, and repeated misconduct despite warnings is listed as serious or repeated misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: Inform the student that any repetition of the misconduct incident will result in the Serious or Repeated Misconduct procedure below being invoked ... Previous misconduct has been repeated despite warnings

questions.question: A student tampers with a fire alarm on College premises; nobody is hurt. A colleague says it cannot be serious misconduct because no one was harmed. Under the Student Code of Conduct, why is the colleague wrong?
options: Any incident involving College property is automatically treated as serious misconduct by Registry
Seriousness depends on whether the student shows regret, not on whether anyone was actually harmed
Serious misconduct includes cases where someone could have been harmed, and Health and Safety breaches
All fire safety incidents are first referred to the police, who then decide how serious the matter is under the Code
questions.explanation: The serious or repeated misconduct list includes situations where another person could have been harmed and breaches of Health and Safety regulations, so actual harm is not required.
questions.source_excerpt: Another person has been harmed or could have been harmed due to the alleged conduct; Breach of Health and Safety regulations

questions.question: Which sequence matches a misconduct panel hearing under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure?
options: Student presents their case; Registrar presents evidence; panel decides in private; Principal sets penalty
Panel member presents evidence; student presents their case; panel decides in private; penalty set if upheld
Panel member presents evidence; panel decides in private; student then responds; penalty set if upheld
Registrar presents evidence; panel sets a penalty; student presents their case; panel confirms it in public
questions.explanation: A panel member presents the Registrar's evidence, the student is then invited to present their case, the panel convenes in private to decide, and only if the allegation is upheld does it decide the penalty.
questions.source_excerpt: The evidence from the Registrar's investigation will be presented to the panel by one of the panel members; The Deputy Vice-Principal shall then invite the student (or representative) to present any evidence ... the panel will convene in private ... Where the allegation(s) has been partly or fully upheld, the panel will further decide about the penalty to be applied

questions.question: Under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, at which points may circumstances presented by the student be taken into account when a disciplinary penalty is being set?
options: By the SCTP when triaging the case, and by the Registrar when drafting the Completion of Procedures letter
Only by the OIA, once the student has exhausted all of the College's internal procedures and appeals
By the panel when deciding whether to uphold, but never by the Principal at the appeal stage
By the panel when deciding the penalty, and by the Principal if varying it on appeal
questions.explanation: The panel may consider circumstances presented by the student when deciding the penalty, and the Principal (or nominee) may take account of mitigating circumstances if varying the penalty on appeal.
questions.source_excerpt: the panel will further decide about the penalty to be applied; In so doing, the panel may take into consideration any circumstances presented by the student. ... Accounts may be taken by the Principal (or nominee) of any mitigating circumstances which have been presented by the student if varying the penalty to be applied

questions.question: Before a hearing, a student is told not to visit a particular College building. After the panel upholds the allegation, the student is excluded from that building for a fixed period. How does the Student Code of Conduct classify these two measures?
options: Both are penalties, so time under the first counts towards the second
Both are precautionary measures that lapse once any appeal is decided
The first is a protective measure, not a penalty; the second is a penalty
The first is a penalty set by the SCTP; the second is an appeal outcome
questions.explanation: Suspension and lesser actions such as not visiting a building are protective measures pending a hearing, not penalties, whereas exclusion from part of the premises is a listed penalty after an allegation is upheld.
questions.source_excerpt: Suspension in this context is not a sanction or penalty but is imposed to protect the College community ... The College may impose other actions short of suspension, such as a requirement that a student does not visit a particular campus or building ... Exclusion from a particular section of the College's premises or facilities for a fixed or indefinite period

questions.question: During a College event, a student deliberately damages equipment belonging to a visiting contractor. If a misconduct panel upholds the allegation, what does the Student Code of Conduct allow it to require regarding the cost?
options: That the student make good the cost, in full or in part, even though the property is a third party's
Nothing, as making good the cost applies only to damage to property owned by the College itself
That the student pay the full cost, as partial payment is not available among the penalties listed in the Code
That the contractor recover the cost through the OIA rather than through the College's procedure
questions.explanation: The penalties include a requirement to make good the cost, in full or in part, of damage or loss to property, whether it belongs to the College or a third party.
questions.source_excerpt: A requirement to make good the cost (in full or in part) of any damage or loss caused to property, whether that of the College or a third party

questions.question: A student lodges a disciplinary appeal in time, but it only says they disagree with the panel and would like a second chance; none of the listed grounds is shown. Under the Student Code of Conduct, what will the Principal (or nominee) do?
options: Review the case file and seek advice from staff with no prior involvement first
Refer the case to a freshly constituted misconduct panel for a full rehearing
Dismiss the appeal and issue the student a Completion of Procedures letter
Forward the appeal to the OIA, as it cannot then be considered by the College
questions.explanation: Where none of the grounds for appeal is met, the appeal is dismissed and a Completion of Procedures letter is issued; reviewing the file and seeking advice applies only to appeals with valid grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: Decide that none of the grounds for appeal have been met. In this instance the appeal will be dismissed, and a Completion of Procedures letter issued to the student

questions.question: A student receives written notification of a misconduct panel's decision 6 working days after the hearing, then lodges a written appeal with the Principal 8 working days after receiving it. Under the Student Code of Conduct, is the appeal in time?
options: No; the 10 working days ran from the date on which the misconduct panel hearing was held
Yes; the 10 working days run from receipt of the written notification of the decision
No; an appeal must be lodged within 5 working days of receiving the written decision
Yes; there is no deadline, provided that the appeal sets out one of the valid grounds
questions.explanation: The 10 working day appeal period runs from receipt of the written notification of the decision, so an appeal 8 working days after receipt is in time even though 14 have passed since the hearing.
questions.source_excerpt: A student may lodge an appeal against the decision of the misconduct panel's findings by writing to the Principal (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the written notification of the disciplinary decision

questions.question: Unhappy with a misconduct panel's decision, a student wants to take the matter straight to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA) without appealing within the College. What does the Student Code of Conduct say?
options: The student may go straight to the OIA, which reviews panel decisions in place of the Principal
The student may go straight to the OIA, provided they apply within 10 working days of the decision
The Deputy Vice-Principal refers the panel's decision to the OIA on the student's behalf on request
The OIA may be approached once the College's internal procedures, including the appeal, are exhausted
questions.explanation: Students may approach the OIA only if they have exhausted the provider's internal procedures, and the appeal to the Principal is the College's final internal stage.
questions.source_excerpt: This appeal is the final internal stage for the College ... If students remain dissatisfied with the decision they may approach the independent review body for Higher Education cases, the OIA, if they have exhausted a provider's internal procedures.

questions.question: For a serious misconduct allegation, the Registrar's letter gives the student 6 working days to send a written reply and sets the Misconduct Panel, with its location and members, for 12 working days after the letter. Under the Student Code of Conduct, which statement is correct?
options: The panel timing breaches the procedure, which requires at least 15 working days' notice of a panel
Both timescales comply, as the student has at least 5 working days' notice for each of the steps
Both timescales breach it, as each must be at least 14 working days from the date of the letter
The reply deadline is too short, as a student is normally given not less than 10 working days
questions.explanation: A student will normally be given not less than 10 working days to reply, so 6 is too short, whereas panel details need only be provided at least 7 working days before the panel, which 12 days satisfies.
questions.source_excerpt: A deadline of not less than 10 working days will normally be given to the student to supply a reply; The letter will include information about the convening of a Misconduct Panel to investigate the alleged misconduct, which the student is required to attend, with information provided about the location and attendance of panel members at least 7 working days before the panel is held.

questions.question: After a Minor Misconduct meeting, the Registrar finds the misconduct occurred and feels a verbal warning alone is not enough. Without a misconduct panel, which further step does the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure allow the Registrar to take?
options: Impose a fine on the student proportionate to the misconduct
Issue a formal written warning within 5 working days of the meeting
Exclude the student from part of the College premises for a fixed period
Require a written apology to everyone affected by the student's actions
questions.explanation: Where minor misconduct is found, the Registrar gives a verbal warning with a written summary and, if appropriate, a formal written warning within 5 working days; fines, exclusion and apologies are listed as penalties for serious or repeated misconduct.
questions.source_excerpt: After the investigation, if the Registrar finds based on the evidence that the minor misconduct has occurred, s/he shall: ... If appropriate, issue a formal written warning to the student within 5 working days of the meeting ... The range of penalties for serious or repeated misconduct include but are not limited to:

questions.question: A student submits an assignment late, saying they emailed you a question on Saturday evening and you did not reply until Monday. What does the Student Email Using Policy say about this?
options: Staff need not reply outside working hours, and an unanswered email does not excuse a late submission
The student should be granted an extension, because staff must reply to any query before the assignment deadline
Staff must reply to student emails within 24 hours, including weekends and holidays, so the delay excuses the late work
The case goes to the IT Department to confirm the send time, and the late penalty is waived if it predates the deadline
questions.explanation: Section 4.4 says staff are not required or expected to answer student emails outside their regular working hours, and an unanswered email to a lecturer does not excuse a student from turning in an assignment.
questions.source_excerpt: There will be no requirement or expectation for staff to answer student emails outside their regular working hours, although they may choose to do so. For example, an unanswered email to a lecturer would not excuse a student from turning in an assignment.

questions.question: A student asks you, as their lecturer, to send all course updates to their personal Gmail address rather than their College account. How does the Student Email Using Policy view this?
options: It is acceptable if the student confirms the request in writing and their tutor records the address on file
It breaches the policy, as students are expected not to use private email for course-related communications
It is acceptable provided the IT Department is copied into each email and the Gmail account is password protected
It is acceptable because email is the College's primary method of communication, whichever account is used
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.1 states students are expected not to use their private email address for College and course-related communications, so the College account should be used.
questions.source_excerpt: Students must use the email in accordance with this policy and are expected not to: 3.8.1. Use their private email address for the College and course-related communications.

questions.question: A student who completed their course last month asks how long they can keep accessing their College email. According to the Student Email Using Policy's access table, what should you tell them?
options: Access ended on the day the course was completed, so emails and documents can no longer be backed up
Access continues for 12 months after course completion, after which the account is closed without notice
Access continues indefinitely, as the account converts to a permanent alumni account on completion
Access continues for 3 months after course completion, and they can back up their emails and documents
questions.explanation: The section 6 table gives completed students access for the study period plus 3 months after course completion, and the note confirms they can back up emails and electronic documents.
questions.source_excerpt: Study period + 3 Months after course completed ... Student can back-up any email or electronic documents after course completion.

questions.question: Under the Student Email Using Policy, how are students' breaches of the email rules dealt with?
options: Through the Academic Appeals Procedure, managed by the Registry team
Through an informal IT Department warning, with no further action taken
Through the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Action Procedure
Through the Staff Disciplinary Procedure, as email is a College system
questions.explanation: Section 3.10 states that failure to comply is a breach of acceptable use and students face consequences under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Action Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Failure to comply with the above email using conditions will be considered as a breach of acceptable use. Students will face consequences of misuse according to the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Action Procedure.

questions.question: You discover that a student has emailed their completed individual coursework to several classmates. How does the Student Email Using Policy treat this?
options: It is allowed, as students may email each other to collaborate on group projects and classes
It is a breach, as students are expected not to send emails sharing assignments or course works
It is a breach if the email was sent or read during a lecture session, and allowed otherwise
It is a breach if the coursework was sent from a private address, and allowed from a College account
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.7 states students are expected not to send emails to share assignments or course works or to promote cheating; the group-project collaboration allowed by section 4.3 does not cover sharing individual coursework.
questions.source_excerpt: Students must use the email in accordance with this policy and are expected not to: ... 3.8.7. Send emails to share assignments/course works or promote cheating in any form.

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, who is responsible for the security of a student's mailbox and for all activities that occur within the account?
options: The student, who must not disclose or share their password with others
The IT Department, as it is responsible for maintaining the email system
Google, as the provider of the G-Suite services the account is part of
The student's lecturer, who sends course content and reminders by email
questions.explanation: Section 3.3 makes students responsible for the security of their own mailboxes and solely responsible for all activity in the account; they must not share their passwords.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are responsible for the security of their mailboxes and must not disclose or share their passwords with others. They are solely responsible for all activities that occur within the email account.

questions.question: A student with a disability tells you they find it difficult to use email as a method of communication. Under the Student Email Using Policy, who should they contact for advice and support?
options: The IT Department
The Learning Resources Centre
The Registry team
The Quality Assurance team
questions.explanation: Section 3.9 directs students with a disability who find email difficult to contact the Registry team for advice and support.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with disability who may find it difficult to use email as a method of communication should contact the Registry team for advice and support.

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, what makes a strong password for a student email account?
options: At least six characters mixing letters and numbers, changed by the student at the start of every academic term
At least eight characters, based on memorable personal information such as a birthday so it can be recalled easily
At least ten characters made up of letters only, avoiding symbols and numbers as they are harder to remember
At least eight characters mixing capital and lower-case letters, symbols and numbers, without personal information
questions.explanation: Section 5.2.1 requires strong passwords of at least eight characters using capital and lower-case letters, symbols and numbers, without personal information such as birthdays.
questions.source_excerpt: Select strong passwords with at least eight characters (capital and lower-case letters, symbols and numbers) without using personal information (e.g. birthdays);

questions.question: Under the Student Email Using Policy, what are students required to do with their College email account?
options: Check it whenever a lecturer tells them a new message is waiting
Forward all messages to a personal address they check more often
Access and regularly check it for information and updates
Check it once per term when their attendance record is reviewed
questions.explanation: Section 3.7 says the College email account is essential for communication, so students must access and regularly check it for information and updates.
questions.source_excerpt: The College email account is essential for communication. Therefore, students must access and regularly check their email accounts for information and updates.

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, what right does the College reserve over student email accounts?
options: To provide access to, or restrict access to, any email account at any time
To restrict access once a disciplinary hearing has concluded, but not before
To restrict access provided the student has first given written agreement
To restrict access after course completion, but not while a student is enrolled
questions.explanation: Section 6.1 states that the College reserves all rights to provide or restrict access to any email account at any time.
questions.source_excerpt: The College reserves all rights to provide access or restrict access to any email account at any time.

questions.question: What does the Student Email Using Policy say about informing students that their email account will be suspended or deleted?
options: Students are informed after their account has been permanently deleted
No notice is given, as the College reserves all rights over accounts
Students are informed if they ask the IT Department directly, not otherwise
Students will be notified before the account is suspended and deleted
questions.explanation: The note to the account access table in section 6 states that students will be notified before email account suspension and deletion.
questions.source_excerpt: Student will be notified before the email account suspension and deletion.

questions.question: Under the Student Email Using Policy, what does all student email pass through so that it can be checked for malware?
options: An on-site antivirus server run by the College
Google Message Security (GMS) at the email gateways
Microsoft Defender filtering for Office 365 accounts
A manual review of messages by the IT Department
questions.explanation: Section 7.1 explains that email is checked for malware at the email gateways, and all student email passes through Google Message Security (GMS).
questions.source_excerpt: All email communication through email gateways is checked for malware via the following strategies: ... All student email will pass through Google Message Security (GMS);

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, who is entitled to use the College's email facilities?
options: Only authorised users of the College computer system
Any student or visitor holding a valid College library card
Anyone with a Google account, whether College-issued or not
Enrolled students and any family member they nominate
questions.explanation: Section 2.1 states that only authorised users of the College computer system are entitled to use email facilities.
questions.source_excerpt: Only authorised users of the College computer system are entitled to use email facilities.
