questions.question: Under the Student Email Using Policy, what is the primary method of communication between the College and its students?
options: Text messages sent to the student's registered mobile number
Email, to the account the College supplies to each student
Email to a personal address the student gives at enrolment
Announcements on the College's virtual learning environment
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 states that email is the primary method of communication between the College and students, and the College supplies all students with an email account.
questions.source_excerpt: Email is the primary method of communication between the College and Students. The College supplies all students with an email account when they enroll in a course.

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, at what point does the College supply a student with an email account?
options: When they pass their first module assessment
When they request one from the Registry team
When they enrol in a course at the College
When they complete their first week of induction
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 says the College supplies all students with an email account when they enrol in a course.
questions.source_excerpt: The College supplies all students with an email account when they enroll in a course.

questions.question: Under the Student Email Using Policy, which College guidance covers how students access and use email services?
options: The Student Handbook issued at induction week
The Registry team's enrolment and welcome pack
The Staff IT Acceptable Use Policy annexes
The Learning Resources Centre and IT Using Guide
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 states that the College's Learning Resources Centre and IT Using Guide covers how to access and use email services.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has a Learning Resources Centre and IT Using Guide, which covers `how to access and use email services to guide students' information about email services.

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, which team is responsible for maintaining the student email system?
options: The IT Department
The Registry team
The Learning Resources Centre
The Quality Assurance team
questions.explanation: Section 3.6 states that the IT Department is responsible for maintaining the email system.
questions.source_excerpt: The IT Department is responsible maintaining the email system.

questions.question: The Student Email Using Policy gives which example of an inappropriate time for a student to send or read email?
options: Late in the evening, after 9pm on weekdays
While they are attending lecture sessions
At weekends and on public bank holidays
During scheduled exam revision periods
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.5 says students are expected not to send or read email at inappropriate times, such as during lecture sessions.
questions.source_excerpt: Send or read email at inappropriate times, such as during lecture sessions.

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, what kind of websites and services are students expected not to sign up for?
options: Any website or service not run by the College itself
Social media platforms and online shopping websites
Illegal, unreliable, disreputable or suspect ones
Services that charge a subscription or membership fee
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.9 states that students are expected not to sign up for illegal, unreliable, disreputable or suspect websites and services.
questions.source_excerpt: Sign up for illegal, unreliable, disreputable, or suspect websites and services.

questions.question: Under the Student Email Using Policy, what do lecturers, support staff and the administrative team send emails to students to communicate?
options: Only formal disciplinary notices and final assessment results
Only urgent matters that cannot wait until the next class
Marketing for other courses and approved third-party offers
Reminders, course content, questions and important information
questions.explanation: Section 4.1 says staff email students to communicate reminders, course content, course-related questions and important information.
questions.source_excerpt: Lecturers, support staff and the administrative team send emails to students to communicate reminders, course content, pose questions related to course and important information;

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, for what purpose may students send emails to other students?
options: To collaborate on group projects and assist with classes
To advertise private services and events to all students
Only to arrange social events outside College hours
To share finished individual assignments for comparison
questions.explanation: Section 4.3 states that students may email other students to collaborate on group projects and assist with classes.
questions.source_excerpt: Students may send email to other students to collaborate on group projects and assist with school classes;

questions.question: Under the Student Email Using Policy, when should students avoid opening attachments and clicking on links?
options: When the email arrives outside normal College working hours
When the content of the email is not adequately explained
When the attachment is larger than the mailbox size limit
When the message is sent from another student's account
questions.explanation: Section 5.2.4 tells students to avoid opening attachments and clicking on links when the content is not adequately explained.
questions.source_excerpt: Avoid opening attachments and clicking on links when content is not adequately explained;

questions.question: What does the Student Email Using Policy tell students to check when they receive email from unknown senders?
options: Their location, by asking the IT Department to trace it
Their enrolment, by contacting the Registry team
Their email and name, to ensure they are legitimate
Their social media profiles, before sending a reply
questions.explanation: Section 5.2.5 tells students to check the email and names of unknown senders to ensure they are legitimate.
questions.source_excerpt: Check email and names of unknown senders to ensure they are legitimate.

questions.question: According to the account access table in the Student Email Using Policy, when does an enrolled (active) student have email account access?
options: For their first academic year of study only
Only during scheduled teaching weeks of each term
Only from the end of their first term onwards
During their study period at the College
questions.explanation: The section 6 table shows that an enrolled (active) student has account access during the study period.
questions.source_excerpt: Enrolled ... Account access During the study period

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy's account access table, once a student has been notified and their account suspended, after what period would the account be permanently deleted?
options: After a 3-month period
After a 6-month period
After a 12-month period
After a 30-day period
questions.explanation: The section 6 table states that the account would be permanently deleted after a 6-month period, with the student notified beforehand.
questions.source_excerpt: Student will be notified, before the account is suspended. The account would be permanently deleted after a 6-months period

questions.question: Under the Student Email Using Policy, what does GMS Policy-Based TLS Encryption provide for student email?
options: Automatic password resets for locked student accounts
Encryption of files saved on the student's own device
Blocking of messages sent from private email addresses
Server-to-server encryption of messages and attachments
questions.explanation: Section 7.1.3 states that GMS Policy-Based TLS Encryption provides server-to-server encryption of messages and attachments.
questions.source_excerpt: GMS Policy-Based TLS Encryption, providing server-to-server encryption of messages and attachments;

questions.question: A student asks whether the Student Email Using Policy is ever updated. Based on the policy's stated aim, what should you tell them?
options: It stays unchanged until Google changes the terms of its G-Suite services
It is reviewed only after a formal complaint from a student or member of staff
It is periodically reviewed and, if necessary, amended within a stipulated timeframe
It is reviewed once at the start of each academic year by the student council
questions.explanation: Section 1.2 says the policy is accompanied by a periodic review and, if necessary, amendment within a stipulated timeframe, which is considered crucial for developing the system.
questions.source_excerpt: Accompanied by a periodic review of the policy and, if necessary, amendment within a stipulated timeframe, which is considered crucial for further development of the system.

questions.question: An offensive email was sent from a student's College account. The student says their flatmate, who knew the password, sent it. Under the Student Email Using Policy, where does responsibility lie?
options: With the flatmate alone, since the student did not write or send the message
With the student, who is solely responsible for all activity in their email account
With the IT Department, since it is responsible for maintaining the email system
With nobody, until the IT Department confirms which device the message came from
questions.explanation: Section 3.3 makes students solely responsible for all activity in their email account and forbids them from disclosing or sharing their passwords, so the student remains responsible.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are responsible for the security of their mailboxes and must not disclose or share their passwords with others. They are solely responsible for all activities that occur within the email account.

questions.question: A student who breached the Student Email Using Policy says nobody explained what appropriate use of email meant. What does the policy say about the duty of every email user?
options: Each user must practise appropriate use and understand their own responsibilities
Each user must follow only the rules a lecturer has explained to them in person
Each user becomes responsible only after signing an IT induction attendance sheet
Each user may rely on the IT Department to decide what counts as appropriate use
questions.explanation: Section 3.5 places a duty on every email user to practise appropriate use and to understand their responsibilities, and section 3.4 requires compliance with College policy without exception.
questions.source_excerpt: email facilities by individuals at London Churchill College must always comply with the stipulated College policy without exception. ... Every user of email systems has a duty to ensure they practice appropriate use and must understand their responsibilities in this regard.

questions.question: A student emails several classmates a message insulting another student because of their religious beliefs. How should this be viewed under the Student Email Using Policy?
options: As acceptable, since students may email each other to collaborate and assist with classes
As a breach only if the student who was insulted makes a formal written complaint
As a matter for the IT Department to settle informally by deleting the message
As a breach of acceptable use, with consequences under the Student Code of Conduct
questions.explanation: Section 3.8 expects students not to send insulting or discriminatory messages, and section 3.10 treats non-compliance as a breach of acceptable use dealt with under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Action Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Send insulting or discriminatory messages and content. ... Failure to comply with the above email using conditions will be considered as a breach of acceptable use. Students will face consequences of misuse according to the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Action Procedure.

questions.question: A student argues that the Student Email Using Policy only stops spam emails with malicious content being sent to people inside the College. Is the student right?
options: Yes, emails to external users fall under the email provider's terms, not the policy
Yes, provided the spam is sent from the College account and not a private address
No, the rule covers email users both within and outside the college facility
No, the rule applies only to users outside the College, not to internal users
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.4 expects students not to create or send spam containing a virus or other malicious content to email users within or outside the college facility.
questions.source_excerpt: Create or send spam emails containing a virus or other malicious content to other email users within or outside the college facility.

questions.question: A student who is off sick asks a classmate to log in to her College email account and read out any messages from lecturers. Under the Student Email Using Policy, what is the position?
options: It is allowed, provided the absent student has given her permission first
It is allowed, provided the messages read out relate only to course content
It is not allowed, as students must not use the account of another person
It is allowed, provided the classmate logs out again straight afterwards
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.8 expects students not to use the account of another person, and section 3.3 forbids students from sharing their passwords, so permission does not make it acceptable.
questions.source_excerpt: must not disclose or share their passwords with others. ... 3.8.8. Use the account of another person.

questions.question: For a group project, a student emails their team an unauthorised scanned copy of a copyrighted textbook. How does the Student Email Using Policy treat this?
options: As allowed, as students may email each other to collaborate on group projects
As allowed, if the textbook is on the reading list and is used only by the group
As a breach only if the scanned copy is also sent to people outside the College
As a breach, as students must not share material that infringes copyright
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.11 expects students not to share any material that infringes copyright or intellectual property rights; the group-project collaboration in section 4.3 does not override this.
questions.source_excerpt: Share any material that infringes the copyright of individuals or organisations including intellectual property rights.

questions.question: A student asks whether they can email the College administration team with a query that is not about their classes. What does the Student Email Using Policy say?
options: Yes, students may email lecturers, support staff or administration with other queries
No, students may contact the administration team only through their personal tutor
No, students may email only their lecturers, and only with questions about classes
Yes, but only from a private address, as the College account is kept for coursework
questions.explanation: Section 4.2 allows students to email their lecturers, support team members or administration with questions or comments regarding class or other queries.
questions.source_excerpt: Students may send emails to their lecturers, support team member or administration with questions or comments regarding class or other queries;

questions.question: A new lecturer believes the Student Email Using Policy forbids staff from replying to student emails in the evening. Which statement reflects the policy?
options: Staff must reply to evening emails by 9am on the next working day
Staff are not required or expected to reply, but may choose to do so
Staff may reply in the evening only with their line manager's approval
Staff are forbidden to reply outside their regular working hours
questions.explanation: Section 4.4 says there is no requirement or expectation for staff to answer student emails outside their regular working hours, although they may choose to do so.
questions.source_excerpt: There will be no requirement or expectation for staff to answer student emails outside their regular working hours, although they may choose to do so.

questions.question: According to the Student Email Using Policy, why does email security matter to the College as well as to individual students?
options: Email-borne attacks and breaches can compromise its reputation, legality and equipment
Any breach would cancel the College's G-Suite licence and close every student account
Google fines the College for each virus that passes through its email gateways
Insecure accounts slow the College network and delay the delivery of lecture content
questions.explanation: Section 5.1 explains that emails are often the medium of hacker attacks, confidentiality breaches and malware, which can compromise the College's reputation, legality and security of equipment.
questions.source_excerpt: Emails are often the medium of hacker attacks, confidentiality breaches, viruses and other malware. These issues can compromise the College's reputation, legality, and security of equipment.

questions.question: A student asks you which of these passwords would meet the Student Email Using Policy's rules for a strong password. Which one should you point to?
options: Tk7#p9 (six characters: capitals, lower case, a symbol and numbers)
kt7#prw29! (ten characters: lower case, symbols and numbers only)
Sam!15Jun01 (the student's name and birthday, with capitals, a symbol and numbers)
Kt7#pRw2q! (ten characters: capitals, lower case, symbols and numbers)
questions.explanation: Section 5.2.1 requires at least eight characters combining capital and lower-case letters, symbols and numbers, without personal information such as birthdays; only Kt7#pRw2q! meets every condition.
questions.source_excerpt: Select strong passwords with at least eight characters (capital and lower-case letters, symbols and numbers) without using personal information (e.g. birthdays);

questions.question: A student has set a strong College email password and written it on a note kept inside their laptop case. What does the Student Email Using Policy say?
options: It is acceptable, as the password already meets the eight-character strength rule
It is acceptable, provided the note never leaves the student's own laptop case
Passwords should be remembered instead of written down, and kept secret
Passwords may be written down, provided the note does not name the account
questions.explanation: Section 5.2.2 asks students to remember their passwords instead of writing them down, and to keep them secret.
questions.source_excerpt: Remember passwords instead of writing them down and keep them secret;

questions.question: A student gets an email from an unfamiliar address claiming to be from IT, with an unexplained link to 'verify your account'. What does the Student Email Using Policy expect them to do?
options: Click the link promptly, as the IT Department is responsible for the email system
Check the sender is legitimate and avoid clicking a link that is not explained
Open the link only on a College computer, where GMS will block any malware it carries
Reply asking for more detail, then click the link if the sender answers within a day
questions.explanation: Sections 5.2.4 and 5.2.5 tell students to avoid clicking links when content is not adequately explained and to check the email and names of unknown senders to ensure they are legitimate.
questions.source_excerpt: Avoid opening attachments and clicking on links when content is not adequately explained; ... Check email and names of unknown senders to ensure they are legitimate.

questions.question: Under the account access table in the Student Email Using Policy, what happens to the email account of a student who moves to an inactive status other than course completion?
options: It keeps full access until the end of the academic year in which the status changed
It is deleted at once and without notice, as the College reserves all rights
It is transferred to a personal address the student nominates to the Registry team
It enters a suspension period, and the student is notified before it is suspended
questions.explanation: The section 6 table gives any other inactive status a suspension period, and the student will be notified before the account is suspended.
questions.source_excerpt: 3 Any other Inactive Status. ... Suspension period ... Student will be notified, before the account is suspended.

questions.question: A colleague assumes Google Message Security only screens email coming into student accounts. According to the Student Email Using Policy, what cover does GMS provide?
options: Inbound cover only, with outgoing mail checked by the IT Department
Outbound cover only, as inbound mail is screened by each student
Both inbound and outbound cover, with protection from spam viruses
Inbound cover for staff accounts and outbound cover for students
questions.explanation: Section 7.1.2 states that Google Message Security provides highly effective inbound and outbound cover with protection from spam viruses.
questions.source_excerpt: Google Message Security provides highly effective inbound and outbound cover with protection from spam viruses;

questions.question: The IT Department wants a GMS setting to apply only to one course group's student accounts. According to the Student Email Using Policy's description of GMS, is this possible?
options: Yes, settings may be set for the entire domain, groups of users, or individually
No, GMS settings can only be applied to the whole College domain at the same time
No, GMS settings can only be applied to one individual account at a time
Yes, but only after every student in the group has given written consent
questions.explanation: Section 7.1.4 states that GMS settings may be set for the entire domain, for groups of users, or individually.
questions.source_excerpt: GMS aliases and distribution lists. Settings to manage sensitive and actions may be set for the entire domain, groups of users, or individually;

questions.question: During the summer break, a student sends offensive messages from their College email account and argues that the Student Email Using Policy does not apply outside term time. How should staff view this?
options: The policy still applies, as use of College email facilities must always comply with College policy without exception
The student is right, as the policy applies only during the scheduled teaching weeks of the study period
The student is right, unless the messages were sent to College staff rather than to friends outside the College
The policy applies, but breaches outside term are settled by the IT Department instead of the Code of Conduct
questions.explanation: Section 3.4 requires use of email facilities to comply with College policy always and without exception, and section 3.8.2 expects students not to send offensive email, so there is no term-time exemption.
questions.source_excerpt: email facilities by individuals at London Churchill College must always comply with the stipulated College policy without exception. ... Create or send harassing, offensive email messages

questions.question: A student forwards to classmates an email written by someone else that makes false and damaging claims about a named lecturer. The student says they only forwarded it. How does the Student Email Using Policy treat this?
options: As acceptable, as the rule covers only defamatory material that the student has written personally
As a breach, as students are expected not to transmit any illegal or defamatory materials
As acceptable, provided the email was forwarded only to students within the College
As a breach only if the lecturer reports it to the IT Department within 24 hours
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.3 expects students not to transmit any illegal or defamatory materials; forwarding is transmitting, whoever wrote the original message.
questions.source_excerpt: Transmit any illegal or defamatory materials.

questions.question: A student emails classmates content urging them to shut supporters of a particular political party out of study groups, claiming political views are not protected by the Student Email Using Policy. Is the student right?
options: Yes, the discrimination rule lists race, gender and disability, but it does not list political beliefs
No, the policy bars any email that mentions politics or religion, whatever its content
Yes, the rule covers religious beliefs only, as political views are a matter of opinion
No, political beliefs are a listed ground on which email content must not encourage discrimination
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.2 expects students not to send content that encourages discrimination on grounds including political or religious beliefs; it does not ban every mention of politics or religion.
questions.source_excerpt: Create or send harassing, offensive email messages or content that encourages discrimination on grounds of race, gender, sexual orientation, disability, political or religious beliefs.

questions.question: A student emails their cohort a link to a service that writes assessed essays for payment, urging classmates to use it. No assignment is attached. How does the Student Email Using Policy treat this?
options: As a breach, as students are expected not to send emails that promote cheating in any form
As acceptable, as the rule covers only emails that attach or share actual assignments or course works
As acceptable, as students may email each other to assist one another with classes
As a breach only if a classmate goes on to submit work bought from the advertised service
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.7 expects students not to send emails that share assignments or promote cheating in any form, so promoting an essay-writing service is a breach even with nothing attached.
questions.source_excerpt: Send emails to share assignments/course works or promote cheating in any form.

questions.question: A student registers their College email address with a suspect website offering free gift cards, but never sends the site any email. Under the Student Email Using Policy, how should this be viewed?
options: As acceptable, as the email rules apply only to messages a student actually sends
As acceptable, as GMS content filters will block any harmful email from the site
As a breach, as students are expected not to sign up for suspect websites
As contrary to the policy only if the site is proven illegal, not merely suspect
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.9 expects students not to sign up for illegal, unreliable, disreputable or suspect websites and services; signing up is itself the problem, whether or not emails are sent.
questions.source_excerpt: Sign up for illegal, unreliable, disreputable, or suspect websites and services.

questions.question: A student missed a deadline change that their lecturer emailed to the class. The student says they check College email about once a month and should have been sent a text. What does the Student Email Using Policy say?
options: Staff must send important course changes by text as well as email to avoid disputes
Email is the primary communication method, and students must regularly check it
The student is excused, as staff emails count only once a student has replied to them
The student is excused, as students need check College email only when a lecturer says to
questions.explanation: Section 3.1 makes email the primary method of communication between the College and students, and section 3.7 requires students to access and regularly check their accounts for information and updates.
questions.source_excerpt: Email is the primary method of communication between the College and Students. ... Therefore, students must access and regularly check their email accounts for information and updates.

questions.question: Which of these would be contrary to the Student Email Using Policy's rules on the email address students use?
options: Emailing group project members from College accounts to plan a joint presentation
Emailing a relative about weekend plans from the student's own personal email account
Emailing the administration team from the College account with a non-class query
Emailing a lecturer about an assignment question from the student's personal account
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.1 expects students not to use a private email address for College and course-related communications; sections 4.2 and 4.3 allow emails to administration and group members, and purely personal emails are outside the rule.
questions.source_excerpt: Use their private email address for the College and course-related communications.

questions.question: A student receives an email from a classmate's genuine College address containing only an attachment and the words 'open this', with no explanation. Under the Student Email Using Policy, what should they do?
options: Avoid opening it, as attachments should not be opened when content is not adequately explained
Open it, as the policy's email checks apply only to messages that come from unknown senders
Open it, as students are permitted to email one another to help each other with classes
Forward it to other classmates so that each can judge whether the attachment is legitimate
questions.explanation: Section 5.2.4 tells students to avoid opening attachments when content is not adequately explained; this applies even though the sender is known, as the unknown-sender check in 5.2.5 is a separate step.
questions.source_excerpt: Avoid opening attachments and clicking on links when content is not adequately explained; ... Check email and names of unknown senders to ensure they are legitimate.

questions.question: None of these students uses personal information in their College email password. Which of them is following all of the Student Email Using Policy's password rules?
options: Ayo: ten mixed-case characters with symbols and numbers, written in a notebook kept at home
Ben: eight lower-case letters and numbers with no personal details, memorised and kept secret
Cara: twelve mixed-case characters with symbols and numbers, memorised and kept secret
Dev: ten mixed-case characters with symbols and numbers, shared only with his mother
questions.explanation: Sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 require at least eight characters using capital and lower-case letters, symbols and numbers, remembered rather than written down and kept secret, and section 3.3 bars sharing passwords; only Cara meets every rule.
questions.source_excerpt: Select strong passwords with at least eight characters (capital and lower-case letters, symbols and numbers) without using personal information (e.g. birthdays); ... Remember passwords instead of writing them down and keep them secret;

questions.question: Two students leave: Priya completes her course, and Tom withdraws part-way through, giving him another inactive status. Under the Student Email Using Policy's access table, how do their email accounts differ?
options: Priya keeps access for 3 months after completion; Tom's account enters a suspension period
Both keep access for 3 months, as the table treats every inactive status in the same way
Tom keeps access for 3 months to collect his work; Priya's account is suspended at once
Both accounts are permanently deleted at once, as neither student is still enrolled
questions.explanation: The section 6 table gives a completed student access for the study period plus 3 months, while any other inactive status leads to a suspension period.
questions.source_excerpt: 3 Any other Inactive Status. ... Study period + 3 Months after course completed ... Suspension period

questions.question: The College restricts an enrolled student's email access mid-course. The student argues that the access table guarantees access throughout the study period. Under the Student Email Using Policy, who is right?
options: The student, as access can be restricted only once the course has been completed
The College, which reserves all rights to restrict access to any account at any time
The student, unless they have first been found in breach at a disciplinary hearing
Neither, as only the IT Department may decide because it maintains the email system
questions.explanation: Section 6.1 states that the College reserves all rights to provide or restrict access to any email account at any time, following its internal policies and procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: The College reserves all rights to provide access or restrict access to any email account at any time. The College will follow internal policies and procedures to manage email account use.

questions.question: The IT Department wants to stop one particular kind of message reaching student accounts while letting all other mail through. Which Google Message Security feature described in the Student Email Using Policy is designed for this?
options: Policy-Based TLS Encryption, which encrypts messages and attachments server to server
Aliases and distribution lists, which group users together under shared addresses
Content filters, which create customised rules for blocking or allowing traffic
Inbound and outbound cover, which gives highly effective protection from spam viruses
questions.explanation: Section 7.1.5 says GMS content filters create highly customised rules for blocking or allowing specific types of email traffic; the other features encrypt, group or give general spam cover.
questions.source_excerpt: GMS Content filters creates highly customized rules for blocking or allowing specific types of email traffic.

questions.question: A student sends a bulk email carrying a virus to external addresses, claiming Google Message Security's outbound cover will stop it, so no rule is broken. How does the Student Email Using Policy view this?
options: As acceptable, as GMS rather than the student is responsible for malware leaving accounts
As a breach only if GMS fails to stop the email from reaching its recipients
As a matter for Google alone, as the student's account is part of its G-Suite services
As a breach, as students must not send spam with a virus to users outside the College
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.4 expects students not to send spam containing a virus to users within or outside the College, and section 3.3 makes them solely responsible for all activity in their account, whatever GMS screening exists.
questions.source_excerpt: Create or send spam emails containing a virus or other malicious content to other email users within or outside the college facility. ... They are solely responsible for all activities that occur within the email account.

questions.question: Which of the following is not provided for in the notes to the Student Email Using Policy's account access table?
options: Students must agree to all terms and conditions for the account
Students can extend access beyond 3 months after completion on request
Students can back up any email or electronic documents after completion
Students will be notified before email account suspension and deletion
questions.explanation: The notes to the section 6 table require agreement to all terms and conditions, allow back-up after course completion and promise notice before suspension and deletion; they say nothing about extending access on request.
questions.source_excerpt: Student must agree to all terms and conditions. Student can back-up any email or electronic documents after course completion. Student will be notified before the email account suspension and deletion.

questions.question: A student keeps reading College emails throughout your lecture, saying the Student Email Using Policy requires them to check their account regularly. How should you respond?
options: The student is right, as the duty to check regularly overrides the other email rules in class
Regular checking is required, but lecture sessions are an inappropriate time to read email
The student is right, provided the lecturer has warned that urgent updates may arrive that day
Regular checking is only a suggestion, so the student may read their email whenever they like
questions.explanation: Section 3.7 requires students to check their College email regularly, but section 3.8.5 expects them not to send or read email at inappropriate times, such as during lecture sessions.
questions.source_excerpt: students must access and regularly check their email accounts for information and updates. ... Send or read email at inappropriate times, such as during lecture sessions.

questions.question: A student emails a lecturer a message insulting them over a mark, with no reference to any protected characteristic, and says it cannot breach the Student Email Using Policy as it is not discriminatory. Is that right?
options: No, the policy expects students not to send insulting or discriminatory messages
Yes, the policy's message rules apply only to content that encourages discrimination
Yes, as students may email lecturers with questions or comments regarding class
Yes, as insults aimed at staff fall under staff policies, not the student email policy
questions.explanation: Section 3.8.10 expects students not to send insulting or discriminatory messages and content, so an insulting message is covered even if it is not discriminatory.
questions.source_excerpt: Send insulting or discriminatory messages and content.

questions.question: A student with no disability says they cannot work out how to access and use their College email. Under the Student Email Using Policy, which College resource covers this?
options: The Registry team, which the policy names as the email advice source for every student
Google's own G-Suite help pages, as the College account is part of G-Suite services
Their personal tutor, who issues each student's email account details at induction
The Learning Resources Centre and IT Using Guide, which covers accessing and using email
questions.explanation: Section 3.2 says the Learning Resources Centre and IT Using Guide covers how to access and use email services; section 3.9 points only students with a disability who find email difficult to the Registry team.
questions.source_excerpt: The College has a Learning Resources Centre and IT Using Guide, which covers `how to access and use email services ... Students with disability who may find it difficult to use email as a method of communication should contact the Registry team for advice and support.

questions.question: A student tells you an email that seems to come from the IT Department asked them to reply with their College email password for a mailbox upgrade. They checked the sender's name and address, which look legitimate. What does the Student Email Using Policy require of the student?
options: Send it, as the sender check the policy requires has shown that the request is legitimate
Send it, as the IT Department is responsible for maintaining the College email system
Keep it secret, as students must not disclose or share their passwords with others
Refuse by email, but give it over the phone if the IT Department rings to confirm
questions.explanation: Sections 3.3 and 5.2.2 say students must not disclose or share their passwords and must keep them secret; checking a sender's legitimacy under 5.2.5, or IT's role in maintaining the system, creates no exception.
questions.source_excerpt: must not disclose or share their passwords with others. ... Remember passwords instead of writing them down and keep them secret; ... Check email and names of unknown senders to ensure they are legitimate.

questions.question: A student with a disability finds their College email difficult to use and asks you to send course materials to their personal email address instead. Under the Student Email Using Policy, what is the appropriate response?
options: Agree, as the policy makes disability an exception to its rule against private email for course matters
Refer them to the IT Department, which maintains the email system and deals with such requests
Ask a classmate to log in to their College account and read the course emails out to them
Refer them to the Registry team for advice and support; private email is not for course matters
questions.explanation: Section 3.9 directs students with a disability who find email difficult to the Registry team for advice and support, and section 3.8.1 expects students not to use a private address for course-related communications; no disability exception is stated.
questions.source_excerpt: Use their private email address for the College and course-related communications. ... Students with disability who may find it difficult to use email as a method of communication should contact the Registry team for advice and support.

questions.question: Two students, Lena and Omar, swap College email passwords. Omar then logs in to Lena's account and emails offensive messages to a classmate. Under the Student Email Using Policy, who has acted contrary to the policy?
options: Only Omar, as he wrote and sent the offensive messages from Lena's account himself
Both of them, as each shared a password and Omar also used another person's account
Only Lena, as she is solely responsible for all activities that occur within her account
Neither of them, until the IT Department confirms which device sent the messages
questions.explanation: Section 3.3 bars students from disclosing or sharing passwords, so both breached it by swapping, and section 3.8.8 expects students not to use another person's account, as Omar did; Lena also remains responsible for activity in her account.
questions.source_excerpt: All students are responsible for the security of their mailboxes and must not disclose or share their passwords with others. They are solely responsible for all activities that occur within the email account. ... Use the account of another person.

questions.question: Which students does London Churchill College's Student Engagement Policy apply to?
options: Students taught on campus, with distance learners covered separately
Elected student representatives serving on College committees
All LCC students, regardless of their programme delivery mode
Full-time undergraduate students, excluding part-time learners
questions.explanation: The policy states that it applies to all LCC students whatever their programme delivery mode, so it is not limited to on-campus, full-time or representative students.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy is applicable to all students of LCC in spite of their programme delivery mode.

questions.question: A student's attendance and engagement have been falling and they mention they are thinking of withdrawing. Which approach reflects the aims of the Student Engagement Policy?
options: Wait until the student formally requests support before taking any action
Start the withdrawal process promptly to protect the programme's success rate
Proactively offer support to help the student avoid a preventable withdrawal
Refer the matter to their student representative to resolve informally with them
questions.explanation: The policy aims to ensure the College applies a proactive approach to providing support when required and avoids any preventable student withdrawals.
questions.source_excerpt: Additionally, it aims to ensure that the College applies a proactive approach to providing support when required and to avoid any preventable student withdrawals.

questions.question: A newly appointed staff member asks where their responsibilities for supporting student representation are set out. According to the Student Engagement Policy, where should you direct them?
options: To the College CPD calendar
To the Student Representation Manual
To the student representatives' role descriptions and service level agreement
To the Minutes of the Programme Committee Meetings
questions.explanation: The policy states that staff responsibilities are underpinned in the Student Representation Manual; the role descriptions and service level agreement cover Student Representatives, not staff.
questions.source_excerpt: The College underpins the responsibilities of staff in the Student Representation Manual; ... The responsibilities of Student Representative are in the role descriptions and service level agreement.

questions.question: You are taking notes at a Programme Committee Meeting when the student representative raises feedback from their cohort. Under the Student Engagement Policy, what should happen to this student feedback?
options: It is recorded and forms part of the formal Minutes of the meeting
It is passed verbally to the Programme Leader and not minuted
It is held back until the next annual student survey is published
It is recorded in a separate confidential note outside the Minutes
questions.explanation: The policy states that at meetings where student representatives are members, including Programme Committee Meetings, student feedback is recorded and forms part of the formal Minutes.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are members of the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings. At these meetings student feedback is recorded and forms part of the formal Minutes of each meeting.

questions.question: A group of students asks for an informal meeting with a senior manager to share their views on how their programme is going. Under the Student Engagement Policy, how should this request be viewed?
options: As inappropriate, as student views must be raised through formal committee channels
As a matter for the student representative system, not for a direct meeting with managers
As premature, since views should be held for the end-of-module questionnaire
As legitimate, since LCC offers students formal and informal chances to engage
questions.explanation: The policy commits LCC to formal and informal meetings with student groups and to giving all students every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers on a formal and informal basis.
questions.source_excerpt: through formal and informal meetings with student groups; ... LCC will ensure all students including distance learners are provided every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers, on a formal and informal basis.

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, how will students be invited to contribute to LCC's drive for quality enhancement?
options: By offering feedback through questionnaires and other procedures
Through their student representatives, not as individual students
By being told of enhancements after the QA team has agreed them
By attending a compulsory annual quality review hearing in person
questions.explanation: The policy states that, as part of the drive for quality enhancement, students will be invited to offer feedback by way of questionnaires and other procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: This includes the drive for quality enhancement in which students will be invited to offer feedback by way of questionnaires and other procedures;

questions.question: A student suggests that learning materials be made available earlier and that classrooms have better multimedia resources. Under the Student Engagement Policy, how should staff treat this suggestion?
options: As outside students' remit, since learning resources are a matter for staff
As an example of the enhancement ideas that students are encouraged to share
As a formal complaint that must be logged under the complaints procedure
As a request to be deferred until a student representative raises it
questions.explanation: The policy encourages students to share ideas for enhancement and gives the availability of learning materials and multimedia resources in the learning space as examples.
questions.source_excerpt: students are encouraged to identify and share ideas and ... opinions for academic, quality and experiential enhancement. Examples of enhancements include adjustments to the availability of learning materials, enhancements within the learning space with regard to multimedia resources, and student-led extracurricular activities.

questions.question: Under the Student Engagement Policy, which group does the Student Engagement Group update when it reviews the progress of student engagement activities?
options: The Board of Directors
The College Oversight Board
The Quality Assurance Department
The Principal Executive Group
questions.explanation: The policy gives the Student Engagement Group a remit to review the progress of student engagement activities for update to the Principal Executive Group.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Engagement Group has a remit to review the progress of student engagement activities for update to the Principal Executive Group.

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, when will training for Student Representatives be decided?
options: At the start of the year
At the end of the first term
After the first committee meeting
Mid-way through the year
questions.explanation: The policy states that training for Student Representatives will be decided at the start of the year, and that it will include mentoring.
questions.source_excerpt: Training for Student Representatives will be decided at the start of the year to include mentoring.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Student Engagement Policy as a body or meeting on which student representatives are members?
options: Board of Directors
Staff Recruitment Panel
College Oversight Board
Programme Committee Meetings
questions.explanation: The policy lists the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings; a staff recruitment panel is not among them.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are members of the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings.

questions.question: Besides student engagement, what does London Churchill College's Student Engagement Policy explicitly intend to improve for all students on relevant programmes?
options: Their attendance
Their employability
Their exam technique
Their digital skills
questions.explanation: The policy states that it intends to improve the engagement and attendance of all students on relevant programmes.
questions.source_excerpt: it intends to improve the engagement and attendance of all students on relevant programmes

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, enabling students to maximise their full potential is intended to increase what?
options: The number of new applications
The success rate and achievement
Graduate employment outcomes
The College's league table rank
questions.explanation: The policy aims to enable students to maximise their full potential, increasing the success rate and achievement.
questions.source_excerpt: to enable students to maximise their full potential, increasing the success rate and achievement.

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, what is the main purpose of the policy?
options: To monitor attendance so that disengaged students can be withdrawn promptly
To raise student satisfaction scores reported in national student surveys
To increase student motivation and participation, enhancing their learning
To define the sanctions that apply to students who fail to attend classes
questions.explanation: The policy states that its main purpose is to increase student motivation and encourage their participation, thus enhancing their learning experience at LCC.
questions.source_excerpt: The main purpose of the policy is to increase student motivation and encourage their participation thus enhancing their learning experience whilst at LCC;

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, LCC will ensure students are provided every possible opportunity to engage with whom?
options: External examiners
Awarding body staff
Alumni mentors
Decision makers
questions.explanation: The policy commits LCC to ensuring all students are provided every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will ensure all students including distance learners are provided every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers, on a formal and informal basis.

questions.question: The Student Engagement Policy says LCC's engagement includes offering students opportunities and encouragement to research. How does the policy describe research?
options: As a key factor in academic development
As an optional activity for postgraduates
As a requirement only in final-year projects
As an activity approved by the Academic Board
questions.explanation: The policy describes research, which LCC offers students opportunities and encouragement to undertake, as a key factor in academic development.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC's engagement includes offering students opportunities and encouragement to research, a key factor in academic development;

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, what will serving on committees enable student representatives to have?
options: A vote on the appointment of new teaching staff
A real say in how programmes are developed and enhanced
The final decision on appeals against assessment results
Access to staff appraisal and performance records
questions.explanation: The policy states that serving on committees will enable student representatives to have a real say in how programmes are developed and enhanced.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives will have the opportunity to serve on committees and for which will enable a real say in how programmes are developed and enhanced;

questions.question: How often does the Student Engagement Policy say LCC will monitor how students progress?
options: Annually, at the end-of-year progression board
Only at the points of formal assessment
Constantly, including successes and future needs
Termly, at each end-of-term progress review
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC will monitor how students progress constantly, including what the successes are and what needs to be done in the future.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will monitor how students progress constantly, what are the successes and what needs to be done in the future.

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, the College ensures that the student engagement process reflects what?
options: Only the views of elected representatives
The priorities of the Academic Board
The needs of its largest cohorts
Its students in all their diversity
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College ensures the student engagement process reflects its students in all their diversity.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures the student engagement process reflects its students in all their diversity.

questions.question: Under the Student Engagement Policy, which College document does the policy adhere to?
options: The College Student Engagement Framework
The College Student Engagement Charter
The College Student Voice Strategy
The College Student Partnership Agreement
questions.explanation: The policy states that it adheres to the College Student Engagement Framework, which is mapped against the AdvanceHE framework.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Student Engagement Policy adheres to the College Student Engagement Framework.

questions.question: Under the Student Engagement Policy, LCC maintains an environment in which students and staff engage in discussions. What do these discussions aim to bring about?
options: A measurable fall in the number of formal complaints
Demonstrable enhancement of the educational experience
Faster approval of new programmes for delivery
Agreed changes to the annual assessment calendar
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC maintains an environment where students and staff engage in discussions aiming to bring about demonstrable enhancement of the educational experience.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC creates and maintains an environment within which students and staff engage in discussions that aim to bring about demonstrable enhancement of the educational experience;

questions.question: The Student Engagement Policy encourages students to identify and share ideas and opinions for which kinds of enhancement?
options: Teaching, welfare and financial enhancement
Curricular, pastoral and employability enhancement
Academic, quality and experiential enhancement
Estates, staffing and marketing enhancement
questions.explanation: The policy encourages students to identify and share ideas and opinions for academic, quality and experiential enhancement.
questions.source_excerpt: students are encouraged to identify and share ideas and ... opinions for academic, quality and experiential enhancement.

questions.question: Under the Student Engagement Policy, over what period are students encouraged to participate actively in every sphere possible?
options: During induction and their first term only
While they serve as student representatives
In the final year of their programme
Throughout the student life-cycle
questions.explanation: The policy states that students are encouraged to participate actively in every sphere possible throughout the student life-cycle.
questions.source_excerpt: Throughout the student life-cycle, the students are encouraged to participate actively in every sphere possible.

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, which of the following will training for Student Representatives include?
options: Mentoring
Safeguarding
Fire safety
First aid
questions.explanation: The policy states that training for Student Representatives will be decided at the start of the year to include mentoring.
questions.source_excerpt: Training for Student Representatives will be decided at the start of the year to include mentoring.

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, where will training for Student Representatives be included?
options: In the Student Representation Manual
In the College CPD calendar
In the student induction plan
In the Academic Board's annual plan
questions.explanation: The policy states that training for Student Representatives will be included in the College CPD calendar.
questions.source_excerpt: Training will be included in the College CPD calendar.

questions.question: According to the Student Engagement Policy, where are the responsibilities of Student Representatives set out?
options: In the student handbook and programme specification
In the College CPD calendar and training records
In the role descriptions and service level agreement
In the Academic Board's terms of reference
questions.explanation: The policy states that the responsibilities of Student Representatives are in the role descriptions and service level agreement.
questions.source_excerpt: The responsibilities of Student Representative are in the role descriptions and service level agreement.

questions.question: A student studying an LCC programme entirely by distance learning asks whether they can meet College decision makers to give their views. Under the Student Engagement Policy, what applies?
options: They may give their views only through end-of-module questionnaires, as meetings are reserved for campus students
They are covered, and LCC must give distance learners every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers
They must first be elected as a student representative before they can meet any College decision makers
They may do so only by attending campus in person, as the policy makes no provision for remote engagement
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all LCC students whatever their delivery mode, and LCC must give all students, including distance learners, every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers formally and informally.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy is applicable to all students of LCC in spite of their programme delivery mode. ... LCC will ensure all students including distance learners are provided every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers, on a formal and informal basis.

questions.question: The quality team wants to gather students' feedback for quality enhancement through a focus group rather than a questionnaire. Under the Student Engagement Policy, is this approach acceptable?
options: No, the policy limits quality enhancement feedback to formal questionnaires
Only if student representatives run the focus group without staff present
Only once the Academic Board has approved the focus group method in advance
Yes, students are invited to give feedback via questionnaires and other procedures
questions.explanation: The policy invites students to offer feedback for quality enhancement by way of questionnaires and other procedures, so it is not limited to questionnaires and sets no approval or staffing condition.
questions.source_excerpt: This includes the drive for quality enhancement in which students will be invited to offer feedback by way of questionnaires and other procedures;

questions.question: A manager suggests delaying the collection of student feedback because student views are a low priority this term. How does this suggestion compare with the Student Engagement Policy?
options: It conflicts with the policy, which says heeding the student voice remains a top priority
It is consistent, provided views are collected at least once before the end of the academic year
It is consistent, as the policy leaves the priority of student views to each manager
It conflicts only if the student representatives have formally objected to the delay
questions.explanation: The policy states that heeding the student voice remains a top priority for LCC, so treating student views as a low priority conflicts with it.
questions.source_excerpt: Heeding to the student voice remains a top priority for LCC.

questions.question: A second-year student asks their lecturer for encouragement to carry out an independent research project. How does the Student Engagement Policy regard supporting this student?
options: As outside the policy, which only covers representation and student feedback
As appropriate only for students who serve as student representatives
As part of LCC's engagement: research is key to academic development
As needing Student Engagement Group approval before any research begins
questions.explanation: The policy states that LCC's engagement includes offering students opportunities and encouragement to research, which it describes as a key factor in academic development.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC's engagement includes offering students opportunities and encouragement to research, a key factor in academic development;

questions.question: A Programme Committee meeting is considering proposed changes to a programme's modules. Under the Student Engagement Policy, what role do student representatives have in this?
options: They are told about the changes once the committee has approved them
They sit as members with a real say in how programmes are developed
They attend as observers but cannot contribute to the committee's decisions
They send written comments afterwards through the Quality Assurance Department
questions.explanation: Student representatives are members of Programme Committee Meetings, and serving on committees gives them a real say in how programmes are developed and enhanced.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are members of the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings. ... Student representatives will have the opportunity to serve on committees and for which will enable a real say in how programmes are developed and enhanced;

questions.question: A department is reviewing what its students' successes have been and what needs to be done in future. Under the Student Engagement Policy, how should students be involved in this?
options: Their voices and participation should be sought in a collaborative way
They should be told the review's conclusions once staff have agreed them
Only their assessment results should be used as evidence of their progress
Only representatives who sit on the Academic Board should be consulted
questions.explanation: When LCC monitors students' progress, successes and future needs, the policy states that students' voices and participation are sought in a collaborative way.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will monitor how students progress constantly, what are the successes and what needs to be done in the future. Students' voices and participation are sought in a collaborative way;

questions.question: A team plans a student engagement activity and invites only full-time students attending on campus, leaving out part-time and distance learners. Under the Student Engagement Policy, what is the problem?
options: None, provided the activity's outcomes are later recorded in the formal committee Minutes
None, as long as the Student Engagement Group has approved the activity in advance
Only that the activity must first be listed in the College CPD calendar for the year
The process must reflect students in all their diversity, whatever their study mode
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all students whatever their delivery mode, and the College must ensure the student engagement process reflects its students in all their diversity.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy is applicable to all students of LCC in spite of their programme delivery mode. ... The College ensures the student engagement process reflects its students in all their diversity.

questions.question: A colleague asks how LCC's Student Engagement Policy relates to the AdvanceHE Framework for Student Engagement Through Partnership. What does the policy say?
options: The policy replaces the AdvanceHE framework for all students studying at LCC
The AdvanceHE framework is mapped directly against the College's policy
It adheres to the College framework, which is mapped against AdvanceHE's
The policy follows AdvanceHE's framework directly, with no College framework
questions.explanation: The policy adheres to the College Student Engagement Framework, and it is that College framework which is mapped against the AdvanceHE framework.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Student Engagement Policy adheres to the College Student Engagement Framework. The framework is mapped against the AdvanceHE Framework for Student Engagement Through Partnership.

questions.question: In their first week, a newly enrolled student offers an idea for improving their course. A colleague says new students should wait until their second year to suggest enhancements. Under the Student Engagement Policy, is the colleague right?
options: No, but the idea must be submitted as a formal complaint to be considered
Yes, since enhancement ideas are sought only from final-year students
Yes, since new students must raise ideas through their student representative
No, students are encouraged to participate throughout the student life-cycle
questions.explanation: The policy encourages students to participate actively in every sphere possible throughout the student life-cycle, so there is no waiting period before they can share ideas.
questions.source_excerpt: Throughout the student life-cycle, the students are encouraged to participate actively in every sphere possible.

questions.question: A newly elected Student Representative is unsure how to arrange and lead their first meeting with the cohort they represent. Under the Student Engagement Policy, how is this need addressed?
options: Through Student Representative training, which covers organising and running meetings
Through the Student Representation Manual, which sets out each rep's meeting duties
Through one-to-one coaching from the Principal Executive Group, arranged on request
Through the Academic Board, which briefs new representatives at its first meeting
questions.explanation: The policy lists organising and running meetings among the areas of training for Student Representatives; the Student Representation Manual sets out staff responsibilities, not training.
questions.source_excerpt: Other areas for training include approaching students, organising and running meetings, giving and receiving feedback and interpersonal skills;

questions.question: The agenda for a Board of Directors meeting is being prepared. Under the Student Engagement Policy, what is the position of student representatives in relation to this Board?
options: They are members of it, as they are of the Academic Board
They may attend only as observers, with no membership rights
They are excluded, as representatives sit only on programme committees
They attend only when the Principal Executive Group invites them for an item
questions.explanation: The policy lists the Board of Directors, alongside the College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings, as bodies of which student representatives are members.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are members of the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings.

questions.question: A student on a fully online-delivered LCC programme has stopped engaging with their studies. A colleague says the support aims of the Student Engagement Policy cover only classroom-taught students. What is the correct position?
options: The colleague is right, as online-delivered students are covered by a separate distance learning procedure
The policy applies whatever the delivery mode, so the College should take a proactive approach to support
The policy applies, but support should be offered only once the student has formally asked for it
The policy applies to their attendance only, so engagement concerns pass to their student representative
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all LCC students regardless of programme delivery mode, and it aims for the College to take a proactive approach to providing support and to avoid preventable withdrawals.
questions.source_excerpt: it aims to ensure that the College applies a proactive approach to providing support when required and to avoid any preventable student withdrawals. ... This policy is applicable to all students of LCC in spite of their programme delivery mode.

questions.question: A student representative raises cohort feedback at an Academic Board meeting; the same week, other students submit comments in a quality enhancement questionnaire. Under the Student Engagement Policy, which feedback is stated to form part of formal meeting Minutes?
options: Both sets, as all student feedback must be minuted by the Academic Board
Neither set, as only Programme Committee Meetings minute student feedback
The Academic Board feedback, as student feedback at its meetings is minuted
Only the questionnaire comments, which the Student Engagement Group minutes
questions.explanation: The Academic Board is one of the meetings with student representative members, where student feedback is recorded in the formal Minutes; questionnaires are a separate route for quality enhancement feedback.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are members of the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings. At these meetings student feedback is recorded and forms part of the formal Minutes of each meeting. ... students will be invited to offer feedback by way of questionnaires and other procedures

questions.question: The Student Engagement Policy names several College bodies. Which one does it mention only as the recipient of updates on student engagement progress, and not among the bodies with student representative members?
options: The Principal Executive Group
The Student Engagement Group
The College Oversight Board
The Programme Committee Meetings
questions.explanation: Student representatives are members of the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings; the Principal Executive Group is named only as receiving the Student Engagement Group's updates.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are members of the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings. ... The Student Engagement Group has a remit to review the progress of student engagement activities for update to the Principal Executive Group.

questions.question: The introduction to the Student Engagement Policy describes how London Churchill College encourages its student body to engage. Which description matches the policy?
options: Involvement on College committees via the student representative system, and formal meetings only with student groups
Involvement on College committees open to every student without representatives, and informal meetings with individuals
An elected students' union, plus formal and informal meetings held between student groups and external examiners
Involvement on College committees via the student representative system, and formal and informal meetings with student groups
questions.explanation: The introduction says LCC encourages engagement through involvement on College committees engaging the system of students' representatives, and through formal and informal meetings with student groups.
questions.source_excerpt: London Churchill College (LCC) encourages its student body to engage, through involvement on College committees engaging the system of students' representatives and through formal and informal meetings with student groups;

questions.question: A colleague says that under the Student Engagement Policy, students' progress is only checked when the Student Engagement Group reviews engagement activities for the Principal Executive Group. Which statement corrects this?
options: The Academic Board reviews student progress termly, while the Student Engagement Group reviews only rep training
LCC monitors student progress constantly; the Student Engagement Group separately reviews engagement activities
The Principal Executive Group monitors student progress and then updates the Student Engagement Group on it
The QA Department monitors student progress annually, alongside the Student Engagement Group's own review
questions.explanation: The policy says LCC will monitor how students progress constantly; separately, the Student Engagement Group reviews the progress of student engagement activities for update to the Principal Executive Group.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will monitor how students progress constantly, what are the successes and what needs to be done in the future. ... The Student Engagement Group has a remit to review the progress of student engagement activities for update to the Principal Executive Group.

questions.question: Students propose running a student-led extracurricular activity to improve their experience at LCC. A colleague says this is not the kind of enhancement the Student Engagement Policy has in mind. Who is right?
options: The colleague, as the policy's enhancements cover only academic and quality matters
The students, but only once a student representative has formally proposed it
The colleague, unless the Academic Board classes the activity as academic enhancement
The students, as student-led extracurricular activities are among the listed examples
questions.explanation: The policy encourages ideas for academic, quality and experiential enhancement, and its listed examples of enhancements include student-led extracurricular activities.
questions.source_excerpt: students are encouraged to identify and share ideas and ... opinions for academic, quality and experiential enhancement. Examples of enhancements include adjustments to the availability of learning materials, enhancements within the learning space with regard to multimedia resources, and student-led extracurricular activities.

questions.question: A draft training plan for Student Representatives is being checked against the Student Engagement Policy. Which set of topics is drawn entirely from the training areas the policy names?
options: Mentoring, safeguarding, and giving and receiving feedback
Approaching students, data protection, and running meetings
Mentoring, approaching students, and interpersonal skills
Interpersonal skills, budgeting, and organising student meetings
questions.explanation: The policy says representative training will include mentoring and names approaching students, organising and running meetings, giving and receiving feedback and interpersonal skills; safeguarding, data protection and budgeting are not named.
questions.source_excerpt: Training for Student Representatives will be decided at the start of the year to include mentoring. Other areas for training include approaching students, organising and running meetings, giving and receiving feedback and interpersonal skills;

questions.question: A new lecturer asks where their own responsibilities towards student representation are set out, and where Student Representative training will be scheduled. Under the Student Engagement Policy, which answer is correct?
options: The Student Representation Manual; the College CPD calendar
The role descriptions and service level agreement; the College CPD calendar
The Student Representation Manual; the Student Engagement Group's Minutes
The College CPD calendar; the Student Representation Manual
questions.explanation: Staff responsibilities are underpinned in the Student Representation Manual and representative training will be included in the College CPD calendar; role descriptions and service level agreements cover the representatives' own duties.
questions.source_excerpt: Training will be included in the College CPD calendar. ... The College underpins the responsibilities of staff in the Student Representation Manual;

questions.question: A newly elected Student Representative asks where their duties are defined and what serving on committees will give them. Which answer reflects the Student Engagement Policy?
options: Duties are in the Student Representation Manual; committee service gives a real say in how programmes develop
Duties are in the role descriptions and service level agreement; committee service gives a real say in programmes
Duties are in the role descriptions and service level agreement; committee service is only as a non-voting observer
Duties are in the College CPD calendar; committee service gives the final decision on programme approval
questions.explanation: Representatives' responsibilities are in the role descriptions and service level agreement, and serving on committees enables a real say in how programmes are developed and enhanced; the Manual covers staff responsibilities.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives will have the opportunity to serve on committees and for which will enable a real say in how programmes are developed and enhanced; ... The responsibilities of Student Representative are in the role descriptions and service level agreement.

questions.question: At a Student Engagement Group meeting, a student representative raises feedback from their cohort, and the Group then reviews how student engagement activities are progressing. Under the Student Engagement Policy, what follows?
options: The feedback is minuted, and the progress review is for update to the Academic Board
The feedback is kept out of the Minutes, and the review is for update to the Principal Executive Group
