The feedback goes to the QA Department, and the review is for update to the Board of Directors
The feedback is minuted, and the progress review is for update to the Principal Executive Group
questions.explanation: Student representatives are members of the Student Engagement Group, so student feedback there forms part of the formal Minutes, and the Group reviews engagement activity progress for update to the Principal Executive Group.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are members of the ... Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings. At these meetings student feedback is recorded and forms part of the formal Minutes of each meeting. ... The Student Engagement Group has a remit to review the progress of student engagement activities for update to the Principal Executive Group.

questions.question: A colleague's briefing notes contain four statements about the Student Engagement Policy. Which statement is consistent with the policy?
options: The student engagement process should reflect LCC's students in all their diversity
Student Representative training is decided by each representative in their role description
LCC monitors how students progress only at the points where formal assessments take place
Students may share enhancement ideas only through their elected student representatives
questions.explanation: The College ensures the student engagement process reflects its students in all their diversity; training is decided at the start of the year, progress is monitored constantly and all students are encouraged to share ideas.
questions.source_excerpt: The College ensures the student engagement process reflects its students in all their diversity.

questions.question: A coordinator plans to decide Student Representative training part-way through the year, as issues arise, and to leave mentoring out. Under the Student Engagement Policy, which requirements does this plan fail to meet?
options: Training must be approved by the Academic Board and must include safeguarding
Training must be set out in each representative's service level agreement
Training must be decided at the start of the year and must include mentoring
Training must be decided at the start of the year and run by the Student Engagement Group
questions.explanation: The policy states that training for Student Representatives will be decided at the start of the year to include mentoring, so a mid-year plan without mentoring fails on both points.
questions.source_excerpt: Training for Student Representatives will be decided at the start of the year to include mentoring.

questions.question: A department is summarising the Student Engagement Policy's approach to quality enhancement for new staff. Which summary is accurate?
options: Staff discuss enhancements among themselves, and students give feedback through questionnaires only
Students and staff discuss demonstrable enhancement, but only representatives may put forward ideas
Students lead enhancement discussions alone, and staff give feedback via questionnaires and other procedures
Students and staff discuss enhancement, and students give feedback via questionnaires and other procedures
questions.explanation: LCC maintains an environment where students and staff discuss demonstrable enhancement, and students are invited to give feedback by way of questionnaires and other procedures as well as to share their own ideas.
questions.source_excerpt: This includes the drive for quality enhancement in which students will be invited to offer feedback by way of questionnaires and other procedures; ... LCC creates and maintains an environment within which students and staff engage in discussions that aim to bring about demonstrable enhancement of the educational experience;

questions.question: A student who does not hold a representative role wants to help shape how their programme is enhanced. Under the Student Engagement Policy, what is open to them?
options: Nothing directly, as only representatives on committees can influence programme enhancement
Sharing enhancement ideas and opinions, and giving feedback via questionnaires and other procedures
Only standing for election, as programme changes are decided at Programme Committee Meetings
Only a formal complaint, which the Quality Assurance Department then reviews for enhancement
questions.explanation: All students, not only representatives, are encouraged to identify and share ideas and opinions for enhancement and are invited to give quality enhancement feedback through questionnaires and other procedures.
questions.source_excerpt: students will be invited to offer feedback by way of questionnaires and other procedures; ... students are encouraged to identify and share ideas and ... opinions for academic, quality and experiential enhancement.

questions.question: The Student Engagement Policy makes some commitments to all students and others only to Student Representatives. Which of these does it extend to all students, including distance learners?
options: Training decided at the start of the year, including mentoring
Membership of the College Oversight Board and Academic Board
Every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers
Duties set out in a role description and service level agreement
questions.explanation: LCC will ensure all students, including distance learners, are provided every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers; training, committee membership and role descriptions relate to Student Representatives.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will ensure all students including distance learners are provided every possible opportunity to engage with decision makers, on a formal and informal basis.

questions.question: A staff briefing says the Student Engagement Policy aims to improve engagement and attendance, increase success rate and achievement, and avoid all student withdrawals. Which part of this summary misstates the policy?
options: Attendance, as the policy aims to improve student engagement only
Avoiding all withdrawals, as the policy refers to preventable withdrawals
Success rate, as the policy aims to increase student achievement only
Engagement, as the policy aims to improve student attendance only
questions.explanation: The policy aims to improve engagement and attendance and increase the success rate and achievement, but it refers to avoiding preventable student withdrawals, not all withdrawals.
questions.source_excerpt: it intends to improve the engagement and attendance of all students on relevant programmes, and to enable students to maximise their full potential, increasing the success rate and achievement. Additionally, it aims to ensure that the College applies a proactive approach to providing support when required and to avoid any preventable student withdrawals.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about student feedback is not supported by the Student Engagement Policy?
options: Feedback is accepted only from students who hold a student representative role
Students are invited to give feedback through questionnaires and other procedures
At the listed committee meetings, student feedback forms part of the formal Minutes
Students' voices are sought collaboratively when LCC monitors how students progress
questions.explanation: The policy invites students to give feedback through questionnaires and other procedures, minutes student feedback at the listed meetings and seeks students' voices collaboratively; it does not limit feedback to representatives.
questions.source_excerpt: students will be invited to offer feedback by way of questionnaires and other procedures; ... At these meetings student feedback is recorded and forms part of the formal Minutes of each meeting. ... Students' voices and participation are sought in a collaborative way;

questions.question: At a Programme Committee Meeting, a student representative passes on their cohort's request for learning materials to be made available earlier. Under the Student Engagement Policy, which statement about this feedback is correct?
options: It is kept out of the Minutes, since enhancement ideas are to be given only through questionnaires
It is minuted, but when learning materials become available is a staff matter, not a student enhancement
It is minuted, and the availability of learning materials is one of the policy's listed enhancement examples
It is minuted only once the Student Engagement Group has reviewed and formally endorsed the cohort's request
questions.explanation: Student representatives sit on Programme Committee Meetings, where student feedback is recorded in the formal Minutes, and the policy lists adjustments to the availability of learning materials as an example of enhancement.
questions.source_excerpt: Student representatives are members of the Board of Directors, College Oversight Board, Academic Board, Student Engagement Group and Programme Committee Meetings. At these meetings student feedback is recorded and forms part of the formal Minutes of each meeting. ... Examples of enhancements include adjustments to the availability of learning materials

questions.question: Monitoring shows attendance falling across one cohort, and some students may be at risk of withdrawing. Which plan for the programme team is consistent with the Student Engagement Policy?
options: Offer support proactively where required, and base next steps on attendance data rather than students' views
Offer support once students formally request it, and seek the cohort's views collaboratively on next steps
Offer support once students formally request it, and base next steps on attendance data rather than students' views
Offer support proactively where required, and seek the cohort's views collaboratively on next steps
questions.explanation: The policy requires a proactive approach to support when required, to avoid preventable withdrawals, and says students' voices and participation are sought collaboratively when monitoring what needs to be done.
questions.source_excerpt: it aims to ensure that the College applies a proactive approach to providing support when required and to avoid any preventable student withdrawals. ... LCC will monitor how students progress constantly, what are the successes and what needs to be done in the future. Students' voices and participation are sought in a collaborative way;

questions.question: A part-time student studying by distance learning asks their tutor for encouragement to pursue a research topic. The tutor says the policy's research commitment is only for campus-based students. What is the correct position under the Student Engagement Policy?
options: The tutor is right, as distance learners engage mainly through questionnaires and other procedures
The tutor is wrong: the policy covers all students whatever their delivery mode, and includes encouraging research
The tutor is wrong, but encouragement to research applies only once a student reaches their final year
The tutor is right, as the policy's commitments to distance learners cover only engaging with decision makers
questions.explanation: The policy applies to all LCC students regardless of delivery mode, and LCC's engagement includes offering students opportunities and encouragement to research, with no restriction by year or mode.
questions.source_excerpt: This policy is applicable to all students of LCC in spite of their programme delivery mode. ... LCC's engagement includes offering students opportunities and encouragement to research, a key factor in academic development;

questions.question: A new quality officer's briefing on the Student Engagement Policy must state which framework the policy adheres to, and which body has the remit to review the progress of student engagement activities. Which pair is correct?
options: The College Student Engagement Framework; the Student Engagement Group
The AdvanceHE framework, directly; the Student Engagement Group
The College Student Engagement Framework; the Principal Executive Group
The AdvanceHE framework, directly; the Principal Executive Group
questions.explanation: The policy adheres to the College Student Engagement Framework, which is itself mapped against the AdvanceHE framework; the Student Engagement Group reviews progress and updates the Principal Executive Group.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Student Engagement Policy adheres to the College Student Engagement Framework. The framework is mapped against the AdvanceHE Framework for Student Engagement Through Partnership. ... The Student Engagement Group has a remit to review the progress of student engagement ... activities for update to the Principal Executive Group.

questions.question: A student with a declared disability asks you how the College will agree the support they need. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what happens?
options: Their personal tutor agrees informal adjustments with each module lecturer and notes them on file
They must apply to the Hardship Fund, which then pays for any adjustments set out in their evidence
The Student Welfare Officer grants extra exam time automatically on declaration, with no meeting needed
They are invited to a confidential meeting with the College Registrar to agree a Support Agreement Plan
questions.explanation: The policy states that students with declared disabilities are invited to a confidential meeting with the College Registrar to work out a Support Agreement Plan.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with declared disabilities are invited to attend a confidential meeting with the College Registrar to work out a Support Agreement Plan that will provide the student with support and opportunities to help them achieve their potential in their chosen courses.

questions.question: A student tells you they are struggling with their mental health and would like to speak privately to a mental health expert. Under the Student Welfare Policy, how can this be arranged?
options: They can ask their personal tutor to provide counselling during their scheduled teaching sessions
They can ask the Student Welfare Officer to book a confidential one-to-one with a mental health expert
They must contact Student Finance England, which arranges and funds mental health appointments for students
They must wait for the College's termly group wellbeing session and raise their concerns with the group
questions.explanation: The policy says students can consult the Student Welfare Officer to book a confidential one-to-one appointment for them with a mental health expert.
questions.source_excerpt: Students can consult the Student Welfare Officer to book a confidential one-to-one appointment for them with a mental health expert;

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, how are students with a long-term mental illness that has a substantial adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities defined?
options: As a mitigating circumstances case under College rules
As ineligible for support until DSA is approved
As disabled under the Equality Act 2010
As temporarily withdrawn from study
questions.explanation: The policy states that such students are defined as disabled under the Equality Act 2010, and that the College does not discriminate against students with mental health issues.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with a long-term mental illness that has a substantial adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities are defined as disabled under the Equality Act 2010.

questions.question: What is the application process for the LCC Hardship Fund under the Student Welfare Policy?
options: Apply online to Student Finance England, which assesses the claim and pays any award to the student
Apply verbally to the personal tutor, who approves it jointly with the College's Finance team
Apply to the Student Welfare Officer, who approves it and then informs the College Registrar of the award
Apply in writing with evidence to the College Registrar, who makes a recommendation to the Principal
questions.explanation: Applications must be sent in writing, with supporting evidence, to the College Registrar, who reviews the merit of the application and submits a recommendation to the Principal for approval/consideration.
questions.source_excerpt: Applications must be sent in writing to the College Registrar with supporting evidence, who will review the merit of the application and submit the recommendation to the Principal for approval/consideration.

questions.question: A student asks whether the LCC Hardship Fund can cover an ongoing gap between their income and expenses that has built up over the year because they did not plan their finances. What does the Student Welfare Policy say?
options: The fund is not suitable for a long-term shortfall caused by impractical planning
The fund can cover it as long as the student has a disability or dependent children
The fund can cover it once the student's personal tutor confirms the shortfall
The fund covers any shortfall provided the student applies within 30 days of it arising
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Hardship Fund is for short-term, urgent needs and is not suitable for a long-term shortfall between income and expenses to compensate for impractical planning.
questions.source_excerpt: The fund, however, is not suitable for long-term shortfall between the student's income and expenses to compensate for impractical planning.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, what is the maximum residual household income a student can have to be eligible for the LCC Hardship Fund?
options: £5,000 per annum
£10,000 per annum
£15,000 per annum
£25,000 per annum
questions.explanation: The policy sets the eligibility threshold at a residual household income that must not exceed £10,000 per annum.
questions.source_excerpt: To be eligible, student's residual household income must not exceed £10,000 per annum.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, which of the following is NOT one of the eligibility criteria for the LCC Hardship Fund?
options: The student must have attended at least 90% of their sessions
The student must be enrolled on a full-time undergraduate (HND) course
The student must have paid their first instalment of the fees
The student must be either a Home or EU student
questions.explanation: The policy lists full-time HND enrolment, Home or EU status and payment of the first fee instalment among the criteria; it sets no attendance percentage.
questions.source_excerpt: a) The student must be enrolled on a full-time undergraduate (HND) course. b) The student must be either a Home or EU student. ... d) The students must have paid their first instalment of the fees.

questions.question: A student has just been approved for Disabled Student Allowance (DSA). Under the Student Welfare Policy, what can the Student Welfare Officer do next?
options: Refer them to a DSA-approved Needs Assessment Centre for an expert report on their needs
Pay the DSA funding to the student directly from the College's Hardship Fund budget each term
Arrange for the College Registrar to carry out the needs assessment tests in-house and write the report
Close the case, as the College has no further role once DSA has been approved
questions.explanation: Once a student is approved for DSA, the Student Welfare Officer can refer them to a DSA-approved Needs Assessment Centre, which carries out tests and produces an expert report on the student's needs.
questions.source_excerpt: Once a student is approved for DSA the Student Welfare Officer can refer the student to a DSA-approved Needs Assessment Centre that will carry out tests with the student to produce an expert report on the needs of the student and how the College can help with the student's needs;

questions.question: A student tells you they plan to apply for Disabled Students' Allowance through both Student Finance England and the NHS scheme to maximise their support. What does the Student Welfare Policy say?
options: They should apply to both, and the College will combine the two awards into a single support package
They must apply to the NHS scheme first and then to Student Finance England
They should apply for only one scheme: either Student Finance England's DSA or the NHS DSA
They should apply through the College, which submits both applications to the funding bodies for them
questions.explanation: The policy states that students should only apply for either Student Finance England's DSA scheme or the NHS's DSA scheme, not both.
questions.source_excerpt: Students should only apply for either Student Finance England's DSA scheme OR NHS's DSA scheme.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, which of the following is listed as support that may be agreed for a student with a declared disability?
options: Automatic approval of any mitigating circumstances claim
Priority access to the Hardship Fund regardless of household income
Exemption from the College's attendance requirements
Extended book borrowing arrangements from the College Library
questions.explanation: The policy lists additional time in exams and presentations, extended submission deadlines, technology-aided learning and extended book borrowing from the College Library as support that may be agreed.
questions.source_excerpt: The support agreed may include additional time in exams and presentations, extended submission deadlines or permission for technology-aided learning during lectures or extended book borrowing arrangements from the College Library;

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, what does the College Registrar do first on receiving an appeal against a Hardship Fund or Bursary decision?
options: Forwards it straight to the Principal, who reviews the evidence and makes the final decision
Arranges a formal hearing with the student within five working days of receiving the form
Carries out an initial evaluation to check it was submitted under the right procedures
Suspends the original decision until the appeal has been fully concluded
questions.explanation: On receipt of an appeal, the College Registrar undertakes an initial evaluation to check that it was submitted under the right procedures, after which it may be referred, rejected or formally considered.
questions.source_excerpt: On receipt of appeal, the College Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation to check that the student's appeal was submitted under the right procedures.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, what does the LCC Bursary Scheme provide to an eligible student?
options: A one-off cash grant paid directly into the student's bank account
A discount of up to £1,000 from their course fees per annum
A free laptop and printing allowance for the first year of study
A loan of up to £1,000 that is repaid after graduation
questions.explanation: The LCC Bursary Scheme entitles the student to receive up to £1,000 discount from their course fees per annum.
questions.source_excerpt: The student will be entitled to receive up to £1,000 discount from their course fees per annum.

questions.question: The Student Welfare Policy names other College policies it should be read in conjunction with. Which of the following is one of them?
options: Safeguarding and Security Policy
Academic Misconduct Policy and Procedure
Fitness to Study Policy
Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Policy
questions.explanation: The Safeguarding and Security Policy is the first policy in the list the Student Welfare Policy says it should be read alongside; the others are not named.
questions.source_excerpt: This Policy should be read in conjunction with the following non-exclusive list of policies and procedures: a) Safeguarding and Security Policy

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, what is the LCC Hardship Fund intended to meet?
options: Accommodation deposits for applicants before they enrol at LCC
Students' short-term, urgent needs so they can continue their studies
Tuition fees for students yet to pay their first instalment of fees
Planned course costs budgeted for at the start of each year
questions.explanation: The fund is to meet students' short-term, urgent needs so that they can continue their studies at LCC without significant hardship.
questions.source_excerpt: The hardship fund is to ensure that it meets student's short-term, urgent needs and thus enables students to continue their studies at LCC, when they could not otherwise do so without significant hardship.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, which facility does the College provide in all of its campuses?
options: An onsite counselling suite
A campus health clinic
Multi-faith Prayer Rooms
A 24-hour open-access library
questions.explanation: Among the services of note, the policy states that the College has multi-faith Prayer Rooms in all of its campuses.
questions.source_excerpt: other services of note include multi-faith Prayer Rooms in all of its campuses

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, when is the Student Welfare service accessible to the student body?
options: Only during office hours, Monday to Friday in term time
By appointment arranged through the student's personal tutor
In the evenings only, outside scheduled teaching hours
Both during office hours and beyond office hours
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Student Welfare service is accessible to the student body both during and beyond office hours.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Welfare service, which provides chaplaincy and pastoral support to students, is accessible to the student body both during and beyond office hours;

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, what type of support does the Student Welfare service provide to students?
options: Financial advice and debt management
Chaplaincy and pastoral support
Academic tutoring and assignment feedback
Legal and immigration advice
questions.explanation: The policy describes the Student Welfare service as providing chaplaincy and pastoral support to students.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Welfare service, which provides chaplaincy and pastoral support to students

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, who is allocated to all students to help them in academic matters outside their scheduled sessions?
options: The College Registrar
Their programme leader
The Student Welfare Officer
Their personal tutor
questions.explanation: The policy states that personal tutors are allocated to all students to help them in academic matters outside their scheduled sessions.
questions.source_excerpt: personal tutors are allocated to all students to help them in academic matters outside their scheduled sessions

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, which of these is an example of help the College's administrative team may give students outside the academic framework?
options: Referral to the counselling service
Approving Hardship Fund applications
Processing DSA applications
Marking resubmitted coursework
questions.explanation: The administrative team may help with IT assistance, organising one-to-one sessions with a relevant member of staff or referral to the counselling service.
questions.source_excerpt: the College also has an administrative team that is available to assist students with other matters outside the academic framework. This may include IT assistance or organising one-to-one sessions with a relevant member of staff or referral to the counselling service.

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, at what point are applicants given the opportunity to declare any additional support they might need?
options: At enrolment after admission
During the application stage
At their first tutor meeting
Before their first assessment
questions.explanation: Applicants are given the opportunity to declare any additional support they might need during the application stage, so the College can assess how best to accommodate them.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants of London Churchill College are provided the opportunity to declare any additional support they might need during the application stage.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, which of the following may make a student eligible for funding from the Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA)?
options: Having a residual household income under £10,000
Being a care leaver
Having dependent children to care for
Having a specific learning difficulty
questions.explanation: Students with a disability, specific learning difficulty or long-term medical condition may be eligible for DSA funding.
questions.source_excerpt: If students have a disability, specific learning difficulty or long-term medical condition, they may be eligible for funding from the Disabled Student Allowances (DSA);

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, which of these is given as an example of an extra cost that the Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA) pays for?
options: Tuition fees for the programme
Rent and daily living costs
The cost of non-medical helpers
Childcare while attending lectures
questions.explanation: DSA pays for extra costs incurred as a direct result of a disability, including specialist equipment, non-medical helpers, photocopying and printer cartridges.
questions.source_excerpt: DSA pays for extra costs that students may incur in attending their programme as direct result of their disability, including but not limited to specialist equipment, non-medical helpers

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, are students who receive Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA) currently required to repay it?
options: Yes, once their earnings pass the repayment threshold
Yes, in full within a year of completing their course
No, at present it does not have to be paid back
Only if they withdraw before finishing the course
questions.explanation: The policy states that students who receive DSA are, at the present time, not required to repay the benefits received.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who receive such loans are, at the present time, not required to repay the benefits received;

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, with whom does the College maintain regular contact to help it comply with the Prevent duty?
options: The local police neighbourhood team
Its relevant Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator
The local authority safeguarding team
A Home Office Prevent inspector
questions.explanation: The College maintains regular contact with its relevant Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator, who arranges campus visits and helps the College comply with the duty.
questions.source_excerpt: The College maintains regular contact with its relevant Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator who arranges visits to the College campus and helps the College to comply with the duty

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, who is the contact point for learning, advice and support on students' emotional health and mental health?
options: The student's personal tutor
The College Registrar
The Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator
The Student Wellbeing Officer
questions.explanation: The policy names the Student Wellbeing Officer as the contact point for students' emotional wellbeing and mental health.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Wellbeing Officer is the contact point for learning, advice and support for students' emotional wellbeing and mental health.

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, the maximum LCC Hardship Fund award of £1,000 is for which students?
options: Students with a disability, dependent children and/or care leavers
International students who pay the full overseas tuition fee rate each year
Students who have also received an LCC Bursary discount in the same year
Students who apply within their first term of study on an HND course
questions.explanation: The policy states that the maximum Hardship Fund award is £1,000 for students with a disability, dependent children and/or care leavers.
questions.source_excerpt: The maximum award is £1,000 for students with a disability, dependent children and/or care leavers.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, how often can an eligible student apply to the LCC Hardship Fund?
options: Once per semester, twice a year
Only once during their whole programme
Only once during an academic year
Whenever needed, while budget remains
questions.explanation: One of the eligibility criteria is that the student can apply only once during an academic year.
questions.source_excerpt: The student can apply only once during an academic year.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, which of the following is a stated aim of the LCC Bursary Scheme?
options: To reduce the need for part-time work
To cover students' housing costs
To fund study trips abroad each year
To repay outstanding student loans
questions.explanation: The bursary aims to ease the transition into higher education, allow access to educational resources and equipment, reduce the need for part-time work and help students complete their studies.
questions.source_excerpt: This bursary will be aimed at easing the transition into higher education, allowing students in these groups to access educational resources and equipment, reduce the need for part-time work and help them successfully complete their studies.

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, where can an applicant obtain the Appeal Form to appeal a Hardship Fund or Bursary decision?
options: By emailing the College Registrar
From the VLE or the College reception
From the Principal's office on request
From their personal tutor after a meeting
questions.explanation: The Appeal Form can be downloaded from the VLE or obtained from the College reception.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants must complete Appeal Form which can be downloaded from VLE or obtained from the College reception.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, what happens to an appeal against a Hardship Fund or Bursary decision that is put forward without valid grounds?
options: It is passed to the Principal to decide
It is held until evidence is supplied
It goes to an independent review panel
It will not be considered by the College
questions.explanation: Applicants may appeal only on valid grounds; appeals put forward without valid grounds will not be considered.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants have the right to appeal a decision, providing that they have valid grounds for an appeal. Appeals put forward without valid grounds will not be considered.

questions.question: According to the Student Welfare Policy, which organisation processes students' applications for Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA)?
options: Student Finance England
The College Registry team
The Student Welfare Officer
A Needs Assessment Centre
questions.explanation: DSA applications are processed by the funding body, Student Finance England; the Student Welfare Officer only guides students on applying.
questions.source_excerpt: Applications will be processed by the funding body, i.e., Student Finance England.

questions.question: A student asks you why some harmful websites cannot be reached on College computers. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what explains this?
options: The College uses filtering to restrict access to harmful content on its IT equipment
The Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator blocks such sites during campus visits to the College
Sites are blocked only for students referred under the Safeguarding and Security Policy
Each campus's internet provider blocks them, as the College does not restrict content
questions.explanation: The policy states that the College uses filtering as a means of restricting access to harmful content on its IT equipment.
questions.source_excerpt: The College uses filtering as a means of restricting access to harmful content on its IT equipment;

questions.question: An applicant who has declared a disability is worried about sitting the College's entrance exam. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what can they do?
options: Wait until they are admitted, as adjustments can only be agreed with a personal tutor after enrolment
Ask Student Finance England to approve DSA first, as entrance exam adjustments depend on DSA approval
Apply to the LCC Hardship Fund, which pays for any adjustments they need for the entrance exam
Meet the College Registrar to discuss adjustments, which could include accommodating their disability
questions.explanation: Applicants who declare a disability can meet the College Registrar to discuss adjustments, which could include accommodating their disabilities for entrance exams.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants of London Churchill College who declare a disability can meet with the College Registrar to discuss any adjustments the College may make. These could include accommodating their disabilities for entrance exams

questions.question: A student needs help with an IT problem, which is not an academic matter. Under the Student Welfare Policy, who is available to assist them with this?
options: Their allocated personal tutor
The College's administrative team
The Student Wellbeing Officer
The Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator
questions.explanation: Personal tutors help with academic matters, while the College's administrative team assists with other matters outside the academic framework, which may include IT assistance.
questions.source_excerpt: While personal tutors are allocated to all students to help them in academic matters outside their scheduled sessions, the College also has an administrative team that is available to assist students with other matters outside the academic framework. This may include IT assistance

questions.question: An applicant asks why they are invited to declare any additional support needs when applying. According to the Student Welfare Policy, what does this allow?
options: It automatically registers them for Disabled Students' Allowance with Student Finance England
It places them on a priority list for the LCC Hardship Fund in their first academic year
It lets the College assess how best to accommodate their needs and helps their decision to study here
It lets their personal tutor set exam adjustments without involving the College Registrar
questions.explanation: Declaring support needs at the application stage allows the College to assess how best to accommodate the applicant's needs and helps the applicant's decision to study at the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants of London Churchill College are provided the opportunity to declare any additional support they might need during the application stage. This allows the College ... to assess how to best accommodate an applicant's needs and help the applicant's decision to study here.

questions.question: A qualifying student wants to obtain Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA). Under the Student Welfare Policy, which sequence of steps is correct?
options: The Student Welfare Officer guides the application, Student Finance England processes it, then a Needs Assessment referral may follow
A Needs Assessment Centre tests the student first, then its report goes to Student Finance England to process the DSA application
The College Registrar submits the DSA application, the Principal approves it, and then the Student Welfare Officer can arrange the tests
Student Finance England assesses the student's needs itself, then the Student Welfare Officer applies for DSA for the student
questions.explanation: The Student Welfare Officer guides a qualifying student on applying to Student Finance, which processes the application; once DSA is approved, the Officer can refer the student to a DSA-approved Needs Assessment Centre.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Welfare Officer can guide a qualifying student on applying for Disabled Student Allowance (DSA) from Student Finance. Once a student is approved for DSA the Student Welfare Officer can refer the student to a DSA-approved Needs Assessment Centre ... Applications will be processed by the funding body, i.e., Student Finance England.

questions.question: A student receiving Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA) asks if it can help with extra photocopying and printer cartridge costs caused by their disability. What does the Student Welfare Policy say?
options: No, DSA pays only for specialist equipment and non-medical helpers, not for everyday study costs
No, these costs must be claimed from the LCC Hardship Fund, which covers disability-related printing
Only if the College Registrar has first added these costs to the student's Support Agreement Plan
Yes, DSA can pay for such related expenses where they arise as a direct result of the disability
questions.explanation: DSA pays for extra costs incurred as a direct result of a disability, including but not limited to specialist equipment, non-medical helpers and related expenses such as photocopying and printer cartridges.
questions.source_excerpt: DSA pays for extra costs that students may incur in attending their programme as direct result of their disability, including but not limited to specialist equipment, non-medical helpers, and other related expenses, i.e., photocopying and printer cartridges.

questions.question: A student is not eligible for Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA) from Student Finance England but is eligible for the NHS Disabled Students' Allowance. Under the Student Welfare Policy, how should they apply?
options: Ask the Student Welfare Officer to reapply to Student Finance England on their behalf
Register or log in to their NHS Bursary account and apply for DSA via the NHS scheme
Apply to the LCC Hardship Fund, which replaces DSA for students funded by the NHS
Ask the College Registrar to award an equivalent allowance in a Support Agreement Plan
questions.explanation: The NHS Disabled Students' Allowance is a separate scheme; eligible students should register or log in to their NHS Bursary account and apply for DSA there.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who are not eligible for DSA from Student Finance England but are eligible for NHS Disabled Students' Allowance, which is a separate scheme, should register or login to NHS Bursary account and apply for DSA via

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, which of the following describes the role of the College's relevant Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator?
options: Approves Support Agreement Plans for students who declare a disability at the application stage
Books confidential one-to-one appointments for students with a mental health expert
Arranges campus visits and provides advice and guidance on risk and the appropriate response
Reviews Hardship Fund appeals that the College Registrar refers on after an initial evaluation
questions.explanation: The Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator arranges visits to the College campus, helps the College comply with the duty and provides advice and guidance on risk and on the appropriate response.
questions.source_excerpt: The College maintains regular contact with its relevant Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator who arranges visits to the College campus and helps the College to comply with the duty and provides advice and guidance on risk and on the appropriate response.

questions.question: A student would like to speak to a counsellor about their emotional wellbeing. Under the Student Welfare Policy, how does the Student Wellbeing Officer help them access this support?
options: Through signposting to third-party wellbeing advisers, counsellors and mental health advisers
By personally providing weekly counselling sessions as part of the Student Welfare service
By asking their personal tutor to include counselling within the student's scheduled sessions
By applying to Student Finance England for DSA funding to pay for a private counsellor
questions.explanation: The Student Wellbeing Officer is the contact point for emotional wellbeing and mental health; through signposting, students can access support from third-party wellbeing advisers, counsellors and mental health advisers.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Wellbeing Officer is the contact point for learning, advice and support for students' emotional wellbeing and mental health. Through signposting, a student can access various forms of support from a third-party of wellbeing advisers, counsellors, and mental health advisers.

questions.question: A student with a long-term mental illness that has a substantial adverse effect on their day-to-day activities asks how the College will support them. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what applies?
options: They are referred to the Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator, who assesses risk before any support is agreed
They can only receive support by submitting a mitigating circumstances claim for each assessment
They are advised to change course, as some programmes cannot accommodate mental health issues
They are defined as disabled, and the College supports them through the support agreement plan
questions.explanation: Such students are defined as disabled under the Equality Act 2010, and the College offers support to them through the support agreement plan.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with a long-term mental illness that has a substantial adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities are defined as disabled under the Equality Act 2010. The College offers support to students through the support agreement plan

questions.question: A part-time HND student with a residual household income of £8,000 per annum meets every other criterion and applies to the LCC Hardship Fund. Under the Student Welfare Policy, are they eligible?
options: Yes, since their residual household income falls below the £10,000 per annum limit
No, as the student must be enrolled on a full-time undergraduate (HND) course
No, because their residual household income is above the fund's permitted threshold
Yes, as part-time students qualify once they have paid their first instalment of fees
questions.explanation: Income under £10,000 is not enough on its own: the student must also meet all the listed criteria, including enrolment on a full-time undergraduate (HND) course.
questions.source_excerpt: To be eligible, student's residual household income must not exceed £10,000 per annum. In addition, they must meet all the eligibility criteria below: a) The student must be enrolled on a full-time undergraduate (HND) course.

questions.question: An extremely talented prospective student from a poor household in a developing country asks what LCC financial support they could receive. Under the Student Welfare Policy, which scheme fits?
options: The LCC Bursary Scheme, with up to £1,000 off course fees per annum
The LCC Hardship Fund, paying up to £1,000 if they apply before enrolling
Disabled Students' Allowance, processed for them by Student Finance England
An NHS Bursary, applied for through an NHS Bursary account before enrolling
questions.explanation: The LCC Bursary Scheme is for prospective students from poor households who are extremely talented and from a Least Developed or developing country; the Hardship Fund is for current students facing unforeseen hardship.
questions.source_excerpt: A Bursary scheme award is available to prospective students from poor households who are extremely talented but are from a Least Developed Country or a developing country. The student will be entitled to receive up to £1,000 discount from their course fees per annum.

questions.question: After the College Registrar's initial evaluation of an appeal against a Hardship Fund or Bursary decision, what may happen next under the Student Welfare Policy?
options: It is always sent to the Principal, who holds a formal hearing and then makes the final decision
It is returned to the student's personal tutor, who re-assesses the original application
It may be referred to a different procedure, rejected, or proceed to formal consideration
It is passed to an independent adjudicator, who decides the appeal within 28 days
questions.explanation: After the Registrar's initial evaluation, the student may be referred to a different procedure, the appeal may be rejected, or it may proceed to formal consideration.
questions.source_excerpt: On receipt of appeal, the College Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation to check that the student's appeal was submitted under the right procedures. The student then may be referred to a different procedure, appeal being rejected or proceeding to formal consideration.

questions.question: Four full-time HND students from developing countries, each facing unforeseen financial hardship and none having applied this academic year, apply to the LCC Hardship Fund. Under the Student Welfare Policy, which one is eligible?
options: A Home student with a residual household income of £12,000 a year who has paid the first fee instalment
An international (non-EU) student with a residual household income of £7,000 who has paid the first fee instalment
An EU student with a residual household income of £9,000 a year who has paid the first fee instalment
A Home student with a residual household income of £6,000 a year who has not yet paid the first fee instalment
questions.explanation: Only the EU student meets every listed criterion: income not exceeding £10,000, Home or EU status and the first fee instalment paid. The others fail on income, fee status or the instalment respectively.
questions.source_excerpt: To be eligible, student's residual household income must not exceed £10,000 per annum. In addition, they must meet all the eligibility criteria below: a) The student must be enrolled on a full-time undergraduate (HND) course. b) The student must be either a Home or EU student. ... d) The students must have paid their first instalment of the fees.

questions.question: A full-time HND Home student from a developing country, who has paid the first fee instalment and not applied this academic year, has a residual household income of exactly £10,000 per annum. Under the Student Welfare Policy, does their income rule them out of the Hardship Fund?
options: Yes; income must be below £10,000, so an income of exactly £10,000 is over the limit
No; income must not exceed £10,000, so an income of exactly £10,000 is within the limit
Yes; the income limit for full-time HND students is lower, set at £5,000 per annum
No; household income is assessed only for students who are not Home or EU students
questions.explanation: The policy requires a residual household income that must not exceed £10,000 per annum, so an income of exactly £10,000 meets that criterion.
questions.source_excerpt: To be eligible, student's residual household income must not exceed £10,000 per annum.

questions.question: A student's LCC Hardship Fund application was refused in October. In March of the same academic year a new, unforeseen hardship arises and they want to submit a fresh application. What does the Student Welfare Policy say?
options: They may apply, as each new unforeseen hardship counts as a separate application
They may apply, provided the Registrar confirms the new hardship is unrelated
They must first appeal the October refusal, after which a new application is allowed
They cannot, as a student can apply only once during an academic year
questions.explanation: One of the Hardship Fund eligibility criteria is that a student can apply only once during an academic year, so a second application in the same year is not permitted, whatever the outcome of the first.
questions.source_excerpt: The student can apply only once during an academic year.

questions.question: A full-time HND student has a long-term mental illness that has a substantial adverse effect on their normal day-to-day activities and applies to the LCC Hardship Fund. Under the Student Welfare Policy, which statement about their maximum award is correct?
options: They fall within the £1,000 maximum stated for students with a disability, as they are defined as disabled
The £1,000 maximum does not apply, as a mental illness is not treated as a disability under the policy
They cannot receive an award, as mental health needs are funded only through DSA from Student Finance
Their maximum is £10,000, as this is the figure the policy sets for students with a disability
questions.explanation: The policy defines students with such a long-term mental illness as disabled under the Equality Act 2010, and states that the maximum Hardship Fund award is £1,000 for students with a disability.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with a long-term mental illness that has a substantial adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities are defined as disabled under the Equality Act 2010. ... The maximum award is £1,000 for students with a disability, dependent children and/or care leavers.

questions.question: A colleague assumes that LCC Bursary Scheme applications follow a different route from LCC Hardship Fund applications. Under the Student Welfare Policy, which statement is correct?
options: Bursary applications go to Student Finance England, while Hardship Fund applications go to the Registrar
The College Registrar approves bursaries alone, while Hardship Fund awards are referred to the Principal
Both go in writing with evidence to the College Registrar, who submits a recommendation to the Principal
Bursary applications are made verbally at interview, while Hardship Fund applications need written evidence
questions.explanation: The policy sets the same process for both schemes: applications are sent in writing with supporting evidence to the College Registrar, who reviews their merit and submits a recommendation to the Principal.
questions.source_excerpt: Applications must be sent in writing to the College Registrar with supporting evidence, who will review the merit of the application and submit the recommendation to the Principal for approval/consideration.

questions.question: Four prospective students ask about the LCC Bursary Scheme. Under the Student Welfare Policy, which of them falls within the group the scheme is available to?
options: An extremely talented student from a wealthy household in a Least Developed Country
An extremely talented student from a poor household in a developing country
A student of average academic ability from a poor household in a developing country
An extremely talented student from a poor household in a high-income country
questions.explanation: The bursary is available to prospective students from poor households who are extremely talented and from a Least Developed Country or a developing country; each other student lacks one of these conditions.
questions.source_excerpt: A Bursary scheme award is available to prospective students from poor households who are extremely talented but are from a Least Developed Country or a developing country.

questions.question: A student asks how their appeal against an LCC Bursary Scheme decision will be handled once it has been submitted. Which statement is supported by the Student Welfare Policy?
options: The Principal carries out the initial evaluation of each appeal before any other step
The appeal moves straight to formal consideration without any initial procedural check
The outcome is given verbally at a meeting with the student's allocated personal tutor
The decision on the appeal will be communicated to the student in writing
questions.explanation: The College Registrar, not the Principal, undertakes an initial evaluation of each appeal, which may lead to referral, rejection or formal consideration; the decision is then communicated to the student in writing.
questions.source_excerpt: On receipt of appeal, the College Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation to check that the student's appeal was submitted under the right procedures. ... The decision will be communicated to the student in writing.

questions.question: An applicant who declared a disability agreed entrance exam adjustments with the College Registrar and has now been admitted. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what applies to their support during the programme?
options: Support ends at admission, and any further help depends on DSA approval by Student Finance England
Continued additional support can be agreed for their programme, with the full support of College staff
The entrance exam adjustments carry over, but no further support can be agreed after enrolment
Their personal tutor takes over and agrees any adjustments informally with each module lecturer
questions.explanation: Adjustments discussed with the Registrar can include agreeing continued additional support during the tenure of the programme, and once admitted students can have the full support of College staff with their additional needs.
questions.source_excerpt: These could include accommodating their disabilities for entrance exams and agreeing continued additional support for them during the tenure of their programmes; ... Once admitted, students can have the full support of the College staff in helping them with their additional needs;

questions.question: A student's Support Agreement Plan gives them additional time in written exams. They ask whether additional time could also be agreed for an assessed presentation. What does the Student Welfare Policy say?
options: No; additional time is listed for exams only, so presentations need a mitigating circumstances claim
Only if Student Finance England approves DSA funding to cover the extra presentation time
Yes; the support that may be agreed includes additional time in exams and presentations
No; presentations can be adjusted only through an extended submission deadline
questions.explanation: The support that may be agreed in a Support Agreement Plan includes additional time in exams and presentations, as well as extended deadlines, technology-aided learning and extended library borrowing.
questions.source_excerpt: The support agreed may include additional time in exams and presentations, extended submission deadlines or permission for technology-aided learning during lectures

questions.question: A student with a long-term medical condition says they have no disability or specific learning difficulty, and asks whether Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA) could still apply to them. What does the Student Welfare Policy say?
options: They may be eligible, as DSA funding also extends to students with a long-term medical condition
They are not eligible, as DSA is limited to disabilities that were declared at the application stage
They must use the NHS scheme, as Student Finance England's DSA excludes long-term medical conditions
They are not eligible unless a Needs Assessment Centre first confirms that they have a disability
questions.explanation: The policy states that students with a disability, specific learning difficulty or long-term medical condition may be eligible for DSA funding.
questions.source_excerpt: If students have a disability, specific learning difficulty or long-term medical condition, they may be eligible for funding from the Disabled Student Allowances (DSA);

questions.question: A student approved for Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA) asks whether it will pay for the standard textbooks that every student on their course must buy. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what is the correct answer?
options: Yes; once approved, DSA pays for any cost the student incurs in attending their programme
Yes, provided the College Registrar first adds the textbooks to the student's Support Agreement Plan
No; DSA pays only for specialist equipment and never for any other related expenses
No; DSA is for extra costs arising as a direct result of the disability, not costs all students bear
questions.explanation: DSA pays for extra costs students incur in attending their programme as a direct result of their disability; standard textbooks that every student must buy are not such an extra cost.
questions.source_excerpt: DSA pays for extra costs that students may incur in attending their programme as direct result of their disability, including but not limited to specialist equipment, non-medical helpers, and other related expenses, i.e., photocopying and printer cartridges.

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, which role both meets students with declared disabilities to work out a Support Agreement Plan and carries out the initial evaluation of Hardship Fund or Bursary appeals?
options: The Student Welfare Officer
The College Registrar
The Principal
The Student Wellbeing Officer
questions.explanation: The College Registrar holds the confidential meeting to work out a Support Agreement Plan and, on receipt of an appeal, undertakes the initial evaluation; the Principal considers the Registrar's recommendations on applications.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with declared disabilities are invited to attend a confidential meeting with the College Registrar to work out a Support Agreement Plan ... On receipt of appeal, the College Registrar will undertake an initial evaluation

questions.question: A student contacts the College one evening, outside office hours, seeking pastoral support. A colleague says nothing is available until the next working day. Under the Student Welfare Policy, is the colleague right?
options: Yes; pastoral support is offered only during office hours, through the Student Welfare Officer
Yes; outside office hours, students must be referred to the Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator instead
No; the Student Welfare service, which provides pastoral support, is accessible beyond office hours
No; out-of-hours pastoral support can be arranged only by the student's allocated personal tutor
questions.explanation: The Student Welfare service, which provides chaplaincy and pastoral support, is accessible to students both during and beyond office hours.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Welfare service, which provides chaplaincy and pastoral support to students, is accessible to the student body both during and beyond office hours;

questions.question: An admissions colleague suggests steering an applicant with a long-term mental illness away from a demanding course. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what is the College's position?
options: It does not discriminate against students with mental health issues in admission or choice of course
It may limit course choice where a mental illness is judged likely to affect academic performance
It may defer admission until the Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator has assessed the applicant's mental health
It considers mental health only after enrolment, through a mitigating circumstances claim
questions.explanation: The College does not discriminate against students with mental health issues in terms of admission, choice of course or the operation of its education and support services.
questions.source_excerpt: The College offers support to students through the support agreement plan and does not discriminate against students with mental health issues, in terms of admission, choice of course and in the operation of education and support services.

questions.question: A student on a two-year programme received a £1,000 LCC Bursary Scheme fee discount in their first year. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what can they receive for their second year?
options: Nothing further, as £1,000 is the limit for the whole programme
Up to £500, as the discount halves after the first year of study
A further £1,000 only after reapplying to Student Finance England
A further discount of up to £1,000, as the limit applies per annum
questions.explanation: The bursary entitles the student to up to £1,000 discount from their course fees per annum, so the limit applies to each year rather than to the programme as a whole.
questions.source_excerpt: The student will be entitled to receive up to £1,000 discount from their course fees per annum.

questions.question: A student refused a Hardship Fund award emails the Principal saying they disagree and asks for the decision to be looked at again. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what must they do to appeal?
options: Nothing further, as an email to the Principal is treated as a formal appeal under the policy
Complete the Appeal Form, from the VLE or College reception, and have valid grounds for appeal
Submit a fresh Hardship Fund application setting out the same circumstances in more detail
Ask Student Finance England to review the decision, as it oversees the College's hardship awards
questions.explanation: Applicants may appeal only where they have valid grounds, and must complete the Appeal Form, which can be downloaded from the VLE or obtained from the College reception.
questions.source_excerpt: Applicants have the right to appeal a decision, providing that they have valid grounds for an appeal. ... Applicants must complete Appeal Form which can be downloaded from VLE or obtained from the College reception.

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, which of these measures is carried out by the College itself rather than by its relevant Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator?
options: Arranging visits to the College campus
Helping the College to comply with the Prevent duty
Filtering to restrict access to harmful content on its IT equipment
Providing advice and guidance on risk and on the appropriate response
questions.explanation: The College itself uses filtering to restrict access to harmful content on its IT equipment; campus visits, help with compliance and advice on risk come from the Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator.
questions.source_excerpt: The College uses filtering as a means of restricting access to harmful content on its IT equipment; ... The College maintains regular contact with its relevant Prevent Duty Co-Ordinator who arranges visits to the College campus and helps the College to comply with the duty and provides advice and guidance on risk and on the appropriate response.

questions.question: Under the Student Welfare Policy, which of these is not a function given to the Student Welfare Officer?
options: Recommending Hardship Fund applications to the Principal for approval
Guiding a qualifying student on applying for DSA from Student Finance
Referring a DSA-approved student to a DSA-approved Needs Assessment Centre
Booking a confidential one-to-one with a mental health expert for a student
questions.explanation: The Student Welfare Officer guides DSA applications, refers DSA-approved students for needs assessment and can book confidential mental health appointments; Hardship Fund applications go to the College Registrar, who recommends them to the Principal.
questions.source_excerpt: The Student Welfare Officer can guide a qualifying student on applying for Disabled Student Allowance (DSA) from Student Finance. Once a student is approved for DSA the Student Welfare Officer can refer the student to a DSA-approved Needs Assessment Centre ... Students can consult the Student Welfare Officer to book a confidential one-to-one appointment for them with a mental health expert;

questions.question: A student with a declared disability, already approved for Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA), needs additional time in exams and specialist equipment. Under the Student Welfare Policy, which pairing of routes is correct?
options: Exam time agreed with the College Registrar in a Support Agreement Plan; the equipment funded through DSA
Exam time funded through DSA from Student Finance England; the equipment agreed in a Support Agreement Plan
Both provided through the LCC Hardship Fund, applied for in writing to the Registrar with supporting evidence
Both approved by the Student Welfare Officer, who grants the exam time and buys equipment from College budgets
questions.explanation: Additional time in exams is support agreed with the College Registrar in a Support Agreement Plan, whereas DSA pays for extra costs arising from the disability, such as specialist equipment.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with declared disabilities are invited to attend a confidential meeting with the College Registrar to work out a Support Agreement Plan ... The support agreed may include additional time in exams and presentations ... DSA pays for extra costs that students may incur in attending their programme as direct result of their disability, including but not limited to specialist equipment

questions.question: An enrolled full-time HND student whose income has suddenly and unexpectedly collapsed mid-year asks to apply to the LCC Bursary Scheme. Under the Student Welfare Policy, which statement is correct?
options: The Bursary Scheme fits, as it gives up to £1,000 off course fees per annum to any student facing financial difficulty
Neither scheme fits, as LCC financial support can only be applied for before a student first enrols on a course at the College
The Hardship Fund fits, as it supports current students facing unforeseen hardship; the Bursary is for prospective students
DSA fits, as Student Finance England funds unexpected costs that arise for any student part-way through their course
questions.explanation: The Hardship Fund's aim is to support current students who experience unforeseen financial hardship during their studies, while the Bursary Scheme is available to prospective students.
questions.source_excerpt: The aim of the Hardship Fund is to provide financial support to all our current students who have experienced unforeseen financial hardship during their studies. ... A Bursary scheme award is available to prospective students from poor households who are extremely talented but are from a Least Developed Country or a developing country.

questions.question: A full-time HND Home student from a developing country, who is a care leaver, has paid the first fee instalment and has not applied this academic year. Their residual household income is £14,000 per annum. Under the Student Welfare Policy, are they eligible for the Hardship Fund?
options: Yes; care leavers can receive up to £1,000, so the household income limit does not apply to them
No; the £1,000 maximum for care leavers does not lift the £10,000 household income limit
Yes, but their award is reduced to £500 because their income is above the usual £10,000 threshold
No; care leavers must apply to the LCC Bursary Scheme rather than to the LCC Hardship Fund
questions.explanation: Care leavers are named only in setting the £1,000 maximum award; every applicant must still have a residual household income not exceeding £10,000 per annum, so £14,000 rules this student out.
questions.source_excerpt: The maximum award is £1,000 for students with a disability, dependent children and/or care leavers. ... To be eligible, student's residual household income must not exceed £10,000 per annum. In addition, they must meet all the eligibility criteria below

questions.question: A student with a long-term mental illness that has a substantial adverse effect on their normal day-to-day activities asks whether Disabled Students' Allowances (DSA) could fund extra study costs it causes. Under the Student Welfare Policy, what is correct?
options: No; DSA covers physical disabilities only, so these costs must be claimed from the LCC Hardship Fund
No; the policy limits mental health support to signposting by the Student Wellbeing Officer
They may be eligible only via the NHS scheme, as Student Finance England's DSA excludes mental illness
They may be eligible, as they are defined as disabled and DSA pays extra costs caused by a disability
questions.explanation: Such students are defined as disabled under the Equality Act 2010, and students with a disability may be eligible for DSA, which pays extra costs incurred as a direct result of the disability.
questions.source_excerpt: If students have a disability, specific learning difficulty or long-term medical condition, they may be eligible for funding from the Disabled Student Allowances (DSA); ... Students with a long-term mental illness that has a substantial adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities are defined as disabled under the Equality Act 2010.

questions.question: A full-time HND EU student from a high-income country has a residual household income of £6,000, has paid the first fee instalment and has not applied this academic year. Under the Student Welfare Policy, are they eligible for the LCC Hardship Fund?
options: No; besides the income limit, the student must also be from a Least Developed Country or a developing country
Yes; the country requirement applies only to the LCC Bursary Scheme and not to the LCC Hardship Fund
Yes; an income below the £10,000 limit is on its own enough to make a student eligible for the fund
No; EU students may apply only to the LCC Bursary Scheme, as the Hardship Fund is open to Home students alone
questions.explanation: Meeting the income limit is not enough: the student must also meet all the listed criteria, including being from a Least Developed Country or a developing country.
questions.source_excerpt: To be eligible, student's residual household income must not exceed £10,000 per annum. In addition, they must meet all the eligibility criteria below: ... b) The student must be either a Home or EU student. c) The student must be a student from a Least Developed Country or a

questions.question: Four current full-time HND students ask the LCC Hardship Fund for help. Under the Student Welfare Policy, which request matches what the fund is intended to meet?
options: Closing a gap between income and spending that has grown all year because they budgeted poorly
Paying their first instalment of fees, which they have not yet paid for this academic year
A second award this academic year, after an earlier application to the fund succeeded
An urgent, short-term need from unforeseen hardship that would stop them continuing their studies
questions.explanation: The fund meets short-term, urgent needs arising from unforeseen hardship so students can continue their studies; it is not for long-term shortfalls from impractical planning, requires the first fee instalment to be paid and allows one application per academic year.
questions.source_excerpt: The hardship fund is to ensure that it meets student's short-term, urgent needs ... The fund, however, is not suitable for long-term shortfall between the student's income and expenses to compensate for impractical planning. ... d) The students must have paid their first instalment of the fees. e) The student can apply only once during an academic year.

questions.question: A student tells you they are struggling with a physical health problem and are thinking of temporarily suspending their studies. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, what should happen in the first instance?
options: They should complete the Student Suspension Form and send it straight to the Assessment Board for approval
They should discuss it with their Personal Tutor, or another appropriate member of staff
They should write to the Registrar requesting an immediate suspension, attaching their medical evidence
They should notify Student Finance (SLC), which approves suspensions for funded students
questions.explanation: The policy states that, in the first instance, students should discuss their intention to apply for a temporary suspension with their Personal Tutor or another appropriate member of staff to decide whether it is appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: In the first instance, students should discuss their intention to apply for a temporary suspension of studies with their Personal Tutor, or other appropriate member of staff, to determine if such a course of action would be appropriate for the student's situation

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, how is a student's completed self-suspension application reviewed and approved?
options: The Personal Tutor reviews and decides the application, then informs the Academic Registry of the outcome in writing
The Assessment Board reviews it first, then passes it to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel for final approval and sign-off
The Registrar approves or declines it directly, without referring it to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel or any board
The Registrar sends it to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel, whose recommendation goes to the Assessment Board for approval
questions.explanation: The Registrar submits the form and evidence to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel for review, and the Panel's recommendation is forwarded to the Assessment Board for approval.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar should submit the Student Suspension Form with all relevant evidence to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel for review. ... The recommendation will be forwarded to the Assessment Board for approval

questions.question: According to the Suspension of Studies Policy, within what timeframe must a student be informed in writing of the decision on their suspension application, whether it is approved or declined?
options: Within seven days of the decision
Within 48 hours of the decision
Within 15 working days of the decision
Within one calendar month of the decision
questions.explanation: The policy requires the student to be informed in writing within seven days of the decision, for both approved and declined applications.
questions.source_excerpt: If the suspension of studies application is approved, the student will be informed in writing within seven days of the decision being taken. ... If a suspension of studies application is declined, the student will be informed in writing within seven days of the decision.

questions.question: A student has received written notification that their suspension application was declined and wants to appeal. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, what should you tell them to do?
options: Appeal verbally to their Personal Tutor within seven days of the decision being taken
Write to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification
Write to the Assessment Board within 30 days of the written notification of the decision
Submit a new Student Suspension Form, as declined applications cannot be appealed
questions.explanation: An appeal is lodged by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision.
questions.source_excerpt: A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of the suspension by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision

questions.question: A student's suspension period has ended, but they have not re-enrolled or returned to classes, assuming their suspension simply continues. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, what is the position?
options: Their suspension is automatically extended for one further term while the College contacts them
Their suspension continues until they next get in touch with the College
It is not automatically extended; they must re-apply for a further suspension if needed
The Registrar automatically extends it using the original evidence submitted with their application
questions.explanation: Failure to re-enrol and attend classes does not automatically extend a suspension; the student must re-apply for a further suspension if it is required and appropriate.
questions.source_excerpt: When a student's period of suspension has come to an end, s/he is obliged to contact the College to determine the enrolment status and to re-enrol on the programme of study. Failure to re-enrol and attend classes will NOT automatically extend a student's suspension of studies and students must re-apply for a further suspension of studies if it is required and deemed appropriate
