questions.question: According to the Suspension of Studies Policy, what happens if a student neither resumes studies on the agreed return date nor re-applies for a further suspension period?
options: They are automatically placed on a further suspension period
They will be terminated from their programme of study
They are referred back to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel
They receive a formal warning and a new return date
questions.explanation: The policy states that a student who does not resume on the agreed return date or re-apply for a further suspension will be terminated from their programme of study.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student does not resume studies on the agreed return date or re-apply for a further suspension period, he/she will be terminated from their programme of study

questions.question: According to the Suspension of Studies Policy, which of the following is a permissible ground for appealing a suspension decision?
options: The student disagrees with the academic judgement the Assessment Board reached when it considered their case
The student's attendance and engagement have improved significantly since the suspension decision was made
New material evidence has emerged that the student could not provide earlier due to exceptional circumstances
The student would now prefer a shorter or longer suspension period than the one set by the Assessment Board
questions.explanation: Appeals are permitted only where the policy was not followed or where new material evidence has emerged that the student could not provide earlier due to exceptional circumstances.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following grounds: 6.2.1. In circumstances where there is evidence that the College's Suspension of Studies Policy has not been followed; 6.2.2. New material evidence has emerged, which the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier in the process

questions.question: A student has persistently failed to engage with their studies and their attendance is unsatisfactory. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, can the College suspend them?
options: No, a suspension of studies must be initiated by the student through the Student Suspension Form
No, attendance concerns must be dealt with under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
Yes, provided the student also has compelling financial reasons for suspension
Yes, non-engagement, including unsatisfactory attendance, is an academic reason for suspension
questions.explanation: The College may suspend a student for academic reasons, which include non-engagement with study, including an unsatisfactory attendance level.
questions.source_excerpt: The College may suspend a student from his/her studies based on academic reasons. These may include: a) Non-engagement with study, including an unsatisfactory attendance level. b) Insufficient academic progression as per the academic regulations.

questions.question: According to the Suspension of Studies Policy, where should a student submit their completed Student Suspension Form?
options: To the Registry Office, together with all relevant supporting evidence
To their Personal Tutor, who countersigns it and forwards it to the Assessment Board
Directly to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel, which reviews it before any other office
To the Finance Office, which then notifies Student Finance (SLC)
questions.explanation: The policy states that students fill in the Student Suspension Form (placed in the student portal) and, where possible, submit it to the Registry Office together with all relevant supporting evidence.
questions.source_excerpt: they should fill the Student Suspension Form (placed in the student portal). Where possible students should submit the form to the Registry Office together with all relevant supporting evidence

questions.question: A student tells you that serious domestic difficulties are substantially affecting their studies. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, may they request an intermission from study?
options: No, serious domestic difficulties are not among the listed grounds for an intermission
No, domestic matters must be handled under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
Yes, provided their attendance has already fallen to an unsatisfactory level as a result
Yes, compassionate reasons, including serious domestic difficulties, are a listed ground
questions.explanation: Compassionate reasons, including serious domestic difficulties, are one of the listed grounds on which a student may request an intermission.
questions.source_excerpt: A student may request an intermission from his/her study based on the following grounds: ... d) Compassionate reasons (including serious domestic difficulties)

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, once a suspension of studies application is approved, which external parties does the Academic Registry inform?
options: The Awarding Bodies, SLC and any other parties the College deems relevant
None; the Registry informs internal departments, not external bodies
The Student Loans Company (SLC), but not the Awarding Bodies, as the student's funding is affected
The Awarding Bodies, but not SLC, as funding is handled by Finance
questions.explanation: On approval, the Academic Registry informs internal departments and also the external parties named in the policy: the Awarding Bodies, SLC and any other parties the College deems relevant.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic Registry will also inform external parties namely the Awarding Bodies, SLC and any other parties deemed relevant by the College

questions.question: When reviewing a self-suspension application, what should the Mitigating Circumstances Panel also indicate under the Suspension of Studies Policy?
options: The grade the student is expected to achieve on their return, with the reasons for this
The amount of tuition fees to be refunded for the suspended period
Whether access to any College facilities should be maintained, with a rationale
Whether the student should also be referred under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
questions.explanation: Alongside its recommendation, the Panel should indicate whether the student's access to any College facilities should be maintained and must give a rationale for this.
questions.source_excerpt: The Mitigating Circumstances Panel should also indicate whether access to any College facilities should be maintained and must provide a rationale for this request.

questions.question: According to the Suspension of Studies Policy, which of the following is the policy intended to clarify about students who are suspended?
options: The tuition fees they must pay to keep their place on the programme while suspended
The marks they will receive for any modules left incomplete when the suspension began
Their entitlement to access services while they are suspended from their studies
Their eligibility to transfer to a different programme while they are suspended
questions.explanation: One of the policy's stated aims is to clarify the entitlement of suspended students to access services.
questions.source_excerpt: The aim of this policy is to outline the procedure to be followed for students seeking suspension, to clarify the entitlement of suspended students to access services

questions.question: How does the Suspension of Studies Policy define a suspension of study?
options: An approved intermission of a specified duration that stops the student continuing the programme
A permanent withdrawal from the College that ends the student's registration on their programme
A reduced timetable allowing the student to keep studying part-time for an agreed period
An open-ended break with no fixed end date, lasting until the student decides to return
questions.explanation: The policy defines a suspension of study as an approved intermission to a specified duration that prevents the student from continuing the programme of study.
questions.source_excerpt: A suspension of study is an approved intermission to a specified duration that prevents a student from continuing the programme of study

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, the College may suspend a student on disciplinary grounds. Under which procedure is such a suspension to be considered?
options: The Academic Regulations governing assessment and progression
The Mitigating Circumstances Panel's review and recommendation procedure
The College Appeals Policy and Procedure, via the Registrar
The Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
questions.explanation: The policy states that a suspension on disciplinary grounds is to be considered under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: The College retains the right to suspend a student for a period in relation to disciplinary grounds where it is deemed appropriate. Suspension in this context is to be considered under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, which body must approve any suspension decision relating to a student's academic progression?
options: The Mitigating Circumstances Panel
The Assessment Board
The Academic Office
The student's Personal Tutor
questions.explanation: The policy states that any suspension decision relating to academic progression must be approved by the Assessment Board.
questions.source_excerpt: Any suspension decision relating to academic progression must be approved by the Assessment Board

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, which health issues can be a ground for a student to request an intermission from study?
options: Physical health issues only, where supported by a hospital or GP letter
Only conditions that have been formally registered with the College as a disability
Mental or physical health issues that are affecting their studies
Mental health issues only, where confirmed by the College's counselling service
questions.explanation: The first listed ground for requesting an intermission is health issues, whether mental or physical, that are affecting the student's studies.
questions.source_excerpt: A student may request an intermission from his/her study based on the following grounds: a) Health issues (mental or physical) that affecting studies

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, students are advised to seek further academic advice from their personal tutor about the impact a suspension may have on which areas?
options: Their attendance record, module choices and expected graduation date
Their disciplinary record, appeal rights and Awarding Body registration
Their access to College facilities, the library and their IT account
Their academic performance, financial situation and Student Finance (SLC)
questions.explanation: Students are advised to ask their personal tutor about the impact a suspension may have on their academic performance, financial situation and Student Finance (SLC).
questions.source_excerpt: Students are advised to seek further academic advice from their personal tutor to determine the impact a suspension of studies may have on their academic performance, financial ... situation, and Student Finance (SLC)

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, where is the Student Suspension Form placed for students who wish to apply for a temporary suspension of studies?
options: In the student portal
On the staff intranet
In the programme handbook
On the Student Finance (SLC) website
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Student Suspension Form is placed in the student portal for students to fill in.
questions.source_excerpt: If students wish to proceed with a temporary suspension of studies application, they should fill the Student Suspension Form (placed in the student portal).

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, who signs off a completed suspension application before the student is formally notified of the outcome?
options: The Chair of the Assessment Board
The Chair of the Mitigating Circumstances Panel
The Registrar and the student's Personal Tutor
The Head of Student Support, on behalf of the College
questions.explanation: The student is notified formally of the outcome once the application has been completed and signed off by the Chair of the Mitigating Circumstances Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: Once the application is completed by both the student and Mitigating Circumstances Panel and signed off by the Chair of the Panel, the student will be notified formally of the outcome

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, which internal departments does the Academic Registry inform when a suspension of studies application is approved?
options: Finance and Student Support only, as the Academic Office is informed by the Panel instead
All teaching departments, including Admissions, IT Services and the Library
The Academic Office only, which then passes the outcome on to Finance
All relevant departments, including Finance, Student Support and the Academic Office
questions.explanation: On approval, the Academic Registry informs all relevant internal departments, including Finance, Student Support and the Academic Office.
questions.source_excerpt: The Academic Registry will inform all relevant internal departments including, Finance, Student Support and the Academic Office.

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, when is a suspended student expected to establish contact with the College?
options: Before the scheduled date of their return to study
Within 15 working days after they have returned to study
Only if they wish to extend their suspension
Once a month throughout the whole suspension period
questions.explanation: The policy expects a student to establish contact with the College before the scheduled return to study, so that any support needed on return can be arranged.
questions.source_excerpt: A student is expected to establish contact with the College before the scheduled return to study. The College ensures to facilitate any support which may be required upon the students return

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, where the Assessment Board has suspended a student for an academic reason, what must the student do before returning to study?
options: Obtain a written reference from their Personal Tutor confirming their readiness
Submit a new Student Suspension Form and supporting evidence to the Registry
Fulfil the conditions stated in the decision, on the agreed timeline, before returning
Pass a re-entry assessment set by the Mitigating Circumstances Panel before returning
questions.explanation: Where the Assessment Board has suspended a student for an academic reason, the student must fulfil the stated conditions before returning to study, on the agreed timeline.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a suspension decision has been taken by the Assessment Board for an academic reason, the student must fulfil the conditions stated before the return to study on the agreed timeline.

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, in accordance with which policy must an appeal against a suspension decision be considered?
options: The Student Complaints Policy and Procedure
The College Appeals Policy and Procedure
The Mitigating Circumstances Policy
The Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
questions.explanation: The policy states that the appeal process must be considered in accordance with the College Appeals Policy and Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: The appeal process must be considered in accordance with the College Appeals Policy and Procedure.

questions.question: The Suspension of Studies Policy gives examples of matters for which students may self-certify. Which of the following is given as one of those examples?
options: Religious holidays and caring responsibilities
Part-time work shifts and graduate job interviews
Driving tests and family celebrations abroad
Travel disruption and moving to new accommodation
questions.explanation: The policy gives religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments and caring responsibilities as examples of matters students may self-certify for.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities.

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, how may lateness by a student with a disability be treated?
options: It must always be recorded as an unauthorised absence under attendance rules
It is excused automatically once the disability is disclosed
It may be noted on file, but it cannot be treated as a reasonable adjustment
It may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis
questions.explanation: The policy gives the example that lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment for a student with a disability, on a case-by-case basis.
questions.source_excerpt: References are made throughout the EIA to ensure that accommodation is made for students with a disability. For example, lateness may be approved as a reasonable adjustment on a case-by-case basis.

questions.question: How does London Churchill College use the term 'suspension' in the Suspension of Studies Policy?
options: Only for an intermission the student requests, never for one imposed by the College
As a temporary status, whether the student seeks the intermission or the College imposes it
As a permanent status that applies only when the College acts on disciplinary grounds
Only for a break imposed by the College, never for one the student asks for
questions.explanation: LCC uses 'suspension' as a temporary status for a student who is either seeking an intermission from studies or has it imposed by the College.
questions.source_excerpt: London Churchill College (LCC) use the term `suspension' as a temporary status for a student that is either seeking an intermission from studies or has it imposed by the College.

questions.question: A student's circumstances are not health, pregnancy, compassionate or financial, but they would substantially impair the student's ability to pursue their programme. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, may the student request an intermission?
options: Yes, the grounds include any other circumstances which would substantially impair a student's ability to pursue their programme
No, a substantial impairment that is not on the named list can only be addressed by the College suspending them for academic reasons
No, the named grounds are exhaustive, so a substantial impairment from any other cause cannot support a request
Yes, but only once the Assessment Board has confirmed that the impairment has caused insufficient academic progression
questions.explanation: The final listed ground covers any other circumstances which would substantially impair a student's ability to pursue their programme.
questions.source_excerpt: A student may request an intermission from his/her study based on the following grounds: ... f) Any other circumstances which would substantially impair a student's ability to pursue their programme

questions.question: A suspension decision was taken on 3 March, and the student received the written notification of it on 8 March. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, from when does the student's 15-working-day period to appeal run?
options: From 3 March, the date on which the suspension decision was taken
From 8 March, when the student received their written notification
From the date the Academic Registry informs the Awarding Bodies and SLC
From the student's scheduled return date at the end of the suspension
questions.explanation: An appeal must be lodged in writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision, so the period runs from 8 March.
questions.source_excerpt: A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of the suspension by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision

questions.question: A student appeals a suspension decision because, they say, the Registrar never submitted their Student Suspension Form to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel as required. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, is this a permissible ground?
options: No, an appeal is permitted only where new material evidence has emerged since the decision
No, complaints about how the Registry handled a form fall under the Student Code of Conduct instead
Yes, evidence that the Suspension of Studies Policy has not been followed is a permissible ground
Yes, but only if the student also provides medical evidence that was not available earlier
questions.explanation: One of the two permissible appeal grounds is evidence that the College's Suspension of Studies Policy has not been followed, which would cover a failure to send the form to the Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following grounds: 6.2.1. In circumstances where there is evidence that the College's Suspension of Studies Policy has not been followed

questions.question: The Registrar has sent a student's Suspension Form to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel, but some required supporting evidence is missing. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, when will the Panel consider the application?
options: Straight away, making its recommendation on the basis of the information it already holds
Only after the Assessment Board has reviewed and approved the missing evidence itself
At its next meeting, noting the gaps in its statement to the Assessment Board
Once all of the required information and supporting evidence are complete
questions.explanation: The Panel considers the application only if all required information and supporting evidence are complete, and then includes a statement of its recommendations.
questions.source_excerpt: If all required information and supporting evidence are complete, the application will then be considered by the Mitigating Circumstances Panel, who will include a statement indicating its recommendations.

questions.question: A student has made insufficient academic progression as per the academic regulations. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, can the College suspend them, and what approval is required?
options: No, the College may suspend students only on disciplinary grounds under the Code of Conduct
Yes, and their Personal Tutor may approve it after discussing the situation with the student
Yes, it is an academic reason, and the decision must be approved by the Assessment Board
Yes, it is an academic reason, and the Mitigating Circumstances Panel approves it
questions.explanation: Insufficient academic progression is an academic reason for which the College may suspend a student, and any suspension decision relating to academic progression must be approved by the Assessment Board.
questions.source_excerpt: The College may suspend a student from his/her studies based on academic reasons. These may include: ... b) Insufficient academic progression as per the academic regulations. ... Any suspension decision relating to academic progression must be approved by the Assessment Board

questions.question: A student whose partner is expecting a baby wants time away from their studies for parental leave. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, may they request an intermission on this basis?
options: No, only a student who is pregnant may request an intermission on maternity grounds
No, parental leave is not a ground, although compelling financial reasons might be
Yes, but only if they can also show health issues that are affecting their studies
Yes, pregnancy, maternity and parental leave are among the listed grounds
questions.explanation: Pregnancy, maternity and parental leave are listed among the grounds on which a student may request an intermission from study.
questions.source_excerpt: A student may request an intermission from his/her study based on the following grounds: ... c) Pregnancy, maternity and Parental leave

questions.question: A student asks to pause their studies indefinitely and return whenever they feel ready. How does this request fit the Suspension of Studies Policy's definition of a suspension of study?
options: It fits, as a suspension is an open-ended intermission that the student ends by giving notice
It does not fit, as a suspension is an approved intermission to a specified duration
It fits, provided the student contacts the College at least once in each academic year
It does not fit, as a suspension can only be imposed by the College and never requested
questions.explanation: The policy defines a suspension of study as an approved intermission to a specified duration, so an open-ended pause does not match the definition.
questions.source_excerpt: A suspension of study is an approved intermission to a specified duration that prevents a student from continuing the programme of study

questions.question: A registered student asks whether they can simply take longer than the normal study period to finish their course. What does the Suspension of Studies Policy expect of them?
options: They may extend informally by up to one year if their Personal Tutor agrees to it
They may take as long as they need, provided they keep paying their tuition fees
To complete within the normal study periods, unless they withdraw or suspend their studies
To complete within the normal study periods, unless the Assessment Board agrees to extend them
questions.explanation: Once registered, students are expected to complete within the normal study periods unless they withdraw from the College or suspend their studies.
questions.source_excerpt: Once a student has registered on a course, they are expected to complete the course within the normal study periods unless they withdraw from the College or suspend their studies

questions.question: A student being considered for suspension has had their attendance at panel hearings affected by their disability. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, what should happen?
options: The Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments to accommodate their attendance at meetings
The panel should proceed in the student's absence and note the disability in its written statement
The student should self-certify each absence, and the hearing is then closed without any decision
The Registrar should refer the case to the Assessment Board so that it can decide without a hearing
questions.explanation: The Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments for students being considered for suspension whose attendance at panel hearings has been affected by their disability, to accommodate attendance at meetings.
questions.source_excerpt: the Academic Department should make reasonable adjustments for students being considered for suspension, whose attendance at panel hearings or others, has been affected by his or her disability to accommodate attendance at meetings.

questions.question: The Suspension of Studies Policy's equality impact assessment concludes that it is not likely to have a negative impact on people who share protected characteristics. What reason does it give?
options: Suspension decisions are always taken by the Assessment Board rather than by individual members of staff
Students who share protected characteristics are exempt from any suspension imposed by the College
Applications are approved automatically wherever a protected characteristic is shown to be involved
It anticipates that personal circumstances may affect ability to appeal and makes reasonable allowances
questions.explanation: The assessment reasons that it anticipates personal circumstances may affect ability to appeal and makes reasonable allowances for this.
questions.source_excerpt: It is not likely that this EIA will have a negative impact on people who share protected characteristics. The reason for this is that the EIA anticipates that personal circumstances may affect ability to appeal and makes reasonable allowances for this.

questions.question: The Suspension of Studies Policy notes that students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical and antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities. Which potential negative impacts is this meant to reduce?
options: Those arising from a student's age, race, sex or sexual orientation
Those arising from religion or belief, disability, and/or pregnancy and maternity
Those arising from marriage or civil partnership, and from gender reassignment
Those arising from nationality, immigration status, or social and economic background
questions.explanation: Allowing self-certification should reduce the potential for negative impact on people as a result of their religion or belief, disability, and/or pregnancy and maternity.
questions.source_excerpt: For example, students may self-certify for religious holidays, medical appointments, antenatal appointments, and caring responsibilities. This should reduce the potential for negative impact on people as a result of their religion or belief, disability, and/or pregnancy and maternity.

questions.question: A student appeals a suspension decision using a medical letter they already held when they applied but chose not to submit at the time. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, is this a permissible appeal ground?
options: Yes, any new material evidence the Panel has not yet seen is a permissible ground, whenever the student obtained it
No, new evidence counts only if exceptional circumstances stopped the student providing it earlier
Yes, provided the appeal is made in writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of the decision being taken
No, medical evidence can be weighed only by the Mitigating Circumstances Panel and never as part of an appeal
questions.explanation: New material evidence is a permissible ground only where the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide it earlier; evidence they held but chose not to submit does not meet this.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following grounds: ... 6.2.2. New material evidence has emerged, which the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier in the process

questions.question: A student's suspension has ended. They emailed the College to say they are well, but did not resume studies on the agreed return date or re-apply for a further suspension. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, what follows?
options: Their suspension is treated as extended, because they have been in touch with the College before the return date
They are referred back to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel, which sets a new return date for them
They will be terminated from their programme, as contact alone is neither resuming nor re-applying
Their suspension continues until they re-enrol, as the email shows a clear intention to return to study
questions.explanation: A student who neither resumes on the agreed return date nor re-applies for a further suspension is terminated from their programme; contacting the College does not extend the suspension.
questions.source_excerpt: Failure to re-enrol and attend classes will NOT automatically extend a student's suspension of studies ... If a student does not resume studies on the agreed return date or re-apply for a further suspension period, he/she will be terminated from their programme of study

questions.question: Shortly before their agreed return date, a suspended student realises they are still too unwell to resume. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, what must they do to avoid being terminated from their programme?
options: Re-apply for a further suspension of studies, as the policy requires if one is needed and deemed appropriate
Stay away until they recover, as the suspension continues automatically while they remain unwell
Ask their Personal Tutor to move the agreed return date, which the tutor may then approve on their own authority
Lodge a written appeal with the Registrar against the original return date within 15 working days
questions.explanation: A suspension is not extended automatically; students must re-apply for a further suspension if it is required and deemed appropriate, and a student who neither resumes nor re-applies is terminated.
questions.source_excerpt: students must re-apply for a further suspension of studies if it is required and deemed appropriate; ... If a student does not resume studies on the agreed return date or re-apply for a further suspension period, he/she will be terminated from their programme of study

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, which option correctly matches each case to how it is handled: (1) suspension for misconduct; (2) suspension for insufficient academic progression; (3) a student's request on health grounds? ("Panel" = Mitigating Circumstances Panel.)
options: (1) Panel review, then Assessment Board approval; (2) Assessment Board approval; (3) Personal Tutor approval after discussion
(1) Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure; (2) Personal Tutor decision; (3) Registrar approval without Panel review
(1) College Appeals Policy and Procedure; (2) Panel review, then Assessment Board approval; (3) Panel review, then Assessment Board approval
(1) Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure; (2) Assessment Board approval; (3) Panel review, then Assessment Board approval
questions.explanation: Disciplinary suspension is considered under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure, academic progression suspensions need Assessment Board approval, and a student's application goes to the Panel, whose recommendation the Assessment Board approves.
questions.source_excerpt: Suspension in this context is to be considered under the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure; ... Any suspension decision relating to academic progression must be approved by the Assessment Board; ... to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel for review. ... The recommendation will be forwarded to the Assessment Board for approval

questions.question: A student's long-term caring commitments are impairing their ability to attend classes, and they fear the College will suspend them for non-engagement. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, may the student themselves request an intermission?
options: No, attendance problems are an academic reason on which only the College may act, not a student ground
Yes, impairment of ability to attend or engage with academic commitments is a ground they may cite
No, a student may request an intermission only for health, pregnancy or compelling financial reasons
Yes, but only after the Assessment Board has formally recorded their attendance as unsatisfactory
questions.explanation: Students may request an intermission on the ground of impairment of ability to attend or engage with academic commitments; this is separate from the College's power to suspend for non-engagement.
questions.source_excerpt: A student may request an intermission from his/her study based on the following grounds: ... b) Impairment of ability to attend or engage with academic commitments

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, which step is stated for an approved suspension application but not for a declined one?
options: The student is informed of the outcome in writing within seven days of the decision being taken
The Mitigating Circumstances Panel reviews the complete form and forwards its recommendation
The Academic Registry informs relevant internal departments and external parties, including SLC
The student may appeal the decision in writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of notification
questions.explanation: Only for approved applications does the policy state that the Academic Registry informs internal departments and external parties; written notice within seven days, Panel review and the right of appeal apply either way.
questions.source_excerpt: If the suspension of studies application is approved ... The Academic Registry will inform all relevant internal departments ... The Academic Registry will also inform external parties namely the Awarding Bodies, SLC ... If a suspension of studies application is declined, the student will be informed in writing within seven days of the decision.

questions.question: A student whose suspension of studies has just been approved asks to keep attending lectures and using the library. What does the Suspension of Studies Policy provide?
options: They may attend lectures and use the library as normal, as a suspension affects only assessment deadlines
Suspension stops them continuing the programme; the Panel indicates, with a rationale, whether facility access is kept
They may carry on attending lectures, but all access to College facilities ends automatically on suspension
They lose access to every College service, as suspended students have no entitlement to services of any kind
questions.explanation: A suspension prevents the student continuing the programme of study, while the Mitigating Circumstances Panel indicates whether access to any College facilities should be maintained and gives a rationale.
questions.source_excerpt: A suspension of study is an approved intermission to a specified duration that prevents a student from continuing the programme of study; ... The Mitigating Circumstances Panel should also indicate whether access to any College facilities should be maintained and must provide a rationale for this request.

questions.question: To reduce administration, a manager proposes that only full-time students should be able to use the suspension procedure. How does this proposal sit with the Suspension of Studies Policy?
options: It is consistent, as the policy lets the College limit the suspension procedure to particular groups of students
It is consistent, provided part-time students are allowed to self-certify their absences instead
It conflicts with the commitment that the procedures be easy to access and available to all without discrimination
It conflicts only if the part-time students affected share a protected characteristic, such as a disability
questions.explanation: The policy commits that the suspension process and procedures will be comprehensive, easy to access and use, and available to all without discrimination, so restricting them to full-time students conflicts with it.
questions.source_excerpt: Equitable procedure is a relevant factor in student attainment. The College always recognises that the process and procedures for suspension will be comprehensive, easy to access and use and available to all without discrimination.

questions.question: The Mitigating Circumstances Panel has completed its statement on a student's suspension application, but the Chair of the Panel has not yet signed it off. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, can the student be formally notified of the outcome?
options: Yes, the Registrar may notify the student formally as soon as the Panel's statement is complete
Yes, as long as the notification is sent within seven days of the Panel's meeting
Yes, provided the student's Personal Tutor countersigns the outcome letter in the Chair's place
No, formal notification follows completion by the student and the Panel and sign-off by the Chair
questions.explanation: The student is notified formally of the outcome only once the application has been completed by both the student and the Panel and signed off by the Chair of the Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: Once the application is completed by both the student and Mitigating Circumstances Panel and signed off by the Chair of the Panel, the student will be notified formally of the outcome

questions.question: A student who self-suspended for health reasons is due to return next month. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, which set of actions is expected of the student?
options: Contact the College before the return date, confirm enrolment status, re-enrol and resume on the agreed date
Wait for the Registry to contact them, then resume classes, as re-enrolment happens automatically on their return
Submit a fresh Student Suspension Form to the Registry Office to confirm that the suspension has ended
Obtain their Personal Tutor's written approval to return, then re-enrol within 15 working days of resuming
questions.explanation: The student is expected to contact the College before the scheduled return, is obliged to determine their enrolment status and re-enrol, and must resume on the agreed return date.
questions.source_excerpt: When a student's period of suspension has come to an end, s/he is obliged to contact the College to determine the enrolment status and to re-enrol on the programme of study. ... A student is expected to establish contact with the College before the scheduled return to study. ... If a student does not resume studies on the agreed return date

questions.question: A student's suspension application was declined on 1 May, but the written notification did not reach them until 14 May. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, which statement is correct?
options: Notification was in time, and any appeal must be lodged within 15 working days of 1 May
They should have been informed within seven days of the decision; any appeal runs 15 working days from 14 May
Notification was in time, as 15 working days are allowed; any appeal runs 15 working days from 14 May
They should have been informed within seven days; any appeal must reach the Registrar within seven days of 14 May
questions.explanation: A declined applicant must be informed in writing within seven days of the decision, and an appeal may be lodged within 15 working days of receiving the written notification, so the appeal period runs from 14 May.
questions.source_excerpt: If a suspension of studies application is declined, the student will be informed in writing within seven days of the decision. ... A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of the suspension by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision

questions.question: Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, which pair of responsibilities belongs to the Registrar?
options: Approving self-suspension applications, and chairing the Mitigating Circumstances Panel
Signing off completed applications as Panel Chair, and approving academic progression suspensions
Submitting the Suspension Form and evidence to the Panel, and receiving students' written appeals
Advising students on the impact on their SLC funding, and making reasonable adjustments for panel hearings
questions.explanation: The Registrar submits the Student Suspension Form and evidence to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel, and students lodge appeals by writing to the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: The Registrar should submit the Student Suspension Form with all relevant evidence to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel for review. ... A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of the suspension by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days

questions.question: A student suspended by the Assessment Board for insufficient academic progression says they will return on the agreed date and meet the conditions set in the decision afterwards. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, is this acceptable?
options: No, they must fulfil the stated conditions before the return, on the agreed timeline
Yes, provided they complete all of the conditions by the end of their first term back
Yes, conditions can be deferred if their Personal Tutor agrees and informs the Registry
No, a student suspended for an academic reason must re-apply to the Panel before returning
questions.explanation: Where the Assessment Board has taken a suspension decision for an academic reason, the student must fulfil the stated conditions before the return to study, on the agreed timeline.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a suspension decision has been taken by the Assessment Board for an academic reason, the student must fulfil the conditions stated before the return to study on the agreed timeline.

questions.question: A student writes to the Registrar 20 working days after receiving notification of a suspension decision, with evidence that the Suspension of Studies Policy was not followed. Which statement correctly describes this appeal under the policy?
options: It is in time, as the limit is 30 working days, and it relies on a permissible ground
It relies on a permissible ground, but it is outside the 15-working-day time limit
It is in time, but failure to follow the policy is not a permissible ground for appeal
It is outside the time limit, and failure to follow the policy is not a permissible ground either
questions.explanation: Evidence that the policy was not followed is a permissible ground, but appeals must be lodged within 15 working days of receiving the written notification.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following grounds: 6.2.1. In circumstances where there is evidence that the College's Suspension of Studies Policy has not been followed; ... A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of the suspension by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision

questions.question: A student considering suspension is worried about their Student Finance (SLC) funding. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, whom should they ask about the impact, and who informs SLC if the suspension is approved?
options: Their Personal Tutor advises on the impact; the Academic Registry informs SLC on approval
The Finance Office advises on the impact; the Finance Office then informs SLC on approval
The Registrar advises on the impact; the student must then inform SLC themselves on approval
The Mitigating Circumstances Panel advises; the Assessment Board informs SLC on approval
questions.explanation: Students are advised to seek advice from their personal tutor on the impact on Student Finance (SLC), and on approval the Academic Registry informs external parties including SLC.
questions.source_excerpt: Students are advised to seek further academic advice from their personal tutor to determine the impact a suspension of studies may have on their academic performance, financial ... situation, and Student Finance (SLC); ... The Academic Registry will also inform external parties namely the Awarding Bodies, SLC

questions.question: The Mitigating Circumstances Panel has reviewed a complete self-suspension application and recommended approval, with continued library access. A colleague tells the student both are now confirmed. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, is that right?
options: Yes, the recommendation takes effect once the Panel's statement gives a rationale for library access
Yes, the Panel approves the suspension, and the Assessment Board decides only on facility access
No, library access is for the Registrar to decide, although the suspension itself is now confirmed
No, the Panel only recommends; its recommendation is forwarded to the Assessment Board for approval
questions.explanation: The Panel reviews the application and makes a recommendation, including on facility access, which is then forwarded to the Assessment Board for approval.
questions.source_excerpt: The Mitigating Circumstances Panel should also indicate whether access to any College facilities should be maintained and must provide a rationale for this request. The recommendation will be forwarded to the Assessment Board for approval

questions.question: Staff reviewing the suspension procedure under the policy's equality section find it is likely to have a positive impact on students who share a particular protected characteristic. Is it therefore 'equality neutral' as the Suspension of Studies Policy uses the term?
options: No, 'neutral' means it will not have a differential impact on any equality group
Yes, any procedure with no adverse impact on protected groups counts as equality neutral
Yes, because a positive impact on one group is balanced by the procedure applying to all
No, 'neutral' means the Assessment Board has approved it as free from any discrimination
questions.explanation: The policy contrasts a positive impact on people sharing protected characteristics with being equality 'neutral', which means having no differential impact on any equality group.
questions.source_excerpt: Is there likely to be a positive impact on people who share protected characteristics, and if so, how? Or is it clear at this stage that it will be equality "neutral"? i.e., will not have a differential impact on any equality group/s?

questions.question: Staff are checking four students' requests for an intermission against the grounds listed in the Suspension of Studies Policy. Which request is not supported by any of those grounds?
options: A student whose partner is due to give birth and who wants time away from study for parental leave
A student with compelling financial reasons, although their health and attendance are both unaffected
A student whose circumstances fit no named category but substantially impair their ability to pursue the programme
A student with no health, family or financial difficulty who wants a year out to gain work experience
questions.explanation: The listed grounds include parental leave, compelling financial reasons and any other circumstances that substantially impair the student's ability to pursue their programme; a wish to gain work experience with no such difficulty meets none of them.
questions.source_excerpt: A student may request an intermission from his/her study based on the following grounds: ... c) Pregnancy, maternity and Parental leave; d) Compassionate reasons (including serious domestic difficulties); e) Compelling financial reasons; f) Any other circumstances which would substantially impair a student's ability to pursue their programme

questions.question: A student self-suspended on health grounds, and their approved suspension did not maintain access to College facilities. They ask whether the College will support them when they return. What does the Suspension of Studies Policy provide?
options: No College support is due on their return, as the approved suspension did not maintain facility access
Support is offered only once they have re-enrolled and completed a full term back in their classes
They should contact the College before the scheduled return; the College facilitates any support needed
They must first re-apply to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel, which then decides what support to provide
questions.explanation: The Panel's indication on facility access concerns the suspension period; on return, the student is expected to make contact before the scheduled date and the College facilitates any support required.
questions.source_excerpt: The Mitigating Circumstances Panel should also indicate whether access to any College facilities should be maintained ... A student is expected to establish contact with the College before the scheduled return to study. The College ensures to facilitate any support which may be required upon the students return;

questions.question: The Assessment Board has suspended a student for insufficient academic progression. The student has heard that only declined self-suspension applications can be appealed. Under the Suspension of Studies Policy, what is the position?
options: They may appeal in writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of notification, on a permissible ground
They may appeal, but only by writing to the Assessment Board itself within seven days of the decision being taken
They cannot appeal, as an academic progression suspension approved by the Assessment Board is final
They cannot appeal under this policy; they must use the Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedure
questions.explanation: A suspension taken by the Assessment Board for an academic reason is a suspension decision, and the policy gives students the right to appeal any suspension decision in writing to the Registrar within 15 working days, on a valid ground.
questions.source_excerpt: Where a suspension decision has been taken by the Assessment Board for an academic reason ... A student has the right to appeal a suspension decision, providing a valid ground for an appeal is lodged; ... by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision

questions.question: A self-funded undergraduate withdraws from their programme in week 5. Under Table 1 of the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what is their fee liability and refund?
options: 25% fee liability; 75% of full tuition fees paid is refunded
0% fee liability; a full refund of the tuition fees paid
50% fee liability; 50% of full tuition fees paid is refunded
100% fee liability; no part of the tuition fees paid is refunded
questions.explanation: Table 1 sets a 50% fee liability, with a refund of 50% of full tuition fees paid, for withdrawals in weeks 4-6.
questions.source_excerpt: 3 weeks 4-6 weeks 7 weeks and thereafter ... 0% of Tuition Fees 25% of Tuition Fees 50% of Tuition Fees 100% of Tuition Fees ... Full Refund 75% of full tuition fees paid 50% of full tuition fees paid

questions.question: A self-funded student who formally accepted their offer 10 days ago tells you they have changed their mind and want to cancel. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what should you advise?
options: They must first meet the Programme Leader and give written reasons for their decision before cancelling
They can no longer cancel, because the full tuition fee became payable once the offer was accepted
They must wait until the programme starts and then submit a formal withdrawal notice to the Finance Department
They can still cancel by completing the Withdrawal Request Form at Reception or emailing the College
questions.explanation: The legal right to cancel lasts for 14 days after formally accepting the offer, without explanation, so at day 10 the student can still cancel; informing the College via the Withdrawal Request Form from Reception or by email is sufficient.
questions.source_excerpt: If for any reason a student changes mind about joining the College after accepting formally the offer of a place, s/he has the legal right to cancel the registration contract for the next 14 days without explanation; ... This can be done by completing the Withdrawal Request Form from Reception or by emailing the College directly;

questions.question: A student funded by the Student Loan Company (SLC) wants to change from full-time to part-time study and asks you about submitting a change of circumstance form. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, who should be contacted?
options: The College's IT and Monitoring department
The College's Finance and Accounts department
The student's Programme Leader
The Student Services team at College Reception
questions.explanation: Changing the mode of study is a change SLC must be notified of, and the policy says the College's IT and Monitoring department should be contacted about submitting a change of circumstance form.
questions.source_excerpt: SLC requires notification of a change of circumstance if students change their programmes of study in any of the following ways: ... e) Changing the mode of study; ... If a student believes that it is necessary to submit a change of circumstance form, then the College's IT and Monitoring department should be contacted;

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what happens to any overpayment of tuition fees for a student in receipt of an SLC Tuition Fee Loan?
options: It is refunded into the student's own bank account within 28 days of a request
It is held by the College as credit against the student's fees for the next academic year
It is paid directly by the College to SLC, not refunded to the student
It is split equally between the student and SLC once the academic year has ended
questions.explanation: Students with an SLC Tuition Fee Loan are not entitled to a refund of any overpayment, because the College pays overpayments directly to SLC.
questions.source_excerpt: Students in receipt of a Tuition Fee Loan from SLC are not entitled for a refund on any overpayment of tuition fees, as any overpayments will be paid directly by the College to SLC;

questions.question: A self-funded student who paid their fees from their own bank account asks for their tuition refund to be paid into a friend's bank account instead. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what should happen?
options: Accept it, provided both the student and the friend sign a written consent form
Reject it; refunds go to the original source and third-party requests are refused
Accept it, as long as the friend's account is held with a UK bank and is debt-checked
Refer it to the Programme Manager, who may approve it at their own discretion
questions.explanation: Refunds are made to the original source (the country and account the money came from) for money laundering compliance, and any request to pay a third-party bank account is rejected.
questions.source_excerpt: Refunds to students will be made to the original source i.e. the country and the account from which the money was sent, where possible. This is to ensure due diligence with national guidelines and compliance with the money laundering regulations; ... Any refund application requesting payment to third party bank accounts will be rejected.

questions.question: A self-funded student on an instalment plan misses a payment and says it is the College's fault because no reminder letter was sent. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what is the correct position?
options: The College must issue a written reminder at least 7 days before each instalment is due
The missed payment is excused, because the College had not issued an invoice for that instalment
The student does not have to pay until the College issues a formal overdue notice by post or email
The student or sponsor is responsible for paying on time; the College sends no reminders
questions.explanation: The policy places responsibility on the student or sponsor to ensure payments reach the College by the due date, whether or not an invoice has been issued, and states the College will not send reminder letters.
questions.source_excerpt: It is the responsibility of each student or sponsor to ensure that the College receives payments by the due date irrespective of whether an invoice has been issued. The College will not send letters reminding the student of outstanding fees.

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what happens when a student paying by instalments falls 2 months in arrears on their payment plan?
options: A formal reminder letter is sent to the student and their sponsor
Their enrolment is withdrawn and they must re-enrol the following year
Their College/Class access and Computer Log-in are suspended
No action is taken until the arrears reach 6 months
questions.explanation: The policy's overdue fees schedule states that at 2 months in arrears College/Class access and Computer Log-in will be suspended; the College does not send reminder letters.
questions.source_excerpt: b) 2 months in arrears - College/Class access and Computer Log-in will be suspended.

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what happens to a student's outstanding fees once they are 3 months in arrears on their payment plan?
options: They are transferred to a Credit Agency, which adds a 10% fee to the amount outstanding
They are transferred to a Credit Agency, which adds a flat £50 administration fee
They are written off, and the student is formally withdrawn from their programme
They are added to the balance of the student's SLC tuition fee loan for later recovery
questions.explanation: At 3 months in arrears the outstanding fees are transferred to a Credit Agency for collection, which adds a 10% fee to the amount outstanding.
questions.source_excerpt: c) 3 months in arrears - The outstanding fees will be transferred to a Credit Agency for collection, and they will add a 10% fee to the amount outstanding.

questions.question: A student whose tuition fee was paid in full by their employer (not SLC) withdraws and asks for the refund to be paid to them. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what is the position?
options: The sponsor is entitled to any refund, once a refund form is submitted to Finance
The student receives the refund, as they are the registered learner on the programme
The refund is split equally between the student and the employer that sponsored them
No refund is possible, because sponsors are charged an annual fee to cover full registration
questions.explanation: Where a sponsor has paid more than the fee liability at withdrawal, the sponsor is entitled to the refund once a refund form is submitted to the Finance Department; the student receives a refund only if they were partially self-funding.
questions.source_excerpt: If the sponsor has paid a fee greater than the liability fee incurred at the time of the student's withdrawal, then the sponsor is entitled to a refund, providing a refund form has been submitted to the College's Finance Department; ... Students will not receive the refund unless the they have been partially self-funding in respect of tuition fees.

questions.question: A self-funded student withdraws from one module but still has 120 credit points for the 3-term year, and asks for a fee refund for that module. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what applies?
options: A pro-rata refund based on the module's credit value is due
No fee refund is due, as the student is still defined as full-time
A full module refund is due if they withdraw within 7 weeks
The refund must be claimed through a Change of Circumstances form
questions.explanation: Self-funding students who withdraw from modules cannot receive a fee refund if they are still full-time (120 credit points for a 3-term year) after the withdrawal.
questions.source_excerpt: Self-funding students who withdraw from one or more modules cannot receive a fee refund if they are still defined as `full-time' (120 credit points for a 3-term year) following the withdrawal;

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what happens when a self-funded student makes a tuition fee refund application to the College?
options: It is automatically approved if submitted within 14 days of withdrawal
It is forwarded to SLC for verification before any refund payment is made
The refund is paid in full, and any arrears are invoiced separately afterwards
The student is debt-checked and any tuition arrears are taken into account
questions.explanation: Every self-funded refund applicant is debt-checked, and if tuition payments are in arrears the final refund amount takes account of the money owed to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Any self-funded student who makes a refund application to the College will be debt-checked; ... the College will confirm that the final refund amount will take into account any outstanding tuition monies owed to the College;

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, within what timeframe will refunds normally be processed after the refund request form is received?
options: Within 5 working days
Within 10-15 working days
Within 20-25 working days
Within 3 calendar months
questions.explanation: Refunds are processed within 10-15 working days of receiving the refund request form, provided the information given is correct and complete; students should then allow up to 28 days for the money to reach their account.
questions.source_excerpt: Refunds will be processed within 10-15 working days of receiving the refund request form, providing that all the information disclosed by the student is correct, accurate and fulfils all requirements.

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, within what period should self-funded and sponsored students who choose to pay in a single payment pay their annual fees?
options: Within 14 days of accepting the offer of a place
Within 30 days of the program start date
Before the end of the first term of study
Within 10 working days of enrolment
questions.explanation: Single payments should be made within 30 days of the program start date; if not, the student incurs supplementary charges.
questions.source_excerpt: Self-funded and sponsored students have the option to pay their annual fees in one instalment. This should be paid within 30 days of the program start date;

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how can a student who does not wish to pay all their tuition fees at once pay instead?
options: Pay nothing upfront and the full balance in 12 monthly instalments
Pay 50% at enrolment and the remaining 50% at the start of term two
Pay an initial deposit and the balance in up to 10 instalments
Pay an initial deposit and the balance in up to 24 instalments
questions.explanation: The policy allows a student to pay an initial deposit and then the balance in up to 10 instalments.
questions.source_excerpt: If the student does not wish to pay all the tuition fees at once, s/he can opt to pay an initial deposit and pay the balance in up to 10 instalments;

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, where should a student submit a request for a refund of a deposit or payment that is not directly covered by the Policy?
options: To the Programme Manager, who forwards it to Finance if deemed acceptable
Directly to the Student Loan Company, which decides whether it is refundable
To the Librarian, who handles deposit refunds not covered elsewhere in the Policy
To the IT and Monitoring department, as a change of circumstance request
questions.explanation: Other deposits and payments are normally non-refundable, but requests not directly covered by the policy go to the Programme Manager for consideration, who forwards them to the Finance Department if deemed acceptable.
questions.source_excerpt: students seeking refunds for deposits or payments that are not directly covered by this Policy, should submit their request to the Programme Manager for consideration, who will forward the requests to the Finance Department if they are deemed acceptable.

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, when does a student (other than a Home/EU student with SLC funding) become liable for the full tuition fee?
options: On formally accepting the offer of a place
Upon registration for their programme
On the date their first instalment is due
At the start of the second term of study
questions.explanation: The policy states that a student is liable for the full tuition fee upon registration, with Home/EU students who have SLC funding excluded.
questions.source_excerpt: a student is liable for full tuition fee upon registration, excluding Home/EU students with SLC funding;

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what is London Churchill College's position on offering bursaries to students?
options: LCC offers bursaries to self-funded students only
LCC offers bursaries in cases of financial hardship
LCC offers a bursary to students who pay in full
LCC does not offer any bursaries to its students
questions.explanation: The policy states plainly that LCC does not offer any bursaries to students.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC does not offer any bursaries to students.

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what must students with SLC funding provide to the College as evidence of their eligibility for funding?
options: Their "Payment Advice" receipt from SLC
Their SLC loan application reference number
A copy of their completed SLC application form
A bank statement showing their first SLC payment
questions.explanation: Students with SLC funding must give the College their "Payment Advice" receipt as evidence of their eligibility for funding.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with SLC funding must provide their "Payment Advice" receipt to the College, as evidence of their eligibility for funding;

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, when must all students enrol with the College?
options: Once only, at the start of the first year of their programme
At the start of each term throughout their programme
At the start of their programme and each subsequent year
Each year, but only if their fees or funding have changed
questions.explanation: All students must enrol at the start of their programme and again at the start of each subsequent year.
questions.source_excerpt: All students must enrol at the start of their program and each subsequent year.

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, at what stage of arrears on a payment plan will a student's Oyster discount be cancelled with TfL?
options: 1 month in arrears
2 months in arrears
3 months in arrears
6 months in arrears
questions.explanation: At 3 months in arrears the outstanding fees go to a Credit Agency and the student's Oyster discount is cancelled with TfL.
questions.source_excerpt: c) 3 months in arrears - The outstanding fees will be transferred to a Credit Agency for ... Your Oyster discount will be cancelled with TfL.

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, why does SLC require students to complete a Change of Circumstances form whenever their circumstances change?
options: So that the College can issue a revised invoice for the year
So that the financial records kept by LCC and SLC remain identical
So that any refund is paid into the student's new bank account
So that the student's attendance is reported to the OfS each term
questions.explanation: The Change of Circumstances procedure ensures that the financial records maintained by LCC and those kept by SLC remain identical.
questions.source_excerpt: SLC requires all students to complete a Change of Circumstances form, whenever students' circumstances change. This procedure ensures that the financial records maintained by LCC and the ones kept by SLC remain identical;

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what may a student do if they began their programme self-funding and were later reassessed as eligible for SLC funding?
options: Reclaim the payments by submitting a Change of Circumstances form to SLC
Ask for the self-funded payments to be credited against next year's fees
Apply to SLC to be reimbursed for the fees paid in the self-funded period
Apply directly to the College for a refund of the payments made while self-funded
questions.explanation: A student who starts self-funding and is later reassessed as eligible for SLC funding may apply directly to the College for a refund of the payments made during the self-funded period.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student begins the programme under self-funding and is later reassessed as eligible for SLC funding, then the student may apply directly to the College for a refund of the payments made during the self-funded period.

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how will the College normally reimburse a self-funded student who cancels within the 14-day grace period?
options: By the same means of payment used for the initial transaction
By cheque posted to the student's registered home address
As a credit held on the student's account for a future enrolment
By bank transfer to any account the student nominates in writing
questions.explanation: Reimbursements are paid using the same means of payment the student used for the initial transaction, unless other conditions have been expressly agreed with the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Reimbursements will be paid using the same means of payment used by the student for the initial transaction/s, unless other conditions have been expressly agreed with the College.

questions.question: According to the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how should a self-funded student submit a claim for a tuition fee refund?
options: By telephoning the Finance Department, which records the claim
Through their Programme Leader, who submits it on their behalf
In writing, with all the required documentation and evidence
Through a Change of Circumstances form submitted to the SLC
questions.explanation: Self-funded students should submit their refund request in writing to the College with all required documentation and evidence; failing to follow the procedure delays the refund.
questions.source_excerpt: To claim a fee refund, self-funded students should submit their request in writing to the ... College, taking care to ensure that all documentation and evidence required has been provided. Failure to follow procedures will delay the refund payment;

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how must a student who intends to withdraw from a programme or module notify the College?
options: Verbally, by informing their personal tutor or lecturer
Formally, in a notification sent by mail or by email
Only through SLC, which then informs the College directly
By asking their Programme Manager to record the withdrawal
questions.explanation: A student intending to withdraw from a programme or module must notify the College formally by mail or email.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student intends to withdraw from a programme or module of study, s/he must notify the College formally by mail or email;

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, within what period must a student who has completed their course request a refund of credit left on their Printing and Photocopying Card?
options: Within 14 days of their course completion date
Within 28 days of their course completion date
Within twelve months of their course completion date
Within three months of their course completion date
questions.explanation: Students who have left or completed the course must request a refund of remaining printing credit within three months of their course completion, withdrawal or termination date.
questions.source_excerpt: Students with credit remaining on their Printing and Photocopying Card may request a refund for the credit by emailing the Librarian. Students who have left or completed the course must do so within three months of their course completion date

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, who must sign off the paperwork for a student's equipment deposit refund, or the refund will be refused?
options: The Programme Leader
The Finance Department
The Head of Student Services
The College Librarian
questions.explanation: Departments provide the paperwork for equipment deposit refunds, but it must be signed off by the Programme Leader or the refund will be refused.
questions.source_excerpt: Departments will provide the student with the necessary paperwork, but this must be signed off by the Programme Leader or the refund will be refused.

questions.question: According to the refund processing arrangements in the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how often will the College make payments under normal business conditions?
options: Once a week
Once a month
Twice a month
Once a term
questions.explanation: The policy states that under normal business conditions the College will make payments once a month.
questions.source_excerpt: Under normal business conditions the College will make payments once a month.

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how will any refund due to a student who is paying via an instalment plan be processed?
options: By cheque sent to the address held on the student record
In cash, collected in person from the Finance Department
On the current active card details held on file with the College
As a credit set against the student's next instalment payment
questions.explanation: For students paying via an instalment plan, any refund due is processed on the current active card details the College holds on file.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student is paying via an instalment plan, any refund due will be processed on the current active card details on file with the College;

questions.question: Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what can a student do if they dispute the amount of refund they are entitled to?
options: Make a complaint under the College's Complaints Policy and Procedure
Appeal to SLC, which makes the final decision on the refund amount
Submit an academic appeal under the Academic Appeals Procedure
Ask the Credit Agency to review the College's refund calculation
questions.explanation: A student who disputes the refund amount, or is dissatisfied with any other matter under the policy, can complain under the Complaints Policy and Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: If a student disputes the amount of refund entitled to or remains dissatisfied with any other ... matter arising from the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, s/he can make a complaint under the Complaints Policy and Procedure

questions.question: A student has to repeat a unit in order to complete the credit value of their qualification. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how is the cost of the repeat treated?
options: It is included in the annual tuition fee, so no further payment is due
A unit repeat fee may be payable, as one of the Charges in addition to Fees
It is payable only if the student's SLC loan does not cover the repeated unit
It counts as a new enrolment, so the full annual tuition fee is payable again
questions.explanation: Unit repeat fees are listed among the Charges that students may be required to pay in addition to Fees when they repeat units to complete their qualification credit value.
questions.source_excerpt: In addition to Fees, students may be required to pay Charges. Charges would include the ... Unit repeat fees is applicable, if a student repeats any units or offered alternative units in order to complete his/her qualification credit value;

questions.question: A student arrives to enrol for their second year with only a verbal assurance that their employer will pay the fees. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, can the College accept the enrolment on that basis?
options: Yes, if the employer confirms the arrangement by telephone to the Finance Department
Yes, provisionally, with the student's Computer Log-in suspended until the employer pays
No; sponsored students must first apply to SLC and supply their Payment Advice receipt
No; it needs a written sponsor guarantee, full payment or an election to pay by instalments
questions.explanation: At enrolment each year a student must provide an acceptable written guarantee from an official sponsor, make full payment or elect to pay by instalments, and the College only accepts enrolments on receipt of payment or sponsor authorisation.
questions.source_excerpt: At that time they must either provide an acceptable written guarantee from an official sponsor accepting responsibility for all fees due or make full payment of their fees ... or elect to pay by instalments; ... The College will only accept student enrolments upon receipt of the relevant payments or sponsor authorisation.

questions.question: A self-funded student opted to pay their annual fees as a single payment but has still not paid six weeks after the programme start date, and no other date was notified. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what follows?
options: The student will incur supplementary charges
The fees are moved onto a 10-instalment plan
The fees are passed at once to a Credit Agency
The unpaid fees are added to their SLC loan
