questions.explanation: If the whole fee is not paid within 30 days of the programme start date or other notified date, the student incurs supplementary charges.
questions.source_excerpt: If whole fees are not paid within 30 days of the start date of the program or other notified date, the student will incur supplementary charges as detailed below.

questions.question: A student on a payment plan stops paying altogether. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, which sequence of actions applies as the arrears build up?
options: 1 month: reminder letter issued; 2 months: access and log-in suspended; 3 months: fees passed to a Credit Agency
1 month: no letters issued; 2 months: fees passed to a Credit Agency; 3 months: access and log-in suspended
1 month: no letters issued; 2 months: access and log-in suspended; 3 months: fees passed to a Credit Agency
1 month: access and log-in suspended; 2 months: final warning letter; 3 months: fees passed to a Credit Agency
questions.explanation: Under the overdue fees schedule, no letters of any type are issued at 1 month in arrears, College/Class access and Computer Log-in are suspended at 2 months, and the fees go to a Credit Agency at 3 months.
questions.source_excerpt: a) 1 month in arrears - No letters of any type will be issued. b) 2 months in arrears - College/Class access and Computer Log-in will be suspended. c) 3 months in arrears - The outstanding fees will be transferred to a Credit Agency for ... collection

questions.question: After an SLC-funded student's change of circumstance has been processed, SLC re-claims overpaid fees from the College. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how is the repayment calculated and what is the effect for the student?
options: It is based on the fee liability weeks, and the student's tuition fee loan is then reduced
It is based on the student's attendance record, and the student must repay SLC directly
It is based on the credits completed, and the College refunds the student before SLC
It is a fixed half of the annual fee, and the student's tuition fee loan is written off
questions.explanation: Repayment calculations are based on the fee liability weeks in Table 1, and once SLC has re-claimed the money from the College the tuition fee loan the student owes SLC is reduced.
questions.source_excerpt: Once a change of circumstance has been processed, SLC will re-claim any overpaid fees directly from the College. Repayment calculations will be based upon the fee liability weeks [see Table 1 below]. Once SLC has re-claimed the money from the College, the tuition fee loan owed by the student to SLC will be reduced.

questions.question: A self-funded student emails the College 13 days after formally accepting their offer to say they intend to cancel, but the cancellation is not processed until day 16. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, was the cancellation made in time?
options: No, because the College must finish processing it within the 14-day period
Yes, because informing the College of the intention within 14 days is sufficient
No, because cancellations must be made in person using the Withdrawal Request Form
Yes, but only if the student also gives a written explanation of their reasons
questions.explanation: To meet the cancellation deadline it is sufficient to inform the College of the intention to cancel before the 14-day grace period ends; emailing the College is an accepted method and no explanation is needed.
questions.source_excerpt: To meet the cancellation period deadline, it is sufficient for students to inform the College of the intention to cancel, prior to the end of the 14-day grace period. This can be done by completing the Withdrawal Request Form from Reception or by emailing the College directly;

questions.question: An international self-funded student has paid their tuition fees, but their visa application is then refused. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how does the visa refusal relate to their fees?
options: It is outside the Policy's scope, so the fees paid remain fully payable
It must be reported to SLC on a Change of Circumstances form before any review
It qualifies the student for a College bursary to offset the fees already paid
It is one of the listed circumstances in which revised fees may be applicable
questions.explanation: Visa refusal for international students is listed among the circumstances in which revised fees may be applicable, and students may be eligible for refunds where tuition fees have been reduced.
questions.source_excerpt: Students may also be eligible for refunds if they have overpaid the tuition fee or tuition fees have been reduced; ... Revised fees may be applicable in the following circumstances: ... d) Visa refusal (International students);

questions.question: A self-funded student is due a £600 tuition fee refund but owes £250 in tuition arrears. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what will the College do?
options: Pay the £600 refund in full and invoice the £250 arrears separately
Pass the £250 to a Credit Agency and pay the full £600 refund
Take the arrears into account and refund the remaining £350
Hold back the entire refund until the £250 has been paid off
questions.explanation: Where tuition is in arrears, the final refund amount takes account of the money owed to the College, and any refund due in excess of the outstanding debt is paid in the usual way.
questions.source_excerpt: If tuition payments are in arrears, then the student will be contacted by the College, and the College will confirm that the final refund amount will take into account any outstanding tuition monies owed to the College; ... Any refunds due to students in excess of outstanding debts will be refunded to them in the usual way

questions.question: A student's tuition fees were paid partly by their employer and partly by the student. After the student withdraws, a refund is due. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, who decides how the refund is distributed?
options: The employer decides, as the sponsor that paid part of the fees
The Programme Manager decides, after consulting the student
The College's Finance Department makes the decision
SLC decides, once a Change of Circumstances form is received
questions.explanation: A student receives a refund only if they were partially self-funding, and in such cases the College's Finance Department decides how the refunds are distributed.
questions.source_excerpt: Students will not receive the refund unless the they have been partially self-funding in respect of tuition fees. In such cases, the College's Finance Department will decide how the distribution of refunds will be made.

questions.question: A student asks for their £10 library deposit to be refunded but still has two books on loan from the Library. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what must happen first?
options: The student must return all their loans to the library before requesting the refund
The cost of the two books is deducted, and the balance of the deposit is refunded
College Reception must sign off the refund before the books are returned
The deposit is refunded now, and library fines are charged if the books go overdue
questions.explanation: Library deposits can be refunded on request in person or by emailing the Librarian, but the student must return all loans to the library before requesting the refund.
questions.source_excerpt: can request a refund of their deposit either in person or by emailing the Librarian; ... The student must return all loans to the library before requesting the refund;

questions.question: A student hands back all the equipment they borrowed against a refundable deposit, but one item has been damaged. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what applies to the deposit refund?
options: The deposit is refunded in full, as all the equipment was handed back
The damage is noted, but the refund is unaffected if the item still works
The deposit is forfeited, and no further charge for the damage can be made
The College may charge for the damage and deduct the cost from the refund
questions.explanation: Equipment deposits are refunded only if the equipment is returned undamaged; where it has been damaged, the College may charge the student and deduct the cost from the refund owed.
questions.source_excerpt: In the event that the equipment has been damaged or lost either fully or partially, the College has the right to charge the student for the loss or damage. Costs will be deducted from of the amount of the refund owed;

questions.question: A student's refund request form was received 20 days ago and the refund has since been processed, but the money has not yet reached their bank account. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what should you advise?
options: Refunds reach the account within 5 working days of processing, so it will be re-issued
Allow up to 28 days for it to arrive, as clearing times vary by bank and country
The refund has lapsed, so the student must submit a new refund request form
Make a formal complaint, as refunds must clear within 15 working days of processing
questions.explanation: Students should allow up to 28 days for a refund to reach their account, since clearing times vary with the banking institution and destination country.
questions.source_excerpt: Students should allow up 28 days for the refund to reach their account, bearing in mind that the length of time taken for refunds to clear beneficiary bank accounts may vary, depending upon the banking institution and/or the destination country.

questions.question: A self-funded student changes from full-time to part-time study partway through the academic year. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what will LCC base their fee liability on?
options: The date the student first registered on the programme
The date the student changed their mode of study
The date Finance issues the student a revised invoice
The date the College receives a refund request form
questions.explanation: LCC determines fee liability based on the date students withdraw or suspend study, or change their mode of study.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will determine the fee liability based upon the date students withdraw or suspend study ... from their programme or modules or if they change their mode of study;

questions.question: A self-funded student who did not pay through an instalment plan is due a refund but has not updated their bank account details. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what is the consequence?
options: Processing of the refund will be delayed
The refund is kept as credit on their account
The refund is sent by cheque to their home address
The refund is paid to SLC to reduce their loan
questions.explanation: For payment methods other than an instalment plan, the student must update their bank account details, and failure to do so delays the processing of the refund.
questions.source_excerpt: For all other methods of payment, the student will be required to update relevant bank account details. Failure to do so will result in a delay in processing the refund.

questions.question: An EU student with pre-settled status meets the eligibility criteria and receives SLC funding. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how does the rule on liability for the full tuition fee upon registration apply to them?
options: They fall within the exclusion for Home/EU students with SLC funding
They are treated as international students and are liable on registration
They remain liable on registration until SLC sends its Payment Advice
They must pay the full fee first and then reclaim it directly from SLC
questions.explanation: Students are liable for the full fee upon registration, but Home/EU students with SLC funding are excluded, and EU students with settled or pre-settled status may receive SLC funding subject to eligibility.
questions.source_excerpt: a student is liable for full tuition fee upon registration, excluding Home/EU students with SLC funding; EU students with settled status or pre-settled status may receive SLC funding, subject to eligibility criteria;

questions.question: A student paid a deposit to join a College field trip, then decided not to go and asked for the deposit back. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how is the request treated?
options: It is refunded in full if requested within the 14-day cancellation period
It is refunded on the Table 1 timeline, by the week the student withdrew
Deposits and charges for field trips are normally non-refundable
It is refunded once the Programme Leader signs off department paperwork
questions.explanation: Field trips are Charges payable in addition to Fees, and deposits/charges for field trips are listed among miscellaneous payments that are normally non-refundable; the 14-day right, Table 1 and Programme Leader sign-off belong to other provisions.
questions.source_excerpt: Extra-curricular activities, i.e. Field trips, competition entries; ... Refunds of any other deposits or payments made by students, including external registration charges, deposits/charges for field trips, etc., are normally non-refundable.

questions.question: A self-funded student notes that the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy lists eligibility for a bursary among circumstances where revised fees may apply, and asks to apply for an LCC bursary. What should you tell them?
options: They may apply to the Finance Department, which awards bursaries case by case
LCC does not offer any bursaries, so there is no College bursary to apply for
Bursaries are available only to Home students who also receive SLC funding
They should apply through the Programme Manager, who forwards it to Finance
questions.explanation: Although bursary eligibility appears in the list of circumstances where revised fees may apply, the policy states plainly that LCC does not offer any bursaries to students.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC does not offer any bursaries to students. ... Revised fees may be applicable in the following circumstances: ... e) Eligibility for a tuition fee discount or waiver or a bursary;

questions.question: A Home student intends to fund their programme with an SLC loan but plans to submit the SLC application after registering, once classes have started. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what is the requirement?
options: They may apply to SLC at any point within 30 days of the programme start date
They may apply to SLC at any time before their first instalment is due
They must apply to SLC within 14 days of formally accepting their offer
They must have applied to SLC for the funding prior to registration
questions.explanation: Students relying on SLC funding must have applied to the Student Loan Company for their programme before registration; the 30-day and 14-day periods belong to single payments and the right to cancel.
questions.source_excerpt: Students must have applied for the funding for their programme with student Loan Company (SLC) prior to registration;

questions.question: A sponsored student chose to pay their annual fees as a single payment, and the College notified a payment date 45 days after the programme start. The full fee arrives on day 40. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, do supplementary charges apply?
options: Yes, because the fee was not paid within 30 days of the programme start date
No, because the whole fee was paid by the other date the College notified
Yes, as a £10 penalty is applied automatically to any payment after day 30
No, because sponsored students are exempt from supplementary charges
questions.explanation: Supplementary charges arise only if the whole fee is not paid within 30 days of the start date or other notified date; here the fee was paid before the notified date.
questions.source_excerpt: If whole fees are not paid within 30 days of the start date of the program or other notified date, the student will incur supplementary charges as detailed below.

questions.question: A student on an instalment plan is one month in arrears and asks the College to write to them setting out what they owe. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what is the position?
options: An arrears letter is issued at one month, enclosing a copy of the payment plan
A final warning letter is issued before access is suspended at two months
No letters are issued, but they may request a copy of the plan and payments to date
An invoice is issued, and the payment plan is paused until the invoice is paid
questions.explanation: At 1 month in arrears no letters of any type are issued and the College sends no reminders, but a student may request a copy of the payment plan and payments made to date.
questions.source_excerpt: The College will not send letters reminding the student of outstanding fees. However, the student may request a copy of the payment plan and payments made to date. ... a) 1 month in arrears - No letters of any type will be issued.

questions.question: An employer has agreed to pay 30% of a student's tuition fee, with the student paying the rest. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what will LCC charge the employer in addition to its share of the fee?
options: An annual fee to cover the costs of the student's full registration
Nothing, as the registration fee applies only to sponsors paying in full
A 10% administration fee added to the share of the fee that it pays
Nothing, as only SLC is charged for registration on a student's behalf
questions.explanation: Where a sponsor other than SLC pays the fee or part of it, LCC charges the sponsor an annual fee to cover the costs of full registration.
questions.source_excerpt: In cases where a sponsor (not SLC) pays the fee, or part of it, on behalf of a student, LCC will charge the sponsor an annual fee to cover the costs of full registration;

questions.question: A self-funded student on an instalment plan has paid several instalments weeks late. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, which statement about a £10 charge is correct?
options: A £10 penalty is added automatically to every instalment that is paid late
Their £10 library deposit is forfeited to cover the College's late-payment costs
The Credit Agency adds £10 to the balance once it is one month in arrears
The College may, at its discretion, apply a £10 penalty for excessively late payment
questions.explanation: A £10 penalty charge may be applied at the College's discretion for excessively late payments; it is not automatic, and the library deposit and Credit Agency fee are separate provisions.
questions.source_excerpt: A penalty charge of £10 will be applied at the discretion of the College for excessively late payments.

questions.question: An SLC-funded student suspended their studies in the autumn term and wants to resume in the spring term of the same academic year. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, is a change of circumstance notification needed for the resumption?
options: No, SLC only needs to be told about the original suspension of studies
No, a resumption is notified only if it falls in a new academic year
Yes, resuming studies within the same academic year is a listed change
Yes, but it is notified to the Finance Department rather than to SLC
questions.explanation: SLC requires notification of a change of circumstance for each listed change, which includes resuming studies after suspending them within the same academic year.
questions.source_excerpt: SLC requires notification of a change of circumstance if students change their programmes of study in any of the following ways: ... c) Resuming studies after having suspended studies within the same academic year;

questions.question: A self-funded student phones the College 12 days after formally accepting their offer to say they want to cancel, then emails their cancellation on day 15. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, was the legal right to cancel exercised in time?
options: Yes, because the phone call on day 12 gave notice of the intention to cancel
No; a phone call is not a stated method, and the email came after 14 days
Yes, because the 14 days run from the programme start date, not acceptance
Yes, provided the College processes the email within 14 days of receiving it
questions.explanation: Cancellation must be notified by a letter sent by post or email, or by the Withdrawal Request Form, before the 14-day grace period after acceptance ends; a phone call is not a stated method and the day-15 email was too late.
questions.source_excerpt: To exercise the legal right to cancel, students must inform the College of the decision in a letter sent by post or email; ... it is sufficient for students to inform the College of the intention to cancel, prior to the end of the 14-day grace period. This can be done by completing the Withdrawal Request Form from Reception or by emailing the College directly;

questions.question: A self-funded student paid a deposit and their first instalment, then cancels on day 12 after formally accepting their offer, following the correct procedure. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what will the College reimburse?
options: All payments received from the student prior to the cancellation
The deposit only, with the instalment held as credit on their account
All payments, less a 25% fee liability under the Table 1 timelines
All payments, less the registration fee charged at the point of enrolment
questions.explanation: A cancellation within the 14-day grace period that follows the procedure entitles the self-funding student to reimbursement of all payments received before cancellation; Table 1 deductions do not apply.
questions.source_excerpt: If students cancel their contracts within the 14-day grace period and follow the procedures set out above, the College will reimburse all payments received from self-funding individuals prior to cancellation;

questions.question: A self-funded undergraduate who paid in full withdraws in week 2 of their programme; the 14-day cancellation period after they accepted their offer ended months ago. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what refund applies?
options: No refund, as the 14-day legal right to cancel has already expired
75% of the full tuition fees paid, reflecting a 25% fee liability
50% of the full tuition fees paid, reflecting a 50% fee liability
A full refund, as Table 1 sets a 0% fee liability for that period
questions.explanation: Once the right to cancel has lapsed, withdrawal refunds follow Table 1, which sets 0% fee liability and a full refund for withdrawals in the 14 days - 2 weeks period.
questions.source_excerpt: The following fee liability and refund timelines apply to all registered students in all academic years: ... 14 days - 2 weeks ... 0% of Tuition Fees ... Full Refund

questions.question: A self-funded undergraduate who paid their fees in full suspends their studies, rather than withdrawing, in week 3 of the programme. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, how is their fee liability determined?
options: Suspension carries no fee liability, as the student intends to resume later
By the date of suspension, which gives a 25% liability under Table 1
By the date of suspension, which gives a 50% liability under Table 1
Liability is 100%, as Table 1 applies only to students who withdraw
questions.explanation: LCC determines fee liability from the date a student withdraws or suspends study, and Table 1 sets a 25% fee liability for the 3-week point.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC will determine the fee liability based upon the date students withdraw or suspend study ... 14 days - 2 weeks ... 3 weeks 4-6 weeks 7 weeks and thereafter ... 0% of Tuition Fees 25% of Tuition Fees 50% of Tuition Fees 100% of Tuition Fees

questions.question: An international self-funded student paid their fees from their own bank account overseas and now asks for their refund to be paid into a new UK account in their name. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, where should the refund go?
options: To the new UK account, because it is held in the student's own name
To whichever account the Programme Manager approves as acceptable
To the overseas account the money was sent from, where possible
In cash at College Reception, to avoid any bank clearing delays
questions.explanation: Refunds are made to the original source, meaning the country and account the money was sent from where possible, to meet due diligence and money laundering requirements.
questions.source_excerpt: Refunds to students will be made to the original source i.e. the country and the account from which the money was sent, where possible. This is to ensure due diligence with national guidelines and compliance with the money laundering regulations;

questions.question: A self-funded student is due a £300 tuition fee refund but owes £500 in tuition arrears. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what happens to the refund?
options: No refund is paid, as only refunds in excess of outstanding debts are paid
The £300 is paid now, and the £500 arrears are invoiced to them separately
The £300 is paid once a Credit Agency has recovered the £500 arrears
The application is rejected and cannot be made again this academic year
questions.explanation: The final refund takes account of outstanding tuition monies, and only refunds in excess of outstanding debts are paid to the student, so a £300 refund is absorbed by £500 of arrears.
questions.source_excerpt: the College will confirm that the final refund amount will take into account any outstanding tuition monies owed to the College; ... Any refunds due to students in excess of outstanding debts will be refunded to them in the usual way

questions.question: A student with no library loans outstanding wants refunds of both their library deposit and their unused Printing and Photocopying Card credit, and would prefer to ask in person. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what applies?
options: Both must be requested by email, as in-person requests are not accepted
Both can be requested in person at College Reception, which pays them out
The printing credit can be requested in person, but the deposit only by email
The deposit can be requested in person; printing credit by emailing the Librarian
questions.explanation: A library deposit refund can be requested in person or by emailing the Librarian, whereas a printing credit refund is requested by emailing the Librarian.
questions.source_excerpt: can request a refund of their deposit either in person or by emailing the Librarian; ... Students with credit remaining on their Printing and Photocopying Card may request a refund for the credit by emailing the Librarian.

questions.question: A student returns all the equipment they borrowed, undamaged, but the deposit they paid was stated to be non-refundable when the loan was made. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, is the deposit refunded?
options: Yes, because all the equipment was handed back in good condition
Yes, once the Programme Leader signs off the department's paperwork
No, because the deposit had to be refundable in the first instance
No, because only sponsored students have equipment deposits refunded
questions.explanation: Equipment deposits are refunded only if all three conditions are met, one being that the deposit was refundable in the first instance; returning the equipment undamaged is not enough on its own.
questions.source_excerpt: students will only be refunded equipment deposits if the College can confirm that they have: ... c) The equipment deposit was refundable in the first instance

questions.question: A student submitted a refund request form 12 working days ago, but the bank account number on it was wrong. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, does the usual refund processing timescale still apply?
options: Yes, the College must process every refund within 15 working days of the form
Yes, the College corrects the details itself and pays within 28 days
No, the refund is forfeited once incorrect bank details have been supplied
No, as the 10-15 working day timescale depends on the information being correct
questions.explanation: Refunds are processed within 10-15 working days only where all the information the student has disclosed is correct, accurate and fulfils all requirements.
questions.source_excerpt: Refunds will be processed within 10-15 working days of receiving the refund request form, providing that all the information disclosed by the student is correct, accurate and fulfils all requirements.

questions.question: A self-funded student who paid their annual fee in full withdraws from two modules, leaving them below the 120 credit points that define full-time for a 3-term year. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, can they claim a fee refund?
options: No, because fee refunds are only available on withdrawal from the entire programme
Yes, but only after a Change of Circumstances form has been processed by IT and Monitoring
Yes, a full refund of the fees for those modules, whatever the date of withdrawal
Yes, if the fee already paid exceeds the fee liability incurred by the withdrawal date
questions.explanation: The bar on module-withdrawal refunds applies only to students still full-time (120 credit points for a 3-term year) afterwards; otherwise a refund may be claimed where the fee already paid exceeds the fee liability incurred by the withdrawal date.
questions.source_excerpt: Withdrawal can be from the entire programme, or one or more modules; ... Students may claim fee refunds if the fee already paid is greater than the fee liability incurred by the withdrawal date ... Self-funding students who withdraw from one or more modules cannot receive a fee refund if they are still defined as `full-time' (120 credit points for a 3-term year) following the withdrawal;

questions.question: A self-funded undergraduate paying by instalments withdraws from their programme in week 9, having paid about 60% of the annual fee, and asks for those instalments to be refunded to their card. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what applies?
options: No refund, as fee liability is 100% for withdrawals from 7 weeks onwards
50% of the instalments paid, refunded to the active card held on file
All instalments paid, as Table 1 applies only to students who pay in full
75% of the instalments paid, as the full annual fee had not yet been paid
questions.explanation: Table 1 sets a 100% fee liability and no refund for withdrawals at 7 weeks and thereafter, and applies to all registered students; a refund can only be claimed where the fee paid exceeds the liability, whatever the payment method.
questions.source_excerpt: Students may claim fee refunds if the fee already paid is greater than the fee liability incurred by the withdrawal date ... The following fee liability and refund timelines apply to all registered students in all academic years: ... 7 weeks and thereafter ... 100% of Tuition Fees ... No Refund

questions.question: An SLC-funded student transfers to another HE provider partway through the academic year and asks the College to send their unused tuition fees to the new provider. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what happens?
options: The College pays the unused tuition fees directly to the new HE provider on request
SLC is notified of the change and re-claims any overpaid fees from the College
The College refunds the unused fees to the student to pass on to the new provider
No notification is needed, as the new provider arranges the funding with SLC
questions.explanation: Transferring to another HE provider is a change SLC must be notified of; once it is processed, SLC re-claims any overpaid fees directly from the College, as overpayments for SLC-funded students go to SLC rather than to the student or elsewhere.
questions.source_excerpt: any overpayments will be paid directly by the College to SLC; ... f) Transferring to a new programme or to another HE Provider; ... Once a change of circumstance has been processed, SLC will re-claim any overpaid fees directly from the College.

questions.question: A student returns all the equipment they borrowed, undamaged, against a deposit that was refundable. The department's refund paperwork has been signed by a department administrator but not by the Programme Leader. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what happens?
options: It is refunded, as all three equipment deposit conditions are met
It is refunded once the Librarian confirms the equipment has been returned
The refund will be refused unless the Programme Leader signs off the paperwork
It goes to the Programme Manager, who forwards it to Finance if acceptable
questions.explanation: Meeting the three equipment deposit conditions is not enough on its own: the department's paperwork must be signed off by the Programme Leader or the refund will be refused.
questions.source_excerpt: students will only be refunded equipment deposits if the College can confirm that they have: ... Departments will provide the student with the necessary paperwork, but this must be signed off by the Programme Leader or the refund will be refused.

questions.question: An international student who cannot obtain SLC funding wants their parents to pay the annual tuition fee from an overseas account in US dollars. Under the Tuition Fee and Refund Policy, what applies?
options: Their parents may pay in US dollars, as the College accepts overseas currencies
Only the student or an official sponsor may pay, so their parents cannot pay
They must first apply to SLC and provide a Payment Advice receipt before paying
Their family may pay, but the payment must be made in pounds sterling
questions.explanation: Students who cannot obtain SLC funding may pay through themselves or their family, among other sources, but all tuition fee payments must be made in pounds sterling.
questions.source_excerpt: The payment of tuition fees must be made in pounds sterling ... Students who cannot or do not wish to obtain funding from the Student Loan Company, can pay through one of the following sources: ... b) The student or his/her family or other.

questions.question: A student tells you they are considering withdrawing from their course. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, who should they discuss their circumstances with?
options: The Admissions team
Their Personal Tutor
The Quality Assurance Officer
The Assessment and Progression Board
questions.explanation: The policy states that a student considering withdrawal should discuss their circumstances with their Personal Tutor, who may provide guidance and direction.
questions.source_excerpt: A student considering withdrawal should discuss his/her circumstances with their Personal Tutor. The Personal Tutor may provide appropriate guidance and direction to the students by considering their circumstances

questions.question: A student has decided to withdraw from their programme and asks you what formal step they must take. What does the Withdrawal of Studies Policy require?
options: Email their Personal Tutor, who will then process the withdrawal on their behalf
Stop attending classes, as the withdrawal will then be recorded automatically
Submit a written request to the Admissions team for their approval
Complete and submit the College Withdrawal Request Form to the Registrar
questions.explanation: The policy requires a student seeking withdrawal to fill in and submit the College Withdrawal Request Form to the Registrar.
questions.source_excerpt: A student seeking withdrawal from the programme of study, must fill and submit the College Withdrawal Request Form to the Registrar

questions.question: A student has received written notification of the College's decision to withdraw them and wants to appeal. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what must they do?
options: Write to the Quality Assurance Officer within 10 working days of the notification
Write to their Personal Tutor within 15 working days of the notification
Write to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the notification
Write to the Registrar within 10 calendar days of receiving the notification
questions.explanation: At Stage One, the student lodges an appeal by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision.
questions.source_excerpt: A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of withdrawal by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision

questions.question: According to the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, who takes a withdrawal decision on the grounds of unsatisfactory academic progress or unacceptable attendance?
options: The Registrar and the Registry department
The Assessment and Progression Board
The student's Personal Tutor and Course Leader
The Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee)
questions.explanation: The policy states that withdrawal decisions on grounds of unsatisfactory academic progress or unacceptable attendance are taken by the Assessment and Progression Board.
questions.source_excerpt: Withdrawal decision on the grounds of unsatisfactory academic progress or unacceptable attendance will be taken by the Assessment and Progression Board.

questions.question: A student who was withdrawn for breaching the Student Code of Conduct applies to re-join the College. What does the Withdrawal of Studies Policy state?
options: They will not be re-admitted to the College
They may be re-admitted if they meet entry criteria
They may re-join after a 12-month exclusion period
They may return if their Personal Tutor supports it
questions.explanation: The policy states that students withdrawn as a result of breaches of the Student Code of Conduct will not be re-admitted to the College.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who have been withdrawn as a result of breaches of the Student Code of Conduct will not be re-admitted to the College.

questions.question: According to the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which of the following is a permissible ground for a student to appeal a College-led withdrawal decision?
options: Disagreement with the academic judgement made by the Assessment and Progression Board
New material evidence the student could not provide earlier owing to exceptional circumstances
An improvement in the student's attendance and engagement since the withdrawal decision was made
The negative effect the withdrawal will have on the student's future career, finances or visa plans
questions.explanation: Appeals are permitted only where the policy has not been followed or where new material evidence has emerged that the student could not provide earlier owing to exceptional circumstances.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following grounds: ... New material evidence has emerged which the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier in the process

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, how must a student request a review of a Stage One appeal decision?
options: By writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome
By writing directly to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator within 10 working days of the outcome
By asking their Personal Tutor to refer the case directly to an Appeal Panel on their behalf
By writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of the outcome
questions.explanation: Stage Two requires the applicant to write to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome.
questions.source_excerpt: An applicant who wishes to have the Stage One decision reviewed must do so by writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome

questions.question: A former student who withdrew by their own choice last year asks how they can re-join the same programme. What does the Withdrawal of Studies Policy say?
options: They can ask the Registrar to reinstate their original enrolment and student record
They must lodge a readmission appeal with the Quality Assurance Officer
They cannot re-join the same programme, although they may apply for a different one
They must make a new admission application, decided by the Admissions team
questions.explanation: Students who withdrew through their own choice must make a new admission application to re-join the same or a different programme, and the Admissions team decides on re-admission.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who have been withdrawn from the programme of study through their own choice should make a new admission application if they wish to re-join whether studying the same or different programme. ... The decision to re-admit will be made by the Admissions team

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what term does the College use for a College-led withdrawal on non-academic grounds that has a disciplinary element?
options: Expulsion
Suspension
Withdrawal
Exclusion
questions.explanation: The policy uses 'withdrawal' for student-led and academic-grounds College-led withdrawals, but a College-led withdrawal on non-academic grounds with a disciplinary element is termed 'expulsion'.
questions.source_excerpt: The College-led withdrawal on the non-academic grounds with `disciplinary element' is termed `expulsion'.

questions.question: According to the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, how does London Churchill College define 'withdrawal'?
options: A temporary break in studies after which the student keeps a guaranteed right to return to the same course
Any unauthorised absence from classes or teaching activities, whether short-term or long-term in duration
A permanent status for a student who leaves other than by successful completion, or imposed by the College
A status that applies when a student chooses to leave their course, but not when a departure is imposed by the College
questions.explanation: Although withdrawal can be temporary or permanent in the wider higher education context, the policy states that LCC defines it as a permanent status for a student who leaves other than by successful completion, or where it is imposed by the College.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC defines the term as a permanent status for a student who may leave the course other than successful completion of their programme of study or imposed by the College

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Withdrawal of Studies Policy as an academic ground for a College-led withdrawal?
options: Unacceptable attendance at classes or teaching activities
Unsatisfactory academic progress
Causing damage to property belonging to the College
A suspended student not meeting the conditions of return
questions.explanation: Damage to College property is listed as a non-academic ground; unacceptable attendance, unsatisfactory academic progress and a suspended student not satisfying the conditions of return to study are academic grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic grounds: Unacceptable attendance and/or unsatisfactory academic progress. ... Non-academic grounds: Non-payment of tuition fees, unacceptable behaviour, assault bullying, damage to College property ... (Academic Grounds) ... A student is unsuccessful in meeting the progression expectations in accordance with the Continuation and Completion Policy ; ... A suspended student not satisfying the conditions of return to study

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, once Stage Two has been exhausted, where may a student who remains dissatisfied take their case?
options: To Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA)
Back to the Registrar to lodge a fresh Stage One appeal
To the Admissions team for a new readmission decision on the case
To the Assessment and Progression Board for a full rehearing of the case
questions.explanation: The policy states that after Stage Two is exhausted, a student not satisfied with the outcome may proceed with their case to Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA).
questions.source_excerpt: Following the exhaustion of Stage Two, following which the student may, if the matter has not been resolved to their satisfaction, proceed with their case to the Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA).

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, once a student has submitted the College Withdrawal Request Form, which department reviews it?
options: The Registry department
The Admissions team
The Quality Assurance team
The Student Services team
questions.explanation: The policy states that the Withdrawal Request Form will be reviewed by the Registry department, which then communicates the outcome letter in writing.
questions.source_excerpt: The form will be reviewed by the Registry department and the outcome letter will be communicated in writing.

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which date must the written outcome letter for a student's withdrawal request contain?
options: The date of the next Assessment and Progression Board
The deadline for handing in any outstanding assessments
The date of the student's last recorded class attendance
The date from which the student's withdrawal will apply
questions.explanation: The policy states that the outcome letter will contain the date from which the withdrawal applies.
questions.source_excerpt: The letter will contain the date from which the withdrawal applies.

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which example does the policy give of a condition of withdrawal that may be detailed in the outcome letter?
options: Payment of an administrative withdrawal fee to the Registry
The return of any outstanding library books or other equipment
An exit interview with the student's Personal Tutor and Course Leader
Completion of an end-of-programme feedback survey for the College
questions.explanation: The outcome letter details any conditions of withdrawal where they apply, and the policy's example is the return of outstanding library books or other equipment.
questions.source_excerpt: The letter will also detail any conditions of withdrawal where these may apply (e.g., the return of outstanding library books or other equipment);

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what happens to any assessment a student submitted before their date of withdrawal?
options: It is voided and removed from the student's academic record without being marked
It is held on file by Registry and marked only if the student is later re-admitted
It is marked and considered at the next available Assessment and Progression Board
It is returned to the student unmarked, along with their written outcome letter
questions.explanation: The policy states that any assessment submitted before the date of withdrawal will be marked and considered at the next available Assessment and Progression Board.
questions.source_excerpt: Any assessment submitted by the student prior to their date of withdrawal will be marked and considered at the next available Assessment and Progression Board;

questions.question: A student who withdrew by their own choice applies to re-join LCC. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what may be taken into consideration, where relevant and in line with academic regulations?
options: Automatic reinstatement to the year of study they previously left
A waiver of the entry criteria for the course they now apply to
A refund of the tuition fees they paid for their earlier study
Recognition of any credit they attained during their previous study
questions.explanation: For students who withdrew by choice and reapply, recognition of any credit attained during previous study may be taken into consideration; the Admissions team still applies the relevant entry criteria.
questions.source_excerpt: Where relevant, and in line with academic regulations, recognition of any credit attained during their previous study may be taken into consideration. The decision to re-admit will be made by the Admissions team, applying the relevant entry criteria

questions.question: According to the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what does a student's failure to achieve the minimum credit value result in, per the academic regulations?
options: The risk of withdrawal from the programme
Possible expulsion under the Disciplinary Procedure
A possible suspension of studies decided by the Registrar
Possible referral to the Quality Assurance Officer
questions.explanation: Under the academic grounds for College-led withdrawal, the policy states that failure to achieve the minimum credit value will result in the risk of withdrawal per the academic regulations.
questions.source_excerpt: Failure to achieve the minimum credit value will result in the risk of withdrawal per the academic regulations.

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, a student may be withdrawn on academic grounds for not meeting the progression expectations set out in which College policy?
options: The College Attendance Policy
The Continuation and Completion Policy
The Assessment and Progression Board Policy
The Student Code of Conduct
questions.explanation: One academic reason for withdrawal is a student being unsuccessful in meeting the progression expectations in accordance with the Continuation and Completion Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: A student is unsuccessful in meeting the progression expectations in accordance with the Continuation and Completion Policy

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, a penalty resulting from the outcome of which procedure is listed as a non-academic reason for withdrawing a student?
options: The Attendance Monitoring Procedure
The Disciplinary Procedure
The Progression Review Procedure
The Student Complaints Procedure
questions.explanation: The non-academic reasons for withdrawal include any penalty compelled on the ground of misconduct or the outcome of the Disciplinary Procedure.
questions.source_excerpt: Any penalty compelled on the ground of misconduct or outcome of the Disciplinary Procedure.

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, a student who was withdrawn for reasons of non-attendance may be considered for re-admittance to which programme?
options: Only a different programme from the one they previously left
Only the same programme, at the stage at which they left it
The same programme or an alternative programme
None, as a withdrawal for non-attendance cannot be reversed
questions.explanation: The policy states that students withdrawn for non-attendance may be considered for re-admittance to the same or an alternative programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who have been withdrawn for reasons of non-attendance may be considered for re-admittance to the same or an alternative programme.

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, when does a student have the right to appeal a withdrawal decision?
options: At any time, whether the withdrawal was student-led or College-led
When the withdrawal is College-led, whatever the grounds for the appeal
Only when the withdrawal is an expulsion following the Disciplinary Procedure
When the withdrawal is College-led and they have valid grounds for an appeal
questions.explanation: The right to appeal applies to College-led withdrawal decisions, provided the student has valid grounds for an appeal.
questions.source_excerpt: A student has the right to appeal a withdrawal decision if it is led by the College, providing that they have valid grounds for an appeal;

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, who conducts the review of a Stage One appeal that is considered to be based on valid grounds?
options: The Registrar, or an appeal reviewer whom the Registrar nominates
The Quality Assurance Officer, or a nominee of their choosing
An Appeal Panel convened by the Assessment and Progression Board
The student's Personal Tutor, supported by their Course Leader
questions.explanation: At Stage One, if the appeal is based on valid grounds, the Registrar conducts the appeal review or nominates an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim.
questions.source_excerpt: If the appeal is considered to be based on the above valid grounds, the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim;

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, besides being communicated to the applicant in writing, where is the outcome of a Stage One appeal listed?
options: In the College's appeal logbook
On the student's transcript
In the Assessment and Progression Board minutes
In the student's Personal Tutor records
questions.explanation: The Stage One appeal outcome is communicated to the applicant in writing and listed in the College's appeal logbook.
questions.source_excerpt: The outcome of the appeal will be communicated to the applicant in writing and listed in the College's appeal logbook;

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, if a Stage One appeal is not upheld, what must the applicant be informed of?
options: Their right to go straight to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
Their right to request a review of Stage One, with instructions and time limits
Their right to apply for readmission through the Admissions team instead
Their right to have their Personal Tutor lodge a second appeal on their behalf
questions.explanation: If a Stage One appeal is not upheld, the applicant must be informed of their right to request a review of Stage One, with instructions on how to do so and the time limits.
questions.source_excerpt: If the appeal is not upheld, the applicant will be informed of their right to request a review of Stage One, as well as instructions on how to do so and the time limits.

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what does the Quality Assurance Officer do with a Stage Two review request that is deemed to be on reasonable grounds?
options: Returns it to the Registrar for a fresh Stage One review
Sends it to the Assessment and Progression Board to decide
Forwards it directly to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator
Refers it to an Appeal Panel for consideration
questions.explanation: At Stage Two, a review request deemed to be on reasonable grounds is referred by the Quality Assurance Officer to an Appeal Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: If the request is deemed to be on reasonable grounds, the Quality Assurance Officer will refer it to an Appeal Panel.

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what is the applicant issued with if their Stage Two review request is rejected?
options: A Final Withdrawal Confirmation letter
A Stage Two Closure Notice
A Completion of Procedures letter
A Notice of Appeal Panel Outcome
questions.explanation: The policy states that if a Stage Two review request is rejected, the applicant shall be issued with a Completion of Procedures letter.
questions.source_excerpt: However, if the request is rejected, the applicant shall be issued with a Completion of Procedures letter;

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which sequence correctly reflects the student-led withdrawal procedure?
options: Submit the Withdrawal Request Form to the Personal Tutor, who refers it to the Assessment and Progression Board to decide
Discuss with the Admissions team, submit the form to the Registrar, then receive a verbal outcome from the Personal Tutor
Discuss with the Personal Tutor, submit the Withdrawal Request Form to the Registrar, then receive a written outcome
Notify the Registrar in writing, attend an exit meeting with the Quality Assurance Officer, then receive a written outcome
questions.explanation: A student considering withdrawal should first discuss their circumstances with their Personal Tutor, then submit the College Withdrawal Request Form to the Registrar; Registry reviews it and communicates the outcome in writing.
questions.source_excerpt: A student considering withdrawal should discuss his/her circumstances with their Personal Tutor. ... A student seeking withdrawal from the programme of study, must fill and submit the College Withdrawal Request Form to the Registrar; ... The form will be reviewed by the Registry department and the outcome letter will be communicated in writing.

questions.question: A student who is withdrawing still has a College laptop on loan. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, where would a requirement to return it be set out?
options: In the College Withdrawal Request Form that the student submits to the Registrar
As a condition of withdrawal detailed in the written outcome letter
In a Completion of Procedures letter issued by the Quality Assurance Officer
In the minutes of the next Assessment and Progression Board meeting
questions.explanation: The written outcome letter details any conditions of withdrawal where they apply, such as the return of outstanding library books or other equipment.
questions.source_excerpt: The form will be reviewed by the Registry department and the outcome letter will be communicated in writing. ... The letter will also detail any conditions of withdrawal where these may apply (e.g., the return of outstanding library books or other equipment);

questions.question: A student withdrawn by the College on academic grounds has evidence that the College did not follow the Withdrawal of Studies Policy in reaching the decision. Under the policy, which is correct?
options: They may not appeal, as the only permissible ground is new material evidence
They may not appeal, as decisions of the Assessment and Progression Board are final
They may appeal only if their Personal Tutor first confirms the evidence in writing
They may appeal, as this is one of the two grounds on which an appeal is permissible
questions.explanation: Students may appeal College-led withdrawal decisions on valid grounds, and evidence that the Withdrawal of Studies Policy has not been followed is one of the two permissible grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: A student has the right to appeal a withdrawal decision if it is led by the College, providing that they have valid grounds for an appeal; ... In circumstances where there is evidence that the College's Withdrawal of Studies Policy has not been followed;

questions.question: A student receives the College's written withdrawal decision on 3 May, appeals, and on 7 June receives a Stage One outcome that does not uphold the appeal. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, how must they request a review?
options: In writing to the Registrar, as a second Stage One appeal, within 15 working days of 7 June
In writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), within 10 working days of 7 June
In writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), within 10 working days of 3 May
In writing to an Appeal Panel, within 15 working days of the original decision on 3 May
questions.explanation: A Stage Two review is requested in writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome, not the original decision.
questions.source_excerpt: A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of withdrawal by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision; ... must do so by writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome;

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, a student's Stage Two review request is rejected and they remain dissatisfied. What follows?
options: The request is passed automatically to an Appeal Panel for a final hearing of the case
They may lodge a fresh Stage One appeal with the Registrar within 15 working days
They receive a Completion of Procedures letter and may take the case to Pearson or the OIA
The Registrar nominates a new appeal reviewer to reinvestigate the original claim in full
questions.explanation: A rejected Stage Two request leads to a Completion of Procedures letter; once Stage Two is exhausted, a dissatisfied student may take the case to Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator.
questions.source_excerpt: However, if the request is rejected, the applicant shall be issued with a Completion of Procedures letter; ... Following the exhaustion of Stage Two, following which the student may, if the matter has not been resolved to their satisfaction, proceed with their case to the Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA).

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which sequence correctly describes the route for challenging a College-led withdrawal decision?
options: Stage One appeal to the Registrar, Stage Two review via the Quality Assurance Officer, then Pearson or the OIA
Stage One review by the Quality Assurance Officer, Stage Two appeal to the Registrar, then Pearson or the OIA
Appeal to the Personal Tutor, then to the Registrar, then a final decision by the Assessment and Progression Board
Complaint to the OIA first, then a Stage One appeal to the Registrar, then a hearing before an Appeal Panel
questions.explanation: Stage One is an appeal in writing to the Registrar, Stage Two is a review requested from the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), and only after Stage Two is exhausted may the student go to Pearson or the OIA.
questions.source_excerpt: A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of withdrawal by writing to the Registrar ... must do so by writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) ... Following the exhaustion of Stage Two, ... proceed with their case to the Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA).

questions.question: A student faces College-led withdrawal for failing to pay their tuition fees. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, how is this reason classified, and which policy outlines the financial commitments?
options: Academic grounds; the commitments are outlined in the Continuation and Completion Policy
Non-academic grounds; the commitments are outlined in the Student Code of Conduct
Academic grounds; the commitments are outlined in the College Attendance Policy
Non-academic grounds; the commitments are outlined in the College's Tuition Fees Policy
questions.explanation: Non-payment of tuition fees is a non-academic ground for College-led withdrawal, and the fees and other financial commitments are those outlined in the College's Tuition Fees Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Non-academic grounds: Non-payment of tuition fees ... Failure to pay tuition fees or other financial commitments to the College as outlined in the College's Tuition Fees Policy;

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy's terminology, which of the following would be termed 'expulsion' rather than 'withdrawal'?
options: A student leaving their course by choice after discussing it with their Personal Tutor
The Assessment and Progression Board withdrawing a student for unacceptable attendance
The College withdrawing a student after a Disciplinary Procedure outcome for bullying
The College withdrawing a student who has not met the expected progression requirements
questions.explanation: Only a College-led withdrawal on non-academic grounds with a disciplinary element is termed 'expulsion'; student-led withdrawals and College-led withdrawals on academic grounds are termed 'withdrawal'.
questions.source_excerpt: Student-led withdrawal is termed `withdrawal'; 2.2.2. The College-led withdrawal on the academic grounds is termed `withdrawal'; 2.2.3. The College-led withdrawal on the non-academic grounds with `disciplinary element' is termed `expulsion'.

questions.question: A Course Leader wants a student with persistently unacceptable attendance withdrawn. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, how should this be handled?
options: The Course Leader withdraws the student directly by notifying the Registry department in writing
The Attendance Policy stages are followed, and the Assessment and Progression Board decides
The student is asked to submit a Withdrawal Request Form, which the Registry department reviews
The Personal Tutor decides after discussing the student's circumstances and attendance with them
questions.explanation: The College Attendance Policy sets out the stages undertaken before a withdrawal decision is imposed, and a withdrawal on attendance grounds is decided by the Assessment and Progression Board.
questions.source_excerpt: The College Attendance Policy clearly states the stages that are undertaken before imposing a withdrawal decision to a student; ... Withdrawal decision on the grounds of unsatisfactory academic progress or unacceptable attendance will be taken by the Assessment and Progression Board.

questions.question: Two former students apply to return to LCC: one was withdrawn for non-attendance, the other for breaching the Student Code of Conduct. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which is correct?
options: Both may be considered by the Admissions team, applying the relevant entry criteria
Only the first may be considered for re-admittance; the second will not be re-admitted
Neither may return, as any withdrawal led by the College is permanent and final
The first must appeal to the Registrar; the second may reapply after twelve months
questions.explanation: Students withdrawn for non-attendance may be considered for re-admittance, but students withdrawn for breaches of the Student Code of Conduct will not be re-admitted.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who have been withdrawn for reasons of non-attendance may be considered for re-admittance to the same or an alternative programme. ... Students who have been withdrawn as a result of breaches of the Student Code of Conduct will not be re-admitted to the College.

questions.question: A student withdrawn for non-attendance applies to join an alternative programme. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, who makes the re-admission decision, and on what basis?
options: The Admissions team, applying the relevant entry criteria for the course applied for
The Assessment and Progression Board, based on the student's previous attendance record
The Registrar, based on any conditions set out in the student's original withdrawal letter
The Personal Tutor, based on their own view of the student's current circumstances
questions.explanation: For students withdrawn for non-attendance, the re-admission decision is made by the Admissions team, applying the relevant entry criteria for the course applied for.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who have been withdrawn for reasons of non-attendance may be considered for re-admittance to the same or an alternative programme. ... The decision to re-admit will be made by the Admissions team, applying the relevant entry criteria for the course for which the student has applied;

questions.question: A student lodges a Stage One appeal against a College-led withdrawal. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what must be established before the Registrar conducts the review or nominates a reviewer?
options: That the student's Personal Tutor supports the appeal and has confirmed this in writing
That the Quality Assurance Officer has referred the appeal on to an Appeal Panel
That the Assessment and Progression Board has agreed to reopen its original decision
That the appeal is considered to be based on the valid grounds set out in the policy
questions.explanation: The Registrar conducts the Stage One review, or nominates a reviewer, only if the appeal is considered to be based on the policy's valid grounds.
questions.source_excerpt: If the appeal is considered to be based on the above valid grounds, the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim;

questions.question: A student appeals a College-led withdrawal using a medical letter they held throughout the process but chose not to submit, with no exceptional circumstances. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, is this a permissible ground?
options: Yes, as any new material evidence submitted with an appeal is a permissible ground
Yes, provided the letter reaches the Registrar within 15 working days of the notification
No, as they could have provided it earlier and no exceptional circumstances prevented this
Yes, provided their Personal Tutor confirms in writing that the medical evidence is genuine
questions.explanation: New material evidence is a permissible ground only where the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide it earlier; a letter held throughout and simply not submitted does not meet that condition.
questions.source_excerpt: An appeal is permissible only on the following grounds: ... New material evidence has emerged which the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier in the process;

questions.question: A student tells their Personal Tutor they are considering withdrawing. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what is the Personal Tutor's role at this point?
options: To review the Withdrawal Request Form and issue the written outcome letter
To decide whether the student's request to withdraw should be approved
To provide appropriate guidance and direction, considering their circumstances
To set the date from which the student's withdrawal from the course will apply
questions.explanation: The Personal Tutor may provide appropriate guidance and direction by considering the student's circumstances; the Withdrawal Request Form itself is reviewed by the Registry department.
questions.source_excerpt: A student considering withdrawal should discuss his/her circumstances with their Personal Tutor. The Personal Tutor may provide appropriate guidance and direction to the students by considering their circumstances; ... The form will be reviewed by the Registry department

questions.question: A suspended student does not satisfy the conditions of return to study, and the College moves to withdraw them. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, how is this classified and termed?
options: College-led withdrawal on non-academic grounds, termed 'expulsion'
Student-led withdrawal, as the student chose not to meet the conditions
College-led withdrawal on non-academic grounds, termed 'withdrawal'
College-led withdrawal on academic grounds, termed 'withdrawal'
questions.explanation: A suspended student not satisfying the conditions of return to study is listed among the academic reasons for withdrawal, and a College-led withdrawal on academic grounds is termed 'withdrawal'.
questions.source_excerpt: Reasons for withdrawing students (Academic Grounds) ... A suspended student not satisfying the conditions of return to study; ... The College-led withdrawal on the academic grounds is termed `withdrawal';

questions.question: A Registry officer is recording four student departures. Under LCC's definition in the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which one counts as a 'withdrawal'?
options: A student whose studies are permanently ended by the College for non-payment of fees
A student who leaves LCC after successfully completing their programme of study
A student whose studies are paused for a term under a suspension, pending return
A student who misses two weeks of classes through illness and then resumes studying
questions.explanation: LCC defines withdrawal as a permanent status for a student who leaves other than by successful completion, or where it is imposed by the College; successful completion and temporary pauses fall outside that definition.
questions.source_excerpt: LCC defines the term as a permanent status for a student who may leave the course other than successful completion of their programme of study or imposed by the College; ... Non-academic grounds: Non-payment of tuition fees

questions.question: A student submitted the College Withdrawal Request Form, received the Registry outcome letter, and now regrets leaving. They ask to appeal under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy. Which is correct?
options: They may appeal to the Registrar within 15 working days, as any withdrawal can be appealed
They have no right of appeal, as that right applies to withdrawal decisions led by the College
They may appeal on the ground of a change of mind if they write within 10 working days
They may ask the Quality Assurance Officer to refer the Registry decision to an Appeal Panel
questions.explanation: The right to appeal applies to withdrawal decisions led by the College; a student who withdrew by choice would instead need to make a new admission application to re-join.
questions.source_excerpt: A student has the right to appeal a withdrawal decision if it is led by the College, providing that they have valid grounds for an appeal; ... Students who have been withdrawn from the programme of study through their own choice should make a new admission application if they wish to re-join

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which pairing of a written communication and the point at which it is issued is correct?
options: Completion of Procedures letter: issued when a student-led withdrawal request is approved
Outcome letter stating the withdrawal date: issued by an Appeal Panel after a Stage Two review
Information on requesting a review of Stage One: given when a Stage One appeal is upheld
Completion of Procedures letter: issued when a Stage Two review request is rejected
questions.explanation: A Completion of Procedures letter is issued when a Stage Two review request is rejected; the outcome letter with the withdrawal date follows Registry's review of the request form, and review information is given when a Stage One appeal is not upheld.
questions.source_excerpt: The form will be reviewed by the Registry department and the outcome letter will be communicated in writing. The letter will contain the date from which the withdrawal applies. ... If the appeal is not upheld, the applicant will be informed of their right to request a review of Stage One ... However, if the request is rejected, the applicant shall be issued with a Completion of Procedures letter;

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which pairing of a task and the party responsible for it is correct?
options: Conducting a Stage One appeal review: the Quality Assurance Officer
Deciding re-admission after a withdrawal by choice: the Registrar
Reviewing a College Withdrawal Request Form: the Registry department
Deciding a withdrawal for unacceptable attendance: the Registry department
questions.explanation: Registry reviews the Withdrawal Request Form; the Registrar (or a nominated reviewer) conducts Stage One reviews, the Admissions team decides re-admission, and the Assessment and Progression Board decides attendance-based withdrawals.
questions.source_excerpt: The form will be reviewed by the Registry department ... The decision to re-admit will be made by the Admissions team ... will be taken by the Assessment and Progression Board. ... the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which two steps taken by a student are both directed to the Registrar?
options: Requesting a Stage Two review, and escalating a case once Stage Two is exhausted
Submitting the College Withdrawal Request Form, and lodging a Stage One appeal
Discussing a withdrawal, and requesting a review of a Stage One outcome
Escalating a case once Stage Two is exhausted, and discussing a possible withdrawal
questions.explanation: The Withdrawal Request Form and a Stage One appeal both go to the Registrar; a Stage Two review goes to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), withdrawal is discussed with the Personal Tutor, and escalation is to Pearson or the OIA.
questions.source_excerpt: must fill and submit the College Withdrawal Request Form to the Registrar; ... A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of withdrawal by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days ... by writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee)

questions.question: A student has excellent attendance and academic progress but has taken action liable to bring the College into disrepute. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, may the College withdraw them?
options: No, as a College-led withdrawal requires unacceptable attendance or unsatisfactory progress
Only if the student first agrees to submit a College Withdrawal Request Form to the Registrar
Yes, as action liable to bring the College into disrepute is a non-academic ground
Only if the Assessment and Progression Board also finds their academic progress unsatisfactory
questions.explanation: The College may withdraw a student on academic or non-academic grounds, and any action liable to bring the College into disrepute is listed as a non-academic ground, regardless of academic performance.
questions.source_excerpt: The College can undertake a withdrawal decision either on academic grounds or non-academic grounds: ... Non-academic grounds: Non-payment of tuition fees, unacceptable behaviour, assault bullying, damage to College property and any action liable to bring the College into disrepute.

questions.question: A student's tuition fees are paid, but they have not met other financial commitments to the College set out in the Tuition Fees Policy. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which is correct?
options: This can be a non-academic reason for withdrawal, in the same way as non-payment of fees
This cannot lead to withdrawal, as only unpaid tuition fees are a financial ground
This is an academic reason for withdrawal, decided by the Assessment and Progression Board
This can lead to withdrawal only after a Disciplinary Procedure finds financial misconduct
questions.explanation: The non-academic reasons for withdrawal include failure to pay tuition fees or other financial commitments to the College as outlined in the Tuition Fees Policy.
questions.source_excerpt: Reasons for withdrawing students (Non-Academic Grounds) ... Failure to pay tuition fees or other financial commitments to the College as outlined in the College's Tuition Fees Policy;

questions.question: A student fails to achieve the minimum credit value and the College moves to end their studies. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, who takes that decision, and what is it termed?
options: The Assessment and Progression Board; it is termed 'expulsion'
The Registry department, after review; it is termed 'withdrawal'
The Assessment and Progression Board; it is termed 'withdrawal'
The Registrar, after a Stage One review; it is termed 'expulsion'
questions.explanation: Failure to achieve the minimum credit value sits under the academic ground of unsatisfactory academic progress, which the Assessment and Progression Board decides, and a College-led withdrawal on academic grounds is termed 'withdrawal'.
questions.source_excerpt: Academic grounds: Unacceptable attendance and/or unsatisfactory academic progress. [Failure to achieve the minimum credit value will result in the risk of withdrawal per the academic regulations.] ... will be taken by the Assessment and Progression Board. ... The College-led withdrawal on the academic grounds is termed `withdrawal';

questions.question: The College ends two students' studies on non-academic grounds: one after a Disciplinary Procedure outcome for assault, the other solely for unpaid tuition fees. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy's terminology, which is correct?
options: Both are termed 'expulsion', as both are College-led and on non-academic grounds
Neither is termed 'expulsion', as that term is reserved for academic-grounds decisions
