Only the second is termed 'expulsion', as unpaid fees breach the Tuition Fees Policy
Only the first is termed 'expulsion', as only it involves a disciplinary element
questions.explanation: 'Expulsion' is used only for a College-led withdrawal on non-academic grounds with a disciplinary element, so only the withdrawal following the Disciplinary Procedure outcome is termed expulsion.
questions.source_excerpt: The College-led withdrawal on the non-academic grounds with `disciplinary element' is termed `expulsion'.

questions.question: A student expelled after a Disciplinary Procedure outcome has new material evidence they could not provide earlier owing to exceptional circumstances. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, may they appeal?
options: No, as only withdrawals on academic grounds carry a right of appeal
Yes, as expulsion is a College-led withdrawal and this is a valid ground
No, as an expulsion can be challenged only through Pearson or the OIA
Yes, but only once their Personal Tutor has endorsed the new evidence
questions.explanation: Expulsion is a College-led withdrawal, so the student may appeal on valid grounds, and new material evidence they were unable to provide earlier owing to exceptional circumstances is a permissible ground.
questions.source_excerpt: The College-led withdrawal on the non-academic grounds with `disciplinary element' is termed `expulsion'. ... A student has the right to appeal a withdrawal decision if it is led by the College, providing that they have valid grounds for an appeal; ... New material evidence has emerged which the student was unable, owing to exceptional circumstances, to provide earlier in the process;

questions.question: A student withdrawn for unacceptable attendance accepts that the policy was followed and has no new evidence, but feels the decision was harsh. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, can they appeal?
options: Yes, as every College-led withdrawal decision carries an automatic right of appeal
Yes, provided they write to the Registrar within 15 working days of the decision
No, as appeals are permitted only for a policy breach or for new material evidence
No, as attendance-based decisions of the Board can be challenged only at the OIA
questions.explanation: The right to appeal depends on valid grounds, and an appeal is permissible only where the policy has not been followed or new material evidence has emerged; feeling the decision was harsh is neither.
questions.source_excerpt: A student has the right to appeal a withdrawal decision if it is led by the College, providing that they have valid grounds for an appeal; ... An appeal is permissible only on the following grounds: ... In circumstances where there is evidence that the College's Withdrawal of Studies Policy has not been followed; ... New material evidence has emerged

questions.question: A student received written notification of a College-led withdrawal decision 12 working days ago and has just found evidence that the policy was not followed. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what should they be told?
options: They have 3 working days left to lodge a Stage One appeal in writing to the Registrar
They are out of time, as a Stage One appeal must be lodged within 10 working days
They must write to the Quality Assurance Officer, as over 10 working days have passed
They have 15 working days from today, as the limit runs from discovering the breach
questions.explanation: A Stage One appeal must be lodged in writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification, so 3 working days remain.
questions.source_excerpt: A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of withdrawal by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision;

questions.question: A student's Stage One appeal was not upheld. Eight working days after receiving that outcome, they write to the Quality Assurance Officer's nominee asking for a review. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which is correct?
options: The request is invalid, as a Stage Two review must be requested from the Registrar
The request is out of time, as a review must be requested within 5 working days
The request is invalid, as only the Quality Assurance Officer in person may receive it
The request meets the policy's requirements for seeking a review of Stage One
questions.explanation: A Stage One decision may be reviewed by writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome, which this request satisfies.
questions.source_excerpt: An applicant who wishes to have the Stage One decision reviewed must do so by writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome;

questions.question: A student withdrawn for non-attendance applies for re-admittance to an alternative programme and asks whether credit from their earlier study counts. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which is correct?
options: The credit is forfeited, as recognition applies only to students who withdrew by choice
Recognition of the credit may be considered for the same or an alternative programme
The credit transfers automatically, as the student is returning to the same College
Recognition of the credit may be considered only if they return to their previous programme
questions.explanation: For students withdrawn for non-attendance, recognition of credit attained during previous study may be taken into consideration where relevant and in line with academic regulations, for the same or an alternative programme.
questions.source_excerpt: Students who have been withdrawn for reasons of non-attendance may be considered for re-admittance to the same or an alternative programme. Where relevant, and in line with academic regulations, recognition of any credit attained during their previous study may be taken into consideration.

questions.question: A nominated appeal reviewer does not uphold a student's Stage One appeal against a College-led withdrawal. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which set of actions must follow?
options: A written outcome, an entry in the appeal logbook, and information on requesting a review
A Completion of Procedures letter and automatic referral of the case to an Appeal Panel
A verbal outcome from the Registrar and a note added to the student's Registry file
A written outcome and direct referral of the case to Pearson or the OIA by the Registrar
questions.explanation: The Stage One outcome is communicated in writing and listed in the appeal logbook, and if not upheld the applicant is told of their right to request a review, with instructions and time limits.
questions.source_excerpt: The outcome of the appeal will be communicated to the applicant in writing and listed in the College's appeal logbook; ... If the appeal is not upheld, the applicant will be informed of their right to request a review of Stage One, as well as instructions on how to do so and the time limits.

questions.question: A student's Stage One appeal is not upheld and they want to take their case straight to the Office of the Independent Adjudicator. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what applies?
options: They may do so at once, as a Stage One outcome is the College's final decision
They may go to Pearson or the OIA only once Stage Two has been exhausted
They must first ask the Assessment and Progression Board to reconsider its decision
They must first lodge a fresh Stage One appeal with a different appeal reviewer
questions.explanation: After an unsuccessful Stage One appeal the student may request a Stage Two review, and only after Stage Two is exhausted may they take the case to Pearson or the OIA.
questions.source_excerpt: If the appeal is not upheld, the applicant will be informed of their right to request a review of Stage One ... Following the exhaustion of Stage Two, following which the student may, if the matter has not been resolved to their satisfaction, proceed with their case to the Pearson or the Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA).

questions.question: A student's withdrawal outcome letter, received on 5 March, states that the withdrawal applies from 20 March. On 12 March the student submits an assignment. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, what happens to that assignment?
options: It is marked and considered at the next available Assessment and Progression Board
It is not marked, as it was submitted after the student had received the outcome letter
It is marked only if the student later makes a new admission application
It is held unmarked by Registry until the withdrawal date, then returned to the student
questions.explanation: The outcome letter sets the date from which withdrawal applies, and any assessment submitted before that date is marked and considered at the next available Assessment and Progression Board; 12 March is before 20 March.
questions.source_excerpt: The letter will contain the date from which the withdrawal applies. ... Any assessment submitted by the student prior to their date of withdrawal will be marked and considered at the next available Assessment and Progression Board;

questions.question: Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy's appeal process, which correctly matches each stage with the test a case must meet and where it goes next?
options: Stage One: on reasonable grounds, then to an Appeal Panel; Stage Two: based on valid grounds, then reviewed by the Registrar or a nominated reviewer
Stage One: based on valid grounds, then to an Appeal Panel; Stage Two: on reasonable grounds, then reviewed by the Registrar or a nominated reviewer
Stage One: on reasonable grounds, then reviewed by the Registrar or a nominated reviewer; Stage Two: based on valid grounds, then to an Appeal Panel
Stage One: based on valid grounds, then reviewed by the Registrar or a nominated reviewer; Stage Two: on reasonable grounds, then to an Appeal Panel
questions.explanation: At Stage One, an appeal based on the valid grounds is reviewed by the Registrar or a nominated appeal reviewer; at Stage Two, a request on reasonable grounds is referred by the Quality Assurance Officer to an Appeal Panel.
questions.source_excerpt: If the appeal is considered to be based on the above valid grounds, the Registrar shall conduct the appeal review or nominate an appeal reviewer to investigate the claim; ... If the request is deemed to be on reasonable grounds, the Quality Assurance Officer will refer it to an Appeal Panel.

questions.question: A student lodges a Stage One appeal with the Registrar 14 working days after receiving the withdrawal notification. It is not upheld, and 12 working days after receiving that outcome they write to the Quality Assurance Officer requesting a review. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which is correct?
options: Both were in time, as each stage allows 15 working days from the relevant decision
The appeal was out of time, but the review request was within the time limit
The appeal was in time, but the review request was outside the time limit
Both were out of time, as each stage allows 10 working days from the relevant decision
questions.explanation: A Stage One appeal must be lodged within 15 working days of the written notification (14 is in time), but a Stage Two review must be requested within 10 working days of the Stage One outcome (12 is too late).
questions.source_excerpt: A Student may lodge an appeal against the decision of withdrawal by writing to the Registrar within 15 working days of receiving the written notification of the decision; ... writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome;

questions.question: The Assessment and Progression Board has a role in both student-led and College-led withdrawal under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy. Which pairing of its roles is correct?
options: Student-led: considers assessments submitted before the withdrawal date; College-led: decides withdrawals for attendance or progress
Student-led: approves or rejects the Withdrawal Request Form; College-led: hears Stage One appeals against a withdrawal decision
Student-led: sets the date from which the withdrawal applies; College-led: refers Stage Two review requests to an Appeal Panel
Student-led: decides applications to re-join the College; College-led: decides expulsions following Disciplinary Procedure outcomes
questions.explanation: Assessments submitted before the withdrawal date are considered at the next available Assessment and Progression Board, and the Board takes withdrawal decisions on grounds of unsatisfactory academic progress or unacceptable attendance.
questions.source_excerpt: Any assessment submitted by the student prior to their date of withdrawal will be marked and considered at the next available Assessment and Progression Board; ... Withdrawal decision on the grounds of unsatisfactory academic progress or unacceptable attendance will be taken by the Assessment and Progression Board.

questions.question: The Registrar nominated an appeal reviewer for a student's Stage One appeal, which was not upheld. Six working days later, the student writes to that reviewer asking for the decision to be reviewed. Under the Withdrawal of Studies Policy, which is correct?
options: It is a valid review request, as the reviewer acted as the Registrar's nominee on the appeal
It is a valid review request, provided the Registrar confirms it within 10 working days
It is not a valid request, as a review must be requested within 5 working days of the outcome
It is not a valid request, as it must be made to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee)
questions.explanation: A review of a Stage One decision must be requested in writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee), not the Registrar's appeal reviewer; six working days is within the 10-working-day limit, so timing is not the problem.
questions.source_excerpt: An applicant who wishes to have the Stage One decision reviewed must do so by writing to the Quality Assurance Officer (or nominee) within 10 working days of receiving the Stage One outcome;
